Q&A Pulled from RFI Responses

Section 7.2.3 states that contractor personnel should have a SECRET security clearance at time of award. Could the Government clarify if this is just for the initial IDIQ award? If so, how are offeror’s evaluated for this – based on the IDIQ PM?

All personnel performing work on the contract are required to have a minimum of SECRET, but many workloads will require higher level of clearances.  For contractors to gain access to government development systems a SECRET clearance is often the minimum requirement for personnel to be granted access.

Could the Government clarify the nature of “threat representative capabilities” as mentioned in section 1.3 Scope? Additionally, which section of the Basic Services aligns this scope statement?

The integration of or creation of intel community models that represent threat systems.

Could the Government clarify the evaluation criteria for subsequent TOs on the vehicle?

This is still being worked, official RFP release will have clear evaluation criteria defined.

Modeling and Simulation capabilities: Is AFSC/SWX seeking a MODSIM environment for multi-level security (MLS) with cross domain solutions (CDS) built-in?

SW has these capabilities, there could be future task orders that require experience in these areas.

How will cloud-based services be used to fulfill the scope?

Many SW developmental systems are interconnected with cloud-based systems.  Specific workloads will identify use of those systems when required.

What is AFSC/SWX’s multi-cloud plan?

SW uses hybrid-edge cloud development environments.

What percentage of the scope will be cloud-based and what percentage will remain in the local government datacenter at Wright-Patterson? 

SW uses hybrid-edge cloud development environments.  Some development drives edge compute requirements for integration with hardware-in-the-loop or other requirements.  The scope of work varies across primary performance locations, their specific workloads, and in some cases may be clarified in specific task orders.

Will Hybrid architecture be in scope; where hybrid is defined as: hyperscale cloud services and on-premises services?

SW uses some of these capabilities today.  In the event that specific work in cloud architecture is required for a specific workload it will be identified in a task order level requirement.


Which Impact Levels will be in scope? Please list if SAP/SAR is required. 

Work is currently performed at IL5 and IL6 levels using SW’s own cloud infrastructure.  IL6+ is also required.

Will cloud-based, NSA raise the bar (RTB) compliant cross domain solutions (CDS) be in scope? Does AFSC/SWX need to connect different cloud-based Impact Levels? 

SW does require RTB compliant CDS when applicable to specific workloads.

Will Virtual Desktop Instances (VDI) be needed? If so, at which Impact Level?

SW does use VDIs at all Impact Levels.

 

Cybersecurity: Is AFSC/SWX planning on adopting cloud-based cybersecurity services that can accommodate both on-premise, cloud-based and disconnected operations? 

SW does use cloud-based cybersecurity services that can accommodate on-premises and disconnected operations.

What platforms or systems will be developed and sustained?

The breadth of systems crosses a majority Air Force Mission Design Series (MDS) aircraft.  The scope of potential work spans a variety of work domains including but not limited to modeling and simulation, aircraft operational flight program (OFP), command and control (C2) systems, mission systems development and integration, space systems, across all generations of systems.

What is the current DevSecOps environment, architecture, and tool set currently being used?

There are multiples DevSecOps environments.  Most of these environments are built upon common COTS and GOTS technologies.

Does the Government desire a solution for contractor managed software development environment or plan to host within government services?

Specific workloads may require a contractor managed solution, but most often the software development environments will be government provided with contractor involvement in the stand up and operation of those government owned and managed systems.

What type of labor categories are required, and will they be located on Government site or Contractor Site for this follow-on effort?

Multiple government sites across the country, specifically Wright-Patterson Air Force Base (AFB), Hill AFB, Tinker AFB, Warner-Robins AFB, Nellis AFB, and other government location as required.  Labor categories are best inferred from the requirements within the PWS.

Confirm that the contractor will use Government provided Desktop and/or Laptop computer equipment, and Government provided Test Equipment to perform daily activities for this program in the WPAFB secure facilities, other CONUS facilities, and OCONUS facilities throughout the contract period. Or specify the contractor requirements to provide these capabilities.

Most often the contractor will use Government provided equipment.  In specific task orders the contractor may be required to procure material for performance of work.

Will the Government please confirm the primary place(s) of performance for this contract?

While the SAM listing identifies Hill AFB, UT, an attached document references core locations including Wright-Patterson AFB, OH; Dayton, OH; and Nellis AFB, NV, with secondary locations as RFI Response Department of the Air Force SMARTEC Notice ID: FA8222-25-R-SMTEC TBD. Clarification of primary and secondary locations, as well as any anticipated TDY requirements, would be appreciated.

Multiple government sites across the country, primary locations: Wright-Patterson Air Force Base (AFB), Hill AFB, Tinker AFB, Warner-Robins AFB, 

Secondary and TDY locations: Nellis AFB, Edwards AFB, Eglin AFB, and other government location as required.

Is all classified work conducted at Government provided facility or does the contractor need to provide a classified space for processing?

Government provided facilities.

Does the contractor need to have knowledge or experience with Joint Simulation Environment (JSE), Next Generation Threat System (NGTS), Distributed Interactive Simulation (DIS), High Level Architecture (HLA), or Live Virtual Constructive (LVC)? 

Will the government identify the preferred tools for DevSecOps?

The specific tooling used in existing pipelines is controlled information.

What operating system is required to develop software in?

Typically, Windows and Linux Operating systems.

Is any work able to be conducted and transferred to government classified systems?

Yes, depending on the work.

Following an agile methodology what process is recommended or required?

SW uses both agile scrum and scaled agile methodologies depending on the workload.

Is the process up to the contractor’s discretion?

Process final decision making is up to Government.  Contractor plays significant role in process development and refinement over time and execution of work.

What advanced model types, simulations, or software capabilities?

The breadth of systems crosses a majority Air Force Mission Design Series (MDS) aircraft.  The scope of potential work spans a variety of work domains including but not limited to modeling and simulation, aircraft operational flight program (OFP), command and control (C2) systems, mission systems development and integration, space systems, across all generations of systems.

What legacy or new platforms and systems?

The breadth of systems crosses a majority Air Force Mission Design Series (MDS) aircraft.  The scope of potential work spans a variety of work domains including but not limited to modeling and simulation, aircraft operational flight program (OFP), command and control (C2) systems, mission systems development and integration, space systems, across all generations of systems.

Is the software sustainment on already existing code? 

Both sustainment on existing code and the development and sustainment of new code.

Does the government have general purpose rights for existing code?

Given the wide variety of workloads, data rights vary depending on the project.  SW tends to have unlimited rights at source code level for existing code bases.  Some code base rights may vary depending on the program.

Is integrating with F-16 virtualized, real-world, or certain components of the airframe?

In some workloads we do integrate M&S products with real world hardware or aircraft systems.

Does the government expect to integrate a M&S solution with this airframe?

In some workloads we do integrate M&S products with real world hardware or aircraft systems.

For software testing and plans what is the expectation of format and types of tests? Is the government looking for unit tests, Common Vulnerability Exposure (CVE) reports, vulnerability testing, or something different?

All of the above, specific requirements vary per Authorizing Official with cognizance over the specific system being used to perform a workload.

Could the government identify the type of cybersecurity testing for vulnerability testing of hardware and software? Recommend minimum experience requirements are: Security Technical Implementation Guides (STIGs), Risk Management Framework (RMF), and auditing syst

Experience with STIGS, RMF, JSIG, code analysis tools, essentially all facets of cybersecurity testing and reporting.

Could the government identify the V&V testing of software and hardware for the government owned software?

What facility security inspections are to be conducted?

All security self and third-party inspections typically required for secure facilities.


Could the government provide specific training that is required? 

The training is in multiple knowledge areas including but not limited to Agile and DevSecOps expertise, Tactics, Techniques and Procedures for air-to-air engagements or other warfighting domains, bespoke training for software products developed by the government and/or contractor teams, see section 2.5.2 of the PWS.

Is this for the software created?

In some cases providing training for software created may be required.

Could the government provide specific security services that are required?

Physical security requirements for all facility classification levels including but not limited to: access control, visit requests, personnel security, mail, logs, authoring and enforcing standard operating procedures, security related training.

Could the government breakout the different security requirements for cybersecurity and facility security?

They are broken out separately in the PWS.

Is the Government considering setting aside certain portions of the PWS for Small Businesses?

At this time, we are anticipating full and open competition on the MAC. However, we are looking into best ways to guarantee small business participation.

Will the contractor receive Intel Community-provided models, or will there be a requirement to develop threat models independently?

Intel Community (IC) provided models when applicable.  Where they do not exist and appropriate the contractor may be tasked with producing such models in collaboration with the IC.

Will RMF accreditation follow a standard DoD ATO process, or are specific cybersecurity frameworks anticipated beyond STIG compliance?

Every Authorizing Official has systems specific requirements they levy as supplemental or in implementation of RMF and the JSIG.

Will integration take place at existing Air Force simulation labs, or does the Government expect contractors to provide test environments for validation?  

In many cases within existing laboratories, on a task order by task order basis contractors may be tasked with establishing additional test environments for new workloads.

Section 2.2.1.4: Define the process or template required for “written consent” for introducing proprietary software/data.

For any specific workload or product development it would be a deliberate decision made by the product owner and the issuer of the task order, worked with the contracting officer to facilitate the consent of introduction of proprietary software/data.

follow the procedures outlined in paragraph (c) of this clause. These actions are in addition to any other

size standard of $40 million.

purpose of the contract is to provide web-based subscription to ASTM International materials and 
standards collections, in electronic format and via Internet–based networking subscription 
arrangement, with instantaneous access with 24/7 availability. Subscription includes ASTM 
Complete Book of Standards to include all volumes and sections of active and historical standards 
accessible from the desktop and mobile device of DoD employees.

Microsoft Word format no later than 23 July 2026 to the Contract Specialist, Kimberly Hall, via 
email kimberly.a.hall124.civ@us.navy.mil.

solicitation for bid or proposals, and is not to be construed as a commitment by the Government. For

Request for Information 
Department of Veterans Affairs Enterprise Artificial Intelligence 
VA-26-00070193 
May 29, 2026 
 
1. Purpose: 
This is a Request for Information (RFI) only issued for conducting market research.  
Accordingly, this RFI constitutes neither a Request for Quote (RFQ), Request for Proposal 
(RFP), nor a guarantee that one will be issued by the Government in the future; furthermore, it 
does not commit the Government to contract for any services described herein. The Department 
of Veterans Affairs (VA) is not, at this time, seeking proposals or quotes, and therefore, will not 
accept, review, or evaluate unsolicited proposals or quotes received in response hereto. This 
notice is not to be construed as a commitment on the part of the Government to award a contract, 
nor does the Government intend to pay for any information submitted because of this request. 
The Government does not reimburse respondents for any costs associated with submission of the 
information being requested or reimburse expenses incurred for responses to this RFI. The 
information provided may be used by VA in developing its acquisition strategy and requirements 
documentation. Any information submitted by respondents to this RFI is strictly voluntary; 
however, any information received shall become the property of the Government and will not be 
returned to the respondent. Respondents are responsible for clearly marking any information they 
consider proprietary or commercially sensitive on a page-by-page basis. VA will use reasonable 
measures to protect legitimately designated proprietary information, but cannot guarantee 
confidentiality under applicable law, including the Freedom of Information Act (5 U.S.C. § 552). 
Interested parties are responsible for adequately marking proprietary, restricted, or competition 
sensitive information contained in their response.  
 
2. Background: 
VA serves 18.25 million Veterans and their families, administering benefits, delivering clinical 
care, and providing Veteran-facing digital services at enterprise scale. The Veterans Health 
Administration, which operates under VA, is the most extensive healthcare system in the U.S., 
serving around 9 million Veterans annually through its 1,200 facilities. 
 
As Artificial Intelligence (AI) capabilities advance rapidly, VA is committed to harnessing AI to 
improve Veterans' lives, delivering faster, higher-quality, and more cost-efficient services, while 
upholding the highest standards of safety, security, and equity. This RFI shares information on 
the current and future state of VA's AI requirements and seeks market insights in preparation for 
a solicitation, in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 10.001.   
 
VA’s vision and priorities for artificial intelligence adoption: 
VA intends to be an industry leader in adopting AI to improve Veterans’ lives by delivering 
faster, higher quality, and more cost-efficient services with strong governance and trust.  
 
There are five priorities: 
1. Expand AI access across the workforce  
2. Build an AI-ready workforce 
3. Reimagine high-impact workflows with AI, automation, and agentic capabilities 

RFI – VA Enterprise AI 
 
 2  
 
4. Invest in data and infrastructure for AI adoption 
5. Run transparent and effective AI governance 
 
This RFI focuses on Priority 1 (expand AI access) and Priority 3 (reimagine high-impact 
workflows), specifically the user-facing tool and Application Programming Interface (API) 
services layers that enable both. Priorities 2, 4, and 5 are addressed through complementary VA 
programs and are out of scope for this acquisition. 
 
On priority 1, expand AI access across the workforce, there have been early wins: 
 
1. VA GPT (a generative AI chat tool co-developed with Microsoft): 95,000 sign-ups to 
date; a small subset of active users report saving 2–3 hours per week. 70% of survey 
respondents report improved job satisfaction. 
2. Microsoft GitHub Copilot: 2,000 developers signed up to use AI-assisted software 
development. Survey respondents report saving 8 hours per week per user. 74% report 
they can focus on work that is more satisfying to them. 
3. In clinical care, there was a 22% decrease in mortality associated with implementation of 
an AI-assisted clinical decision support tool. 
4. With AI-powered colonoscopy devices, there was a 21% increase in adenoma detection.  
5. More AI-embedded use cases are available publicly through VA’s 2025 AI Inventory 
interactive dashboard. 
 
3. Current generative AI use: 
The federal AI tool landscape has expanded significantly, consistent with the Administration's 
directive to leverage commercially available solutions to the maximum extent practicable. 
Microsoft's 365 Copilot is now available to federal agencies under enterprise licensing, while the 
General Services Administration’s (GSA) OneGov initiative and associated pilots has broadened 
access to generative AI capabilities across many federal agencies. VA is actively piloting tools 
from multiple Frontier AI Labs to evaluate user experience, performance, and value at enterprise 
scale. 
 
As of May 2026, VA has concurrent generative AI pilots for user-facing tools through Microsoft 
and GSA OneGov – Anthropic's Claude for Government, Google’s Gemini for Government, and 
OpenAI’s ChatGPT Enterprise FedRAMP. In addition, large language model (LLM) API 
services are used through cloud providers, as part of VA Enterprise Cloud: AWS Government, 
Azure Government, and Azure Commercial, consistent with Executive Order (EO) 14271's 
directive to leverage commercially available solutions to the maximum extent practicable.  
 
Current adoption of generative AI, user-facing tools with chat capabilities: 
Products in Table 1have passed VA's Authority to Operate (ATO) requirements for use with 
Protected Health Information (PHI) and Personally Identifiable Information (PII).

5. Where VA is going, three illustrative examples: 
VA is building enterprise-grade AI infrastructure to support the full spectrum of AI interaction, 
from assistive to collaborative to agentic, spanning compute, foundation models, data 
integration, orchestration, and user-facing surfaces, with governance embedded at every layer.  
This architecture prioritizes commercially available solutions consistent with EO 14271 and the 
Federal Acquisition Streamlining Act (FASA) and is informed by deployments at leading AI-
forward public sector and enterprise organizations in healthcare and financial services, including 
government digital services agencies and health systems. 
 
For this specific RFI, the focus is: 
1. User-facing layer: User-facing surface(s) with chat and agentic capabilities including 
advanced tooling (connectors, skills, plugins), managed-assistants, and managed-agents. 
2. Compute and foundation model layer: The most direct, programmatic access to closed 
foundation models from multiple frontier labs. 
 
Together, these building blocks will address VA’s knowledge worker, operator, and 
engineer/quant needs as users move between assistive, collaborative, and agentic based to 
improve internal operations and Veterans services.

Statement of Work 
Introduction 
Understanding the eƯects of land use and land cover (LULC) change and ecosystem 
disturbances on wildﬁre vulnerability and fuel loading is a critical requirement for national 
safety and resource management. Modeling how changes in vegetation and land 
management inﬂuence ﬁre behavior is a priority goal identiﬁed for the USGS Ecosystems 
Mission Area. The USGS has previously developed methodologies to quantify past and 
current LULC change and project future scenarios, linking these data with ecological 
models to estimate how "fuels"—represente d by biomass and carbon stocks—accumulate 
and interact with natural disturbances over space and time. 
While initial assessments provided a foundation for understanding landscape change, 
signiﬁcant technical gaps remain regarding the integrated linkage between LULC dynamics 
and wildﬁre risk. Speciﬁcally, there is a need for an integrated, easy-to-use, open-source 
model that emphasizes the spatial and temporal variability of fuel loads and the resulting 
ﬁre consequences. Through a collaboration between a contractor and USGS, a proof-of-
concept model was developed: the Land Use and Carbon Scenario Simulator (LUCAS). 
Built upon the SyncroSim/ST-Sim state-and-transition simulation modeling framework, 
this tool was designed to produce reliable estimates of changes in LULC and the 
associated biomass (carbon) stocks that serve as primary ﬁre fuels. 
The next phase of this eƯort involves reﬁning the model to better simulate ﬁre regimes, fuel 
transitions, and the impact of various land-management strategies on ﬁre risk. This 
includes structural improvements to how the model treats biomass accumulation and 
decay, enhancements to ﬁre-spread visualization, and the ability to run high-resolution 
simulations in high-performance computing environments. 
The USGS seeks to continue the development of this model to track land-based fuels and 
ﬁre risk across the conterminous U.S. This contract supports the development of 
operational and scientiﬁc improvements to the model, focusing on its ability to project how 
natural and anthropogenic processes—including climate change, urbanization, and land 
management—alter the wild ﬁre landscape. 
As speciﬁed in this contract, the Contractor will design and complete enhancements to the 
ST-Sim software as requested and approved by the USGS Point-of-Contact to support 
these wildﬁre and land-use objectives. 
Deliverables 

Page 2 of 4 
 
Anticipated deliverables are divided into two categories and will be speciﬁcally deﬁned as 
individual tasks: 
A. General Technical Support Provide technical support to the USGS in the use, 
application, and customization of the SyncroSim/ST-Sim software module. This includes: 
• Assisting in the conﬁguration and parameterization of fuel load variables and ﬁre 
transition probabilities. 
• Calculating and processing external data (e.g., remote sensing vegetation data) to 
provide input model parameters. 
• Developing post-processing analytical tools to translate model outputs into ﬁre-risk 
maps and hazard assessments. 
• Collaborating on scientiﬁc meetings, publications, and reports regarding LULC-
driven ﬁre dynamics. 
B. Software Enhancements Provide software enhancements to the SyncroSim/ST-Sim 
application to support ongoing program requirements. This includes: 
• Adding new features to simulate complex ﬁre-regime interactions and fuel 
treatment eƯectiveness. 
• Modifying underlying code to improve the scaling of large-area wildﬁre simulations. 
• Updating documentation and training materials to reﬂect new wildﬁre-centric 
modeling capabilities. 
• Ensuring ongoing compatibility of the software with current USGS data standards 
and high-performance computing requirements.

Performance Work Statement (PWS)

For

Information Technology Automation Management Support Services (AMSS)

United States Army Garrison – Hawaii (USAG-HI)

1.0. BACKGROUND

This requirement is for the U.S. Army Garrison – Hawaii (USAG-HI). USAG-HI is located at Schofield Barracks (SB), Wheeler Army Airfield (WAAF), Fort Shafter (FS), Helemano Military Reservation (HMR), Aliamanu Military Reservation (AMR), and Tripler Army Medical Center (TAMC) on the Island of Oahu, and at Pohakuloa Training Area (PTA) and Kilauea Military Camp (KMC) on the Island of Hawaii. USAG-HI's mission is to provide quality services and infrastructure from the Strategic Support Area for quality of life and mission readiness to Soldiers, Civilians, and Families in the Military Ohana Community.

The USAG-HI Information Management Office (IMO), working under the USAG-HI Garrison Commander, is responsible for providing Automation Management Support Services (AMSS) to all USAG-HI organizations. Sustainment of current and emerging Information Technology (IT) support is a critical enabler to accomplishing all USAG-HI missions. With the shortage of IT Government personnel, USAG-HI organizations cannot meet required mission objectives without the use of contract support personnel.

1.1. Place of Performance

Accomplishment of the results contained in this PWS requires work at USAG-HI locations on Oahu and Hawaii Islands. The Contractor's primary duty location (HQ) is Building 107, Wheeler Army Airfield (WAAF). Service is delivered across all eight (8) USAG-HI locations:

1.2. Period of Performance

Period of Performance is for a twelve (12)-month base period consisting of a thirty (30)-calendar-day phase-in period and eleven (11) months of full performance, followed by four (4) one-year Option Periods exercisable under FAR 52.217-9. This is a non-personal services contract (FAR 37.101, DFARS 237.104) acquired on a Firm-Fixed-Price basis as a Performance-Based Acquisition (FAR Part 37.6 and FAR Part 39).

2.0. SCOPE

Contractor shall provide qualified IT Support Technicians and transportation for delivery of AMSS to USAG-HI across all eight (8) locations listed in Section 1.1. Services support approximately 1,500 personnel across four (4) functional service areas. Webmaster and Database Administration functions are excluded. The Contractor shall complete 100% of ticket submissions in accordance with the performance standards defined in this PWS. The Contractor shall propose staffing in its technical proposal sufficient to meet all PWS performance standards; the Government does not prescribe FTE counts on this Firm-Fixed-Price contract.

2.2. Historical Workload Estimates

The following table provides historical data for informational purposes to aid offerors in developing their staffing approach. The Government does not guarantee future volumes will match this historical data. The Contractor is responsible for proposing a solution that can meet the PRS metrics across this range of potential workloads.

Note: Historical data based on previous 24 months from the USAG-HI S6 SPO Ticketing System. Scorecard weighting: Help Desk 40%, VTC/AV 25%, Knowledge Management 20%, IT Asset & Device Management 15% (see Section 19.0 PRS).

2.3. Comprehensive Workload Execution (100% Requirement)

The workload estimates provided above are historical and informational, intended solely to assist Offerors in developing their staffing and pricing strategies. The Contractor shall be responsible for receiving, processing, and successfully resolving 100% of the actual workload generated during the period of performance across all service areas. Regardless of volume fluctuations, peaks, or surges, the Contractor must continuously meet or exceed all Service Level Agreements (SLAs) and Acceptable Quality Levels (AQLs) defined in the Performance Requirement Summary (PRS) and monitored through the Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan (QASP).

2.4. Mission-Outcome Orientation

Requirements in this PWS are stated as mission outcomes the Contractor shall achieve (e.g., maintain user account accessibility, sustain VTC/AV mission readiness, preserve IT asset accountability), rather than as prescriptive tasks or FTE inputs. The Contractor has full discretion over methods, tooling, and staffing mix used to deliver these outcomes, provided all PRS metrics and applicable regulations are met.

2.5. External Dependencies and SLA-Pause Conditions

The Government owns and maintains the underlying network infrastructure (servers, routers, switches, WAN/LAN backbone, NIPR/SIPR transport, enterprise identity, and Tier 2/3 escalation platforms). Failures or degradations of Government-owned infrastructure, enterprise software, or vendor-provided services are Government responsibility and shall not count against Contractor SLA/AQL performance. The SLA clock shall pause when a ticket status is set to Pending Government, Pending Vendor / External, or Pending User Response, with the reason and duration documented in the SPO Ticketing System, per the definition of SLA Clock “Pause” in Section 21.

2.6. Phase-In

This requirement includes a 30-day phase-in period. The Contractor shall follow the transition plan submitted as part of the proposal and keep the Government fully informed throughout. The Phase-In period is to allow the Contractor sufficient time to recruit and on-board all personnel proposed in its staffing plan, obtain clearances and required certifications, stand up Contractor-developed systems (VTC/AV Event Tracking, IT Asset / Printer-MFD / Mobile Device / Software License trackers, Conference Room Booking System), submit required plans, and achieve full operational capability NLT the 23rd working day after award.

Measurable Phase-In Milestones:

2.6.1. Retain Qualified Staff

The Contractor shall provide the full amount of contracted personnel designated for this contract for the full duration of the performance period. Vacancies shall be backfilled per Section 11.0.

Measurable Staffing Standards:

3.0. CONTRACTOR PERSONNEL

3.1. Staffing Requirements

The Contractor shall provide sufficient qualified personnel to meet all performance standards defined in this PWS. The Contractor shall propose their complete staffing plan, in their technical proposal.

At minimum, the Contractor's staffing plan shall ensure:

Continuous coverage during normal business hours (0700–1700, Monday–Friday).

Coverage at Pohakuloa Training Area (PTA), Big Island.

Island-wide support coverage for Directorate of Emergency Services (DES) facilities including all gates, offices, and DES equipment (AIE terminals, printers, computers, phones). NOTE: DES support does NOT include NCIC/FBI systems.

Priority response capability for TAP office and fingerprint systems (two (2)-hour response).

For COOP/EOC activations or publicly and reasonably covered events (flooding, natural disasters, installation outages, etc.), the Contractor must be able to support the Emergency Operations Center (EOC) within two (2) hours of notification. The Contractor shall develop and maintain a dedicated COOP/EOC Support Plan and process as part of their Emergency/Disaster Support Plan deliverable.

3.2. Key Personnel

The Contractor shall designate the following Key Personnel positions. Résumés and qualifications for proposed Key Personnel shall be submitted with the technical proposal and are subject to Government approval.

3.2.1. Team Lead / Project Manager (Key Personnel)

Serves as the primary Government point of contact and COR liaison.

Manages all contractor personnel and daily operations.

Coordinates emergency response and surge staffing.

Ensures performance standard compliance across all service areas.

Minimum Qualifications: meets all baseline qualifications in Section 3.3; minimum five (5) years of IT support experience with at least two (2) years in a lead, supervisory, or project management role; demonstrated experience managing geographically dispersed teams; PMP, ITIL, or equivalent management certification preferred.

3.2.2. Key Personnel Replacement

Key Personnel shall not be removed or replaced without prior written approval from the Contracting Officer. If a Key Personnel position becomes vacant, the Contractor shall:

Notify the COR within twenty-four (24) hours.

Provide a qualified replacement within fifteen (15) calendar days.

Submit replacement résumé for Government approval.

Failure to backfill within fifteen (15) calendar days results in daily rate deductions of 1.5× the position's daily rate for each day the position remains vacant beyond the 15-day window.

3.3. Minimum Qualifications — All Contractor Personnel

All contractor personnel shall meet the following minimum qualifications:

Three (3) years of verifiable, related IT support experience.

Associate's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, or related field — OR an equivalent combination of certifications, education, and experience as approved by the Government.

CompTIA Security+ certification (or successor certification per DoDM 8140.03) obtained within sixty (60) calendar days of contract award or position start date.

Demonstrated proficiency in problem-solving, troubleshooting, communication, and customer service.

Experience with Army-required platforms including (or demonstrably similar platforms): SharePoint Online (SPO), Power BI, Power Automate, Power Apps, Microsoft Teams, and Army-authorized Generative AI tools as directed by USAG-HI IMO.

Familiarity with Microsoft 365 / Army365 productivity and collaboration tools as approved and directed by the Government during the period of performance.

Experience with mobile device management (MDM) tools and platforms including but not limited to cell phones, iPads, tablets, and enterprise MDM solutions such as Microsoft Intune.

3.4. Coverage Requirements

3.4.1. Normal Business Hours Coverage

The Contractor shall provide coverage during normal USAG-HI business hours: 0700–1700, Monday through Friday (excluding Federal holidays).

3.4.2. Geographic Coverage

The Contractor shall provide coverage at the following locations:

Wheeler Army Airfield (Primary HQ): Building 107 — primary contractor workspace and COR co-location.

Schofield Barracks: on-call response capability.

Fort Shafter: on-call response capability.

Tripler Army Medical Center (TAMC): on-call response capability.

Helemano Military Reservation (HMR): on-call response capability.

Aliamanu Military Reservation (AMR): on-call response capability.

DES Sites Island-Wide (Oahu): all gates, offices, and DES facilities — Contractor shall ensure coverage.

Pohakuloa Training Area (PTA), Big Island: Contractor shall ensure coverage.

Kilauea Military Recreation Camp (KMC), Big Island: Contractor shall ensure coverage during scheduled visits or from Oahu-based personnel.

3.4.3. Inter-Island Support Model

The Contractor shall ensure coverage at PTA, Big Island.

Quarterly site visits from Oahu-based staff to PTA/KMC (minimum four per year).

One to two (1–2) additional TDY trips per year based on mission needs, with COR approval.

PTA response times shall be the same as Oahu standards (Contractor personnel local to Big Island).

3.5. Geographic Coverage and Facility Operations

The Contractor shall provide comprehensive IT support services across multiple USAG-HI locations. The Government will provide dedicated workspace (GFP) to facilitate Contractor operations at the following primary locations.

3.5.1. Centralized Oahu Operations

The Government will provide primary workspace for the Contractor’s team on Oahu (e.g., Building 107, Wheeler Army Airfield). The Contractor shall utilize this location as the central hub for dispatching support, coordinating with the COR, and executing the requirements of this PWS. To ensure effective management and communication, the Contractor’s designated Team Lead shall be available for in-person meetings with the COR at this primary duty location with no more than one (1) hour’s notice during Core Hours.

3.5.2. Pohakuloa Training Area (PTA) and Kilauea Military Camp (KMC) Operations

Due to the geographic isolation of PTA and KMC (Island of Hawaii), remote dispatch from Oahu is insufficient to meet the required Service Level Agreements (SLAs). The Government will provide dedicated workspace at PTA. The Contractor shall utilize this provided workspace to maintain a continuous, daily on-site operational presence at PTA during Core Hours. To account for the geographical separation on the island, response times for on-site “touch labor” shall be as follows:

PTA On-Site Response (Priority 1 & 2): ≤ 30 minutes from ticket creation (as the technician is operating out of the provided PTA workspace).

KMC On-Site Response (Priority 1 & 2): ≤ 2 hours from ticket creation (allowing for travel time from PTA). The Contractor is expected to perform initial remote triage before dispatching personnel to KMC.

Routine (Priority 3) Support (PTA & KMC): Handled remotely or scheduled for resolution during standard weekly/bi-weekly site visits to KMC, ensuring optimal use of travel time.

3.5.3. Inter-Island Travel

The Government will provide travel funding for Contractor inter-island TDY (Oahu ↔ Big Island) beyond the resident PTA presence, subject to advance COR approval. Offerors shall not inflate their Firm-Fixed-Price to cover speculative inter-island travel; reimbursable travel shall be handled under Section 10.8 (Travel / TDY).

3.6. Staffing Stability and Continuity

The Contractor shall minimize personnel turnover to maintain service quality and institutional knowledge.

All personnel changes (except Key Personnel, which require Government approval) shall be reported to the COR within five (5) business days.

Replacement personnel shall meet all minimum qualifications before assignment.

The Contractor shall provide a minimum thirty (30)-day overlap for personnel transitions when practicable.

3.7. Contractor-Proposed Staffing Plan

The Contractor shall submit their proposed staffing plan as part of the technical proposal, including:

Position descriptions and assignments.

Coverage schedule (normal business hours, PTA, DES).

Key Personnel résumés.

The Government will evaluate the proposed staffing plan based on its ability to meet all performance standards defined in Section 16.0.

Sections 3.8 through 3.12 below define the technical service-area requirements that the staffing plan in Sections 3.1–3.7 shall support.

3.8.0. Help Desk and End User Support Requirements

3.8.1. Contractor personnel shall have knowledge of AR 25-2 (Army Cybersecurity), DoDI 8500.01 and 8510.01, the AMD procedures, and applicable cybersecurity policy.

3.8.2. Contractor personnel shall provide Tier I and Tier II help desk and desktop touch labor on NIPRNet and SIPRNet, including incident triage, troubleshooting, account management, software installation, hardware break/fix co

Statement of Work (SOW) 
 
1. PROJECT TITLE: UniPOC Glucometer Software Requirement for Crow/Northern Cheyenne 
Hospital, Lodge Grass Clinic, and Pryor Health Station. 
 
2. BACKGROUND/PURPOSE: The contractor shall provide software that will interface the 
glucometers with the computer electronic health record at Crow Service Unit and make the 
management website available to the program coordinator via Microsoft Edge. This will allow 
the results from glucose tests to cross the interface and be in the RPMS/HER system without user 
entry. This will save time and reduce errors.  
 
3. SCOPE: Current Point of Care Glucometer contract has lapsed.  The contractor shall 
implement software and maintain software for use by the facilities. User identification numbers, 
training requirements, quality control and reagents information are all kept by the program and 
the point of care coordinator uses the software to input all the necessary information through this 
program. 
 
4. TASKS: The contractor shall: 
a. Install UniPOC software for use with current glucometers in use at Crow/Northern 
Cheyenne Hospital, Pryor Health Station and Lodge Grass Clinic. 
1. Manage the incoming reagents, quality control, and strip lots. 
2. Manage the access codes for all employees. 
3. Store quality control results and create printouts for hard copy 
storage. 
4. Create reports for critical value patients and compliance to 
reporting requirements. 
b. Provide training for all staff on the UniPOC® software. 
c. Maintain quality control, reagent lot and expiration dates, and 
critical value monitoring through the new program. 
 

5. DELIVERABLES AND DELIVERY SCHEDULE: The contractor shall produce software 
license for document record and training to ensure full functionality within 30 days of award. 
6. GOVERNMENT-FURNISHED EQUIPMENT AND INFORMATION: Indian Health Service 
computers are used to access the software and complete the interfacing. 
 
7. PLACE OF PERFORMANCE: 
Crow/Northern Cheyenne Hospital 
1010 7650 E, Crow Agency, MT 59022 
 
Pryor Health Station 
2 Pryor Gap Rd, Pryor, MT 59066 
 
Lodge Grass Clinic 
418 Harding Ave, Lodge Grass, MT 59050 
 
8. PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE: 1 year performance with 4 option years; 10/01/2026-
09/30/2031 
 
9. SECURITY: Work will require IT clearance and installation.

SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE

Tracking Number 832675110

The Defense Information Systems Agency (DISA) is seeking sources for Portfolio Acquisition Executive (PAE) Cyber’s Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) Sustainment requirement. 

CONTRACTING OFFICE ADDRESS: Defense Information Technology Contracting Organization - National Capital Region (DITCO-NCR / PS6)

INTRODUCTION:

This is a SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE to determine the availability and technical capability of small businesses (including the following subsets: Small Disadvantaged Businesses, Certified 8(a), Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses, HUBZone Small Businesses and Woman-Owned Small Businesses) to provide the required products and/or services. 

DISA PAE Cyber, PKI Division is seeking information from potential sources for: sustainment and sustainment-engineering support of the existing PKI platform, and continued program management and sustainment support. This will include operational monitoring and reporting support, multi-tiered support, training support, and system integration/deployment support. 

The anticipated Period of Performance is 4 May 2027 – 3 May 2032. 

The anticipated Place of Performance is DISA, Ft. Meade, MD, and the contractor facility located within the National Capital Region.

DISCLAIMER: 

 

THIS SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL.  IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT.  RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS NOTICE.  NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS NOTICE.  ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY.

CONTRACT/PROGRAM BACKGROUND: 

PKI Sustainment is a follow-on requirement, with current contract details listed below. A portion of the existing contract’s requirement is being removed and competed through a separate acquisition.  The enablement support within the existing contract will not be included in this recompete action. 

Contract Number: HC104719D2035 / HC102823F2002

Contract Vehicle: SETI Small Business Suite 

Incumbent and their size: Riverside Engineering LLC; Small Business Joint Venture 

Method of previous acquisition: SETI, Small Business

Period of performance: 4 October 2023 – 3 December 2026  

REQUIRED CAPABILITIES:

Registration Authority (RA). The Department of Defense (DoD) PKI team supports RA requirements for the DoD and its Federal Partners, managing the end-to-end lifecycle (issuance, renewal, and revocation) of both User credentials, and Non-Person Entity (NPE) certificates.  Describe and provide an example of your company’s experience providing RA and Local Registration Authority (LRA) support services within the DoD or other Federal agencies. What was the size and scope of the user and device base supported?

Secure Testing Lab Operation and Maintenance. The DoD PKI team operates an Operations & Maintenance (O&M) lab, and Compliance lab for the purpose of testing enhancements, and maintaining compliance with application and security updates to maintain compliance of PKI systems.  Describe and provide an example of your company’s experience establishing, operating, and maintaining a secure testing lab designed to support PKI O&M and Compliance.  Specifically, detail your structured process for ensuring a baselined configuration, analyzing and tracking Information Assurance Vulnerability Alerts (IAVAs), Bulletins (IAVBs), and third-party software updates from initial identification through to operational deployment.  Describe all tools used for these processes.

Commercial Off the Shelf (COTS) Technology. The DoD PKI team maintains support at operational PKI sites that are heavily reliant upon Commercial Off the Shelf (COTS) technology.  Describe  and provide an example of your company’s experience with using Red Hat (RH) Products (RH Enterprise Linux, RH Directory Server, RH Certificate System), Hardware Security Modules (HSMs), F5 BigIP’s, and any other directory service technologies.

Enterprise PKI Customer Support. DoD PKI exists to support our customers; therefore, customer support and outreach are the PKI program’s top priorities. Describe and provide an example of your company’s support functions with respect to deploying systems related to enterprise PKI. This support should include a focus on help desk operations, development and updates to technical guides, on-site visits, and ServiceNow/ITSM+/Helix support.

SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS: 

Must have final Secret Facility Clearance.  Please provide your current Facility Clearance level.

Must be CMMC Level II Self Certified. Please provide your current CMMC level.

The North American Industry Classification System Code (NAICS) for this requirement is 541512 – Computer Systems Design Services, with the corresponding size standard of $34M.

PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT (PWS)

1.  Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR).  

Primary COR. See DITCO Additional Text G1 – Points of Contact

Alternate COR. See DITCO Additional Text G1 – Points of Contact

Alternate COR. See DITCO Additional Text G1 – Points of Contact

2.  Task Order Title.  Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) Sustainment

3.  Background.  The Department of Defense (DoD) PKI Portfolio is the mechanism for providing Public Key (PK) certificates that support mission critical DoD applications. PKI satisfies the DoD’s Information Assurance (IA) requirement for confidentiality and authentication of network transactions, identification and verification of data integrity, and non-repudiation of communications or transactions. 

As PKI capabilities have expanded and become more ubiquitous, requirements for its security benefits and systems enhancements have increased to better meet the reliability and availability requirements of the DoD community. 

4.  Objectives.  The objective of this Task Order (TO) is to provide sustainment and sustainment-engineering support of the existing PKI platform, and continued program management and sustainment support. This will include operational monitoring and reporting support, multi-tiered support, training support, and system integration/deployment support. 

5.  Scope.  The scope of this TO includes the operations and sustainment of existing PKI Government Off the Shelf (GOTS) code; requirement analysis and definition; procurement; IA analysis; Risk Management Framework (RMF) support; integration of Commercial Off the Shelf (COTS) products and services; quality assurance/system evaluation; developmental testing; installation support; documentation; operational reporting and monitoring; and system performance analysis to improve and expand DISA PKI system on Defense Information Systems Agency (DISA) utilized networks to include Non-Secure Internet Protocol Router Network (NIPRNET) and Secret Internet Protocol Router Network (SIPRNET). These sustainment activities shall remain in effect and fully supported until the PKI infrastructure is upgraded, modernized, or otherwise tech-refreshed, ensuring uninterrupted mission capabilities throughout the transition to new or enhanced platforms.  The contractor shall perform as an integrated team member with other vendors, other Government contractors, and Government organizations in providing services under this PWS.  

In order to meet Presidential EO 13587 Acquisition Category (ACAT) Information Assurance Management (IAM), and DoD Chief Information Officer/DISA directed enhancements, the main sub-components to include: Non-Classified Internet Protocol Router Network (NIPRNet) PKI, Common Service Provider, Token Management System, Global Directory Services, Non-Person Entity, NIPRNet Enterprise Alternate Token System, Robust Certificate Validation System, External Certificate Authority, Purebred, and Public Trust.

The NIPRNet and Secret Internet Protocol Router Network (SIPRNet) PKI deployments have varying Certificate Authority (CA) lifecycles and requires frequent deployments to ensure operational capability to meet requirements, or example Web Content Filtering (WCF), Hardware certificates, Software Certs, mobile device certs (PureBred), Non-Person Entity, Code Signing.

Common Service Provider (CSP):

The Committee on National Security Systems (CNSS) recognized that it was not cost-effective for each Federal Agency to establish and operate a separate PKI.  As a result, CNSS Policy No. 25 created a CSP, which would operate the National Security System (NSS) PKI and provide certificate management services for Participating Agencies (PAs).  The CNSS Directive #506 establishes the requirement for all federal agencies to implement the NSS-PKI to promote interoperability and secure information sharing and to use PKI to provide strong authentication on Secret level networks.  The DoD PKI Program Management Office (PMO), using previous NIPRNet and SIPRNet PKI experience, responded and built an NSS PKI infrastructure for the DoD.  The DoD is currently issuing SIPRNet hardware tokens from this infrastructure to personnel in the PAs.

The DoD PKI PMO, under the guidance of the CNSS and primary management of DISA, has been working with the CNSS PKI Member Governing Body to incorporate the capabilities needed by the CSP into the NSS PKI.  The CSP began issuing certificates on hardware tokens in June 2013.  DISA manages the certificate life cycle for PAs. 

Token Management System (TMS):

The SIPRNet TMS allows SIPRNet users to generate credentials and store them on a hardware token.  The SIPRNet TMS consists of Red Hat 8.1 Certificate Server (CS) software packages and the Red Hat Directory Server 8.1 software packages.  The SIPRNet TMS consists of the following new components: Certificate Manager, Token Key Service (TKS), Token Processing System (TPS), Registration Portal, Data Recovery Manager and Directory Server.

Non-Person Entity (NPE):

The NPE system provides certificates to devices (e.g., workstations, mobile devices, web servers, network equipment) from a trusted CA on both the NIPRNet and SIPRNet.  Certificates for NPEs will increase security by enhancing the identity and authentication of devices to DoD networks.  NPE also provides Secure Socket Layer (SSL) certificates for encryption purposes to enhance data authenticity. 

The NPE system is one of the DoD PKI Certificate and Token Issuance systems within the DoD PKI.  Its primary mission is to issue certificates for devices and services on the NIPRNet and SIPRNet.  In order to accomplish this mission, the NPE system also provides services that support user registration and management, compromise management, and reporting.   

NIPRNet Enterprise Alternate Token System (NEATS): 

NEATS provides confidentiality, integrity, authentication, and non-repudiation services by providing a centralized token management system for NIPRNet medium assurance certificates on NEATS tokens, known as Alternate Tokens, for use cases to include groups, roles, code signing and individuals not authorized to receive a CAC.  NEATS will issue, revoke, suspend, provide key recovery, and provide token issuance and inventory management of each Alternate Tokens received into the system and until removed from the system permanently.  NEATS improves security by leveraging PKI credentials for authentication and it strengthens accountability across the NIPRNet by tracking access to these PKI credentials.  NEATS uses the Authoritative Data Repository as the authoritative data source and the CAC infrastructure to register users and issue tokens.

STATEMENT OF NEED (SON) 
 
Page 1 of 3 
 
 
 
1.0 TITLE 
 
iLab Solutions Subscription Renewal for CCR Core Facilities 
  
2.0 BACKGROUND 
 
The CCR core facilities under the Office of Science Technology Resource (OSTR) in the Center for Cancer 
Research (CCR) at the National Cancer Institute (NCI) require the renewal of its iLab Operations Software 
which has been in use since 2015.  This modular, web -based, asset management software supports the 
operation of 8 cores in addition to other shared resources. The iLab Core Facility Management Software is 
essential for the day -to-day operations of our core facilities, enabling these facilities to operate more 
effectively and efficiently. The software allows for seamless service request processing, project 
management, and billing, all while streamlining administrative functions. Its use has been crucial for our 
six current core facilities and  will become even more critical as we expand to include two more core 
facilities. Without the software, it would be exceedingly difficult to manage the increased operational 
complexity of these facilities. 
3.0 OBJECTIVES 
 
The OSTR requires a web -based tool for research management  to support various operational functions 
across eight (8) core facilities at the CCR, including service request management, customer and project 
management, billing and invoicing, as well integration with internal financial systems.  The iLab Operations 
Software streamlines the management of the core facilities, ensuring operational efficiency, and enhancing 
the ability to track and manage costs. The software will allow government to continue benefiting from these 
advantages and further streamline operations at the NCI/CCR. 
 
4.0       TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS  
 
4.1 PRODUCT FEATURES/SALIENT CHARACTERISTICS 
 
 
The following product features/characteristics are required for this requirement:  
 
• Software shall be modular, web-based with functionality to include Core facilities 
management, instrument access and control, sample processing management and publication 
tracking 
• Sample processing management must allow for the creation of customized processor types, 
request forms, and associated services to support many technologies, instrumentation, and 
workflows across multiple Core types. 
• Sample processing module must have the ability to generate customizable sample sheets 
(Sanger, Nanostring nCounter, ddPCR) for upload into instrument software to preserve 
current Core workflows  

   
STATEMENT OF NEED (SON) 
 
Page 2 of 3 
 
• Lab management software shall be capable of integrating with our institutional financial 
systems (Business Management Systems [BMS]) providing unified and streamlined billing 
and invoicing process across multiple core facilities. 
• The software must have an intuitive billing platform to ensure accurate accounting and timely 
compensation with the billing and invoicing module 
• Must have usage tracking kiosk interface to provide real-time equipment usage tracking to 
allow for more efficient confirmation and billing process. 
• Software must have the ability to manually block users from using individual pieces of 
equipment that require verification of training before the equipment may be used. 
 
 
4.2 TRAINING  
N/A 
 
4.3 SPECIAL ORDER REQUIREMENTS 
 
The Contractor shall provide Software Service and updates in accordance with the manufacturer’s latest 
established service procedures, to include telephone access to technical support for use of program 
software and troubleshooting of the operating systems, at no additional cost to the Government.  The 
contractor shall receive advance approval for the installation of all software updates and revisions from 
the Government.  Defective software shall be replaced at no additional cost to the government. 
 
5.0 TYPE OF ORDER 
 
This is a Firm Fixed-Price Purchase Order. 
 
 
Upon delivery and acceptance of the item(s) described in SECTION 4.0 of this contract and identified in 
the schedule of charges below, the Government shall pay to the Contractor the unit price(s) set forth 
below: 
 
SCHDULE OF THE CHARGES FOR THE BASIC AWARD PERIOD 
Item Description Quantity (Units) Unit Price ($) Total ($) 
    
    
 
6.0 DELIVERY / INSTALLATION 
Delivery shall be within 7-10 business days of purchase order award. All shipping/handling (including 
F.O.B. Destination) and delivery/installation fees shall be included. Upon shipment, the Contractor shall 
email the NCI Technical Point of Contact (TPOC) with a shipping tracking number. Upon delivery, the 
Contractor shall notify the NCI TPOC to schedule the installation date and time. Installation shall occur 
within 7-10 business days of delivery, and shall be performed, or under the direct super vision of, an 
Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) certified technician. Equipment shall be delivered and installed 
to the following address: 
 
 

   
STATEMENT OF NEED (SON) 
 
Page 3 of 3 
 
7.0         CONTRACTING OFFICERS REPRESENTATIVE OR TECHNICAL POINT OF CONTACT  
 
 
All work delivered to the Contracting Officers Representative (COR) or Technical Point of Contact 
(TPOC) will be deemed to have been accepted upon written confirmation of acceptance by the 
COR/TPOC. The COR/TPOC’s approval or revision to the work delivered shall be within the general 
scope of work for the Purchase Order.  
 
Performance of work under this Purchase Order must be subject to the technical direction of the 
COR/TPOC identified above. The term "technical direction" includes direction to the Contractor that fills 
in details and otherwise serves to ensure that tasks outlined in this requirements document are 
accomplished satisfactorily. Technical direction must be within the scope of this requirements document.  
 
The COR/TPOC does not have authority to issue technical direction that: 
a. Constitutes a change of assignment or additional work outside of this requirements document 
b. Constitutes a change as defined in the clause 52.212-4 (c) governing "Changes"; 
c. In any manner causes an increase or decrease in the contract price, or the time required for 
contract performance; 
d. Changes to any of the terms, conditions, or requirements of the contract; 
e. Interferes with the Contractor's right to perform under the terms and conditions of the contract; or 
f. Directs, supervises, or otherwise controls the actions of the Contractor's employees. 
 
Technical direction may be oral or in writing. The COR/TPOC shall confirm oral direction in writing 
within five business days, with a copy to the Contracting Officer. The Contractor shall proceed promptly 
with performance resulting from the technical direction issued by the COR/TPOC. If, in the opinion of 
the Contractor, any direction of the COR/TPOC, or their designee, falls within the 
limitations in (b), above, the Contractor shall immediately notify the Contracting Officer no later 
than the beginning of the next Government business day. 
 
Failure of the Contractor and the Contracting Officer to agree that technical direction is within 
the scope of the contract shall be subject to the terms of the clause 52.212-4 (d) titled "Disputes." 
 
 
8.0  WARRANTY 
The Contractor shall warrant all supplies furnished under this award against any defects in design, 
material, or manufacture for a period of at least 12-months from date of installation. The Contractor shall 
also warrant and imply that all items delivered as a result of this order are merchantable and fit for use for 
the particular purpose described in the order in accordance with FAR 52.212-4(o).  
 
If a defect results in lost or decreased performance of supplies or services furnished under this order, the 
Contractor shall cover all parts, materials, labor, and/or travel expenses required to repair or replace the 
supplies at no cost to the Government.  
 
Supplies which are repaired or replaced shall be warranted for the remainder of the initial warranty period 
or for 90-days – whichever is greater.

BRAND NAME JUSTIFICATION 
 
Imaris is the brand name for this requirement. Imaris is required because NIH/CIT/HPC 
currently relies on BITPLANE Imaris software to visualize, segment, and analyze complex 
3D and 4D microscopy datasets that support NIH research activities. This acquisition is a 
renewal of existing licenses and maintenance services, ensuring continued compatibility 
with the current computing environment, uninterrupted access to vendor technical 
support, software updates, security patches, and maintenance. Procuring a diƯerent 
software product would disrupt established research workﬂows, require migration and 
retraining eƯorts, and could negatively impact ongoing scientiﬁc projects. Therefore, 
renewal of the existing Imaris licenses and associated maintenance is necessary to 
maintain continuity of operations and research support.

Title: Notice of Intent to Award Sole Source – Imaris License Renewal 
Agency: Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) 
Operating Division: Assistant Secretary for Financial Resources (ASFR) 
Contracting OƯice: OƯice of Mission Acquisition Solutions (OMAS)

Notice 
The Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), Assistant Secretary for Financial 
Resources (ASFR), OƯice of Mission Acquisition Solutions (OMAS), on behalf of the 
National Institutes of Health (NIH), Center for Information Technology (CIT), intends to 
award a sole-source, ﬁrm-ﬁxed-price contract to:  
• Andor Technology, Inc. 
300 Baker Avenue, Suite 150 
Concord, MA 01742 
for the renewal of annual subscriptions and licenses for the following commercial software 
products: 
• BPI-Maintenance Inﬁnity-152390 Maintenance on Imaris 11.0 for Core Facilities (CF) 
and 152392 Maintenance on Imaris 11.0 for Neuroscientists (FL) 
The anticipated contract will consist of a one-year base period from 08/01/2026 through 
07/31/2027. 
This acquisition is being conducted using the authority of FAR 13.106-1(b), Soliciting from a 
Single Source, under the procedures of FAR Part 13. 
Description of Requirement 
NIH/CIT/HPC currently utilizes Bitplane’s Imaris software application to provides NIH 
researchers necessary functionality for visualization, segmentation and interpretation of 
3D and 4D microscopy datasets. The existing software licenses and associated 
maintenance/support services are due to expire on 1 August 2026. This procurement is 
required to maintain uninterrupted access to the software, vendor support, security 
updates, patches, and maintenance services necessary for ongoing operations. 

The contractor shall provide renewal of existing software licenses, maintenance, and 
technical support for the products identiﬁed in this SOW. 
The renewal shall include: 
• Continued software usage rights  
• Vendor-provided maintenance  
• Security patches and updates  
• Technical support  
• Access to software upgrades/releases (if applicable)  
No new software development or customization is required under this eƯort unless 
speciﬁcally identiﬁed herein. 
Sole-Source Rationale 
Market research has determined that Imaris software is proprietary to Andor Technology, 
Inc. and is not available through NIH enterprise software programs, or other Government-
wide acquisition mechanisms. Andor Technology is the sole provider of Imaris products 
and maintenance services and does not authorize third parties to provide this support. 
Existing licenses, updates, maintenance, and technical support are proprietary to Andor 
Technology. 
Responses to this Notice 
This notice is not a request for competitive quotations or proposals. It is a notice of the 
Government's intent to award a sole-source contract. 
Interested parties may submit a capability statement demonstrating their ability to satisfy 
the Government's requirement. Capability statements must clearly demonstrate the 
vendor's ability to provide the required products and services described above, or an 
equivalent capability that fully satisﬁes the Government's minimum requirements without 
disruption to ongoing operations. 
Capability statements shall be submitted electronically by the response date in this notice. 
Responses shall be submitted via email to the Contract Specialist: 
Matthew Fein, matthew.fein@hhs.gov 
The Government will review all timely responses received solely for the purpose of 
determining whether another responsible source is capable of meeting the Government's 

requirement. Responses that do not suƯiciently demonstrate the capability to satisfy the 
Government's requirements may not be considered. 
If no aƯirmative responses are received that demonstrate the capability to meet the 
Government's requirements, HHS intends to proceed with award to Andor Technology, Inc 
without further notice.

FAR Part 11—Describing Agency Needs 
 
PURCHASE DESCRIPTION 
 
 
1. Statement of Need and Purpose: 
Our group studies how the thalamus influences the cortical network's contribution to 
cognition. To assess the role of specific cortical regions in different forms of cognition as 
part of a network, we need to acquire a variety of recording equipment to selectively 
record from these regions using chronic neural probes. Our experimental approach 
relies heavily on this equipment. Animals will undergo behavioral testing in their home 
environment while their brain activity is simultaneously recorded. 
Using multiple recording channels across various cortical regions will enable us to 
analyze the relationship between neural activity and behavioral performance. The design 
of these probes — small size, light weight, and wireless interface — will enable us to 
precisely identify the processing of behavior-related information in the recorded cortical 
area and assess its integration within the cortical network. Our ability to modify the 
animal's condition using MRI-guided injections targeting the thalamus, in conjunction 
with electrophysiological recordings in behaving monkeys, is crucial for understanding 
any causal link. 
This will be the first time this concept has been employed in marmosets because we will 
use it with freely moving animals in their home environment to capture more natural 
behavioral signatures. Combining electrophysiology and behavior in marmosets will 
significantly help us understand the role of specific brain nuclei in neurodevelopmental 
and neuropsychiatric disorders. 
 
2. Background Information and Objective: 
At the Section on Cellular and Cognitive Neurodevelopment (SCCN), we explore the role 
of thalamocortical circuits in psychiatric disorders using a comprehensive "cell-to-
system" approach. Our research focuses on the neurodevelopmental connections 
between cognition, brain activity, and cellular circuits. Given the complexity of modeling 
such systems, we employ diverse techniques. Previous studies in our non-human 
primate (NHP) model have revealed that early-life disruptions to cellular circuits can lead 
to long-term behavioral changes and associated physiological alterations. Our current 
objectives are twofold: (i) to deepen our understanding of the consequences of early 
neurodevelopmental perturbations and (ii) to refine our knowledge of the underlying 
mechanisms. To achieve this, we aim to leverage more advanced technologies to 
enhance our research's precision and quality. By integrating these innovations with our 
existing methodologies, we strive to advance our understanding of neurodevelopmental 
processes and their implications for psychiatric disorders. 
 
 

Version 11-30-2016-1 
FAR Part 11—Describing Agency Needs 
 
3. Generic Name of Product: 
Home-cage electrophysiology recording equipment 
 
4. Purchase Description: 
Home-cage electrophysiology recording equipment from Spike Gadgets 
 
5. Salient characteristics 
Hardware: 
The Spike Gadgets wireless headstage interface is an ultralightweight, fully featured 
neural datalogger designed to record from neural probes for experiments with our 
primate model (i.e. marmoset monkey). The system is using radio frequency 
communication with the different components of the central unit, supporting pairing of 
several headstages simultaneously. The system is also equipped with on-board 
gyroscope and accelerometer sensors for motion tracking and is chargeable via any 5V 
USB port. 
The system contains the following items: 
• Eight Sprite32 Bundle (full-data rate broadband neural data logging to micro 
SD, 3.8 grams, integrated battery, with low-power standby mode, battery and 
status monitoring over radio, 32 channels of neural data, accelerometer and 
gyroscope) 
• Logger Dock 2 Bundle (connect and record from multiple Sprite32 
headstages simultaneously, features 3 digital inputs and 1 analog input, 
charge and update the Sprite32 via built-in USB) 
• Main Control Unit Bundle (supports low-latency data streaming via gigabit 
ethernet for tethered recording, wirelessly control neural recording 
experiments with SpikeGadgets data-logging headstages, integration with 
SpikeGadgets other units to sync, control and record environmental stimuli, 
mounting kit necessary) 
Other items are necessary for interfacing and synchronizing the probes with the system 
for recovering the data: 
• General Purpose Commutator Bundle 
• Headstage Signal Converter 
• Mini-Mouse Headstage 32-Channels Bundle 
• Data Logging Bundle 
• Cambridge Molex64 128ch Adapter 
• Lynx Adaptor 
 
6. Quantity: 
One set

7. Delivery Date: Within 30-60 days after the award of the contract. 
Deliver to: 
Dr. James Bourne 
49 Convent Dr. Room 3A35 
Bethesda, MD 20892 
 
8. Period of Performance: 
The recording equipment is fully warrantied for two years. Equipment is expected to be 
fully functional for greater than five years with minor service, as required. 
 
9. Option(s): 
N/A
