PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT (PWS) 
FOR USE OF Cloud-Based Software for the Lab 
 
 
1. GENERAL: The Department of Pathology and Area Laboratory Services is requesting a 
site license for cloud-based software in line with FedRAMP moderate authorization for up to 
150 users across ten (10) clinical sites  to be used at Dwight D. Eisenhower Army Medical 
Center (DDEAMC), Fort Eisenhower, GA. 
 
1.2 Background: Cloud-based software manages for clinical laboratories, document control, 
inspection readiness, compliance education, laboratory personnel documentation and Continuing 
Education (CE) requirements. 
 
1.3 Objectives: The procurement of cloud-based software will enhance and sustain the 
Department of Pathology’s inspection readiness, compliance education and document control 
requirements. Overall, this software enables the department to organize and facilitate our 
accreditation with The Joint Commission, the College of American Pathologists and the 
Association for the Advancement of Blood and Biotherapies. 
 
1.4 Period of Performance: This contract entails a 5-year software subscription starting from 
the date of execution of the license. This contract will include one base year and four Option 
Years (OYs).  
 
Base Year: 21 August 2026 through 20 August 2027 
Option Year One (1): 21 August 2027 through 20 August 2028 
Option Year Two (2): 21 August 2028 through 20 August 2029 
Option Year Three (3): 21 August 2029 through 20 August 2030 
Option Year Four (4): 21 August 2030 through 20 August 2031 
     
1.5 Quality Control: The contractor shall develop and maintain an effective quality control 
program (QCP) to ensure services are performed in accordance with this PWS.  The contractor 
shall develop and implement procedures to identify, prevent, and ensure non-recurrence of 
defective services.  The contractor’s quality control program is how they assure that work 
complies with the requirement of the contract. The QCP is to be delivered within 30 days after 
the contract has been awarded. After acceptance of the quality control plan the contractor shall 
receive the contracting officer’s acceptance in writing of any proposed change to his QC system.   
 
1.6 Quality Assurance: The government shall evaluate the contractor’s performance under this 
contract in accordance with the Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan.  This plan is primarily 
focused on what the Government must do to ensure that the contractor has performed in 
accordance with the performance standards.  It defines how the performance standards will be 
applied, the frequency of surveillance, and the minimum acceptable defect rate(s).   
 
According to the Inspection of Services clause, the U.S. Government will evaluate the 
contractor's performance under this contract.  For those tasks listed on the performance 
requirements summary (PRS), the contracting officer’s representative (COR) or evaluators will 

 
Page 2 of 9 
 
 
follow the methods of surveillance specified in this contract.  U.S. Government personnel will 
record all surveillance observations.  The initialing of the observation does not necessarily 
constitute concurrence with the observation, only acknowledgment that he or she has been made 
aware of the defective performance.  U.S. Government surveillance of tasks not listed in the PRS 
or by methods other than those listed in the PRS (such as provided for by the Inspection of 
Services clause) may occur during the performance period of this contract.  Such surveillance 
will be done according to standard inspection procedures or other contract provisions.  Any 
action taken by the contracting officer because of surveillance will be according to the terms of 
this contract. 
 
1.6.1 Performance Evaluation Meetings :  The contracting officer may require the contract 
manager to meet with the contracting officer, contract administrator, COR, and other U.S. 
Government personnel as deemed necessary.  The contractor may request a meeting with the 
contracting officer when he or she believes such a meeting is necessary.  Written minutes of any 
such meetings shall be recorded in the contract and signed by the contract manager and the 
contracting officer or contract administrator.  If the contractor does not concur with any portion of 
the minutes, such nonoccurrence shall be provided in writing to the contracting officer within 10 
calendar days following receipt of the minutes. 
 
1.7 Records: The contractor shall be responsible for creating, maintaining, and disposing of only 
those U.S. Government required records.  For the purposes of this contract, required records 
include documentation management, incident and event management, competency ass essment, 
personnel documentation, continuing education, and analytics and performance management.  If 
requested by the U.S. Government, the contractor shall provide the original record or a 
reproducible copy of any such record within 5 working days of receipt of the request. A copy of 
all maintenance and validation records will be left by the technician in a folder by the analyzer. 
 
1.8 HOURS OF OPERATION: 
 
1.8.1 Normal Hours of Operation:  The contractor shall perform the services required under this 
contract during the following hours:  Monday through Friday between the hours of 0730 – 1630 
EST except Federal holidays or when the Government facility is closed due to local or national 
emergencies, administrative closings, or similar Government directed facility closings. 
 
1.8.2 The contractor shall provide direct customer service and support during normal business 
hours. 
 
1.8.3 Recognized Holidays:     
Services shall not be required on Federal holidays or the day of observance of federally 
established holidays and local base holidays. In general, federal holidays falling on a Saturday 
are observed on the preceding Friday whereas holidays falling on a Sunday are observed on the 
following Monday.  Additional federal holidays as authorized by the President of the United 
States and/or executive orders shall be considered part of standard Federal Government holidays.   
 
• Government Escort. If no Government employee is unavailable to provide 
required escort services during routine maintenance or system outages, the 

 
Page 3 of 9 
 
 
COR shall assume escort responsibilities or provide alternate escort 
arrangements.  The Contractor shall not remain on site without a required 
escort and shall follow all instructions issued by the KO or COR.  
 
• In the event of a Government shutdown, the Contractor shall contact the COR 
to receive guidance. The Contracting Officer may issue a Stop-Work Order in 
accordance with FAR 52.242-15 if services under this contract are deemed 
non-essential. 
1.9 Place of Performance: The work to be performed under this contract will be performed at: 
                                        Dwight D. Eisenhower Army Medical Center (DDEAMC)  
                                         Building 300 East Hospital Road 
                          Fort Gordon, GA 30805-5650 
 
2. CONSERVATION OF UTILITIES: N/A 
 
3. CONTRACTOR PERSONNEL: 
 
3.1 Contract Manager. The contractor shall provide a contract manager who shall be responsible 
for the performance of the work.  The name of this person, and an alternate or alternates, who shall 
act for the contractor when the manager is absent, shall be designated in writing to the contracting 
officer. 
 
3.2 The contract manager or alternate shall have full authority to act for the contractor on all 
contract matters relating to daily operation of this contract. 
 
3.3 The contract manager or alternate shall be available during normal duty hours (0730 -1630 
Eastern Standard Time Zone (EST)) within 24hrs to meet on the installation with U.S. Government 
personnel (designated by the contracting officer) to discuss problem areas.  After normal duty 
hours, the manager or alternate shall be available within 48 hours. 
 
3.4 Contractor Employees.  The contractor shall not employ persons for work on this contract if 
such employee is identified to the contractor by the contracting officer as a potential threat to the 
health, safety, security, general well -being or operational m ission of the installations and their 
population. 
 
3.5 Contractor personnel shall present a neat, business -like appearance and be easily recognized 
as contractor employees.  Contractor personnel shall either wear a distinguishable uniform or 
badge on the exterior of their clothing while performing any service  at any U.S. Government 
facility.    
 
3.6 The contractor shall not employ any person who is an employee of the U.S. Government if 
employing that person would create a conflict of interest.  Additionally, the contractor shall not 
employ any person who is an employee of the Department of Defense, e ither military or civilian, 
unless such person seeks and receives approval according to DOD 5500.7R, “Joint Ethics 
Regulation”.  The contractor shall not employ any person who is an employee of the Department 
of Defense if such employment would be contrary to local policies. 

 
Page 4 of 9 
 
 
 
3.7 The contractor is cautioned that off -duty active military personnel hired under this contract 
may be subject to permanent change of station, change in duty hours, or deployment.  Military 
Reservists and National Guard members may be subject to recall to active duty. The abrupt absence 
of these personnel could adversely affect the contractor's ability to perform; however, their absence 
at any time shall not constitute an excuse for nonperformance under this contract. 
 
4. SECURITY REQUIREMENTS:  
 
4.1 Access and General Protection/Security and Procedures :  This standard language text is for 
contractor employees with an area of performance within an Army controlled installation, facility 
or area.  Contractor and all associated sub -contractors’ employees shall comply with applicable 
installation, facility and area commander installation/facility access and local security policies and 
procedures (provided by government representative).  The contractor shall also provide all 
information required f or backgrou nd checks to meet installation access requirements to be 
accomplished by installation Provost Marshal Office, Director of Emergency Services or Security 
Office.  Contractor workforce must comply with all personal identity verification requirements 
directed by DOD, HQDA and/or local policy.  In addition to the changes otherwise authorized by 
the changes clause of this contract, should the Force Protection Condition (FPCON) at any 
individual facility or installation change, the Government may require changes in contractor 
security matters or processes.   
 
Contractor personnel performing work under this contract must have regulatory requirements as 
defined by NIST SP 800 -53, Control PS -3 (Personnel Screening).  For a Moderate baseline, 
personnel must undergo background checks and suitability screening (typically a Tier 1 or Tier 2 
investigation, leading to a Public Trust position). 
 
4.2 Contractor Employees Who Require Access to Government Information Systems .  All 
contractor employees with access to a government info system must be registered in the ATCTS 
(Army Training Certification Tracking System) at commencement of services and  must 
successfully complete the DOD Information Assurance Awareness prior to access to the 
information systems and then annually thereafter. 
 
4.3 Physical Security:  The contractor shall be responsible for safeguarding all U.S. Government 
property provided for contractor use or access. 
 
4.4 Contracting Officer Representative (COR): The (COR) will be identified by separate letter.  
The COR monitors all technical aspects of the contract and assists in contract administration. 
The COR is authorized to perform the following functions: assure that the Contractor performs 
the technical requirements of the contract: perform inspections necessary in connection with 
contract performance: maintain written and oral communications with the Contractor concerning 
technical aspects of the contract: issue written interpretations of technical requirements, 
including Government drawings, designs, specifications: monitor Contractor's performance and 
notifies both the Contracting Officer and Contractor of any deficiencies; coordinate availability 
of government furnished property, and provide site entry of Contractor personnel.  A letter of 
designation issued to the COR, a copy of which is sent to the Contractor, states the 

 
Page 5 of 9 
 
 
responsibilities and limitations of the COR, especially regarding changes in cost or price, 
estimates or changes in delivery dates.  The COR is not authorized to change any of the terms 
and conditions of the resulting order.  
 
4.6  Organizational Conflict of Interest:  Contractor and subcontractor personnel performing 
work under this contract may receive, have access to or participate in the development of 
proprietary or source selection information (e.g., cost or pricing information, budget information 
or analyses, specifications or work statements, etc.) or perform evaluation services which may 
create a current or subsequent Organizational Conflict of Interests (OCI) as defined in FAR 
Subpart 9.5.  The Contractor shall notify the Contracting Officer immediately whenever it 
becomes aware that such access or participation may result in any actual or potential OCI and 
shall promptly submit a plan to the Contracting Officer to avoid or mitigate any such OCI.  The 
Contractor’s mitigation plan will be determined to be acceptable solely at the discretion of the 
Contracting Officer and in the event the Contracting Officer unilaterally determines that any 
such OCI cannot be satisfactorily avoided or mitigated, the Contracting Officer may affect other 
remedies as he or she deems necessary, including prohibiting the Contractor from participation in 
subsequent contracted requirements which may be affected by the OCI.  
 
5.  DEFINITIONS/ACRONYMS: 
 
5.1 DEFINITIONS.  Following is a list of basic definitions.   
 
5.2 CONTRACTING OFFICER: A person with the authority to enter, administer, and/  or 
terminate contracts and make related determinations and findings. 
 
5.3 CONTRACTING OFFICER'S REPRESENTATIVE (COR):  A U.S. Government employee 
selected and designated in writing by the Contracting Officer to act as his/her designated 
representative in administering a contract. 
  
5.4 QUALITY ASSESSMENT AND IMPROVEMENT.  Those actions taken by the U.S. 
Government to check services to determine if they meet the requirements of the CLIA/DoD CLIP 
’88 & ’03, CAP, JCAHO, U.S. Army Medical Command, quality assurance and risk management 
program and ensure compliance with the terms and conditions of the contract

# Solicitation Reference Section/Exhibit Question Answer
1 Evaluation Factor 1 Section L, Factor 1 requires the offeror or its subcontractor/teaming partner to be licensed and incorporated to do business in Mexico. Please confirm this requirement is met 
when a named Mexican-incorporated subcontractor or teaming partner holds that status, rather than the prime offeror itself. Yes; That is acceptable as the arrangement is consistent with Mexican law.
2 SICAS integration (SOW 4.6; Attachment 2, 
Item 015). 
The brand-name justification confirms SICAS uses a web-services API with Google Meet integration. Will the Government provide the SICAS API documentation, credentials, and a 
non-production test environment to the awardee to perform the integration? And is SICAS a single uniform system across the candidate states, or does each state judiciary run a 
different version?
Yes, the required API documentation will be provided to the selected vendor upon contract award. SICAS is a 
uniform system; however, the management model is handled individually on a state-by-state basis.
3 Attachment A, Item 005
Does "150 MB dedicated" require a clear-channel circuit with a committed information rate, or is a business-grade symmetric service acceptable?
The requirement should be understood as a guaranteed bandwidth capacity for the service, preferably 
expressed as dedicated symmetric 150 Mbps, with enterprise-grade quality conditions. A "clear-channel" or 
point-to-point circuit is not strictly required; a business-grade symmetric service is acceptable, provided the 
carrier guarantees a committed information rate (CIR), link stability, low latency, low jitter, minimal packet 
loss, and service levels through a Service Level Agreement (SLA).
4 Attachment A, Item 005 For remote penitentiary sites without terrestrial fiber, is satellite service (for example, Starlink Bus iness/Priority) acceptable to meet this requirement? The acceptability of satellite service will depend on the outcomes of the working group sessions, which will 
determine the specific penitentiary facilities where the system is to be installed.
5 Attachment A, Item 005 Given the sensitivity of the judicial data, does the Government require in-country or terrestrial data r outing, or is satellite routing acceptable? The data routing requirements will depend on the outcomes of the working group sessions, which will 
determine the specific penitentiary facilities where the system is to be installed.
6 Place of Performance Place of performance. Which states does the Government anticipate for the base year, and roughly how many penitentiary and courtroom sites per state should offerors plan to 
equip and connect?
The selected contractor will be informed of the two specific states for the base year upon contract award. 
The number of penitentiary facilities per state may vary, however will not exceed five (5) per state.  Each 
state will only have one judiciary site. The total equipment per state will not exceed the equipment specified 
on Attachment A.
7 Attachment 6 Secure Software Development Attestation (Attachment 6). Should the attestation come from the software producer (e.g., Google, Microsoft), or from the offeror as the 
integrator/reseller of those commercial products?
The form should be filled out by the software producer per the form instructions:
"Software Producer Information
Please provide a description of the software and information about the software producer. All fields in the 
attestation form are required to be appropriately completed by the software producer. Incomplete forms will 
not be accepted.
The form must be signed by the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of the software producer or their designee, who 
must be an employee of the software producer and have the authority to bind the corporation. "
8 SOW 8.2.1.1
Equipment consolidation and inspection location. SOW 8.2.1.1 specifies a contractor warehouse in Mexico City for initial inventory and inspection. Since the place of performance 
is the northern border states, may the contractor consolidate and stage equipment closer to the awarded sites (for example, in Sonora), with the Government's physical 
inspection and Receiving Report conducted there rather than in Mexico City?
For security and logistical reasons, and to facilitate physical inventory inspections by INL, equipment 
consolidation and inventory must be conducted in Mexico City (CDMX). 
9 Teaming, Set-Aside Structure & Eligibility To satisfy the Factor 1 threshold (“licensed and incorporated to do business in Mexico”), does the Government confirm that this requirement may be met by the prime’s Mexican-
incorporated subcontractor or teaming partner, rather than by the prime offeror itself? Yes, see Answer #1.
10 Teaming, Set-Aside Structure & Eligibility Under FAR 52.219-14 (Limitations on Subcontracting), what percentage of the contract amount must be performed by the prime and similarly situated entities, and how will the 
Government treat work performed by Mexican subcontractors in that calculation?
Contractors should apply the clause as they would for any other procurement conducted in the U.S. Mexican 
subcontractors could be considered a U.S. small businesses if they qualify as such based on the SBA 
government contracting size rules.
11 Teaming, Set-Aside Structure & Eligibility Will a Mexican-incorporated subcontractor be treated as a “similarly situated entit y” for purposes of the limitations-on-subcontracting analysis? No special adjustments to the application of the clause will be m ade.  See question and answer 10.
12 Teaming, Set-Aside Structure & Eligibility Are formal teaming arrangements or SBA-approved joint ventures permitted for this r equirement, and is either structure preferred by the Government? The government has no preference as long as the offeror complies with small business set-aside 
requirements.
13 Teaming, Set-Aside Structure & Eligibility Must all proposed subcontractors hold an active SAM.gov registration at the time of  quote submission, or only at the time of award? As this is a small business set aside, at a minimum the prime contractor must be registered in SAM as a small 
business under the correct NAICS code at the time the quote is submitted.  
14 Technical Capacity & Scope Can the Government confirm the exact number of courts and penitentiary facilities to be equipped per state, and identify which two states constitute the base year versus the 
option year?
The places of performance will be in border states as described in the SOW; the selected contractor will be 
informed of the 2 specific base year states upon contract award. The number of penitentiary facilities per 
state may vary, but will not exceed five per state.  Only one judiciary site is required per state.  Regardless of 
the number of total sites per state, equipment in excess of what is specified on Attachment A is not required.
15 Technical Capacity & Scope Will the Government provide a baseline inventory of existing network, endpoint, and audiovisual inf rastructure at each site, or arrange pre-award or post-award site surveys?
As specified in Attachment 1 (SOW), the selected contractor shall conduct initial workshop sessions with the 
designated Government of Mexico (GOM) partners at each project location following contract award. These 
sessions will ensure that all sites provide the necessary support and infrastructure for successful project 
implementation.
16 Technical Capacity & Scope For the dedicated 150 MB communication links, is the contractor responsible for procuring and maintaining these from Mexican carriers, and are the recurring monthly costs to 
be borne by the contractor throughout the period of performance?
Yes, the contractor is responsible for procuring and maintaining the dedicated 150 Mbps communication 
links through carriers operating in Mexico. The recurring costs associated with these links shall be covered by 
the contractor for the entire period of performance on a per-state basis.
17 Technical Capacity & Scope For the brand-name items (Microsoft Office, Google Workspace Enterprise, Google Cloud), must the contractor procure the licenses, and should they be provisioned under a 
Government of Mexico tenant or under the contractor’s tenant? Please confirm the required number of seats.
Yes, the contractor is responsible for procuring all brand-name licenses (Microsoft Office, Google Workspace 
Enterprise, and Google Cloud). All licenses shall be provisioned under a Government of Mexico tenant. The 
required number of seats for each license is specified in Attachment A.
18 Technical Capacity & Scope Does the Government require that recorded hearings and associated data reside within Mexico (data r esidency), or is a U.S. or global Google Cloud region acceptable? All recorded hearings and associated data shall reside within Mexican territory. A U.S. or global Google Cloud 
region is not acceptable for this requirement.
19 Technical Capacity & Scope Will the Government of Mexico provide SICAS API documentation, a test environment, and a technical point of contact to enable the required scheduling and video-delivery 
integration?

PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT (PWS) 

Workflow Data Extraction Service

1. General: This is a non-personal services contract to provide data extraction services. The Government shall not exercise any supervision or control over the contract service providers performing the services herein.  Such contract service providers shall be accountable solely to the Contractor who, in turn is responsible to the Government. 

1.1 Description of Services/Introduction: The Contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and other items and non-personal services necessary to perform data extraction services as defined in this Performance Work Statement (PWS), section 5 except for those items specified as government furnished property and services. The Contractor shall perform to the standards in this contract.

1.2 Background: The United States Criminal Investigation Laboratory (USACIL) requires secure extraction of historical and active data, broken into its constituent parts, and exported into a standardized format compatible with a new QMS application.

1.3 Objectives:  

Analysis: Review of our existing workflow data structures and attachments to map out an extraction strategy.

Tool Development: Creation of the script or tool designed specifically to break out and extract the workflow data.

Data Formatting: Parsing and formatting the extracted data for direct ingestion into the new QMS.

Testing & Support: Sample test runs for data validation, plus a designated number of support hours for the actual import process.

Deliverables: The final extraction tool/scripts, technical documentation, and a comprehensive breakdown of estimated billable hours, rates, and total costs.

Provide additional technical specifications you will need from our team regarding the target QMS (such as preferred target data formats like CSV, XML, JSON, or specific data volume estimates).

1.4 Scope: The contractor will provide service and support for a period of one (1) year (12 months) to ensure all data has successfully been removed from their database and ingested into the new database. 

Period of Performance: The period of performance shall be for one (1) base year of 12 months and 2 (two) option years. The period of performance reads as follows:

Base Year			15AUG2026 – 14AUG2027 

1.6 General Information

1.6.1 Federal Observed Holidays: The contractor is not required to work on the following days:  

New Year’s Day					Labor Day

Martin Luther King Jr.’s Birthday			Columbus Day

President’s Day					Veteran’s Day

Memorial Day						Thanksgiving Day

Independence Day					Christmas Day

Juneteenth

1.6.2 Hours of Operation: The Contractor is responsible for conducting business, between the hours of 0800 – 1600 Monday through Friday except Federal holidays or when the Government facility is closed due to local or national emergencies, administrative closings, or similar Government directed facility closings.  The Contractor must at all times maintain an adequate workforce for the uninterrupted performance of all tasks defined within this PWS when the Government facility is not closed for the above reasons.

1.6.3 Place of Performance: The work to be performed under this contract will be performed at the location of the vendor.

1.6.4 Quality Assurance:  The contractor shall comply with the government’s quality assurance program as defined in the Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan. It defines how the performance standards will be applied, the frequency of surveillance, and the minimum acceptable quality level(s) (AQL).  Government surveillance of contractor performance is not limited to the Performance Objectives as outlined in this PWS.  The Government reserves the right to conduct compliance surveillance of any contractual requirement of this acquisition. 

1.6.5 Type of Contract:  The Government will award a Fixed-Price Service contract.

1.6.7 Security Requirements: Contractor personnel performing work under this contract must have personal security clearance at time of the contract start date and must maintain the level of security required for the life of the contract.  

1.6.7.1 Physical Security: The Contractor shall safeguard all government equipment, information and property provided for Contractor use.  Contractor shall maintain a physical security checklist/log which will be forwarded to the COR on a monthly or quarterly basis.  

1.6.7.2 Key Control: NA.

1.6.8 Special Qualifications: Qualifications should be consistent with the vendors’ requirement(s).

1.6.9 Post Award Conference/Periodic Progress Meetings: The Contractor agrees to attend any post award conference convened by the contracting activity or contract administration office in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Subpart 42.5. The KO and Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR) shall meet periodically with the contractor to review the contractor's performance.  At these meetings the KO will apprise the Contractor of how the Government views the contractor's performance and the contractor will apprise the Government of problems, if any, being experienced.  Appropriate action shall be taken to resolve outstanding issues. 

1.6.10 Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR): The COR Management System Tool (Virtual Contracting Enterprise (VCE)-Acquisition Resource Center (ARC) https://arc.army.mil/COR) for nomination, tracking, documentation, and management of CORs will be used. The COR will be identified by separate letter.  The COR monitors all technical aspects of the contract and assists in contract administration The COR is authorized to perform the following functions: Assure that the Contractor performs the technical requirements of the contract; perform inspections necessary in connection with contract performance; maintain written and oral communications with the Contractor concerning technical aspects of the contract; issue written interpretations of technical requirements, including Government drawings, designs, and specifications; monitor Contractor's performance and notifies both the  KO and Contractor of any deficiencies; coordinate availability of government furnished property, and provide site entry of Contractor personnel.  A letter of designation issued to the COR, a copy of which is sent to the Contractor, states the responsibilities and limitations of the COR, especially with regard to changes in cost or price, estimates or changes in delivery dates.  The COR is not authorized to change any of the terms and conditions of the resulting order.

The name of this person and an alternate who shall act for the contractor when the manager is absent shall be designated in writing to the contracting officer.  The contract manager or alternate shall have full authority to act for the Contractor on all contract matters relating to daily operation of this contract.  The contract manager or alternate shall be available between 0800 – 1600, Monday through Friday except Federal holidays or when the Government facility is closed for administrative reasons.

PART 2

DEFINITIONS, ACRONYMS, AND ABBREVIATIONS

2. Definitions and Acronyms:

2.1 Definitions: 

2.1.1 Cannibalize.  Remove parts from Government property for use or for installation on other Government property. 

2.1.2 Contractor.  A supplier or vendor awarded a contract to provide specific supplies or service to the government.  The term used in this contract refers to the prime. 

2.1.3 Contractor Acquired Property.  Property acquired, fabricated, or otherwise provided by the contractor for performing a contract and to which the Government has title.

2.1.4 Contracting Officer (KO).  A person with authority to enter into, administer, or terminate contracts, and make related determinations and findings on behalf of the government.  Note: The only individual who can legally bind the government.

Equipment is not intended for sale and does not ordinarily lose its identity or become a component part of another article when put into use. Equipment does not include material, real property, special test equipment or special tooling. 

2.1.9 Government Furnished Property.  Property in the possession of, or directly acquired by, the Government and subsequently furnished to the contractor for performance of a contract. Government-furnished property includes, but is not limited to, spares and property furnished for repair, maintenance, overhaul, or modification. Government-furnished property also includes contractor-acquired property if the contractor-acquired property is deliverable under a cost contract when accepted by the Government for continued use under the contract.

2.1.10 Government Property.  All property owned or leased by the Government. Government property includes both Government-furnished property and contractor-acquired property. Government property includes material, equipment, special tooling, special test equipment, and real property. Government property does not include intellectual property and software.

2.1.11. Key Personnel.  Contractor personnel that are evaluated in a source selection process and that may be required to be used in the performance of a contract by the Key Personnel listed in the PWS. PRE-SOLICITATION NOTICE 
IT Global Operation Support Services (DOWEA) 
DOWEA-ITGOSS-PS-2601 
 
The Department of War Education Activity (DoWEA) will solicit proposals for the provision of 
comprehensive IT Global Operation Support Services to support its global educational 
mission. DoWEA will operate approximately 160 schools worldwide, serving more than 69,000 
students and supporting over 11,800 employees across the United States, Puerto Rico, Guam, 
Europe, and the Pacific. 
This acquisition is anticipated to be a Small Business Set-Aside and will result in the award of a 
competitive Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contract. The contract will 
support enterprise-wide IT operations and modernization initiatives through the issuance of task 
orders.  
The anticipated period of performance is a multi-year ordering period consisting of one (1) 12-
month base period with nine (9) 12-month option periods. 
 
Primary NAICS 541519, Other Computer Related Services (Size Standard: $34 Million).  
The scope of work includes providing integrated support for: 
• Security Operations Center (SOC) services, including 24x7 cybersecurity monitoring, 
incident response, threat hunting, and vulnerability management.  
• DevSecOps and cloud-native application development services, including software 
development lifecycle management, secure coding, testing, deployment, and sustainment.  
• Enterprise Device Management, including Microsoft Intune, Apple School Manager, 
ChromeOS, mobile devices, and IoT device administration.  
• Enterprise Network Operations Center (NOC) support for SD-WAN, LAN, wireless, 
firewall, and cloud networking environments.  
• Cloud Operations (CloudOps) support for Microsoft Azure and Google Workspace 
environments.  
• Agile Project Management services to support planning, execution, coordination, 
reporting, and continuous improvement activities.  
• Business Case and Requirements Analysis services, including stakeholder engagement, 
requirements development, requirements traceability, and governance support.  
• Technical Writing services supporting policies, procedures, system documentation, 
operational guides, architecture diagrams, and other technical deliverables.  

Contractor performance shall comply with applicable Department of Defense (DoD), NIST, 
RMF, Zero Trust, DISA STIG, Section 508 Accessibility, cybersecurity, and information 
assurance requirements. Contractor personnel may be required to obtain appropriate background 
investigations, CAC eligibility, and security clearances as determined by the Government.  
The solicitation will be posted on SAM.gov, and all responsible small business concerns are 
encouraged to participate. Interested vendors should monitor SAM.gov for the official 
solicitation release and any subsequent amendments.

This notice is issued solely for informational purposes and does not obligate the Government to 
issue a solicitation or award a contract. The Government will not reimburse respondents for any 
costs incurred in connection with this notice. The Government reserves the right to revise, 
amend, or cancel information contained herein at any time.

U.S. COURTS INTEGRATED LIBRARY SYSTEM 
REQUIREMENTS  
Statement of Work 
 
Table of Contents 
Background: ............................................................................................................................................................................ 2 
Definitions: .............................................................................................................................................................................. 2 
Scope: ...................................................................................................................................................................................... 2 
Network Monitoring ........................................................................................................................................................... 4 
Software Modules ............................................................................................................................................................... 4 
Bibliographic: ...................................................................................................................................................................... 4 
Ingesting Procurement Data: .............................................................................................................................................. 5 
Documentation ................................................................................................................................................................... 5

Custom Programming ......................................................................................................................................................... 5 
Optional Functionality during the contract Period that requires pricing: .............................................................................. 6 
Option 1: Option to include the Federal Judicial Center (FJC) ............................................................................................ 6 
Option 2: Option to include the United States Sentencing Commission (USSC) ................................................................ 6 
Attachment A: Instances and Modules per Instance .............................................................................................................. 7 
Attachment B: Custom Reports .............................................................................................................................................. 9 
 
  

 
2 
 
Background: 
The Federal Court Library System (the Libraries) has for the past thirty years used an Integrated Library System (ILS) to 
manage the purchase of legal research materials for all chambers and libraries, as well as to maintain the library catalogs 
of all of the Circuit and Branch libraries.  The ILS is of critical importance to both the functioning of the Libraries and for 
the maintenance of the chambers legal research collections.  
In order to ensure that the Libraries have a cost effective ILS system that will meet the Libraries needs, the 
Administrative Office of the United States Courts (the AO) requires a consortia model ILS, including maintenance and 
services, for the Administrative Office, twelve court libraries nationwide, and a test environment. 
The Court Libraries also require a web-based discovery platform that integrates all of the resources of the component 
libraries (See attachment A), allowing them to be searched individually or in aggregate. 
Definitions: 
 Consignee: Class of institution (e.g. Library, Circuit Judge, District Judge, Clerks, etc.)  
 Public: Public refers to court stakeholders who are not judges within the circuit.  
 General Public: Non-court users of the library 
Scope: 
 
The scope of this contract includes the acquisition of a FedRAMP certified or equivalent Integrated Library 
System. The solution will contain fourteen ILS instances (thirteen production instances; one test instance). The 
AOUSC will have the option to have multiple instances combined into a single instance and others remaining 
separate.  The instances can either have separate bibliographic databases or utilize a shared bibliographic 
database. 
  
Requirements 
1) The Contractor shall provide 99.5% availability between the hours of 7:00 a.m. to 11:00 p.m. Eastern Time, 
Monday through Friday on business days.  Scheduled maintenance is to be provided outside of these hours. 
a. The instances are to be maintained so that each instance remains unique, discrete and separate 
from each other instance (although some instances may share a bibliographic database) and from 
any external instance or system.   
2) The Contractor shall ensure that the ILS software operates fully and successfully in this environment. 
3) The Contractor shall ensure that each ILS instance is able to interface, through secure file transfer, with the 
federal judiciary’s financial system (currently CGI Momentum Enterprise) housed at a separate hosting facility. 
4) The Contractor shall provide one account with shell access for each of the fourteen instances.  Each account’s 
access shall be limited to only that instance. 
5) The contractor shall maintain an IP restricted single search interface for all court libraries’ resources with ability 
to search only a single Court’s resources separately as well, deduplicated as necessary. 
a. Regular, monthly development meetings for refinement and ongoing training 
b. The Contractor shall provide hardware, firmware, and operating system maintenance and upgrades 
as prudent and necessary for technology and security purposes.  
c. Development of harvest methods for external digital products.  Resources may or may not be Open 
Archives Initiative (OAI) enabled. 

 
3 
 
6) The Contractor shall ensure that all fourteen ILS instances listed in Attachment A are used solely by the staff of 
the federal judiciary.  No instance shall be made available to the general public.  
7) Contractor shall provide a solution that can integrate with the AO’s SAML based Single Sign-On capability 
The Solution will provide functionality in the following core areas: 
1) Acquisitions is the primary reason for the ILS.  The courts require the ability to create a standard format 
purchase order document that can contain multiple lines (sourced from the catalog data) and up to 3,000 
consignees (sourced from the circulation/user data).  These orders are then transmitted to the vendor/publisher 
as the official procurement document. Data contained in these documents are then securely transmitted to our 
external financial system. (currently CGI Momentum Enterprise) Upon receipt of the materials, and payment in 
our financial system, the solution will retrieve payment data from the external financial system.  
2) As a majority of our orders are subscriptions/renewals, the courts require a method to perpetually track changes 
to the order quantities, subscribers and contract changes.  We currently use a “Master Order” per title.  
Additionally, the acquisitions module should have the option of “auto-filling” frequently used text in acquisitions 
documents. 
3) Authorities, the System should support separate authority files for personal names, corporate bodies, uniform 
titles, series, subject headings, genres, and geographic names. Batch and single record import and export should 
be supported, with focus on standard records based in Library of Congress systems. 
4) Cataloging, including Online Computer Library Center (OCLC) Integration.  It should be a Unicode, standards-
based system should allow for batch-ingestion of bibliographic records, and the system should also allow for 
original cataloging.  Shall accept brief and full Machine-Readable Cataloging (MARC) records without limit to the 
record or field length plus tags and necessary indexes.  The ILS shall operate in interactive mode with the 
capability to create, update, maintain and access all data for library materials and borrowers in real-time. 
5) Circulation Charge/discharge items. In addition to maintaining information about our users/consignees, the 
circulation module is used by some courts to track materials used (charged).  The materials may or may not be 
individually barcoded, may be only used for a brief period or for an extended period, and may or may not leave 
the library.  The courts require a means to track these materials as they are used.  The system should have the 
ability to record demographic information about users/consignees (district, judge type, co-location with a 
library, judge status etc.). 
6) Serials Administration.  Should allow for sorting issues by date received, and editing of auto-fill data, automated 
prediction of forthcoming issues, and ideally automated printing of spine labels. Should allow ability to check in 
items as received; ability to locate missing issues for claiming; and display latest issue received and MARC 
holdings in bib record 
7) Analytic Reporting.  System allowing for complex analytic reports to be designed by users and run with either 
automated or manual execution. Provide for production of pre-formatted reports, with the option to view and 
print reports, and export data in CSV and pipe delimited format.  Must have capability to generate a formatted 
inventory report with associated costs per title per consignee 
8) System Administration should allow for APIs to interact in elevated ways with standard library resources, and 
with the Judiciary SharePoint website. 
9) Online Public Access (restricted access) Catalog/Discovery Layer, that includes a well-developed Knowledge Base 
of secondary sources. (anonymous authentication).  Each court requires online anonymous access to the publicly 
available titles (i.e., titles not held in judges’ chambers).     
Requests i.e., holds, and purchase requests (Associated with Cataloging and Circulation). The system should 
allow staff to submit requests for transfers and cancellations of subscriptions, and display requests associated 
with a specific consignee 

 
4 
 
10) Material management/Inventory: The courts require the ability to track the movement of materials between 
locations and desire the ability to see the history of any title’s location movements via transfer between 
locations, and interlibrary loans.  Many of our locations are not subject to circulation (e.g. titles purchased for a 
judge and held in the judge’s chambers) and must not appear in a public catalog. 
11) Data extraction from all modules: The Administrative office and the circuits require statistical data to be 
extracted from the system based on various inputs (e.g. vendor, judge type, title, location).  The system must be 
able to produce statistics, either through static reports, or dynamic queries of the data to satisfy those 
requirements. See Attachment B.   
Network Monitoring 
The Contractor shall immediately notify the Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR), and other designated personnel 
at the Administrative Office of any network, system, or security breach which involves the federal judiciary’s ILS 
instances. 
 
Software Modules 
Software modules installed on each instance shall be included under the ILS software maintenance. Modules may be 
implemented in one or more than one installed instance. Contractor shall ensure that all existing data must be 
maintained, accessible, and searchable by judiciary staff. Contractor shall ensure, at a minimum, the same level of 
module functionality currently enjoyed by the courts. 
Special considerations for the Acquisitions Module: 
1) Purchase order format is to be consistent with specific federal and administrative office guidelines, which are 
subject to modification, and amendment.  Such changes must be made in a timely manner to the ILS instances. 
2) Purchase orders must support multi-line, multi-consignee orders.  This information must be accurately recorded 
and transmitted to the judiciary’s financial system. 
3) Purchase orders must contain standard terms and conditions, which may change and should be editable by the 
individual courts. 
4) System interface should allow users to work in multiple modules without requiring the users to have multiple 
screens open simultaneously. 
5) Pre-order searching (the ability to search existing purchase orders linked to a specific bib record, user/consignee 
or vendor) 
6) Cancellation of orders (including updating of associated accounting information) 
7) Receiving (ability to record receipt including partial shipments) 
8) Ability to locate unfilled orders for claiming 
9) Fund accounting (ability to track expenditures and encumbrances against available funds in multiple accounts in 
accordance with accounting practices) 
Bibliographic: 
Must have MARC import and export utilities for Unicode MARC records.  System should allow for batch-ingestion of 
bibliographic records.  It should be able to ingest data from both Connexion Client and  OCLC Records Manager. It should 
also allow for simultaneous deletion of both holdings and item records.  The system should allow for keyword searching, 
‘fuzzy searching’ and allow users in one court to view bibliographic records of another court. It should ideally allow for 
the automated printing of spine labels.   

 
5 
 
Ingesting Procurement Data:  
Ideally, the ILS will be able to ingest historic acquisitions data from a .CSV file or a pipe-delimited .TXT file for use in 
analytic reports 
Documentation 
Release notes and other documentation related to each software release shall be available via the ILS software 
vendor's website prior to the general release of the version. 
 
Help Desk Support 
The Contractor shall provide help desk support, via an online ticketing system, and be available to answer technical 
questions submitted by a designated point-of-contact (POC) for each of the thirteen court sites and by the POC in the 
AO's national program office.  Any requests for assistance by the AO POC or any of the ILS Administrator contacts for 
each circuit should not be posted on a listserv accessible by members of the public. 
 
Technical support shall be available through the Contractor's help desk from 8:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. Eastern time, 
Monday through Friday, or as provided as part of a “white glove” services package.   
 
Help desk assistance shall cover all modules of the ILS software, 
 
Custom Programming 
The Contractor shall provide custom programming support, as required by the Government. Examples of support may 
include, but are not limited to: 
1) Modifications to existing custom programming work, such as custom reports developed by either the AO or the

Performance Work Statement (PWS)

For 
Financial Data Subscription Services for 
EBSA 
 

Performance Work Statement (PWS) Template Mar 2023

PART 1 
General Information 
 
 
 
1.1. Description of Services/Introduction:   
The contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, tools, materials, supervision, and 
other items and non-personal services necessary to provide a subscription for  financial data 
services as defined in this Performance Work Statement, except as Specified in section C-3 
as government furnished property and services.  The contractor shall perform to the 
standards in this contract action. 
 
1.2. Background:   
The Department of Labor’s (DOL) Employee Benefits Security Administration (EBSA) 
administers and enforces the reporting, disclosure, and fiduciary requirements of Title I of the 
Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974 (ERISA). EBSA’s oversight ensures the 
security of the private -sector, employer-sponsored retirement, health, and other workplace 
related benefits of American workers and their families. EBSA is committed to educating and 
assisting Americans covered by private retirement, health, and other welfare benefit plans, as 
well as plan sponsors and members of the employee benefits community. EBSA balances 
proactive enforcement with compliance assistance and works diligently to provide quality 
assistance to plan participants and beneficiaries. EBSA’s policy is to provide the highest quality 
of service to its customers. To fulfill its policy, research, and regulatory responsibilities, EBSA 
requires comprehensive coverage of financial markets, including equities, mutual funds, 
bonds, alternative inv estments, and pension portfolios. This financial data subscription will 
allow EBSA’s economists and investigators to conduct data analysis, and it will cover an array 
of investment vehicles, including both pension plan and retail mutual funds. This financi al 
subscription will have an advanced ability to search for, manipulate, and download large 
amounts of data. This ability to evaluate a plan’s investments in a user -friendly way will help 
targeting plans governed by ERISA and aid EBSA’s national and region al offices in this 
endeavor. Furthermore, EBSA intends to use financial data to inform its current risk -ranking 
model. The model will help EBSA use the financial and enforcement indicators to predict the 
likelihood a plan incurs an ERISA violation. Therefore, acquiring this financial data subscription 
is important to support EBSA and its mission.   
 
1.3. Objectives:  
To obtain a subscription for Financial data services. 
 
1.4. Scope: 
The subscription will include: 
• An advanced investment research platform that unites global investment data and 
EBSA’s proprietary information with tools for highly customized analysis.  

Performance Work Statement (PWS) Template Mar 2023 
 
3 
 
• Tools that allow the user to evaluate investments and portfolios at the individual 
security level and to support research with a searchable database of public filings.  
• Tools that provide an in -depth balance sheet, income statements, cash flows, and 
global equity analysis information.  
• A comprehensive and timely review of total net assets and flow data in the 
marketplace.  
• Real-time data from global sources, including all major equity exchanges.  
• Tools that allow the user to create highly customized fact sheets, reports, data sets, 
spreadsheets, and presentation templates. 
 
1.5. Period of Performance:   
The period of performance shall be for one (1) 12-month base period and four (4) 12-month 
option periods. The Period of Performance reads as follows: 
 
Base Period:   September 27, 2026 – September 26, 2027 
Option Period I:   September 27, 2027 – September 26, 2028 
Option Period II:   September 27, 2028 – September 26, 2029 
Option Period III:   September 27, 2029 – September 26, 2030 
Option Period IV:  September 27, 2030 – September 26, 2031 
 
The government reserves the right to extend the term of this contract action at the prices set 
forth in Section B in accordance with the terms and conditions contained in clause 52.217-9 
entitled, “Option to Extend the Term of the Contract”. 
 
1.6. General Information 
 Quality Control:   
Not Applicable 
 
 Quality Assurance:   
The government shall evaluate the contractor’s performance under this contract action in 
accordance with the Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan. This plan is primarily focused on 
what the government must do to ensure that the contractor has performed in accordance 
with the performance standards. It defines how the performance standards will be applied, 
the frequency of surveillance, and the minimum acceptable defect rate(s). The performance 
standards are listed in Technical Exhibit 1. 
 
 Government Remedies:   
The Contracting Officer shall follow FAR 52.212-4, “Contract Terms a nd Conditions -
Commercial Items” or 52.246-4, “Inspection of Services-Fixed Price” for contractor’s failure to 
perform satisfactory services or failure to correct non-conforming services.

4

Martin Luther King Jr.’s Birthday  Columbus Day

Independence Day    
 
 Hours of Operation:  
The contractor is responsible for conducting performance between the hours of  9:00 am – 
5:30 pm Monday thru Friday (or as mutually agreed upon) , except Federal holidays or when 
the government facility is closed due to local or national emergencies, administrative closings, 
or similar government directed facility closings. The contractor must at all times maintain an 
adequate work  force for the uninterrupted performance of all tasks defined within this 
statement of work when the  government facility is not closed for the above reasons. When 
hiring personnel, the contractor shall keep in mind that the stability and continuity of the work 
force are essential. Telecommuting or “work  at home” is not authorized under this contract 
action unless under emergency situations as determined by  the Contracting Officer’s 
Representative (COR). 
 
 Place of Performance: 
The work to be performed under this contract action will be performed remotely at the 
contractor’s facility. 
 
 Type of Contract:   
The government anticipates award of a firm, fixed-price contract.

 Post Award Conference/Periodic Progress Meetings:   
The contractor agrees to attend any post award conference convened by the contracting 
activity or contract administration office in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation 
Subpart 42.5. The Contracting Officer, Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR), and other 
government personnel, as appropriate, may meet periodically with the contractor to review

PRE-SOLICITATION NOTICE 
Data and Artificial Intelligence (AI) Modernization Support 
Notice ID: DoWEA-PSN-26-002 
Purpose. This pre-solicitation notice announces the Department of War Education 
Activity (DoWEA) intent to issue a Request for Proposal (RFP) for comprehensive data 
modernization, artificial intelligence (AI) integration, and enterprise analytics support 
services for its Chief Data and Artificial Intelligence Office (CDAO). This notice is 
issued for planning and informational purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation, 
request for proposal, or commitment by the Government to award a contract. 
The requirement spans seven broad functional areas, including but not limited to: 
• Data Architecture and Engineering 
• Analytics and Business Intelligence 
• Data Governance 
• AI Integration 
• Data and AI Literacy 
• Student Information System (SIS) Modernization Support 
• Program Management 
1. Anticipated Contract Details 
• Period of Performance: One (1) 12-month base period with four (4) 12-month 
option periods. 
• NAICS Codes: Primary NAICS 541512, Computer Systems Design Services (Size 
Standard: $34 Million).  
• The Government is currently anticipating a Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contract.  
2. Anticipated Solicitation 
The formal RFP is anticipated to be released through SAM.gov. Proposal submission 
instructions, deadlines, and requirements will be provided in the solicitation. 
3. Eligibility 
The solicitation will identify any applicable small business or socio-economic set-asides. 
All proposals must be submitted in accordance with the instructions contained in the 
solicitation. 
4. Disclaimer 
This notice is issued solely for informational purposes and does not obligate the 
Government to issue a solicitation or award a contract. The Government will not 
reimburse respondents for any costs incurred in connection with this notice. The 
Government reserves the right to revise, amend, or cancel information contained 
herein at any time.

Introduction:

This is a Request for Information (RFI) only issued for conducting market research. Accordingly, this RFI constitutes neither a Request for Quote (RFQ), Request for Proposal (RFP), nor a guarantee that one will be issued by the Government in the future; furthermore, it does not commit the Government to contract for any services described herein. The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) is not, at this time, seeking proposals or quotes, and therefore, will not accept, review, or evaluate unsolicited proposals or quotes received in response hereto. This notice is not to be construed as a commitment on the part of the Government to award a contract, nor does the Government intend to pay for any information submitted because of this request. The Government does not reimburse respondents for any costs associated with submission of the information being requested or reimburse expenses incurred for responses to this RFI. The information provided may be used by VA in developing its acquisition strategy and Performance Work Statement (PWS) or Product Description (PD).  Any information submitted by respondents to this RFI is strictly voluntary; however, any information received shall become the property of the Government and will not be returned to the respondent. Interested parties are responsible for adequately marking proprietary, restricted, or competition sensitive information contained in their response. This is a request for information and does not obligate the Government in any way, nor does it commit the Government to any specific course of action. Product information, brochures, part numbers, and/or other description information may be included with the submission.  

Requirement:

The Department of Veteran’s Affairs (VA) Office of Information & Technology (OI&T), Information Technology Budget and Finance (ITBF) has a requirement for cost modeling and financial management software with the ability to categorize and report costs against OIT’s Budget Structure, in addition to calculating Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) for IT Products and Services through a series of allocations based on cost category and operational data sets. The VA IT dollars that must be managed within the application is approximately $9 Billion annually or up to 100,000 financial transactions annually.

The desired outcome of the software purchase is to have a single, unified view of IT cost and related resource consumption categorized against the OIT Budget Structure, in addition to calculating the TCO for all VA IT Products and Services. The contractor shall provide ongoing configuration support, mentoring, and education so that OIT can fully utilize the capabilities of the product and configure in the most efficient manner. The contractor shall provide software updates, platform upgrades (if applicable), product support, and periodic technical health assessments. Please provide a Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) for your product as is needed to meet the salient characteristics listed in the System Capability Requirements for Sections 1.1.1 – 1.1.5.

System Capability Requirements:

1.1.1 IT Cost Transparency

Must be able to model multiple dollar types, including budget, obligations, expenditures, and expenses

Ability to calculate, visualize, and optimize application Total Cost of Ownership (TCO), including fully burdened TCO.

Support demand-driven decision-making by aligning IT spend to business processes, capabilities, and outcomes.

Against all business units, at a minimum, the following metrics:

Business unit percentage of total solutions spend

Total cost of ownership by application and service

Cost per employee or contractor

Business unit percentage of total IT spend

Vendor spend

Service Desk spend and consumption

Cloud spend and consumption

Infrastructure spend and consumption

Against all Products and Services, the following breakouts, at a minimum, for the above metrics:

Business unit

Direct allocation

Indirect allocation

Overhead allocation

Enabling Application allocation

Cost Pools and Sub-Pools

Towers and Sub-Towers

Towers broken out into Cost Pools

Fixed costs

Variable costs

OpEx costs

Capital Expenditure (CapEx) costs

The ability for the government to configure model health reporting, including the strength of the data relationships as part of each allocation from one layer in the model to the next.

The ability to allocate costs in a myriad of ways, including but not limited to:

The ability to allocate costs in a recursive fashion.

The ability to allocate costs using % of total and % of FTE ratios.

The ability to allocate costs using data relationships between financial data and operational data sets (Data Center ID, Server ID, Storage Device ID, Ticket ID, etc.).

The ability to allocate costs in a sequential order.

The ability to allocate costs to Products only and not Services that are in the same Cost Object Layer

1.1.2 Support Services - Product Mentoring

Provide technical product expertise, ongoing guidance and enablement to include weekly office hours, and 24/7 enhanced product support. Specific tasks include:

Provide guidance regarding how to work with available data and how to transform datasets that will fit within the solution’s core capabilities around data automation and data quality.

Help the government understand how to architect the solution to better leverage the government’s data and expose key insights

Help the government learn how to build reports leveraging current capabilities to engage your end users in insight-hunting

Share best practices around solution design, performance and scalability. Mentor government admins to configure more efficiently with performance and long-term maintainability in mind.

E.g. Software should be capable of providing insights into specific calculation time for individual reports

E.g. Support should be capable of identifying formulae that burden the calculation engine excessively

Recommend new use cases to evolve use of the solution

1.1.3 Product Education

Provide access to training delivered via WebEx/video conference, live, or as part of a web education library.

1.1.4 Accessibility, Security, and SLAs, and Performance

Proposed product must meet all salient characteristics without developing an interface, performing any kind of custom development, or requiring extensive configuration by the government.

The product must have achieved FedRAMP Authorization. The Contractor shall comply with FedRAMP requirements as mandated by Federal laws and policies, including making available any documentation, physical access, and logical access needed to support this requirement.  

1.1.5 Additional Information

All functionality listed above must be part of a stand-alone solution that does not depend on another third-party product or bundled system comprised of more than one third party product

Each module set should be capable of providing backend and front-end environment access to specific users

Reporting access should be configurable on a Report-by-Report basis for each persona or user configured

Custom personas should be configurable
