DEPARTMENT OF VETERANS AFFAIRS

Office of Information & Technology

Financial Service Center

Active Navigation (Brand Name or Equal) Discovery Center

Date: July 15, 2026

VA-27-00000574

Product Description 

Version Number:  1.0

1.0	PRODUCT REQUIREMENTS

The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Financial Service Center (FSC) requires Brand Name or Equal Active Navigation to provide an agentless Advanced Electronic File Analysis Solution to index, categorize, and tag documents within 10 terabyte (TB) TB of unstructured repositories. The Advanced Electronic File Analysis Solution (hereafter referred to as “the Solution”) shall discover redundant, obsolete, and trivial data and remediate information at risk of spillage. The Solution must also inventory electronic content holdings in VA File Shares to identify duplicated content and de-duplicate files as appropriate, remediate sensitive content such as personally-identifiable information (PII), protected health information (PHI), agency confidential documents, and other information that should be controlled to minimize risk. The number of repositories will be determined by the electronic file analysis Solution but should not be limited. The file types within the repositories are based on the data owners and include but not limited to common office file types such as xlsx, docx, pptx, pdf, etc.  

The Period of Performance shall be a 12-month base period with three (3) 12-month Option Periods for maintenance and support.  The Solution shall be server based and its location and control will be managed by the FSC. 

Vendor access will be configured using existing cybersecurity methodologies in VA Directive & Handbook.( https://vaww.va.gov/vapubs/search_action.cfm?dType=2)

VA’s requirements are detailed in the table below.

ADVANCED ELECTRONIC FILE ANALYSIS SOLUTION SALIENT CHARACTERISTICS

The Solution’s salient characteristics are specified below:

Definitions:

Electronic File Analysis Solution – electronic file analysis Solution that extracts meaningful metadata universally from all supported file types. This Solution will enable VA to quickly identify and categorize documents by using policy metadata extraction rules.

Agentless – Software is not loaded on each workstation/area, rather centrally located.

Records Management Standards:

Develop rule-based records taxonomies and file plan structures that can be used to discover and auto-categorize files into retention schedules and manage this content in place or migrate it to restructured file shares or other systems. 

Provide an automated method of monitoring ongoing compliance with information governance policies and periodically updating taxonomies and records metadata.

Security and Compliance:

Authentication: Users and services must authenticate with SMART Card aware with the ability authenticate with a username/password as a requirement for accountability.

Software: All software to be installed/used will be evaluated on and approved by the Department of Veterans Affairs One‐VA Technical Reference Model (One‐VA TRM) approved list and be locally installed behind the VA FSCfirewall to meet VA security requirements (www.va.gov/trm/searchpage.aspx). Contractor must submit names of all software to be used. 

Accountability: Create an audit log entry that includes the minimum requirements:

Date/timestamps for activity

Username associated with activity/action

Status 

Starting / stopping services. The VA FSC  uses windows integrated authentication, and do not store this information anywhere.

Request Type: For tasks such as index processing and deletions, the VA FSC store an edited by and created by value, along with an updated date record

Software Support:

24 x 7 x 365 software ticketing

Software Updates as released

Software Upgrades as released

On-site support as needed (within 24 hours)1.1.1 ADVANCED ELECTRONIC FILE ANALYSIS SOLUTION GENERAL REQUIREMENTS

 The Solution shall:

Extract meaningful metadata universally from all supported file types. The Solution shall enable VA to quickly identify and categorize documents by using policy metadata extraction rules.

Be Agentless software is not loaded on each workstation/area, rather centrally

Adhere to Records Management Standards at a minimum,

Develop rule-based records taxonomies and file plan structures that can be used to discover and auto-categorize

Place files into retention schedules and manage this content in place or migrate it to restructured file shares or other systems. 

Provide an automated method of monitoring ongoing compliance with information governance policies and periodically updating taxonomies and records metadata.

Be scalable to millions of files per day. 

Identify documents that are due for disposition based on internal or external policies, tag metadata, and mark-up documents for review, deletion, migration etc.

Discretely categorize documents regardless of format

Be an agentless Solution that has 3% or less of total index size of total content under management.

1.1.2 ADVANCED ELECTRONIC FILE ANALYSIS SOLUTION TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS

Theolution has multiple phase requirements: Classification, Metadata creation and Extraction, and auto-classification. Specifically:

Classification Requirements:

Solution shall classify documents by textual analysis, keywords or layout, and then extract data from unstructured files.

Rules sets may be written to help identify the location of the text to be used for classification and extraction.

Shall pull key information directly from electronic documents fast and accurately.

Shall be able to identify and make sense of a wide variety of documents, regardless of their size, use of symbols, and language.

Shall recognize, sort and extract data from unstructured documents.

Metadata Extraction Requirements:

Metadata extraction rulesets shall be able to be modeled against the extracted metadata to refine logic sets and utilize regular expressions (RegEx) for pattern match and recognition.

All Metadata extraction structures shall be fully customizable in order to refine the categorization/classification rules for document identification.

Work packages shall be exportable to ensure integration with business processes.

Once index values have been identified, the software shall be able to extract data for review later in the validation process.

Software shall be able to compare recognized data to data that exists in unstructured environments.

Delivery Requirements:

After document repositories have gone through the previous stages, the documents along with its metadata, index information shall be able to be released to any of the following: database, Content Management System, file system, Line of Business Application, archive location, XML file, API with third party applications, or other specified destinations.

1.1.3 ADVANCED ELECTRONIC FILE ANALYSIS SOLUTION SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS

Provide Security and Compliance including:

Authentication: Users and services shall authenticate with a unique id as a requirement for accountability.

Software: All software to be installed/used will be evaluated on and shall pass the Department of Veterans Affairs One‐VA Technical Reference Model (One‐VA TRM) approved list and be locally installed behind the VA FSC firewall to meet VA security requirements (www.va.gov/trm/searchpage.aspx). Contractor shall submit names of all software to be used.

Accountability: Create an audit log entry that includes the minimum requirements including:

Date/timestamps for activity

Username associated with activity/action

Status

Starting / stopping services. The FSCuses windows integrated authentication, and do not store this information anywhere.

Request Type: For tasks such as index processing and deletions, the VA FSC store an edited by and created by value, along with an updated date record

Support at a minimum, the following Operating Systems:

Windows Platforms

Windows Server 2008 64 bit

Windows Server 2008 R2

Windows Server 2012

Windows Server 2012 R2

Windows Server 2016

Windows Server 2019 (once AGM approved)

Windows 10

Support at a minimum, the following Databases:

Microsoft SQL Server 2012 (X64) - All Versions

Microsoft SQL Server 2014

Microsoft SQL Server 2016

Support at a minimum, the following Browsers:

Internet Explorer current version

Chrome current version

Microsoft Edge current version

SOLUTION MAINTENANCE, LICENSING AND SUPPORT

The Contractor shall provide twelve-months of software maintenance updates and software licensing for the software included in this PD.  

The maintenance services shall adhere to the following requirements:

Support services shall be available by phone 24 hours per day, 7 days a week, 365 days per year.

The contractor shall provide current versions of all software included in this PD throughout the maintenance period.

The Contractor shall provide Premium software maintenance and technical support services covering software in this effort to include the following:

Direct access (phone and email) to Technical Support team on a 24-hours a day, 7 days a week basis (24/7).

Online support, providing access to: Software upgrades and updates to include major releases, point releases, service releases and security releases of applicable software.

The ability of the Facility Records Officer to extract reports from the system by department at the user access level.

Update the system with the current record control schedules.

Provide a user interface dashboard for ease of access by the Facility Records Officer.

The dashboard must define deficiencies based upon the current record control schedule. The granularity must be at the directorate and department level. 

Data Mining support 

Record Management support 

SUPPLEMENTAL REQUIREMENTS

The contractor shall provide the following additional services.

CONTRACTOR PROJECT MANAGEMENT PLAN

The Contractor shall deliver a Contractor Project Management Plan (CPMP) that lays out the Contractor’s approach, timeline and tools to be used in execution of the contract.  The CPMP should take the form of both a narrative and graphic format that displays the schedule, milestones, risks and resource support.  The CPMP shall also include how the Contractor shall coordinate and execute planned, routine, and ad hoc data collection reporting requests as identified within the Product Description.  The initial baseline CPMP shall be concurred upon and updated in accordance with Section B of the contract.  The Contractor shall update and maintain the VA PM approved CPMP throughout the Peroid of Performance (PoP). 

The Project Manager shall serve as the single primary and direct Point of Contact (POC) throughout the PoP.  The Project Manager shall conduct calls a minimum of every other week with the VA PA, COR, and PM beginning one week after award and continuing throughout the duration of the effort.

 R

Deliverable:  

Contractor Project Management Plan

REPORTING REQUIREMENTS

The Contractor shall provide the COR with Monthly Progress Reports in electronic form in Microsoft Word and Project formats.  The report shall include detailed instructions/explanations for each required data element, to ensure that data is accurate and consistent.  These reports shall reflect data as of the last day of the preceding Month.

The Monthly Progress Reports shall cover all work completed during the reporting period and work planned for the subsequent reporting period.  The report shall also identify any problems that arose and a description of how the problems were resolved.  If problems have not been completely resolved, the Contractor shall provide an explanation including their plan and timeframe for resolving the issue. It is expected that the Contractor will keep in communication with VA accordingly so that issues that arise are transparent to both parties to prevent escalation of outstanding issues.

Deliverable:  

Monthly Progress Report

ADDITIONAL SERVICES

The Contractor shall provide Subject Matter Expertise services in support of this effort in the areas of Data Mining and Records Management. Any contractor discussion, analyses, recommendations, and conclusions shall be documented in the VA Monthly Activity Report.

DATA MINING SERVICES

The contractor shall provide Data Mining Subject Matter expertise for ongoing support of the data analysis and management of the VA digital file environment. The subject matter expert be expert in the proposed Solution and setup, configure and customize the Solution to meet VA requirements. At a minimum the Data Mining Subject Matter expert shall:

a. Be fully trained on all aspects of the Advanced Electronic File Analysis Systems.

b. Provides support related to the installation, capabilities, and use of the Advanced Electronic File Analysis specific to the VA FSC.

c. Provide comprehensive Advanced Electronic File Analysis System orientation to VA FSC focused on system configuration, application installation, application capabilities, and Advanced Electronic File Analysis System use cases.

d. Provide Advanced Electronic File Analysis System administration and user documentation where required in either a digital or paper form that provides information on system configuration, application installation, application capabilities, and application products.

e. Guide and assist in the configuration of the computer system in preparation for the application installation.

f. Install the Advanced Electronic File Analysis System application.

g. Train selected VA on the operation and maintenance of the Advanced Electronic File Analysis System

h. Train selected VA FSC staff on the use and workflow of Advanced Electronic File Analysis System

i. Guide and assist VA FSC staff in selecting candidate sets for use in Advanced Electronic File Analysis System

j. Guide and assist VA FSC staff in producing Advanced Electronic File Analysis System products in either digital or paper form.

Please Note: The Data Mining Subject Matter Expert Will Not directly interact with the data; will not have network access, VPN access will not be authorized; Actual interaction will be performed by agency personnel

GENERAL INFORMATION

PLACE OF PERFORMANCE

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

DESCRIPTION

Introduction

This Request for Information (RFI) is for planning purposes only and shall not be considered an Invitation for Bid, Request for Task Execution Plan, Request for Quotation or a Request for Proposal. Additionally, there is no obligation on the part of the Government to acquire any products or services described in this RFI. Your response to this RFI will be treated only as information for the Government to consider. You will not be entitled to payment for direct or indirect costs that you incur in responding to this RFI. This request does not constitute a solicitation for proposals or the authority to enter into negotiations to award a contract. No funds have been authorized, appropriated or received for this effort. Interested parties are responsible for adequately marking proprietary, restricted or competition sensitive information contained in their response. The Government does not intend to pay for the information submitted in response to this RFI. 

The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) for this requirement is projected to be 541519 with a size standard of $34 million.

VA is contemplating a potential requirement to renew software maintenance and support of its deployed Network-based Encryption Key Recovery Storage System (NBEKRSS) solution. VA is conducting Market Research into potential providers of that software maintenance, as well as assessing the market conditions for new potential entrants and capabilities of like solutions. At this time, VA is conducting research, and as such this RFI shall not bind VA in any way. See attached draft Product Description for additional details.

 2. Submittal Information:

All responsible sources may submit a response in accordance with the information below.  

There is a page limitation for this RFI of 15 pages. The Government will not review any other information or attachments included that are in excess of the (15) page limit. 

NO MARKETING MATERIALS ARE ALLOWED AS PART OF THIS RFI.  Generic capability statements will not be accepted or reviewed. Your response must address capabilities specific to the services required in the attached PD and must include the following:

Interested Vendors shall at a minimum provide the following information in the initial paragraph of the submission [For SDVOSBs and VOSB, proof of verification in SBA Small Business Search (SBS) website https://search.certifications.sba.gov/]:

Name of Company

Address

Point of Contact

Phone Number

Email address

Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) Code

Unique Entity Identifier (UEI)

Company Business Size and Status

North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code

Socioeconomic data

Existing Contractual Vehicles (Governmentwide Acquisition Contract (GWAC), Federal Supply Schedule (FSS), etc.)

Provide a summary of your ability to meet the requirements contained within the draft Product Description (PD) for the following areas:

1. Company Qualifications and Product Overview

Describe your organization’s experience providing enterprise on-premises cryptographic or key-management software to federal agencies of comparable scale to the Department of Veterans Affairs.  Provide a high-level description of your encryption key recovery storage system and its primary functional components. Include Certificate Authority (CA) and Hardware Security Module (HSM) integration experience and any requirements/limitations for the configurations.

Identify any existing contract vehicles under which your product and support services are offered.

Confirm whether your product fully supports a ‘customer-applied update’ model in an on-premises, non-cloud environment.

2. Federal Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) and Security Compliance

Explain how your solution complies with: 

Federal PKI policy requirements

National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) cryptographic standards

Federal Information Processing Standard (FIPS) 140-2 or 140-3 validated modules

Provide documentation or references validating these claims.

3.   Licensing Model

Provide your pricing/licensing structure, including: 

Perpetual vs subscription licensing

Per-user, per-server, per-appliance, or usage-based metrics

Any separate costs for HSM/CA integration or PKI modules

4. Release Management & Patching

Describe how all software updates can be provided to the VA (e.g., secure download portal, customer portal, offline packages), ensuring that:
– All updates can be applied by VA personnel only
– No contractor login to VA systems is required
– No remote access sessions into the VA environment are required


Explain your software maintenance lifecycle for: 

Patches

Security updates

Hotfixes

Major/minor version releases


 Describe your approach to ensuring patches and updates do not disrupt operational cryptographic workflows, including how VA staff can validate updates in an offline or isolated environment.

5. Technical Support Model

Describe your technical support offerings including: 

Tiers of support

Response times

Availability (business hours vs 24/7)

Escalation procedures


Describe your technical support model, including:
– How troubleshooting is performed without contractor access to VA networks or systems
– Methods for VA-only log collection, diagnostic exports, or offline troubleshooting

BACKGROUND

The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Office of Information & Technology (OIT), Infrastructure Operations (IO) provides secure and reliable information technology services that support VA’s mission to deliver timely and effective care and benefits to Veterans. VA depends heavily on Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) technologies to protect sensitive information, including encrypted electronic messages and documents transmitted across the enterprise.

VA’s PKI environment issues Federal Information Processing Standards (FIPS)-compliant x.509 certificates for secure messaging and encryption. The U.S. Department of the Treasury Shared Service Provider (SSP) PKI hosts two Certificate Authorities (CA) that issue VA’s Secure/Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions (S/MIME) Key Management certificates: VA Certificate Authority (VACA)1 and VA Certificate Authority (VACA)2. These certificates enable VA personnel to protect sensitive information and support mission-critical operations.

To comply with federal directives, including the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) and requirements for litigation discovery and records access, VA must maintain the ability to recover private keys associated with VA-issued encryption certificates. Private keys are escrowed within the PKI structure to support authorized decryption when necessary.

The current Network-based Encryption Key Recovery Storage Solution (NBEKRSS) is a critical component of VA’s PKI ecosystem. The system supports secure key recovery, high-volume S/MIME decryption, operational investigations, and e-Discovery workflows. The solution must integrate with VA’s Treasury-hosted Certificate Authorities, enterprise directories, existing Hardware Security Module (HSM) infrastructure (including VA’s Luna T-5000 HSMs), and related VA PKI services. This current solution is comprised of brand name Zeva DecryptNaBox licenses and supported via brand name maintenance. 

PRODUCT REQUIREMENTS

VA OIT has a requirement to renew maintenance of its existing solution. The current system is a Commercial-Off-The-Shelf (COTS) software solution with some customization to meet Government requirements as well as software maintenance, (releases, patches, and hotfixes), and software support services. 

The Network-based Encryption Key Recovery Storage Solution (NBEKRSS) must provide secure recovery, storage, management, and operational use of cryptographic private keys associated with VA user encryption certificates issued under the U.S. Treasury SSP PKI (VACA1 and VACA2). The solution must support large-scale S/MIME decryption for investigations, cybersecurity operations, litigation discovery, and other authorized VA use cases. The solution must be fully hosted on VA-owned infrastructure and integrate with VA’s PKI services, directory services, certificate authorities, and hardware security modules.

SALIENT CHARACTERISTICS

Offerors must demonstrate their solution meets all of the following minimum characteristics and can support minimum encryption keys of 3.5 million or more supporting the enterprise at any given time.


These characteristics define what is considered “Brand Name or Equal.”

Minimal Salient Characteristics

PKI Compatibility

Fully interoperable with the U.S. Treasury SSP PKI issuance environment, including VACA1 and VACA2. VACA provides the ability to connect and retrieve private key material from Entrust Security Manager Administration CAs.

Integration with VA enterprise directory services for user lookup and authorization.

On-Premises Operation

All components must operate entirely within VA facilities on VA owned networks and hardware.

Cryptographic Requirements

Uses FIPS-validated cryptographic modules. Per NIST FIPS 140‑3 validated modules (or FIPS 140‑2 validated where 140‑3 is not yet available for the specific module).

Supports modern Transport Layer Security (TLS) configurations appropriate for federal environments. TLS 1.2/1.3 configured per NIST SP 800‑52 Rev. 2.

Key Recovery Capabilities

Secure ingestion, cataloging, and recovery of VA user encryption private keys, providing authorized personnel with a controlled and auditable process for restoring encrypted content while maintaining strict access controls, chain‑of‑custody, and alignment with VA security and privacy policies.

Decryption Capabilities

Maintains metadata and forensic integrity.

Achieve ≥ 95% successful decrypt on eligible items with proper keys, with detailed failure logging for ineligible/invalid cases; sustain ≥ 50,000 email items/hour (combined messages + attachments) on VA‑standard compute or provide sizing to meet the same throughput, with linear/near‑linear scaling via additional workers.

HSM Integration

Compatible with VA’s Luna T-5000 HSMs and Personal Identification Numbers (PIN) Entry Device (PED)-based key controls.

Role-Based Access Controls

Least-privilege model with separate operator, approver, and auditor roles.

Software Maintenance Model/ Technical Support Model (VA-Applied)

The Contractor shall provide 12 months of support services for the software and licenses included in this PD. The initial support period shall commence upon VA inspection and acceptance.

The support services shall adhere to the following requirements:

Support services shall be available by phone 24 hours per day, 365 days per year.

Support services must be provided from U.S. based personnel and facilities located within the Continental United States (CONUS).

Support services shall assist with remediation of all vulnerabilities identified through Government security scans. 

The Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) shall provide current versions of all software included in this PD throughout the maintenance period.

Software and firmware updates, including major releases, point releases, patch management, newly released features, service releases, security releases, and bug fixes.

Introduction

This Request for Information (RFI) is for planning purposes only and shall not be considered an Invitation for Bid, Request for Task Execution Plan, Request for Quotation or a Request for Proposal. Additionally, there is no obligation on the part of the Government to acquire any products or services described in this RFI. Your response to this RFI will be treated only as information for the Government to consider. You will not be entitled to payment for direct or indirect costs that you incur in responding to this RFI. This request does not constitute a solicitation for proposals or the authority to enter into negotiations to award a contract. No funds have been authorized, appropriated or received for this effort. Interested parties are responsible for adequately marking proprietary, restricted or competition sensitive information contained in their response. The Government does not intend to pay for the information submitted in response to this RFI.

The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) for this requirement is 541519 with a size standard of $34 million.  

2. Submittal Information:

All responsible sources may submit a response in accordance with the below information.  

There is a page limitation for this RFI of 10 pages. The Government will not review any other information or attachments included, that are in excess of the 10-page limit. PRODUCT REQUIREMENTS

The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Office of Information Technology (OI&T), Connectivity and Collaboration Services (CCS), has a requirement for brand name Cisco Switches to be used in our AITC PITC datacenters in Austin, TX and Philadelphia PA. These are additions to the preexisting network. This is a hardware only procurement, these switches will be added to the VA’s Cisco Enterprise Infrastructure and Advanced Engineering Service Agreement (CEIAESA). The Switches shall be delivered to the VA with the address’s registered to the Ship to address with Cisco so warranty work can be accomplished without delay.

The Period of Performance (PoP) shall include one 12-month base period.

Delivery times shall be in coordination with the PoP. Estimated delivery times shall be provided within 5 days of award.

NOTICE OF THE FEDERAL ACCESSIBILITY LAW AFFECTING ALL INFORMATION AND COMMUNICATION TECHNOLOGY (ICT) PROCUREMENTS (SECTION 508)

On January 18, 2017, the Access Board issued a final rule that updated accessibility requirements covered by Section 508 and refreshed guidelines for telecommunications equipment subject to Section 255 of the Communications Act.  The final rule went into effect on January 18, 2018.  The revisions and updates to the Section 508-based standards and Section 255-based guidelines are intended to ensure that information and communication technology (ICT) covered by the respective statutes is accessible to and usable by individuals with disabilities.

SECTION 508 – INFORMATION AND COMMUNICATION TECHNOLOGY (ICT) STANDARDS

The Section 508 standards established by the Access Board are incorporated into, and made part of all VA orders, solicitations and purchase orders developed to procure ICT.  These standards are found in their entirety at: Revised 508 Standards and 255 Guidelines (access-board.gov).  A single PDF file version of the Revised Section 508 Standards and 255 Guidelines will be supplied upon request, or can be obtained from the Access Board website.  Federal agencies must comply with the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, as amended. 

The Contractor shall comply with “508 Chapter 2: Scoping Requirements” for all electronic ICT and content delivered under this contract. Specifically, as appropriate for the technology and its functionality, the Contractor shall comply with the technical standards marked here: 

E205 Electronic Content – (Accessibility Standard -WCAG 2.0 Level A and AA Guidelines)

E204 Functional Performance Criteria

E206 Hardware Requirements

E207 Software Requirements

E208 Support Documentation and Services Requirements

COMPATABILITY WITH ASSISTIVE TECHNOLOGY

The standards do not require installation of specific accessibility-related software or attachment of an assistive technology device. Section 508 requires that ICT be compatible with such software and devices so that ICT can be accessible to and usable by individuals using assistive technology, including but not limited to screen readers, screen magnifiers, and speech recognition software.

ACCEPTANCE AND ACCEPTANCE TESTING

Deliverables resulting from this solicitation will be accepted based in part on satisfaction of the Section 508 Chapter 2: Scoping Requirements standards identified above.

The Government reserves the right to test for Section 508 Compliance before delivery.  The Contractor shall be able to demonstrate Section 508 Compliance upon delivery.

INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY USING SUSTAINABLE PRODUCTS

The Contractor shall comply with Sections 524 and Sections 525 of the Energy Independence and Security Act of 2007; Section 104 of the Energy Policy Act of 2005; Executive Order 14148, “Initial Rescissions of Harmful Executive Orders and Actions,” dated January 20, 2025; Executive Order 13221, “Energy-Efficient Standby Power Devices,” dated August 2, 2001; and the Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul (RFO) to provide ENERGY STAR® certified and Federal Energy Management Program (FEMP) Designated Low Standby Power information technology products, see https://www.energy.gov/femp/search-energy-efficient-products.  See http://www.energystar.gov for complete product specifications and updated lists of Energy Star certified products.  FEMP low standby power product listing can be found at https://www.energy.gov/femp/low-standby-power-product-list.

The Contractor shall provide products that meet the definition of sustainable products if the products are delivered to the Government; furnished by the Contractor for use by the Government, incorporated into the construction of a public building or public work, or acquired by the Contractor for use in performing services under a Government contract where the cost of the products is a direct cost to a Government contract (versus costs which are normally applied to a contractor's general and administrative expenses or indirect costs).

Specifically, the Contractor shall provide sustainable products under this contract in accordance with RFO 52.223-23 (NOV 2025).  The applicable products with their associated certification and/or designation required (e.g. Energy Star, FEMP Low Standby Power) are identified within the product requirements specifications in this PD.  The Contractor shall self-certify that its proposed products meet the certification(s) and/or designation(s) specified.

Visual Inspection:
- Check area for any safety concerns that may affect the safety of the technician and or the customer.
- Check subassemblies, wiring harnesses, contacts, cables and other major components for burns or broken 
wires.
- Clean or replace all air filters.
- Check all fans for slow start and free rotation.
N0018926QW265
Page 2 of 27

- Check AC input and output for proper wiring, grounding and verify to NEC code standards.
- Check input and output grounding is proper and sufficient for customer application.
- Check and record alarm logs.
- Check all circuit boards and connections for cleanliness and or possible problems.
- Check all breakers, power connections, fuses and controls for excessive heating or swelling via thermal scan 
and reading.
- Check AC and DC capacitors for swelling or leakage.
- Check for DC capacitor vent caps that have extruded more than 1/8 inch.
- Check all nuts, bolts, screws and connectors for tightness and heat discoloration.
Power Checks
- Check input voltage, amperage, and frequency readings for proper levels and balance. Also check power 
quality and harmonic distortion levels on special request.
- Check output voltage, amperage, and frequency readings for proper levels and balance. Also check power 
quality and harmonic distortion levels on special request.
- Check bypass voltage and frequency for proper available power.
- Check input power and harmonic filters for proper operation and balance.
- Check output power and harmonic filters for proper operation and balance.
- With customer approval, perform operational test of the system including unit transfer and battery discharge.
- Review system performance with customer to address any questions and to schedule any repairs, depending on 
availability of customer.
Internal Component Checks
- Check and calibrate any logic and control signals as specified in the manufacturer’s maintenance procedures.
- Check all indicators and meters for proper operation and calibration adjusting as necessary in accordance to the 
manufacturer’s maintenance procedures.
- Check and calibrate all power supply settings in accordance with manufacturer’s specified settings.
- Check rectifier voltage and current balance for proper operation.
- Check inverter voltages and balance for proper operation.
- Check static switch voltages and inspect for any leakage.
- Check fuses on the DC capacitor deck for continuity if applicable.
- Install or perform Engineering Field Change Notices (FCN) as necessary.
External Environmental Checks
- Check ambient temperature of the UPS room.
- Check location for cleanliness and accessibility.
VRLA Battery System
- Inspect the appearance and cleanliness of all batteries, connectors, cabinet(s) or rack(s), and room(s).
- Check each battery for signs of damage to the case, cover or terminals, staining of the case, terminals or 
surrounding areas, excessive swelling, evidence of melting or thermal damage to the cover and terminal post-
seal plus support cabinet(s) or rack(s) for signs of physical damage, corrosion, etc.
- Confirm battery cabinet(s) or rack(s) hardware integrity and tighten connections as necessary.
- Clean and retighten all terminal connectors and check for NO-OX grease or oil on all connections (when 
needed and/or accessible).
- Check system float voltage and current and adjust if necessary to manufacturer’s specified settings.
- Measure and record DC bus ripple voltage when applicable.
- Measure and record all internal impedance readings.
- Measure and record all battery connection resistances in micro-ohms when applicable.
- Measure individual battery temperatures and check for any hot spots or readiness which are out of the 
manufacturer’s recommend temperature variance when accessible.
- Perform individual battery load testing when accessible.
- Record battery date codes, number of cells and strings.

STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW)

IT Hardware Support Services for VistA PACS

Phoenix Indian Medical Center (PIMC)
Phoenix Area – Indian Health Service (IHS)
U.S. Department of Health & Human Services

1.0 BACKGROUND

Phoenix Indian Medical Center (PIMC) is a tertiary referral hospital operated by the Phoenix Area Indian Health Service (IHS). PIMC provides comprehensive inpatient, outpatient, emergency, and specialty healthcare services to American Indian and Alaska Native populations throughout Arizona and the surrounding region.

PIMC operates the IHS Veterans Health Information Systems and Technology Architecture (VistA) Radiology Package integrated with a Picture Archiving and Communication System (PACS) to support diagnostic imaging services. The PACS environment supports radiology modalities including, but not limited to:

Computed Tomography (CT)

Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI)

Digital Radiography (DR)

Fluoroscopy

Ultrasound

Mammography

Nuclear Medicine

The PACS infrastructure includes enterprise servers, storage arrays, diagnostic reading workstations, clinical review stations, networking components, modality interface hardware, and supporting rack-mounted equipment located within the PIMC data center and clinical areas.

This Statement of Work defines requirements for comprehensive IT hardware support services for the PIMC VistA PACS environment to ensure continuous clinical operations.

2.0 OBJECTIVE

The objective of this requirement is to maintain high availability, reliability, performance, and regulatory compliance of hardware supporting the PIMC VistA PACS environment through preventive maintenance, corrective maintenance, emergency support, and lifecycle management services.

3.0 PLACE OF PERFORMANCE

Phoenix Indian Medical Center
4212 N. 16th Street
Phoenix, Arizona 85016

Services shall be performed on-site at PIMC and remotely when authorized and compliant with IHS security requirements.

4.0 SCOPE OF WORK

The Contractor shall provide all personnel, supervision, equipment, tools, materials, transportation, and parts necessary to perform hardware support services for the PIMC VistA PACS infrastructure.

Covered hardware includes, but is not limited to:

PACS application servers (physical hardware)

Database servers (hardware layer only)

Storage Area Network (SAN) / NAS devices

RAID arrays and storage controllers

Diagnostic radiologist reading workstations

Clinical image review workstations

Modality interface hardware

DICOM routing appliances

Network switches dedicated to PACS (if designated by PIMC OIT)

Rack-mounted infrastructure components

Hardware-level backup appliances supporting PACS

5.0 TASK REQUIREMENTS

5.1 Corrective Maintenance

The Contractor shall:

Diagnose and repair hardware failures impacting PACS operations.

Replace defective components with OEM or OEM-certified parts.

Coordinate warranty repairs with original manufacturers.

Restore affected systems to full operational status.

Provide root cause analysis for all critical failures.

5.2 Preventive Maintenance

The Contractor shall:

Perform preventive maintenance per OEM specifications.

Conduct firmware verification and hardware health checks (as authorized).

Inspect system components for signs of wear, overheating, or failure.

Validate redundancy configurations (power supplies, RAID, network paths).

Document all preventive maintenance activities.

Preventive maintenance shall be scheduled during non-peak clinical hours and coordinated with the PIMC Office of Information Technology (OIT) and Radiology Department.

5.3 Emergency Support

The Contractor shall provide 24/7/365 emergency support.

Response requirements:

Remote Response: Within 1 hour of notification

On-Site Response (Critical System Failure): Within 4 hours

On-Site Response (Non-Critical): Next business day

Critical failures include:

Inability to acquire images

Inability to retrieve or view diagnostic images

Server or storage array failure

PACS workstation hardware failure impacting patient care

5.4 System Availability

The Contractor shall support system uptime of at least:

99% availability, excluding scheduled maintenance windows approved by PIMC OIT.

5.5 Hardware Inventory and Lifecycle Management

The Contractor shall:

Maintain a current hardware asset inventory.

Track:

Serial numbers

Warranty status

Firmware versions

End-of-life (EOL) dates

Provide annual lifecycle replacement recommendations.

Identify hardware posing operational or security risk.

5.6 Security and Compliance

The Contractor shall comply with:

Federal Information Security Modernization Act (FISMA)

NIST SP 800-53 security controls (as applicable)

HHS Information Security Policy

IHS OIT security requirements

HIPAA Security Rule

Additional Requirements:

All personnel must complete IHS-required cybersecurity and privacy training.

Personnel must pass required federal background investigations prior to system access.

No hardware modifications shall occur without written approval from PIMC OIT.

Contractor must coordinate all firmware updates with PIMC IT Security.

6.0 HOURS OF OPERATION

Normal Business Hours:
Monday – Friday
8:00 AM – 5:00 PM (Mountain Standard Time – Arizona does not observe Daylight Saving Time)

Emergency services must be available 24/7/365.

7.0 GOVERNMENT-FURNISHED PROPERTY (GFP)

The Government will provide:

Access to PACS hardware inventory records

Physical access to server rooms and imaging areas (escorted as required)

System access credentials (as authorized)

Workspace during on-site visits

The Contractor shall supply all other necessary tools and equipment.

8.0 DELIVERABLES

9.0 PERFORMANCE METRICS

Performance will be monitored by the Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR) at PIMC.

10.0 PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE

Base Period: 12 months from date of award


11.0 ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

Services will be considered acceptable when:

Hardware is restored to operational status within required timelines

Preventive maintenance is completed as scheduled

Deliverables are accurate and timely

Federal security and compliance standards are met

12.0 APPLICABLE REGULATIONS

Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR)

HHS Acquisition Regulation (HHSAR)

FISMA

NIST SP 800-53

HHS Information Security Policy

IHS OIT Policy

Performance Work Statement (PWS) for

Army Enterprise Identity, Credential and Access Management (E-ICAM) Delivery Contract 

FOR

Army Capability Program Executive (CPE) Command and Control Information Network (C2IN)

DATE: 03 March 2026

VERISON: Army E-ICAM Delivery v1

Controlled by: Department of Army 
Controlled by: CPE C2INEO EIS
CUI Category(ies): Procurement and Acquisition 
Distribution: FEDCON
POC: David Thompson

Section 1 – General

1. Description of services

The Contractor shall provide all non-personal services, supervision, and resources necessary to perform the continuous delivery and modernization of the Army's enterprise Identity, Credential, and Access Management (ICAM) platform, as defined in this Performance Work Statement (PWS). These services encompass the continuous operation, maintenance, and Tier 3 helpdesk support for existing capabilities, including the Army Master Identity Directory (AMID), Army Enterprise Identity Provider (IdP), Identity Governance and Administration (IGA), Privileged Access Management (PAM), and auditing services across all classification levels. Concurrently, the contractor will incrementally develop, deliver, and integrate modernized ICAM capabilities using an agile methodology to incorporate Zero Trust principles, automate account provisioning and access controls, and improve identity governance. This effort requires a Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) model that utilizes a continuous delivery pipeline that ensures proactive security patching and automated capability enhancements without disrupting mission operations.

The contractor shall replace manual 'break-fix' routines with automated, self-healing infrastructure that comply with Zero Trust concepts and ensure Army Unified Network ICAM capabilities never stagnate; adaptations are deployed in hours, not months.  The Army E-ICAM services must guarantee critical access capabilities remain highly available to the warfighter, while seamlessly integrating continuous security and feature updates. These comprehensive services are designed to improve the Army's cybersecurity posture, drive IT efficiencies by eliminating redundant systems, and ensure compliance with Federal, DoD, and Army mandates.

1.2. Background 

The Department of the Army operates a suite of enterprise Identity, Credential, and Access Management (ICAM) capabilities that are foundational to securing the Army’s network and data. This existing infrastructure, while operational, requires significant flexible modernization to align with current Department of Defense (DoD) and Army cybersecurity strategies, including the transition to a Zero Trust Architecture. This initiative is driven by the urgent need to enhance security, improve IT efficiency by consolidating disparate systems, and ensure compliance with federal mandates and audit requirements.

This modernization effort is a critical enterprise-wide initiative that impacts and requires coordination across a broad spectrum of Army organizations. The contractor's performance will be integral to meeting the complex requirements of these varied stakeholders as the Army evolves its ICAM platform to provide a more robust, centralized, and automated solution for managing digital identities and access control.

1.3. Scope

Base Requirements: The scope of this Performance Work Statement (PWS) encompasses the full lifecycle of services required to sustain and modernize the Army's enterprise Identity, Credential, and Access Management (ICAM) platform. This includes continuing to deliver all current ICAM capabilities while simultaneously developing and integrating modernized solutions using an agile framework. A critical component of this scope is providing direct support for audit compliance, including the remediation of findings from financial and cybersecurity audits. The contractor shall provide all necessary program management, systems engineering, and technical support to enhance the platform in alignment with Zero Trust principles, automate controls to address audit requirements, and integrate Army applications into the enterprise and tactical operating environments to improve the Army's overall cybersecurity posture and IT efficiency.

Optional Surge Capability: The Government, at its sole discretion, may require the contractor to provide agile based surge support beyond the level of effort defined for the base requirements. This optional capability provides for increased support for any task area within this PWS in response to unforeseen requirements, new mandates, or changes in schedule. All surge support shall be ordered by the Contracting Officer in accordance with the terms of the contract."

1.4. Place of performance

The contractor can perform work at a remote location that can support the mission requirements in accordance with DoD and Army regulations, including access to NIPRNet, SIPRNet, Top Secret (if applicable) and Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI) known as the Joint Worldwide Intelligence Communications System (JWICS) and commercial cloud services. The government will also provide on-site access at Fort Belvoir, VA.

1.5. Travel requirements will be dependent on the contractor's proposed solution. It is anticipated that travel outside of the National Capital Region will be required at least five times per year. The specific details regarding locations, dates, and the number of participants is to be determined and proposed by the contractor.

1.6. FEDERAL HOLIDAYS. 

Non-Performance Days: The contractor is not required to perform services on the federal holidays listed below. The U.S. Government observes the following days as holidays:

New Year's Day (January 1st)

Martin Luther King, Jr.'s Birthday (Third Monday in January)

Washington's Birthday / Presidents' Day (Third Monday in February)

Memorial Day (Last Monday in May)

Juneteenth National Independence Day (June 19th)

Independence Day (July 4th)

Labor Day (First Monday in September)

Columbus Day (Second Monday in October)

Veterans Day (November 11th)

Thanksgiving Day (Fourth Thursday in November)

Christmas Day (December 25th)

Holidays on Non-Workdays: When a holiday falls on a Saturday, it is observed on the preceding Friday. When a holiday falls on a Sunday, it is observed on the following Monday.

Other Declared Holidays: In addition to the days designated as holidays, the Government observes any other day designated by Federal Statute, Executive Order, or Presidential Proclamation. The Contracting Officer will notify the contractor of any such additional holiday observances.

1.7. Security Clearance

The Contractor requires a Secret/Non-Possessing Facility Clearance. Currently, all labor categories, including the ICAM delivery, are set at the Secret level, consistent with the base contract. However, future requirements may necessitate an upgrade to a Top Secret clearance. All Personnel working directly on design, engineering, or installation activities shall have an ACTIVE (not interim) and CURRENT DoD Clearance at the appropriate level required to complete their assigned duties on their assigned systems. It is anticipated that personnel will require varying levels of clearances based on their assigned duties and systems. The Contractor shall manage their personnel as appropriate to properly protect classified information and to ensure a tailored performance. While current baseline labor categories are set at Secret, some Contractor personnel may require an Active/Current DoD JWICs/Top Secret clearance for advanced or future requirements. Specifically, a DoD JWICs Top Secret clearance is required for those personnel designated as admin users of classified network devices. IAW DD 254, DoD Contract Security Classification Specification, the Contractor shall ensure all personnel are cleared and compliant to complete implementation requirements. The Contractor shall be responsible for ensuring compliance with security requirements and that all personnel take the appropriate measures to protect classified information.

1.8. Building and Swipe Access

Contractor personnel requiring on-site access to government facilities at Fort Belvoir will be processed for and provided with appropriate building and swipe access. All personnel must comply with the physical security policies and procedures of the facility at all times.

1.9. Information Assurance and Cybersecurity Training

All contractor personnel performing information assurance (IA) or cybersecurity functions must comply with the requirements outlined in DoD Directive 8140.01 and DoD 8570.01-M. The contractor is responsible for ensuring all employees maintain the required certifications for their respective roles throughout the contract's period of performance.

1.10. Mandatory Government Training

The contractor is responsible for completing all required government-provided training courses. This includes, but is not limited to, Army Cybersecurity Awareness training and Operations Security (OPSEC) training. Proof of completion must be provided as required.

1.11. Contractor Personnel and Supervision

The Contractor shall provide a fully qualified and supervised workforce to accomplish all tasks set forth in this Performance Work Statement (PWS). The Contractor is solely responsible for ensuring all its personnel possess the necessary training, professional certifications, and security clearances required to perform their duties. As this is a non-personal services contract, the Government will not exercise supervision over contractor employees. The Contractor shall provide its own management and supervision for its personnel and ensure they are identified as contractors in all forms of communication.

1.12. Data Rights and Retention

(a) Government Rights in Data and Software: All technical data, computer software, computer software documentation, and other intellectual property developed, delivered, or generated in the performance of this contract shall be subject to the data rights clauses specified herein and, in the Defense, Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS). The Government shall receive, at a minimum, Government Purpose Rights (GPR) to all technical data and computer software developed under this contract. For all deliverables, reports, documentation, and data generated specifically to fulfill the requirements of this Performance Work Statement (PWS), the Government shall have Unlimited Rights, as defined in DFARs 252.227-7013 and 252.227-7014.

(b) Deliverables: All deliverables and work products produced in the execution of this contract shall become the sole property of the U.S. Government. The contractor shall deliver all source code, build scripts, configuration files, and technical documentation created or modified under this contract upon request by the Government or at the conclusion of the period of performance.

(c) Data Retention: The Contractor shall be responsible for the retention of all project data, records, and correspondence generated during the performance of this contract. Such records shall be maintained in a secure and accessible manner for the entire period of performance and for a period of three (3) years following the final payment of this contract, or as otherwise directed by the Contracting Officer, to support Government audit and record-keeping requirements.

1.13. Organizational Conflict of Interest (OCI)

Purpose: The purpose of this clause is to prevent conflicting roles that may bias the Contractor’s judgment and to preclude the Contractor from obtaining an unfair competitive advantage in subsequent acquisitions. The Contractor’s performance of this contract requires access to proprietary and sensitive Government and third-party information and involves providing advice and recommendations that will influence future Army acquisitions.

General: The Contractor shall not have any personal or organizational conflicts of interest, as defined in the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Subpart 9.5. The Contractor shall be ineligible for future Army contracts where the Contractor's involvement in the work under this contract would provide an unfair competitive advantage or result in biased ground rules.

Specific Prohibitions:

Impaired Objectivity: The Contractor is prohibited from providing any services, systems, components, or software in which it or a subsidiary/affiliate has a direct financial interest as part of the ICAM modernization effort. The Contractor shall provide impartial and objective advice and analysis. If the Contractor recommends a product in which it has a financial interest, it must be fully disclosed to the Contracting Officer, and the Government must approve its use in writing.

Unequal Access to Information: The Contractor shall not use any non-public information acquired during the performance of this contract to prepare proposals or bids for any other Government contracts. This includes, but is not limited to, information regarding operational requirements, system vulnerabilities, acquisition strategies, or evaluation criteria.

Biased Ground Rules: The Contractor, its affiliates, or its subcontractors are prohibited from participating as a prime contractor or major subcontractor in any future competitive acquisition for systems or services that are based on the work products, specifications, or recommendations generated under this contract.

Disclosure and Mitigation: The Contractor has a continuing obligation to identify and disclose any potential or actual OCIs to the Contracting Officer immediately upon discovery. The Contractor shall submit a comprehensive OCI Mitigation Plan for Government approval prior to contract award and shall update the plan as new potential conflicts arise. Failure to disclose an OCI or to comply with the approved Mitigation Plan may result in contract termination.

1.14. Contract Transition In/Out

1.14.1. General: The Contractor shall ensure a seamless and transparent transition of responsibilities during both the commencement (Transition-In) and completion (Transition-Out) of this contract to prevent any degradation of service or loss of operational continuity for the Army's ICAM platform.

1.14.2 Transition-In / Phase-In Period:

The first sixty (60) days of the Base Period of Performance are designated as the Transition-In period. During this time, the Contractor shall work closely with the incumbent contractor and Government personnel to conduct a comprehensive knowledge transfer.

The Contractor shall deliver a detailed Transition-In Plan to the Contracting Officer's Representative (COR) within ten (10) days after contract award. This plan shall outline the Contractor's approach, schedule, and milestones for assuming full responsibility for all tasks within this PWS.

The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Office of Information and Technology (OIT), requires support for the National Cemetery Administration's (NCA) Enterprise Interment Services System (EISS) modernization and enterprise data integration effort. The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Office of Information and Technology (OIT) is charged with supporting the National Cemetery Administration (NCA) modernization and enterprise data integration activities associated with the Enterprise Interment Services System (EISS) implementation, data reconciliation, governance, and operational process improvement. EISS supports spatially aware cemetery operations and planning activities that require coordination across NCA, OIT, and Department of War (DoW) stakeholders. The work is intended to improve data quality, strengthen cross-system interoperability, enhance operational efficiency, and support accurate, timely, and standardized information management across participating organizations in line with established OIT and VA products, frameworks and best practices.

These activities will support improved decision-making, reduced manual processing and data redundancy, increased traceability of person-level records, and more effective enterprise governance and oversight of NCA business operations and data assets. The effort will also support improved coordination of burial eligibility, operational planning, cemetery management, and related Veteran services through more integrated business processes, data reconciliation, and enterprise governance capabilities both within NCA and across the VA enterprise. The contractor shall leverage existing VA Office of Data Governance and Analytics DGA enterprise data management tools, standards, and governance processes, with all deliverables designed for compatibility with VA’s Palantir Foundry environment. 

This PWS is intended to extend and apply existing VA DGA enterprise data management, business architecture, data engineering, and governance capabilities to the NCA EISS modernization effort. This effort shall coordinate with existing DGA enterprise data support activities, including data engineering, authoritative data source alignment, enterprise data standards, business architecture artifacts, Enterprise Information Model artifacts, Common Operating Platform capabilities, Palantir/Foundry data object development, and VA Data Governance Council-aligned governance processes. Deliverables produced under this effort shall be designed to be compatible and interoperable with VA's existing Palantir/Foundry environment where data objects, schemas, pipelines, metadata, lineage, dashboards, or analytic workflows are intended for enterprise reuse or integration.

This PWS is not intended to replace or duplicate existing DGA enterprise data engineering, business architecture, governance, or platform support. Rather, it applies those existing enterprise capabilities to the NCA-specific EISS use case, including cemetery operations, burial eligibility, interment scheduling, person-level record reconciliation, EISS MVP configuration, DoW/ANC coordination, and NCA data migration readiness.

BACKGROUND

The U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), National Center for Posttraumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD), Dissemination and Training Division (NCPTSD) is responsible for creating training and educational products to support evidence-based care of Veterans with PTSD and related problems.  PTSD is very common among Veterans and has a significant impact on Veterans’ quality of life.  Most Veterans with PTSD do not access evidence-based treatments for PTSD, and many Veterans are either unable or choose not to access available mental health services of any kind.  Lack of available services, distance from clinics, and stigma associated with mental health care are just a few of the barriers to providing care for Veterans and those living with a Veteran with PTSD.  The rapid transition to telehealth in recent years has also greatly increased the burden on VA providers to offer mobile tools and services to support delivery of evidence-based telehealth.  NCPTSD has developed mobile phone applications (apps) to overcome these and other barriers to care.  The apps are designed to assist Veterans and their family members with understanding PTSD and related problems, tracking their improvement over time, obtaining support and resources, and managing symptoms using a variety of brief relaxation/stress coping tools.

NCPTSD has developed a variety of mobile applications in the past fifteen years, including, most notably, the multi-award winning PTSD Coach (Winner of the Advancements in Accessibility Award from the Federal Communications Commission 2011 and Winner of the President’s Innovation Award from the American Telemedicine Association 2012).  NCPTSD currently maintains a portfolio of 37 mobile apps (e.g., PTSD Coach, Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Insomnia (CBTI) Coach, Mindfulness Coach, Prolonged Exposure therapy (PE) Coach, Stay Quit Coach), that have been downloaded over 5 million Veterans and others.  Each mobile app aims to address specific implementation challenges faced by Veterans and their family members in receiving education, training, and treatment.

In addition to these public-facing apps, NCPTSD also develops and maintains a suite of research applications that support active and ongoing research on the public-facing apps.  These apps currently support over two dozen clinical trials and 463 investigators.  Each of these research apps are kept up-to-date with its corresponding public app and are vital to the development and innovation of evidence-based treatments for PTSD and its symptoms.

The NCPTSD has also been charged with 1) ensuring that NCPTSD mobile apps are capable of supporting scientific research and 2) being capable of responding to the needs of Veterans, VA providers, and other stakeholders.  To meet this charge, NCPTSD has a multi-phase coordinated research program to study the usability, efficacy, and implementation of these applications and works directly with Mental Health Services in VA Central Office to ensure that products are aligned with the mission to enhance and optimize mental health care for Veterans.

GENERAL INFORMATION

PLACE OF PERFORMANCE

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

DESCRIPTION

THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION ANNOUNCEMENT. THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. This Sources Sought Notice is intended for information and planning purposes only at this time; and shall not be construed as a solicitation or as an obligation on the part of the Department of Veterans Affairs. Because this is a Sources Sought announcement, no evaluation letters and/or results will be issued to the respondents. No solicitation exists. Therefore, do not request a copy of a solicitation.

The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), VISN 4, Network Contracting Office 4 (NCO 4), is seeking information and potential qualified sources capable of providing Dell Tower PCs. The equipment will be delivered to the Philadelphia VA Medical Center, located in Philadelphia, PA 19104.

  

  Statement of Need

The CMCVAMC Radiation Oncology Service has a bona-fide need for the procurement of twelve (12) Dell Pro Tower computers, brand name only, with twelve (12) accompanying Dell 24 Monitor Plus (P2425H GOV) displays. The Radiation Oncology Department currently relies on Varian Eclipse software for patient treatment planning and Varian Aria software to record, verify, document, schedule, and track patient treatments, as well as to communicate patient information throughout the department.

The department is currently running Varian Aria version 13.1, which is now obsolete and unsupported by the vendor. The department is required to upgrade to Varian Aria version 18 within the next year. This upgrade carries increased hardware requirements that the department's current computer fleet cannot support, and there is an immediate need for additional computers capable of running the Aria v18 platform at the performance level required for safe, timely clinical operation.

Aria v18 requires Windows 11 Personal Computers with the processing power, memory, and graphics capability to load and render high-resolution diagnostic images, treatment plans, and patient records rapidly and reliably. These computers will be used department-wide by nursing staff, therapists, dosimetrists, medical physicists, and physicians at every stage of the patient treatment workflow.

The Aria/Eclipse software suite cannot be deployed on standard VA administrative computers because those systems are governed by privacy and information-security configurations that are incompatible with the application's handling of Protected Health Information (PHI), Personally Identifiable Information (PII), and Sensitive Information (SI). Consequently, the department requires a dedicated set of high-specification clinical workstations separate from the general VA administrative computing environment.

Currently, eighteen (18) personnel in the department share four (4) Aria-capable computers to perform the full range of tasks directly tied to patient care. This severe shortage of compatible workstations is actively slowing clinical workflow and creating a documented patient safety concern, as staff must wait for terminal access to review images, verify treatment plans, and document care during active treatment sessions.

Salient Characteristics of the Twelve (12) Dell Pro Tower Computers: 

The following salient characteristics define the minimum acceptable technical configuration for each of the twelve (12) towers and are required to support the Aria v18 imaging and processing workload:

Processor: Intel Core Ultra 9 285 (24 cores, up to 5.6 GHz, 13 TOPS NPU), labeled Intel Core Ultra 9

Operating System: Windows 11 Pro, plus support upgrade license

Productivity Software: Microsoft Office Home and Business 2024 license; Adobe Acrobat Pro for Teams subscription

Memory: 64 GB (2 x 32 GB), DDR5, up to 5600 MT/s, non-ECC

Storage: M.2 512 GB PCIe NVMe Class 35 Solid State Drive, with M.2 caddy hard drive cables and brackets

Graphics: AMD Radeon RX 7400, 8 GB GDDR6, full height, 4x Mini DisplayPort to DisplayPort

Optical Drive: 8x DVD+/-RW 9.5mm Slimline ODD

Power Cord: System power cord configured for United States standard outlets

Security: Trusted Platform Module (TPM)

Audio: Internal speakers

Certification: ENERGY STAR qualified; unit registered (Silver tier)

Documentation: Safety, Environmental, and Regulatory guide (English) and Quick Start Guide included with each unit

Display: One (1) Dell 24 Monitor Plus — P2425H GOV per unit (twelve (12) total)

 Scope of Work

The Contractor shall provide the CMCVAMC Radiation Oncology Department with the following supplies and associated services:

The Contractor shall provide a quantity of twelve (12) Dell Pro Tower computers meeting or exceeding the salient characteristics specified above.

The Contractor shall provide a quantity of twelve (12) Dell 24 Monitor Plus (P2425H GOV) displays, one per tower unit.

The Contractor shall ensure all units are new, unused, and the current production model offered by Dell at the time of order, with manufacturer warranty coverage intact.

The Contractor shall deliver all units to the CMCVAMC Radiation Oncology Department loading dock/receiving to the designated point of contact.

 Schedule for Deliverables

If, for any reason, the scheduled delivery date cannot be met, the Contractor is required to notify the point of contact (POC) and Contracting Officer (CO) in writing, explaining the reason for the delay.  

Responses to this RFI should include company name, address, point of contact, phone number, and point of contact e-mail, DUNS Number, Cage Code, size of business pursuant to North American Industry Classification code (NAICS) 541519, Other Computer Related Services. The Small Business Size Standard for this NAICS code is $34,000,000.00.

General pricing of your products/solution is encouraged. Pricing will be used for the purpose of market research only. It will not be used to evaluate for any type of award.

This Sources Sought Notice will be conducted in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 13. Telephone responses will not be accepted. Responses must be received via e-mail to mcdaniel.brayboy@va.gov no later than, 1:00 PM Eastern Standard Time (EST) on July 28, 2026. This notice will help the VA in determining available potential sources only. Do not contact VA Medical Center staff regarding this requirement, as they are not authorized to discuss this matter related to this procurement action. All questions will be addressed by the Contract Specialist, McDaniel Brayboy III.

All firms responding to this Sources Sought Notice are advised that their response is not a request for proposal, therefore will not be considered for a contract award.

If a solicitation is issued, information will be posted on the Contract Opportunities website for all qualified interested parties at a later date, and interested parties must respond to the solicitation to be considered for award. This notice does not commit the government to contract for any supplies or services. The government will not pay for any information or administrative cost incurred in response to this Source Sought Notice. Information will only be accepted in writing by e-mail to Contract Specialist, McDaniel Brayboy III at mcdaniel.brayboy@va.gov

1.  Contracting Agency and Activity. The Department of the Interior, United States Geological 
Survey. 
 
2.  Nature of Action Being Approved. A new contract for Wave Glider piloting services 
provided by Liquid Robotics. 
 
3.  Description of Supplies or Services.  The Earthquake Science Center requires piloting 
services to assist with the operation of the ESC Wave Glider during the collection of seafloor 
geodetic data.  
 
4.  Estimated Dollar Value. cluding Base and One Option Year. 
 
5.  Statutory Authority.  The proposed action may be awarded on a sole source basis under the 
authority of RFO FAR 12.102(a) - For acquisitions valued at or below the simplified acquisition 
threshold (SAT), document the decision that only one source is available and the basis for the 
decision. 
 
6.  Rationale Supporting Use of Citation in No. 5.  Liquid Robotics developer of the wave 
glider and the Wave Glider Management System used for management and operation of wave 
gliders.  Liquid Robotics provides piloting services, and their pilots are uniquely qualified and 
experienced in the operation of wave gliders and have access to and understanding of features 
and function of the WGMS that are proprietary to Liquid Robotics.  
 
7.  Other Information.  N/A 
 
8.  The Efforts to Identify Additional Sources Including the Market Research Conducted. 
Market research includes conducting internet searches for wave glider pilot services all result in 
Liquid Robotics, as well as posting Sources Sought 140G0326Q0158 to SAM.gov for four days. 
Information gathering was conducted among colleagues in similar scientific fields of study and 
Liquid Robotics is the only vendor that is being used to provide pilot services for the wave 
glider.  
9.  Future Plans to Permit Competition.  Any future requirements undergo market research 
and will be competed at the maximum extent practicable,

STATEMENT OF NEED

Description of Work:
The USGS Central Energy Resources Science Center’s Microscope laboratory has a need to modify the current data parser 
VBA code to accommodate changes to the Point Count instrument report.
Requested modifications for parser, CU8552_Point_Count_Parser, or create new parser, due to changes to the instrument 
output file format.
The Point Count instrument output file has had substantial changes to the format, which requires the 
CU8552_Point_Count_Parser to be modified or completely redone.  The columns that originally contained the results for 
multiple samples have been transposed and the output file will contain results for a single sample instead of multiple samples.  
The report to parse will be on a single worksheet. The parser should provide the option (setting) to create a single parsed file 
for each file in the designated folder, or loop through all files in a single folder and create a single file containing the 
combined data from all report files.
<Test> “Point Count” – Sample Master Test field.  Test will be set statically in the Settings worksheet.  
Below is a list of the cells to capture and the Sample Master field they map to.
Data worksheet:
Cell B1 – LIMS ID: Sample Master SampleNumber. 
Cell B2 – Sample ID: Result value for parameter named Sample Identifier. (Sample Master Result field)  
Ex: Sample ID: 70.4-70.6 
      Parameter is Sample Identifier 
      Result is 70.4-70.6  Result field
Cell B4 – Date Analyzed: Sample Master TestDate field (no time captured) 
Cell B5 – Analyst: Sample Master AnalysisEmployee field.  
Cell B6 – Objective: Sample Master Instrument field.
Ex: Objective: 50x/1.0 Oil Pol
                Instrument is 50x/1.0 Oil Pol
Cell B7 – Light Sources: Result value for the parameter named Light Sources. (Sample Master Result field)
Cell A9 – Mineral-Inclusive or Exclusive: Result value for the parameter named Mineral-Inclusive_Exclusive. (Sample 
Master Result field)

1.1 Background 
Mass spectrometry (MS) is the gold standard for chemical characterization. As such, DBCMS has many 
MS instruments from various manufacturers. Each manufacturer produces proprietary software to analyze 
the MS data originating from their instruments. Compound Discoverer is Thermo Fisher’s proprietary 
software for MS data. Each software purchase includes one license which means it can be used on only 
one computer. With multiple DBCMS projects using Thermo Fisher instruments, there is a high demand 
to process data from multiple projects simultaneously. Therefore, an additional license for Compound 
Discoverer is needed. 
Compound Discoverer converts the raw data from Thermo Fisher MS instruments (“.raw”) into 
qualitative and quantitative information- peaks and intensities, respectively. Thousands of peaks and 
intensities are common for each sample, so statistical capabilities are inherent requirements for this 
software. The combined features of data processing and statistical analysis allow our users to produce 
publication-quality graphs and figures for use by industry and regulators. 
 


1.2 Objective 
Compound Discoverer is a mass spectrometry data processing and statistical software for data produced 
from Thermo Fisher analytical instruments. Our division (DBCMS) uses several Thermo Fisher 
instruments which equate to many group members needing access to this software to process their data to 
meet various project goals and objectives.

1.4 Technical Requirements 
The contractor must: 
• Identify compounds through multiple automatic databases and spectral library search tools. 
• Access mzCloud libraries and utilize both DIA and DDA scans for searching. 
• Determine elemental composition using high-resolution fine isotopes and MS/MS data. 

• Workflows are modular and assembled from a suite of advanced algorithms (nodes). 
• Workflow templates are customizable for different applications and included with the software. 
• Workflows can be enhanced with custom nodes. 
• Analyze biological pathways with high- quality data processing and statistical analysis —support 
for stable isotope labeling workflows to analyze differences in samples 
• Find real differences between sample sets with heat-map-like tables, interactive PCA, partial least 
squares discriminant analysis (PLS-DA), etc. 
• Visualize spectral trees along with fragmentation annotations and mzLogic algorithm for ranking 
chemical database hits using spectral library similarities for structural elucidation. 
Required features, capabilities, or performance parameters 
• Must be able to search spectral databases to identify compounds. 
• Must be able to acquire data both dependently and independently. 
• Must be able to determine molecular formula using high- resolution, fragmentation, and isotopic 
patterns. 
• Must have a customizable workflow using nodes. 
• Must be able to perform a differential analysis using various statistical tools. 
• Must be able to rank the possible matches from databases according to fragmentation and structural 
similarity. 
Applicable industry standards or certifications 
• Includes quality control features in compliance with good laboratory practices (GLPs) and good 
clinical practices (GCPs).

2.2 Contracting Officer’s Authority 
 
The Contracting Officer (CO) is the only person with authority to act as agent of the Government under 
this contract. Only the Contracting Officer has authority to: (1) direct or negotiate any changes in the RFQ; 
(2) modify or extend the period of performance; (3) change the delivery schedule; (4) authorize

anyone other than the Contracting Officer, shall be interpreted as modifying the terms and conditions of 
this award. It is the Contractor’s responsibility to contact the CO immediately if there is even the 
appearance of any technical direction that is or may be outside the scope of the award. The Government 
will not reimburse the Contractor for any work not authorized by the Contracting Officer, including work 
outside the scope of the award.  
 
The Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR) is responsible for: (1) monitoring the Contractor's

problems encountered during performance.

modify or otherwise affect the terms and conditions of this contract. Requests for interpretations, 
modifications or changes must be made in writing to the CO. The technical point of contact can only 
respond to technical matters that do not result in a change of scope to this contract. 
2.4 Security and Privacy 
A. Baseline Security Requirements 
 
1) Applicability. The requirements herein apply whether the entire contract or order (hereafter 
“contract”), or portion thereof, includes either or both of the following: 
 

a. Access (Physical or Logical) to Government Information:  A Contractor (and/or any
