or logical (electronic) access to government information. 
 
b. Operate a Federal System Containing Information:  A Contractor (and/or any subcontractor) 
will operate a federal system and information technology containing data that supports the 
HHS mission. In addition to the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Subpart 2.1 definition 
of “information technology” (IT), the term as used in this section includes computers, ancillary 
equipment (including imaging peripherals, input, output, and storage devices necessary for 
security and surveillance), peripheral equipment designed to be controlled by the central 
processing unit of a computer, software, firmware and similar procedures, services (including 
support services), and related resources. 
 
2) Safeguarding Information and Information Systems.  In accordance with the Federal 
Information Processing Standards Publication (FIPS)199, Standards for Security Categorization 
of Federal Information and Information Systems, the Contractor (and/or any subcontractor) shall: 
a. Protect government information and information systems in order to ensure: 
• Confidentiality, which means preserving authorized restrictions on access and disclosure, 
based on the security terms found in this contract, including means for protecting personal 
privacy and proprietary information; 
• Integrity, which means guarding against improper information modification or destruction, 
and ensuring information non-repudiation and authenticity; and 
• Availability, which means ensuring timely and reliable access to and use of information. 
b. Provide security for any Contractor systems, and information contained therein, connected to an 
FDA network or operated by the Contractor on behalf of FDA regardless of location.  In 
addition, if new or unanticipated threats or hazards are discovered by ei ther the agency or 
contractor, or if existing safeguards have ceased to function, the discoverer shall immediately, 
within one (1) hour or less, bring the situation to the attention of the other party.  This includes 
notifying the FDA Systems Management  Center (SMC) within one (1) hour of 
discovery/detection in the event of an information security incident. 
c. Adopt and implement the policies, procedures, controls, and standards required by the 
HHS/FDA Information Security Program to ensure the confidentiality, integrity, and availability 
of government information and government information systems for which the Contractor is 
responsible under this contract or to which the Contractor may otherwise have access under this

STATEMENT OF WORK

Title: WEB-BASED TRAINING DEVELOPMENT 

1. Background 

Post traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and substance use disorders /(SUD) are two of the most common and debilitating mental health disorders among service members and Veterans, and they often co-occur. Approximately 30-60% of individuals with PTSD also meet criteria for SUD. The need to advance knowledge and promote increased access to and availability of effective treatments for co-occurring PTSD/SUD is a national health care priority. The Clinical Practice Guidelines (CPG) put forth by the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) and the Department of Defense (DoD) recommend trauma-focused, integrated treatment in which both PTSD and SUD are addressed. However, few providers have been trained in this approach. The proposed project is designed to directly address this critical gap in provider education and training to improve the healthcare of Veterans with PTSD/SUD. 

Concurrent Treatment of PTSD and Substance Use Disorders Using Prolonged Exposure (COPE) is a 12-session, individual, manualized, trauma-focused treatment that integrates two theory-driven and empirically supported interventions: Prolonged Exposure (PE) for PTSD and Relapse Prevention (RP) for alcohol and drug use disorders. Randomized controlled trials demonstrate the efficacy of COPE in significantly reducing PTSD, substance use, and associated features (e.g., depression, trauma-related guilt) among Veterans and civilians. Moreover, most Veterans with PTSD/SUD prefer an integrated treatment approach7. Despite the strong evidence base supporting the efficacy of COPE, few VA providers have been trained in COPE. Recent data show that 96% of PTSD/SUD Specialists in the VA healthcare system (N=130) are interested in obtaining COPE training, and 99.1% would use a web-based COPE provider training if available. Given the significant financial and emotional burden that PTSD/SUD places on Veterans, their families, and the VA healthcare system, novel efforts to effectively and efficiently train providers to treat co-occurring PTSD/SUD are warranted. 

This proposal will (1) develop an innovative, web-based training for providers (COPEWeb) to strengthen providers’ capacity to deliver COPE to Veterans with co-occurring PTSD/SUD, and (2) compare the effects of the COPEWeb training versus in-person training on (a) knowledge acquisition, (b) provider satisfaction, and (c) fidelity (behavior). The proposed web-based training will address limitations of conventional in-person workshops (e.g., time, travel costs) and extend training to providers working in rural VA-affiliated community-based outpatient clinics (CBOCs) where opportunities may be less accessible.

The COPEWeb content will be based on the 12 sessions of the COPE intervention (plus three additional support modules) that contain the following efficacious components: introduction to content, psychoeducation about the interrelationship between PTSD and SUD, in vivo and imaginal exposure, and relapse prevention skills (e.g., managing cravings, drink refusal skills), telehealth considerations. Each module of COPEWeb will include: (a) video introductions to the technique, (b) an overview of the module's learning objectives, (c) a description of each technique and step-by-step instructions for how to implement them, including sample scripts for introducing the techniques to patients, (d) multiple video demonstrations of the techniques being properly implemented (including telehealth implementation), (e) example homework assignments, (f) discussion of common clinical challenges that may arise in practice, (g) directions for including family members in relevant therapeutic activities, and (h) graded pre- and post-tests to assess prior knowledge and information learned from the module (i) digital and graphic design enhancements, (j) interactive learning activities and (j) additional training recordings with audio and video. Technology tools (e.g., VA- and DoD-developed PE Coach app) will be integrated into the training. The website will function across operating systems, web browsers, and devices (e.g., computers, tablets) to be deployable in any setting (e.g., home, office). Text-based material will be minimized, and video demonstrations and interactive features will ensure the site is highly engaging. 

2. Objectives 

a. Develop a web-based provider training platform (i.e., COPEWeb). The following modules will be included in the platform: 

b. Test and validate COPEWeb

c. Add digital and graphic enhancements, interactive learning activities and additional filming and voiceover recordings. 

d. Provide real-time support during the ongoing use of COPEWeb during the comparison trial (i.e., randomized controlled trial of COPEWeb compared to in-person COPE training)

3. Scope 

Develop and support COPEWeb, as detailed within the above-mentioned objectives. COPEWeb will need to be fully operational by January 1, 2027. Real-time support of COPEWeb will be needed for two years.

2. Description of supplies or services required to meet agency needs (including the estimated
value). This software is needed to operate Fourier transform near infrared spectrometers to scan
otoliths to predict ages for use in stock assessment in support of MSA requirements. The current
software is no longer supported for Windows 11, thus we must upgrade to maintain IT compliance
and continue instrument operation.
3. Identification of the single source or the brand name to be solicited. Bruker Corporation, 40
Manning Road, Manning Park, Billerica, MA 01821, USA, +1 (978) 439-9899 or +1 (978) 663-3660
4. Supporting rationale. Only one source or brand name is reasonably available as detailed below:
Ɛ Compatibility to existing systems or equipment - The procurement of this Bruker OPUS
software upgrade is functionally mandatory to ensure seamless compatibility with our
existing laboratory infrastructure. Because it is a direct upgrade from our current, older
version to the newer version within the same software ecosystem, it integrates perfectly with
our established hardware. Any alternative, third-party software is entirely incompatible and
will not work with our instruments. Utilizing this specific upgrade protects the integrity of our
historical data and prevents critical operational failures, allowing our fish age production
workflows to continue without disruption.
Ɛ Other - Only one source is capable - This procurement qualifies as a sole source acquisition
because Bruker is the proprietary developer and exclusive vendor of the OPUS software. No
other external vendor, manufacturer, or third-party distributor sells, licenses, or supports this
specific platform. Because our laboratory requires this exact software to interface with our
current instrumentation for fish age production, no alternative product or vendor can fulfill
this operational requirement.
5. Market Research.
Our market research has been unable to find any other company/vendor that sells the OPUS
software.

GENERAL INFORMATION

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

DESCRIPTION

The Department of Veterans Affairs, Network Contracting Office (NCO) 6 intends to award a sole source purchase order to Varian Medical Systems for the provision of software support and maintenance services for high-cost, high-tech Radiation Oncology equipment at the Durham VA Medical Center, Material Management.

This requirement covers support and maintenance for TrueBeam linear accelerators, the ARIA Radiation Oncology Information System, and the Eclipse Treatment Planning System. Services include software maintenance, upgrades, inspections, and training to ensure optimal functionality, minimize downtime, and maintain state-of-the-art clinical operations.

Varian’s FullScale on Premise (FSoP), Clinac, TrueBeam, Halcyon Delivery System products, and ARIA, Eclipse, and Velocity products are proprietary and utilize Varian’s unique software and remote diagnostic-support tools (SmartConnect) that meet VA cyber-security, PHI, and MOU/ISA requirements. Only Varian can provide and install software upgrades, firmware patches, customized system components, and utilize proprietary technician training and procedures. All technical support, escalations, repairs, parts replacement, and training are handled exclusively by Varian-certified employees. No third parties are trained, sanctioned, or permitted to perform maintenance, and support contracts may be terminated if non-Varian parts or services are used. The loss of vendor support after September 30, 2025, would critically impact patient care and clinical outcomes.

The period of performance will be one base year and 4 option years. The justification for this sole source procurement is in accordance with FAR 12.102, soliciting from a single source, due to proprietary technology, exclusive capabilities, and compatibility requirements with existing clinical infrastructure.

This notice of intent is not a request for competitive quotations. No solicitation documents are available and telephone requests will not be accepted. However, any business that believes it can meet this requirement may submit a written response with sufficient evidence to demonstrate capability to provide the required services and all proprietary maintenance features described above. Responses received by 10:00 am EST on July 15, 2026, will be considered by the Government, though a decision not to compete the proposed acquisition is solely at the Government’s discretion.

NAICS Code: 518210 – Data Processing, Hosting, and Related Services. PSC: J065 – Maintenance, Repair, and Rebuilding of Equipment: Medical, Dental, and Veterinary Instruments/Equipment. All inquiries and responses must be emailed to Ricard.McIntosh@va.gov. No telephone requests will be accepted.

Statement of Work
SCOPE: Network Equipment 
1 
1. Introduction
The Indian Health Service (IHS) is responsible for providing federal health services to American 
Indians and Alaska Natives. In support of the agency mission, IHS uses secure Information 
Technology (IT) to improve health care quality, enhance access to care, reduce medical errors 
and modernize administrative functions consistent with the Department of Health and Human 
Services (HHS) enterprise IT initiatives.  
2. Objective
The objective of this acquisition is to acquire new network equipment to replace older devices 
that are more than 5 years old. The new network devices must integrate and coexist with existing 
network equipment within the agency IT network.   
3. Scope
The scope of this acquisition is to acquire the following equipment. 
• Network routers and software licenses
• Wireless controllers, access points and software licenses
4. Bill of Materials
The list of required network equipment is specified in Attachment 1 – Network Equipment - 
Bill of Materials.  It includes vendor part numbers with the software versions current at the time 
of creation. In some cases, the software version number is embedded in the part number. In the 
event the software versions have been updated by the vendor since the Bill of Materials was 
created, the new software part numbers should be included in the Offeror’s respond.  
5. Equipment Condition
The following requirements apply to network equipment acquired through this acquisition. 
• Only Cisco certified original and new equipment should be quoted.
• No grey market equipment should be quoted.
• All optics and cables must be Cisco certified original and new.
• No third party or compatible optics and cables should be quoted.
• Only Cisco provided maintenance coverage should be quoted.
6. Authorized Reseller

2 
 
Offerors must provide information confirming they are authorized Cisco equipment resellers.    
7. Maintenance and Subscription Start Date 
 
The Cisco product configurator allows the selection of a Service Start Date for maintenance 
coverage and subscription services. IHS requires the Service Start Date to align with the 
projected equipment delivery date published on the Cisco Commerce Workspace (CCW) portal. 
After the contract is awarded, the contractor will contact the IHS Project Officer to select the 
service and subscription start date for each applicable item. 
8. Equipment Delivery 
 
The equipment shall be delivered to IHS locations specified in the Bill of Materials. The vendor 
shall assign a project manager to work with the IHS Project Officer to schedule equipment 
deliveries.  The vendor’s project manager shall schedule biweekly meetings with the IHS Project 
Officer to provide updates on equipment delivery dates. 
 
Software licenses and subscriptions acquired through this acquisition shall be electronically 
delivered via email or assigned to the IHS Smart virtual account IHS-HQ-OIT on the Cisco 
portal. After contract award and prior to invoice submission, the contractor shall provide

virtual account IHS-HQ-OIT on the Cisco portal.

☐52.225-8 Duty-Free Entry (OCT 2010) 
 
(a) Definition. "Customs territory of the United States" means the States, the District of Columbia, and Puerto 
Rico. 
 
(b) Except as otherwise approved by the Contracting Officer, the Contractor shall not include in the contract 
price any amount for duties on supplies specifically identified in the Schedule to be accorded duty-free entry. 
 
(c) Except as provided in paragraph (d) of this clause or elsewhere in this contract, the following procedures 
apply to supplies not identified in the Schedule to be accorded duty-free entry: 
 
(1) The Contractor shall notify the Contracting Officer in writing of any purchase of foreign supplies 
(including, without limitation, raw materials, components, and intermediate assemblies) in excess of 
$20,000 that are to be imported into the customs territory of the United States for delivery to the 
Government under this contract, either as end products or for incorporation into end products. The 
Contractor shall furnish the notice to the Contracting Officer at least 20 calendar days before the 
importation. The notice shall identify the- 
 
(i) Foreign supplies; 
(ii) Estimated amount of duty; and 
(iii) Country of origin. 

6   V12 APR 2026 
 
 
(2) The Contracting Officer will determine whether any of these supplies should be accorded duty-free 
entry and will notify the Contractor within 10 calendar days after receipt of the Contractor’s notification. 
 
(3) Except as otherwise approved by the Contracting Officer, the contract price shall be reduced by (or 
the allowable cost shall not include) the amount of duty that would be payable if the supplies were not 
entered duty-free. 
 
(d) The Contractor is not required to provide the notification under paragraph (c) of this clause for purchases of 
foreign supplies if- 
 
(1) The supplies are identical in nature to items purchased by the Contractor or any subcontractor in 
connection with its commercial business; and 
 
(2) Segregation of these supplies to ensure use only on Government contracts containing duty-free entry 
provisions is not economical or feasible. 
 
(e) The Contractor shall claim duty-free entry only for supplies to be delivered to the Government under this 
contract, either as end products or incorporated into end products, and shall pay duty on supplies, or any portion 
of them, other than scrap, salvage, or competitive sale authorized by the Contracting Officer, diverted to 
nongovernmental use. 
 
(f) The Government will execute any required duty-free entry certificates for supplies to be accorded duty-free 
entry and will assist the Contractor in obtaining duty-free entry for these supplies. 
 
(g) Shipping documents for supplies to be accorded duty-free entry shall consign the shipments to the 
contracting agency in care of the Contractor and shall include the- 
 
(1) Delivery address of the Contractor (or contracting agency, if appropriate); 
 
(2) Government prime contract number; 
 
(3) Identification of carrier;

Customs Forms 7501 and 7501-A and any required duty-free entry certificates."; 
 
(5) Gross weight in pounds (if freight is based on space tonnage, state cubic feet in addition to gross 
shipping weight); and 
 
(6) Estimated value in United States dollars. 
 
(h) The Contractor shall instruct the foreign supplier to-

contracting agency; and

use by the District Director of Customs at the port of entry. 
 
(i) The Contractor shall provide written notice to the cognizant contract administration office immediately after 
notification by the Contracting Officer that duty-free entry will be accorded foreign supplies or, for duty-free 
supplies identified in the Schedule, upon award by the Contractor to the overseas supplier. The notice shall 
identify the- 
 
(1) Foreign supplies; 
 
(2) Country of origin; 
 
(3) Contract number; and 
 
(4) Scheduled delivery date(s). 
 
(j) The Contractor shall include the substance of this clause in any subcontract if- 
 
(1) Supplies identified in the Schedule to be accorded duty-free entry will be imported into the customs 
territory of the United States; or 
 
(2) Other foreign supplies in excess of $20,000 may be imported into the customs territory of the United

cannot perform a BPA call that is unilaterally issued, the BPA holder shall promptly notify the CO or the card holder of the issue(s)
and provide the reasons the call cannot be performed. The BPA holder shall refund or cancel any purchase card order that cannot be
performed, if applicable.
 
BPA Calls will be places by purchase card holders or Contracting Officers from the judiciary organizations detailed Volume 14,
Chapter 1, §110.40 Applicability in the Guide to Judiciary Policy (Guide) as well as Organizations listed under Guide to Judiciary
Policy, Vol. 1, Chapter 13, § 1320 Courts Outside the Third Branch as listed in Attachment J.1 SOW Section C.5.8 Ordering.
 
Discounts will be posted on an AO Intranet Site that may be potentially accessible to judiciary contractor staff. If the BPA holder
does not want their discounts posted on the judiciary's intranet site than they must communicate that to the CO and the COR after
award and provide a plan for efficiently providing judiciary staff with the discount information. The judiciary will not compensate the
conttractor for any additional effort needed to provide this information to the judiciary organizations that request it. 
 
3. ORDERING CONSIDERATIONS AND LIMITATIONS
Orders maybe placed anytime within the BPA's ordering periods. If order is established properly, the period of performance may go
beyond the BPA's ordering periods expiration date.
 
Judiciary organizations placing call orders against this BPA shall comply with all applicable policy and regulations related to
procurement of learning and development/training services applicable to their organization. Please see the Guide to Judiciary Policy,
Volume 12, Chapter 11 or AO Manual Volume 4, Chapter 7. This also includes consideration on how the training is related to an
employee(s) duties and responsibilities and any limitation on the funds being used for the order. 
 
4.  BPA OBLIGATION
 
4.1.  Extent of Obligation
4.1.1.  The Government estimates, but does not guarantee, that the volume of purchases through this BPA will be $3,150,000.00.
4.1.2  The Government is obligated only to the extent of authorized purchases actually made under this BPA via BPA Calls and
purchase card orders.
 
4.2.  Funds Obligation
This BPA does not obligate any funds. Funds will only be obligated on BPA Calls and purchase card orders.
 
5.  AUTHORIZED USERS
BPA Calls will be places by purchase card holders or Contracting Officers from the judiciary organizations detailed Volume 14,
Chapter 1, §110.40 Applicability in the Guide to Judiciary Policy (Guide) as well as Organizations listed under Guide to Judiciary
Policy, Vol. 1, Chapter 13, § 1320 Courts Outside the Third Branch as listed in Attachment J.1 SOW Section C.5.8 Ordering.
 
6. BPA CALL ORDERING PROCEDURES
 
6.1  BPA Calls will be solicited in accordance with Vol 14 § 325.50.30 (Open Market Single Award BPA) through Vol 14 § 325.50.40
(a) (Ordering Under BPAs).
 
6.2  The BPA holder shall not respond to solicitations from non-authorized users.
 
7. SCOPE OF BPA CALLS
All BPA Calls must fall under the product categories as laid out in the BPA SOW, see Attachment J.1.

HYDROLOGICAL DATABASE (HDB) SUPPORT SERVICES IDIQ 
DRAFT PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT 
1. SCOPE:
1.1. OBJECTIVE: 
The objective of this performance -based contract is to maintain , support, and  further 
develop the Bureau of Reclamation's Hydrological Database (HDB) through the Contractor's 
provision of services for on -call technical support, troubleshooting of HDB malfunctions, 
development of modifications to HDB, support of HDB enhancements, and the 
development, documentation, and distribution of software applications that interface with 
HDB. 
1.2. BACKGROUND: 
HDB is currently used in production in the Upper Colorado Basin Region, in all four of its 
area offices, in the Lower Colorado Basin Region in the Boulder Canyon Operations Area 
and Yuma Area Offices, in the Missouri Basin and Arkansas-Rio Grande-Texas Gulf Region in 
the Eastern Colorado Area Office, in the California Great Basin Region in the Lahontan Basin 
Area Office and  in the Klamath Basin Area Office. Each of these offices support separate 
instances of HDB for the collection and storage of vital hydrological data within their 
operational jurisdiction to aid in decision support and reporting for Reclamation facilities 
managed within each of these offices.  
The HDB system is a critical decision support tool for day-to-day operations of many of 
Reclamation’s major water storage and distribution facilities throughout the Western 
United States.  HDB is critical for enabling and supporting ongoing modeling activities that 
include (but are not limited to) basin inflow forecasting, National Environmental Policy Act 
(NEPA) and Endangered Species Act (ESA) compliance processes, long- and mid-term 
modeling and planning efforts, and day-to-day operational control and management. HDB 

2 
 
is also utilized to support Reclamation’s website and other publicly available data portals 
such as Reclamation Information Sharing Environment (RISE), and public and internal 
Application Programming Interfaces (APIs).  
 
The HDB is the foundation for Reclamation's Database of Record. As conceptualized by the 
Database of Record defining document, the driving vision for the Hydrologic Database is 
to:   
 
• Consolidate data previously existing in various systems and personal spreadsheets. 
• Assure complete and consistent data collection and storage; documentation of data 
sources. 
• Provide historical information on other existing HDB data versions including 
information on when the data was either used or available for use. 
• Perform as a means of quality control. 
• Allow the user access, at any time interval, to the original source data for calculated 
or summarized data 
• Provide for an automated generation of time-aggregated summary data as well as 
automated computations that compute data parameters based on collected inputs. 
 
Reclamation managers are often interrogated formally or informally regarding the basis for 
operational decisions - decisions that are usually based on data such as forecasts, flows, 
available water supply and downstream water and/or energy demands. Reasonable 
explanation of decisions requires maintaining the exact data considered in the decision and 
being able to reproduce the overall state of the system and retrieve forecast information 
available at the time the decision was made. Enhanced capability to document the basis for 
the past decisions is urgently needed to assist Reclamation's defense in litigation and other 
processes.  
 
Development of the database of record will facilitate Reclamation's continued ability to rely 
on and interpret their data in order to make sound operational decisions, provide an 
indisputable record of data used to make past decisions, and provide a complete record of 

3 
 
best available historical and forecast data for research proposed and policy development. 
 
The HDB system is comprised of the Oracle based HDB databases combined with a collection 
of software applications (computer programs) that are set up to automatically collect and 
store a variety of operational and hydrologic data from various data sources. Software 
applications within the system also allow operational staff to access the data for quality 
control as well as hydrologic modeling studies, water accounting efforts, and day-to-day 
operations and modeling of dams, reservoirs and related assets and features. Some of these 
software applications collect and store data in HDB while others allow data to be retrieved 
from HDB and displayed in ways that assist operations staff and the public to interpret the 
state of the hydrologic system. 
 
2. REFERENCES: 
 
2.1. Hydrological Database - Bureau of Reclamation  
http://hydrodb.net 
 
2.2. National Environmental Policy Act  
http://www.epa.gov/nepa 
 
2.3. Endangered Species Action  
https://www.law.cornell.edu/wex/endangered_species_act_(esa) 
 
3. DEFINITIONS: 
 
3.1. Qualified Contractor Personnel : means those Contractor employees directly performing 
work under this contract who collectively possess and maintain all of the following skills, 
capabilities, and knowledge to provide a high -quality level of technical support services . 
Individual personnel assigned to specific tasks must have the relevant qualifications for 
those tasks ; however,  the full set of qualifications may be met and maintained by the 
contractor’s team as a whole  throughout the life of the contract . These qualifications 

4 
 
include: 
 
3.1.1. High level of knowledge with regard to the HDB database structure, including 
database relationships in HDB, including DECODES and the Computational 
Processor. 
3.1.2. Full understanding of the HDB objectives with respect to time-series data 
management including, but not limited to: computation management, interval 
data consistency, model data management, validation and quality assurance, etc. 
3.1.3. Expert-level proficiency in Oracle database Operations and Maintenance and 
programming, as well as other computer programming languages such as JAVA, C, 
python, C#, Perl, and VB.net. 
3.1.4. Ability to develop and support internal and external tools to access and modify 
data through API and specialized software tools.  
3.1.5. Demonstrated ability to develop or support tools in full compliance with federal 
cybersecurity standards, including adherence to Software Development Life Cycle 
(SDLC) and Secure Software Development Framework (SSDF) practices, and 
working knowledge of NIST and FISMA requirements. 
3.1.6. Ability to adapt to emerging technologies and evolving technical requirements 
over the life of the contract, including acquiring and applying new programming 
languages, database platforms, data visualization tools, and cybersecurity 
protocols.  
3.1.7. Maintenance of certifications and training necessary to support future IT systems 
and hydrological data management technologies relevant to HDB operations. 
 
3.2. Call: refers to any request for technical assistance or support initiated by Reclamation 
personnel through approved communication channels. This includes phone calls, emails, 
instant messages, and submissions through the designated online issue -reporting tool. A 
call may involve routine inquiries, troubleshooting requests, or urgent issues requiring 
immediate attention. 
 
3.3. Urgent Call:  means any request for technical assistance that involves system outages, 

5 
 
critical data loss, cybersecurity incidents, or issues that significantly impact operational 
decision-making. Note: While the Minimum Acceptable Quality Level for urgent calls is two 
(2) hours, the Contractor shall make every reasonable effort to immediately engage in 
resolving urgent issues upon receiving the call.  Reclamation will flag any urgent calls , 
messages, or submissions as “urgent”. 
 
3.4. Responded Call: A call is considered responded to when the Contractor initiates direct 
engagement with the original caller and begins steps toward resolving the reported issue 
or inquiry. 
 
3.5. Task Order: means a written order issued by the Contracting Officer under this IDIQ contract 
that authorizes specific work, deliverables, and performance requirements. 
 
4. HOURS OF AVAILABILITY: 
 
Reclamation’s normal operating hours are 8:00 a.m. –5:00 p.m.,  Monday through Friday, Mountain 
Standard Time, excluding Federal Holidays. The Contractor shall be available to provide on-call support 
during these hours as specified in this Performance Work Statement. For urgent matters, Reclamation 
may contact the Contractor outside normal business hours, and the Contractor shall provide assistance 
within the response timeframes defined in the Performance Requirements Summary. The Contractor 
may perform work at its convenience, provided that all required response and r esolution timeframes 
are met. Only time spent performing authorized work is billable. 
 
5. TASKS:   
 
All tasks described herein, including development, maintenance, compliance, and documentation, shall 
be performed by qualified Contractor personnel as defined in Section 3.1. The tasks listed in this section 
define the scope of services that may be ordered under this IDIQ contract. Performance of any task 
occurs only upon issuance of a Task Order by the CO and shall be carried out as needed consistent with 
the requirements of the applicable Task Order. 
 
5.1. Provide On -demand Technical Support : Provide on -demand HDB technical support to 

6 
 
Water Resources users. These services shall be provided by qualified Contractor personnel 
during normal Reclamation business hours and within the performance standards outlined 
in section 7. Examples of on-demand technical support include but are not limited to the 
following: 
 
5.1.1. Provide technical support in the installation and configuration of HDB and all 
supporting applications for instances of HDB. 
5.1.2. Consult with Reclamation on identification of problems and solutions, including 
development of new functional requirements for the database instances. 
5.1.3. Provide information to Reclamation by way of informational meetings, and/or 
developing additional technical documents as requested. 
5.1.4. Respond to emails, phone calls, and requests for information and/or assistance in 
any matters dealing with HDB instances. These requests may include but are not 
limited to adding new data types, creating or modifying computations, restoring 
data, decoding GOES satellite data, troubleshooting scripts, etc. 
5.1.5. Provide support in relation to HDB connections to RiverWare, or similar modeling 
platform, through connection packages and procedures as requested. 
5.1.6. Provide support for server operating systems (currently Red Hat Enterprise Linux) 
as requested for instances of HDB. 
5.1.7. Provide documentation of the number of hours worked per month by task order. 
Provide monthly meetings for technical support team status reports and delineate 
the work performed on the various HDB instances. 
5.1.8. Provide on demand support for other issues that may arise over the lifecycle of 
the HDB System. 
 
5.2. Database System Maintenance and System Malfunction Resolution Services : 
Troubleshoot, diagnose, and solve software and database management problems involving 
HDB system malfunctions as expeditiously as possible and within the performance 
standards outlined in section 7. Examples of database system maintenance and system 
malfunction resolution services include but are not limited to the following: 
 

7 
 
5.2.1. Support database strategic planning and assistance to Reclamation with respect to 
currently available and supported products and versions of the database. 
5.2.2. Install and test modifications and regular updates to operational systems and 
applications to keep functioning and operational both the production and 
test/development versions of the HDB databases and all installed applications. 
5.2.3. Maintain all existing loader programs and applications on database instances, and 
new loader programs and applications as they are implemented. This will include 
the open source TSTool software data loaders and all stored procedures and 
packages for various external loading applications. 
5.2.4. Provide system maintenance and system malfunction resolution services for other 
issues that may arise over the lifecycle of the HDB System. 
 
5.3. HDB Development, Coordination and Documentation : Develop, test, and integrate HDB 
enhancements; maintain code and documentation; coordinate with stakeholders; support 
data tools; ensure secure knowledge transfer and consistent operations across all instances. 
Examples of HDB development, coordination, and documentation include but are not 
limited to the following. 
 
5.3.1. Develop enhancements to HDB as requested by Reclamation's HDB Water 
Resources Group to be transferable, functional, and available to other instances of 
HDB. 
5.3.2. Install and test available enhancements and regular updates to production and 
test/development databases, systems and applications at each HDB instance.  All 
enhancements and modifications prepared by contractor shall be fully tested on a 
test environment maintained with the Reclamation network.  Reclamation will be 
responsible for maintaining the test environment and access to the contractor for 
this purpose. Documentation of successful testing shall be submitted to 
Reclamation.  Only after Reclamation review of testing results and approval by 
Reclamation shall contractor install enhancements or modifications onto the HDB 
production environment. 
5.3.3. Integrate HDB enhancements and code modifications into the HDB source code 

8 
 
and database scripts baseline. 
5.3.4. Maintain and support the HDB source code and the computation processor 
algorithms for HDB to be consistent as possible with other HDB installations. 
5.3.5. Coordinate development of programs/systems used for data acquisition, data 
logging, feedback control, and configuration (currently OPENDCS) with the other 
participating entities. 
5.3.6. Documentation of new developments shall be provided with new deliverables. 
Maintain all other documentation related to HDB, OpenDCS, the Computational 
Processor, data loaders, etc. 
5.3.7. The contractor shall develop and maintain a comprehensive, transferable 
knowledge base that includes system architecture documentation, annotated 
source code, configuration guides, and training materials. This knowledge base 
shall be structured to support onboarding of future contractor staff or federal 
personnel and maintained in a secure, centralized location accessible to 
authorized Reclamation staff. 
5.3.8. Provide download capabilities of HDB installation scripts, documentation and 
application software on the HDB web site. 
5.3.9. Attend and participate in conference calls, user groups, team, or other impromptu

Statement of Requirement 
(SOR) 
 
“Battlefield Operations Support System 
(BOSS) Product Gold Support” 
at 
Joint Base Langley-Eustis 
July 7 2026” 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
1.0 Introduction 
 
1.1 Mission: The Primary mission of the Air Combat Command Communication Support (ACC CSS) Squadron’s 
Special Missions Flight, Tactical Systems Test Element (SCPT), Department of the Air Force Participating Test 
Unit (DAFPTU) it to provide the Air Force with tested and certified software systems for use by the Warfighter in 
worldwide operations.  These certified systems meet the highest standards of quality assurance that is required to 
support air combat operations involving the Joint Services, Air Expeditionary Forces , or other special combat 
operations utilizing ACC/s networked communications infrastructure.   
  
1.2 Background: Mission has been in place since the early 1980s and was an outcrop of the Vietnamese War where 
interoperability between agency C2 and Weapons platforms did not meet requirements.  The Joint  Interoperability 
Test Command (JITC) was formed and resulted in each agency being required to perform service level operations to 
complete service level interoperability testing prior to Joint interoperability testing.  The DAFPTU was formed to 
resolve this requirement for the USAF.  Similar operations exist for the Army, Navy, and Marine Corps. 
  
1.3 Scope: The contractor shall provide Product Support Gold for nine (9) contracted BOSS platforms, three (3) laptop 
versions, five (5) rack mount versions, and one (1) Tower PC.  Period of Performance from 18 September 2026  
through 17 September 2027 in accordance with Product Support Gold TCG-PSG SLB.  Four (4) option years are 
included in the contract.  
 
2.0 General Requirements 
 
2.1 Business Relations: The Contractor shall successfully integrate and coordinate all activity needed to execute this 
requirement. The Contractor shall manage the timeliness, completeness, and quality of problem identification. The 
Contractor shall promptly identify issues to the Government and take timely corrective action. The Contractor shall 
seek to ensure mission partner satisfaction and professional and ethical behavior of all contractor personnel.  
 
2.2 Contract Management & Administration 
 
2.2.1 Contract Management: The Contractor shall establish clear organizational lines of authority and 
responsibility to ensure effective management of resources assigned to the requirement. The Contractor 
must maintain continuity between the mission partner and the contractor’s corp orate offices. 
 
2.2.2 Contract Administration: The Contractor shall establish processes and assign appropriate resources to 
effectively administer the contract. The Contractor shall respond to the Governments requests for 
contractual actions in a timely fashion. The Contractor shall have a single point  of contact between the 
Government and contractor personnel assigned to support the contract. The Contractor shall assign 
resources in order to maintain proper and accurate records related to this contract.  
 
2.3 Subcontract Management: If applicable, the Contractor shall be responsible for any subcontractor and any 
subcontractor management necessary to integrated work executed under this contract. 
  
2.4 Hours of Work: Work days are from Monday through Friday excluding US federal holidays. Work hours are from 
0800 to 1700 local Eastern Standard time. 
 
3.0 Product Specifications & Installation Requirements 
 
3.1 The contractor must provide  
• Unlimited helpdesk support  
• Annual release of software 
• 1 site (CONUS) visit for up to 3 days 
• Extended warranty is provided on TCG-supplied hardware and software  

• Customers covered by a Gold Plan for three consecutive years are eligible to receive a new, replacement server 
computer to re-host their TCG software at no additional cost (the 1553 and Link-11 hardware, if applicable, is 
reused) 
• For sites with more than 1 system, the purchase of Product Support - Additional Unit is required for each BOSS 
system beginning with system 
• Plans are renewable annually and reinstatement fees apply for lapses in coverage. Payment for product support 
subscription due in full at commencement of support. 
• If on-site work by contractor becomes necessary, contractor personnel shall ensure an up-to-date Visit Request 
is submitted to the ACC CSS Security office and remain on file for one year. 
• Contractor shall ensure the pass and identification items required for contract performance is obtained for 
employees and non-government owned vehicles. 
• Contractor and its employees shall comply with base traffic regulations found in Air Force Instructions 31-204,  
Air Force Motor Vehicle Traffic Supervision. 
• Contractor employees are prohibited from possessing weapons, firearms, or ammunition, on themselves or 
within their contractor-owned vehicle or privately-owned vehicle while on JBLE. 
• A U.S. SECRET clearance will be required for any contractor personnel performing work at the customer’s site. 
• Period of Performance: 
.1  Base Year: 18 September 2026 – 17 September 2027   
.2 Option Year 1: 18 September 2027 – 17 September 2028  
.3 Option Year 2: 18 September 2028 – 17 September 2029  
.4 Option Year 3: 18 September 2029 – 17 September 2030  
.5 Option Year 4: 18 September 2030 – 17 September 2031  
 
3.2 Delivery of all products identified in section 3.1 must be made to the location identified in section 4.3 on or before 
17 September 2027. 
 
4.0 Special Requirements 
 
4.1  Security & Safety 
 
4.1.1 Operational Security (OPSEC): If any installation is required to take place in a Government 
facility, the Contractor shall be familiar with the organizational critical information and indicators 
list (CIIL) and OPSEC policy of any installation they require access to. The required CIIL can be 
provided by the Contracting Officer. 
 
4.1.2 Safety: The Contractor and any of its subcontractors (if applicable) shall promptly report pertinent 
facts regarding mishaps involving Government property damage or injury to 
Government/Contractor personnel that take place on an installation. The Contractor shall notify 
the cognizant Contracting Officer within 24 hours of all mishaps or incidents. The Contracting 
Officer will notify the Safety Office. The Contractor shall cooperate in any resulting safety 
investigation. 
 
4.2 Contractor Access to Installations: Access to DoD installations is limited to personnel with a valid installation 
access pass. Failure to submit required information to obtain required documentation will result in the exclusion of 
such employees from the installation until such documentation is obtained. Contractor employees may be subject to 
personal and vehicle searched when entering or leaving a DoD installation. If installation access is required, the 
Government will provide the Contractor with the required information and documents for installation access passes  
upon award.  Subsequently, the Contractor shall provide a list of all employees along working under this contract, 
along with the required documentation upon receipt of contract award, and no later than 30 days prior to the 
projected need for any new installation access pass requirements. The Contractor is responsible for maintaining an 
adequate number of personnel with active installation access passes, and adhering to the timeframes stated in t his 
section. The cognizant mission partner is responsible for the coordination of installation access passes. Upon 
termination of employment, termination or cancellation of the contract, or expiration of the contract the Contractor 
is responsible for collecting employee installation access passes and turning them in to the CO, or the cognizant 
mission partner in a timely fashion.   

 
4.3 Shipping Instructions 
DoDAAC: F2QT32 
ACC CSS SCXI, 37 Elm St, Langley AFB, VA 23665-2009  
Terry Elhajj 
Email:  terrance.elhajj@us.afmil 
Telephone:  7577646527 
    
4.4 Government Furnished Material: N/A 
 
4.5 Applicable Directives: N/A

Request for Information

The purpose of this Request for Information (RFI) is to identify qualified contractors and identify brands of nursecall systems with a code blue communication system capable of integrating with existing Hill-Rom hospital beds to relay all the required bed data back to the nurse stations without the use of middleware.

Introduction

This is a RFI only. Accordingly, this RFI does not constitute a Request for Quote, Request for Proposal, or a guarantee that a solicitation will be issued by the Government in the future; furthermore, it does not commit the Government to contract for any products or services described herein. Additionally, this RFI does not restrict the Government as to the ultimate acquisition approach. In accordance with Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation Overhaul 15.101(c), responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract.

The purpose of this RFI is to identify qualified contractors and identify brands of nursecall systems capable of integrating with existing Hill-Rom hospital beds without the use of middleware to capture all the required bed data as well as other patient/room data and provide that information in a visual dashboard accessed via the workstations located at the nurse stations. The purpose of this RFI is to obtain market information on capabilities and capable sources. All responses to this RFI will be treated only as information for the Government to consider. The Government is not responsible for any cost incurred by industry in furnishing this information. All costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the interested vendor's expense. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude a vendor’s participation in any future solicitation should one be issued. Any Service-Disabled Veteran-owned small businesses (SDVOSBs) or Veteran-owned small businesses (VOSBs) responding to this RFI must include their intent and ability to meet any set-aside requirements for performance of this effort in accordance with the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Acquisition Regulation (VAAR) 852.219-73 or 852.219-74, VA Notice of Total Set-Aside for Certified SDVOSB or VOSB respectively. Any information submitted by industry to this RFI is strictly voluntary. All submissions will become Government property and will not be returned. Interested vendors are responsible for adequately marking proprietary, restricted or competition sensitive information contained in their response. VA is under no obligation to provide feedback to the company or to contact the company for clarification of any information submitted in response to this RFI.

Companies interested in participating in this effort please respond to this RFI, indicating the company’s interest and providing its respective capabilities to perform the effort, as described in the paragraphs below. Any information provided in response to this RFI may be used by VA in developing its acquisition strategy and Product Description (PD). 

Be advised that set-aside decisions may be made based on the information provided in response to this RFI. Responses should be as complete and informative as possible.

It is the responsibility of interested parties to monitor this site for updates and/or additional information pertaining to this requirement.

Background:

The VA, Veterans Health Administration (VHA) Birmingham VA Health Care System (BVHCS) is performing market research related to a potential requirement for brand name or equal Hillrom Voalte nurse call system with a code blue communication system, staging services, installation services, termination/testing/labeling of cables, and installation. The requirement would include providing server/switch implementation in the BVHCS main server room, the system shall integrate with the 107 Hillrom beds that are in use at the BVHCS, and an installation plan for implementation of the new system and removal of the existing system.

The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code considered for this requirement is 541519 (Other Computer Related Services); the small business size standard for this NAICS is 150 employees.

See the DRAFT PD attached to this RFI for additional information.

VA is seeking to identify qualified contractors and identify brands of nursecall systems with a code blue communication system capable of integrating with existing Hill-Rom hospital beds without the use of middleware to capture all the required bed data as well as other patient/room data and provide that information in a visual dashboard accessed via the workstations located at the nurse stations. If interested and capable of providing for this requirement, please see the “How to Respond” section below.

How to Respond: 

All responsible sources may submit a response in accordance with the information below:

NO MARKETING MATERIALS ARE ALLOWED AS PART OF THIS RFI. Generic capability statements will not be reviewed.

It is requested that the vendor respond to the following.

Note: Provide a capability package that is clear, concise, and complete. VA is under no obligation to provide feedback to the company, or to contact the company for clarification of any information submitted in response to this RFI. Responses shall be limited to no more than 10 pages and include the following: 

Provide the following information in the initial paragraph of the submission.

*If you believe there is a more appropriate NAICS code, please provide that to the Government with your rationale.

**For Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business (SDVOSB)/Veteran Owned Small Business (VOSB) concerns, indicate whether you could meet the requirement that a Government information technology procurement classified under SDVOSB/VOSB is in accordance with Veterans First Contracting Act for the applicable NAICS.

Brief summary describing your company’s technical capabilities to meet the requirements outlined above requirement and in the attached PD. Brand name or equal Hillrom Voalte nurse call system, staging services, installation services, termination/testing/labeling of cables, and installation is being contemplated. If your company is proposing an ‘or equal’ solution, be sure to demonstrate how your product/service meets the salient characteristics identified in the Draft PD attached hereto, including how the proposed ‘or equal’ solution is able to integrate with the existing Hillrom hospital beds without the use of middleware to provide all the requisite bed data identified in the Draft PD.

Identify if the proposed ‘or equal’ solution includes Room Control Boards (RCB) that can function in a standalone mode while experiencing loss of system communication with homerun or equivalent wiring topology.

Provide commercially available list pricing for the identified products and/or services that can meet the Government’s minimum requirements, including recommended quantities and unit pricing. If commercially available list pricing is not available, provide a Rough Order of Magnitude, including estimated quantities, unit pricing, and any additional anticipated costs to meet the Governments minimum requirements.

Indicate the likelihood of your company responding to a solicitation should this effort result in an acquisition. Note: Small businesses should include intent and ability to meet set-aside requirements for performance of this effort, if applicable.

Respondents are requested to identify any additional information considered applicable to this RFI.

Has the draft PD provided sufficient detail to describe the technical/functional requirements that encompass the brand name or equal Hillrom Voalte nurse call system, staging services, installation services, termination/testing/labeling of cables, and installation to be provided under this effort.

DESCRIPTION

NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE

The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) intends to issue a sole source order to ALVAREZ LLC, a Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) and HUBZone Small Business, under the NASA Solutions for Enterprise-Wide Procurement (SEWP) V Governmentwide Acquisition Contract (GWAC), Contract No. NNG15SD19B, for the procurement of Philips IntelliVue Microstream Extension modules (Product No. 867041), B06 Add Dual IBP, Temp, and associated accessories required to support patient monitoring operations.

The required equipment is manufactured by Philips Healthcare and is necessary to maintain and expand the existing Philips IntelliVue patient monitoring platform utilized by the Department of Veterans Affairs. The equipment will provide continuous end-tidal carbon dioxide (EtCO₂), invasive blood pressure (IBP), and temperature monitoring capabilities for clinical patient care.

The Government intends to issue this order to ALVAREZ LLC, an authorized NASA SEWP contract holder capable of providing the required Philips equipment and associated implementation services available under its SEWP V contract. Procuring these items from the identified source ensures compatibility with the Government's existing Philips IntelliVue monitoring infrastructure, existing accessories, software, and biomedical support environment. Acquisition of an alternate solution would require replacement of existing components, additional integration efforts, staff retraining, and could result in unnecessary duplication of cost and disruption to clinical operations.

This procurement is being conducted in accordance with FAR 16.505(b)(2)(i), Exception to Fair Opportunity, as only one source is capable of providing the required supplies and services at the level of quality required by the Government.

The applicable NAICS Code is 541519 – Other Computer Related Services.

Responses

This notice is not a request for competitive quotations. However, interested parties may identify their interest and capability to satisfy the Government's requirement by submitting sufficient technical documentation demonstrating their ability to provide:

Philips IntelliVue Microstream Extension modules (Product No. 867041);

B06 Add Dual IBP, Temperature functionality;

Full compatibility with the Department of Veterans Affairs' existing Philips IntelliVue patient monitoring system;

Any required implementation and integration services available under the NASA SEWP V contract.

Responses must demonstrate the capability to provide equipment that is fully compatible with the existing Philips monitoring environment without degradation of performance or functionality.

Responses shall be received no later than 11:59 p.m. Central Time on 07/24/2026 and shall be submitted via email to: mario.russell@va.gov

The required equipment is manufactured by Philips Healthcare and is necessary to maintain and expand the existing Philips IntelliVue patient monitoring platform utilized by the Department of Veterans Affairs. The equipment will provide continuous end-tidal carbon dioxide (EtCO₂), invasive blood pressure (IBP), and temperature monitoring capabilities for clinical patient care.

The Government intends to issue this order to ALVAREZ LLC, an authorized NASA SEWP contract holder capable of providing the required Philips equipment and associated implementation services available under its SEWP V contract. Procuring these items from the identified source ensures compatibility with the Government's existing Philips IntelliVue monitoring infrastructure, existing accessories, software, and biomedical support environment. Acquisition of an alternate solution would require replacement of existing components, additional integration efforts, staff retraining, and could result in unnecessary duplication of cost and disruption to clinical operations.

This procurement is being conducted in accordance with FAR 16.505(b)(2)(i), Exception to Fair Opportunity, as only one source is capable of providing the required supplies and services at the level of quality required by the Government.

The applicable NAICS Code is 541519 – Other Computer Related Services.

Responses

This notice is not a request for competitive quotations. However, interested parties may identify their interest and capability to satisfy the Government's requirement by submitting sufficient technical documentation demonstrating their ability to provide:

Philips IntelliVue Microstream Extension modules (Product No. 867041);

B06 Add Dual IBP, Temperature functionality;

Full compatibility with the Department of Veterans Affairs' existing Philips IntelliVue patient monitoring system;

Any required implementation and integration services available under the NASA SEWP V contract.

Responses must demonstrate the capability to provide equipment that is fully compatible with the existing Philips monitoring environment without degradation of performance or functionality.

Responses shall be received no later than 11:59 p.m. Central Time on 07/24/2026 and shall be submitted via email to: mario.russell@va.gov

Section C - Description/Specifications/Statement of Work
The contractor, OCLC, Inc., shall provide, implement, and host a comprehensive, FedRAMP-authorized Library Services Platform (LSP) 
encompassing WorldShare Management Services (WMS) and Hosted EZproxy to support the Naval Air Warfare Center (NAWC) Aircraft Division 
Library for Innovation and Technology. The contractor shall execute a full system implementation and secure data migration of approximately 6,500 
physical item records and associated electronic resource licenses from the terminating legacy system (SirsiDynix). This effort requires configuring 
native integration with the WorldCat database and establishing secure, remote authentication (EZproxy) to ensure uninterrupted, seamless research 
access for off-site and deployed personnel. The contractor shall complete all implementation, configuration, and data migration tasks within a 4-to-6-
month performance window, delivering a fully operational and tested system prior to the legacy system's termination on 31 December 2026.

SECTION C - Description/Specifications/Statement of Work 
The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), headquartered in Washington, D.C., 
is required to adhere to the section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act to eliminate barriers to 
information communications and technology (ICT). Section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act, 
applies when federal agencies develop, procure, maintain, or use information and 
communications technology. They must ensure that federal employees with disabilities have 
access to ICT that is comparable to the access enjoyed by federal employees without disabilities 
unless doing so would impose an undue burden on the agency. The statute also makes the same 
requirement with respect to members of the public with disabilities seeking information or 
services. HHS must ensure that digital content is “perceivable, operable, understandable, and 
robust.”
 HHS’ Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) is responsible for providing 
services to the Operating and Staff Divisions (Op/StaffDivs), which comprise HHS. The HHS 
Section 508 Operations Board mandated all ICT conform to the most current WCAG AA success 
criteria. The overall objective is for HHS/ASA/OCIO to obtain services to support the HHS and 
OS Section 508 Program. 
The following legislative mandates, instructions, and policies form the basis from which HHS 
works to remain compliant with requirements for digital products and services. 
1. Overarching Policies 
1.1. Connected Government Act 
1.2. OMB M-17-06, Policies for Federal Agency Public Websites and Digital Services 
1.3. OMB Circular A-130 
1.4. Digital Government Strategy (May 2012) 
1.5. E-Government Act of 2002 
1.6. Accessibility/Section 508 
2. Accessibility for Teams 
2.1. 18F Accessibility Guide 
2.2. Section 508 Law and Technical Standards 
2.3. Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 
2.4. WCAG Quick Reference and WCAG Web tutorials 
2.5. Technology Accessibility Playbook 
2.6. Federal CIO Council Accessibility Best Practices 
2.7. Governmentwide Section 508 Strategic Plan (2013)

1 GENERAL INFORMATION 
• Title: RegScale, Inc. Policy & Compliance Software Licenses (or Equivalent 
• Requiring Activity: Air Force Sustainment Center (AFSC) 
• Contract Type: Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) 
2 SCOPE 
This document outlines the minimum technical requirements for a brand name or equal GRC 
platform. The platform is required for the Air Force Sustainment Center Software Enterprise 
(AFSC/SW) to manage compliance for Software Defined Networking (SDN) and SDN-Secret 
(SDN-S) architectures. The objective is to centralize and automate core compliance services to 
support a diverse array of major weapon systems and programmatic portfolios, including 
Mission Planning, E3, E7, ATCALS, F-16, and A-10. 
2.1 Operational Objectives & Business Impact 
The procurement of the GRC platform is intended to transition the Requiring Activity from 
manual, static compliance processes to an automated, continuous assurance model. The platform 
must deliver the following operational outcomes: 
2.1.1 Continuous Authorization (cATO) Support: Enable a transition from point-in-
time authorizations to a Continuous Authority to Operate (cATO) posture 
through real-time, automated security control monitoring. 
2.1.2 Acquisition Velocity: Accelerate compliance timelines (e.g., RMF, FedRAMP) 
by automating control inheritance and documentation generation. 
2.1.3 Audit Efficiency: Minimize manual labor associated with audit preparation by 
utilizing automated evidence collection and API-driven telemetry. 
2.1.4 Exposure Reduction: Improve cyber resilience by providing near real-time alerts 
on control failures, thereby reducing the window of vulnerability. 
3 TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS & SPECIFIC TASKS 
The contractor shall provide a GRC platform that meets the following minimum requirements. 

 
Page 2 of 4 
CUI 
CUI 
3.1 Core Platform Capabilities 
3.1.1 The platform shall be architected to leverage Application Programming 
Interfaces (APIs), artificial intelligence, and machine-readable data structures for 
compliance and risk management. 
3.2 Compliance as Code 
3.2.1 The platform shall natively support the National Institute of Standards and 
Technology (NIST) Open Security Controls Assessment Language (OSCAL) to 
convert regulatory frameworks into machine-readable formats. 
3.2.2 The platform shall provide dynamic documentation capabilities, where 
compliance artifacts are automatically updated in real-time, replacing static 
document generation.  
3.2.3 The platform shall support the mapping of a single control implementation across 
multiple overlapping regulatory frameworks (e.g., FedRAMP, SOC 2). 
3.3 Automated Data Collection 
3.3.1 The platform shall integrate with the organization’s technology stack via API to 
automate the collection of evidence. Supported integrations must include, but are 
not limited to, AWS, Azure, Jira, Tenable, and DevSecOps pipelines. 
3.3.2 The platform shall continuously pull telemetry and security data from integrated 
systems to provide a real-time view of compliance status. 
3.3.3 The platform shall provide an event-driven workflow engine that triggers 
automated notifications (e.g., via Slack, Microsoft Teams) in response to control 
failures or compliance drifts. 
3.4 Artificial Intelligence in Control Management 
3.4.1 The platform shall utilize artificial intelligence (AI) to automatically parse 
existing corporate policies and generate compliant control implementation 
statements. 
3.4.2 The platform shall provide an automated feature to perform control gap analysis, 
identify weaknesses, and recommend contextual improvements.  

 
Page 3 of 4 
CUI 
CUI 
3.5 DevSecOps Integration 
3.5.1 The platform shall embed Continuous Compliance Automation (CCA) directly 
into DevSecOps processes to enforce security guardrails, ensuring that new 
products and updates meet regulatory standards by design before production 
deployment. 
3.6 Risk Management Framework (RMF) Automation 
3.6.1 The platform must automate all steps of the NIST Risk Management Framework 
(RMF) process (Prepare, Categorize, Select, Implement, Assess, Authorize, and 
Monitor) to support a state of Continuous Authority to Operate (cATO). 
3.6.2 The platform shall support ongoing accreditation through continuous assessment 
of systems, ensuring compliance status is dynamically synchronized with system 
posture. 
3.6.3 The platform shall provide automated workflows to transition from manual, 
checklist-based compliance to live, threat-aligned accreditation. 
3.7 Comprehensive Risk and Exception Management 
3.7.1 The platform shall include a quantitative risk analysis module that utilizes 
techniques such as Monte Carlo simulations to translate cyber risks into 
quantifiable financial metrics.  
3.7.2 The platform shall provide a Third-Party Risk Management (TPRM) capability 
for continuous monitoring of vendor and supply chain partner security posture 
within a centralized dashboard. 
3.7.3 The platform must maintain immutable audit trails, recording all changes to 
compliance records throughout their lifecycle to ensure a transparent and 
undisputable history. 
4 WARRANTY 
The contractor shall provide a standard commercial warranty on all software licenses provided.

DISCLAIMER 
 
This RFI is issued solely for information and planning purposes only and does not constitute a

The submission of pricing, capabilities for planning purposes, and other market information is highly 
encouraged and allowed under this RFI In Accordance With (IAW) FAR Part 15.201(e). 
 
SOURCES SOUGHT DESCRIPTION 
 
This is NOT a solicitation announcement. This is a RFI/sources sought only. The purpose of this sources 
sought/RFI is to gain knowledge of potential qualified sources and their size classification relative to 
NAICS 541511. Responses to this sources sought will be used by the Government to make appropriate 
acquisition decisions. After review of the responses to this sources sought, a solicitation announcement 
may be published. Responses to this sources sought synopsis are not considered adequate responses for 
a solicitation announcement.  
 
The information identified below is intended to be descriptive, not restrictive, and to indicate the quality 
of the supplies/services that will be satisfactory. It is the responsibility of the interested source to 
demonstrate to the government that the interested parties can provide the supplies/services that fulfill 
the required specifications, or brand name equal. 
 
If you are interested and are capable of providing the sought out supplies/services, please provide the 
requested information as well as the information indicated below. Response to this notice should 
include company name, address, point of contact, size of business pursuant to the following questions:  
 
Please indicate the size status and representations of your business, such as but not limited to: Service 
Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business (SDVOSB), Veteran Owned Small Business (VOSB), Hubzone, 
Woman Owned Small Business (WOSB), Large Business, etc.). 
 
Is your company considered small under the NAICS code identified under this RFI? 
 
Are you the manufacturer, distributor, or an equivalent solution to the items being referenced? 
What is the Country of Manufacture for the items being referenced? 
 
Does your company have an FSS contract with GSA, VA NAC, NASA SEWP, or any other federal 
contract, that can be utilized to procure the requirement listed above? If so, please provide the 
contract number. 
 
Please submit your capabilities that show clear, compelling, and convincing evidence that you can meet 
the requirement described in the attached SOW.

The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), VISN 15 Network Contracting Office, is seeking sources that 
can provide the following; 
Statement of Work 
 
The contractor shall provide HL7 integration, licensing, and support for the existing Medgraphics 
Pulmonary function lab system. 
All software and equipment must be compatible with currently installed MGC Server. 
Contractor shall not perform any service that will result in additional charges. The cost of this contract 
covers all cost necessary to assure acquisition, delivery of equipment and warranty. Contractors shall 
include all software necessary to meet the functional requirements; the contractor shall not have direct 
access to VA computer equipment or other media which contain electronic patient information(ePHI). 
The HL7 software and support must fulfill these requirements: 
• Must integrate with CPRS and VISTA imaging (the current VA standard). 
• Must be compatible with the Somnoware and Cerner patient record system. 
• Must be compatible with the MGC PFT equipment, including Ultima, USB Connect, PFTs and 
Platinum Elite PFT. 
• Must be able to use the currently installed Medgraphics database server without requiring new 
hardware. 
• Must provide training support on implementation. 
 
(End of Statement of Work)

DESCRIPTION

The purpose of this amendment is to respond to a vendor question. The response date and time remains unchanged. 

We understand that we need to respond to the 22 sections under the Requested Capability Information and answer the 10 questions under Response Instructions. Given that the page limit is set to a maximum of 10 pages, can the government be a little flexible on the page count.

Response: The page limit is amended to 15 pages. 

What level of clearance does personnel need to have for this contract?

Response: A VA background check is required.

Can we provide candidates who are eligible to get clearance, but do not have active clearance?

Response: Yes

Should the offeror have the ability to provide security clearances to the personnel being provided?

Response: As stated in question 2, a VA background check is required. However, if an offeror is required to provide security clearances for the personnel being proposed, this requirement will be clearly identified in the solicitation

PWS Section 5.2.2 outlines requirements for advanced database administration and geodatabase maintenance. Does the current ArcGIS implementation within the Corporate Data Warehouse (CDW) heavily utilize standard ESRI out-of-the-box system tables, or are there significant schema customizations and proprietary extensions that the contractor will be required to maintain?

Response: EGT’s databases are SDE enabled and use the standard out of the box schemas and tables.  However, EGT also uses SQL/SSIS to create views, query data, ETL data, and modify it without the use of ArcGIS Pro.  All our databases are within CDW and follow CDW rules.  We are required to support geospatial needs and data requirements with and without ESRI.  Expert knowledge in SQL especially the ST functions is a must.

PWS Section 5.2.1 and Section 5.2.3 reference troubleshooting and integrating interfaces between ArcGIS Enterprise and third-party systems. Could the Government provide a specific list of these external IT platforms, databases, or application names referenced in Attachment 3?

Response: Power BI is one of the key systems we support.  We also must support researchers who use Python and R outside of ArcGIS to do analysis.  We also feed our data into other key applications via the ArcGIS REST API.  This allows users to embed our web maps in web applications outside of the ArcGIS Portal framework.

The RFI requests experience with ArcGIS Indoors, and the PWS references creating indoor floor plans using CAD, BIM, and LAS datasets. Does the VA currently have a standardized data model and schema established for facility footprints across its administrations, or will the contractor be tasked with establishing the initial spatial framework and data pipeline definitions for these facility layers?

Response: VA uses the ESRI ArcGIS data model for indoor and 3D data.  For 2D utility and facility data VA uses a customized version of the Spatial Data Standards for Facilities, Infrastructure and Environment (SDSFIE).  All other data (such as Census) is typically in the format that the creator publishes it as.

PWS Section 5.4 outlines migrating and consolidating multiple VA ArcGIS instances into a unified platform within the VA Enterprise Cloud (VAEC). To assist in accurately projecting workload, what is the approximate size (e.g., in terabytes or record counts) of the geospatial datasets slated for cloud migration and consolidation?

Response: Currently the existing data is within the 10-20 TB range for all systems.  This includes databases, files on SAN drive, and portal contents.  However, we are expecting significant growth of 10-20 TB per year for the next several years to support ArcGIS Indoors.

Example metrics:

sPatient addresses: 249,932,233 

NCA: 

5,429,154 graves features

4,136,039 markers features

Common data:

EGT data: 70 tables

ORNL data: 78 tables

EGT Portal contents: 2,015 items

GSSC Portal contents: 3,714 items

PWS Section 5.2.1 states that incident volume can trend between 15 to 20 incidents per week. Is there an existing backlog of data anomalies, mismatched data features, or unresolved help desk tickets, or is the incoming contractor expected to focus primarily on steady-state operations?

Response: Currently, tickets are completed in 1-2 days and no backlog exists.

PWS Section 5.1.5 notes that the contractor must track all requirements, testing results, and risks in project management tools like Jira. Does the Government currently manage an enterprise-wide instance of Jira with pre-configured workflows for the Product Engineering Service (PES), or will the contractor be responsible for setting up and managing the team’s workspace and traceability matrices?

Response: Yes, the PES has our own Jira instance.  Usage has been on and off over the years but is used to track metrics for leadership.  Contractor will be able to use these Jira boards.

PWS Section 4.5.1 lists four critical labor categories as Key Personnel (GIS System Admin, GIS DBA, GIS Analyst, GIS Programmer) but does not define the full required headcount. Is the Government expecting a 1-to-1 staff allocation for these roles, or are contractors expected to propose a scalable staffing mix based on incident volume, and if so, will all personnel be considered key if there are more than one per LCAT?

Response: Currently, VA has 2 SA (1 senior, 1 junior), 1 senior DBA, and 1 Analyst, with a vacant programmer contractor position.  VA will be expecting to need 2 additional analysts in year 1 to meet expected workload.  Additional staff may be needed in later years.

PWS Section 5.1.5 mandates tracking code coverage and risks using Agile tools. Will the VA GIS program operate under an enterprise Agile Release Train (ART), or will it run on  localized Scrum/Kanban teams?

Response: VA uses Github for code storage and issue tracking.  We do not run formal scrum/kanban teams/processes at this time.  

PWS Section 5.2.2 tasks the contractor with database storage management, trend analysis, and geodatabase archiving. Does the VA currently utilize third-party tools for data optimization, and what are these third-party tool names, or are these workflows built entirely using native SQL Server/ESRI tools?

Response: VA has several customer scripts that check for things like long running queries.  We use standard SQL Server and ArcGIS tools for usage tracking.

PWS Section 5.3.3 requires knowledge of CAD, BIM, and LAS data to maintain indoor floor plans. Are these source files centrally managed and standardized, or will the contractor be responsible for clean-up, projection conversion, and schema mapping from disparate local facility offices?

Response: The local facilities will be required to clean up the contents (snapping, correct layer assignment, etc) all files before submitting to EGT.  Contractor may need to give guidance to local facilities should submitted files not be clean.  Contractor may need to project files and map CAD layer to feature class was part of normal duties.

PWS Section 5.3.1 mandates a minimum of two training sessions per month and weekly virtual office hours. Could the Government provide the estimated number of cores vs. casual users to help appropriately size the training and customer support communication plan?

Response: For weekly office hours, we have roughly 10-15 normal attendees.  Several have expert GIS knowledge while many are new to GIS.  New attendees are almost always new to GIS.  For larger training, typically it is within the range of 25-50 people, although we have had trainings top 300+ in the past. 

Attachment 3 is referenced several times in the PWS but does not appear to have been included. Can VA please provide Attachment 3?

Response: Attachment 3 is a boiler plate text that was not removed.

Can VA provide any additional details regarding the current ArcGIS Enterprise environment, including approximate number of environments, hosting locations, and whether the environment is currently federated/high availability?

Response: Currently, the VA hosts 2 on-prem GIS portal (EGT and VACO Indoors) and 1 cloud GIS portal (GSSC).  EGT and GSSC are in the process of merging key GSSC applications into EGT.  However, the GSSC portal will not be fully merged into after the combined VA GIS portal in the VA cloud has been completed.

Can VA provide approximate operational metrics such as:

Number of users

Average monthly ticket volumes

Approximate number of integrated systems/interfaces

Response: Tickets are typically handled via email or MS Teams.  They are put into Jira as worked on.  Tickets volume is round 10-15 per week. 

EGT Portal users: 

174 Content creators

5,471 Viewers
