322 Content creators

4,787 Viewers

Regarding the planned GIS consolidation into the VAEC environment, can VA provide any additional detail regarding:

Approximate number of GIS environments anticipated for migration/consolidation

Whether migration sequencing or prioritization has already been established

Response: 3 main environments will be consolidated: EGT, GSSC, VACO Indoors.  EGT and GSSC consolidation are already underway.  VACO indoors will be done last.

Is ArcGIS Indoors/facility mapping expected to be a significant component of the operational environment?

Response: Currently, no. However, expected growth is 5 VA Medical Center campus per year for the foreseeable future.  Each medical center is the size of a college campus and is estimated to take 5-10TB of storage each. 

Is ESRI software (ArcGIS Enterprise) the target for hosting and management of GIS data or is open-source technologies like GeoServer, QGIS, or other a potential for implementation?

Response: QGIS and Mapbox both are approved for VA use but are not used within the EGT/GSSC/VA Indoor systems.  ESRI and SQL Server software will be used for this implementation.

Will there be any data collection like GPS, survey, scanning, or remote sensing be included as part of this work?

Response:  NCA has GPS collection efforts, and the contractor may be asked to assist with moving GPS data and photos from ArcGIS Online to VA GIS system.  However, no GPS, survey, scanning, or remote sensing will be part of the work for this contract.

Regarding large datasets (100+ million records), approximately how many datasets/feature classes are in questions.  Or are these few datasets with very large tables?

Response: Almost all large geospatial datasets are tied to addresses.  We are working to normalize this data to allow for 1-2 large tables with several reference/crosswalk tables to link things like patients and enrollees to the same address records.  Currently, there are 2-5 large addresses tables within VA for this.  

CDW, which EGT is part of, has Trillions of records across all databases.  Many of these tables are related to patient care.  Contractor may be required to join and publish patient data with address to the portal.  Example: Join all prescriptions for X Drug to patient records and publish them to portal.

Since the data is large, is the target database SQL Server?  Is other RDBMS optional like Oracle or PostgreSQL/PostGIS especially since replication and scaling may be necessary.

Response: CDW runs SQL Server for almost all databases.  Other database is not viable option at this time.

Can any of the work be processed at contractor’s location like software development, testing, or data modification to improve performance and manageability? 

Response:  Limited work can be done on non-VA systems such as code develop.  All data must remain of the VA network due to Personal Health Information (PHI) concerns.  

Will there be a need for onsite staffing for support?

Response: No. All positions are remote.  Travel, if any, will be for training such as attending ESRI UC.  

Is the GIS a single site or a multi-site implementation?

Response: There are 3 current VA GIS systems within the VA and 1 ArcGIS Online instance.  This will be consolidated to 1 VA GIS system (Test and Production versions) and 1 ArcGIS Online instance.

Is customer training to include vendor certified training like (ESRI)?

Response: No certifications are required.  

Is the Company Information section, Response Instructions items 1–10, included within the 10-page limit?

Response: Yes, unless Company Information is included in the cover letter. 

Should the Industry Recommendations section, Question 22, Parts A–G, also be included within the same 10-page limit?

Response: Yes

When referencing the "transmittal page," is the Government referring to the cover letter/transmittal letter accompanying the response?

Response: The Government referring to the cover letter accompanying the response.

Announcement:  
1 Background and Purpose  
The USCB recently posted Special Notice ID # YA1323-26-CENTAMSN-0002 including draft 
solicitation materials to SAM.gov (April 20, 2026). Vendors were strongly encouraged to 
submit all questions and comments in response to this notice, with final 
responses/feedback due May 11, 2026. The USCB greatly appreciates the robust 
participation, feedback, and questions submitted in response to the notice.  
In response to the feedback received, the USCB intends to host a Virtual Industry Day. The 
purpose of this event is to address notable themes from the feedback, clarify the 
acquisition strategy, refine the technical requirements, and outline the upcoming 
procurement process to assist vendors in preparing high-quality quotations.  
2 Event Logistics 
• Date: Tuesday, July 21, 2026 
• Time: 11:00 am ET to 12:00 pm ET 
• Location: Virtual via Webex 
3 Registration Instructions 
Pre-registration is mandatory to receive the virtual meeting link and access instructions. 
• How to Register: Click the link below or copy and paste it into your browser to 
complete the registration form: 
https://uscensus.webex.com/weblink/register/r5e4bcaa6cec4a95e083396be1b21
28cf 
 
 
 

 
 
2 
 
4 Important Notes to Industry  
• Attendance: Attendance at Industry Day is voluntary and is not required to submit a 
quotation. Participation, or non-participation, will not affect a vendor’s eligibility to 
compete or the government’s evaluation of any future quotation. 
 
• Q&A: The USCB will not conduct a live question-and-answer session or provide 
vendor-specific guidance during this event. Additionally, the USCB will not be 
providing a formal response to each individual vendor’s question.  
 
• Post-Event Materials: The Government anticipates posting the Industry Day 
presentation materials on SAM.gov after the event. The presentation materials are 
provided for information purposes only and are not controlling procurement 
documents. 
 
• Disclaimer: This Industry Day is for planning and informational purposes only. It 
does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or Request for Quotation (RFQ) 
and shall not be construed as a commitment by the Government to award a 
contract. Verbal responses provided during the event are not binding; the final 
solicitation will remain the official governing document.

1. Introduction  
 
This Request for Information (RFI) is issued for conducting market research and 
planning purposes only. Accordingly, this RFI constitutes neither a Request for Quote, 
Request for Proposal, nor a guarantee that one will be issued by the Government in the 
future; furthermore, it does not commit the Government to contract for any services 
described herein. Additionally, this RFI does not restrict the Government as to the 
ultimate acquisition approach. In accordance with Revolutionary Federal Acquisition 
Regulation Overhaul 15.101(c), responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be 
accepted by the Government to form a binding contract.  
The purpose of this RFI is to identify qualified vendors, who can meet Department of 
Veterans Affairs (VA) requirements for

Software and Support. The purpose of this RFI is to obtain market information on 
capable sources. Your response to this RFI will be treated only as information for the 
Government to consider. The Government is not responsible for any cost incurred by 
industry in furnishing this information. All costs associated with responding to this RFI 
will be solely at the interested vendor's expense. Not responding to this RFI does not 
preclude participation in any future solicitation if any is issued. Any information 
submitted by respondents to this RFI is strictly voluntary. All submissions will become 
Government property and will not be returned. Interested vendors are responsible for 
adequately marking proprietary, restricted or competition sensitive information 
contained in their response.
 VA is under no obligation to provide feedback to the 
company, or to contact the company for clarification of any information submitted in 
response to this RFI. 
Be advised that set-aside decisions may be made based on the information provided in 
response to this RFI.  Responses should be as complete and informative as possible. 
 
2. Background: 
The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), the VISN 8 Sunshine Network has a 
requirement to implement weight base inventory management system in secondary 
inventory locations with a brand name or equal (BNE) PAR Excellence (PAR Ex) 
Weight-based Inventory Management System.

VISN 8 Sunshine Network and the Secondary inventory locations listed below, including any 
ancillary components that may be required for the system to be fully operational. The BNE PAR 
Excellence system shall have the salient characteristics of section 2.1-Salient Characteristics.

encouraged to submit alternative solutions that may depart from this specific framework. VA is

• Technical Architecture: A detailed description of how the alternative solution functions

1.0  BACKGROUND 
The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), the VISN 8 Sunshine Network has a 
requirement to implement and support a Weight Base Inventory Management System 
(WBIMS) in secondary inventory locations with a brand name or equal (BNE) PAR 
Excellence (PAR Ex) WBIMS.   
 
BNE PAR Ex is an inventory management technology that uses calibrated or weighted 
bins to capture data related to end user usage, stock replenishment, and other inventory 
related transactions in a supply closet. This technology captures transactions and usage 
data and keeps it stored on the user’s workstation, allowing them to run reports, analyze 
data, and manage inventory. The primary purpose of BNE PAR Ex is to identify on-hand 
quantities and values between VISTA Generic Inventory Package (GIP) and the BNE 
PAR bins system. 
 
The period of performance shall be 12-months from date of award, with two 12-month 
option periods to be exercised at the Governments discretion. 
2.0  PRODUCT REQUIREMENTS 
The Contractor shall provide and install a BNE PAR Excellence system at facilities listed 
below within the VISN 8 Sunshine Network to include Secondary inventory locations 
within those facilities. This shall include any ancillary components that may be required 
for the system to be fully operational. The BNE PAR Excellence system shall be able to 
meet the salient characteristics detailed in section 2.1-Salient Characteristics. 
Installation shall include all bins, scales, accessories, parts, labor, hardware, software, 
and training. The Contractor shall provide all tools or services required to complete the 
installation of the BNE PAR Excellence system.  
 
During the base year the Contractor shall provide and install all bins, scales, 
accessories, parts, labor, hardware, software, and training at each VISN 8 Medical 
Facility locations as identified in Appendix A.1: TBD. The Contractor shall provide a 1-
year warranty for all installed equipment and software, which includes replacements for 
defects or damage not caused by VA personnel. Warranties shall start upon completion 
of the installation and after VA verifies the system operates correctly. In each option 
period the Contractor shall provide necessary sustainment and support of the installed 
system to include software and hardware.

Source Selection Information – See FAR 2.101 and 3.104 
Document Number: 26-206  
JUSTIFICATION RESTRICTING COMPETITION DOFEMS MAINTENANCE 
1. Identification of Agency and Contracting Activity.
This justification is executed by the NAVSUP Fleet Logistics Center Norfolk (FLCN), Philadelphia on 
behalf of the Navy to meet Naval Medical Readiness Logistics Command (NMRLC) Naval Ophthalmic 
Readiness Activity (NORA) Directorate, Yorktown VA requirements. 
2. Description of the Action Being Approved.
This is a sole source action for the provision of as a follow-on contract requirement to Optical Lab 
Software Solutions, Inc. Services are currently being performed under Contract N6264521P2012. The 
contract was awarded 25 July 2021 and will expire 24 July 2026. The Government has a requirement for 
a maintenance and support contract for the product packaged and contracted to the government as the 
Defense Optical Fabrication Enterprise Management System (DOFEMS) that includes the Lab 
Management System (LMS) software manufactured by Optical Lab Software Solutions Inc. under the 
commercial software brand Optuitive. 
This requirement is for procurement that the Government intends to award a Firm, Fixed-Price (FFP) 
contract. The proposed manufacturer is Optical Lab Software Solutions, Inc., 13515 North Stemmons 
Fwy, Dallas, TX 75234 and is the only source of providing the required pieces of equipment. 
3. Description of Supplies/Services.
This service contract shall provide software maintenance, technical support services, and cyber security 
maintenance of the system per Department of Defense (DoD) and Defense Health Agency (DHA) 
guidance's and Risk Management Framework (RMF) for the Lab Management System (LMS) and all 
associated software packaged to operate with or in support of the product known to the government as 
DOFEMS as well as web services between the government's Spectacle Request Transmission System 
{SRTS) order entry system to ensure the DoD Optical Fabrication Enterprise maintains operational 
readiness to its beneficiaries.  The DOFEMS Production Environment is live operational environment 
installed on virtual servers located inside DoD Datacenters. The Test Virtual Machine Environment is a 
non-production static environment installed and managed by DHA/DCOPS (Data Center Operations) 
and maintained and used by the vendor and NOSTRA personnel to test and validate the systems 
operational performance post modifications before deployment to the actual Production Environment. 
The DOFEMS maintenance contract ensures system reliability, data integrity, cybersecurity compliance, 
and uninterrupted lab operations. 

Source Selection Information – See FAR 2.101 and 3.104 
The resultant contract will be funded with FY26 Operations Procurement Navy (OPN) appropriations. 
The estimated dollar value of the procurement will be $1,086,151.00.

Total $1,086,151 $1,120,908 $1,156,777 $1,193,793 $1,231,995 $5,789,924.00 
4. Statutory Authority Permitting Sole Source.
41 U.S.C. 1901 
The statutory authority permitting this sole source action is 41 U.S.C. 1901, Simplified acquisition 
procedures - a sole source acquisition using simplified procedures for the acquisition of commercial 
products and/or commercial services, as implemented by FAR 12.102(b). 
5. Rationale Justifying Use of Cited Statutory Authority.
The Defense Optical Fabrication Management System (DOFEMS) is an optical fabrication Laboratory 
Management System (LMS) currently approved to operate on the DoD Network. It is a proprietary 
Commercial Off the Shelf (COTS) product of Optical Lab Software Solutions (OLSS).  
Market research determined that no other vendors are authorized or technically capable of providing 
comprehensive maintenance services for the existing system. Third-party providers lack access to 
proprietary code and would be limited to superficial support, increasing risk to operations.  Replacing 
the system or transitioning to a different vendor for maintenance would require: Significant financial 
investment in system redevelopment or replacement, extensive data migration and validation efforts, 
operational downtime and retraining of personnel, and increased cybersecurity and compliance risks 
during transition. 
Failure to procure maintenance services from the original vendor would likely result in: increased 
system downtime and unresolved technical issues, exposure to cybersecurity vulnerabilities due to lack 
of timely patches, loss of system functionality or degraded performance, risk of data corruption or loss, 
and disruption to lab operations and associated services. The identified vendor is the original developer 
and exclusive provider of the IT Lab Management System currently deployed within the organization. 
The vendor possesses unique qualifications that make them the only responsible source for maintenance 
and support services 

The ability to award and fulfill this contract order expeditiously will mimic current LMS maintenance 
contract with no interruptions in current services nor affect peripheral devices.
6. Description of Efforts Made to Solicit Offers from as Man y Offerors as Practicable.
The proposed DOFEMS maintenance contract represents the most cost-effective solution when 
considering system continuity, risk mitigation, and avoidance of replacement costs. Alternative 
approaches would result in significantly higher total cost of ownership.  Efforts to identify alternative 
sources included market analysis and vendor outreach. No other qualified or authorized providers were 
identified who could meet the requirement without unacceptable risk.  The identified vendor is the 
original developer and exclusive provider of the IT Lab Management System currently deployed within 
the organization. The vendor possesses unique qualifications that make them the only responsible source 
for maintenance and support services. 
7. Determination of Fair and Reasonable Cost.
T
he Contracting Officer has determined that the anticipated cost to the Government of the 
supplies/services c
overed by this Justification will be fair and reasonable.   
8. Actions to Remove Barriers to F uture Competition.
For the reasons set forth in Paragraph 5, NAVSUP Fleet Logistics Center Norfolk (FLCN) 
BUMED/FM&C Directorate has no plans at this time to compete future contacts for the types of 
supplies/services covered by this document.  If another potential source emerges, the Contracting Office
will assess whether competition for future requirements is feasible. 
With future contracting support in place and Program Objective Memorandum (POM) approved and in 
place for future optica
l fabrication system replacement contracts the conditions to preclude the use of 
full and open competition for acquiring same or similar equipment in the future should decline and 
prohibit compelling urgency mandated in this request. 
Future competition for a system award such as this would be a minimum of five years from current 
contract award.  
The Government (or Program Office) expects to obtain a technical data package or develop a 
performance specification that will support competition for future acquisitions of the same or similar 
items.  
The requirement to issue a sources sought notice was waived by the Head of the Contracting Activity or 
designee. 
Source Selection Information – See FAR 2.101 and 3.104 

Source Selection Information – See FAR 2.101 and 3.104 
As such, the actions to attempt to remove the barriers to competition have been completed.   The 
circumstances requiring the acquisition be conducted pursuant to FAR Subpart 6.5 remain unchanged.  
Any subsequent follow-on requirements will be handled on a case-by-case basis.  Market Research will 
be conducted for any future requirements to determine if there are any potential sources for competition.

1. Description of action being approved: The Joint Electromagnetic Warfare Center (JEWC) 
currently is supporting a task to further EMS modeling at the campaign level. An associated 
subtask is to assess and evaluate current Comm ercial off the shelf (COTS) and Government off 
the Shelf (GOTS). As such, JEWC Modeling a nd Simulation Engineers are evaluating several 
different existing software and tr ailing them in real use cases. MACE, along with others, is one 
of the COTS being evaluated. This requirement shall be solicited as a brand name requirement and 
shall allow all authorized resellers, including small and other than small businesses, to compete.  
 
2. Statute and/or Regulation supporting determination: Pursuant to Revolutionary Federal 
Acquisition Regulation Overhaul (RFO) 12.102(a), which allows for restricting competition for 
acquisitions at or below the SAT, and as  supplemented by R-DFARS PGI 211.204, this 
document justifies the use of a brand-name specification. This justification which follows RFO 6.104 
is based on a review of the acquisition history, an assessment of government risk, and a 
determination of the most logical and suitable solution that serves the best interest of the 
government. 
 
a. Agency and Nature/Description of the action being approved: The purpose of this 
statement of need is to acquire MACE Ex tended Warfare and associated equipment. 
MACE is a full-spectrum battlespace simu lation software for building and executing 
scenarios across multiple domains, simulated in high detail including the full 
electromagnetic spectrum. 
 
b. Description of supplies/services required to meet agency needs: The MACE software 
suite is essential to the Government's requirements as no other product can meet the 
agency's needs without unacceptable schedule delays and duplication of cost. 
 
 
3. Rationale: MACE provides a unique, physics-based, pulse-level modeling of the electromagnetic 
spectrum. This level of detail is not found in other commercially available simulation products and 
is critical for providing realistic training for electronic warfare officers. The MACE software is 
currently approved for use on Department of the Air Force networks per AFI 17-101, Risk 
Management Framework (RMF). Procuring any other brand would require a new, lengthy, and 

CUI 
CUI 
 
 
 
CUI 
costly RMF certification process, causing unacceptable mission delays. MACE is fully integrated 
into the JEWC's existing Live-Virtual-Constructive training architecture. A different brand would 
not be compatible, requiring cost-prohibitive re-integration and testing of the entire network (See 
Attachment 1 – AFI 17-101). 
 
Failure to procure the MACE software licenses would result in a significant degradation of 
advanced electronic warfare training for joint force personnel. Without MACE, warfighters 
cannot be trained in a high-fidelity, contested electromagnetic spectrum that accurately 
replicates modern adversary capabilities. This would directly decrease combat readiness and 
survivability for personnel deploying to operational theaters, creating an unacceptable risk to 
the mission 
 
4. Efforts to Obtain Competition: To maximize competition for this brand name requirement, 
the contracting team conducted market research that yielded seven responses from capable 
vendors, including the manufacturer and severa l small businesses. In itially the results 
support a 100% Small Business Set-Aside,  ensuring robust pri ce competition among 
authorized providers. However, the lowest  quote submitted by small business vendors 
showcased a price of $109K. This is at least $66k more than the IGCE provided by the 
customer. In accordance with RFO 12.102( a) and R-DFARS 211.204, utilizing the Mace 
Software is essential to avoid a substantia l duplication of costs related to full system 
replacement and to preserve existing warranties. The 502 CONS will continue to monitor the 
market for future opportunities to enhance comp etition. or modified fo r compatibility with 
the Mace Software from other companies to meet the agency's needs (See File element 143 for 
more information). 
 
5. Determination of Fair and Reasonable Cost: The CO anticipates that the resulting price for 
MACE software will be fair and reasonable if the government intends to solicit it to small 
and other than small businesses. This determination will be based on adequate price 
competition among the IGCE and vendor quot es received through source sought VIA 
NASW SWEP. IGCE is estimated at $43K, while the quotes submitted by multiple small 
business vendors on their own resulted in the lowest one estimated at $109K, which is a 
153.5% increase. Utilizing this brand name sp ecification ensures the continued integrity 
of existing live virtual constructive traini ng architecture at JBSA, preventing mission 
disruption. Price reasonableness will be determined in accordance with RFO 12.204(a) and R- 
DFARS 212.204 (Attachment 2 & 3). 
 
6. Action taken to Preclude Future Brand Name Awards: To preclude the need for future 
brand name awards, the 502 CONS and the requiring activity will continuously monitor the 
commercial marketplace for emerging MACE softwa re. Prior to subseque nt acquisitions, the 
team will conduct updated market research to determine if other manufacturers have 
developed non-proprietary or open-architecture components th at are fully inter operable 
with the existing infrastructure. Until such comp atible alternatives become available without 
causing a substantial duplication of costs or avoiding existing warranties, the Government will 
continue to maximize business competition by restricting requirements to the solicitation via a 
brand name requirement to small and other than small businesses.

evidenced by my signature below, I certify that the justification is accurate and complete to the

United States Special Operations 
Command (USSOCOM) 
 
 
 
 
Sources Sought Notice 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 


SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE 
Notice Type: Sources Sought / Request for Information (RFI)  
Title: Everfox Cross Domain Solutions (CDS) Hardware and Management Support  
Response Due Date: 15 July 1600PM 
Issued By: HQ USSOCOM 
1. PURPOSE 
This is a Sources Sought Notice for market research purposes only. This is NOT a Request 
for Proposal (RFP), Request for Quote (RFQ), or Invitation for Bid (IFB). No solicitation is 
being issued at this time, and this notice shall not be construed as a commitment by the 
Government to issue a solicitation, nor does it restrict the Government to a particular 
acquisition approach. 
HQUSSOCOM is conducting market research to identify qualiﬁed sources, particularly 
small businesses (including 8(a), HUBZone, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned, and 
Women-Owned small businesses), that are capable of providing the speciﬁc brand name 
hardware, software, and associated services detailed below. 
2. BACKGROUND AND REQUIREMENT 
The Government has a requirement to acquire and deploy secure cross-domain transfer 
capabilities to support mission-critical network environments. To maintain absolute 
compatibility, interoperability, and security compliance with existing cyber security 
infrastructure, the Government requires speciﬁc brand name products from the Original 
Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) Everfox (formerly Forcepoint Federal). 
The government requires the following speciﬁc brand name hardware, software, and 
licensing bundles: 
• Everfox High Speed Guard (HSG) Generation 5 Hardware Bundles 
o Description: High-performance cross domain guard hardware, including 
required platform software and baseline security policies. 
• Everfox Control Center Management Servers 
o Description: Centralized administration and management servers for CDS 
appliance monitoring, conﬁguration, and policy orchestration. 
• Everfox One-Way Transfer Data Diodes 

o Description: Hardware-enforced one-way data transfer appliances to secure 
network segmentation boundaries. 
Note: The Government is seeking authorized resellers capable of providing the exact OEM 
products listed above. Substantial equivalents or "or-equal" items are not being considered 
at this time due to strict cross-domain accreditation and system interoperability 
requirements. 
3. CAPABILITY STATEMENT REQUIREMENTS 
Interested vendors capable of providing the required brand name products are requested 
to submit a Capability Statement. To effectively evaluate market availability, competitive 
viability, and potential contract vehicle pathways, responses must include the following 
information: 
1. Company Proﬁle: 
o Company Name and Address 
o Point of Contact (Name, Title, Email, Phone Number) 
o UEI Number and CAGE Code 
2. Socio-Economic Status: 
o Identify your business size standard for NAICS code 541519 (Other 
Computer Related Services - Information Technology Value Added Resellers - 
150 Employee Size Standard) or alternative suggested NAICS. 
o List any applicable socio-economic designations (e.g., Small Business, 8(a), 
SDVOSB, WOSB, HUBZone). 
3. Contract Vehicles: 
o Identify any Government-Wide Acquisition Contracts (GWACs), Multiple 
Award Schedules (MAS), or Agency-Speciﬁc Contracts (e.g., GSA MAS, NASA 
SEWP V/VI, NIH CIO-CS) your company holds that include the required 
Everfox products. Please provide the speciﬁc contract number(s). 
4. OEM Partnership / Authorized Reseller Status: 
o Provide explicit proof or documentation demonstrating that your company is 
a current, authorized reseller in good standing with Everfox. 
o Important: Indicate whether you are capable of securing independent, 
competitive pricing directly from the OEM for this requirement, or if pricing is 

subject to exclusive OEM deal-registration restrictions that may preclude you 
from offering competitive quotes on this speciﬁc effort. 
4. SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS 
Responses to this Sources Sought must be submitted via email to Kristen Colyer, 
Contracting Officer at kristen.colyer@socom.mil NLT 15 July 1600 
• Please include "Sources Sought Response: Everfox CDS Hardware" in the email 
subject line. 
• Capability statements should be limited to no more than 3 pages. 
5. DISCLAIMER 
Respondents are advised that the Government will not pay for any information or 
administrative costs incurred in response to this Sources Sought. All costs associated with 
responding to this notice will be solely at the responding party's expense. Information 
received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a 
competitive procurement and to determine the appropriate small business set-aside 
strategy.

Vision Statement 
To deliver to the Air Force Weather warfighter, combatant forces, and decision makers a web presence 
for rapid prototype numerical weather products, including Artificial Intelligence based Severe Weather 
Decision tools and a platform for continued, collaborative sharing of the application of numerical weather 
products, and weather forecast techniques. 
 
 
1 Introduction 
This Statement of Need specifies the 16th Weather Squadron’s (16 WS) requirements for a new, 
sustainable cloud computing platform. To meet the ever-changing information environment, 16 WS 
must innovate and rapidly deploy capabilities to match the needs of the warfighter and be equipped to 
communicate the best practices and uses of provided numerical weather products. Additionally, 
Continuity of Operations (COOP) provided by cloud-based computing is critical in meeting the 
previously stated objectives. The requirement is the delivery of access to Amazon Web Services (AWS), 
a Cloud Service Provider (CSP) as defined by the DoD Cloud Computing Security Requirements Guide 
(SRG) in the form of credits, where a credit relates to a dollar of CSP services as purchased by the 
Government. The Contractor shall ensure the CSP is compliant with Federal Risk and Authorization 
Management Program (FedRAMP) and the DoD Cloud Computing SRG. The CSP services/features 
shall comply with the Government’s requirements stated in this document. 
This Statement of Need establishes the parameters for the  BPA as well as overall goals, objectives, 
expectations, responsibilities, and nature of CSP credit delivery orders. The requirements identified 
within this Statement of Need are described in general terms.  Each delivery order shall specifically 
address individual project requirements, project schedules, and other related performance criteria. 
 
 
2 General Requirements 
 
This section describes the general requirements for this BPA (Blanket Purchase Agreement).  The following 
sub-sections provide details of various considerations concerning performance other than desired outcomes. 
2.1 Business Relations 
The Contractor shall coordinate all activity needed to deliver the required capabilities. The Contractor 
shall manage the timeliness, completeness, and quality of the overall contract, as well as the individual 
orders. The Contractor shall be transparent and provide timely notice of any real or perceived problems 
that affect the cost, schedule or performance of orders. The Contractor shall seek to ensure customer 
satisfaction and will ensure the ethical behavior of all Contractor personnel. 
2.2 Closeout 

FA4600-XX-X-XXXX 
Section J, Attachment 1 
 
For all orders, the Contractor shall complete all closeout actions and provide a final release of claims to 
the contracting officer within 180 calendar days after the delivery order is physically complete, as defined 
by FAR 4.804-4. 
For the BPA contract, the Contractor shall complete all necessary closeout actions within one (1) 
calendar year after the BPA is physically complete, as defined by FAR 4.804-4. 
2.3 Data Rights 
Contractor will not have access to the data supplied to the CSP for the Government’s use of the Cloud. 
Government retains all rights to data that it places into the Cloud. With respect to the CSP, the 
Government shall have only the rights specified in the license under which the commercial computer 
software or commercial computer software documentation was obtained IWS R-DFARS 227.7202-3, 
Rights in commercial computer or commercial computer software documentation. 
 
 
3 Requirements 
The following section specifies the overall technological performance required under the BPA and Call 
Orders. 
3.1 Account Management 
The Contractor shall provide the Government root credentials to any and all CSP accounts. The 
Contractor will provide the Government, a Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) hardware token for each 
root account. The Contractor shall be responsible to maintain the payor account for all accounts 
provisioned with the CSP. At the conclusion of the BPA and Call Orders, the Government shall maintain 
all rights to the accounts and credentials as provided. 
3.2 Usage Monitoring/Alerts 
The Contractor shall provide the Government with a 24/7 real-time monitoring capability of credit usage. 
Cautionary Levels of Usage shall be defined as 75% of credits expended. Critical Levels of Usage shall

Where an agency provides support documentation or services for ICT, such documentation and services shall

The technical requirements in Chapter 6 shall apply to ICT support documentation and services where required by 508 
Chapter 2 (Scoping Requirements), 255 Chapter 2 (Scoping Requirements), and where otherwise referenced in any 
other chapter of the Revised 508 Standards or Revised 255 Guidelines. 
 E603.1 General - 
ICT support services including, but not limited to, help desks, call centers, training services, and automated self-service 
technical support, shall conform to 603. 
 E603.2 Information on Accessibility and Compatibility Features - 
ICT support services shall include information on the accessibility and compatibility features required by 602.2. 
 E603.3 Accommodation of Communication Needs - 
Support services shall be provided directly to the user or through a referral to a point of contact. Such ICT support 
services shall accommodate the communication needs of individuals with disabilities. 
Functional Performance Criteria: 
 301.1 Scope - The requirements of Chapter 3 shall apply to ICT where required by 508 Chapter 2 (Scoping 
Requirements), 255 Chapter 2 (Scoping Requirements), and where otherwise referenced in any other chapter of 
the Revised 508 Standards or Revised 255 Guidelines. 
 302.1 Without Vision - Where a visual mode of operation is provided, ICT shall provide at least one mode of 
operation that does not require user vision. 
 302.2 With Limited Vision - Where a visual mode of operation is provided, ICT shall provide at least one mode of 
operation that enables users to make use of limited vision. 
 302.3 Without Perception of Color - Where a visual mode of operation is provided, ICT shall provide at least one 
visual mode of operation that does not require user perception of color. 
 302.4 Without Hearing - Where an audible mode of operation is provided, ICT shall provide at least one mode of 
operation that does not require user hearing. 
 302.5 With Limited Hearing - Where an audible mode of operation is provided, ICT shall provide at least one mode 
of operation that enables users to make use of limited hearing. 
 302.6 Without Speech - Where speech is used for input, control, or operation, ICT shall provide at least one 
mode of operation that does not require user speech. 
 302.7 With Limited Manipulation - Where a manual mode of operation is provided, ICT shall provide at least one mode 
of operation that does not require fine motor control or simultaneous manual operations. 
 302.8 With Limited Reach and Strength - Where a manual mode of operation is provided, ICT shall provide at least one 
mode of operation that is operable with limited reach and limited strength. 
 302.9 With Limited Language, Cognitive, and Learning Abilities - ICT shall provide features  making its use by 
individuals with limited cognitive, language, and learning abilities simpler and easier.

• The VPAT
Please carefully review the Essential Requirements and Best Practices sections before 
using the VPAT to create an Accessibility Conformance Report. 
The purpose of these instructions is to promote accurate and consistent reporting of 
product accessibility information. 
The VPAT is a template used to document a product's conformance with accessibility 
standards and guidelines.  The purpose of the Accessibility Conformance Report is to 
assist customers and buyers in making preliminary assessments regarding the 
availability of commercial "Electronic and Information Technology," also referred to as 
“Information and Communication Technology” (ICT) products and services with features 
that support accessibility. 
The Information Technology Industry Council (ITI) provides the VPAT.  Use of the 
template and service mark does not require membership in ITI. 
CUI

Essential Requirements and Best Practices for 
Information & Communications Technology (ICT) 
Vendors 
This section provides guidance for reporting product conformance for major accessibility 
standards and guidelines using the VPAT® to produce the Accessibility Conformance 
Report.  Deviating from these guidelines precludes vendors from referencing the 
template by name and/or the VPAT acronym. 
Getting Started 
1. Before creating a report, read all of the materials provided in this document.
2. Determine which accessibility standards/guidelines will be included in the product
conformance report and use the appropriate VPAT file.
3. It is the vendor’s responsibility to maintain the integrity of the data in the report.
Essential Requirements for Authors 
The following are the minimum requirements to produce an Accessibility Conformance 
Report based on the VPAT®. 
1. The VPAT name and template are registered service marks of ITI.  Use of the
VPAT template and name requires the inclusion of the registered service mark
(i.e., “VPAT®”).  Users of the VPAT agree not to deviate from the Essential
Requirements for Authors.
2. The template file can be used as is or replicated in a different delivery format, for
example as HTML or PDF.  The final conformance report must be accessible.
3. A report must contain the following content at a minimum:
• Report Title – In the heading format of “[Company Name] Accessibility
Conformance Report”
• VPAT Heading Information – Template version
• Name of Product/Version – Name of Product being reported, including
product version identifier if necessary
CUI

• Report Date – Date of report publication. At a minimum, provide the month
and year of the report publication. For example, “May 2016”. If date is
included, ensure it is clear “4 May 2016” or “May 4, 2016”.
• Product Description – A brief description of the product
• Contact Information – Contact Information for follow-up questions. Listing an
email is sufficient.
• Notes – Any details or further explanation about the product or the report.
This section may be left blank.
• Evaluation Methods Used – Include a description of evaluation methods
used to complete the VPAT for the product under test.
• Applicable Standards/Guidelines – A clear indication of which
Standards/Guidelines this Conformance Report covers.
• The list must include only the Standards/Guidelines used to evaluate
the product.
• A report must contain a minimum of one Standard/Guideline or any
combination of the Standards.
• The applicable Standards/Guidelines that may be included are:
 Web Content Accessibility Guidelines 2.0 or WCAG 2.0
(ISO/IEC 40500) 
 Web Content Accessibility Guidelines 2.1 or WCAG 2.1
 EN 301 549 Accessibility requirements suitable for public
procurement of ICT products and services in Europe, - V3.1.1
(2019-11) 
• If other Standards/Guidelines are reported then use the appropriate
VPAT edition.
• This information can be in a table format at the top of the report with
the table heading ‘Standards/Guidelines’ and the reported
Standards/Guidelines identified. This information can alternatively be
supplied in the introductory text of the report. In the VPAT we have
used a table as an example and listed “(yes / no)” for each
standard/guideline. To indicate what the report covers leave the
appropriate yes or no on each standard/guideline.
• If multiple Standards or Guideline tables are included, each table must
identify the Standard or Guideline that the criteria in that table
represent.
• Terms – The report must list the definition of the terms used in the
Conformance Level column. ITI recommends the following terms. If a vendor
CUI

deviates from the ITI definitions, the vendor shall reference this change in the 
heading Notes section. If a term is not used it can be removed from the list. 
The ITI definitions are:   
• Supports: The functionality of the product has at least one method
that meets the criterion without known defects or meets with equivalent
facilitation.
• Partially Supports: Some functionality of the product does not meet
the criterion.
• Does Not Support: The majority of product functionality does not meet
the criterion.
• Not Applicable: The criterion is not relevant to the product.
Note: When filling in the WCAG tables, a response may use 'Supports' where 
one might otherwise be inclined to use 'Not Applicable'.  This is in keeping 
with 
WCAG 2.0 Understanding Conformance: This means that if there is no 
content to which a success criterion applies, the success criterion is satisfied. 
• Not Evaluated: The product has not been evaluated against the
criterion.  This can only be used in WCAG 2.x Level AAA.
• Tables for Each Standard or Guideline – Tables showing the responses to
the criteria.
5. WCAG Conformance Information – The answers in the WCAG success criteria
are based on the level of conformance being reported (Level A, AA or AAA).
• These tables are used to answer:
• EN 301 549 Standard:
• Chapter 9 Web
• Chapter 10 Non-Web
• Chapter 11 Software
• Chapter 12 Documentation and Support Services
• The selected levels of WCAG 2.x Guidelines.
• The WCAG conformance information can either be included in the provided
WCAG section of the report which is cross-referenced from the EN 301 549
responses, or the WCAG information can be incorporated within the EN 304
549 section of the report. The information does not need to be duplicated.
• If using summary tables, due to answers applying to multiple criteria, when
answering for the EN 301 549, the answers need to be clear about which
individual criteria the answer applies to. It is possible to either use a
summary, selecting the worst case for the criteria, or to have separate
CUI

answers or even tables for software, support documentation, authoring tools, 
etc., so long as the methodology used is made clear. 
6. Remarks and Explanations – Detailed remarks should be provided in the
Remarks and Explanations column to justify your answer in the Conformance
Level column.
• When the conformance level is ‘Partially Supports’ or ‘Does Not Support’, the
remarks should identify:
1. The functions or features with issues
2. How they do not fully support
• If the criterion does not apply, explain why.
• If an accessible alternative is used, describe it.
Best Practices for Authors 
ITI suggests that authors adopt the following best practices when using the VPAT® to 
create an Accessibility Conformance Report.  
• Branding Header: Company logo or branding information
• Report Date Changes: If a report is revised, change the report date and
explain the revision in the Notes section.  Alternately, create a new report and
explain in the Notes section that it supersedes an earlier version of the report.
• Notes: Add any notes applicable to product or the report
• Additional information about the product version that the document
references
• Any revisions to the document
• Links to any related documents
• Additional information describing the product
• Additional information about what the document does or does not
cover
• Information suggested by the WCAG 2.0 Conformance Claim
• Information needed to satisfy ISO/IEC 17050-1:2004, Supplier’s
Declaration of Conformity
• Evaluation Methods Used – Information to enter may include the following:
• Testing is based on general product knowledge
• Similar to another evaluated product
CUI

• Testing with assistive technologies
• Published test method (provide name, publisher, URL link)
• Vendor proprietary test method
• Other test method

• Information regarding the testing of a given criteria.
• Information on application dependencies to support accessibility (e.g.
OS, app frameworks, browsers recommended).
• How the customer can find more information about accessibility issues.

Statement of Work Mission First Solutions LLC (Data Innovations Instrument Manager) 
STATEMENT OF WORK 
1. Introduction 
This Statement of Work (SOW) is issued in accordance with FAR Part 12 for the acquisition 
of commercial items. The contractor shall provide all Instrument Manager licenses and 
develop instrument interfaces/drivers for all the instruments used at the donor center (to 
include current equipment: Ortho Vision, Dynex DS2, Abbott Alinity S, and Panther Hologic 
and future equipment to include similar equipment with the same testing profiles [ex: Ortho 
Vision Max]) that will interface (non-APIUPLD; direct HL7/TCP-IP transfer) and enable 
secure, automated electronic transfer of donor testing results to the donor’s center Enterprise 
Blood Management System – Donor (EBMS-D).  
2. Description of Service 
- Establish automated data transfer from analyzers into EBMS-D. 
- Replace manual dual-entry processes that pose safety risks and require two technicians. 
- Provide drivers and instrument interfaces for current or future FDA required tests to include: 
ABO/Rh typing, titers, syphilis, HIV , HTLV 1/2, hepatitis (HBsAg, HCV , HBc), Chagas, 
Nucleic Acid Testing (NAT) Ultrio, Babesia, West Nile Virus. 
- Ensure automated data transfers into EBMS-D that pass Quality Control, Calibrations, 
Analyzer Self-Checks/Equivalents or ASBBC (Armed Services Blood Donor Center) listed 
criteria to prevent erroneous or unwanted results from being transferred into EBMS-D.  
- Ensure interoperability with DHA-certified middleware and EBMS-D environments. 
The Defense Health Agency (DHA) cybersecurity, FDA 510(k), and Risk Management 
Framework (RMF)/Authority to Operate (ATO) certification requirements must be fully met. 
DHA Server Configuration Management (CM) will be provided by the Government. 
- Provide turnkey implementation with vendor-supplied coding, configuration, and guidance 
on validation.  
- The contractor’s software must currently reside on the active DHA Approved Products List 
(APL) and possess an active, fully validated DHA Authority to Operate (ATO) at the time of 
contract award to prevent mission-critical testing and delivery delays. 
- The software solution must fully integrate into the existing Armed Services Blood Program 
Configuration Management (CM) baseline. Maintaining this identical CM baseline is a non-
negotiable technical requirement to ensure interoperability and real-time synchronization 
with the Enterprise Blood Management System - Donor (EBMS-D). 
- The contractor must hold exclusive proprietary and distribution rights for the specific 
integration drivers and middleware configurations required to interface the local blood donor 
testing instrumentation with EBMS-D. 
 
 

Statement of Work Mission First Solutions LLC (Data Innovations Instrument Manager) 
3.Contractor requirement 
Data Innovations Instrument Manager licenses and drivers for all the analyzers used at the donor 
center.  
- Development of instrument interfaces (non-APIUPLD; direct HL7/TCP-IP transfer). 
- Configuration of workflows to allow technician certification of results inside EBMS-D. 
- Onsite and remote installation, integration, and coding support. 
- Initial onsite support for at least one week during implementation. 
- Training for ASBBC personnel in troubleshooting, adding new analyzers/tests, and 
maintaining interfaces. 
- Ongoing customer service, including remote and on-site support as needed. 
- The Contractor shall create a dedicated reporting drive within Data Innovations Instrument 
Manager to allow automated compilation and export of donor testing data. 
o Eligibility Reports:  
 Prescreening report: A specific report must be designed to track donor 
eligibility for future donations. The report will display whether a donor is 
cleared or deferred based on infectious disease testing results.  
 Custom reports: The ability to create and configure costume reports for 
specific data points.  
o Template: ASBBC staff will provide the reporting template, and the Contractor will 
configure and validate the report accordingly. 
o Access & Usability: Reports must be easily accessible to authorized users, exportable 
in standard formats (e.g., PDF, Excel), and stored securely in compliance with DHA 
and DoD IT standards. 
o Performance Standard: Reports must generate accurate results 100% of the time and 
be updated in real time with certified test data. 
- The contractor shall adhere to FDA regulations and requirements for medical devices. Refer 
to the Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) Food and Drugs: Title 21 Part 210, 211, 600, 601, 
606, 607, 610, 630, 640, 660, Part 820, Part 1270, Part 1271, and Public Health, Title 42 Part 
493. 
- Contractor shall perform initial onsite setup, coding, and configuration of DI IM, remaining 
onsite for at least one week to support implementation, then provide additional remote 
support as needed. 
- Contractor shall collaborate with DHA EBMS program offices and local Information 
Technology Department (ITD) to align interface validation and ticket submissions. 
The contractor must ensure the software maintains its status on the DHA Approved Products 
List (APL) and complies with all active RMF/ATO requirements. Any software deployed 
must possess an active ATO without a valid ATO, the program cannot be added to the 
network, which would prevent automated result entry and review. 

Statement of Work Mission First Solutions LLC (Data Innovations Instrument Manager) 
- Contractor shall ensure flexible interface architecture to support future analyzer swaps or 
additions without major recoding. 
- Contractor shall provide a schedule of standard maintenance and expected downtimes 
4. Inspection and acceptability 
Deliverables shall be inspected and accepted by ITD and ASBBC’s designated Technical POC. 
Acceptance criteria: successful bi-directional transfer of results into EBMS-D, verified through 
validation protocols and technician approval workflows. 
- Installation shall be initiated within 90 days of contract award.  
- Installed and configured DI IM system. 
- Documented interface specifications and configuration guides. 
- Training materials and user troubleshooting manuals. 
- Final validation test report demonstrating successful end-to-end transfer into EBMS-D. 
5. Responsibilities 
Contractor: Develop drivers, configure interfaces, code system integrations, provide training and 
support (shall accommodate for Japan Time Zone).  
- Government: Provide servers, workstation hardware, secure network access, and SMEs to 
support validation.  
6. Location of services  
Services will be performed at the ASBBC Okinawa facility, with a combination of onsite 
(minimum of one week during initial implementation) and remote support thereafter. 
Location: 
 
Building #: Camp Foster building 968 
Room#: Room 206 and Room 203A  
 
7. Period of Performance  
Implementation shall be completed within 180 days of contract award. 
8. Warranty and support  
The Contractor shall provide maintenance, including software patching, driver updates, and 
customer service support yearly. Custom service support will be provided to accommodate Japan 
Standard Time Zone (Monday to Friday 0700-1800).

Notice of Intent to Sole Source 
HT941026N0060 
 
THIS IS A NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD A SOLE SOURCE SUPPLY CONTRACT AND IS 
NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE QUOTES. The Defense Health Agency Contracting Activity 
(DHACA), Healthcare Contracting Division – West (HCD-W), San Diego, intends to negotiate and award 
a firm fixed price contract for Data Innovations Instrument Manager Licenses and Drivers for all 
analyzers used at Armed Services Blood Donor Center (ASBBC) in accordance with Federal Acquisition 
Regulation Overhaul (RFO) 12.102(a), for purchases valued at or below the simplified acquisition 
threshold, only one source reasonably available to: 
 
Locked Core Tech, LLC (Mission First Solutions LLC) 
18304 Cabin RD 
Triangle, Virginia 22172 
 
The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is 541511 - 
Custom Computer Programming Services; the business size standard is $34.0M. The Product Service 
Code (PSC) is DA01 - IT and Telecom - Business Application/application Development Support Services 
(labor). 
 
The objective of this sole source award is to procure Data Innovations Instrument Manager (DI IM) 
middleware platform for the Armed Services Blood Bank Center (ASBBC) located at U. S. Naval 
Hospital Okinawa (USNHO), Japan. 
 
The requirement is to procure and implement the Data Innovations Instrument Manager (DI IM) 
middleware through Locked Core Tech LLC (formally Mission First Solutions LLC) to establish 
automated bidirectional interfaces between five infectious disease testing analyzers at the Armed Services 
Blood Bank Center (ASBBC) Okinawa and the Enterprise Blood Management System – Donor (EBMS-
D). The DI IM middleware will automate transmission of test orders, specimen data, quality control 
information, and finalized results between laboratory instruments and EBMS-D, eliminating manual data 
entry and reducing the risk of transcription and reporting errors. The solution will improve workflow 
efficiency, enhance data integrity and regulatory compliance, minimize turnaround time for infectious 
disease testing, and support the rapid release and availability of donor testing results for blood product 
processing and distribution operations. 
 
Only two sites within the DoD maintain donor infectious disease testing capabilities: Lackland AFB 
Blood Donor Center and ASBBC Okinawa. This severely limits the Government’s options for 
middleware solutions, as interoperability and standardization between these two sites is critical to mission 
readiness. Currently, technicians at ASBBC Okinawa are required to manually enter results, a process that 
introduces safety concerns due to transcription errors, and requires two technicians to verify results. 
 
Locked Core Tech LLC, utilizing the Data Innovations Instrument Manager (DI IM) middleware 
platform, is the only known source capable of providing a fully validated and DoD-acceptable 
middleware solution that interfaces multiple blood donor infectious disease analyzers with the Laboratory 
Information System (LIS) while satisfying all Department of Defense cybersecurity, Defense Health 
Agency (DHA) accreditation, and enterprise interoperability requirements. 
 
 
Period of Performance: 
Base Period:   01 September 2026 to 31 August 2027 
Option Period 1: 01 September 2027 to 31 August 2028 

Option Period 2: 01 September 2028 to 31 August 2029 
Option Period 3: 01 September 2029 to 31 August 2030 
Option Period 4: 01 September 2030 to 31 August 2031 
 
Services will be performed at the ASBBC Okinawa facility, with a combination of onsite (minimum of 
one week during initial implementation) and remote support thereafter. 
Location: 
U. S. Naval Hospital Okinawa, Japan 
Building: Camp Foster building 968 
Room: Room 206 and Room 203A

REQUEST FOR INFORMATION  
 
A. Introduction 
 
1. The NATO Communications and Information Agency (NC IA) is conducting market 
research to identify potential sources and gather information regarding industry 
capabilities to suppor t the development of a comprehensive red team operations 
management system . This Request for Information (RFI) is issued solely for 
informational purposes and does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), 
Request for Quotation (RFQ), or invitation for bid.  
 
B. Purpose 
 
1. The purpose of this RFI is to obtain input from industry to help inform the NCIA’s 
acquisition planning. Responses to this RFI will assist in refining requirements, 
identifying capabilities, and shaping the strategy for any future solicitation. 
 
C. Background 
 
1. NCIA requires a Red Team Mission Planning, Execution, and Debriefing (RT-MPEDS) 
system to manage the complete lifecycle of NATO red team operations, from initial 
planning through active execution to comprehensive debriefing and archiving. The RT-
MPEDS system must integrate multiple specialized components that address specific 
phases of the red team operations lifecycle. 
 
2. Current tooling in this domain is fragmented: planners rely on generic platforms with no 
Red Team context; operators use disconnected custom-built tools; debriefing is handled 
offline, resulting in loss of knowledge, Indicators of Compromise (IOC) reuse risk, and 
inadequate audit trails.  
 
3. The RT-MPEDS system will support NATO's cyber defense capabilities by providing 
red teams with advanced tools for mission planning, real -time operations 
management, evidence collection, and comprehensive reporting, while ensuring 
operational security and compliance with NATO policies. 
 
4. High-level Objectives: 
1. Deliver an integrated, open -source platform that covers the full Red Team 
lifecycle: mission planning, execution, and debriefing. 
2. Eliminate dependence on fragmented, generic tooling by providing purpose -
built components with Red Team operational context. 
3. Implement dual -control (four -eyes) security mechanisms for sensitive 
operations including Tool Vault access. 
4. Ensure all intellectual property is fully owned by NCIA, with full source code 
access and no proprietary lock-in 
 
5. Expected Outcome: 
The target outcome is to use the information collected to develop our acquisition 
strategy for an upcoming procurement. The procurement will aim to establish a partner 
to deliver the required system with the following high-level components:  
• Mission Planning Component: Provide comprehensive mission planning 
capabilities with automated infrastructure provisioning and configuration 
management.  

 
 
 
  
 Page 6 
 
 
• Mission Execution Component: Provide real -time operational management, 
monitoring, and collaboration capabilities during active red team engagements.  
• Mission Debriefing Component: Enable comprehensive post-mission analysis, 
reporting, knowledge capture to improve future operations, archiving and 
auditing capabilities.  
• Mission Debriefing Component: Enable comprehensive post-mission analysis, 
tracking of findings and remediation measures,  reporting, knowledge capture 
to improve future operations, archiving and auditing capabilities.  
 
The scope and initial requirements are further elaborated in Annex B, C and D.

costs incurred in responding to this RFI.  The NCIA will consider and  analyse all 
information received from this RFI and may use these findings to develop a future 
solicitation. The NCIA will consider all responses as confidential commercial 
information and will protect it as such.

SINGLE SOURCE DETERMINATION USING 
SIMPLIFIED ACQUISITION PROCEDURES (SAP)   
FOR AN ACTION NOT EXCEEDING THE SIMPLIFIED ACQUISITION THRESHOLD 
 (AUTHORITY: 12.102(a) and 41 USC 1901)  
 
PR# 143011-26-0164 
 
 
1. Agency and contracting activity. Department of Commerce, Fisheries OMB Field Delegates and 
National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS), Office of Law Enforcement (OLE), Pacific Islands 
Division (PID) 
 
2. Description of supplies or services required to meet agency needs (including the estimated 
value).  
The NOAA OLE Pacific Islands Division (PID) requires a web-based, satellite and terrestrial 
Automatic Identification System (AIS) data analysis application service. This subscription will 
provide three (3) concurrent-user accounts with uncompromised, wide-breadth satellite AIS data 
showing real-time and historical positions of U.S. and foreign commercial fishing vessels. 
• Intended Use: This application is mission-critical for remote tracking, compliance analysis, 
and detecting illicit maritime activity, such as dark-vessel behaviors, illegal transshipments, 
and Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) boundary incursions, to detect, investigate, and 
counter Illegal, Unreported, and Unregulated (IUU) fishing. 
• Period of Performance / Delivery: Access must be active within one (1) calendar week of 
contract award. The service must include access to not less than 3 years of historical vessel 
position data. 
• Estimated Value: $75,000 
• Contract Type: Firm-Fixed-Price (Subscription Service) 
  
3. Identification of the single source or the brand name to be solicited.  
Vendor Name: Starboard Maritime Intelligence Limited 
c/o NORTHWEST REGISTERED AGENT SERVICE 
8 The Green Suite Suite A 
Dover, DE 19901 
Unique Entity Identifier (UEI): ZA59BMNSBL29 
Contact Info: Mat Brown (mat.brown@starboardintelligence.com)
 
 
4. Supporting rationale. Only one source or brand name is reasonably available as detailed below:  
 
□ Exclusive Licensing Agreement/Restrictive Rights/Authorized Reseller - The source has one 
or more of the following: an established exclusive licensing agreement, proprietary data, 
limited rights in data, patent rights, OEM required certifications or OEM authorized reseller, 
copyrights or secret processes with regard to the supplies or services required.  
 
Only the Starboard Maritime Intelligence web application is capable of providing the 
supplies or services required at the level of quality required because the supplies or 
services are unique or highly specialized.  
 
Supporting Narrative & Unique Qualifications: While multiple commercial vendors 
provide general-purpose maritime AIS tracking data, Starboard Maritime Intelligence is 
the only specialized web-based platform built from the ground up to support the 
international, multilateral counter-IUU fishing (IUUF) in the Pacific. 

 
 
PR# 143011-26-0164 
 
2 of 3 
 
 
• Mandated International Interoperability: Under the SAFE Act and the U.S. 
Interagency Working Group on IUU Fishing 5-Year Strategy, OLE PID is required to 
execute a whole-of-government approach and coordinate enforcement with regional 
partners. Starboard is uniquely designed to integrate directly with the systems used by 
major regional fisheries management bodies, specifically the Western and Central 
Pacific Fisheries Commission (WCPFC) and the Pacific Islands Forum Fisheries Agency 
(FFA). 
• Alignment with Regional Joint Operations: Starboard is the designated AIS analyst 
tool of the FFA. It utilizes exact data formatting, standards, and export functionalities that 
seamlessly cross-verify against the FFA's Regional Surveillance Picture (RSP) and 
registry compliance tracking datasets. No other software natively aligns with these 
regional threat vectors. 
• Actionable Mission Collaboration: PID analysts routinely support and collaborate with 
the FFA’s Regional Fisheries Surveillance Center (RFSC) and joint U.S. Coast 
Guard/Shiprider missions. Because Starboard is already utilized by the USCG, JIATF-
West, and the FFA, it provides a common IUUF operating picture across the Pacific. 
This allows PID to seamlessly generate and share actionable intelligence regarding 
high-risk "dark" vessel behavior and unsanctioned high-seas transshipments. 
 
Mission Impact if Not Approved: If forced to procure a standard, general-purpose 
commercial maritime tool, NOAA OLE PID will lose its technical compatibility with key 
international defense and enforcement partners. Technicians will be unable to readily 
export or correlate data within multinational joint operations windows, creating critical 
blind spots during high-seas enforcement operations and directly degrading the agency's 
ability to successfully investigate and prosecute sensitive international fisheries cases. 
 
5. Market Research. 
 
Market research was conducted by PID personnel who have actively tested, demoed, or utilized all 
primary maritime surveillance tools in this space. Three major U.S. Small Business schedule 
holders were evaluated: 
1. Kpler Inc. (Marine Traffic Enterprise): Evaluated at ~$25,000/year for 5 licenses. While cost-
effective, it is a general-purpose tool that lacks native integrations (such as EO/IR or RF 
overlays) and features no tailoring for the counter-IUUF mission or regional partner frameworks. 
It cannot meet the international interoperability requirements of the PID. 
2. Windward US Inc.: Evaluated as an excellent AI-driven maritime analysis tool containing the 
required AIS feeds. However, it is not tailored to regional partner frameworks or joint Pacific 
operations. Furthermore, it is cost-prohibitive at approximately $90,000 per single license 
(~$270,000 for the required three concurrent-user seats), making it financially unviable. 
3. Starboard Maritime Intelligence: Priced at $75,000 for three licenses. It possesses identical 
core AIS tracking data as competitors but stands alone as a highly specialized, mission-tailored 
platform that natively meets all international interoperability, Class B priority filters, and partner-
sharing capabilities required by the government. 
 
6. Technical/Requirements Representative Certification  
 
I certify that this requirement constitutes the Government’s minimum needs and the 
supporting data provided herein is accurate and complete to the best of my knowledge and 
belief. 
  

 
 
PR# 143011-26-0164 
 
3 of 3 
 
 
 
_____________________________________ __6/25/2026_________  
Sylvia Scott Date 
Budget Analyst, NOAA OLE

reasonably available. This determination is accurate and complete to the best of my knowledge and 
belief.

Questions and Answers – RFI Amendment 0002

	

Date: January 8, 2026

The following questions have been submitted for Request for Information 36C10B26Q0104, IBM Mainframe as a Service. Please see Question and Answer matrix below for further details. All questions submitted on December 22, 2025, through January 8, 2026, have been captured in this document.  

Question # | Question | Government Response

1 | I am attempting to find out if there is an incumbent contract. Can you please send me the previous contract information/incumbent info?
 | There is currently no single incumbent contract that performs all requirements listed in the RFI. The current solution is made up of one task order for IBM mainframe capacity, one task order for mainframe contractor support and multiple task orders for the software solutions listed in RFI Attachment 1. 

The IBM mainframe capacity is currently being provided through VA’s IBM Capacity as a Service (CaaS) Task Order with Sirius Computer Solutions, Inc. 

The mainframe contractor labor is currently being provided through VA’s Franchise Fund Support Services (FFSS) Task Order with Tista Science and Technology Corporation.


2 | Is the ability for a contractor candidate to be able to provide Mainframe Hosting a requirement, or would a candidate providing primarily Mainframe SW Support also be considered? If the answer is the latter (Mainframe SW Support only), then:

Can you provide the SW version/release and/or maintenance levels for each OEM product listed in VA’s “Attachment 1” spreadsheet?
  
In the RFI, section “2.0 Background” indicates that a staff mix of VA full-time employees and contractors. Is the direction of the VA to retain their current staff mix and/or seek outside staff augmentation, or is the VA looking to have the existing staff be available to be hired/rehired by the potential vendor awarded the Support contract?
 | The VA is seeking a Contractor that can provide a complete Mainframe as a Service (MFaaS) solution to include all hardware support, software support, and labor. If you cannot provide all components of requirement, list any limitations you may have in your response.

All Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) software used in conjunction with the Mainframe is tested internally and at the current vendor supported versions. VA requires that the software continues to be tested and upgraded as new versions are released.

VA is seeking a Contractor to perform all labor for a complete MFaaS solution.

3 | In your Mainframe-as-a-Service model, do you anticipate the provider assuming ownership of the underlying hardware and software entitlements, or will those entitlements remain under the agency’s authority? Understanding your approach to entitlement management will help us better align with your objectives around governance, control, and portability.
 | The VA does not intend to own the hardware or subscription-based software. VA’s intent is for the Vendor to provide all needed hardware (currently being provided as a Capacity as a Service model with IBM equipment, detailed in RFI section 2), subscription-based software, and software maintenance for VA-owned perpetual licenses.

VA would retain ownership of VA-owned perpetual licenses. 
The Vendor would be responsible for providing continued maintenance on VA-owned perpetual licenses. 
For subscription-based licenses, the Vendor would be responsible for ownership and renewal of those annual entitlements.


4 | Is it at all possible to request a one or two week extension on the due date and have a January 16 or 23 due date, instead of January 9th?
 | VA will extend to January 16, 2026, but does not anticipate further extension.

1.0 INTRODUCTION

THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) ONLY.  This request is for planning purposes only and does not constitute a Request for Quotation (RFQ), a solicitation, or an indication that the Government will award a contract for the items contained in this RFI. In accordance with FAR 15.201(e), responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. The Government does not reimburse respondents for any costs associated with submission of the information being requested or reimburse expenses incurred for responses to this RFI. Responders are solely responsible for all expenses associated with responding to this RFI. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future RFQ, if any issued. Any information submitted by respondents to this RFI is strictly voluntary. All submissions become Government Property and will not be returned. Companies are encouraged to respond if they have the capability and/or capacity to provide the items identified in this RFI. This RFI notice is part of the Government’s Market Research, a continuous process for obtaining the latest information from industry, with respect to their current and near-term abilities. Interested parties are responsible for adequately marking proprietary, restricted or competition sensitive information contained in their response. All information received in response to this RFI that is marked as proprietary will be handled accordingly.

The NAICS for this requirement is 518210 (Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services). The Small Business Size Standard is $40 Million average annual receipts. Small Business companies with the capability to perform this requirement, in total or in part, are encouraged to participate. If you are interested only in subcontracting opportunities, please indicate this fact clearly in your submission. Should you believe a different NAICS code better applies to the requirement requested under this request for information please provide your suggestions in your response to the RFI. Please indicate your company size and socio-economic status for applicable NAICS codes.

Be advised that set-aside decisions may be made based on the information provided in response to this RFI. Responses should be as complete and informative as possible.

The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) is seeking a contractor with deep expertise and proven experience in running, operating, and managing mainframe environments, specifically tailored to the comprehensive requirements outlined in this RFI. The prime contractor, not a subcontractor, shall possess deep expertise and proven experience in running, operating, and managing these environments and must have a demonstrated track record of recruiting strong mainframe talent. This RFI seeks vendors, with experience in International Business Machines Corporation (IBM) mainframe support, to submit their capabilities and suggested approaches to meeting the specified outcomes-based requirements through a Mainframe-as-a-Service (MFaaS) solution. 

Currently, the IBM mainframe support team operates in the Office of Information Technology (OIT) Infrastructure Operations (IO) pillar, providing critical support for IBM Mainframes hosting various applications critical for VA business and mission initiatives.

 

2.0 BACKGROUND

Hardware: VA applications run on two IBM Z16 Mainframes hosted by the Enterprise Data Centers located in Austin, TX and Philadelphia, PA. The solution also consists of two Virtual Tape Systems, IBM TS7770, one located at the Austin Information Technology Center and the second located at the Philadelphia Information Technology Center.

Software: The current software solution consists of software from 22 separate original equipment manufacturers (OEM) software providers that are procured, installed, managed, and run on the IBM Z16 Mainframes. A complete list of software is included as Attachment 1.   

Applications: The VA hosts approximately 60 VA applications on the IBM Z16 mainframes. VA can flex the number of applications up or down depending on VA’s needs. As VA needs change, applications may migrate on or off the IBM Z16 platform, thus increasing or decreasing the number of hosted applications.

Services/Labor: The VA currently manages the solution with a mix of VA full-time employees and contractor staff. The labor force operates primarily in a remote setting and performs during normal business hours with call back. In the event of an emergency or hardware upgrade, employees may be required to be temporarily on-site for the fix or upgrade.

The Contractor shall offer support across multiple scenarios defined below, including day shifts, normal business hours, callbacks, after hours, weekends, and Federal holidays.
