Earthquake Science Center Science and Technical Services Support (ESATS) 
Statement of Work (SOW) 
 
A.  INTRODUCTION 
General Background 
The Earthquake Science Center (ESC) is home to earthquake hazard and mitigation 
research as well as several ground motion monitoring and earthquake notiﬁcation eƯorts – 
the Earthquake Notiﬁcation Service (ENS), the National Strong Motion Project (NSMP), the 
Northern California Seismic Network (NCSN), the Paciﬁc Northwest Seismic Network 
(PNSN), the Southern California Integrated Geodetic Network (SCIGN), the Southern 
California Seismic Network (SCSN), Operational Aftershock Forecasting (OAF), Induced 
Seismicity, and the USGS ShakeAlert Earthquake Early Warning Project (EEW).  These 
scientiﬁc and monitoring eƯorts collaborate closely with university partners in their 
respective geographic regions.  These combined eƯorts advance scientiﬁc research in 
numerous ﬁelds of seismology, geodesy, and geophysics. Collectively they operate more 
than 2000 ground motion monitoring stations, over 200 telemetry relays, and several data 
collection and analysis centers.  Field data is telemetered in near real time to collection 
and analysis centers, where geophysical software creates and distributes a variety of 
products based on the data received.  The ﬁeld data is also archived and used for research 
projects, which advance the state of the art in seismology, geodesy, and geophysics and is 
used to improve monitoring eƯorts and products.  These combined research and 
monitoring eƯorts provide earthquake monitoring and hazard mitigation to a geographic 
region containing over 50 million people and help prepare for expansion of earthquake 
early warning into other areas. In addition, these eƯorts have substantial impact on 
earthquake monitoring and notiﬁcation standards and methods across the USGS 
Advanced National Seismic System and provide earthquake response products used both 
nationally and globally. 
 
Contract Background 
This will be an Indeﬁnite Delivery / Indeﬁnite Quantity (IDIQ) contract for a broad range of 
services where the scope includes, but is not limited to scientiﬁc software development, 
data science, full stack dev/ops, network engineering, cybersecurity, and systems 
administration services and support for scientiﬁc monitoring systems as described in the 
general service areas listed herein.  Under the IDIQ contract, individual Task Orders (TOs) 

140G0326R0003  SOW, Page 2 of 25 
 
covering speciﬁc software, science, or IT related services will be issued for various tasks 
within the general scope of this statement of work.  These individual TOs will specify the 
nature of the work, the objectives, the desired results of work performed, milestone 
schedule(s), and similar task requirements to be accomplished, along with applicable 
metrics used to evaluate successful performance for the TO at hand. 
 
Contract Type 
Task Orders will be issued either on a Performance-Based Firm-Fixed Price (FFP) basis; or 
on a Time and Materials (T&M) – Labor Hour (LH) basis, depending on the nature of the 
tasks.  The government’s preference is for performance-based ﬁxed price (FFP) orders to 
the maximum extent possible, although situations may dictate that T&M/LH orders would 
be appropriate in particular circumstances.  The contract is structured to allow TOs of 
either (or both) type to be issued as circumstances warrant, and as determined by the 
contracting oƯicer. 
 
B.  CONTRACTOR REQUIREMENTS 
The scope of the contract activities will encompass scientiﬁc software development, data 
science, and scientiﬁc monitoring systems-related IT across ESC.  While speciﬁc tasking 
will be detailed in individual task orders issued against this contract, the general scope of 
the support activities that could be or may be ordered is described throughout this 
Statement of Work.  The Contractor shall provide the capacity, capability, and resources 
necessary to perform and manage all the technical and management activities required for 
successful and timely completion of task orders issued under this contract. 
 
C.  SCIENTIFIC AND TECHNICAL SERVICES REQUIRED 
The Contractor shall provide non-personal services in the following service areas to various 
organizational units of the ESC as speciﬁcally deﬁned in individual task orders.   As 
currently established, the needs of ESC are represented in the four major subparagraphs in 
this Section C (C.1, C.2, C.3, and C.4).  While these Section C requirements are organized 
in this way for convenience, there is overlap between and among the ESC’s scientiﬁc 
software packages, ground motion monitoring networks, data science projects, and 
research projects.  Task orders may reﬂect this. 

140G0326R0003  SOW, Page 3 of 25 
 
The types of scientiﬁc software development, data science projects, research support, and 
information technology services to be ordered under this IDIQ contract include, but are not 
limited to: scientiﬁc software maintenance, operations, and development; scientiﬁc data 
and information management and analytics; computer system administration in support of 
scientiﬁc research and ground motion monitoring networks; technical applications 
engineering; database design and development;  full stack Dev/Ops engineering; and 
computer network engineering in support of scientiﬁc research and ground motion 
monitoring networks.  All work will be performed in Linux/Unix environments that are 
subject to US Government cybersecurity and other regulations (OWASP Top 10 and federal 
mandates, e.g. FISMA, NIST SP 800-53, etc.). 
It should be noted that as an IDIQ contract, the exact description of the scientiﬁc software, 
data science projects, research support, and IT services to be ordered is, by design, 
indeﬁnite.  When this Statement of Work (SOW) uses the phrase “the contract may 
require” , or “services may be ordered” , or other similar phraseology, the intent is that the 
listing or recitation of services or functions that follow are typical examples of the services 
that may be ordered, not a limitation on the services to be ordered.  In addition, generally 
when a list of tools or software development languages appears (e.g., “Python, C++, 
Django, etc. ” or “ActiveMQ, NATS, etc. ”) these listings are also considered to be typical 
examples, rather than exhaustive lists or limitations. 
 
C.1. Scientiﬁc Application Services 
 Task order requirements in the scientiﬁc application services area may include: 
 C.1.1 Scienti ﬁc Software Development – Requires expertise and contractor staƯ 
support for the entire software development life cycle from the requirements, design, and 
implementation stages to maintenance, performance analysis, and technical support 
functions for geophysical software applications (both research and operational).  Maintain 
and upgrade existing applications, as well as design and write new applications using the 
appropriate languages (e.g. Python, C++, Java, etc.).  Migrate scientiﬁc software packages 
to the USGS Cloud Hosting Solutions (CHS) environment.  Prepare documentation for 
technical and scientiﬁc applications; prepare code level test plans, develop data to test 
code changes, and perform parallel tests of old and modiﬁed systems.  Most geophysical 
software applications used at the ESC require a deep knowledge of seismology, geodesy, 
geophysics, mathematics, or physics for proper bug detection and ﬁxing, as well as 
analysis of code results for scientiﬁc soundness. 

140G0326R0003  SOW, Page 4 of 25 
 
C.1.2 Scienti ﬁc Application Support – Requires expertise in operation and 
performance analysis of scientiﬁc computer systems suƯicient to  perform the following 
functions:  scientiﬁc application conﬁguration, application backup, software installation 
and maintenance, software license maintenance, analysis of  server utilization and 
application performance; execute security audits  to ensure compliance with established 
USGS policies; system administration, resource management, and systems analysis  to 
ensure eƯicient use of computing resources. 
 
 C.1.3 Database Development and Integration – Requires knowledge of database 
integration standards such as RESTful APIs and ETL pipelines, database architectures such 
as MongoDB, MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQL, and NoSQL solutions, along with cloud-native 
services (e.g. AWS RDS, Azure SQL, etc.).  Services required may include software 
installation, maintenance, enhancements to existing databases, troubleshooting, 
performance tuning, capacity planning and resource management, setup of new database 
instances from data design documents, the development of new and modiﬁed database 
implementation designs, development of user interfaces, database system administration 
tasks including access controls and IT security, maintenance of inventory of database 
software licenses, development and administration of data management applications 
software and associated tools; advise on software technology and database design as they 
relate to project needs; design enhancements to databases, applications, and services; 
provide support and coordination in loading, conﬁguring, operating, maintaining, 
optimizing, scaling, replicating, and upgrading database supporting software. 
 
C.1.4 Message-Oriented Middleware – Re quires expertise in installing, conﬁguring, 
administering, and maintaining Message-Oriented Middleware (MOM) platforms—such as 
ActiveMQ, NATS, Kafka, and other industry-standard MOM solutions—to enable reliable, 
scalable, and secure messaging for complex scientiﬁc monitoring systems. Services 
required may include: ensuring seamless integration of MOM platforms with existing 
scientiﬁc applications, telemetry systems, and distributed data pipelines; supporting 
interoperability across heterogeneous environments including the CHS cloud; designing 
and implementing MOM conﬁgurations which support high-throughput, low-latency 
messaging for real-time seismic and geodetic data processing; optimizing, load balancing, 
and fault tolerance to maintain resilience under peak loads; applying best cyber security 
practices for MOM platforms; and implementing robust monitoring and alerting tools to 
track message ﬂow, latency, and system health.  All MOM operates within a 24/7 scientiﬁc 

140G0326R0003  SOW, Page 5 of 25 
 
data acquisition, analysis, and product generation environment.  Work must not only 
support this environment but minimize disruption to it while ensuring resilience, fault 
tolerance, and scalability for mission-critical seismic and geodetic data messaging and 
products. 
 
 C.1.5 Full –Stack Development – Requires advanced knowledge of front-end and 
back-end development for scientiﬁc web applications. Services shall include building new 
scientiﬁc software applications and maintaining and improving existing ones using modern 
frameworks; ensuring responsive design and cross-platform compatibility for scientiﬁc 
applications; developing interactive visualization tools to analyze, interpret, and display 
real-time seismic, geodetic, and other geophysical data; implementing secure coding 
practices aligned with OWASP Top 10 and federal mandates (e.g. FISMA, NIST SP 800-53, 
etc.); integrating role-based access control, TSL encryption, and secure authentication 
mechanisms; optimizing applications for high-performance rendering and analysis of large 
geophysical datasets; supporting cloud-native deployments and containerization for 
scalability and fault tolerance; and incorporating automated unit and integration testing 
into Continuous Integration / Continuous Delivery (CI/CD) pipelines for continuous delivery 
and quality assurance. 
C.1.6 DevOps – Requires advanced knowledge of software deployment, 
infrastructure management, and Continuous Integration / Continuous Delivery (CI/CD) 
pipelines to support mission-critical scientiﬁc applications.  Services required may 
include: developing and maintaining automated deployment scripts for provisioning and 
conﬁguration management; implementing automated deployment of distributed systems – 
including MOM superclusters – across geographically distributed AWS and Azure 
environments for resilience and scalability; utilize containerized deployments, ensuring 
portability, fault tolerance, and eƯicient resource utilization; integrating secure CI/CD 
pipelines, enabling automated builds, unit testing, integration testing, and deployment; 
incorporating static and dynamic security testing (SAST/DAST) and vulnerability scanning 
into the pipelines; applying DevSecOps principles to embed security controls throughout 
the deployment lifecycle; implementing monitoring and alerting solutions for real-time 
visibility into system health, performance, and deployment status; and designing and 
implementing rollback strategies and disaster recovery procedures to maintain high 
availability and minimize downtime during deployments. 
C.1.7 On-call requirement – Since the Earthquake Science Center’s ground motion 
monitoring networks operate 24/7/365, some task orders may have an on-call requirement 
in which the incumbent participates in a 24/7 duty rotation shared with Government 

140G0326R0003  SOW, Page 6 of 25 
 
employees and University partners.  Each duty cycle lasts 1 week (usually Wednesday to 
Wednesday), and all members of the duty pool work together to ensure that everyone’s 
scheduling needs are met.  Being on call requires carrying a cell phone to receive and 
respond to system notiﬁcations or earthquakes.  Speciﬁc response times will be indicated 
in the task order if on call duties are required for that task. 
 
C.2. DATA SCIENCE AND ANALYTICS 
In general, this service area supports scientiﬁc research, data product 
development, and research dissemination by providing data science expertise, analytical 
methods, and advanced computational capabilities consistent with federal and USGS 
requirements.  Task order requirements in the data science and analytics area may include: 
C.2.1 Data Stewardship and Preservation  –  Requires advanced knowledge of 
scientiﬁc data and metadata collection, management, preservation, and curation.  
Services required may include:  Data management planning; metadata creation and data 
integration; provenance tracking and version control; ensuring consistency and non-
duplication in the areas of data management plan development and approval and

Practices (FSP), Records Management, and other federal directives which require 
management and preservation of research data and metadata through the entire lifecycle – 
planning, acquiring, processing, analyzing, preserving, curating, publishing, sharing, 
documenting, managing quality, securing, and archiving.

1.  Purpose:  

1.1 The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Eastern Colorado Health Care System (ECHCS), requires procurement of new Vocera V5000 Smartbadge equipment and associated licenses, accessories, and OEM warranty/support to replace end-of-life Vocera B3000n Smartbadges.

1.2 This requirement is for approximately 800 new Smartbadge devices, associated software licenses, batteries, chargers, clips, lanyards, and OEM warranty/support services. Installation and construction are not required.

2.  Salient Characteristics:  

Hands-free clinical communication

Secure messaging and wireless calling

Nurse call and Code Blue integration

FIPS 140-2 compliant encryption

Fully compatible with existing Vocera platform

3. Warranty

3.1 Manufacturer Warranty

The contractor shall provide manufacturer (OEM) warranty coverage for all components beginning on the date of acceptance.

The warranty shall include, at a minimum:

Coverage for defects in materials and workmanship

Parts and labor included during the warranty period

OEM-authorized service and technical support

Access to OEM software and firmware updates released during the warranty period

OR MORE OF THE FOLLOWING: OWNERSHIP OR INTERLOCKING MANAGEMENT , IDENTITY OF 
INTERESTS AMONG FAMILY MEMBERS, SHARED FACILITIES AND EQUIPMENT, AND THE 
COMMON USE OF EMPLOYEES. THERE MAY BE MORE THAN ONE IMMEDIATE OWNER (E.G., 
JOINT VENTURES). 
PREDECESSOR MEANS AN ENTITY WHOSE ASSETS WERE ACQUIRED BY THE OFFEROR OR 
ANOTHER ENTITY (MOST OFTEN THROUGH MERGER OR ACQUISITION) AND WHOSE AFFAIRS 
ARE NOW CARRIED OUT BY THE OFFEROR OR THE OTHER ENTITY UNDER A NEW NAME. 
TAXPAYER IDENTIFICATION NUMBER MEANS THE NUMBER REQUIRED BY THE INTERNAL 
REVENUE SERVICE (IRS) TO BE USED BY THE OFFEROR TO REPORT INCOME TAX AND OTHER 

RETURNS. IT MAY BE EITHER A SOCIAL SECURITY NUMBER OR AN EMPLOYER IDENTIFICATION 
NUMBER.

13, SYSTEM FOR AWARD MANAGEMENT—MAINTENANCE, OF THIS SOLICITATION.

TO HTTPS://WWW.SAM.GOV FOR INSTRUCTIONS ON OBTAINING A UEI. 
(ii) THE OFFEROR SHALL ENTER, IN THE BLOCK WITH ITS NAME AND ADDRESS ON

(iii) THE CONTRACTING OFFICER WILL USE THE UEI TO VERIFY THAT THE OFFEROR

(2) TAXPAYER IDENTIFICATION NUMBER (TIN).

Page 1 of 6 
 
SOURCES SOUGHT SYNOPSIS (SSS)/ REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) 
Enterprise Resource Planning Common Services (ERP CS)  
7 July 2026 
 
1. SYNOPSIS 
THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) ONLY. THERE IS NO SOLICITATION 
AVAILABLE AT THIS TIME. REQUESTS FOR A SOLICITATION WILL NOT RECEIVE A  
RESPONSE.
 
The Air Force Materiel Command (AFMC), Air Force Life Cycle Management Center 
(AFLCMC) Business and Enterprise Systems Directorate (BES), Engineering Division (GBE), 
Maxwell AFB-Gunter Annex, Alabama is conducting market research seeking vendor interest 
for Enterprise Resource Planning Common Services (ERP CS). 
This is a Request for Information (RFI) only.  This RFI is issued solely for market research 
purposes. It does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFP in the 
future. This request for information does not commit the Government to contract for any supply 
or service whatsoever. Further, the Air Force (AF) is not seeking proposals, nor will it accept 
unsolicited proposals at this time. 
 
Respondents are advised that the United States Government will not pay for any information or 
administrative costs incurred in response to this RFI. All costs associated with responding to this 
RFI will be solely at the interested party’s expense. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude 
participation in any future RFP, if any is issued. It is the responsibility of the potential offerors to 
monitor the Government’s point of entry (www.sam.gov) for additional information pertaining to 
this requirement. 
 
2. PURPOSE   
This RFI seeks industry partners to help the AFLCMC/GBE ERP CS Program Management 
Office (PMO) build, integrate, and sustain a suite of common services on the Cloud One Oracle 
Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) platform. Our objective is to enhance a standardized, shared-services 
model that empowers the PMO to enhance internal and external collaboration, streamline 
business functions, and continuously integrate current and emerging technologies to deliver a 
decisive information advantage to the warfighter. 
 
3. PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE 
 
The Period of Performance is projected to be one (1) base year with four (4) one (1)-year options 
plus a six (6)-month Extension of Services. 

Page 2 of 6 
 
 
 
 
4. ANTICIPATED CONTRACT ELEMENTS 
 
This work covers a comprehensive range of services aimed at ensuring the effective 
management, enhancement, and operation of the ERP CS environments. The Contractor shall 
provide IT services for a wide range of tasks. The contractor will adhere to Government-
mandated standards and industry best business practices. The following disciplines should be 
considered; environment migrations, development, automated testing, integration, cybersecurity, 
maintenance, sustainment of ERP CS capabilities, services, and transition management. 
• The Contractor shall proactively collaborate on topics related to common infrastructure 
services with ERP CS PMO, DISA, Cloud One and other stakeholders including OEMs such 
as Oracle and other companies providing products and support for ERP CS.  
• The Contractor shall design, develop, deploy, document, implement, integrate, automate, 
operate, and sustain ERP common services. 
• The Contractor shall support, manage, and operate the continued performance of the assets 
deployed in the existing ERP CS environments.  
• The Contractor shall provide sustainment activities to encompass service management, 
storage management & administration, database management, capacity management, backup 
and restore management, patching, disaster recovery, incident management, and 
troubleshooting. 
• The Contractor shall provide continued operations and sustainment support for the 
capabilities and services. The contractor shall provide subject matter advice and leverage the 
Department of Defense (DoD) Enterprise Services Management Framework (DESMF). 
• The contract scope shall require the contractor to leverage cutting-edge IT disciplines and 
processes. Offerors must demonstrate capabilities in integrating emerging technologies and 
employ modern software development practices such as comprehensive Test Automation. 
Furthermore, the contractor shall operate within Integrated Team Structures to ensure agile 
and responsive execution throughout the contract's lifecycle. The Contractor must ensure that 
all tasks are aligned with the System Lifecycle and agile policies and executed in accordance 
with the Government’s agile strategy. 
 
5. OBJECTIVES 
The AFLCMC/GBE ERP CS PMO has established the following key objectives for this 
initiative.  

Page 3 of 6 
 
• Provide a Scalable Shared Services Model: To stand up a robust, scalable, and secure 
portfolio of common IT services within the Cloud One-provisioned Oracle Cloud 
Infrastructure (OCI) that can be leveraged across the enterprise. 
• Drive Efficiency and Effectiveness: To significantly improve efficiency, effectiveness, and 
user experience of core business functions through the delivery of standardized and 
consolidated services. 
• Integrate Artificial Intelligence (AI): To leverage AI and machine learning technologies to 
automate processes, generate actionable insights from data, and introduce intelligent 
capabilities that enhance mission performance. 
• Implement Comprehensive DevSecOps and Test Automation Strategy: To embed modern 
DevSecOps robust test automation and practices throughout the service lifecycle, ensuring 
high-quality, secure, and rapid delivery of new capabilities and updates. 
• Foster Seamless Collaboration with Integrated Teams: To operate using Integrated Team 
Structures where personnel work collaboratively, ensuring alignment, transparency, and 
shared ownership of project outcomes. 
• Spearhead Innovation and Integration: To serve as a center for innovation, enabling seamless 
and agile integration of the common services with other critical mission systems to create a 
unified and more capable enterprise ecosystem. 
• Ensure Continuous Mission Support and Operational Availability: To provide 24/7/365 
operational support and system monitoring for all common services and support tools, 
ensuring maximum uptime, near real-time data replication between Production and 
DR/COOP, rapid incident response, and uninterrupted availability for all global stakeholders 
and mission-critical functions. 
• Streamline service management and onboarding processes. 
• Ensure Continuity of Operations and Disaster Recovery: To support environment availability 
of systems for Mission Partners. 
 
6.  EXPERIENCE, CAPABILITIES AND SOFTWARE/APPLICATION 
To assist in our market research and acquisition planning, the government is seeking responses 
from industry.  Detail your corporate experience, strategic approach, and capacity to perform 
work of this scope and complexity. Interested parties are requested to provide a summary of your 
company’s experience and technical capabilities in the following areas:  
 
• For up to three relevant prime contracts, provide the Contract Number, Sponsoring Agency, 
Period of Performance, Total Contract Value, and a brief description of the scope. 
• How are you able to leverage Automation in workflows and processes? 
• How are you able to establish and sustain enterprise-level common services on a cloud 
platform, preferably Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI)?? 
• Providing 24/7/365 operational support for mission-critical systems. 

Page 4 of 6 
 
• Provide a staff of personnel who possess the necessary security clearances and technical 
certifications within 30 days of a potential contract award.  
• Maintain a fully staffed team up to 90% at all times and have remediation strategies in place 
to get to 90% within 30 days. 
• Identify any potential risks, challenges, or issues you foresee, particularly concerning the 
Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) environment. 
o Provide recommendations for mitigating these identified risks. 
• Provide recommendations for Oracle Integration Cloud vs SOA Suite 
• Provide recommendations for OCI GoldenGate Microservice vs Oracle GoldenGate 
• Provide recommendations for items such as OCI IAM SSO Asserter vs Oracle Identity and 
Access Management SSO 
• Provide recommendations for items such as Oracle Identity Directory (OID) vs.  Oracle 
Unified Directory (OUD).  
• Provide recommendations for items such as OAC Analytics Cloud vs OAS Analytics 
• Provide recommendations for items such as Risk Management Cloud vs SafePaaS 
• Audit compliance SOC1 Type 2 experience with Federal Financial Management systems 
migrating to the cloud. What level of compliance has the contractor supported? 
• Provide data migration strategies and management recommendations for identifying and 
remediating redundant data before migrating to the cloud.  
• Provide archive and purge strategy recommendations for financial management data sets.  
• Provide recommendations for maintaining enterprise security posture. 
• Specifically detail examples of large-scale projects where you interfaced directly with 
Government roles such as Product Owners, System Engineers, and Test Authorities. Describe 
the communication rhythm, governance structure, and the outcomes of this collaboration. 
• Identify all Government Wide Acquisition Contracts (GWACs), Indefinite 
Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQs), or other contract vehicles your company holds that you 
believe are suitable for this effort. Provide a recommendation for the most appropriate 
contract vehicle and contract type (e.g., FFP, T&M, Cost-Plus) for this work and provide a 
strong rationale for why your recommendation maximizes value and flexibility for the 
government. 
• The government is interested in implementing Artificial Intelligence (AI) in its 
modernization efforts. Provide recommended PWS verbiage and any relevant AI 
recommendations. Also, please provide example(s) of how AI has been used in program(s) of 
similar scope for modernization efforts. 
• For your most significant ERP implementation, describe your approach to balancing out-of-
the-box (OOTB) functionality with required customizations. What was the approximate 
percentage of custom development, and what methodology guided those decisions? 
• What is the maximum number of concurrent users supported by the largest ERP system your 
company has developed, sustained, or supported?  

Page 5 of 6 
 
 
7. ADMINISTRATIVE INFORMATION REQUESTED 
The Contractor's RFI response shall be: 
 
• 12 pages or less (cover page is not included in page count) 
• Times New Roman 12 font 
• One (1)-inch margins 
• Page size should be 8.5 x 11 inches 
• Foldouts are permitted but will be assessed toward total page count 
• Company/Institute Name 
• CAGE Code 
• UEI Number 
• Address 
• Point of Contact 
• Phone Number 
• E-mail Address 
• Web Page URL 
• A statement as to whether your company is domestically or foreign owned (if foreign, please 
indicate the country of ownership). 
• Prime vs. Subcontractor: State your company’s intention to bid on a potential future RFP for 
this effort as a Prime contractor or to seek opportunities as a Subcontractor. 
Subcontracting Strategy: If you intend to act as Prime, describe your subcontracting strategy. 
Identify which key capability areas (e.g., AI/ML, OCI specialization, specific ERP modules) 
you would likely subcontract and estimate the percentage of the total effort this would 
represent. This helps us understand your core competencies. 
 
8. ORGANIZATIONAL CONFLICT OF INTEREST 
Conflict of Interest (COI), as defined and discussed in Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) 9.5, 
Organizational and Consultant Conflicts of Interest, is a concern in all acquisitions across the 
Department of War.  Early involvement with our industry partners is a key element of the COI 
process, and it is critical for the Government to be able to identify any potential COI issues as 
early as possible for acquisition.  This would allow ample time to address and evaluate any 
potential COI issues, if required, prior to contract award with minimal impact to critical 
acquisition schedules.  Interested offerors are requested to notify the government of any potential 
COI issues in your RFI response.  
Note: All interested contractors must be registered in SAM to be eligible for award of 
Government contracts. The Government reserves the right to consider a small business set-aside 
based upon responses hereto for any subsequent action.   

Page 6 of 6 
 
 
Due Date:  Responses should be submitted electronically to the Contracting Officer, Ms. 
Amanda Stull at amanda.stull@us.af.mil by Close of Business (COB) 21 Jul 2026. Late 
responses may not be reviewed.  
 
Provide any questions or comments concerning the ERP CS requirements or RFI Questions 
above NLT COB 15 Jun 2026. 
 
9. SUBMISSIONS/QUESTIONS 
 
If submitting company proprietary information or competition sensitive information, please 
make sure it is CLEARLY MARKED. To aid the Government, please segregate proprietary 
information to the maximum extent possible. All segregated proprietary information will be 
protected by the Government. 
 
THIS IS AN RFI ONLY. The information provided in this RFI is subject to change and is not 
binding on the Government. The AF has not made a commitment to procure any of the items or 
services discussed above, and release of this RFI should not be construed as such a commitment 
or as an authorization to incur cost for which reimbursement would be required or sought. All 
submissions become Government property and will not be returned.  
 
Any questions should be directed to the Contracting Officer as identified above.

M0 GENERAL 
 
M0.1 Introduction.  Section M describes the criteria the Government will use in evaluating the Offerors’ proposals 
submitted for the J6 Program Management Support Services (PMOSS) contract. The Government will evaluate each 
Offeror’s capabilities and proposal elements against this evaluation criteria. This is a competitive, best value, source 
selection using a tradeoff process that will be conducted in accordance with (IAW) Federal Acquisition Regulation 
(FAR) 15.101-1, Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) Part 215.101, and FAR 15.404. The 
Government intends to make a single prime contract award under this solicitation. 
 
M0.2 Evaluation. The Government will evaluate each Offeror’s proposal against the evaluation criteria set forth 
below. The Government will award the J6 PMOSS contract from this solicitation to the Offeror whose proposal 
conforming to the solicitation is determined most advantageous to the Government. Technical execution, past 
performance, price, and other factors will be considered. 
 
 
M0.3 Basis for Award.  Award of the contract resulting from this solicitation will be made to the Offeror whose 
proposal complies with the solicitation requirements, who is deemed responsible and whose proposal is deemed to 
represent the best value to the Government based on the factors listed in Table M.1 below.

This is a notice of intent to issue a modification to task order 70RSAT25FC0000007 for 
Information Technology Support Services (ITSS) issued against Blanket Purchase Agreement 
(BPA) 70RSAT22A00000001 with Silosmashers, Inc., 12001 Sunrise Valley Drive, Suite 202, 
Reston, VA 20191.  The task order will be modified to extend performance for 10 months with a 
2-month option period on a non-competitive basis. The statutory authority permitting other than 
full and open competition is 41 U.S.C. 3304(a)(1) implemented by the FAR Subpart 6.103-1 
(FAR Class Deviation 25-11) entitled “Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or 
Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements.”    
Background  
This modification to existing task order 70RSAT25FC0000007 for Information Technology 
Support Services (ITSS) will maintain support services to Department of Homeland Security 
(DHS) Science & Technology Directorate (S&T) Office of the Chief Information Officer 
(OCIO) in the areas of program management, business management, enterprise architecture 
alignment, IT governance, and regulatory compliance for platforms such as SharePoint, 
ServiceNow, and Microsoft Power Platform.  The task order includes labor, travel, and materials 
necessary to assist DHS S&T OCIO fulfill its mission.  The task order has a period of 
performance that began on September 30, 2025, and will expire on July 31, 2026, unless 
extended. The market research for the re-compete of 70RSAT25FC0000007 is under 
development. Due to the lapse in DHS appropriations in FY26, preparations for the re-compete 
have been significantly delayed.  
 
Silosmashers is the current contractor for the requirement, and they possess unique and 
specialized knowledge of DHS S&T CIO requirements, activities, and stakeholders to ensure 
seamless, continuous support during the acquisition activities required for the re-compete. 
Efforts to conduct a competitive procurement and then potentially transition to a new contractor 
prior to the end of the current period of performance would introduce unacceptable risk to 
ongoing S&T CIO activities and potential delays, misalignment with stakeholder and partner 
expectations, and significant loss of continuity in execution. Anything other than an extension of 
the existing task order would seriously and materially compromise the work of the S&T OCIO 
and the mission of DHS.   
 
The information provided below provides an overview of the specific critical activities the 
current contractor will perform: 
 
Enterprise Architecture (EA) Alignment and Maintenance 
Critical Activity: 
 
The incumbent contractor plays an essential role in guiding and supporting the development, 
implementation, and ongoing maintenance of a comprehensive, enterprise-wide IT strategy and 
architecture for S&T. This work ensures that S&T’s IT portfolio remains fully aligned with 
federal mandates—including frameworks such as FEAF, TOGAF, and DoDAF, and that all 
activities comply with DHS Enterprise Architecture requirements and Technology Business 
Management (TBM) standards. 

Risk if Performed by Another Contractor: 
Without a transition period, a new contractor would lack critical context, increasing the risk of 
misalignment, duplication of efforts, and inefficiencies. Additionally, any lapse in continuity 
could result in non-compliance with federal and DHS mandates, which may lead to audit 
findings, funding delays, or system vulnerabilities. Finally, the disruption of ongoing strategic 
initiatives could delay critical modernization efforts, directly impacting mission delivery and 
operational effectiveness. 
 
Information Assurance (IA) and Information System Security Officer (ISSO) Support 
Critical Activity: 
The current contractor’s Information System Security Officers (ISSOs) serve as principal 
advisors on all matters related to the security of S&T’s information systems. Their 
responsibilities include implementing DHS 4300 policy, managing day-to-day security 
operations, maintaining IT Security Plans, conducting vulnerability scans, responding to 
Information Security Vulnerability Messages (ISVMs), and supporting classified systems and 
Sensitive Compartmented Information Facilities (SCIFs). 
 
Risk if Performed by Another Contractor: 
The inability to transition these duties to a new contractor would pose a substantial risk to S&T’s 
security posture. ISSO roles require continuous awareness of system configurations, 
vulnerabilities, and remediation actions, all of which are built on established knowledge and 
experience with S&T’s unique environment. A new contractor would not have immediate access 
to this information, increasing the likelihood of security incidents or compliance failures. 
Furthermore, unfamiliarity with existing systems and processes could delay responses to 
vulnerabilities and classified system requirements, potentially exposing sensitive data. The 
established relationships with federal stakeholders, SCIF management, and COMSEC support 
are also critical to effective coordination and trust; these relationships would be disrupted, further 
increasing risk. 
 
IT Operations and Maintenance (O&M) Oversight and Help Desk Support 
Critical Activity: 
The contractor is responsible for the daily oversight of all IT support functions, including Tier 1 
and Tier 2 help desk services, network infrastructure maintenance, asset management, patch 
management, and after-hours emergency support. This work is essential to maintaining 
uninterrupted IT operations across S&T. 
 
Risk if Performed by Another Contractor: 
If another contractor were to assume these responsibilities without a proper transition period, 
S&T would likely experience service disruptions due to gaps in support coverage, delayed 
incident resolution, and a loss of continuity in asset tracking and inventory management. New 
personnel may not be fully trained on S&T-specific workflows, tools (such as ServiceNow), or 
escalation procedures, which could result in non-compliance with established service level 
agreements and decreased user satisfaction. Additionally, asset management and inventory 
processes require a high degree of accuracy and consistency; a new contractor without a 
transition period may introduce errors or fail to maintain proper documentation, negatively 
impacting audit readiness and property accountability. 

If the current task order is not extended while the recompete is completed, the Agency mission 
would be jeopardized, and S&T CIO would lose the ability to integrate innovative technology 
into everyday use by the DHS operational components. DHS S&T IT support will include all 
hardware, networks, enterprise architecture, information assurance and service delivery support. 
DHS S&T requires this support to maintain and evolve its organizations required to meet mission 
needs.  
 
Period of Performance: The ITSS task order requires an extension of 10 months from August 1, 
2026, through May 31, 2027. 
A determination by the Government to modify the existing task order without competition based 
upon responses to this notice is solely at the discretion of the Government. 
This is a notice of the intent to modify a task order on a sole source basis. It is published for 
informational purposes only and not a request for competitive proposals. Therefore, no 
solicitation document exists for this requirement.  Any firm believing that they can fulfill the 
requirement may be considered by the agency. Interested parties may identify their interest and 
capabilities in response to this synopsis. All questions and/or comments regarding this notice 
shall be addressed in writing to the Contracting Officer, Danette.Williams@hq.dhs.gov.

Digital Pathology

1. Introduction

The purpose of this Performance Work Statement (PWS) is to detail the minimum technical requirements of the digital pathology system solicitation and define the tasks and responsibilities of the successful offeror for the procurement of a Food and Drug Administration (FDA) 510(k) cleared digital pathology system for participating Veterans Health Administration (VHA) laboratories.

2. Background

The VA National Precision Oncology Program (NPOP) was established in 2016 with the goal of implementing standardized, streamlined methods for molecular testing of Veterans with cancer. The molecular testing technologies offered under NPOP include next generation sequencing (DNA and RNA-seq), immunohistochemistry, fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH), PCR and microarray-based methods.

To accelerate the adoption of molecular diagnostics, in addition to testing more patients, there is also a need to build the VA infrastructure to support today's virtual healthcare environment, bringing VA-wide expertise together in the practice of precision medicine. More specifically, adoption of molecular testing and precision medicine must also be supported by educational efforts to bring together multidisciplinary experts in the form of a molecular tumor board. To accomplish this initiative, virtual tumor boards require pathology support with equipment that can capture images for broader distribution and interpretation of the patient's tumor tissue.

The procurement of a digital pathology system will provide the infrastructure required and the access to testing needed to deliver appropriate training and education, a second opinion consult service, a virtual molecular tumor board for clinician case-based learning and ongoing professional practice evaluation.

Overall, these efforts in molecular diagnostics strongly tie clinical care and research together in the broader VA precision oncology initiative where there are continuous learning opportunities for clinicians, researchers and patients and shared decision making with an ultimate goal of providing the highest quality oncology care to Veterans.

3. Scope

The VA intends to award a single contract to the overall best-value contractor capable of meeting the requirements outlined herein for a complete, fully operational digital pathology system (including both hardware and software), the associated installation and configuration services, and the incorporated staff training requirement. The Contractor shall implement the system across twelve (12) VA Medical Centers in the base period, with option years to award additional VA Medical Centers. 

The digital pathology system shall provide capability for large-scale real-time and archived collections of histopathology specimens requiring an image library server(s) for historical archives, remote viewing features for consultation, retrieval, digital management, and preservation of patient specimens referred for outside consultation.

Functionality shall include whole slide digital scanning, documentation, remote consultation, specialty consultation, and computer-assisted digital image analysis. The product must have FDA 510(k) clearance for basic surgical pathology functions including but not limited to: support for virtual tumor boards, consultative services; second review for newly diagnosed malignancies; coverage for pathologist absences; quality assurance review; and primary diagnoses. 

The Contracting Officer shall conduct post-award orientations in accordance with FAR 42.503 and VAAM M842.503 within the first five (5) calendar days of the contract award date.

4. General System Requirements

The minimum requirements for a Digital Pathology System, hereafter referred to as the "System," shall be met or exceeded by this acquisition. The Contractor shall provide narrative descriptions demonstrating FDA 510(k) clearance and compliance with all requirements below.

4.1 Clinical

4.1.1. The System shall have FDA 510(k) clearance for primary diagnosis using minimally hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining. (Contractor to provide a list of all cleared applications for consideration.)

4.1.2. The System shall provide all necessary equipment giving VHA facilities the ability to scan slides into their local system for both local and remote pathologist viewing when utilizing the same manufacturer's system.

4.1.3. The System shall include all items necessary to support a fully functioning system as follows:

4.1.3.1. Capable of purging scanned images at user-defined intervals or no less than thirty (30) days.

4.1.3.2. Ability to archive scanned slides for at least three (3) years.

4.1.3.3. Ability to read slide barcode data.

4.2 Hardware and Software

4.2.1. System server and test server platform at each site.

	4.2.1.1. Contractor-provided or VA provided virtual server platform

4.2.2. The ability to support multiple concurrent users.

4.2.3. The ability of the server to host additional scanners/sites that can be supported with a 1 gigabit per second WAN bandwidth for future pathology expansion or be easily upgraded to provide this capability.

4.2.4. The capability of the System server and test server, to run VA-approved anti-virus software.

4.2.5. Evidence that the System server and test server are currently sold and supported by its original manufacturer.

4.2.6. The capability of the software to permit remote, web-based image viewing by authorized users.

4.2.7. The Contractor may be responsible for all operating system patching, anti-virus and security updates, and application updates/upgrades to meet VA security requirements/vulnerability remediation for all components of the System and compliance with Department of Homeland Security, Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency's Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 22-01 and its successors. The VA will designate the criticality of updates/upgrades, and the Contractor shall address them within the timeline identified per VA policy.

4.2.8. The ability to provide the necessary hardware, operating systems, driver software, computer accessories, and manuals required to operate the slide scanners, as well as all necessary cables and power unit components.

4.2.9. The ability to provide a local storage solution that is easily and highly scalable to provide additional storage to support pathology expansion.

4.2.10. Vendor shall supply all necessary hardware and software to support upgrade of existing digital pathology systems including migration of existing data and system configuration.

4.3 Network Security and Integration Requirements

4.3.1. Compliance of all hardware and software with VA network security and Enterprise Risk Analysis requirements. The Contractor shall supply responses to required documents for connection of medical devices to the VA network, including but not limited to the VA Directive 6550, ports and protocols, and services, application inventory, network diagram, and MSD2.

4.3.1.1. Contractor shall have a Memorandum of Understanding/Information Security Agreement (MOU/ISA) with the VA or the capability to obtain an MOU/ISA without creating significant implementation delays.

4.3.1.2. The hardware must meet all VA minimum specifications, and the software version must be approved for use on the VA network.

4.3.2. The capability of the System design and subsequent deployment to be installed on Medical Device Virtual Local Area Networks (VLANs) and behind Access Control Lists (ACLs) or firewalls.

4.3.3. All unused services on all deployed components are disabled. The System shall be hardened to the greatest extent possible without impacting clinical performance or utility.

4.3.4. The capability of slide image data transfer via a secure transmission protocol.

4.3.5. System deployment with Federal Information Processing Standards (FIPS) 140-2 (or its successor) compliant encryption of sensitive data at rest.

4.3.6. Any web-based applications shall be fully functional with VA baseline versions of Edge and Chrome browsers and accept the VA browser security settings.

4.3.7. The capability of the System server and test server to integrate with the VA's active directory and PIV/Single Sign On (SSO) system.

4.3.8. The capability of the System to integrate with VistA Imaging and Oracle CareAware MultiMedia (CAMM) and provide export of images to those repositories. The System shall be capable of producing and fully utilizing images in DICOM format for storage and export.

4.3.9. The ability of the System manufacturer, in conjunction with the VA, to develop and provide a validated bidirectional interface with the Laboratory Information System (LIS) (e.g., VistA, Oracle Health, or third-party Anatomic Pathology LIS) within an agreed-upon reasonable timeline after implementation. The System shall include outbound communication of result/information objects (i.e., scanned slide images) to the VA LIS conforming to DICOM standards. If the LIS vendor does not support a bidirectional interface, the Contractor shall develop and provide a validated unidirectional interface within the same agreed-upon timeline. For a unidirectional interface, the System shall use a non-proprietary HL7 interface capable of accepting patient demographic information (ADT) and order (ORM) messages from the VA LIS

5. Technical System Requirements

The Contractor shall provide a System that meets the VHA Labs Technical System Performance Requirements outlined below. A response shall be provided that addresses qualitatively and/or quantitatively how specifications are met or exceeded.

5.1 Slide Image Manager/Viewing System

5.1.1. Digital pathology images reviewed through the image manager/viewing system shall meet medical grade image quality standards.

5.1.2. All participating facilities shall be able to read pathology slides for any other participating site for either primary diagnosis or consult as needed, even when not hosted on the same slide image system.

5.1.3. The System shall be capable of producing and fully utilizing images in DICOM format. The ability to save, review, and display multiple file formats such as JPG, TIFF, or JPEG2000 for upload/export to electronic health record or other applications is also required.

5.1.4. Workflow management tools in the proprietary viewer software shall include, at minimum:

5.1.4.1. Ability to make image annotations.

5.1.4.2. Ability to take accurate measurements.

5.1.4.3. Ability to bookmark slides for quick access for tumor board and panel discussions.

5.1.5. The slide image manager/viewing system shall be accessible through a web browser.

5.1.6. A work list for each pathologist of their assigned caseload that can be sorted by patient name, number of slides per case, and tissue type.

5.1.7. A full resolution image shall be available for viewing within no more than three (3) seconds across the Local Area Network (LAN).

5.2 Digital Pathology Scanner System

5.2.1. Scan at a minimum of 40X magnification.

5.2.2. A minimum scanning throughput of 50 slides per hour at 40X magnification.

5.2.3. Perform continuous auto-focusing when scanning.

5.2.4. Allow for continuous loading of slides into the digital pathology scanner.

5.2.4.1. The ability to prioritize slides is highly desirable.

5.2.5. A fully automated load and walkaway functionality.

5.2.6. Integration with proprietary viewer software to allow the scanner operator to assign individual cases to one or more local or remote pathologists for viewing, consultation, and interpretation.

5.2.7. An image preview of the scan so the scanner operator can assess image quality and accurate identifying information before uploading to servers for local and remote access.

5.2.8. Read barcoded slides.

5.2.9. A barcode read accuracy of 99% or greater.

5.2.10. High quality scanned images with less than a 2% failure rate for:

5.2.10.1. Color reproducibility

5.2.10.2. Spatial resolution

5.2.10.3. Focusing tests

5.2.10.4. Whole slide image coverage

5.2.10.5. Stitching error

5.2.11. Ability to perform Z-stacking to capture multiple focal layers of a tissue sample

5.3 Display Monitor

5.3.1. A minimum 27" diagnostic display screen utilizing a medical grade high resolution image display for primary and other diagnostic work. The display's front consistency sensor shall automatically align image quality every time the display is switched on. The Contractor shall provide the display monitor if it is part of the FDA 510(k) clearance for primary diagnosis. If the display monitor is not part of the FDA 510(k) clearance, the Contractor shall provide specifications to the VA.

6. Other System Support Items

6.1. An uninterruptible power supply (UPS) shall be supplied with a line conditioner for each scanner provided. Each UPS must provide electrical power for a minimum of 15 minutes after electrical power fails, and the system must allow for an automatic controlled shutdown to prevent damage to the instrument and data records.

6.2. A scanner table/bench shall be provided that minimizes scanner noise and vibrations.

7. System Support Features

7.1 Warranty 

7.1.1. All equipment service programs shall be provided, including preventative maintenance, corrective maintenance, remote diagnostics, and software updates for all instrumentation and ancillary items within the pathology system.

7.1.2. The System and accessories shall be covered under the manufacturer's warranty and shall minimally include all OEM parts and labor for at least one (1) year following acceptance by the VAMC. This warranty must include scheduled preventative maintenance as required by the manufacturer. The manufacturer's factory-trained field service engineers shall perform installation and maintenance during the warranty period.

7.1.3. A technical assistance center shall be available by telephone during normal business hours of operation, Monday through Friday, with a maximum callback response time of four (4) hours.

7.1.4. All equipment, including ancillary equipment, repair service shall be provided Monday through Friday during laboratory business hours. The Contractor is required to coordinate services with the designated facility points of contact. 

7.1.5. Preventative maintenance shall be performed as frequently as published in the manufacturer's operator's manual and within a timely manner with regard to scheduled due dates to ensure compliance with accrediting agency requirements:

7.1.5.1. Quarterly/every quarter = every 3 months (90 days), plus or minus 10 days.

7.1.5.2. Every 6 months = 6 months (180 days) from the last event, plus or minus 20 days.

7.1.5.3. Annually/every 12 months = 1 year from the last event, plus or minus 30 days.

7.1.6. A malfunction incident report shall be furnished to facility points of contact including Laboratory and Healthcare Technology Management, upon completion of each repair call. The report shall include, at a minimum:

606-8220 or via the internet at https://sam.gov.

Sources Sought & Request for Information (RFI)

DESCRIPTION: Artificial Intelligence (AI) Engineering Services

REQUIRING AGENCY: Department of Labor (DOL) Office of the Assistant Secretary for Administration and Management (OASAM) Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO)

NOTICE TYPE: Sources Sought / RFI
CLASSIFICATION CODE: D - Information Technology Services
NAICS CODE: North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) 541512 - Computer Systems Design Services
SIZE STANDARD: $34 Million
PLACE OF PERFORMANCE: Washington, DC 20210 (200 Constitution Ave NW); Telework authorized case-by-case.

PART I — SYNOPSIS AND DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT

The U.S. DOL OCIO, within the OASAM, is conducting market research to identify qualified sources capable of providing enterprise AI Engineering Services in support of the Directorate of Technology, Innovation, and Engineering (TIE).

THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT / RFI ONLY. This notice does not constitute a solicitation, Request for Proposal (RFP), or Request for Quote (RFQ). No award will be made from this notice. Responses are strictly voluntary, will not be returned, and the Government will not pay for information provided. Do not submit proprietary information.

Submission of a response does not guarantee participation in any subsequent solicitation.

Background

DOL is a nationwide Cabinet-level organization with Regional, District, Field, and headquarters offices supporting a broad mission across workers, employers, job seekers, and benefit recipients.

OCIO serves as DOL’s enterprise information technology (IT) organization; within OCIO, TIE leads emerging technology adoption including AI and Machine Learning (ML) to improve service delivery, automate processes, and strengthen data-driven decision-making.

DOL programs manage large volumes of structured and unstructured information — including regulatory documents, case files, program records, and operational data — creating opportunities for AI-enabled automation, search, analysis, summarization, and decision support across the Department’s major operating agencies (Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), Wage and Hour Division (WHD), Employment and Training Administration (ETA), Employee Benefits Security Administration (EBSA), Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS), and others).

Program Context: New Program Start

This is a new AI engineering program with no incumbent contractor. There is no existing contract in place for enterprise AI engineering services of this scope at DOL OCIO. The anticipated contractor will establish the program from a cold start, conducting discovery of DOL’s existing AI landscape, data sources, and technical environment through Government-Furnished Information (GFI) provided at contract start. Respondents should assess their cold-start mobilization capability accordingly.

Requirement Overview

DOL anticipates a requirement for performance-based AI engineering, development, operations, governance, and support services covering the full lifecycle of AI systems across the Department. All capability areas below are mandatory requirements not a menu of options.

Primary AI Engineering Capabilities Required:

Large Language Model (LLM) Integration and Production Deployment within the Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program (FedRAMP)-authorized cloud environments using FedRAMP-authorized cloud AI services (e.g., Amazon Web Services (AWS) Bedrock, Azure OpenAI Service, Google Cloud Platform (GCP) Vertex AI) and leading foundation models, subject to each model’s FedRAMP authorization status and DOL approval.

Context Engineering the deliberate design and management of model context windows including token budgeting, memory architectures (short-term, long-term, episodic, semantic), context compression, dynamic context assembly, and structured output enforcement. This is the primary LLM competency required, distinct from prompt engineering.

Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) Pipeline Design and Optimization including standard RAG, Advanced RAG, hybrid dense/sparse retrieval, Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation (GraphRAG) and knowledge graph-based retrieval (Neo4j or equivalent), multi-hop reasoning, and parent-child chunking for DOL’s environment.

Agentic AI and Multi-Agent Orchestration including implementation of Model Context Protocol (MCP) to manage context flow, tool definitions, memory, and state across AI agents and services; orchestration using LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, or equivalent frameworks.

Multimodal AI Capabilities models and workflows involving text, images, audio, video, document layout models, and optical character recognition (OCR)/vision-based AI; multimodal pipelines with structured evaluation metrics, security controls, and privacy safeguards.

Machine Learning Operations (MLOps) and Development, Security, and Operations (DevSecOps) including experiment tracking, model versioning, drift detection, automated retraining, and continuous integration/continuous delivery (CI/CD) integration for AI systems.

Adversarial AI Security Testing integrated as an automated gate in CI/CD pipelines before every production release, including prompt injection scanning, jailbreak detection, perturbation testing, and data poisoning defense.

Responsible AI Governance including Responsible AI Impact Assessments (RAIA) aligned to National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) AI Risk Management Framework (RMF) 1.0 and Office of Management and Budget (OMB) M-25-21 required quarterly (full assessment) and per production release (streamlined summary), with trigger-based RAIA when defined criteria are met.

Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) Design for AI systems that inform or support consequential decisions affecting individual rights, benefits, employment, or enforcement actions.

AI Incident Response aligned to a four-tier severity matrix (SEV-1 through SEV-4) with defined notification timelines; AI Incident Response Plan (AIRP) required within 30 days of award.

FedRAMP Cloud AI Deployment at Federal Information Security Modernization Act (FISMA) Moderate baseline; all data at rest in contiguous United States (CONUS) data center regions; Federal Information Processing Standards (FIPS)-validated cryptography.

AI-Specific Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) Production covering custom source code, third-party libraries, AI frameworks, model weights, embedding pipeline dependencies, and vector database versions; CycloneDX 1.4+ or Software Package Data Exchange (SPDX) 2.3+ format required.

Full-Stack AI Application Development including Python/FastAPI backend and React/TypeScript front-end or equivalent with real-time LLM streaming interfaces (server-sent events (SSE)/WebSocket); Section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, as amended / Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 A/AA compliant.

Three-Environment AI Testing across DEV, TEST/STAGING, and PROD (canary, smoke, monitoring-based validation in live traffic); no direct DEV-to-PROD promotion.

Knowledge Base Refresh Management per defined service level agreement (SLA) (monthly for regulatory/policy documents; immediate on material change triggers).

Business Continuity and Continuity of Operations Plan (COOP) for AI systems including recovery time objectives (RTOs)/recovery point objectives (RPOs) per production AI system, failover procedures for RAG pipelines and vector databases, and annual tabletop testing per NIST Special Publication (SP) 800-34.

AI Use-Case Inventory Support per OMB M-25-21 requirements; quarterly inventory updates for all AI systems under contract.

Secondary Supporting Capabilities:

Data engineering and extract, transform, load (ETL)/extract, load, transform (ELT) pipeline development for AI workloads.

AI governance program support including model cards, bias/fairness evaluation, explainability documentation.

User Interface/User Experience (UI/UX) design including wireframing, prototyping, and Figma-based design with Section 508 compliance.

AI Application Helpdesk (Tier 1/2/3 support with defined SLA coverage).

Innovation and research assessments; proof-of-concept (POC) development.

Agile project management (Jira, Confluence, sprint ceremonies).

Transition-In (cold start; 45-day maximum) and Transition-Out support.

Innovation, Research, and Transition-to-Production Capability

In addition to demonstrated production delivery experience, DOL seeks information on respondents’ capability to conduct AI innovation, technical research, prototyping, POC development, and feasibility assessments directly tied to enterprise implementation. The anticipated requirement may include evaluation of emerging AI technologies, experimentation in controlled environments, and transition of validated capabilities into secure, compliant production operations. Respondents should address both operational past performance and innovation/research and development (R&D) experience in their response (see Section 2O).

Mandatory Certifications: All Three Key Personnel Roles:

All three Key Personnel roles (Lead AI Engineer / Architect, Senior AI Engineer, and AI Project / Program Manager) shall each hold at least one current certification from the following acceptable list: Microsoft Azure AI/Applied Skills, AWS Generative AI/ML, Google Cloud Generative AI/ML, Databricks Generative AI Engineer, Snowflake SnowPro Advanced, NVIDIA Generative AI, Certified Artificial Intelligence Practitioner (CAIP), or equivalent. Credential IDs or verifiable badge URLs are required at proposal submission. The Government is also assessing whether certification expectations should apply to additional non-key labor categories; respondents shall address this in Section 3D and Section 5J.

Response limit: 25 pages (Sections 2–5). Section 1 (Company Profile) does not count against the page limit. Submit in PDF or Microsoft Word. Organize responses by section and question number.

2A(i). LLM Integration and Production Deployment in FedRAMP Environments

Describe your experience deploying LLMs in production federal environments within FedRAMP Moderate or higher authorized boundaries. Specify: LLMs deployed (GPT-4o, Claude, Llama, Mistral, Gemini, or other); FedRAMP-authorized platforms used; nature of production workloads; and any capability limitations encountered within FedRAMP authorization boundaries versus commercial equivalents.

2A(ii). LLM Fine-Tuning and Adaptation Within FedRAMP Boundaries

The anticipated requirement may include model fine-tuning or adaptation when directed and approved by the Government. Describe whether your firm has performed LLM fine-tuning or parameter-efficient adaptation (e.g., supervised fine-tuning (SFT), Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), Quantized Low-Rank Adaptation (QLoRA), reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF)) within a FedRAMP Moderate or higher authorized environment. If yes, address: (a) the authorized platform(s) used; (b) which fine-tuning or adaptation techniques were available within the authorization boundary; (c) data-governance controls applied to training datasets, including personally identifiable information (PII)/Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) handling, lineage, and access control; and (d) capability gaps between FedRAMP-authorized fine-tuning and commercial equivalents. If you have no production FedRAMP fine-tuning experience, describe your approach, known constraints, and the conditions under which fine-tuning would or would not be advisable in a FedRAMP environment.

2B. Context Engineering

The anticipated requirement identifies context engineering as the primary LLM competency distinct from prompt engineering. Context engineering encompasses token budgeting, memory architectures (short-term, long-term, episodic, semantic), context compression and summarization, dynamic few-shot example selection, and structured output enforcement.

Describe your firm’s context engineering capabilities. Address: (a) token budgeting and context prioritization in production systems; (b) memory architecture patterns implemented (specify types deployed); (c) context compression techniques for long-running conversations or agentic tasks; (d) structured output enforcement tooling (Instructor, Outlines, Guidance AI, or equivalent); (e) how context engineering is operationally distinct from prompt engineering in your team’s workflow. Cite federal or enterprise examples. Responses describing only prompt engineering techniques will not be considered responsive.

2C(i). Standard and Advanced RAG Pipelines

Describe your RAG pipeline implementation experience for document-heavy federal use cases. Specify: chunking strategies; embedding models; vector databases used (Pinecone, Weaviate, pgvector, Chroma, Qdrant, or other); hybrid dense/sparse retrieval; re-ranking; and retrieval evaluation metrics tracked (precision, recall, mean reciprocal rank (MRR), normalized discounted cumulative gain (NDCG), context relevance).

2C(ii). GraphRAG and Knowledge Graph Retrieval

The anticipated requirement specifically includes GraphRAG and knowledge graph-based retrieval for DOL’s regulatory documents, case files, and program records. Standard RAG experience alone does not address this requirement.

15. Describe the reports your solution can generate. Can the system produce examination 
workpapers, compliance summaries, audit reports, correction recommendations, proposed 
tax adjustments, and supporting legal citations? 
16. Provide information regarding the volume of documents, records, and users your 
solution can support. Include performance metrics, processing times, and scalability 
considerations for enterprise-wide deployment. 
17. Describe how your solution complies with Section 508 accessibility requirements and 
interoperates with assistive technologies such as screen readers, voice recognition

18. Describe available deployment options, including cloud-hosted, hybrid, on-premises, or 
government-controlled environments. What are the infrastructure requirements and

19. Provide examples of federal agencies or large regulated organizations where your

1. Governance and Compliance Baseline. The RFI states that solutions must provide 
"secure, explainable, and governed AI outputs. " Can the Government clarify which 
governance frameworks and policies the eventual solution will be expected to demonstrate 
conformance with, speciﬁcally IRM 10.24.1 (IRS Policy for AI Governance), OMB 
Memoranda M-25-21 and M-25-22, and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework? In 
addition, will vendors be expected to support the accountable agency official's AI Use Case 
Inventory documentation, risk assessment, and PCLIA obligations? 
 
The IRS anticipates that any future solution would be expected to comply with all 
applicable Federal laws, regulations, policies, and IRS requirements. The purpose of this 
RFI is to better understand industry capabilities. 
2. High-Impact Designation. Given that the contemplated use case involves analysis of 
taxpayer return information protected under IRC § 6103 and may inform compliance 
determinations affecting plan sponsors and participants, does the Government anticipate 
this use case being designated high-impact AI under OMB M-25-21? If so, what pre-
deployment testing, ongoing monitoring, and human-oversight requirements does the 
Government expect vendors to address in their responses? 
No determination has been made regarding AI classiﬁcation or applicable oversight 
requirements. 
3. Independent Assurance. Does the Government intend for AI governance functions, 
including explainability validation, bias and drift monitoring, and audit-ready 
documentation of AI outputs, to be delivered by the solution provider itself, or is the 
Government considering independent third-party assessment of the AI system as a 
separate or complementary capability? 
 
The approach to AI governance and assurance has not been determined. The IRS is 
seeking industry input on available capabilities and approaches. 
4. Acquisition Structure. Does the Government anticipate a single integrated award 
encompassing the AI solution, systems integration, and governance/assurance functions, 
or is the Government open to a modular acquisition approach that separates the AI 
solution from independent assessment and assurance services? 
 
No acquisition strategy has been determined. 
 

5. Small Business Considerations. Will the Government consider small business set-
asides, including Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) set-asides or 
sole-source awards, for all or discrete portions of any resulting requirement, and should 
small business capability statements address teaming arrangements in their RFI 
responses? 
No determination has been made regarding small business participation or set-asides. 
Responses from all interested vendors are encouraged. 
1. Small-business / SDVOSB participation: For any requirement resulting from this RFI, will 
the IRS consider a small-business or SDVOSB set-aside — in whole or in part (for example, 
reserving the AI-engineering scope) — or is a single unrestricted award anticipated? 
The IRS has not made any determination regarding potential set-asides or award structure. 
Responses from all interested vendors are encouraged. 
 
2. Teaming vs. single-vendor domain expertise: Would the IRS consider a solution delivered 
by an AI-engineering ﬁrm teamed with retirement-plan/ERISA and actuarial subject-matter 
experts, or does the IRS expect a single vendor to hold all retirement-plan compliance and 
actuarial expertise in-house? 
Respondents may describe their teaming approach and capabilities. The IRS has not 
established any requirements regarding teaming arrangements. 
 
3. Solution maturity — COTS vs. conﬁgurable: Is the IRS primarily seeking a commercially 
available product with demonstrated retirement-plan compliance capability today, or is it 
open to conﬁgurable AI platforms tailored to Employee Plans' requirements? How turnkey 
must the retirement-plan domain capability be at the outset? 
The IRS is interested in understanding the range of available solutions. Respondents 
should describe their solution and its level of maturity 
 
4. Retirement-plan calculations: For the calculations referenced (for example, 
discrimination, coverage, top-heavy, vesting, allocation, funding, and correction), does the 
IRS expect the solution to natively perform these, or to integrate with an IRS-provided or 
third-party validated calculation engine? 
Respondents should describe how their solution supports retirement plan calculations, 
including any native or integrated capabilities. 
 
5. Authoritative rule sources and data: For any pilot or prototype, will the IRS furnish 

representative (de-identiﬁed) plan data and the authoritative rule corpus (Code, Treasury 
Regulations, Revenue Procedures, Notices, and guidance), or is the vendor expected to 
source and maintain that corpus? 
Government-furnished data and documentation requirements have not been determined. 
 
6. Security boundary: Will the contractor operate within the IRS's existing authorization 
boundary / ATO, or is an independent FedRAMP authorization expected, and which cloud 
environment(s) are in scope? 
Security and authorization requirements have not been established for this effort.  
Compliance Frameworks: Can the Government specify which regulatory frameworks—
such as the NIST AI Risk Management Framework (RMF), Executive Order 14110, or agency-
level AI safety policies—will serve as the primary compliance baseline for evaluating the 
"governed" nature of proposed solutions? 
Any future solution would be expected to comply with applicable Federal and IRS 
requirements. Speciﬁc requirements have not been established. 
Data Sensitivity & Security: Regarding the "secure" ingestion of retirement plan data, 
should vendors align their technical approaches with speciﬁc FISMA impact levels (e.g., 
Moderate or High) or FIPS 140-3 encryption standards for the handling of unstructured plan 
data? 
Applicable information security requirements have not yet been determined.  
Human-in-the-Loop Requirements: To assess the "explainable" component of the AI 
outputs, does the Government anticipate a requirement for "Human-in-the-Loop" (HITL) 
checkpoints within the retirement plan calculation and compliance analysis workﬂow, or is 
the goal to move toward fully autonomous, system-driven reporting? 
Operational requirements, including the checkpoints for and level of human oversight 
within the workﬂow, have not been determined. 
Legacy Integration & Data Governance: For integration with existing enterprise systems 
(PegaSystems and Salesforce), are there existing data governance constraints or API-
security protocols that vendors must adhere to to ensure that the data pipeline remains 
secure during the transformation from legacy static formats to dynamic AI-enabled 
analysis? 

Integration requirements have not been ﬁnalized. Respondents are encouraged to 
describe relevant integration capabilities. 
1. FedRAMP / FTI. Given the AI Assistor would handle Federal Tax Information (FTI), 
should responses assume IRS Publication 1075 safeguarding in addition to NIST SP 800-
53, and what FedRAMP impact level (Moderate vs. High) does the IRS anticipate? Is a

Integration requirements have not been ﬁnalized. Respondents are encouraged to

calculations natively (e.g., coverage and nondiscrimination testing, top-heavy, vesting, DB 
funding), or interface with existing IRS actuarial/testing tools? Is a reference specification 
or representative test-case set available? 
Respondents should describe how their solution supports retirement plan calculations,

retirement-plan documents — and/or a document-type taxonomy or data dictionary — 
available to inform vendors' technical approaches or any future pilot/prototype phase?

any follow-on solicitation (e.g., a small-business or 8(a) set-aside, GSA MAS, or a GWAC), 
and does the IRS plan an industry day or one-on-one sessions? 
 
No acquisition strategy has been determined. 
Responses from all interested vendors are encouraged.
