REQUEST FOR INFORMATION  
 
A. Introduction 
 
1. The NATO Communications and Information Agency (NC IA) is conducting market 
research to identify potential sources and gather information regarding industry 
capabilities to support a Malware Analysis and Detection Engineering Platform . This 
Request for Information (RFI) is issued solely for informational and planning purposes 
and does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Quotation (RFQ), 
or invitation for bid.  
 
B. Purpose 
 
1. The purpose of this RFI is to obtain input from industry to help inform the NCIA’s 
acquisition planning. Responses to this RFI will assist in refining requirements, 
identifying capabilities, budget planning and shaping the strategy for any future 
solicitation. 
 
C. Background 
 
1. Malware analysis within NCIA is performed by the NCSC Cyber Threat Investigation 
Section. The section provides in -depth cyber threat analysis, malware analysis, and 
digital forensics in support of incident response activities, as well as proactive efforts 
to identify and investigate cyber threat activity . Its work supports the development of 
actionable cyber threat information to strengthen the defensive posture of the NATO 
Enterprise and NATO Operations and Missions networks. 
2. Within this section, the service provides technical analysis capabilities in response to 
cybersecurity incidents and other cyber investigation requirements. This includes both 
digital forensics and malware analysis. The service is often engaged where more 
advanced or specialized technical analysis is required, comparable to a higher -tier 
technical support function for cyber investigations. 
3. In addition to incident response, the team conducts continuous service improvement 
activities and maintains the specialized skills required to keep pace with evolving 
adversary techniques, including methods intended to hinder forensic examination, 
malware reverse engineering, detection engineering, and technical analysis. 
4. The current malware analysis capability is supported by a distributed ecosystem of 
tools and environments. This includes a small cloud -based foothold used to receive 
suspicious samples, store analysis artefacts, and access general IT capabilities such 
as t eam collaboration and source code versioning. Suspicious samples may be 
received through a dedicated mailbox and are analysed using isolated workstations 
that are disconnected from NATO networks. 
5. Analysis activities are typically performed using purpose -built virtual machines, 
including static analysis environments, dynamic analysis or victim environments, and 
anonymization environments used to access external or higher -risk resources where 
required. The team also makes use of commercial tools, vendor -provided 
documentation, and capabilities provided by other NATO entities and partner nations, 
often delivered as Software-as-a-Service. 
6. The team also uses an automated malware analysis platform to support the automated 
detonation, triage, and enrichment of suspicious files and related artefacts. This RFI is 
not primarily seeking to replace that automated malware analysis capability. 
Respondents should therefore focus their feedback on the capabilities described in the 

 
 
 
  
 Page 5 
 
NCIA-ACQ-1.017(07.25) 
 
attached Epics and User Stories, rather than assuming that the objective is to replace 
every element of the existing malware analysis ecosystem. 
7. On premises, the team uses Jira to receive, manage, and report on malware analysis 
tasks; Confluence to document procedures, findings, and threat knowledge; and 
Splunk to support case -by-case research of logs and other telemetry, particularly in 
proactive investigation scenarios. 
8. This RFI seeks industry feedback on how a future Malware Analysis and Detection 
Engineering capability could be delivered primarily as a fully managed service, 
implemented and maintained by the Contractor. The intended outcome is to enable 
Purchaser personnel to perform secure malware analysis, detection engineering, and 
related workflows with minimal administrative effort, while making use of Commercial-
Off-The-Shelf products, standard service capabilities, and limited customization 
wherever feasible. 
 
D. Submission Instructions 
 
1. Interested parties are invited to respond in accordance with the instructions below: 
 
a. Submit responses via the email address in section G no later than 12:00 hours 
Central European Time (CET) on 17 July 2026. 
 
b. Responses should be submitted using the Excel Response template provided in 
Annex C 
 
c. The following can be included as a reference in your responses and attached as 
separate documents: 
i. Company brochures or product literature (optional) 
ii. Attachments such as past performance references (optional) 
 
d. Use the following subject line for submission 
i. “Response to RFI [424314-NPKI-TPT] – [Company Name]” 
 
e. All responses should address the items listed in Annex A – Requested Information. 
 
E. Disclaimer 
 
1. This RFI is for planning and informational purposes only and shall not be construed as 
a solicitation or obligation on the part of the NCIA. The NCIA does not intend to award 
a contract based on responses to this RFI. Respondents are solely responsible for all 
costs incurred in responding to this RFI.  The NCIA will consider and  analyse all 
information received from this RFI and may use these findings to develop a future 
solicitation. The NCIA will consider all responses as confidential commercial 
information and will protect it as such. 
 
2. NCIA reserves the right, at any time, to cancel this informal market survey, partially or 
in its entirety. No legal liability on the part of NCIA for payment of any sort shall arise 
and in no event will a cause of action lie with any prospective participant for the 
recovery of any costs incurred in connection with the preparation of documentation or 
participation in response hereto. All effort init iated or undertaken by prospective 
informal market survey participants shall be done considering and accepting this fact.

1. Confidentiality of Responses 
 
The NCIA may incorporate industry comments and responses, in part or in whole, into a 
future release of a solicitation.  Should respondents include proprietary data in their 
responses that they do not wish to be disclosed to the public for any purpose, or used by 
NCIA (except for internal evaluation purposes), they must:

b. Mark each sheet of data it wishes to restrict with the following legend:

A.1 Purpose and Desired Outcome 
The purpose of this Request for Information is to obtain industry feedback on the attached 
draft Epics and User Stories for a Malware Analysis and Detection Engineering capability, 
provided in Annex B. 
 
The Purchaser’s intent is to validate whether the required operational outcomes can be 
achieved primarily through existing Commercial-Off-The-Shelf products, standard 
managed service offerings, configuration, and limited integration wherever possible. The 
Purchaser does not intend to drive the requirement toward a fully custom-developed 
solution unless industry feedback demonstrates that this is necessary to achieve the 
required operational outcomes. 
 
The desired outcome of this RFI is to help the Purchaser refine the attached Epics and 
User Stories before any potential future solicitation. Industry feedback should help

approach, risks, constraints, and recommendations.  
 
Marketing material may be included as supporting information; however, respondents are 
invited to complete the response template in Annex C to allow consistent comparison of

A.2 Scope of Requested Feedback

Stories.

or bespoke development.

that should be considered but are not currently reflected in the Epics and User 
Stories. 
8. How the capability would be implemented, operated, maintained, upgraded, and 
supported by the Contractor.

Project Summary 
The Selective Service System (SSS) is seeking additional information for market 
research and future procurement purposes for Moodle Learning Management 
System (LMS) modernization.  
This capability is intended to enhance proficiency, compliance, and accountability in 
daily operations, mandatory training, and mission support for conscription related 
duties and responsibilities. 
 
Background 
 
SSS operates a Moodle-based LMS that supports Federal employees, Contractors, 
State Directors, Reserve Service Members, and Local Board Members. Training 
includes operational, federally mandated, and task‑specific learning that builds 
knowledge, skills and abilities across the Agency.  
 
To meet future mission demands, SSS requires LMS modernization, including upgrades 
to the platform, improved administrative support, enhanced reporting and analytics, 
accessibility compliance, and the ability to support increased user capacity. 
 
General Capability Areas of Interest 
 
SSS seeks industry input regarding the following capabilities: 
• Ability to modernize, upgrade, and sustain a Moodle based LMS environment, 
including core platform components and system integrations. 
• Ability to provide scalable and secure LMS solutions capable of supporting both 
routine operational loads and surge population requirements. 


2  
• Ability to support LMS administration functions such as configuration, user 
management, reporting, troubleshooting, and system monitoring. 
• Ability to design, develop, update, and maintain SCORM/xAPI compliant training 
content in support of SSS learning and mission readiness needs. 
• Ability to provide Moodle technical subject matter expertise related to 
architecture, performance optimization, plugin management, and integration 
support. 
• Ability to support analytics and reporting functions that provide insight into 
training usage, readiness indicators, and data-driven decision support. 
• Ability to ensure compliance with federal cybersecurity, data protection, 
accessibility, and operational continuity requirements across the LMS 
environment. 
 
Schedule 
SSS anticipates that delivery of the Moodle modernization with contracted support 
would occur between October 2026 and October 2027, subject to the results of this 
market research and subsequent acquisition planning. 
 
Note to Vendors 
This RFI is issued solely for conducting market research and does not constitute a 
Request for Proposal or a Request for Quote and does not obligate the Government to 
any current or future commitments. The Government will not pay/reimburse any costs or 
charges resulting from contractors’ responses to this RFI. 
 
The Government greatly appreciates your response, which will be used for planning 
purposes in enhancing our specifications and further acquisition development for this 
critical requirement. Once a solicitation is released, we will forward your point of contact 
with a link to the site. 
 
The requested organization address is: Selective Service System (National 
Headquarters), 1501 Wilson Blvd, Arlington, VA 22209-2461. 
 
Instructions to Respond to the RFI 
If your firm is interested, capable, and qualified to provide the Government’s 
requirements described herein, please submit the following: 
 
1) Your company’s capability statement including relevant past performance, 
2) A projected timeline for completing the work, 
3) Estimated costs associated with delivering the requirement, and 
4) Any other relative information supporting this requirement. 
 

3  
The Government will allow for questions on this RFI. The suspense date for vendor 
questions to this RFI is 2:00 PM Eastern Standard Time (EST), on June 16, 2026. 
Please email your questions to the Contract Specialist contact indicated below. 
 
The RFI closes at 2:00 PM EST, on June 30, 2026. Please e-mail your submission 
and vendor information to: Ms. Shimere Cooper, Contract Specialist, 
shimere.cooper@sss.gov by the closing date and time or sooner. The vendor’s e-mail 
subject line shall state: SSS LMS Modernization. Telephone calls regarding this RFI 
will not be accepted.

Request for Information (RFI) 
Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA) 
National Center for Credibility Assessment (NCCA) 
A/V System Evaluation and Upgrade 
 
 
1. Description 
 
The Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA) is issuing this Request 
for Information (RFI) in support of the National Center for Credibility Assessment 
(NCCA). This RFI is issued solely for market research and planning purposes. It does 
not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), solicitation, or commitment by DCSA to 
issue an RFP or to award a contract. Responses are voluntary, nor does it obligate the 
Government, and will not result in reimbursement. 
 
2. Background 
 
The National Center for Credibility Assessment (NCCA) requires a comprehensive 
technical assessment and engineering design effort across its instructional spaces. The 
core requirement is to assess the specific hardware currently installed, evaluate the 
physical space constraints, and verify the exact types and capabilities of the existing 
A/V equipment. This engineering evaluation is necessary to address system 
performance gaps within NCCA's current footprint, specifically regarding audio quality in 
36 training labs and centralized remote viewing capabilities for 18 isolated "pods" and 2 
main classrooms. 
 
The contractor will serve as an expert A/V Design Consultant to provide professional 
A/V and network design and engineering services. This Phase 1 contract is strictly for 
design and consultation services. The core requirements are detailed below: 
 
Phase 1 Objective Description of Contractor Deliverables 
On-Site Analysis Conduct a comprehensive physical and technical audit of the 
existing A/V equipment, space configurations, and current 
system architecture. 
Course of Action 
(COA) Briefing 
Deliver a technical briefing outlining three (3) viable 
engineering COAs based on the assessment findings. 
Final 
Implementation 
Package 
Produce a complete, build-ready package (including a Draft 
PWS, Bill of Materials, and Engineering Drawings) that the 
Government can utilize for a future Phase 2 Implementation 
contract. 
 
 
 

3. Capability Statement 
 
To assist the Government in determining market capability, responding vendors should 
provide documentation demonstrating their technical qualifications and experience in 
the following areas: 
Focus Area Capability & Information Requested 
Corporate 
Experience 
Provide summary references for up to three (3) projects of 
similar scale and complexity completed within the last five 
(5) years, demonstrating experience with federal or 
defense-sector enterprise A/V systems. 
Industry-Standard 
Design Credentials 
Demonstrate that the proposed Lead System Designer 
holds recognized, senior-level industry design 
certifications (e.g., tier-one, independent professional A/V 
design credentials). 
Control System & 
Architecture 
Expertise 
Demonstrate certified, enterprise-level engineering 
capabilities with major commercial control systems, 
including the ability to analyze, program, and evaluate 
uncompiled system source code to inform design 
recommendations. 
Audio DSP 
Expertise 
Demonstrate certified partnership status and technical 
expertise in configuring, programming, and calibrating 
enterprise-grade Digital Signal Processors (DSPs) to 
resolve complex acoustic and audio-quality issues. 
 
 
3.1 Company Information 
 
a) Company Name: 
b) Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) Code: 
c) Address (including telephone number and email address):

4. 8(a) Certified (Yes/No) 
5. HUBZone Certified (Yes/No)

Vendors that wish to respond to this RFI should send responses via email no later than 
July 16, 2026  10AM EST to Tracey Fann at tracey.a.fann.civ@mail.mil or Noemi 
Cordova-Vazquez at noemi.v.cordovavazquez.civ@mail.mil. 
 
 
4. Security: 
 
Contractor will not have unsupervised access to systems and networks. The 
contractor shall coordinate with the responsible DCSA Office of the Chief 
Information Officer (OCIO) or Program staff prior to any visit. The visiting 
contractor shall be escorted at all times by the responsible DCSA OCIO staff. 
 
Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) / Receive, Store, or Generate 
Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI): Contractor will be provided and will 
abide by DoD Regulation 5400.7, DoD Freedom of Information Act Program, and 
DoD 5200.01-M, Information Security Program. Guidance provided under 
separate cover. In accordance with DoD Instruction 5200.48 (DoDI 5200.48) 
dated March 6, 2020, Contractors are required to ensure all personnel receive 
and complete Initial and Annual Refresher CUI education and training and 
maintain documentation of this training for audit purposes. Initial and Annual 
Refresher CUI security education, training and awareness on the required topics 
identified in Section 2002:30 of Title 32 CFR, including protection and 
management of CUI, to DoD personnel and contractors through the Center for 
Development of Security Excellence (CDSE). 
 
Operations Security (OPSEC): 
 
The contractor shall comply with OPSEC requirements contained in the contract, 
addendum thereto, or identified herein. The contractor will comply with all 
security and OPSEC policies, directives, instructions or mandates as directed. 
OPSEC and other security guidance issued to the Prime Contractor shall also 
apply to subcontractors working on this effort. 

 
The contractor will ensure compliance with the Agency’s OPSEC Policy 
Statement, Critical Information and Indicators List (CIL), and unclassified 
document destruction procedures. Items of critical information are those facts, 
which individually, or in the aggregate, reveal sensitive details about the mission, 
operation, etc., and thus require protection from adversarial collection or 
exploitation. 
 
Include OPSEC as part of the security awareness program. The contractor shall 
be familiar with OPSEC and will be required to take government furnished initial 
and annual refresher OPSEC training and will be reminded of their continued 
responsibility to protect sensitive information as directed by DoDM 5205.02. 
Sensitive unclassified information includes, but is not limited to, agency identified 
critical information, legacy “For Official Use Only” (FOUO), Controlled 
Unclassified Information (CUI), Privacy Act of 1974, Personally Identifiable 
Information (PII), Department of Defense Unclassified Controlled Nuclear 
Information (DoD UCNI) and company proprietary information. 
 
The contractor shall take the necessary precautions to ensure employees with 
access to the sensitive and critical information are instructed not to disclose or 
disseminate any information relating to the conduct and performance of the 
contract to any individual not authorized to perform on this contract. Assigned 
personnel shall be knowledgeable of the designated critical information and 
measures in place to protect it. 
 
For programs protected by a Program Protection Plan (PPP) and have identified 
Critical Program Information (CPI) and/or Critical Technologies Information (CTI), 
must be identified and protected in accordance with DoD Instruction 5200.39, 
CPI Identification and Protection within RDT&E. The contractor shall ensure that 
any program with CPI or CTI has the corresponding supplements and associated 
plan, such as an OPSEC plan, approved and in effect in support of the PPP. 
 
The contractor shall comply with OPSEC content review policies within the 
Agency. A content review is an evaluation of all information, to include all CUI, 
intended for release outside the control of the organization or release to the 
public. OPSEC focuses on identifying and protecting the organization’s 
unclassified information that may individually or in the aggregate lead to the 
compromise of classified information and sensitive activities. The contractor will 
ensure that these reviews are conducted according to agency guidance in 
accordance with mandates from DoDD 5205.02E, DoD OPSEC Program, DoDM 
5205.02-M, DoD OPSEC Program Manual, DoDI 5230.09, Clearance of DoD 
Information for Public Release, DoDI 5230.29, Security and Policy Review of 
DoD Information for Public Release, DoDI 5400.04, Provision of Information to 
Congress, DoDM 5400.07, DoD FOIA Program, and DoDI 8170.01, Online 
Information Management and Electronic Messaging. 
 

Further OPSEC guidance may be obtained by the Prime contractor contacting 
the OPSEC PM by group e-mail: dcsa.quantico.dcsa-hq.mbx.operations-
security@mail.mil. 
 
All programs and materials developed at government expense during the 
performance period of this contract are the property of the US Government.  
 
Contractor personnel shall utilize US Government or official company e-mail for 
transmitting official US Government business. Official US Government business 
shall NOT be transmitted via personal, private, and/or commercial e-mail 
accounts, i.e., YAHOO, HOTMAIL, GMAIL, JUNO, AOL, COMCAST, KNOLOGY, 
VERIZON, etc.

1.0  BACKGROUND 137 
The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Office of Information and Technology (OIT), 138 
Infrastructure Operations (IO) Enterprise Service Management (ESM) requires the 139 
acquisition of cloud-based Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) solution delivered via a 140 
multi-instance Platform-as-a-Service (PaaS) and Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) 141 
subscription model. The Government requires a fully integrated enterprise operating 142 
model in which the Contractor served as Enterprise System Integrator, is accountable 143 
for the service delivery, performance, reliability, maintainability, scalability, 144 
supportability, and continuous improvement of the enterprise IT Service Management 145 
platform and associated enterprise services.  146 
 147 
This requirement supports the VA mission to enhance IT service delivery, strengthen 148 
operational efficiency, and advance digital transformation across the enterprise. The 149 
required solution must provide enterprise-wide integration and functionality consistent 150 
with leading ERP in the marketplace 151 
 152 
VA OIT currently leverages a SaaS platform to manage critical enterprise operational 153 
practices, including enterprise service desk operations, incident and event triage, 154 
request fulfillment, change enablement, and problem resolution. Additionally, the 155 
platform supports application provisioning, clinician support, and telehealth availability. 156 
The SaaS platform is central to maintaining uptime for essential systems, including 157 
Veterans Health Information Systems and Technology Architecture (VistA) and the new 158 
Oralce/Cerner Electronic Health Record Management (EHRM) platform. 159 
 160 
As demand increases for real-time support, automation, cybersecurity compliance, and 161 
adaptability to evolving legislative and policy requirements, VA requires acquisition of a 162 
next-generation ERP solution with capabilities that meet or exceed industry standards 163 
for federal environments. This solution must span across IT Service Management 164 
(ITSM), IT Asset Management (ITAM), IT Operations Management (ITOM), IT Business 165 
Management (ITBM), Human Resource Service Delivery (HRSD), and other service 166 
domains. 167

Healthcare Contracting Division-Southeast 
 
 
 
Performance Work Statement 
Automated Texting Software Services 
 
  


 
Page 2 of 19 
PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT 
 
PART 1: GENERAL INFORMATION 
 
1. Background: This is a non-personal service base requirements contract for an automated 
texting software service. The software service will send automatic notifications by text 
message to patients when their prescription is loaded into the IntelliCab Will-Call System at 
participating Military Treatment Facility (MTF) Pharmacies. The IntelliCab Will-Call 
System is a sole proprietary system used for storing prescription medications. This base 
contract serves as a vehicle to support the automated texting software service requirements 
of Defense Health Agency (DHA) MTFs. 
 
2. Scope: The Contractor shall provide automated texting software service to send automatic 
notifications via text message to patients when their prescription is loaded into the IntelliCab 
Will-Call System at the participating DHA MTFs. The automated texting software service 
must fully integrate with the existing hardware infrastructure and the proprietary architecture 
of the IntelliCab Will-Call Solution portfolio. The system acts as an automated 
communication bridge managed externally by the contractor. It delivers opt-in and opt-out 
voice and text alerts to patients, ensuring they are promptly informed when medications are 
ready and reminding them before uncollected items are returned to pharmacy stock.
 To 
ensure patients are notified efficiently without receiving duplicate messages, the system 
categorizes communications into specific workflows: 
 
 Standard notifications: Triggered after a set time interval following the completion of the 
final prescription in a patient’s daily batch. Consolidates alerts so the patient receives 
only a single, batched notification once all their daily medications are ready. 
 
 Expedited notifications: Dispatched instantly the moment the prescription is filled. 
Exclusively used to prioritize patients who are physically waiting on-site at the 
pharmacy. 
 
 Pickup Reminders: Sent a customizable number of days after the initial alert. Can repeat 
on an “x-day” cycle. The pharmacy caps the maximum number of reminders. Example: 
“[Pharmacy Name]. You have [x] prescriptions overdue for pickup.” 
 
 Return to Stock Warning: Sent exactly once, a configurable number of days before 
uncollected items are restocked. Serves as a final notice. 
 
2.1.1. Number of messages: The number of messages per month will be estimated at the 
Task Order Level based on the MTF’s needs.  

 
Page 3 of 19 
 
2.2.The Contractor shall provide, at no additional cost to the Government, software revisions 
and upgrades for proper operations. 
 
2.3.Technical Support: Contractor shall provide technical phone assistance Monday through 
Friday 0700-2000 hours Eastern Standard Time (EST) excluding holidays and MTF 
closures. The contractor must provide troubleshooting and technical support via phone, 
email, or remote access within 24 hours of a reported issue. 
 
3. Base Requirement Contract Ordering Period and Task Order Period of Performance 
(POP): 
 
3.1.The performance for Task Orders (TO) under the base requirements contract shall end on 
or before July 20, 2031. 
 
3.1.1. The base requirements contract may be extended under the authority of FAR 
52.217-8, which would extend the TOs POP to January 20, 2032. 
  
3.2.The POP for individual task orders issued under the base requirements contract shall be 
for one (1) year or less. 
 
4. Place of Performance: The Contractor shall perform all work under this contract at the  
Task Order specified locations. 
 
5. Hours of operation: The contractor is responsible for conducting business Monday through  
Friday except Federal holidays or when the Government facility is closed due to local or 
national emergencies, administrative closings, or similar Government directed facility 
closings. The contractor must always maintain an adequate workforce for the uninterrupted 
performance of all tasks defined within this PWS when the Government facility is not closed 
for the above reasons. 
 
6. Documentation and Invoicing: The contractor must submit their invoice monthly. The 
invoice shall include the usage in terms of the number of messages sent for that month per 
MTF and Contract Line Item Number (CLIN). 
 
7. Quality Control: The Contractor shall submit a quality control inspection system.  This must 
include descriptions of people and positions charged with the responsibility of making 
inspections, methods of identifying deficiencies in services, and in quality control functions.  
The Contractor’s Quality Control Plan shall be submitted to the Contracting Officer (KO) for 
approval within 15 days after the contract award. 

 
Page 4 of 19 
 
8. Security Requirements 
 
8.1. Operational Security: Neither the Contractor nor any of its contract service providers 
shall disclose or cause to disseminate any information concerning operations of military 
activities. Such action(s) could result in violation of the contract and possible legal 
actions. U.S. Government records, copies of original results and reports, verified original 
data, corrected data, and corrected supporting final reports are maintained by the 
Contractor but remain the property of the U.S. Government. These files/results must be 
surrendered to the Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR). 
 
8.2. Training: The contractor shall complete required training as identified at the TO level. 
 
8.3. HIPAA AND PRIVACY ACT TRAINING. Contractor personnel requiring network 
access to the hosted applications shall successfully complete the MHS Privacy Act and 
Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) Privacy and Security 
training prior to access to the hosted applications and then annually thereafter. The 
Contractor shall submit a copy of the Privacy Act and HIPAA course certificate along 
with the completed System Authorization Access Request (SAAR) and DoD IA 
Awareness training certificate to the COR for each affected Contractor personnel. The 
Contractor is responsible for maintaining an active database of Contractor employee 
HIPAA and Privacy Act training status and providing initial and annual training 
certificates to the TO COR, as requested. The course is accessible via Joint Knowledge 
Online (JKO). Please refer to the Joint Knowledge Online (JKO) Instructions on 
accessing JKO. 
 
8.4. PII/PHI, AND FEDERAL INFORMATION REQUIREMENTS: See Part 4 of this 
PWS. 
 
8.5. The contractor must comply with the Telephone Consumer Protection Act (TCPA). 
 
9. Installation Access: The contractor and all associated subcontractors’ employees shall 
comply with applicable installation, facility, and area commander installation and facility 
access and local security policies and procedures (provided by the Government 
representative). The contractor shall also provide all information required for background 
checks to meet installation access requirements. The contractor workforce must comply with 
all personal identity verification requirements as directed by Department of War (DoW), 
HQDA, DHA and/or local policy. Should the Force Protection Condition (FPCON) at any 
individual facility or installation change, the Government may require changes in contractor 
security matters or processes. 

 
Page 5 of 19 
 
10. Contractor Identification: Contractor personnel performing services in a contractor 
capacity in a Government facility are required to possess and wear an identification badge 
that displays his or her name and the name of their company.  Ensure all those with whom 
the person interacts in any face-to-face dealings while supporting the Government understand 
that the person is contractor support personnel. 
 
11. Safety Requirements: The Contractor shall maintain safety and health standards compliant 
with requirements of the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA). 
 
 
PART 2: GOVERNMENT FURNISHED PROPERTY, EQUIPMENT, AND SERVICES 
 
The Government will not provide physical hardware, equipment, materials, or facilities to the 
Contractor in support of this contract. 
 
 
PART 3: CONTRACTOR FURNISHED ITEMS AND RESPONSIBILITIES 
 
The Contractor shall furnish all technology, materials, supplies, facilities, and services required 
to perform work under this contract. The Contractor shall be responsible for all upgrades and 
maintenance of the software as required. 
 
PART 4: PERSONALLY IDENTIFIABLE INFORMATION, PROTECTED HEALTH 
INFORMATION, AND FEDERAL INFORMATION REQUIREMENTS  
(Revised May 23, 2017) 
 
 
1. General Requirements Overview - Personally Identifiable Information (PII), Protected Health 
Information (PHI) and Federal Information Laws. 
 
This Section addresses the Contractor’s requirements under The Privacy Act of 1974 (Privacy 
Act), The Freedom of Information Act (FOIA), and The Health Insurance Portability and 
Accountability Act (HIPAA) as set forth in applicable statutes, implementing regulations and 
Department of Defense (DoD) issuances. In general, the Contractor shall comply with the 
specific requirements set forth in this Section and elsewhere in this Contract. The Contractor 
shall also comply with requirements relating to records management as described herein.  
 
This Contract incorporates by reference the federal regulations and DoD issuances referred to in 
this Section. If any authority is amended or replaced, the changed requirement is effective when 

 
Page 6 of 19 
it is incorporated under contract change procedures. Where a federal regulation and any DoD 
issuance govern the same subject matter, the Contractor shall first follow the more specific DoD 
implementation unless the DoD issuance does not address or is unclear on that matter. DoD 
issuances are available at http://www.dtic.mil/whs/directives.  
For purposes of this Section, the following definitions apply.  
DoD Privacy Act Issuances means the DoD issuances implementing the Privacy Act, 
which are DoDD 5400.11 (October 29, 2014) and DoD 5400.11-R (May 14, 2007).  
 
HIPAA Rules means, collectively, the HIPAA Privacy, Security, Breach and 
Enforcement Rules, issued by the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) 
and codified at 45 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) Part 160 and Part 164, Subpart E 
(Privacy), Subpart C (Security), Subpart D (Breach) and Part 160, Subparts C-E 
(Enforcement), as amended.  
 
Additional HIPAA rules regarding electronic transactions and code sets (45 CFR Part 
162) are not addressed in this Section and are not included in the term HIPAA Rules.  
 
DoD HIPAA Issuances means the DoD issuances implementing the HIPAA Rules in the 
DoD Military Health System (MHS). These issuances are DoD 6025.18-R (January 24, 
2003), Department of Defense Instruction (DoDI) 6025.18 (December 2, 2009), and 
DoDI 8580.02 (August 12, 2015).  
 
Defense Health Agency (DHA) Privacy Office means the DHA Privacy and Civil 
Liberties Office. The DHA Privacy Office Chief is the HIPAA Privacy and Security 
Officer for DHA, including the National Capital Region Medical Directorate (NCRMD).  
 
2. Records Management  
 
When creating and maintaining official government records, the Contractor shall comply with all 
federal requirements established by 44 United States Code (U.S.C.) Chapters 21, 29, 31, 33 and 
35, and by 36 CFR, Chapter XII, Subchapter B – Records Management. The Contractor shall 
also comply with DoD Administrative Instruction No. 15 (DoD AI-15), “OSD Records and 
Information Management Program” (May 3, 2013) and Records Management requirements 
outlined in the current TRICARE Operations Manual (TOM).  
 
3. Freedom of Information Act (FOIA)  
 
The Contractor shall comply with the following procedures if it receives a FOIA request and 
immediately contact the DHA FOIA Officer for evaluation/action:  

 
Page 7 of 19 
The Contractor shall inform beneficiaries that DHA FOIA procedures require a written request 
addressed to the DHA Freedom of Information Service Center, 7700 Arlington Boulevard, Suite 
5101, Falls Church, Virginia 22042-5101 (or email requests addressed to 
DHA.FOIA@mail.mil), and that the request shall describe the desired record as completely as 
possible (ideally with Contract or modification number) to facilitate its retrieval from files and to 
reduce search fees which may be borne by the requestor. Although the administrative time limit 
to grant or deny a request (ten working days after receipt) does not begin until the request is 
received by DHA, the Contractor shall act as quickly as possible.  
 
In response to requests received by the Contractor for the release of information, unclassified 
information, documents and forms which were previously provided to the public as part of 
routine services shall continue to be made available in accordance with previously established 
criteria. All other requests from the public for release of DHA records and, specifically, all 
requests that reference FOIA shall be immediately forwarded to DHA, ATTENTION: Freedom 
of Information Officer, for appropriate action. Direct contact, including interim replies, between 
TRICARE contractors and such requestors is not authorized. The Contractor shall process 
requests by individuals for access to records about themselves in accordance with directions 
from the DHA Freedom of Information Service Center. If such a requestor specifically makes the 
request under the Privacy Act or does not make clear whether the request is made under FOIA or 
the Privacy Act, the Contractor shall process the request in accordance with directions from the 
DHA Privacy Office. If requestor specifically seeks PHI under HIPAA, the Contractor shall 
follow paragraph 8.1.6, relating to individual rights of access to PHI.  
 
4. Systems of Records  
 
In order to meet the requirements of the Privacy Act and the DoD Privacy Act Issuances, the 
Contractor shall identify to the DHA Contracting Officer (CO) systems of records that are or will 
be maintained or operated for DHA where records of PII collected from individuals are 
maintained and specifically retrieved using a personal identifier. Upon identification of such 
systems to the CO, and prior to the lawful operation of such systems, the Contractor shall 
coordinate with the DHA Privacy Office to complete systems of records notices (SORNs) for 
submission and publication in the Federal Register as coordinated by the Defense Privacy, Civil 
Liberties, and Transparency Division, and as required by the DoD Privacy Act Issuances.

B.4  PERFORMANCE Work STATEMENT (PWS) 
Performance Work Statement (PWS) 
Mixed Reality Volumetric Capture Learning Platform 
Central Arkansas Veterans Healthcare System (CAVHS) 
1.0 PURPOSE: The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) requires a brand-name or equal 
mixed-reality volumetric capture learning platform equivalent to GigXR to support nursing and 
allied health clinical simulation. The platform must deliver high-fidelity, 360-degree 
volumetric video of real human subjects, enabling realistic clinical assessment and 
decision-making. Computer-generated imagery (CGI), polygonal avatars, or animated/manual 
renderings do not meet Government performance requirements. 
This PWS applies to four (4) VA pilot locations. 
The naming of GigXR within this requirement is for the limited purpose of identifying the 
minimum essential technical, functional, and performance characteristics necessary to meet 
the Government’s needs, as permitted under FAR 11.104 and VAAR 811.104. 
The use of a brand name in this requirement does not restrict offerors to the specific brand 
identified. Products offered as “equal” shall meet or exceed the salient characteristics listed in 
the Performance Work Statement (PWS). Offerors providing “equal” products must furnish 
supporting documentation demonstrating compliance with all specified requirements.
 
2.0 SCOPE: The Contractor shall deliver all labor, software, licenses, platform access, training, 
maintenance, and technical support necessary to enable mixed-reality instructional capability for 
up to 375 learners across the four participating VA medical facilities. The Contractor shall 
ensure that the platform is fully functional, accessible, secure, and compliant with VA 
regulations.

U.S. Department of Commerce

Institute for Telecommunication Sciences 
 
1. BACKGROUND 
The Institute for Telecommunication Sciences (ITS) will conduct research and engineering projects that 
examine the feasibility of deploying Open Radio Access Network (RAN) systems consisting of radio 
subsystems from multiple vendors. This test equipment will be used to test Open RAN systems deployed 
in the CRAIN laboratory.  The CRAIN 5G Laboratory currently uses a Viavi testing solution, TM500, as 
testing for 5G base stations in ORAN. The TM500 is a load tester that uses software to simulate test 
cases. The software requires specific licenses to run specific scenarios, and these licenses are required to 
operate with specific vendors and test cases. 
 
2. OBJECTIVE 
NTIA.ITS requires the purchase and renewal of specific TM500 licenses to continue operating the 
TM500 for ORAN research. These licenses are required for functionality of test cases on JMA and Nokia 
equipment as well as licenses required for video test cases.

STATEMENT OF WORK 
Deployable Asymmetrical ISAC Testbed 
I. BACKGROUND 
The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), Communications Technology Laboratory 
(CTL), Wireless Networks Division, Radio Access and Propagation Metrology Group (673.02), requires a 
highly portable, asymmetrical dual-node computing and radio system designed for Integrated Sensing and 
Communication (ISAC) experimentation. 
The purpose of this procurement is to establish a flexible research testbed capable of simultaneously 
emulating a next-generation wireless communications network and a high-fidelity radar sensing system. 
The testbed will support experimentation involving 5G/6G physical-layer communications, synchronized 
software-defined radio operations, radar sensing topologies, and offline post-processing of high-
bandwidth RF data collected within a Government-furnished anechoic chamber.  
 
II. SCOPE 
The Contractor shall provide one (1) turnkey Deployable Asymmetrical ISAC Testbed consisting of: 
• One (1) Transmit/Protocol Server (C1)  
• One (1) ISAC Sensor Server (C2)  
• Two (2) Software Defined Radios (R1)  
• One (1) Clock Distribution Hub (K1)  
• One (1) Local Oscillator Sharing Interconnect (L2)  
• All RF interconnects and antennas  
• Mobile rack enclosure and power management system  
• All integration, assembly, cabling, testing, and configuration services  
The Contractor shall provide a fully assembled and operational system capable of meeting all 
performance requirements identified in this Statement of Work.  
 
III. TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS 
3.0 Deployable Asymmetrical ISAC Testbed 
Quantity: One (1) Each 
The Contractor shall provide a complete Deployable Asymmetrical ISAC Testbed meeting the following 
minimum requirements. 
 

3.1 Mobile Enclosure and Power Management (M1) 
The system shall be housed within a portable rack enclosure. 
Rack Enclosure 
The rack shall: 
• Be a 19-inch EIA standard rack  
• Be mounted on heavy-duty casters  
• Not exceed 48 inches in total height including wheels  
• Include horizontal and vertical cable management  
• Allow flush mounting of SDR units  
• Position SDRs approximately 24 inches above floor level  
Acoustic Requirements 
The integrated rack shall: 
• Not exceed 50 dBA at idle  
• Not exceed 60 dBA at full load  
• Utilize low-noise cooling technologies  
• Prohibit the use of uncontrolled high-RPM server fans  
Electrical Requirements 
The system shall: 
• Operate on 120V / 20A power  
• Utilize a NEMA 5-20P plug  
• Include a minimum 20-foot power cord  
• Include a rack-mounted PDU  
• Provide a minimum of 20 percent spare outlet capacity  
UPS Requirements 
The system shall include: 
• Minimum 2200 VA / 1980W UPS  
• Minimum 5-minute runtime at full load  
• Graceful shutdown capability when battery capacity reaches 30 percent  
 
3.2 Radio and RF Front-End Subsystem 
Software Defined Radios (R1) 

The Contractor shall provide two (2) SDRs meeting the following requirements: 
• Commercial Off-The-Shelf equipment  
• Minimum 500 MS/s streaming per channel  
• Minimum 1 GHz instantaneous bandwidth  
• Frequency range of 10 MHz to 20 GHz  
• Compatible with UHD API  
• Equivalent to Ettus USRP X420 or better  
Clock Distribution Hub (K1) 
The Contractor shall provide one (1) timing hub containing: 
• Integrated GPSDO  
• 10 MHz reference output  
• 1 PPS timing output  
• Equivalent to NI OctoClock-G CDA-2990 or better  
LO Sharing Cable (L2) 
The Contractor shall provide: 
• One SMA-to-SMA phase stable cable  
• Rated to 18 GHz  
• Maximum insertion loss of 1.5 dB  
RF Cabling 
Provide: 
• Four (4) one-meter external RF cables  
• Two (2) five-meter transmit cables  
• Two (2) one-meter receive cables  
All RF cables shall: 
• Be microwave grade  
• Be phase stable  
• Utilize SMA connectors  
• Meet insertion loss requirements specified herein  
Antennas 
The Contractor shall provide: 
Ku-Band Set 

• One transmit antenna  
• Three receive antennas  
X-Band Set 
• One transmit antenna  
• Three receive antennas  
All antennas shall include compatible waveguide adapters. 
 
3.3 Data Interconnects 
The Contractor shall provide: 
• Two (2) 100 GbE QSFP28 DAC cables  
The cables shall support full-rate communication between SDRs and server network interfaces. 
 
3.4 Server Requirements 
General Server Requirements (C1 and C2) 
Each server shall include: 
Processor 
• Enterprise workstation-class CPU  
• Exactly 24 physical cores  
• Exactly 48 threads  
• Minimum 128 PCIe Gen5 lanes  
Motherboard 
• Enterprise workstation motherboard  
• Minimum six PCIe 5.0 x16 slots  
• Minimum four PCIe 5.0 M.2 slots  
Memory 
• Minimum 128 GB DDR5 ECC RDIMM  
• Minimum 6000 MT/s  
High-Speed Network Interface 

• Dual-port 100 GbE QSFP28 adapter  
• NVIDIA/Mellanox ConnectX-5 or ConnectX-6  
• DPDK hardware offload support  
Storage 
High-Speed Storage: 
• Minimum 4 TB enterprise NVMe RAID 0 array  
• Sustained write speed greater than 6 GB/s for 10 minutes  
Archival Storage: 
• Minimum 16 TB enterprise HDD  
Additional NIC 
• One four-port 1 GbE adapter  
Power 
• Minimum 1200W power supply  
Cooling 
• 360 mm AIO liquid cooling  
Operating System 
• Ubuntu 24.04 LTS installed  
Video Adapter (C1) 
The C1 server shall include: 
• Low-profile workstation graphics card  
• HDMI output  
• DisplayPort output  
 
3.5 ISAC Sensor Server Additional Requirements (C2) 
The C2 server shall additionally include a professional GPU meeting or exceeding: 
GPU Memory 

• Minimum 48 GB ECC GDDR7  
Bus Interface 
• PCIe Gen5 x16  
Processing 
• Minimum 14,080 processing cores  
• Minimum 440 Tensor cores  
• Minimum 110 RT cores  
Memory Bandwidth 
• Minimum 1,344 GB/s  
Thermal Requirements 
• Maximum 300W TDP  
• Active blower cooling  
• Dual-slot FHFL design  
Equivalent to NVIDIA RTX PRO 5000 Blackwell or better. 
 
IV. DELIVERABLES 
The Contractor shall provide: 
1. Fully integrated Deployable Asymmetrical ISAC Testbed  
2. All required hardware and software  
3. System assembly and integration  
4. Ubuntu operating system installation  
5. Benchmark testing results  
6. Configuration documentation  
7. Warranty documentation  
8. OEM warranty transfer documentation  
Electronic copies of benchmark and testing results shall be provided to: 
rick.candell@nist.gov 
 
V. DELIVERY 

FOB Destination 
National Institute of Standards and Technology 
ATTN: Rick Candell 
Mail Stop 673.02 
100 Bureau Drive 
Gaithersburg, MD 20899 
Delivery shall be completed no later than: 
31 December 2026 
 
VI. PLACE OF PERFORMANCE 
All assembly, integration, configuration, and testing shall occur at the Contractor's facility. 
Final delivery shall be made to NIST Gaithersburg, Maryland. 
Government acceptance testing shall occur at the Government facility. 
 
VII. GOVERNMENT ACCEPTANCE TESTING 
Acceptance shall occur within 30 business days after delivery. 
The Government will perform: 
System Initialization Testing 
• BIOS POST verification  
• Operating system verification  
Network Connectivity Testing 
• 100 GbE connectivity verification  
• SDR synchronization verification  
Storage Testing 
• fio benchmark demonstrating greater than 6 GB/s sustained writes for 10 minutes  
Receive Data Testing 

• 6 GB/s data capture verification  
Transmit Data Testing 
• 6 GB/s data transmission verification  
Final acceptance shall occur upon successful completion of all testing requirements. 
 
VIII. WARRANTY 
The Contractor shall provide: 
System Warranty 
• Minimum one-year comprehensive warranty  
• Coverage for labor and parts  
• Coverage for integration and workmanship  
OEM Pass-Through Warranty 
All original manufacturer warranties shall transfer directly to NIST. 
RMA Support 
Defective components shall be repaired or replaced at no additional cost through standard manufacturer 
RMA procedures. 
 
IX. VENDOR REQUIREMENTS 
The Contractor shall: 
1. Possess an Export Control Classification Number (ECCN) at time of award.  
2. Maintain an active SAM.gov registration and UEI.  
3. Provide all equipment as new commercial products.  
4. Provide a turnkey integrated solution.  
 
X. PAYMENT 
Payment shall be made in accordance with Net 30 terms upon: 
1. Delivery of the complete system.  

2. Successful completion of Government acceptance testing.  
3. Receipt of a proper invoice.  
100% payment shall be made after Government acceptance.

STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW) 
1. BACKGROUND
T
he Office of Terrorism and Financial Intelligence (TFI) develops and implements U.S. 
government strategies to combat terrorist financing domestically and internationally and 
develops and implements the National Money Laundering Strategy as well as other policies and 
programs to fight financial crimes. As a component of TFI, the Office of Intelligence and 
Analysis (OIA) is responsible for TFI's intelligence functions, integrating the Treasury 
Department into the larger intelligence community (IC), and providing support to both Treasury 
leadership and the IC. TFI oversees several component offices and bureaus, including the Office 
of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC), which administers and enforces economic and trade 
sanctions based on US foreign policy and national security goals against targeted foreign 
countries and regimes, terrorists, international narcotics traffickers, those engaged in activities 
related to the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction, and other threats to the national 
security, foreign policy or economy of the United States. Treasury's Office of International 
Affairs protects and supports U.S. economic prosperity by strengthening the external 
environment for U.S. growth, preventing and mitigating global financial instability, and 
managing key global challenges. 
I
n support of these missions, TFI (including OFAC, OIA, and TFFC) and the Office of 
International Affairs require a subscription to a web-based online search and data visualization 
service to assist with investigative and compliance functions. The subscription product must 
offer:  
• P
roactive network analysis of persons on OFAC’s Specially Designated Nationals
(SDN) list and other global watch lists
• Direct access to the source materials (e.g., media reports, business records, etc.)
2
. SCOPE
T
he purpose of this requirement is to acquire a subscription for at least 3 accounts to an existing 
off-the-shelf service that provides proactive, network-based analysis of sanctioned or trade-
restricted parties. This standalone service must assist with developing linkages, allowing for 
exploration without significant lead information. Additionally, the service must offer multiple 
degrees of separation analysis and permit a user to explore any node for additional links. Finally, 
this service must also contain copies of the documentary materials underlying the analysis (i.e., 
media reports, business records, etc.). 
3
. SPECIFIC TASKS
C
ontractor shall provide 24/7 access to an online subscription service for up to 3 user accounts 
per period of performance.

here is no GFE or GFI in support of this requirement.

S
ervices will be available online via the contractor’s website. This subscription service will be

STATEMENT OF WORK 
Revenue Enhancement Services for Billings Area Indian Health Service 
 
1.0 GENERAL: 
This statement of work (SOW) describes the requirements of the IDIQ Contract for non-
personal Revenue Enhancement Services to be performed at the health centers and 
hospitals located within Billings Area Indian Health Service (BIL-IHS).  
 
1.1 Scope: The Contractor shall provide Revenue Enhancement Services to the health 
centers and hospitals within the BIL-IHS in accordance with this SOW. Duties and 
responsibilities consist of providing Revenue Enhancement Services to support the 
mission of the Indian Health Services.   
 
1.2 Background: The Billings Area Indian Health Service (BIL-IHS) oversees the 
delivery of public health, environmental health, health care services and community-
based disease prevention services to more than 70,000 American Indian and Alaska 
Native people in Montana and Wyoming. These services are delivered through five 
IHS-operated Service Units.  
 
1.3 Purpose: The purpose of this contract is to acquire services for revenue 
enhancement and generation with Medical Coding, Accounts Receivable and Third 
Party Billing. The contractor shall be responsible for providing revenue generation 
consultative services and compliance audit for Medical Coding, Accounts Receivable 
and Third Party Billing services on an “As Needed Basis”. Allowing for coding, data 
entry, auditing and coding queue review. The Contractor shall provide Specialist(s) 
with expertise in reimbursement guidelines, full internal control policy compliance 
and knowledge of Resource Patient Management System (RPMS).  
 
1.4 Period of Performance:  
One (1) Base period of 12 months; 
 
1.5 Places of Performance:  
Contracted revenue enhancement services shall be performed for the following 
locations: 
 
Blackfeet Service Unit (BFSU): 
o Blackfeet Community Hospital; Browning Montana 
o Heart Butte Health Station; Heart Butte, Montana 
 
Crow Service Unit (CSU): 
o Crow/Northern Cheyenne Hospital; Crow Agency, Montana 
o Lodge Grass Health Clinic; Lodge Grass, Montana 
o Pryor Health Station; Pryor, Montana 
Fort Belknap Service Unit (FBSU);  
o Fort Belknap Hospital; Harlem, Montana 
o Eagle Child Health Station; Hays, Montana 
 
 
 

Fort Peck Service Unit (FPSU); 
o Verne E. Gibbs Clinic; Poplar, Montana 
o Chief Redstone Clinic; Wolf Point, Montana 
 
Northern Cheyenne Service Unit (NCSU);  
o Northern Cheyenne Health Clinic; Lame Deer, Montana 
 
2.0 GENERAL REQUIREMENTS:  
 
2.1 Revenue Enhancement Services: Duties and responsibilities shall encompass 
revenue enhancement / revenue cycle management coordination to assist the health 
centers and hospitals of the BIL-IHS  
 Familiar and knowledgeable of Electronic Health Record (EHR) system. 
 Familiar and knowledgeable of Health Information Portability Accountability 
Act (HIPAA) requirements. 
 Comply with industry standards, Indian Health Service Rules and Regulations. 
 Comply with State and Federal Laws including but not limited to Office of 
Inspector General (OIG) recommendation and guidelines. 
 Services to review data from PCC/Superbill/HER to ensure IHS is receiving 
appropriate levels of reimbursements based on codes and provider 
documentation. 
 Services to review and provide accuracy and completeness for appropriate 
ICDIO-CM and CPT/HCPCS codes. 
 Services to review and provide reports on findings of Revenue Generation. 
 Service to provide audit service and recommendation. 
 Contractor shall provide Personnel with Charge Master Functions and 
Transaction Code Assignment 
 Contractor shall provide Personnel of credentials and experience of billing and 
Accounts Receivable. 
 Contractor shall be responsible for recording, keeping, and securing backup 
for transaction information by the Government for maximum of three (3) years 
and not less than one (1) year. 
 Contractor shall have minimum of three (3) years of experience with 
private/Medicare and Medicaid billing industry. 
 Contractor shall provide all necessary resources to complete service, 
administrative supplies, transportation, personnel and any other applicable 
charges. 
 
2.2 Hours of Operation: 
Normal Business Hours are Monday thru Friday; 8:00am – 5:00pm (MST), excluding 
federally recognized holidays.  
 
2.3 Federal Holidays: 
The following holidays are observed by the Billings Area IHS: New Year’s Day, 
Washington’s Birthday, Martin Luther King’s Birthday, Memorial Day, Juneteenth, 
Independence Day, Labor Day, Columbus Day, Veterans Day, Thanksgiving, 
Christmas, any day specifically declared to be a national holiday.  
 
 
 

2.4 Changes to the Statement of Work: Any changes to this SOW shall be authorized 
and approved only through written correspondence from the Contracting Officer 
(CO). Costs incurred by the contractor through the actions of parties other than the 
CO shall be borne by the contractor.  
 
 
3.0 GOVERNMENT RESPONSIBILITIES:  
 
3.1 The Billings Area IHS gives permission to the Contractor to provide Revenue 
Enhancement Services that are to be performed in accordance with this Statement of 
Work.  
 
3.2 The Government will provide technology equipment with on-site access to EHR for 
Contractor’s personnel to complete requirement. The Government will provide on-
going method of monitoring and evaluation of the quality and appropriateness of 
coding and coding queue, along with information entered into RPMS and EHR as it 
crosses over to the Business Office.  
 
 
4.0 CONTRACTOR RESPONSIBILITIES:  
 
4.1 Contractor Employees: The Contractor shall ensure that appropriate contractor 
staff’s credentials (e.g., security clearance, computer security training, and 
degrees/certifications, etc.) are current and approved within the BIL-IHS.  
 
4.2 Supervision: The Government will neither supervise Contractor employees nor 
control the method of performance. The Contractor is responsible for personnel 
management and shall promptly notify the Contracting Officer (CO) and Contracting 
Officer’s Representative (COR) of any Government action that appears to create a 
personal services relationship. 
 
4.3 Authorized Services: Contractor shall perform only revenue enhancement services 
that are authorized through this contract. Only those services specified within the 
contract are authorized. Before performing any service of a non-contract nature, the 
CO or his/her designee must be advised of the reason for this additional work. If 
appropriate, the CO or his/her designee may authorize the additional services under 
a separate purchase mechanism.  
 
4.4 Customer Service: The Contractor shall identify a lead point-of-contact to assist IHS 
staff with administrative questions and issues related to services performed through 
this contract.  
 
4.5 Special Contract Requirements: The contractor shall comply with all federal 
regulations and comply with the Indian Health Service’s Third Party Resource and 
Internal Control Policy, the Debt Collection Policy, and the Indian Health Service’s 
statistical and reporting systems for all departments. The contractor will comply with 
the American Hospital Association (AHA) Official Coding Guidelines for ICD and the 
Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) Guidelines, and any specific IHS coding and 
data entry policies and procedures. 
 

4.6 RPMS: The contractor will have access, and will be required, with restrictions as 
defined by the Service Unit, to the following Service Unit RPMS modules and other 
access as requested by the contractor and agreed upon by the Service Unit. 
1. Patient Registration System 
2. Third Party Billing System 
3. Accounts Receivable System 
4. Patient Care Component/EHR, Medical and Ancillary Services; and 
5. Any others deemed necessary by Service Unit/Area Staff 
 
4.7 Invoices: The Contractor shall submit invoices no later than the 5th of each month. 
Invoices shall be broken down per Contract Line Item Number (CLIN) to ensure 
matching in the Invoice Processing Platform (IPP).  
 
 
5.0 CONTRACTOR RESPONSIBILITIES: 
Specific areas of performance include the following: 
 
5.1 Third Party Resource Billing 
5.1.1 The contractor shall bill third party resources that include Private 
Insurance, Medicaid/CHIP, VA, Medicare Part A and B, and those claims 
that encompass coding. 
5.1.2 The contractor shall provide third party resource billing services. IHS 
approval must be granted for direct access and use of the current RPMS 
(Resource Patient Management Systems) via VPN. The Government will 
provide access to the RPMS system.  
5.1.3 Editing, approving, and exporting (electronic or hardcopy) shall include 
inpatient/outpatient, and medical and ancillary services. 
5.1.4 Visit data from PCC/Superbill/EHR will be reviewed for accuracy and 
completeness for appropriate ICD, CPT, HCPCS, and CDT codes. Flag, if 
incomplete, and return to Coding department. 
5.1.5 The contractor shall process and submit claims directly to the appropriate 
carrier or clearinghouse. 
5.1.6 The contractor shall not charge for any claims rejected prior to 
submission to the carrier. Rejects or denied claims due to coding will 
require the contractor to make appropriate corrections and re-approve at 
no charge.  
5.1.7 The Contractor shall submit a Quality Assurance Plan with associated 
reports as described within the plan. Upon request, the report(s) shall be 
submitted on, or within 15 days, to the requesting IHS facility. 
5.1.8 The Indian Health Service will schedule management meetings, as 
needed, to discuss project needs.  
5.1.9 The Contractor will be responsible for their own travel, lodging and other 
miscellaneous travel arrangement associated with the consultation 
services. 
5.1.10 If an audit or other legal action should arise after the expiration of this 
contract, the contractor will still prepare any documentation that may be 
necessary to complete the audit.  

5.1.11 The Contractor shall have a minimum of three (3) years experience in the 
billing industry, with proof of experience in electronic claim 
submission/maintenance (three years minimum) 
5.1.12 All remittance/receipts from the carrier shall be mailed to the appropriate 
lock box for the particular facility in which the services were performed.  
 
 
 
5.2 Patient Accounts Receivable: 
5.2.1 The contractor shall provide accounts receivable posting and follow-up 
services in accordance with the Third Party Internal Controls policy. 
 
5.3 Consultant Services / Compliance Auditing Functions and Processes: 
5.3.1 The contractor shall provide consultant services to the BAIHS health 
centers and hospitals on revenue generation cycle functions and 
processes, including, but not limited to the following:  
a. The contractor will provide on the job training for individual staff and 
program development on the various functions of the revenue 
enhancement process. The contractor will also serve as a technical 
advisor to the Service Unit multi-disciplinary revenue enhancement 
teams at the Service Units in addressing the revenue enhancement 
work plan.  
b. The contractor will identify key management objectives and 
accountability in the revenue generation cycle. Develop timelines to 
accomplish key management objectives and develop methods for 
accountability.  
c. Eliminate redundancy of work within the revenue generation cycle, 
refine and implement new or assist to re-establish workflow 
processes. Identify best possible physical location of staff in the 
revenue generation process. Provide staff training to accommodate 
new tasks for each job per workflow process changes.  
d. The contractor will develop a concurrent program for providers and 
other staff to improve documentation to ensure proper and accurate 
coding for revenue generation purposes.  
e. Perform compliance audits on individual processes per request of the 
Service Units or Area Office in accordance with Standard Auditing 
Practices. 
f. The contractor will be responsible for their own travel, lodging and 
other miscellaneous travel arrangements.  
 
5.4 Coding, Data Entry, Auditing, and Reporting: 
5.4.1 Shall code and make complete and accurate medical ancillary visits via 
the IHS EHR, RPMS, PCC and Admission/Discharge/Transfer (ADT) 
systems. Apply IHS and National Reporting and Coding Guidelines. The 
contractor shall code the medical visits and/or inpatient stays assigned by 
the facility. 
5.4.2 The IHS “visit verification coding queue” (VVQ) will be accessed for 
auditing, accuracy, and completion of all medical visits before a claim can 
be generated. When processes cannot be completed in the Q – the 

vendor needs to access the PCC data entry and supervisor options to 
complete.  
5.4.3 Editing, appending, merging, moving data elements and deleting 
duplicate entries will be part of the process with application of reporting 
requirements via the PCC system. 
5.4.4 The Indian Health Service will schedule management meetings, as 
needed, to discuss project needs.  
5.4.5 The contractor, when working incomplete visits in EHR, will send provider 
“Notifications” for any record deficiencies (coding, data entry, 
documentation), utilizing the Coding Queue Notification Template, if 
available. The contractor will be paid only one time per visit and/or 
inpatient stay, they will code the visit on first encounter. If they have to 
incomplete the visit, they will do the notification, facility will let contractor 
know when the notification is completed. Contractor will then complete 
the visit. 
5.4.6 The contractor shall have a minimum of three (3) years experience and/or 
be a certified coder (copy of certification) with coding.
