Statement of Work 
West Publishing Clear Software or EQUAL 
1. Background: 
The Office of Criminal Investigations (OCI) is the Food & Drug Administration’s law enforcement arm 
responsible for investigating suspected criminal violations of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, 
the Federal Anti-Tampering Act, and other related federal statutes. OCI’s Investigative Analysis Branch 
(IAB) is tasked with the responsibility of supporting criminal investigations through researching 
resources to validate and corroborate data obtained during criminal investigations.   
2. Objective: 
OCI’s IAB needs a secure, aggregate, web-portal resource for access to public and commercial telephone 
directories and law enforcement records.   
3. Summarized Scope of Work: 
FDA/OCI requires access to a secure database (West Publishing Clear OR EQUAL) to access public, 
commercial and law enforcement records for all city, county, state, and federal records in the United 
States.  The database shall have the following salient functional characteristics: 
• Secure Access to this resource shall be via a hypertext transfer protocol secure web-based 
interface from public access and limited to only authorized end users. 
• Queries submitted by FDA/OCI end users shall be cloaked from the Contractor due to the 
sensitivity of OCI’s investigations.  Neither the Contractor nor any third parties may have access 
to the actual query and results for any internal review purposes.  
• The reports obtained from this database shall be collected, collated, and collaborated to provide 
an overview of the entities of interest to OCI.  
• Telephone numbers:  Search for/Provide 
o Reverse residential and commercial landline telephone numbers; 
o Reverse cell phone numbers; 
o Reverse voice over internet protocol (VoIP) phone numbers in the United States and 
Canada 
o Address (street number, street name, city, state, ZIP code) for all telephone queries 
o Carrier contact information 
 
•  Person Search:  Search for a person based on combinations of first name, middle name, last 
name, SSN, age range, date of birth, address, city, state, zip. 
• Credit Reporting:  The database shall provide current credit header information from Trans 
Union, Equifax and Experian.  This information shall provide the most current, up-to-date 

address information as well as high-risk address alerts such as mail drops, known fraudulent site 
activity and non-existent addresses. 
• People at Work Search:  Search for people based on possible business relationships and places 
of employment. 
• Workplace Locator:  Search for a subject’s possible workplaces. 
• People in the News:  Search for news articles based on a person. 
• Batch Person Search:  Search for current “best” information on a limited list of subjects 
• Advanced Person Search:  Search for a person using advanced criteria such as previous city and 
state, relatives’ names, and previous last name. 
• Death Records Search:  Search death records nationwide. 
• Email Search:  Search Email records (including reverse search) 
• Virtual Identity Search:  Search for Virtual Identities 
• Social Media Monitor:  Searches must include the ability to query social networking sites, blogs, 
chat rooms, RSS feeds, and avatars.  The social networking sites must, at a minimum, include 
Facebook, Twitter, YouTube, Google + and Instagram. The results of these searches shall contain 
available names, e-mail addresses, user names, photos, hashtags and telephone numbers. 
• Power search:  Search using people, business, and proper ties using Boolean logic. 
• Business search:  Search for businesses based on combinations of company name, individual 
names, TIN, FEIN, address, city, state, zip, or telephone. 
• Corporate Filings Search:  Search for corporate filings based on combinations of company name, 
officer names, address, city, state, zip.  This information shall also include any fictitious business 
names/doing business as (“dba”) listings. 
• UCC Filings Search:  Search by company name or address to find UCC (commercial lien) filings. 
• Automated Valuation Models:  Provides a composite report of residential property information, 
including three valuation models, to provide the best estimate of the current market value of 
the property interest. 
• Internet Domains Search:  Search by company name, contact name, address or domain name to 
find internet domain registrations. 
• FAA Aircraft Search:  Search for aircraft registrations based on combinations of names, address, 
or aircraft number.  

• Motor Vehicle Search:  Search for motor vehicle registrations based on combinations of first 
name, middle name, last name, VIN, driver’s license number, license plate, company name, SSN, 
address, city, state, county, zip. 
• Real-Time Motor Vehicle Registrations Search:  Search for current and historical motor vehicle 
registrations. 
• Property Search:  Search by name, company, address, or parcel number for property tax 
assessment and/or property deed records. 
• Watercraft Search:  Search commercial and personal craft by name, company, address, hull ID, 
or vessel name. 
• Driver’s License Search:  Search driver’s license registrations based on combinations of first 
name, middle name, last name, driver’s license number, SSN, date of birth, address, city, state, 
zip. 
• Driver’s License Wildcard:  Search the DL Wildcard search window allows you to query 
combinations of Driver’s License data. Wildcard Search accesses DL data to run matches on 
partial license numbers. 
• Professional Licenses:  Search by name, social security number, address, or professional license 
number to find individuals that have or have had a professional license. 
• Utility Records:  Search for utility records (electricity, water, cable, telephone) for businesses 
and individuals. 
• FAA Certifications Search:  Search by name or address to find individuals that have or have had 
pilot, mechanic, trainer, or other FAA certifications. 
• Hunting and Fishing Licenses:  Search by name, address, or SSN to find individuals that have or 
have had hunting or fishing licenses. 
• Federal Firearms & Explosives:  Search by name, address, or license number to find individuals 
or businesses that have or have had ATF firearms and explosives licenses. 
• Concealed Weapon Permit:  Search by name or address to find individuals that have or have had 
a permit to carry a concealed weapon. 
• DEA Controlled Substances Search:  Search by name, address, or SSN to find individuals or 
businesses that have or have had DEA controlled substances licenses. 
• Voter Registration Search:  Search for Voter Registration records 
• Phones Plus:  Search for phone numbers not found in traditional Directory Assistance searches. 

• Directory Assistance:  Search listed phone numbers based on combinations of first name, middle 
initial, last name, phone number, address, city, state, zip. 
• Civil Court Records:  Search by name or address to find civil court records. 
• Bankruptcy & Liens and Judgments Search:  Search for individuals or businesses that have filed 
for bankruptcy and/or tax liens or judgments. 
• Official Records Search:  Search by name and location for miscellaneous official court filings and 
other documents. 
• Marriages & Divorces:  Search marriage and divorce records by name and location. 
• Sexual Offenders Search:  Search by name, social security number or address to find records in 
an integrated database of public sexual offenders. 
• Advanced Sexual Offender Search:  Search by name, social security number, date of birth, 
address, or radius, including unregistered, historical, and associated addresses in addition to 
registered addresses. 
• Global Watch List Search:  Search government lists provided by several organizations, including 
the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC), the United Nations Named Terrorist lists and the US 
Bureau of Industry and Security Denied Entity and Person list.  
•  Criminal Records Search:  Search Criminal records based on combinations of first name, middle 
name, last name, SSN, DOC#, address, city, state, and county.  Criminal records searches must 
include any incarceration records and photo images of criminal suspects. 
• Foreclosures Search:  Search foreclosure records by name, company, or address. 
• National Motor Vehicle Accidents:  Search accident reports by name, company, address, 
accident number, license number, VIN, or tag number. 
• Wildcard Search:  Provides “wildcard” searching of motor vehicle data to generate matches on 
partial license plate tags or VINs, as well as car makes, models, colors.  
• Relationship Analysis:  Graphically presents relationships between individuals, addresses, 
vehicles, and corporations.  
• Custom Comprehensive Reports:  Creates a combined, customized, comprehensive report 
compiled from all datasets for either a company or a person. 
• Comprehensive Reports:  Creates a comprehensive report compiled from all datasets for either 
a company or a person.  

• Business Reports:  Creates a combined, customized, comprehensive report for a company, 
including address, contact information, phone, and TIN. 
• Alerts and Notifications:  Establish automatic alerts and receive notifications.   
• Web-based User Guide 
• Dynamic Chain:  Searching Select individual or groups of records from the results of one search 
and use them as input records for another query. 
• Query History:  When enabled, records all queries run along with their results. Allows user to 
organize queries, full or partial results, and other files into cases. 
• Query List:  Lists queries run in current session and provides the capability to rerun them.  
• Results and Reports:  Print and/or save results and report. 
• Unified searching capability.  The unified searching would allow OCI to search the Contractor's 
database as well as other affiliated third-party databases which include credit bureaus and 
telephone service providers.  
• All query results must be provided to the end user within five (5) minutes.   
• All reports must be in Microsoft Excel, Rich Text, or Adobe Acrobat format.   
• The Contractor shall provide a means of searching its web-portal resource via a CPU, laptop and 
Blackberry device.  Any information requested and generated via the Blackberry device shall be 
retained for a minimum of a week by the Contractor and available to OCI end users for later 
viewing.   
• The Contractor shall provide a toll-free helpdesk support phone number or e-mail.  Helpdesk 
support must be available to end users at a minimum of 360 days of the year. The web-portal 
resource shall be made available to end users at any location with an internet connection.  
4. Deliverables 
 
Schedule of Deliverables 
Deliverables Timeframe (after contract award) 
Deliver twenty (20) West Publishing Clear OR 
EQUAL licenses with the capacity to increase up to 
twenty West Publishing Clear Licenses OR EQUAL 
over five (5) years. 
Deliver Twenty (20) concurrent licenses:  10 
days after award 
 
Optional  Line Item:  Deliver up to an additional 
20 concurrent licenses a year within over the 

five-year potential period of the contract 
Helpdesk Support As required 
 
5.  Technical Environment Constraints 
The web-portal database shall be accessible via the internet and accessible to the ender user through 
Microsoft Explorer, Google Chrome and Mozilla Firefox browsers. 
6. Section 508 
 
If any of the work performed in this SOW impact the accessibility of the product as defined under 
Section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act (29 U.S.C. '794 d), the FDA will require an updated Voluntary 
Product Accessibility Template (VPAT) or HHS Section 508 Evaluation Template Product Accessibility 
Template (PAT) for TeamPage (see http://www.hhs.gov/od/vendors/index.html
). 
 
Pursuant to Section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 (29 U.S.C. 794d) as amended by Public Law 
105–220 under Title IV (Rehabilitation Act Amendments of 1998), all Electronic and Information 
Technology (EIT) developed, procured, maintained, and/or used under this contract shall be in 
compliance with the ‘‘Electronic and Information Technology Accessibility Standards’’ set forth by the 
Architectural and Transportation Barriers Compliance Board (also referred to as the ‘‘Access Board’’) in 
36 CFR part 1194. The complete text of Section 508 Final Standards can be accessed at 
http://www.access-board.gov/sec508/standards.htm. 
 
The standards applicable to this requirement are: 
 
Subpart B, 1194.21 Software applications and operating systems 
(a) When software is designed to run on a system that has a keyboard, product functions shall be 
executable from a keyboard where the function itself or the result of performing a function can be 
discerned textually.  
(b) Applications shall not disrupt or disable activated features of other products that are identified as 
accessibility features, where those features are developed and documented according to industry 
standards. Applications also shall not disrupt or disable activated features of any operating system that 
are identified as accessibility features where the application programming interface for those 
accessibility features has been documented by the manufacturer of the operating system and is 
available to the product developer.  

(c) A well-defined on-screen indication of the current focus shall be provided that moves among 
interactive interface elements as the input focus changes. The focus shall be programmatically exposed 
so that assistive technology can track focus and focus changes.  
(d) Sufficient information about a user interface element including the identity, operation and state of 
the element shall be available to assistive technology. When an image represents a program element, 
the information conveyed by the image must also be available in text.  
(e) When bitmap images are used to identify controls, status indicators, or other programmatic 
elements, the meaning assigned to those images shall be consistent throughout an application's 
performance.  
(f) Textual information shall be provided through operating system functions for displaying text. The 
minimum information that shall be made available is text content, text input caret location, and text 
attributes.  
(g) Applications shall not override user selected contrast and color selections and other individual 
display attributes.  
(h) When animation is displayed, the information shall be displayable in at least one non-animated 
presentation mode at the option of the user.  
(i) Color coding shall not be used as the only means of conveying information, indicating an action, 
prompting a response, or distinguishing a visual element.  
(j) When a product permits a user to adjust color and contrast settings, a variety of color selections 
capable of producing a range of contrast levels shall be provided.

Performance Work StatementMission Planning Support Tools72ndTES Whiteman AFB8 May 20261.0 MissionThe Mission Planning Support Tool (MPST) is utilized by the 72dTest & Evaluation Squadron (TES) at Whiteman Air Force Base (WAFB). The required effort includes in-person and remote maintenance and support of the MPST system.1.1 ScopeNo tasks described within this Performance Work Statement shall be construed as inherently governmental. To ensure compliance with federal regulations regarding contractor support, the following limitations apply:System & Data Validation: While the Contractor shall perform testing and provide performance data, the Government retains the absolute authority to officially verify, validate, and accept all mission planning databases, algorithms, and software.Capability Representation: The Contractor shall propose technical models, but the Government is solely responsible for determining and certifying that those models accurately represent aircraft capabilities.Assessment Metrics: The Contractor may draft and recommend metrics or assessment products; however, the Government retains the exclusive authority to approve the final criteria used to evaluate systems and mission effectiveness.The Contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, tools, materials, vehicles, supervision and other items and services necessary to perform MPST maintenance and support services as defined in this PWS both at Whiteman AFB and remotely.1.1.1 The contractor shall provide MPST database and software maintenance to ensurecompatibility with upgrades to the B-2 Mission Planning System (MPS) software, hardware and databases or to USAF/DoW standardized Information System (IS) workstation configurations. The contractor shall also provide MPST database and softwaremaintenance to accurately represent new and/or improved aircraft capabilities, and to correct errors and address limitations encountered during operational use. Activities shall include, but are not limited to:Installing and verifying MPST software releasesDeveloping and maintaining 72 TES custom databases and softwareVerifying MPST databases and algorithms

CUI
CUI
Providing demonstrations and training on MPST capabilitiesParticipation in meetings and working groups that impact mission planning processes or databases used in the MPST1.1.2 The contractor shall support the operational use of MPST modeling and simulation capabilities to address 72 TES requirements. These activities include, but are not limited toConducting modeling and simulation studiesReviewing or generating mission planning system inputsDeveloping metrics and products for assessmentsGenerating briefings and reports for MPST evaluationsPerforming pre-test predictions and post-test analysis with the MPST Participating in open-air flight test activitiesValidating MPST databases and algorithmsAttending meetings related to B-2 testing, mission planning and survivabilityDelivering Monthly Status Reports detailing activities and any problem areas1.1.3 The Contractor shall provide MPST distribution support on-site and at Temporary Duty (TDY) locations as needed. The software produced under this contract is Government-owned, and the Government retains all distribution rights. All distribution, support, and travel must be approved and coordinated with the Contracting Officer's Representative (COR).1.1.4 The contractor shall provide software upgrades to meet 72 TES requirements, includingintegrating new features available in the modeling and simulation engine, Suppressor orAdvanced Framework for Simulation, Integration, and Modeling (AFSIM).1.1.5 The contractor shall maintain the MPST software baseline, associated documents, and training materials.1.1.6 The Contractor shall provide support for MPST installation, configuration, and training. This involves installing MPST software, configuring existing databases for use in the MPST, and providing user training to enable other organizations at Whiteman AFB to use MPST as an interface to Suppressor or AFSIM. Support will be needed in both on-site and off-site locations.1.1.7 The Contractor shall provide dedicated information system administration support as part of this contract. This requirement is necessary because newly developed software requires extensive operating system compatibility and interoperability checks before delivery. The Contractor will perform these functions to ensure all software arrives fully functional for Government use. This role must be part of the contract to enable troubleshooting of 

CUI
CUI
operating system and compatibility issues on the Contractor's side, preventing such problems from affecting Government systems. The Contractor will also provide support for the Modeling & Simulation Flight and its facility. Responsibilities include maintaining computer systems in accordance with approved security procedures through activities such as:Maintaining user accounts and monitoring network and user access.Performing computer system audits, security updates, and digital file transfers.Upgrading or replacing system components.Reporting security-related incidents to the Information System Security Officer (ISSO).Installing approved software, security patches, and deploying operating system upgrades.Performing installation and verification testing for MPST upgrades.2.0 Non Personal ServicesThe Government shall not supervise contractor employees or control their method of performance. The contractor is responsible for managing its employees and guarding against any actions that could be perceived as personal services. The contractor must immediately notify the Contracting Officer (CO) if it believes any such actions are occurring.2.1 Business RelationsThe contractor shall employ qualified personnel with the appropriate combination of education, training, and experience to accomplish all work.2.1.1Identification of Contractor Employees: All contractor must identify themselves as such in meetings, when answering Government telephones, and in other situations where their status is not obvious. The Contractor shall ensure all documents or reports they produce are marked as Contractor products or that their participation is appropriately disclosed. An employee's "Contractor" status shall be predominantly displayed in all correspondence, including email signature blocks. 2.1.2Contractor Required Identification: Contractor personnel shall wear identifying badges at all times. Although no specific dress code is required, they are expected to maintain a professional appearance, which extends to their personal workspace in government facilities.3.0 RequirementsAll Contractor personnel shall possess the computer programming skills required to fully support MPST software maintenance. Personnel must have a minimum of two years of operational experience working as or directly with aircrew. They must be trained as 

CUI
CUI
necessary on the latest and upcoming version of MPST. Personnel shall also be familiar with B-2 aircraft capabilities, survivability, ground and airborne threat systems, and intelligence products for B-2 mission planning. They must be able to successfully leverage the modeling and simulation capabilities of the MPST to meet 72 TES requirements and provide a timely response (within one business day) to all support requests. 4.0 Security and SafetyThe Contractor shall wear appropriate security and line badges as required by the security procedures of the squadron where work is performed. Contractor personnel shall use company-owned or privately-owned vehicles for transportation on the installation and must meet unescorted installation requirements per AFI 31-101. Requests for installation identification must be submitted to the 509th Security Forces Squadron (SFS) at least 72 hours prior to requiring entry. Personnel not meeting the minimum standards will be denied access. The Contractor will provide employee information for an entry authorization list, in accordance with Whiteman AFB Security Forces instructions and any applicable REAL ID Act requirements. Information may include full name, Social Security Number, date of 4.0.1 On-site Contractor personnel must have a current, adjudicated background investigation and be eligible for access to Top Secret, SCI, and SAP information as required. The Contractor must also have the required facility clearance issued by the Defense Security Service. Security requirements are specified in the DD Form 254. The 72 TES Program Security Manager (PSM) will locally manage program access and clearances for Contractor personnel.5.0 Period of PerformanceOn-site Contractor support is expected to be performed during regular working hours (07301600) on weekdays, excluding Federal holidays and Whiteman AFB down days. Any on-site support required outside of regular hours will be coordinated with the COR. The primary on-site work location will be Building 706, 72nd TES. The Government will provide office supplies, appropriate workspace, and access to unclassified and classified computer networks and databases as required.5.0.1 Travel to Whiteman AFB (for off-site personnel) or other facilities may be requiredand. will be coordinated with the COR.5.0.2Travel to TDY locations requires pre-approval from the COR. Trip reports must besubmitted within 5 business days after completion of travel.6.0 Operational Security (OPSEC)Purpose:This section provides OPSEC guidance to contractors and subcontractors to ensure the protection of critical information (CI).

CUI
CUI
Definition: OPSEC is a systematic process used to identify CI, analyze threats and vulnerabilities, assess risks, and implement countermeasures to protect information related to friendly intentions, capabilities, and activities. Unauthorized disclosure of CI could lead to mission failure. OPSEC supplements, but does not replace, traditional security disciplines.Applicability:The 509th Operations Support Squadron (OSS) OPSEC Program Manager has determined that this contract requires additional safeguards. The Contractor shall adhere to the following minimum requirements:The introduction of personal electronic devices into government spaces is strictly controlled and may be forbidden in certain areas.Photography and recording are prohibited without an official permit.Contractor personnel shall not discuss government operations in public or over unencrypted communications.The Contractor shall not post to any media (websites, publications, etc.) any images or information that reveal sensitive government operations, personnel, equipment, or classified/controlled unclassified information. All company press releases related to this contract must be coordinated through the 509th Contracting Office.Government-issued identification shall be concealed when off-station and must not be left in unprotected areas. Lost or stolen identification must be immediately reported to the 509th Security Forces at (660) 687-3700.The Contractor shall implement countermeasures provided by the 509th OSS to protect CI. It is strongly recommended that the Contractor mark and protect internal production schedules, deliverables, and inventories as sensitive information (e.g., "Business Sensitive").All critical and sensitive unclassified information shall be destroyed (e.g., shredded) when no longer needed to prevent inadvertent disclosure.CI identified by the 509th OSS will be marked and handled as Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI). This includes, but is not limited to, system vulnerabilities and details of military operations, movements, and missions

Questions and Answers - 0001 
  
Date: July 2, 2026 
 
The following questions have been submitted for RFI 36C10B26Q0492, VAEC 
Brokerage Service. See below Question and Answer table for further details. All 
questions submitted from June 2, 2026, through June 10, 2026, have been captured in 
this document.   
 
Overall Feedback: This Request for Information (RFI) represents the initial step in 
identifying potential ideas to a key challenge facing VA Infrastructure Operations. 
Specifically, this effort seeks industry input on how to expand the range of Cloud 
Service Provider (CSP) offerings available to stakeholders while maintaining a 
centralized credit purchasing model.  
 
The objective is to enable scalable access to CSP environments while promoting 
efficiency, simplicity, and transparency in both consumption and cost for all users. 
Vendors are expected to adhere to FinOps Open Cost and Usage Specification 
(FOCUS) standards to ensure consistent, transparent reporting of cloud costs and 
usage. Additionally, proposed approaches should demonstrate how the scale of VA 
demand can be leveraged to achieve more efficient cloud pricing and overall cost 
optimization without introducing unnecessary overhead or additional costs. 
 
This solution must operate in alignment with other VA enterprise service contracts, 
including those supporting Infrastructure Engineering and Application Hosting. 
Respondents should describe how their approach will enable close, transparent 
collaboration with these service providers to ensure coordinated delivery, shared 
visibility into usage and costs, and seamless integration across the VA cloud 
ecosystem. Responses to this RFI will help inform future acquisition strategies and 
solution approaches.

1.0  BACKGROUND 
The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Office of Information and Technology (OIT), 
Infrastructure Operations (IO) Enterprise Service Management (ESM) requires the 
acquisition of cloud-based Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) solution delivered via a 
multi-instance Platform-as-a-Service (PaaS) and Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) 
subscription model. 
 
This requirement supports the VA mission to enhance IT service delivery, strengthen 
operational efficiency, and advance digital transformation across the enterprise. The 
required solution must provide enterprise-wide integration and functionality consistent 
with leading ERP in the marketplace 
 
VA OIT currently leverages a SaaS platform to manage critical enterprise operational 
practices, including enterprise service desk operations, incident and event triage, 
request fulfillment, change enablement, and problem resolution. Additionally, the 
platform supports application provisioning, clinician support, and telehealth availability. 
The SaaS platform is central to maintaining uptime for essential systems, including 
Veterans Health Information Systems and Technology Architecture (VistA) and the new 
Oralce/Cerner Electronic Health Record Management (EHRM) platform. 
 
As demand increases for real-time support, automation, cybersecurity compliance, and 
adaptability to evolving legislative and policy requirements, VA requires acquisition of a 
next-generation ERP solution with capabilities that meet or exceed industry standards 
for federal environments. This solution must span across IT Service Management 
(ITSM), IT Asset Management (ITAM), IT Operations Management (ITOM), IT Business 
Management (ITBM), Human Resource Service Delivery (HRSD), and other service 
domains.

Aspose SW for OEDIS and Patent Center  
 
1. Background 
 
The United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) utilizes commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) 
software to support automated document generation, document conversion, and image 
processing across multiple mission-critical enterprise applications: 
• Patent Center: The Patent Center Automated Information System (AIS) is a modern, 
scalable application supporting the patent processing business under the eCommerce 
Modernization effort. Patent Center utilizes Aspose.Imaging for .NET and Aspose.Words 
for .NET to perform document processing and convert non-Scalable Vector Graphics 
(SVG) to SVG formatted images (including JPEG, TIFF, PNG, EMF, and WMF) for 
downstream system consumption. 
• OEDIS: The Office of Enrollment and Discipline Information System (OEDIS) requires 
platform-independent, Java-based software libraries (Aspose.Words for Java) to replace 
legacy mailing systems. This software allows OEDIS to generate, edit, and convert HTML, 
CSS, and Word documents into PDF formats programmatically. 
 
2. Purpose and Scope 
  
The purpose of this procurement is to acquire software maintenance and enterprise support for 
existing perpetual Aspose COTS software licenses used by Patent Center and OEDIS. The scope 
includes the renewal of maintenance and support for Aspose.Words for Java, Aspose.Words for 
.NET, Aspose Imaging for .NET, and Aspose Enterprise Support. 
 
3. Requirements 
 
The Contractor shall provide software maintenance and enterprise support for the following 
existing perpetual Aspose software licenses. The requirements are divided into a Base Period for 
OEDIS and an Option Period for Patent Center.

The Contractor shall ensure that all software maintenance and enterprise support services are 
active, uninterrupted, and accessible to the USPTO for the duration of the respective periods of 
performance. This includes access to all software updates, patches, version upgrades, and 
technical support provided by the publisher. 
 
4. Period of Performance 
The anticipated Period of Performance consists of a 14-month Base Period (for OEDIS) and a 
concurrent 12 -month Option Period (for Patent Center): 
• Base Period (OEDIS): 08/07/2026 through 11/07/2027  
• Option Period 1 (Patent Center): 11/08/2026 through 11/07/2027  
 
5. Delivery and Acceptance 
All maintenance renewal confirmations, updated license files/keys (if applicable for version 
updates), and support access instructions shall be delivered electronically to the designated 
USPTO Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR) or Technical Point of Contact (TPOC). The 
Government will accept performance upon successful electronic delivery and verification of 
active maintenance and support status with the software publisher. 
 
6. Supply Chain Risk Management 
 
The Department of Commerce (DOC) utilizes a Supply Chain Risk Management (SCRM) Program 
to identify, assess, and monitor supply chain risks of critical vendors. The Contractor agrees that 
the Government may, at its own discretion, perform audits of supply chain risk processes or 
events consistent with other terms in the contract regarding access to records and audits. If 
supply chain risks are identified and corrective action becomes necessary, mutually agreeable 
corrective actions will be sought based upon specific identified risks. Failure to resolve any 
identified risk may result in contract termination.

The United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) has a requirement for Aspose software and enterprise 
support to include Aspose.Words for Java OEM Developer license, Aspose.Imaging for.Net, Aspose Enterprise 
Support, and Aspose.Words for.Net utilizing North American Industry Classification (NAICS) code 541519 for 
the anticipated base year period of performance of August 7, 2026 – November 7, 2027.  The USPTO intends to 
procure this requirement using its authority under the Patent and Trademark Office Efficiency Act (PTOEA), 35 
U.S.C. § 2(b)(4)(A), and Patent and Trademark Office Acquisition Guidelines (PTAG), 78 Fed. Reg. 61185 (Oct. 
3, 2013). 
The USPTO intends to award a purchase order for renew Aspose.Words for Java OEM Developer license, 
Aspose.Imaging for.Net, Aspose Enterprise Support, and Aspose.Words for.Net to TechAnax, a Service-
Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business (SDVOSB), in accordance with the Patent and Trademark Office 
Efficiency Act, 35 U.S.C. § 2(b)(4)(A). Any other vendor that is part of the SDVOSB program may contact the 
Contracting Officer to express interest in competing for the requirement within the synopsis period. When 
contacting the Contracting Officer, vendors must submit a capability statement that does not exceed two pages in 
length that shows their ability to perform the requirement and that they are an authorized reseller of the required 
Aspose software and enterprise support as stated in the draft Statement of Work. 
This synopsis is not a request for competitive proposals.

1.0 INTRODUCTION
1.0.1 The Naval Surface Warfare Center Philadelphia Division (NSWCPD) is a Department of Defense entity responsible for research

and unmanned vehicles. This requirement is for NSWCPD Code    533, responsible for voyage data recorder system which is

inherent, or implied
1.0.3  Government/Contractor Relationship
1.0.3.1  The services to be delivered under this Contract/Task Order are non-personal services and the parties recognize and agree that 
no employer-employee relationship exists or will exist under the Contract/Task Order between the Government and the Contractor's 
personnel.  Therefore, it is in the best interest of the Government to provide both parties a full understanding of their respective 
obligations.

Contractor personnel and displaying distinguishable badges or other visible identification for meetings with Government personnel. In 
addition, Contractor personnel shall appropriately identify themselves as Contractor employees in telephone conversations and in 
formal and informal written correspondence.
1.0.3.3   Contractor personnel under this Contract/Task Order shall not engage in any of the inherently Governmental functions listed 
at FAR Subpart 7.5 or DFARS Subpart 207.5. 
1.0.4  Employee Relationship:
1.0.4.1  The services to be performed under this Contract/Task Order do not require the Contractor or its personnel to exercise personal 
judgment and discretion on behalf of the Government.  Rather the Contractor's personnel will act and exercise personal judgment and 
discretion on behalf of the Contractor. 
1.0.4.2  Rules, regulations, directives, and requirements that are issued by the U. S. Navy and NSWCPD under its responsibility for 
good order, administration, and security are applicable to all personnel who enter a Government installation or who travel on 
Government transportation.  This is not to be construed or interpreted to establish any degree of Government control that is 
inconsistent with a non-personal services contract.
1.0.4.3  Inapplicability of Employee Benefits: This Contract/Task Order does not create an employer-employee 
relationship.  Accordingly, entitlements and benefits applicable to such relationships do not apply.  
1.0.4.4  It is the Contractor's, as well as the Government's, responsibility to monitor Contract/Task Order activities and notify the 
Contracting Officer if the Contractor believes that the intent of this Section has been or may be violated. 
1.0.4.4.1  The Contractor shall notify the Contracting Officer in writing via letter or email within three (3) calendar days from the date 
of any incident that the Contractor considers to constitute a violation of this Section.  The notice should include the date, nature, and 
circumstances of the conduct; the name, function, and activity of each Government employee or Contractor official or employee 
involved or knowledgeable about such conduct; identify any documents or substance of any oral communication involved in the 
conduct; and the Contractor's estimated date when, absent a response, cost, schedule or performance will be impacted.
1.0.4.4.2  The Contracting Officer will, within five (5) calendar days after receipt of notice, respond to the notice in writing.  In 
responding, the Contracting Officer will either:
(i)        Confirm the conduct is in violation and when necessary direct the mode of further performance,
(ii)       Countermand any communication regarded as a violation,
(iii)      Deny that the conduct constitutes a violation and when necessary direct the mode of further performance, or

establish the date by which it should be furnished by the Contractor. 
 1.1    BACKGROUND 
This material is to support data extraction of voyage data recorder (VDR) data on all DDG 51 class ships. These laptops will be used 
by Ship's Force to monitor, extract, and view data recorded by the VDR aboard the DDG51-class fleet in support of post-mishap 
incident reconstructions. This procurement is in support of the Navy's requirement to outfit all surface fleets with a Voyage Data 
Recorder (VDR). A laptop has been included as part of the VDR delivery in order to provide Ship's Force the immediate ability to 
reconstruct a shipboard incident/mishap, as well as to provide a training tool for post-event debriefs. This Getac brand and model 
laptop, with its specific configuration, is already currently in use as part of multiple VDR installs.

Annex A – Summary of Requirements 
Project No. 2022/0IS03005, CP9A3201 
 
1. Project Objective 
The project aims to establish a state-of-the-art cyber threat analysis platform. The Contractor 
shall build an updated and effective solution to receive existing commercial and specific 
internal feeds, perform the analysis and processing, and integrate to other existing cyber 
security systems to allow timely, accurate and effective use of the intelligence.  
 
2. Scope of Work 
The project encompasses the design, implementation, and licensing of a commercially off-
the-shelf (‘COTS’) platform for the processing and ingestion of CTI data/information 
originating from different sources already existing in NATO. The work includes:  
1. Refinement of Solution Requirements and design; 
2. Any implementation activity (installation, configuration, ...) on required network 
segments with different classifications including NATO UNCLASSIFIED, NATO 
RESTRICTED and NATO SECRET;  
3. Integration to existing systems for input / output flows and hosting infrastructure;  
 
4. Documentation of the implemented solution (e.g. system manuals, administration 
manuals, user manuals, CIS descriptions, Service Level Agreements, etc.); 
  
5. Support to testing and validation of the solution (i.e. FAT, SAT, and UAT) prior to final 
deployment;  
 
6. Support to transitioning the implementation from the contractor to operations; and  
 
7. Training on the new CTI capabilities, their operation and usage, and enhancements 
that these may bring in terms of doctrine (i.e. processes) and interoperability (i.e. 
ingestion/consumption of CTI data from other sources).  
 
The expected outcome of this project is to have improved CTI handling and sharing capability 
by introducing automation, improved control and better visibility. This will be achieved through 
a state-of-the-art CTI capability that is integrated across NATO systems and entities. 
This capability will be procured with BOA+ on a Firm Fixed Price Basis to the Lowest Priced 
Technically Compliant Bidder.

SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE

Project Title: Maritime Operations Support

Notice Type: Sources Sought

NAICS Code: 541614
PSC Code: R408

1. PURPOSE

This is a Sources Sought Notice issued solely for market research and planning purposes. This is not a solicitation for proposals or quotations. No contract will be awarded from this announcement. The information provided in response to this notice will be used to determine the availability and capability of qualified sources.

2. DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT

Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) has a requirement to create an operational maritime operations group to design, develop, and implement a dedicated maritime operational group. The contractor will be expected to analyze processes, automated business workflows, and visualizations. The contractor will be responsible for standing up the Maritime group, ensuring it is operational, and sustaining its ongoing operations. This maritime group will serve as a critical resource for drafting operational documents, facilitating interagency collaboration, and supporting joint initiatives aimed at enhancing maritime security and disrupting illicit networks. It will address a wide range of threats in the maritime domain and quickly adapt to new national security challenges.

NOTE: The attached PWS document is a draft and subject to change in any resultant solicitation.

3. SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS

Interested parties are requested to submit a capability statement that demonstrates relevant experience, past performance and capacity to meet the scale and complexity of the proposed requirement to provide the services identified in the attached Performance Work Statement with the following information:

Company name, address, and point of contact (phone and email)

UEI number and CAGE code

Business size and type (e.g., Small Business, 8(a), HUBZone, SDVOSB, WOSB, etc.)

Relevant experience and past performance

Capability to perform the required services

Any applicable certifications or qualifications

4. RESPONSES

Responses are due by July 9, 2026, 3:00pm CST. Please submit your response via email to the following emails:

Contract Specialist: Cory Chandler, Cory.Chandler@ice.dhs.gov 
Contracting Officer: Christopher Jackson, Christopher.L.Jackson@ice.dhs.gov

Responses should not exceed 3-5 pages in length.

5. DISCLAIMER

This Sources Sought Notice is for informational purposes only and does not obligate the Government to award a contract. The Government will not pay for any information submitted in response to this notice.

Performance Work Statement (PWS)

Maritime Operations Support

Department of Homeland Security (DHS)

Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE)

Homeland Security Investigations (HSI)

May 26, 2026

INTRODUCTION

Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) is the principal investigative arm of Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and the second largest investigative agency in the Federal government. HSI’s primary mission is to promote homeland security and public safety through the criminal and civil enforcement of Federal laws governing border control, customs, trade, and immigration. HSI has a complex and broad public safety mission to enforce, collect, analyze and share timely, accurate and actionable information on criminal suspects, Transnational Criminal Organizations (TCOs) and Foreign Terrorist Organizations (FTOs) with HSI field offices and its domestic and foreign partners. This effort is being led by HSI and FBI’s newly formed Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF), National Coordination Center (NCC), created specifically in response to President Trump’s Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. 

BACKGROUND

The HSTF NCC serves as the primary coordination entity for the United States Government to ensure law enforcement, Department of Defense, and intelligence efforts are deconflicted and aligned to reduce duplicative efforts, increase officer safety, and enhance United States Government collaboration for all established and future task forces, fusion cells/centers, and/or other coordination efforts with a focus on countering cartels, designated foreign terrorist organizations, and transnational organized crime impacting the United States. The HSTF NCC’s mission is to prevent, protect against, and respond to threats to the homeland presented by TCOs and FTOs involved in criminal activities.

DHS Joint Task Force – Maritime (JTF-M),   CBP, ICE/HSI, USCG task force, unifies action to secure the United States border and maritime approaches by integrating DHS agency resources and authorities. This approach allows JTF-M to address a wide range of threats in the maritime domain and quickly adapt to new national security challenges. JTF-M’s primary focus area includes support to the newly established HSTFs, specifically focusing on maritime threats posed by FTOs. JTF-M coordinates and employs the full range of capabilities, capacity, and authorities of DHS components in the maritime domain through the modernized Maritime Operations Coordination Plan (MOC-P). The MOC-P’s framework directly supports and is integral to the HSTF NCC and all regional HSTF Central Operations and Regional Enforcement (CORE)s.

Furthermore, HSI and DHS Science and Technology (S&T) are engaged in a Cooperative Research and Development Agreement (CRADA) focused on transforming how ICE/HSI utilizes commercial vendor data to support HSTF’s investigations. The CRADA is focused on improving the analysis of HSI’s post-seizure data, resulting in intelligence that leads to increased visibility and understanding of the networks used to produce and distribute fentanyl and other dangerous drugs.

The HSTF NCC has formalized its organizational structure and established operational groups. The next priority is to develop and sustain a Maritime Operations Group dedicated to addressing maritime threats associated with Transnational Criminal Organizations (TCOs) and Foreign Terrorist Organizations (FTOs). It is mission critical that HSI utilizes a Subject Matter Expert (SME) with strong experience working with JTF-M and the MOC-P, to ensure the completion and incorporation of the investigative processes developed by the CRADA into the HSTF NCC Maritime operational group.

SCOPE

The contractor shall design, development and implement a Maritime Operations Group and shall lead the planning, creation, and maintenance of a Maritime operation group within the HSTF NCC.

To achieve this, the contractor shall demonstrate the capability to conduct any of the activities or a combination of the following:

Provide a cleared SME that possesses an in-depth understanding of the HSTF NCC, regional HSTFs, JTF-M, the MOC-P, and joint initiatives such as the CRADA focused on transforming how HSI utilizes commercial vendor data to support investigations related to the disruption and dismantling of FTOs.

Draft all necessary Maritime operational group documents essential to HSTF NCC and the regional HSTFs.

Ensure SMEs collaborate with DHS components, federal partners, and regional HSTFs.

Deliver weekly threat briefs.

Develop target packages and network analysis.

Document after-action reports.

The Contractor shall document operational tasks in Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs).

Identify correlating data points and transform them into actionable insights.

Maintain effective working relationships, both within and outside of ICE, including members of the intelligence and law enforcement communities and other government agencies or government contractors.

Protect all data consistent with DHS/NIST standards and HSI policy.

Ensure SMEs and staff maintain required security clearances.

Surge Only: provide cleared Intelligence Analysts for targeting, investigative case support, and operational surge.

OBJECTIVE

The objective of this contract is for the contractor to design, develop, and implement a dedicated maritime operational group in support of HSTF NCC and regional HSTFs.  The contractor will be expected to analyze processes, automated business workflows, and visualizations. The contractor will be responsible for standing up the Maritime group, ensuring it is operational, and sustaining its ongoing operations. This Maritime group will serve as a critical resource for drafting operational documents, facilitating interagency collaboration, and supporting joint initiatives aimed at enhancing maritime security and disrupting illicit networks. 

This would allow HSI HSTF NCC to create an operational Maritime operations group that will be established at the HSTF NCC and provide support to all regional HSTFs. It will address a wide range of maritime threats and further combat the criminal activities of FTOs and TCOs. The contract will incorporate CRADA, which will imp the analysis of HSI’s post-seizure data, resulting in intelligence that leads to increased visibility and understanding of the networks used to produce and distribute fentanyl and other dangerous drugs.

SPECIFIC REQUIREMENTS TASKS

The Subject Matter Expert (SME) shall be considered the lead for this contract and shall be responsible for the ultimate performance of the tasks specified in the performance work statement.  Additionally, all tasks will be completed in compliance with HSI policies and procedures.

5.1  TASK 1 – REVIEW EVALUATION OF PROCESSES

Review all current procedures and processes within HSTF NCC, HSI, and JTF-M.

Evaluate processes that are working and those that need to be evolved.

Provide a comprehensive evaluation summary to HSTF NCC leadership.

5.2  TASK 2 – CREATION OF A MARITIME GROUP

Establish a dedicated Maritime Group to enhance operational effectiveness in maritime domain awareness, response and case support. 

Establish processes and procedures to address tasks intake and assignments, standardize information sources, implement protocols for data validation and quality assurance,

Establish analytic frameworks for maritime risk assessment, thread identification, and situational awareness.

Develop case tracking procedures and ensure secure storage and access controls for sensitive information.

5.3  TASK 3 – PROGRAM MANAGEMENT

 Establish seamless collaboration and information sharing across all federal agencies with maritime responsibilities to enhance operational effectiveness and support national security

.Coordination with primary federal agencies involved in maritime operations. Coordination may also involve state and local law enforcement, port authorities, and international partners.

.Lead or support projects and teams as required.

5.4  TASK 4 – DOCUMENTATION OF PROCESSES

Develop Standard Operating Procedures (SOP)s to document the creation of a HSTF NCC Maritime group.

Document all process flows that are developed.

5.5  TASK 5 – TRAINING SUPPORT

Provide maritime training support to HSTF NCC for multi-agency, multi-disciplinary maritime operations. 

Joint operational planning and coordination

Incident command system training

Maritime tactics and procedures

Interagency communications and interoperability

5.6  TASK 6 – PROGRESS REPORTS

Monthly and quarterly progress reports will be submitted by Contractor that will include the comprehensive details from the prior and ongoing month of work performed to include type and response time related to technical support request.

5.7  TASK 7 – FIELD SUPPORT

As directed, Subject Matter Expert (SME) will provide technical support to ongoing HSTF maritime investigations and operations.

5.8  TASK 8 – JOINT OPERATIONS WITH HSTF PARTNERS

Consolidation  to assist HSI in joint initiatives with Customs and Border Protection (CBP), Unites States Coast Guard (USCG), and  other HSTF partner agencies.

5.9  TASK 9 – OPTIONAL SURGE CLAUSE

In the event of a documented need identified by HSTF NCC leadership for an operational surge, the Contractor shall provide five (5) additional Intelligence Analysts to assist. The Intelligence Analysts  will ensure that surge work is completed in accordance with the PWS and documented in reporting requirements. (See 6.0 Contractor Personnel for details).

CONTRACTOR PERSONNEL

The total number of required contractor employees is one (1) subject matter expert with a surge capacity of five (5). The Contractor shall propose the staffing plan/labor mix to perform the tasks described above. No later than 15 days into transition/performance, the contractor will be required to provide resumes to be submitted as part of contract administration. During contract administration, these personnel will require Government approval prior to replacement: the Contractor shall submit a written notice of intent to replace the Key Personnel along with the resume of the proposed replacement(s) to the CO a minimum of ten (10) business days prior to the proposed date of change. All proposed replacement(s) shall possess qualifications equal to or superior the requirements for the position.

6.1  Continuity of Support

The Contractor shall ensure that the contractually required level of support is maintained at all times. The Contractor shall ensure that all contract staffing levels are maintained for all hours of the workday. If for any reason the Contractor staffing levels are not maintained due to vacation, leave, appointments, etc., and replacement personnel will not be provided, the Contractor shall provide e-mail notification to the Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR) and related investigative unit program lead POC prior to employee’s extended absence. Otherwise, the Contractor shall provide a fully qualified replacement.

6.2  Key Personnel

Before replacing any individual(s) designated as Key Personnel by the Government, the Contractor shall notify the Contracting Officer no less than ten (10) days in advance, submit written justification for replacement, and provide the name and qualifications of any proposed substitute(s). The Contractor shall not replace the Key Personnel without approval from the Contracting Officer. The following Contractor personnel are designated as Key Personnel for this requirement.  Note: The Government may designate additional Contractor personnel as Key Personnel during contract administration.

The Key Personnel under this contract is minimally required to meet the following requirements:

6.2.1 (1) One Senior Subject Matter Expert

The SME will be responsible for the  contract activities: planning, organizing, directing, controlling, staffing as well as reporting status, deliverables and schedules to the Government.

United States Citizen

Master’s degree in International Security, Criminal Justice, Data Science, or related field.

20 years of experience in maritime intelligence, transnational crime investigations, or federal law enforcement operations.

Page 1 of 16 
Joint Clothing and Textile Modernization Initiative (JCTMI) 
Other Transaction (OT) Opportunity 
Call for Solutions (CFS) 
W91CRB-26-S-JCTM 
In Cooperation with Army Open Solicitation (W9128Z-25-S-A002) 
SECTION 1 - Overview 
1.1 Background and Introduction 
Joint Clothing Textile Modernization Initiative (JCTMI) is a United States (US) Army Product Manager 
(PdM) Soldier Clothing and Individual Equipment (SCIE) effort to fundamentally modernize the 
acquisition of Clothing and Textile (C&T) items through the adoption of Apparel Tech Packs (ATPs) and 
an apparel Commercial off the Shelf (COTS) Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) software system. 
This initiative aligns with Department of War (DoW) executive directives and Secretary of War 
(SECWAR) priorities to modernize acquisition processes, strengthen the defense industrial base, reduce 
barriers to entry for industry partners, and build supply chain resiliency to meet operational readiness and 
force modernization goals.  
The Army Contracting Command – Aberdeen Proving Ground (ACC-APG), on behalf of PdM SCIE, 
intends to competitively award agreements for a JCTMI prototyping project as detailed below. PdM SCIE 
seeks innovative software solutions, with a preference for commercial or commercially based modified 
software solutions, that can be rapidly prototyped and offer significant improvements over current 
capabilities.  
The Government anticipates using Other Transaction (OT) Authority, leading to one (1) or more JCTMI 
Prototype OT Agreement(s) (OTAs) under the authority of 10 U.S.C. § 4022, however, the Government 
reserves the right, at its sole discretion, to award solution(s) through one or more authorities specified in 
the Army Open Solicitation (AOS). The Government’s intent is to award agreement(s) to prime 
contractor(s) who provide full prototype solutions either individually or through creative teaming or 
subcontracting arrangements. The Government encourages competent providers (and any subcontractors) 
to be on multiple teams if necessary to achieve the vision and best solutions. Agreement awards will be 
dependent on available funding and criteria established in this CFS.  
The Government’s expectation is that initial prototype software capabilities will be delivered rapidly after 
award of any resulting OT agreement(s) as identified in the draft Statement of Work (SOW). The 
Government reserves the right to cancel this opportunity or make no awards in conjunction with this 
opportunity.   
To be considered for an OTA award, interested vendors must comply with at least one of the following 
conditions of 10 US Code §4022(d):  
(A) At least one (1) Non-Traditional Defense Contractor (NTDC), as defined in section 3014 of Title 
10 US Code §3014, is participating to a significant extent in this prototype project.  
(B) All significant participants in the transaction other than the Federal Government are small 
business or NTDCs.  
(C) At least one third of the total cost of the prototype project is to be paid out of funds provided by 
parties to the transaction other than the Federal Government.  

Page 2 of 16 
1.2 Prototype Project – Problem Statement 
The anticipated scope of the JCTMI project entails the procurement of a commercial PLM software 
system as detailed in the draft SOW, and includes but is not limited to the following objective 
specifications: 
• Apparel-Focused PLM Software 
• FedRAMP Certified Cloud-Hosted Environment 
• Capability Maturity Model Integration (CMMI) Level 2 Certified 
• Authorization to Operate (ATO) Impact Level (IL) 4 with privacy overlay compliance 
• Low-Code/No-Code Platform with a search-based design 
• Integration capabilities with systems including but not limited to Adobe Illustrator, Browzwear or 
Clo. 
• Mult-tenant user licenses 
The procurement will include commercial-based multi-tenant user licenses, plug-ins, cloud hosting, 
maintenance, and support for a minimum of 12 months and a maximum of 60 months, in alignment with 
SOW objective timelines. This will allow for the configuration, testing, finalization of system 
requirements, and determination of the feasibility of integrating the PLM system with C&T industry 
partners. 
1.3 Call for Solutions (CFS) Procedures 
This CFS is a competitive procedure seeking innovative prototype solutions that can address the stated 
prototype requirements contained in the draft SOW and the associated supporting documents included 
within this opportunity. Subject to the availability of funds, this CFS will result in the award of OT(s) for 
prototype project(s) in accordance with 10 U.S.C. § 4022, however, the Government reserves the right, at 
its sole discretion, to award solution(s) through one or more authorities specified in the Army Open 
Solicitation. This CFS, and any OT agreement awarded as a result of this CFS, is not subject to the FAR 
or its supplements.  
This CFS is soliciting in accordance with the below instructions and the associated documents provided 
as attachments. All responses to this announcement will be governed by this CFS. 
2-phase Competitive Process. The Government will employ a 2-phased competitive solicitation process 
to award the OTA(s), as outlined below: 
Phase 1 
Step 1: Request for White Papers (RWP). The Government requests interested vendors to provide 
white papers on their proposed innovative JCTMI solution. White papers will present the vendor’s 
planned approach to address the JCTMI draft SOW objectives, with a primary focus on the vendor’s 
proposed technical solution and schedule compliance. White papers will be limited to twenty-five (25) 
pages. NOTE: Vendor white papers are expected to propose a system level JCTMI solution. White papers 
addressing only subsets or portions of the JCTMI solution may not be considered for awards or invited to 
subsequent Steps under this CFS. Vendors that are interested in providing only portions of the solution 
should seek to privately team or perform as subcontractors with vendors planning to propose as prime 
offerors for the JCTMI solution. 
 

Page 3 of 16 
Phase 2 
Step 2: Solutions Demonstration (Government Option). Vendors whose white papers receive a 
favorable evaluation in accordance with CFS Section 4.1 may be invited to present their Solutions 
Demonstrations virtually through Microsoft Teams. The Government reserves the right to limit the 
number of vendors invited to this step.  
The solutions demonstration may not be required for all solutions to proceed to Step 3 and will be 
requested at the Government’s discretion based on the results of evaluations of the Step 1 White Paper 
submissions.  If requested, the vendor’s solution demonstration will focus on software capabilities 
demonstrations, areas not able to be covered in the white paper submissions, and other details as provided 
below.  
Step 3: Request for Prototype Proposals (RPP) and OTA Awards. Following Government evaluation 
of white papers and solution demonstrations (if requested), favorable vendor(s) who are selected for 
potential award will be requested to submit formal technical and cost proposals and to enter alpha 
negotiations on OTA terms and conditions. The Government reserves the right to limit the number of 
vendors invited to submit a proposal. 
SECTION 2 – DEFINITIONS  
“Call for Solutions” is the terminology used for this action to competitively award prototyping 
agreements under the authority of 10 U.S.C. § 4022.  Please note, any references to “Request for 
Solutions” found elsewhere in the documentation associated with W91CRB-26-S-JCTM shall be 
understood to mean “Call for Solutions.” 
“Nontraditional Defense Contractor” is defined in 10 U.S.C. § 3014 as an entity that is not currently 
performing and has not performed, for at least the one-year period preceding the solicitation of sources by 
the DoW for the procurement or transaction, any contract or subcontract for the DoW that is subject to 
full coverage under the cost accounting standards prescribed pursuant to 41 U.S.C. § 1502 and the 
regulations implementing such section. This includes all small business concerns under the criteria and 
size standards in 13 C.F.R. § 121. 
“Prototype Project” can generally be described as a proof of concept, model, reverse engineering to 
address obsolescence, pilot, novel application of commercial technologies for defense purposes, agile 
development activity, creation, design, development, demonstration of technical or operational utility, or 
combinations of the foregoing. A process, including a business process, may be the subject of a prototype 
project. Although assistance terms are generally not appropriate in OTA, ancillary work efforts that are 
necessary for completion of the prototype project, such as test site training or limited logistics support, 
may be included in prototype projects. A prototype may be physical, virtual, or conceptual in nature. The 
quantity should generally be limited to that needed to prove technical or manufacturing feasibility or 
evaluate military utility. 
“Nonprofit Institution” means a nonprofit institution, as defined in 15 U.S.C. § 3703 as an organization 
owned and operated exclusively for scientific or educational purposes, no part of the net earnings of 
which inures to the benefit of any private shareholder or individual. 
“Small Business” is defined under Section 3 of the Small Business Act (15 U.S.C. 632) 
 “Innovative” means any new technology, process, method, or business practice; or any new application 
of an existing technology, process, method, or business practice that contributes to enhancing the mission 

Page 4 of 16 
effectiveness of personnel of the Department of Defense/Department of War or improving platforms, 
systems, components, or materials proposed to be acquired or developed by the Department of 
Defense/Department of War, or to improvement of platforms, systems, components, or materials in use by 
the armed forces. 
SECTION 3 – INSTRUCTIONS FOR WHITE PAPERS, SOLUTIONS DEMONSTRATIONS 
AND REQUEST FOR PROTOTYPE PROPOSALS (RPP) 
3.1 General Guidelines 
a.  Unnecessarily elaborate brochures or proposals are not desired. 
b.  Use of a diagram(s) or figure(s) to depict the essence of the proposed solution is strongly encouraged. 
c.  (If applicable) Technical data with military application may require appropriate approval, 
authorization, or license for lawful exportation. 
d.  All White Papers, Solutions Demonstrations and Prototype Proposals are strongly encouraged to be 
UNCLASSIFIED. White Papers, Solutions Demonstrations and Prototype Proposals containing data that 
is not to be disclosed to the public for any purpose or used by the Government except for evaluation 
purposes shall include the following on the cover page (or slide, handout, etc. for Solutions 
Demonstrations and Oral Presentations): 
"This [select one: White Paper, Solutions Demonstration or Prototype Proposal] includes data that shall 
not be disclosed outside the Government, except to non-Government personnel for evaluation purposes, 
and shall not be duplicated, used, or disclosed -- in whole or in part -- for any purpose other than to 
evaluate this submission. If, however, an agreement is awarded to this Company as a result of --or in 
connection with - the submission of this data, the Government will attain certain data rights, subject to 
the negotiated terms contained in the resulting agreement. This restriction does not limit the 
Government's right to use the information contained in this data if it is obtained from another source 
without restriction. The data subject to this restriction are contained in sheets [insert numbers or other 
identification of sheets]"  
Each restricted data sheet should be marked as follows:  
"Use or disclosure of data contained on this sheet is subject to the restriction on the title page of  
this proposal. " 
 
e.  Submissions must be submitted electronically via the instructions included herein. 
 
f.  Submissions sent through other channels or after the CFS period (identified on SAM.gov) has ended 
will not be reviewed nor evaluated. 
 
3.2 STEP 1 - White Paper Instructions  
The Government may be unable to evaluate the white paper if a vendor fails to provide the information 
requested below. 
White Papers are limited to twenty-five (25) pages, not including the Cover sheet, Executive Summary, 
and required Annexes. White paper submissions that exceed the page limits in the Request for White 
Papers (RWP) will not be evaluated beyond the stated limitations. If vendors can adequately address the 

Page 5 of 16 
RWP and all requested Step 1 contents in less than 25 pages, vendors are encouraged to do so. Vendors 
shall organize their white papers as described in the attached RWP.  
 
If applicable (see CFS Section 10.6), vendors shall include their OCI Identification and Mitigation plan as 
an additional Annex with their white paper submission.  If submitted, the OCI Identification and 
Mitigation Plan is limited to five (5) pages. 
 
Vendors shall not include any other items (e.g., brochures, data sheets, etc.) with their white paper 
submission.  White paper submissions may be in one combined PDF or separate files for each section 
identified in the RWP, so long as the files are able to be transmitted via email to the Government Points 
of Contact identified below. 
Aside from diagrams and similar exhibits which may require larger page-format files and variable font 
sizes, vendors shall generally format their white papers in accordance with the following:

Special Notice: Intent to Sole Source 
Global Economic Modeling 
July 1, 2026 
Contracting Office: Treasury Common Services Center (TCSC), 200 3rd St Parkersburg, WV 26101 
SS-OIA-26-041  
 
  
The Treasury Common Services Center (TCSC), on behalf of Office of Intelligence and Analysis (OIA)), 
intends to contract with Oxford Economics USA, Inc., New York, on a sole source basis. Oxford 
Economics USA, Inc. has developed a global forecasting and simulation model that uniquely meets 
OIA’s needs. This information is proprietary in nature and is not available from other sources.  
 
OIA has a demonstrated need for a global interdependent macroeconomic model to support its 
analyses of an array of economic/global financial/energy/international trade topics – and indeed is 
required to strengthen its econometrics capabilities in FY26, based on the inclusion of OIA’s 
econometrics initiative in both its FY26 legislative authorization and appropriation. To enhance OIA’s 
ability to quantify how policies, trends, and events affect the economic interests of the United States, as 
well as those of our partners and adversaries, our primary need is for the customizable analysis of 
national and regional economies and international capital flows that Oxford’s Global Economic Industry 
Model provides. 
 
OIA economists anticipate using Oxford’s model to inform our global and regional economic analysis, 
including by addressing key data gaps; anticipating the direct impacts of policies, trends, and events; 
forecasting and evaluating indirect or collateral effects on global markets; and validating or challenging 
claims observed in other information channels. OIA’s analysis goes to policymakers at the highest 
levels of the US government.  
 
Over the past two decades, Oxford Economics has developed a global forecasting and simulation 
model that uniquely meets OIA’s needs. Only a handful of firms offer similar services, and none are 
able to provide the coverage (85 core countries and a model extension that creates proxy models for 
108 additional countries), depth (models that incorporate over 70,000 equations), and data fidelity (at 
least monthly updates by a team of over 550 economists) that Oxford offers. 
  
The period of performance for the purchase order/contract is anticipated to be one 12-month base 
period and one 12-month option period. 
 
NO SOLICITATION IS AVAILABLE.  A request for more information, or a copy of the solicitation, will 
not be considered an affirmative response to this Special Notice. Telephone responses or inquiries to 
this Special Notice will not be accepted.  
 
All responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation, which shall be 
considered by the agency. Treasury Common Services Center will consider responses received no 
later than 07/10/2026. Responses shall be submitted electronically to starla.kalb@treasury.gov, SS-
OIA-26-041 /Attn: Starla Kalb. Responses must include sufficient evidence that clearly shows your 
company is capable of providing the requirement described in this notice. Responses received will be 
evaluated; however, a determination by the Government not to compete the proposed procurement 
based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. If no written 
response is received by the aforementioned deadline that clearly demonstrates an ability to meet all 
requirements, and that is more advantageous to the Government, Treasury Common Services Center 
will make award on a sole source basis to Oxford Economics USA, Inc. 
 
NAICS: 518210 
Product Service Code: 7A21

Qualified Contractors must provide the following:  
 
1. The name and location of your company, contact information, and identify your business size 
(Small Business, Small Disadvantaged Business, 8(a), Service Disabled Veteran Owned Small 
Business, HUBZone, Women Owned Small Business, Other than Small Business etc.).  Please 
ensure contact information includes the name of the point of contact, email address, and 
telephone number, should the Government have questions regarding individual responses. 
 
2. UEI Number. 
 
3. Specific details of the product(s) that your company offers in regard to this notice. 
 
4. Whether your content is available through a Government contract vehicle or Open Market. 
 
5. A brief capabilities statement (not to exceed 5 pages) that includes a description of your

currently provides the specific required content.  
 
The following file extensions are not allowable and application materials/data submitted with these

.bat, .cab, .cmd, .com, .cpl, .dot, .dotx, .exe, .hqx, .hta, .mim, .mp3, .mp4, .pif, .rar, .scr, .vbs, .uu, .uue, 
.vbs, .wsf, xxe,.wmv, html, mhtml, and .zip files 
 
The allowable Microsoft Office and Adobe PDF file types as follows: 
 
Microsoft Office (.doc, .docx, .xls, .xlsx, .ppt, .pptx) and Adobe PDF (.pdf) are acceptable. 
 
No other information regarding this Special Notice will be provided at this time.
