PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT (PWS)

Shore Forces GIS Support Services

1.0 GENERAL

1.1 BACKGROUND

The Office of Shore Forces (CG-741) utilizes an Enterprise Geospatial Platform (EGP) that leverages ESRI’s ArcGISEnterprise geospatial capabilities to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of Shore Forces operations. The EGP serves as a centralized geospatial solution for managing and analyzing data, providing real-time spatial context to aid decision-making across sea, land, and business operational domains. It provides out-of-the-box application builders (e.g., Looking Glass, Dashboards, StoryMaps, Survey123, and Experience Builder) to assist Shore Forces users in creating actionable information products. 

1.2 SCOPE

The purpose of this Task Order is to provide front-end geospatial web development, user training, and backend data advisory support for the Office of Shore Forces (CG-741). This support is dedicated to the Shore Forces Enterprise, encompassing Command Centers, SECTORs, Marine Safety Units, and Response/Prevention capabilities. 

2.0 SPECIFIC TASKS

2.1 TASK ONE: FRONT-END GEOSPATIAL PROJECT SUPPORT

The Contractor shall manage the lifecycle of web-based GIS applications for CG-741.

Requirements Gathering: Interface directly with Shore Forces stakeholders to elicit, define, and document user interface (UI) and user experience (UX) requirements for custom web maps, dashboards, and spatial portals.

Agile Project Support: Manage the agile development pipeline for web GIS products, ensuring iterative delivery tailored to Shore Forces operational requirements.

Quality Assurance (QA): Conduct rigorous usability testing and quality control on all front-end deliverables to ensure optimal performance, accessibility compliance, and visual clarity of shore-based data.

2.2 TASK TWO: WEB GIS DEVELOPMENT & FRONT-END EXPERIENCES

The Contractor shall serve as the primary developer for front-end geospatial applications within the Shore Forces Enterprise.

Dashboard & Application Creation: Design, build, and deploy interactive web applications utilizing Esri Experience Builder, Web AppBuilder, or custom JavaScript/Arcade.

StoryMaps & Briefing Tools: Develop dynamic geospatial briefing products, including StoryMaps, for CG-741 and SECTOR leadership.

Front-End Customization: Write, test, and deploy front-end scripts (Arcade, HTML/CSS, JavaScript) to customize map widgets, pop-ups, and data symbology.

2.3 TASK THREE: BACKEND DATA ADVISORY & SUPPORT

Note: The Contractor is not responsible for enterprise database administration. The Contractor shall act as a technical advisor to ensure backend systems deliver data optimized for CG-741 web consumption.

Backend Data Informing: Advise Government data engineers regarding the geospatial formats (e.g., REST endpoints, GeoJSON, feature services) required to power high-performing web applications.

Schema Recommendations: Provide documented recommendations on attribute table structures and indexing strategies designed to minimize front-end latency for Command Center users.

Integration Advisement: Provide technical guidance on optimal methods for exposing operational sensor feeds and incident data via web services.

2.4 TASK FOUR: END-USER TRAINING & CAPACITY BUILDING

The Contractor shall ensure Shore Forces personnel are proficient in utilizing deployed front-end web experiences.

Curriculum Development: Develop and maintain tailored training materials, including Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), quick-reference guides, and video tutorials for CG-741 GIS tools.

Training Execution: Conduct training sessions (over-the-shoulder, virtual, or classroom) for Command Center watchstanders and SECTOR staff.

Feedback Integration: Establish a feedback loop during training sessions to capture user feedback and inform future UI/UX improvements.

2.5 TASK FIVE: DATA SECURITY & WEB PUBLISHING COMPLIANCE (IL5)

The Contractor shall strictly adhere to DoD/DHS IL5 and CG-741 operational security constraints.

CUI Web Publishing: Ensure that all web applications displaying Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI)—such as law enforcement or port security data—enforce proper access controls and display mandatory IL5/CUI security banners.

PII/PHI Prohibition: The Contractor shall actively ensure that no front-end applications display, process, or search for Personally Identifiable Information (PII) or Protected Health Information (PHI). Operations must remain strictly focused on mission, asset, facility, and environmental data.

3.0 PROJECT COMPONENTS & INITIATIVES

3.1 COMPONENT ONE: GIS USER REQUIREMENT ANALYSIS & TRAINING ENHANCEMENTS

The Contractor shall conduct on-site assessments and execute training exercises at selected Shore Forces Command Centers. The Contractor shall document workflows, facilitate discussions to identify high-frequency GIS tasks, and provide actionable recommendations to improve Personnel Qualification Standards (PQS) documentation.

3.2 COMPONENT TWO: ACTIVE PROJECT INITIATIVES & PORTFOLIO SUPPORT

The Contractor shall provide direct development and advisory support for the following CG-741 initiatives in accordance with the schedule established in the Project Management Plan (PMP):

4.0 KEY PERSONNEL

4.1	The Contractor shall provide two key personnel consisting of one (1) GIS Project Manager and one (1) GIS Specialist. All personnel shall be United States citizens or aliens lawfully admitted for permanent residence and possess the necessary technical proficiencies to execute the mission requirements of the Office of Shore Forces (CG-741).

GIS Project Manager: JR PM and GIS 

GIS Specialist: CG EXP 

4.2 Travel CLIN 

Travel may be required to support CG-741 site visits, training exercises, and strategic engagements as identified in Section 5.0. All travel under this Task Order will be executed and funded via a Cost-Reimbursable, Not-To-Exceed (NTE) Contract Line Item Number (CLIN). 

Pre-Approval Requirement: All travel must be explicitly requested by the Contractor and approved in writing by the Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR) a minimum of ten (10) business days prior to the commencement of travel. 

Regulatory Compliance: Reimbursement for travel-related expenses (e.g., airfare, lodging, per diem) shall be strictly in accordance with the current Joint Travel Regulations (JTR). 

Cost Restrictions: The Contractor shall not apply profit, fee, or unallowable markups to travel costs. Receipts must be provided for all expenses exceeding the threshold established in the JTR.

4.3 Option CLIN to Surge Additional ADHOC Support  

The Government anticipates the potential need for surge support to address unforeseen operational requirements, disaster response contingencies, or rapidly emerging GIS technology integrations that fall within the general scope of this PWS but exceed baseline capacity. 

Scope of Surge Operations: Ad Hoc support may include, but is not limited to, accelerated dashboard development for emergency incidents, unprogrammed system integrations, or additional training seminars not accounted for in the baseline Agile Sprint schedule. 

Authorization Protocol: Surge support will be funded via a dedicated optional CLIN. The Contractor shall not commence any surge work without a formal written Task Order modification executed by the Contracting Officer (KO). 

Limitation of Authority: The COR may technically define the surge requirements, but is not authorized to direct surge support, authorize the initiation of ad hoc work, or commit Government funds.

5.0 PERIOD AND PLACE OF PERFORMANCE

Period of Performance: The Task Order consists of a 12-month Base Period and two (2) 12-month Option Periods.

Place of Performance: The primary place of performance is the Contractor’s facility (remote work authorized). Anticipate occasional travel to support CG-741 site visits, training, and strategic engagements. The contractor will be required to attend meetings at USCG Headquarters occasionally. 

Location of USCG Headquarters: 2703 Martin Luther King Jr. Avenue SE, Washington, D.C., 20593

6.0 SECURITY & GOVERNMENT FURNISHED EQUIPMENT

Security: Contractor access to classified information is not required. The Contractor will handle CUI and must execute a Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA). Employees requiring logical/physical access must obtain a Common Access Card (CAC) via a favorably adjudicated Tier 1 background investigation.

Government Furnished Equipment (GFE): The Government shall provide one (1) Government-issued laptop equipped with a functioning CAC reader per Contractor employee within ten (10) business days of award.

7.0 DELIVERABLES AND PERFORMANCE METRICS

7.1 DELIVERABLES SCHEDULE

7.2 PERFORMANCE REQUIREMENTS SUMMARY (PRS)

Objective: The purpose of this plan is to provide a quality surveillance plan for the subject contract. This plan provides a basis for the Contracting Officer's Representative (COR) to evaluate the quality of the Contractor's performance. The oversight provided for in this plan shall ensure performance levels meet or exceed the quality standards stated below. This plan will provide the COR with a proactive way to avoid unacceptable or deficient performance and corrective actions that can improve performance. This plan will provide the contractor with a roadmap for performance stands that will meet or exceed contract requirements. This plan will provide verifiable input for annual past performance evaluations for Contractor Performance Assessment Reporting System (CPARS). 

Performance Standards:

Management Responsiveness: The COR shall determine whether the Contractor has managed the contract effectively and efficiently with regards to the performance stated herein.  

Ratings: 

Exceeds Expectations: Exceeds performance standards of the contract to the benefit of the Government. 

Meets Expectations: Meets performance standards of the contract to the benefit of the Government. 

Deficient: Performance standards are below expectations to the detriment of the Government. 

 

Evaluation Methods:

The COR shall conduct performance evaluations based on the required performance levels as set forth in the contract.

Frequency: The COR shall evaluate the current levels of performance according to the standards set forth in this contract. During performance of this contract, the COR shall perform periodic inspections on an as needed basis or at the request of end-users. 

Inspections: The COR shall conduct inspections to ensure that the deliverables are provided on time and per the performance standards stipulated herein.

7.3 GOVERNMENT FURNISHED EQUIPMENT (GFE)

The Government will provide the following equipment to the Contractor to ensure all work is performed within the secure USCG environment. No contractor-owned hardware or software is authorized for this mission.

 

7.3.1 CONTRACTOR RESPONSIBILITY FOR GFE:

Custodianship: The Contractor shall maintain a GFE Inventory Log and report any loss or damage to the COR within 24 hours.

Maintenance: The Contractor shall utilize USCG IT support channels (e.g., CSD/SNOW) for hardware/software issues.

Return: All GFE shall be returned to the Government in working order within three (3) business days of contract completion or personnel off-boarding.

7.3.2  GOVERNMENT FURNISHED INFORMATION (GFI)

The Government will provide access to the following information and datasets to enable the Contractor to develop front-end configurations and workforce strategies.

Introduction

This Request for Information (RFI) is for planning purposes only and shall not be considered an Invitation for Bid, Request for Task Execution Plan, Request for Quotation or a Request for Proposal.  Additionally, there is no obligation on the part of the Government to acquire any products or services described in this RFI.  Your response to this RFI will be treated only as information for the Government to consider.  You will not be entitled to payment for direct or indirect costs that you incur in responding to this RFI.  This request does not constitute a solicitation for proposals or the authority to enter into negotiations to award a contract.  No funds have been authorized, appropriated or received for this effort. The Memorial Benefits and Services (MBS) Products provide technology solutions to support National Cemetery Administration (NCA) programs and services. They deliver digitization, modernization, automation, and interoperability solutions to provide Veterans and their families with efficient and timely services and benefits. 

 System Acronym  | System Name  | System Description 

VA-EISS | VA- Enterprise Interment Services System (EISS) | 
VA-EISS supports a broad range of NCA business functions, including but not limited to:
Processing pre-need burial eligibility applications and state cemetery eligibility requests;
Generating pre-need determination correspondence;
Supporting time-of-need burial and memorial benefit processing;
Recording and tracking family preference;
Scheduling green burials and other specialized interment services;
Managing plaque, urn, and memorial benefits requests;
Creating, updating, and maintaining burial and interment records;
Managing subsequent interment requests and remains locations updates;
Creating and maintaining marker templates;
Scheduling, approving, and certifying interment services;
Ordering headstones, markers, and niche covers;
Performing quality assurance activities on decedent records; and
Administering system functions, including user account management, resource configuration, marker order maintenance, email template management, and cemetery settings administration.
The VA-EISS application is developed using Microsoft technologies, including C#, .NET, and the Blazor framework, and integrates with Geographic Information System (GIS) capabilities to support cemetery mapping and operational functions

MBMS | Memorial Benefits and Management System | The first major area of NCA operations to use MBMS is the National Cemetery Scheduling Office (NCSO), the central call center for anyone scheduling a burial, interment, or inurnment at a National Cemetery. The Case Management, Eligibility, and Outreach (CaMEO) module uses the Salesforce COTS platform, which brings case management functionality and automated workflow processes into one integrated system. 
A companion module, Cemetery Regulations, Reports and Testing (CeRRT), allows individual cemeteries to indicate, on a calendar-type form, the hours and capacity for services. This information is displayed to NCSO to enable accurate and consistent scheduling for Veterans and their families. Additionally, MBMS automates all business processes associated with tracking orders and delivery of monuments. It provides a complete historical record for each monument application and automates all manual, paper-intensive record keeping and information and forms processing associated with over 135,000 yearly interments. Finally, using one system, MBMS enables NCA end-users to perform eligibility, benefits, and cemetery management functions.


MEL | Memorial Enterprise Letters | The Memorial Enterprise Letters (MEL) application allows the NCA to build new letter templates to generate letters related to suspending or denying an application for a government headstone, marker, or medallion. The NCA Case Managers use these templates to create letters to the next of kin or cemetery explaining why their application for the government headstone, marker, or medallion has been suspended or denied. The MEL application also supports the print vendor, which prints and mails letters to the recipients. The current MEL custom solution will be replaced with a configurable lightweight correspondence engine, allowing NCA to build new letter templates and automate business rules for template approval. This eliminates NCA's dependency on Information Technology (IT) support for letter template management.

VLM | Veteran Legacy Memorial | The Veterans Legacy Memorial (VLM) is an interactive online memorialization platform designed to honor the service and sacrifice of the nation’s Veterans. The digital memorialization platform enables visitors to honor and pay their respects to Veterans interred at VA national cemeteries by allowing public contributions to Veterans’ pages. VLM’s online portal includes digital pictures of headstones and markers, and burial records that family members, survivors, and friends can view. VLM has incorporated architecture and functionality specializing in Cloud infrastructure, principles and protocols of user experience (UX), and human-centered design. The project is the latest from VA’s IT and Digital Modernization program and aligns with the President’s Management Agenda.
The public can search the site for Veterans, find out which of the National Cemetery they are buried, and read summary details of their lives and service. Future capabilities will allow families, survivors, fellow Veterans, and others to add historical photos, view gravesite photographs, view gravesites on a map, get directions to a gravesite, and share memories on a deceased Veteran’s memorial page. Such capabilities will include provisions that allow NCA to manage the site in a manner that maintains the same level of decorum that customers experience in VA’s National Cemeteries.
As a digital, Cloud-based, and internet-enabled platform, VLM enhances the Veterans Legacy Program concept. It includes more than 4.5 million Veterans currently laid to rest in National Cemeteries. Most importantly, VLM allows the American public to share in NCA’s mission to “honor all Veterans in perpetuity.”

BINCA | Business Intelligence National Cemetery Administration | NCA has implemented a business intelligence system using an enterprise Tableau Server. Tableau is the platform for BINCA to achieve true self-service capabilities for NCA analytics. It creates visualizations to manage and understand data, provides a method to share data among users, and exposes patterns and trends in a secure environment. The NCA Leadership team uses the output of BINCA on their dashboard for decision-making purposes.

BOSS-E | Burial Operations Support System - Enterprise | BOSS-E is a system comprising 10 VA legacy sub-systems that will be part of a future decommissioning effort. The multi-year goal is to transition users from these legacy systems by leveraging MBMS, VA systems, and COTS solutions. VA will migrate the functionality of the following mission-critical IT systems into MBMS and then decommission these systems as part of BOSS-E:
Burial Operations Support System (BOSS)
Automated Monument Application System (AMAS)
Eligibility Office Automation System (EOAS)
Nationwide Gravesite Locator (NGL)
Presidential Memorial Certificate (WebPMC)
Daily Burial Schedule (DBS)
National Gravesite Locator (NGL)
National Cemetery Kiosk (KGL)
Gravesite Assessment Reporting (GAR) Management 
Memorials Administration Decision Support System (MADSS)

BOSS | Burial Operations Support System | BOSS automates all the manual, paper-intensive record keeping and information and forms processing associated with over 150,000 yearly interments from National and State Veterans, Arlington National Cemetery, post/military, Department of Army, and Department of Interior cemeteries. BOSS creates and maintains a complete historical record for each interment and is considered an NCA mission critical system.

AMAS | Automated Monument Application System | AMAS automates all business processes associated with monument ordering, delivering, and tracking. It provides for creating and maintaining a complete historical record for each monument application. AMAS receives, processes, and tracks over 335,000 applications each year for government-furnished monuments (i.e., headstones, markers, niche covers) for graves of Veterans and beneficiaries buried in National, State, Arlington National Cemetery, post/military, Department of Army, Department of Interior, and private cemeteries. AMAS is considered an NCA Mission critical system.

EOAS | Eligibility Office Automation System | EOAS provides case processing functionality, case tracking, productivity reporting, and tracking reports for pre-need request submissions for the Eligibility Office (EO). 

NGL | Nationwide Gravesite Locator | NGL is a system designed to assist the public with locating a gravesite for which a government marker was provided. The NGL receives a data feed from both BOSS and AMAS databases and is kept constantly up to date. NGL is considered an NCA mission critical system.

WebPMC | Presidential Memorial Certificates | A PMC is an engraved paper certificate bearing the signature of the current President. The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) has a clear and critical need to modernize its legacy core Financial Management System (FMS). The FMS is 30 years old and continued reliance on it presents enormous risk to VA operations. The technical and functional ability to support the legacy application becomes more difficult with each passing year. New audit issues have surfaced including security related issues that cannot be fixed in the older software.  In addition to non-compliance with security standards, the FMS is no longer compliant with the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) circulars A-123, Appendix A, Internal Control over Financial Reporting and A-127, Financial Management Systems; and there is no way to bring it into compliance.

Modernize the existing financial system with an easy to manage low cost solution

PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT (PWS)

(Includes associated Performance Requirements Summary (PRS))

Microsoft Sentinel Implementation for the Army University

PART 1
GENERAL INFORMATION

1. General: This is a non-personal service(s) contract under which the personnel rendering the service(s) are not subject, either by the contract’s terms or by the manner of its administration, to the supervision and control usually prevailing in relationships between the Government and its employees.

1.1 Description of Services/Introduction: This is a non-personal service(s) contract to design, implement, and operationalize Microsoft Sentinel as the centralized Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) and Security Orchestration, Automation, and Response (SOAR) platform for Army University (AU). This initiative will strengthen the AU’s defense posture by providing real-time monitoring, advanced threat detection, and automated incident response capabilities across approximately 350 Intune-managed endpoints. Furthermore, this deployment will support compliance alignment with NIST SP 800-53 security control frameworks and deliver a scalable foundation to accommodate future integration needs.

1.2 Background: AU’s current SIEM does not provide seamless integration with MS365 services, particularly exchange devaluing the SIEMs ability to alert technicians of incidents and issues. To optimize the security architecture and reduce operational friction, the Government is pivoting toward utilizing native Microsoft 365 (M365) tools, specifically Microsoft Sentinel. Transitioning to a native M365 solution establishes a more comprehensive and cohesive ecosystem, mitigating the risk of API integration failures frequently associated with maintaining connections between M365 and third-party platforms. Furthermore, this deployment aligns with the Government's long-term strategic objective to consolidate all M365-related services under a single contract vehicle, thereby streamlining and simplifying future procurement processes.

1.3 Scope: The Contractor shall provide non-personal service(s). The Contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and other items necessary to perform services as described in the PWS and associated contract documents, except for those items specified in Part 3 Government Property and Services. The Contractor shall perform to the standards and acceptable quality levels identified in this PWS and associated contract documents.

1.4 Objectives: The objective of this contract is to provide the professional services necessary to establish a fully operational Microsoft Sentinel Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) and Security Orchestration, Automation, and Response (SOAR) platform. This will equip AU with a modern, centralized capability for advanced threat detection, automated incident response, and continuous security monitoring. A key outcome of this effort is to ensure Government personnel receive the necessary training and knowledge transfer to achieve long-term administrative self-sufficiency in operating the platform.

1.5 General Information:

1.5.1 Quality Control Plan (QCP): This acquisition is for commercial services and will be performed using FAR Part 12 procedures. The contractor’s existing quality assurance system shall be utilized In Accordance With (IAW) FAR 12.208.

1.5.2 Quality Assurance: The Government will evaluate the Contractor’s performance under this contract IAW the Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan (QASP). This plan is primarily focused on what the Government must do to ensure that the Contractor has performed IAW the performance standards. It defines how the performance standards will be applied, the frequency of surveillance, and the acceptable quality levels (performance thresholds).

1.5.3 Recognized Holidays: The following provides information on recognized holidays for the purpose of the PWS. If submittal of any tasks or documentation (e.g., deliverables, submittals, etc.) deadlines fall on a holiday, the closest workday prior to the holiday will apply as the deadline for submittal. 

1.5.3.1 U.S. Holidays: Work shall not be performed on U.S. federally recognized holidays occurring during the normal workweek unless otherwise directed by the Contracting Officer. When a U.S. holiday occurs on a Saturday or a Sunday, the holiday is observed on the preceding Friday or following Monday, respectively. 

New Year’s Day	Labor Day

Martin Luther King Jr.’s Birthday	Columbus Day

President’s Day	Veteran’s Day

Memorial Day	Thanksgiving Day

Juneteenth 	Christmas Day

Independence Day

1.5.4 Operating Hours: The Government facility office hours, facility operating hours, and the Contractor support hour requirements often coincide, however, they may differ. Please refer to the following. 

1.5.4 Government Facility Office Hours: The Government facility office hours are 0800 to 1700, Monday through Friday except U.S. Holidays identified in paragraph 1.5.3.1 above or when the Government facility is closed due to local or national emergencies, administrative closings, or similar Government directed facility closings. 

1.5.5 Place of Performance: The work to be performed under this contract will be performed from a location from which the Contractor can perform all aspects of this Contract. No performance is required to be on-site at a Government facility.

1.5.5.1 Telework Capabilities: All work under this contract shall be performed via telework from the Contractor's own facilities or other appropriate remote location.

1.6 Clearance Requirements: Not Applicable. No Security clearance is required for performance under this contract.

1.6.1 Facility Clearance Program: Not Applicable

1.6.2 Personnel Security Clearance Requirements: Not Applicable

1.6.3 Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI): Not Applicable

1.7 Installation Access: Access to U.S. installations, buildings and controlled areas is limited to personnel who meet security criteria and are authorized. Failure to submit required information/data and obtain required documentation or clearances will be grounds for denying access to U.S. installations, buildings, and controlled areas. The Contractor shall ensure that any subcontractors used in performance of this contract complies with these requirements and that all employees, of both the Contractor and any subcontractor utilized by the Contractor, are made aware of and comply with these requirements.

The Contractor shall be aware of and comply with the requirements associated with Installation Access Control. The Government is not liable for any costs associated with performance delays due solely to a firm’s failure to comply with Installation Access Control System (IACS) processing requirements. 

The Contractor shall return installation passes and/or issued identification to the issuing IACS office when the contract is completed or when a Contractor employee no longer requires access. This includes when an individual is terminated or at the expiration of their employment or when the contract ends (whether due to expiration, termination, or cancellation).

1.7.1 Background Checks: Not Applicable

1.7.2 Common Access Cards (CAC): Not Applicable

1.7.2.1 For contractors requiring Common Access Card (CAC): Not Applicable

1.7.2.1.1 The Contractor shall provide the following information: Not Applicable

1.7.2.2 For contractors that do not require CAC but require access to a DoD facility or installation: Not Applicable

1.8 Physical Security: The Contractor shall safeguard all Government equipment, information, and property provided for Contractor use. 

1.8.1 Operations Security (OPSEC) Requirements: Contractor personnel shall adhere to facility security policies and restrictions. The Contractor shall immediately report suspicious activities to security personnel. Government-issued access badges shall not be worn outside designated facilities where visible to the general public. 

1.8.2 Key (Card) Control: Not Applicable 

1.9 Post Award Conference/Periodic Progress Meetings: The Contractor shall attend any post award conference convened by the contracting activity or contract administration office IAW FAR Subpart 42.5. The Contracting Officer, COR, and other Government personnel, as appropriate, may meet periodically with the Contractor to review the Contractor's performance. At these meetings the Contracting Officer will apprise the Contractor of how the Government views the Contractor's performance and the Contractor shall apprise the Government of problems, if any, being experienced. Appropriate action shall be taken to resolve outstanding issues. These meetings shall be at no additional cost to the Government.

1.9.1 The Contractor shall attend, participate in, and furnish input to scheduled and unscheduled meetings, conferences, and briefings that relate to the functions and services herein as required by the Government to provide effective communication and impart necessary information. The Contract Manager or designated representative shall attend meetings as requested by the Government. Meeting attendees shall at times include Contractor managerial, supervisory, and other personnel knowledgeable of the subject matter. Meetings may start or end outside of regular duty hours.

1.10 Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR): Refer to Part 2 of this PWS for the definition of a COR. As determined by the Contracting Officer, a COR will be appointed and identified by letter of designation, a copy of which will be provided to the Contractor by the Contracting Officer. The designation letter states the responsibilities and limitations of the COR, especially with regard to changes in cost or price, estimates, or changes in delivery dates. The COR is not authorized to change any of the terms and conditions of the resulting order. The COR monitors all technical aspects of the contract and assists in contract administration. The COR is not authorized to obligate the Government. If the work is not written in the contract, the COR is not authorized to request new work. The COR is authorized to perform the following functions: assure that the Contractor performs the technical requirements of the contract, perform inspections necessary in connection with contract performance, maintain written and oral communications with the Contractor concerning technical aspects of the contract, issue written interpretations of technical requirements, including Government drawings, designs, specifications, monitor Contractor's performance and notifies both the Contracting Officer and Contractor of any deficiencies, coordinate availability of Government property, and coordinate site entry of Contractor personnel. 

1.11 Key Personnel: The following personnel are considered key personnel by the Government: Contract Manager, Alternate Contract Manager, and Lead Sentinel Architect. The Contractor shall provide a Contract Manager who shall be responsible for the performance of the work. The name of this person and an Alternate Contract Manager, who shall act for the Contractor when the Contract Manager is absent, along with the name of the Lead Sentinel Architect, shall be provided in writing to the Contracting Officer Representative no later than five (5) days after contract award (Deliverable #). The Contract Manager and Alternate Contract Manager shall have full authority to act for the Contractor on all contract matters relating to daily operation of this contract. The Contract Manager, Alternate Contract Manager, and Lead Sentinel Architect shall be available during the operating hours listed in PWS 1.5.4.

1.11.1 Key Personnel Qualifications: Required qualifications are listed in Attachment 1 (Deliverable #A.001).

1.11.2 Additional Key Personnel Requirements: Certain experienced professional and/or technical personnel are essential for successful accomplishment of the work to be performed under this contract. These Key Personnel must be identified by name within the contractor’s offer for their resumes (and any additional documents) to be evaluated during the source selection process. 

1.11.2.1 The contractor agrees that such personnel shall not be removed or replaced within the performance of this contract unless the following measures are taken:

(a) If one or more of the key personnel, for any reason, becomes or is expected to become unavailable for work under this contract for a continuous period exceeding 30 work days, or is expected to devote substantially less effort to the work than indicated in the proposal or initially anticipated, the contractor shall, subject to the concurrence of the KO or COR, promptly replace personnel with personnel who possess equal or better qualifications as the original employee.

(b) All requests for approval of substitutions hereunder must be in writing and provide a detailed explanation of the circumstances necessitating the proposed substitutions. The request must contain a resume for the proposed substitute, and any other information requested by the KO or COR. The KO or COR must concur in writing with the change.

1.11.2.2. If the KO or COR determines that suitable and timely replacement of Key Personnel who have been reassigned, terminated, or have otherwise become unavailable for the contract work is not reasonably forthcoming or that the resultant reduction of productive effort would be so substantial as to impair successful completion of the contract, the KO may terminate the contract for default or for the convenience of the Government, as appropriate, or make an equitable adjustment to the contract to compensate the Government for any resultant delay, loss or damage.

1.12 Identification of Contractor Employees: All Contractor personnel attending meetings, answering Government telephones, and working in other situations where their contractor status is not obvious to third parties must identify themselves, to include proper marking of signature blocks in correspondence, to avoid creating an impression in the minds of members of the public that they are Government officials. The Contractor shall ensure that all documents or reports, produced by Contractors are suitably marked as Contractor products or that Contractor participation is appropriately disclosed. 

1.12.1 Contractor Identification Badges: Not Applicable. All work is conducted remotely.

1.13 Contractor Travel: Not Applicable. All work is conducted remotely.

1.14 Other Direct Costs (ODCs): Not Applicable.

1.15 Data Rights: The Government has unlimited rights to all documents and materials produced under this contract. All documents and materials, to include the source codes of software, produced under this contract shall be Government owned and are the property of the Government with all rights and privileges of ownership and copyright belonging exclusively to the Governmen

Page 1 
 
 
The purpose of this notice is to accomplish market research pursuant to Federal Acquisition 
Regulation (FAR) Part 10, and to identify qualified and experienced HUBZone, WOSB, 
SDVOSB, and small businesses capable of and interested in providing the services described 
herein.  This notice is issued solely for information and planning purposes and does not 
constitute an Invitation for Bid (IFB), Request for Quotation (RFQ), or Request for Proposal 
(RFP). Additionally, there is no obligation or commitment on the part of the Government to 
acquire any products or services described within this notice now or in the future. The 
Government does not intend to award any contract(s) based solely on the submission of this 
notice. Respondents are advised that the Government will not pay for information submitted in 
response to this notice, nor will it compensate respondents for any costs incurred in the 
development/furnishing of a response. The Government will not entertain telephone calls or 
questions for this RFI notice.  Please note that a decision not to submit a response will not 
preclude a vendor from participating in any future solicitation. 
 
The Government is providing a draft Statement of Work (SOW) as a courtesy to inform potential 
offerors of anticipated requirements. The Government will not accept questions on the SOW at 
this time. However, submission of comments and recommendations are optional. 
 
  

Bureau of Intelligence and Research Request for Information 
Boundaries and Sovereignty Encyclopedia (BASE) 19AQMM26N0269 
Page 2 
 
 
BACKGROUND 
 
The Boundaries and Sovereignty Encyclopedia (BASE) is the U.S. Government’s (USG) official 
repository of geography and foreign policy information pertaining to the depiction and 
description of international land boundaries as well as disputed territories and sovereignty issues. 
BASE is maintained by the Department of State’s (DOS) Office of the Geographer and Global 
Issues (GGI) within the Bureau of Intelligence and Research (INR) and hosted on the StateToday 
site. BASE serves as the authoritative source of information on historical and contemporary 
boundary and sovereignty issues for cartographers, analysts, diplomats, and policymakers. GGI 
relies on BASE to fulfill the responsibilities given by OMB Circular A-16 and the Federal 
Geographic Data Committee.  The Encyclopedia is the companion to the Department’s only 
National Geospatial Data Asset, the Large Scale International Boundaries (LSIB) dataset. 
 
 
Purpose: 
 
This Request for Information (RFI) is to identify qualified and experienced vendors capable of 
providing Boundaries and Sovereignty Encyclopedia (BASE) to INR/GGI. The desired outcomes 
for its customers and end-users are to obtain information on the following:  
1) BASE-related corporate experience in a Federal Government environment 
2) Required Functionality  
3) Software Utilization and Geospatial Data 
4) Security, Compliance, and Risk Management 
5) Rough Order of Magnitude estimate 
 
 
RFI Submission Instructions: 
 
RFI responses shall be submitted in writing via email to: Nicolas Wilhelm, Contracting Officer at 
WilhelmNA@state.gov; James Tyson, Contract Specialist at TysonJC@state.gov and Annie Harlow, 
Contract Specialist at HarlowAL@state.gov no later than 12:00 noon, EST on July 22, 2026. 
 
All responses shall be submitted electronically (Adobe PDF format). Responding to this RFI is 
not a prerequisite to bid on a subsequent RFP, if one is issued.  All responses must adhere to the

I. Background 
The Boundaries and Sovereignty Encyclopedia (BASE) is the U.S. Government’s (USG) official 
repository of geography and foreign policy information pertaining to the depiction and description of 
international land boundaries as well as disputed territories and sovereignty issues. BASE is maintained 
by the Department of State’s (DOS) Office of the Geographer and Global Issues (GGI) within the Bureau 
of Intelligence and Research (INR) and hosted on the StateToday site. BASE serves as the authoritative 
source of information on historical and contemporary boundary and sovereignty issues for cartographers, 
analysts, diplomats, and policymakers. GGI relies on BASE to fulfill the responsibilities given by OMB 
Circular A-16 and the Federal Geographic Data Committee.  The Encyclopedia is the companion to the 
Department’s only National Geospatial Data Asset, the Large Scale International Boundaries (LSIB) 
dataset. 
II. Objective 
The function of BASE is to provide access to the most recent geographic policy guidance, background 
information, and historical documentation of policy origins of the USG’s views on the alignment of the 
world’s international land boundaries and the status of geographic sovereignty disputes.  The background 
information includes narrative text describing the specific boundary, a standard set of metadata, historical 
documents describing the policy context, as well as reference materials, including geospatial datasets, 
treaties, maps, news articles, and photographs.  
This document outlines the operation, sustainment and ongoing feature enhancement needed for BASE, 
which resides on the StateToday site, to remain operational and in step with ongoing technological 
advancements.   
III. Required Functionality 
For this project, we are seeking the following services for a base plus four (4) option years as follows: 
BASE must be able to accomplish the following:  
1. Manage and display changes in the boundary alignment/spatial geometry and attributes associated 
with boundary lines and segments through space and time through the proper handling of the 
SpaceTimeID concept. 
2. Manage and display the hierarchical assembly of constituent line segments into international 
boundaries, through implementation of SpaceTimeIDs. 
3. Build and maintain linkages between geographic line segments and the various relevant artifacts. 
4. Provide visualization, search, and access functions for boundary lines, segments, and relevant 
documentation. 
5. Be accessible to anyone with valid USG credentials. The platform should be hosted in such a way that 
it provides stability and complies with security best practices, such as being hosted in the AWS 
GovCloud (US).   
 
IV. Technical Requirements  
1. Infrastructure 
BASE should be built upon a modern infrastructure that complies with all Department of State 
technical and security requirements (e.g., Authority to Operate (ATO), security patches, vulnerability 
monitoring, etc.).

information on site traffic and cost metrics, robust documentation on its operations, and accessible 
management and user guides.

System Advisor Model (SAM) Software Development

1.0 Introduction and Purpose 
 
This is a Sources Sought Notice (SSN) issued by the Alliance for Energy Innovation, LLC 
(Alliance). The purpose of this SSN is to conduct market research and gather information on the 
current capabilities of potential sources to provide support, maintenance, and expansion of the 
System Advisor Model.  
 
The National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) develops and maintains SAM, an open-source 
software platform used by researchers, industry, utilities, and government organizations to 
evaluate the technical and economic performance of renewable energy technologies. SAM 
supports a wide range of energy technologies, including solar, wind, and geothermal systems, 
and provides performance, financial, and incentive modeling capabilities.  
 
This effort includes software architecture improvements, implementation of new modeling 
capabilities, user interface enhancements, cross-platform software support, and troubleshooting 
of issues identified by users and development staff. The work supports annual software releases 
and ongoing modernization of the platform. 
 
The information received will be used for planning purposes and to inform the potential 
development of a future solicitation. 
 
2.0 Scope of Need 
 
The information received in response to this SSN will guide Alliance’s focus for writing a 
requirements document to meet our overall research goals. The project objective, at a high level, 
is to provide detailed architecture and debugging support, software development, maintenance, 
and enhancement support for NLR's System Advisor Model (SAM) platform.:

o Demonstrated high level expertise in C++ software development and architecture 
design, and object-oriented programming methodologies.  
o Demonstrated Experience developing and supporting graphical user interface 
widgets for desktop software applications, preferably experience building upon 
the open-source  wxWidgets package.  
o Demonstrated expertise with detailed engineering models of energy systems and 
financial models for multiple energy markets.  
o Demonstrated experience supporting software development and automated build 
processes across multiple operating systems, including Windows, Linux, and 
macOS.  
o Demonstrated ability to troubleshoot, debug, test, and maintain production 
software applications.  
o Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively with technical subject matter experts 
on a variety of technical subjects and communicate solutions, results, and 
problems clearly.

Statement of Work
Engineering Support for the Washington Interagency VLBI Correlator
 
The Haystack Observatory shall perform the following task:
 
I. Executive Summary
 
The deliverables and/or support of the products or deliverables will cover three general areas:
-       Correlation of special projects
-       Data storage and transfer
-       20m Antenna VGOS Compliance
The work focuses on assistance related to the S/X VLBI (dual-frequency, S/X) VLBI (herewith called "legacy VLBI"), 
thus providing continuity from the past to the present. Since the VLBI technique is in transition from legacy VLBI to the 
VLBI Global Observing System VLBI (VGOS), the contractor shall extend support to also include VGOS product support.
 
II. Statement of Work
 
The interagency VLBI correlator at USNO has been a fundamental infrastructure for space geodesy since it began 
operations in 1986. That (MarkIIIA) hardware correlator was designed and constructed by the contractor, who has been 
providing engineering support to USNO ever since. Support has covered the various hardware correlator updates and 
upgrades, such as to MarkIV, as well as the more recent (in the 2010s) transition from hardware to software correlation 
(SWC), such as to the distributed FX-type correlation (DiFX).
 
The primary purpose of the correlator at USNO is to support rapid turnaround of geodetic VLBI observations to provide 
the most timely and accurate values for time-varying Earth orientation parameters (EOP) such as the UT1-UTC, Length-of-
Day (LOD), polar motion, and celestial pole offsets. These observations are also used to estimate the positions of the 
extragalactic radio sources that define the celestial reference frame (CRF) and the positions (and velocities) of the radio 
telescopes that define the terrestrial reference frame (TRF), being the EOP the parameters that link the two frames together.
 
The contractor will provide assistance and support to USNO for post-correlation programs for both legacy and VGOS data, 
for post-processing requiring special attention, for electronic VLBI capabilities, and in the general area of VLBI data 
storage and transfer.
 
In support of the USNO correlator, the following tasks listed in the Scope of Work shall be performed, as listed in Section 
III.
N0018926QL187
Page 4 of 29

III. Scope of Work
MIT/HO shall perform the following tasks:
 
Task 1: Consultation of special processing
Occasionally, situations may arise where unusually complex geodetic experiments, especially as USNO transitions to 
correlation of VGOS experiments, must be processed, or where difficulties encountered during the VLBI data 
collection experiments may need special treatment during processing. The contractor shall then consult with the 
processing personnel at USNO and advise them, via remote (e.g., telephone, email, audio/video) communication, on 
approaches to overcome the complex or difficult situations, and on diagnosing problems at the VLBI stations.
 
Task 2: Data storage and transfer
The contractor shall be responsible for maintaining a VLBI data depot, temporarily storing and validating data prior to 
submittal to the DiFX correlator servers at USNO via eTransfer (etc/etd). The storage will act as a buffer for eTransfers 
from potentially compromised sources. The contractor shall be responsible for receiving said data and for validating the 
incoming data for proper format and content by scanning for tampering and defects. Once validated, the contractor 
personnel shall make the data available to USNO for eTransfer and correlation. If data is deemed invalid, USNO will 
still be notified of the comprised data and anomalies discovered.
 
Task 3: 20M Antenna VGOS Compliance
The contractor shall be responsible for making all modifications required to make the 20m Antenna Backend VGOS 
compliant up to 14GHz. The contractor will provide USNO "as-built" technician, user documentation and spare 
equipment for any items in the signal processing chain developed for making the 20m Antenna Backend VGOS 
compliant which are not commercial off the shelf. Spare equipment will be maintained at KPGO. If a situation arises 
where specialized equipment must be fabricated in order to perform this work, then the contractor shall provide for the 
fabrication of that equipment and that equipment shall be considered property of USNO and remain on site at KPGO 
for future reuse.
 
Task 4: Program management
The contractor shall manage all MIT-related contractual activities, communicate with USNO, and ensure sufficient 
attention to system engineering, documentation, configuration management, and information technology (IT) security.

GENERAL INFORMATION   1.0 DESCRIPTION OF SERVICES    The objective of this effort is to support the Air Force Research Laboratory (AFRL) in both maintaining and enhancing the Contribution-based Compensation System Software (C2S2). This includes coding system software and providing help desk support to AFRL/DPPP. The contractor shall provide technical support to maintain and improve the system and user experience to effectively utilize the system. Additionally, the contractor shall conduct data analysis and collection to provide a comprehensive evaluation and provide recommendations to optimize the effectiveness and administration of the DoD Science and Technology Reinvention Laboratories (STRLs) and AFRL Laboratory Personnel Demonstration Project System (Lab Demo) for scientists and engineers, business management and professionals, technicians, and mission support personnel.    AFRL plans and executes Department of the Air Force (DAF) programs in the areas of basic research, applied research, and advanced technology development, AFRL plays an integral role in leading the discovery, development, and integration of affordable warfighting technologies for our air, space, and cyberspace force. AFRL/DPP and AFRL/DPPP serve as the corporate C2S2 help desk and superuser for the AFRL Enterprise. C2S2 is a system that provides management and employee support, facilitating the administration of Lab Demo personnel processes. The contractor shall support AFRL/DPPP to ensure the system operates effectively and efficiently to benefit the workforce.     The objective is to acquire services to support AFRL/DPP in administrating Lab Demo. At a minimum, these services include the following: Assist in planning, implementation, design and execution of Lab Demo flexibilities and authorities; data analyses, customer support; C2S2 help desk support; software development, maintenance and enhancement; and the development and maintenance of all C2S2 training materials as well as the computer-based Lab Demo training materials for users. Requirements  In accordance with the requirements set forth in this PWS, the contractor shall satisfy the following:   The contractor shall support and assist in the design of additions and/or modifications to Lab Demo initiatives based on provided requirements and historical knowledge of Lab Demo. These initiatives include but are not limited to employee assessment, compensation, broadbanding, position classification, and other personnel flexibilities.   The contractor shall assist in analyzing topics such as Lab Demo employee assessment and 

 
 
compensation results, workforce impact and trends, cost studies, and initiative effectiveness, and document the analysis in reports and/or briefings. Analysis results may be provided and reviewed by the Air Force and Department of Defense (DoD).  The contractor shall provide meeting, legislative, and policy analysis support for the Office of the Under Secretary of Defense for Research and Engineering (OUSD(R&E)) on Lab Demo at the individual STRL and aggregate DoD Level.   The contractor shall provide meeting, legislative, technical, training, and policy analysis support, software/database design, revisions, testing, training, and user support.   The contractor shall support the re-certifications and accreditation of the AFRL Contribution-based Compensation System Software (C2S2) and cybersecurity compliance requirements in coordination with the hosting organization to maintain Enterprise Business System (EBS) Authority to Operate (ATO).   The contractor shall develop and maintain simulation models that enable leadership to more effectively plan and manage the costs of their Lab Demo workforce. This planning shall be based on anticipated hiring, attrition, promotion, and other salary and payroll dynamics.   The contractor shall develop and assist in implementation of initiatives that assure the ability of the DoD STRLs to effectively recruit, retain, and manage workforces to meet STRL missions and DoD S&T priorities.   The contractor shall analyze and perform comparative analyses of selected other pay plans to Lab Demo pay system focusing on cost comparison and effectiveness.  oThe contractor shall provide an analysis of annual salary compensation costs for employees including salary and awards costs; and an assessment of how the demonstration project impacts mission goals, employee recruitment, retention and satisfaction and other data elements available through the Federal Employee Viewpoint Survey data for the STRLs.   The contractor shall analyze and provide feedback on the outcomes of implementing Lab Demo initiatives, focusing on their effectiveness and success. Additionally, address statutory and congressional issues relevant to AFRL as they arise, providing insights into the potential impacts and benefits of implementation.  All submitted analyses and materials (including briefing charts, reports, spreadsheets, etc.) shall be thorough and understandable. Unless an alternative standard is explicitly mentioned, they shall be 98% accurate with any identified errors to be corrected by the contractor within the specified timeframe outlined in the task description of this PWS.   The contractor shall resolve products and requests for C2S2 identified as high priority by following the priority levels identified in the Service Level Agreement (SLA), section 3.9 and changes will be submitted to the EBS Support Center within 48 hours of notification or 

 
 
identification of required resolution. The C2S2 software is a critical component used to ensure AFRL employees are accurately assessed and compensated; therefore, no critical errors affecting employees and/or pay are allowed. If errors are identified, a write-up will be issued every day the issue remains unresolved. Responses to communications from the Lab Demo team must be provided within a 2-hour timeframe, unless an alternative deadline is explicitly stated in the request.     Provide data analysis and administrative support for the PERC.      The contractor shall analyze the overall effectiveness of Lab Demo for the previous Contribution-based Compensation System (CCS) assessment cycle and document the results of the analyses in briefing charts and reports for all pay pools and provide Enterprise-wide comparison. A format provided by AFRL/DPP shall be utilized for each of these charts and reports. These briefing charts will be used during the Project Evaluation Review Committee (PERC) meeting which takes place at least once, but up to twice per year. These materials will provide context for Lab Demo effectiveness in order to interpret changes or trends over time and provide recommendations to the PERC. Thus, there is a requirement to update the charts with the differences and trends in the data. Following the PERC, all comments and suggestions from the meeting will be compiled by the contractor and used to update the briefing charts and reports, and to prepare the CCS Results Briefing Templates for the Pay Pools as well as the Cycle Results Briefing for AFRL.CA and Pay Pool Managers. The results will also be used by the contractor to create an Assessment & Compensation Cycle Data Analysis report. This report provides an analysis of the current cycle year and comparison of the last five cycles. The analysis includes but is not limited to the evaluation of the assessment, compensation and broadband movement data. (CDRL A001)  1.4.1.2  Subtask 2  Administrative Support The contractor shall provide analytical and administrative support for up to two meetings of the PERC each year. Support shall include preparing and distributing meeting materials (hard copy and/or electronic) such as agendas, meeting minutes, etc. and providing other administrative support for the meeting. DPP will review and specify material requirements prior to finalizing the product.     

 
 
  1.4.3.1 Subtask 1- Lab Demo Cost Discipline AnalysisThe contractor shall conduct a Cost Discipline Analysis and create a report to support the  recommendation for the next cycle and document the analyses and results in a report and briefing charts. The contractor shall utilize Demo workforce and government comparison group data and other appropriate methodologies to conduct analyses focused on cost discipline. (CDRL A003) 1.4.3.2  Subtask 2  OUSD Analytics The contractor shall provide legislative and policy analysis support for OUSD(R&E) on Lab Demo implementation at the individual STRL level and aggregate DoD level.  The contractor shall analyze and summarize in a report, data on matters such as Demo cost, workforce trends, Lab Demo assessments, broadband movements, and other interventions. The contractor shall also provide an analysis in a report of annual salary compensation costs, assessment of the impact of the demonstration project on mission goals, employee recruitment, retention and satisfaction. The report shall consist of workforce characteristics and significant trends from the baseline time to present time, to include tracking changes in the workforce over a period of time and an analysis on cost discipline. The contractor shall analyze and perform comparative analyses of other personnel systems to the Lab Demo system.  The contractor shall analyze personnel system evaluation metrics and frameworks and submit a report on implementation mechanisms. (CDRL A004) 1.4.4 Task 4  Workforce Trend Analysis The contractor shall analyze government-provided workforce data and document trend analysis results in a report in order to assist AFRL management in making informed decisions. The Workforce Trend report shall consist of workforce characteristics and significant trends from the baseline time to present time, tracking changes in the workforce over time. (CDRL A005)  1.4.5 Task 5  Internal Evaluation Summary Report The contractor shall analyze and summarize data on matters such as cost analysis, workforce trends, CCS analysis data, and other flexibilities and authorities in a report. The Government will supply the contractor with all required data on lab demo personnel and flexibilities and authorities to facilitate the completion of their reporting. The contractor shall compare the current results with the data from historical collections efforts. Using these measures, the contractor shall evaluate the overall effectiveness of the flexibilities and authorities in meeting AFRL goals for the Demonstration Project. (CDRL A006)  1.4.6 Task 6  AdHoc Requirements The contractor shall conduct unplanned analyses and respond to unanticipated questions from AFRL/DPP. An initial response shall be provided within 24 hours, and any requested product shall be 

 
 
delivered within two business days unless an alternative timeframe is specified or approved by the AFRL/DPP team member who requested the analysis. The final product should contain no more than 3 errors. The results may be presented in various forms such as charts, tables, spreadsheets, briefing slides, etc. Additionally, the contractor shall assist AFRL/DPP in developing briefings for management and attend those briefings as required.1.4.7 Task 7C2S2 Maintenance and ModificationsC2S2 is developed using oracle APEX pages, report queries and layouts, supplemented by stored procedures programmed with PL/SQL, JavaScript, CSS, HTML and VBA programming within Microsoft Excel spreadsheets. The system adheres to a least-privilege, role-based model of access control ensuring users have appropriate authorization to application modules and data based on their assigned role, organization and supervisory structures. standards for handling Top Secret data. This capability is critical for ensuring compliance with d ata security  
protocols and mitigating the risk of data spillage.  Th e sy stem must provid e a complete, verifiable audit 
trail of the erasure and destruction process for accountability and reporting purposes.

6. Specific characteristics of the supplies or services that limit the availability to this/these 
source(s), i.e., unique features, form-fit-function, etc.). State why the requested material or 
service represents the minimum requirement(s) of the Government. Describe in detail why only 
this/these suggested source(s) can furnish the requirement(s) to the exclusion of other sources.  
 
The CFID is a handheld, portable device designed for forward-operating military and law 
enforcement personnel.  
 It is the only commercially available specialized tool that provides the following unique combination 
of capabilities in a single field-deployable unit: 
 
 Immediate Drone Forensics: Utilizes the integrated SkySafe technology to directly extract, 
process, and preview flight logs, media files, and other metadata from a wide range of 
commercial UAVs, including newer encrypted models.
 Real-time Triage: Allows operators to view extracted flight paths and other critical data instantly 
on a connected Android device, enabling rapid threat assessment and intelligence gathering at the 
point of capture.  
 Multi-Faceted Exploitation: Beyond drone forensics, the CFID provides comprehensive digital 
media exploitation, including SIM card extraction and preview against watchlists (IMSI, etc.), 
imaging of USB and SD media, and content extraction from iOS and Android devices.  
 Forensically Sound: Creates industry-standard outputs compatible with major forensic analysis 
software suites like those from Cellebrite, which has recently acquired SCG Canada, the maker of 
the CFID.  
 
7. Determination of fair and reasonable pricing.  
 
Pricing will be reviewed prior to award based on price analysis techniques available per FAR 15.404-
1(b)(2). 
 
8. Brief description of Market Research conducted and results or why market research was not 
conducted.  
 
Initial Market Research was conducted by the Requirement Owner. No other device was found 
capable of meeting the needs of the government. Teel Technologies, a small business, used to be the 
sole distributor of these items in the US. Via additional Market Research, the Contract Specialist 
verified that Cellebrite bought the CFID original OEM and is now the sole proprietary owner and 
distributor, with several resellers. Teel is no longer an exclusive distributor. 
 
The OEM informed the CS that the devices will be available under a GSA MAS schedule soon, but 
only under Cellebrite. The devices are available on NASA SEWP under 2 small businesses.

N/A

PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT (PWS) 
AFCEC 2026 FIAR Initiative  
30 June 2026 
 
1. GENERAL  
The Contractor shall provide support for the Office of the Under Secretary of Defense (Comptroller) Financial Improvement 
and Audit Readiness (FIAR) initiative. This PWS describes the support and deliverables required at specific Department of Air 
Force (DAF) installations for their respective Air Force Civil Engineer Center (AFCEC) Real Property and Real Estate Services 
offices. Such support primarily includes analyzing and updating real property records and coordinating results/corrective 
actions with various Government stakeholders to achieve acceptable Air Force real property and real estate Audit readiness 
reporting metrics.  
Proper resourcing of AF requirements is accomplished thru reviews of existing records and performing existence and 
compliance (E&C) validation, for which the contractor will provide support, to the real property and real estate services 
throughout the period of performance. Place of performance for on-site support shall be at specific DAF Installations 
(locations in table below) for the duration of the contract,  
 
2. SCOPE 
The Contractor will provide the DAF with Real Property Support by 1) providing the validation and correction of NexGen IT 
asset records for assets at each installation identified in the table below, and 2) correction and assembly of real property 
information records physical and electronic folders to enable DAF to effectively manage their real property portfolio to meet 
the Chief Financial Officer’s Audit (CFOA) compliance and standards. The Contractor shall provide support to the AFCEC  Air 
Force Financial Improvement and Audit Readiness (FIAR) team by performing quality control reviews and updates of 
installation real property and real estate transactions utilizing the NexGenIT technology platform.  
 
3. DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF WORK: 
The primary purpose of this task is the validation of complete and accurate real property/real estate inventory records for 
the assets at the selected installations.   
• The Contractor shall be responsible for the collection, analysis and,  assembly of complete and accurate data 
necessary for populating the NexGen IT database.   
• The contractor will produce and upload any necessary key supporting documentation (KSD)  for each asset listed in 
section 5.   
• The Contractor will work with assigned installation POC’s to obtain missing Real Property information and/or 
supporting files.  If records are found to be deficient or non-existent, the contractor will record the deficiency found 
and notify the Government of the deficiency for their resolution. It will be the responsibility of the contractor to 
create any new pieces of real property documentation.   
• The Contractor shall be responsible for the assembly of facility folders of real property records once they have been 
confirmed complete and accurate.  A summary of the approximate total record assets can be found in  the table in 
section 5.  The expectation is that the Contractor will complete the requirements phased by location and 
government priority.  The government will identify the priority installations and real property facility asset types at 
the kickoff meeting.  
The contractor will adhere to DAF standards, and utilize the following primary tools to perform these activities to ensure 
compliance with FIAR/CFOA and DAF requirements:  
• DAF Financial Improvement and Audit Readiness (FIAR) plan and financial statement audit requirements initiated 
and/or required Guidance from the Office of the Under Secretary of Defense (Comptroller) (OUSD(C))  
• Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Circular A-123 (Management’s Responsibility for Internal Control), 
Appendix A (Internal Control over Financial Reporting) 

2 
 
 
• Real Estate and Real Property Accountability Handbook 
• AFI -32-9001, 9002, 9003, 9004, 9005 
• DoD 4165.14 Real Property Inventory (RPI) and Forecasting 
• DAF Office of the Under Secretary of Defense (OUSD) Package Reference Guide  
• Existing business process narratives and flowcharts 
• Internal Control documentation 
• Real Property Information Model (RPIM) 
• Real Property Categorization System (RPCS)  
• DoD 7000.14-R (Financial Management Regulation) 
 
4. LOCATION OF WORK: 
Primary work location will be onsite at DAF installations listed under section 5 (Base Task Requirements). The contractor 
shall determine the mix and cost to use either local hires or TDY support to perform the daily work required for this contrac t 
utilizing office facilities provided by the DAF. Centralized review and management of assessment teams by senior personnel  
can be performed by non-local personnel. To the extent possible, Contractor should ensure use of personal vehicles is 
allowed for access to locations on the installations. It is expected that the contractor will verify use of personal vehicles to 
access all locations to include remote or difficult to access locations prior to commencing work on the installation. On the 
occasions where a personal vehicle is not allowed or cannot access remote site locations, Contractor should determine how 
they plan to access those work areas. It is expected that some locations will be remote and not accessible via paved 
roadway, in these instances a 4x4 will be required.  
DAF will provide an office area including a desk and a work area for each Contractor position identified for that location as 
well as MCEN Non-Classified (MCEN-N) network connectivity, which will provide internet access and a DOD email capability 
with a .mil address assigned to authorized contractor personnel.   
DAF will provide access to MCEN-N and standard software applications.  MCEN network connectivity shall not be used to 
conduct personal business nor maintain data of a personal nature.  
DAF will provide for each contractor position ordered under this contract an installation specific, government imaged,  
Contractor Furnished computer that can access the MCEN-N network.   
DAF will provide the Contractor with access to Government mapping, charting, and GeoBase property when necessary for 
this task order. 
The Contractor shall be responsible for damage to DAF provided office, furnishings, equipment, and systems, normal wear 
and tear excluded.  All such items shall remain the property of DAF during and after completion of the contract. 
5. BASE TASK REQUIREMENTS 
TABLE NOTE: The table below are estimates and do not account for assets that can be found active or demolished on site 
during contractors E&C analysis which can be approximately 5 to 10 percent plus or minus of the table estimates. Air Force 
installations encompass all areas within the installation’s officially designated boundaries. Geographically separated units 
(GSUs) and other site codes will be excluded for field inspections depending if the aggregate asset value of the GSU is under 
7 million deemed cost book value.

5.1. MEETINGS 
Contract Kickoff Meeting 
The Contractor shall coordinate and attend a virtual Kick-off Meeting within 30 days of Task award. The Contractor will 
develop meeting materials including an agenda and PowerPoint briefing to be presented during the meeting.  The purpose 
of the kick-off meeting is to provide an introduction of Contractor and Installation personnel, discuss specific Task s and 
objectives, Task schedules, Data Requirements, establish communication protocols, establish procedures for Installation 
access, collection of any Government Furnished Information (GFI) not already provided, and general expectations.  The 
Government will also provide the Contractor with access to the most current electronic files and provide access to the 
existing permits, plans, specifications, surveys, studies, and general information.  Meeting minutes will be developed by the  
Contractor after the kick-off meeting and submitted via email to the USACE PM, AFCEC Workflow, and Installation POC 
within 7 duty days of the meeting.  The Government will provide comments within 10 duty days , the contractor will submit 
the final minutes within 5 duty days of receipt of Government comments on the Draft.  
Draft Kickoff Meeting Presentation Slides 
Contractor shall submit draft meeting agenda and In-Brief Presentation to the Government PM listed in Appendix B 
five days prior to the PM approved kick-off meeting date. PM will review Agenda and In -Brief Presentation and provide 
comments to be addressed; Contractor shall consider PM comments and revise the meeting agenda and In- Brief 
Presentation and submit to the PM. Following approval, the Contractor will submit the agenda and In- Brief 
Presentation to customer contacts with request for customer acceptance to the schedule. 
Installation Kickoff Meeting  
Contractor is required to participate in a teleconference coordination meeting with the PM and installation 
representative(s) to discuss the agenda, and to confirm HQ acceptance to the proposed on -site meeting schedule. 
Meeting Agenda and In-Brief Presentation as approved by the PM shall be distributed to contacts outlined in this PWS. 

4 
 
 
In-brief shall outline, at a minimum, agenda, background, purpose,  Contractor execution plan, government 
expectations, coordination schedule, and project site visit and virtual collection schedule.  
During the teleconference coordination meeting, the Contractor will be responsible fo r requesting missing data such 
as but not limited to; Floor Plans, Real Estate documents that outline property boundaries, POC Interview schedules, 
building/facility accesses, and other data. Because the operations of the Installation may vary regarding primary POCs 
availability for site visits, an additional purpose of this meeting shall be to identify those POCs and the best method for 
communication within the Installation. It is expected that this activity will require one (1) day and should be conducted 
by a Contractor with experience performing multiple kickoff presentations for NextGen data collection for the 
purposes of field investigations and survey.  
Contractor will be responsible for documenting meeting minutes of each meeting. Meeting minutes are required NLT 5 
working days following the conclusion of a meeting. Meeting minutes are required to all attendees with a request for 
comment and revision. Contractor will advise all attendees of a 5-day window to review and revise meeting minutes. 
Contractor will present finalized meeting notes 10 days following the conclusion of any meeting.  
 
5.2. REAL PROPERTY RECORDS MANAGEMENT 
Real property record management requires validation to ensure assets are reported accurately.  The purpose of this 
initiative is to complete the validation and correction of NexGen IT records for all assets and records managed by DAF; as 
well as the assembly of facility folders to enable DAF to sustain effective management of real property assets.  
The Contractor will execute administrative and analytic actions to include reviewing, analyzing, documenting, generating key 
supporting documents (KSDs) and providing list recommended corrective actions needed in NexGen IT and supporting 
facility folders.  Upon approval of the Government, the Contractor will execute actual corrective actions within the NexGen 
IT application and create or edit supporting facility folders. To further support FIAR requirements AFCEC/CI Quality 
Assurance, provide Air Force Financial Managers with guidance, oversight, and standard capability to leverage data sources 
from multiple systems, with timely data; perform business analytics/intelligence to monitor and assess organizational 
performance; and take efficient actions to remediate deficiencies (automating processes where possible) and promote 
process improvements to support operational requirements and capabilities  
 
5.3. ASSET RECORD ANALYSIS/VALIDATION 
The Contractor shall conduct a full validation of assets, which includes reviewing NexGen IT real property data, facility 
folders, and physical inspection surveys to document all incomplete, inaccurate, missing, expired instruments, and 
outstanding real property assets for compliance to IAW CFOA FIAR DAF standards. The assessment shall include:  
• Analysis of real property data in NexGen IT 
• Analysis of real property physical information facility folders 
• Analysis of functional space assignment/space utilization in NexGen IT  
• Analysis and creation of documentation for the execution of expired instrument  
The Contractor will work with the Installation Real Property Accountability Office (RPAO) to find and address real property 
line items that may not yet be in NexGen IT, but are valid data to be included in both the validation report and NexGen IT 
system.  The Contractor shall coordinate with DAF and other specialized government agencies to determine database 
problems, database year conflicts, system integration issues, a nd real property category codes that may not populate due to 
coding requirements.  
Based on the above, the Contractor shall discuss the finding with the installations, address installation comments, and 
finalize review of outstanding real property line items. The Contractor shall provide the action list needed including 
Instrument Number Request (INR) AFCEC FORM 100, DD Form 1354 updates to bring DAF records and physical facility 
folders up to date and audit compliant. Where necessary, the Contractor shall produce both electronic and hard copies of 
the information and shall produce asset, tabbed files if necessary. 
The Contractor shall produce a Validation Report detailing the finding. The report document will include, but is not limited
