THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE FOR INFORMATION AND PLANNING 
PURPOSES ONLY. This announcement closes 12:00 p.m. Eastern Time on Wednesday, 
08 July 2026. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) for this 
requirement is 541519, Other Computer Related Services, with a corresponding size standard 
of $34M. Interested parties must be registered under NAICS 541519 in the System for Award 
Management (SAM) at www.sam.gov. The Government plans to consider all information 
submitted in response to this Sources Sought Notice. 
 
The contractor shall provide full-service maintenance coverage 5 days a week, with a four (4) phone 
response and 24-hour onsite response objective provided for critical system problems, and a 72-hour 
plus response for non- critical issues. The contractor shall provide support services that include on 
call services, remote support, on site-troubleshooting as needed, repair, and parts replacement. 
Support services will be conducted on Video Teleconferencing (VTC) and Secure Video 
Teleconferencing (SVTC).  
 
Performance will consist of one (1) 12-month base period, and four (4) one-year option periods. 
The Government anticipates making award on or about 30 August 2026, with the Request for 
Quote (RFQ) release date on or about 30 July 2026. 
 
Please note: This is an estimated posting timeframe, and it is the responsibility of the interested 
parties to monitor the System for Award Management website at www.sam.gov for all 
subsequent postings. The unique requirement’s draft Statement of Work (SOW) are posted in 
conjunction with this notice to provide the size, scope, and complexity of this requirement. 
 
This is not a formal Request for Quote, and no contract will result from this notice, nor does it 
commit the Government to any acquisition for these services. All interested parties shall submit

1.0 PURPOSE
This Performance Work Statement (PWS) outlines the nonpersonal service contract to provide Test Support 
Equipment Control and Monitoring Systems (TSECMS) contractor requirements for the 412th Test Wing 
Electronic Warfare Group (EWG)/Electronic Warfare Joint Logistics (EWJX) Division at the Avionics 
Test and Integration Complex (ATIC) at Edwards AFB, CA, The respective site leadership shall oversee 
upgrades, repairs, modifications, all related operations, and maintenance performed on the TSECMS assets 
and capabilities used at these locations under the support services agreement. These assets are used to 
maintain and optimize existing TSECMS that primarily supports test operations in buildings 1020, 1030, 
and 1040 at Edwards AFB, CA, This effort shall be performed on government owned equipment. 
 
2.0 BACKGROUND AND SYSTEMS DESCRIPTION 
TSECMS is a system used in anechoic chambers and B1020/1040 test facilities to operate, control and 
monitor Aircraft Support Equipment (ASE) utilities and HVAC in order to maintain system readiness in 
support of customer test operations. System readiness involves being able to adjust, control and monitor all 
critical ASE control parameters that are used to provide required utilities and controlled media such as 
high-pressure cooling air, hydraulic fluid, liquid cooling fluid such as Polyalphaolephine (PAO), Colanool, 
Ethylene-Glycol Water, and 400Hz Aircraft Power. For example, hydraulic fluid is provided to aircraft 
under test to operate aircraft landing gear and other aircraft hydraulic systems on board an aircraft to 
support various kinds of testing. In addition, cooling air is provided from a custom-built high-pressure 
Avionics Cooling Unit (ACU) used to provide required cooling air at pressures with varying pressures and 
flows to aircraft and other Avionics Systems Under Test (SUT). The ACU software related system that 
controls the ACU is from a Siemens Desigo CC platform using Continuous Function Chart (CFC) or 
Structured Control Language (SCL) that was developed and written by Siemens to support a wide range of 
SUTs. The Liquid Cooling Unit System is monitored to provide avionics cooling fluid at varying system 
pressures and flows to support liquid cooled onboard aircraft systems. Also, a custom built 400Hz 
Electrical System is controlled and monitored to provide 400Hz power to various aircraft and other SUT. In 
general, a TSECMS is primarily used to control critical equipment and systems to operate, control and 
monitor aircraft support equipment parameters and connected secondary systems. 
3.0 SCOPE OF WORK 
The work covered by this PWS consists of a contractor furnishing all supervision, labor, equipment and 
materials necessary to maintain existing hardware and software Siemens Control Systems (SCS) in order to 
maintain proper operation of affected TSECMS. The Contractor shall maintain, manage, troubleshoot, 
repair, replace, install, configure, connect and commission SCS of both the hardware and software. 
Hardware types include Siemens PXC Modular Building Controller (MBC) panels/enclosures, with 
Siemens Automation-level processors, digital input and output modules, analog input and output modules, 
and field-level controllers and Siemens actuators and control valve assemblies. The contractor shall be 
available 24 hours per day, 7 days per week to provide technical support with the government TSECMS 
system operators. This shall be accomplished via phone support as required to maintain TSECMS. In the 
event of an emergency, the contractor shall provide phone support within 2 hours. If phone support cannot 
remedy the situation, the contractor shall arrive on-site within 6 hours for mission critical corrective 
maintenance 24 hours a day. Additionally, this acquisition includes contractor providing preventive and 
corrective maintenance support to maintain existing Siemens hardware and software control systems that 
controls and operates government test support equipment. This shall be accomplished via annual onsite 

preventive inspections and up to 6 days of customer directed support days and/or corrective maintenance 
support when coordinated/requested by the government to restore operations to a failed test system 
controlled by the TSECMS. To support a planned phased migration of the TSECMS, up to 60 hours of 
engineering support shall be available to the government, as requested/required. This encompasses the 
Siemens automation systems at  Edwards AFB . In addition, the contractor shall conduct technology audits, 
as-required, ensuring the latest software system performance updates and upgrades as they are provided. 
 
4.0 Inherently Governmental Function.
The Contractor shall not perform Inherently Governmental functions as defined in FAR Subpart 7.503 in 
relationship to this PWS

6.1 The objective of this requirement is to define the type of support that shall be provided from 
Siemens to the Government as needed, upon the receipt of Unfunded Requirement (UR) requests 
for Siemens Support Special Projects. 
6.2 Special Projects that require support from Siemens may include, but are not limited to; Computer-
Aided Design drawing support pertaining to the modification of existing and/or development of 
Control Systems to support test equipment; Siemens engineering support; Hardware 
installation/integration of the Siemens hardware product-line to include but not limited to PXC 
controllers; CFC/SCL programming; System hardware and software upgrades; and graphics 
modifications and development. 
6.3 In the event a project is identified as pertains to the support outlined in this section, or not 
otherwise specifically covered, but clearly within the scope of this contract, the contractor shall 
submit a fixed-price proposal to be negotiated by the Contracting Officer and the Project Manager 
prior to the government providing the authorization to proceed.

STATEMENT OF WORK 
Space Scheduling System for the  
Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) 
 
1 Background  
In order to continue adapting to the agency’s growing technical needs, the FAA requires a digital and 
electronic workspace management system that is a cloud -based Software as a Service (SaaS) platform 
featuring an easy-to-use and consumer-grade interface that is responsive to any sized device for use across 
the agency at various FAA Enterprise locations  across the US . The S aaS solution must include 
comprehensive implementation, dat a migration, systems integration, user training and support and 
maintenance. This SaaS software solution will allow users to reserve conference rooms, workplace spaces 
(desks, meeting rooms), and more in one centralized location using a ny device. This cloud-based solution 
must provide reservations of 1200 conference rooms and 700 workspaces with options for more licenses 
as more locations or other asset types  (i.e., ﬂeet, equipment) are included. The current FAA reservation 
system supports at least 100 locations and at least 100,000 users. 
2 SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS 
The software must be a SaaS product and have the following features and functions: 
Architectural and Hosting 
 
2.1 Must be on a Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program (FEDRAMP) authorized 
cloud provider. 
2.2 Ability to be easily accessed through application programming interfaces (API) connections 
for data exchanges, as required. 
2.3 Provide high availability with at least 99.5% availability uptime. 
2.4 Must have a clear disaster Recovery Time Objective (RTO) and Recovery Point Objective 
(RPO) per impact level targets. 
2.5 Must be scalable to over 100,000 users in different time zones and locations. 
Security 
2.6 Must be compliant with FEDRAMP , FISMA and NIST SP 800-53 latest version. Refer to  
http://www.cloudcomputing.ieee.org/standard and www.fedramp.gov.  
2.7 Integrate the contractor’s application with the following technologies used with the FAA for 
identiﬁcation and multi-factor authentication: 
- FAA/DOT MyAccess Single Sign On (SSO) system which is FAA’s Active Directory 
- FAA Windows Active Directory user authentication process 
- HSDP-12 Personal Identiﬁcation Veriﬁcation (PIV) 

 
2 
 
2.8 Comprehensive auditing of all reservations, access, changes and administrative actions 
(SIEM integration) 
2.9 Comply with Section 508 Web Content Accessibility Guidance (WCAG) 2.1 AA for 
accessibility to include email, exported or generated reports. 
2.10 Provide Role-based access control (RBAC) with least privilege. 
2.11 Documented incident response procedures with 1-hour detection/notiﬁcation for incidents. 
2.12 Supports continuous monitoring with mature standardized patch management procedures 
in place. 
2.13 Availability of annual cloud service provider reassessments per FedRAMP standards. 
2.14 Must be Zero-trust ready. 
2.15 All data must be encrypted in transit using Transport Layer Security (TLS) 1.3 (or latest 
Federal standard) and at rest utilizing Federal Information Processing Standards (FIPS) 140-
3 validated cryptographic modules with Advanced Encryption Standard (AES)-256 or better. 
Core Reservation Functionality 
2.16 Request and Reserve shared spaces such as conference rooms, offices, workstations, 
equipment and transportation. 
2.17 Fully support Microsoft 365 and/or Google Workplace integration to enable users to reserve 
rooms within the mail service offerings to include calendar optimization. For example, user 
should have the ability to connect to the service via their email exchange provided by 
Microsoft Outlook and/or Google service calendar to make and manage space reservations 
within the system. (Preferred solution can integrate with both Microsoft 365 and Google 
Workplace.) 
2.18 Ability to autogenerate email conﬁrmations and notiﬁcations of changes to reservations. 
2.19 Ability to customize rules and requirements for spaces by role, organization and location. 
2.20 Ability to conﬁgure custom forms for onboarding spaces, locations, policies, users and 
group management. (For example, users have the ability to indicate conﬁguration and 
equipment requests such as hollow square and perimeter seating requirements (based on 
max capacity per conﬁguration), panel head table, microphones, ﬂags, and quantity). 
2.21 Ability to support enterprise-level conﬁguration options to accommodate local policies and 
business unit rules by space across FAA buildings throughout the agency. This means the 
application must provide the ability to set speciﬁc business rules by space, as needed, to 
tailor the application to meet business unit’s unique needs. 
2.22 Ability to establish multiple POCs for at least 100 locations. 
2.23 Ability to upload ﬂoor plans and multiple photos for all spaces and locations. 
2.24 Ability to modify approval workﬂow for spaces requiring approval. 
2.25 Ability to conduct universal searches.  
2.26 Ability to modify existing reservations for Space Manager and System Administrators.  
2.27 Ability to auto-bump reservations where the user has not checked in by a speciﬁed time or 
after a grace period allowing others to reserve the space. 
2.28 System should be intuitive and user friendly with minimal clicks to reserve a room and offer 
intuitive search functionality with additional ﬁltering such as, ﬂoor plans, capacity and 
conﬁguration type, equipment. 

 
3 
 
2.29 Allow delegation so others can make, approve, modify reservations or spaces on behalf of 
another user. 
2.30 Allow multiple user types with varying roles and responsibilities with access. At a minimum, 
10 System Administrators, 100 Space Managers, 200 Approvers, and 100,000 Regular Users 
are required.  
2.31 Ability to make reoccurring reservations. 
2.32 To have a landing page that is manageable to add downloadable resources. 
2.33 Ability to conduct mass updates to the database such as managing user proﬁles and 
permissions as a bulk or per group basis. 
2.34 Ability to support all users and reservations in different time zones based on location. 
2.35 Ability to accept ﬂoor plans in JPEG or PDF and update as needed without having any effect 
on the existing resources or reservations. 
2.36 Ability to perform the FAA Use Cases 
2.37 Ability to print or export pages from the application, ex. Listing of the reservations for all user 
types. 
Analytics and Reporting 
2.38 Access to user activity and reservation activity logs in a reporting functionality. 
2.39 Ability to track space onboarding and offboarding activities, archived locations, user 
management and engagement. 
2.40 Offer dashboard and reporting templates to manage portfolios and programs by location, 
building, regions, or communities and share with other users. 
2.41 Ability to identify or locate which point of access to the application. 
2.42 Ability to create customized reports based on all data points, export data to standard 
reporting formats (ex: xls, xlsm, html, txt, xml, csv, pdf). 
2.43 Ability to automatically generate reports on set frequency levels and email to 
designated recipients. 
3 TASKS 
3.1 Program Management  
3.1.1 Program Administration  
The contractor must provide ancillary project management services to support the planning 
and execution of this project. The Contractor must implement and document a Management 
Program.  The contractor must submit a  Management Plan (MP), documenting its 
management program, for Government approval.  The Contractor must revise this plan as 
necessary. The Contractor must implement this plan upon approval.  The MP must identify 
the Contractor's management, organization, authority, responsibility, controls, and the 
extent to which these apply to the space scheduling system. The MP must detail the 

 
4 
 
Contractor's methodology to ensure that the program management requirements set forth 
in this SOW are met.  The MP should detail the speciﬁc plans, schedule, and logistical 
approach to support the implementation of the system for each of the FAA facilities covered 
under this requirement and training of FAA administrators  and users. The contractor must: 
At a minimum, the Contractor must perform the following tasks in managing this contract: 
• Produce the schedules of work that reﬂect and track the delivery of products as speciﬁed by 
this SOW. 
• Use methods and metrics for assessing the schedule, technical performance of the work, 
and risks of this program. 
• Use procedures for relating risks and costs to schedule and technical performance to 
assess the impact of risks and costs on successful completion of the scheduling system 
work efforts 
• Designate a Program Manager (PM) who is responsible for integrating and maintaining the 
total Contractor effort as described in this SOW. The PM must be prepared at all times, 
given reasonable notice, to present and discuss with the FAA the status of contract 
activities. 
An integral factor in the success of the space  scheduling system is the Contractor's plans for 
interaction with the Government and their support contractors. The MP must include the 
Contractor's plan for ensuring that all interaction is managed and conducted to provide maximum 
beneﬁt toward successful design, implementation and operations and maintenance of the space  
scheduling system. The Contractor must also conduct ongoing risk management activities during 
the period of the contract. The risk management activities must be an integral part of the Contractor's 
management process, as described in the MP . 
 
 CDRL    001   Management Plan   
 
3.1.2 Project Schedule  
The Contractor must develop and maintain a project schedule of events planned for accomplishing 
the work effort identiﬁed in the SOW. The Contractor must monitor and report project performance 
using an automated scheduling tool.  The schedule must provide time phasing for all activities 
described in this SOW, relationships between the various activities, and milestone review points.  A 
revised project schedule must be delivered quarterly thereafter, or as required based on the volume 
of changes. 
 CDRL    002   Project Schedule   
 
3.1.3 Financial Reporting  
The Contractor must establish and maintain a ﬁnancial control system that plans and controls cost 
and schedule.  The system must also assess and report project cost and schedule status to the FAA. 

 
5 
 
The Contractor must prepare and submit cost performance reports on a monthly basis with each 
invoice that provide: 
- Summary information by contract line item number (CLIN), task order, sub-total, and total 
- Supporting detailed information that identiﬁes quantities, CLIN, task order, unit prices, 
which separately identify the monthly lease price and the monthly maintenance price for 
each piece of equipment, and total amounts 
- A ﬁnancial status report that identiﬁes by task order and CLIN, funding or hours remaining, 
as of the reporting date. 
 
 
 CDRL    003   Financial Technical Report   
 
3.1.4 Project Status Monitoring  
The Contractor must continuously monitor schedule, and technical performance on this contract.  
The Contractor must provide a timely assessment of project progress at monthly project reviews.  The 
monthly project reviews will be held at FAA Headquarters unless otherwise directed by the FAA.  The 
key contractor and sub-contractor personnel must attend the monthly project reviews. 
The project reviews must: 
- Include a review of the technical and schedule,  aspects of contractor's performance, and 
program accomplishments (e.g., milestones met), problems, forecasts, and subcontractor 
activities 
- Provide a summary of procurement activity, including what is on order, pending, and 
projected lead times and/or arrival times 
- Address project status as related to projected and actual milestones and accomplishments 
- Present price summaries (total price for period and total price to date) by CLIN for all 
invoices submitted since the last review 
- Address schedule delays, problems, or other discrepancies in planned, actual and 
forecasted project progress and address the cause, effect and proposed correction 
- Provide status of action items 
The Contractor must provide Project Status Reports on a monthly basis.  The Project Status Reports 
must include the corrective actions being pursued if there is a deviation from the planned schedule, 
budgeted cost, or performance requirements.  
The Contractor must conduct technical interchange meetings with the FAA or its designated 
representatives to resolve speciﬁc technical issues.  Technical interchange meetings must be 
conducted at the Contractor's facility or a site designated by the FAA.  The Contractor must provide 
administrative support for the project reviews and TIMs, including preparation of agendas and 
minutes for each project review and technical interchange meetings in accordance with Section 
3.1.6.
 
 CDRL    004   Project Status Report   

 
6 
 
 
3.1.5 Quality Assurance  
The Contractor must provide and maintain a documented quality system as a means of assuring 
compliance with the hardware and software requirements of the contract.  The quality system should 
be established and maintained in accordance with ANSI/ASQC Q9002 -1994 and  must be 
documented in the Quality System Plan. 
 
 CDRL    005   Quality Assurance Plan   
3.1.6 Meetings, Conferences, and Reviews  
The Contractor must conduct meetings, conferences, and reviews (hereinafter referred to as 
reviews) with the FAA to discuss program progress, identify potential problems, and resolve identiﬁed 
problems.  
The Contractor must prepare and submit a meeting agenda for all reviews to the Government for 
approval.  The Contractor must formerly notify the Government of its readiness to conduct a review 
if the review is a mandatory requirement of this contract (i.e., design review).  Delivery of all CDRL 
Items req uired prior to the mandatory review is a prerequisite to notiﬁcation of readiness.  If 
prerequisites to holding the review have not been fulﬁlled, the FAA will have the option of 
postponement without prejudice to other task requirements. 
Upon receiving approval of the review agenda, the Contractor must promulgate the agenda, date, 
and location of the review to all attendees.  The Contractor must make key Contractor personnel 
available to respond to FAA questions.  For each event at which a  presentation will be given, the 
Contractor must prepare and submit the presentation materials.  The Contractor must record, 
prepare, and submit the review minutes and action items for each review. The Contractor must track 
action items identiﬁed at each event.  For each action item, the Contractor must assign an agreed 
upon suspense date and provide status at agreed upon intervals until the action item is closed.  The 
Contractor must respond to all action items in writing with a writ

Part I. Performance Work Statement (PWS)

Title: GFM Decision-Ready Data Products (Gold Tables) Services in the SIPRNet War Data Platform
Program: Department of War Federated Data Platform – War Data Platform (formerly Advana)
Managed By: OSW Chief Data and Artificial Intelligence Office (CDAO)
Environment: SIPRNet War Data Platform (WDP)

1.0 Purpose

This PWS defines the requirements for contractor support to engineer, implement, and sustain a modernized, next-generation Global Force Management (GFM) data lifecycle within the SIPRNet War Data Platform (WDP). Transitioning away from legacy methodologies, the contractor shall apply modern Digital Engineering and DataOps best practices to accelerate the movement of GFM data from originating Authoritative Data Systems (ADS). To minimize development time and align with existing ecosystems, the contractor must leverage proven, deployed Government Off-The-Shelf (GOTS) and Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) technologies, using a mix of cloud-native (e.g., serverless functions) and non-native architectures for optimal data pipeline automation.

Operating within the WDP Lakehouse architecture, the contractor shall process GFM data from Bronze (raw, source-aligned ingestion) to Silver (cleaned, validated, and enriched data) layers. Crucially, the contractor will employ Advanced Data Modeling techniques to develop “Single Source of Truth” GFM Gold Tables. These Gold Tables must be architected to strictly align with Joint Fires Network (JFN) and Intelligence Community (IC) "Golden Objects" (Red and Blue Object Management) – highly refined, authoritative, and standardized version of data entities.

To support advanced analytics and autonomy, the contractor shall use a diverse, multi-tool suite of Artificial Intelligence (AI) capabilities for data hygiene, conversion, and interpretation. The ultimate objective is to ensure all final GFM Gold Tables are delivered in a universally "AI-Ready State" – eligible for ingestion by any platform or model without vendor lock-in. Finally, all updates to data, scripts, and models must be executed using a Blue/Green deployment architecture to ensure continuous, zero-downtime availability for production applications supporting the GFM mission across the Department.

2.0 Background

The Department of War Federated Data Platform is the War Data Platform (WDP), managed by OSW CDAO. WDP is a Federated Data Lakehouse environment that supports ingestion, transformation, storage, governance, analytics, BI, applications, APIs, ML models, and LLM-enabled capabilities across Department mission and enterprise domains. WDP organizes data using a Bronze/Silver/Gold architecture, in which Bronze preserves raw ingested source data, Silver provides cleaned and enriched data, and Gold provides highly curated, aggregated, business-ready data optimized for Department use cases.

The Government requires contractor support to operationalize WDP capabilities on SIPRNet to create trusted GFM Gold Tables for Joint and Service communities in support of the GFM mission across the Department.

3.0 Scope

The contractor shall:

Establish repeatable processes for the end-to-end GFM data lifecycle in the WDP.

Ingest GFM data from approved Joint and Service source systems as WDP Bronze Tables.

Clean, validate, enrich, standardize, and align data as WDP Silver Tables.

Curate, version, govern, and publish decision-ready WDP Gold Tables in an accessible location within WDP.

Ensure availability of GFM Data in a common location where all GFM Gold Tables.

All GFM Gold tables shall be connected to the WDP Data Catalog for downstream access, search, and consumption through approved WDP-native access patterns.

Establish and execute a comprehensive Data Intelligence & Active Data Governance framework, including automated data quality monitoring, end-to-end data lineage, active metadata management, and process governance to ensure all GFM data products are trusted, auditable, and decision-ready.

Execute continuous Data Requirements Engineering & Discovery to define target schemas in coordination with GFM stakeholders.

Engineer AI Vectorization & Embedding Generation pipelines to convert GFM Gold Tables into AI-ready formats.

Leverage existing WDP AI capabilities to accelerate mapping, profiling, alignment, anomaly detection, and documentation.

Provide program management, training, sustainment, and operational support using Agile methodologies (e.g., SAFe, Scrum).

Out of scope unless specifically authorized:

Development of new WDP core platform capabilities.

Modification of authoritative source systems.

Delivery outside SIPRNet.

4.0 Definitions

GFM Data: Global Force Management data supporting force structure, force sourcing, readiness, allocation, assignment, availability, directed readiness related operational decision-making and their associated assessments.

Bronze Layer/Tables: Raw source data ingested as received, with source fidelity preserved.

Silver Layer/Tables: Cleaned, validated, standardized, and enriched data derived from Bronze.

Gold Tables: The most refined data asset in the WDP, representing a curated, consumption-ready, and mission-focused data product. It is designed for high-performance analytics and is the authoritative source for specific business domains or mission areas. Gold Tables must meet the following criteria:

Schema Standards: Data is explicitly modeled into analytical schemas optimized for read performance, such as Star or Snowflake schemas, and strictly aligned with JFN/IC "Golden Objects" (Red and Blue Object Management).

Storage & Performance: Stored in optimized Databricks Datalake format to support high-performance, low-latency analytical queries from tools like Power BI, Qlik, and Tableau, as well as AI/ML model training.

Aggregation & Business Logic: Contains business-level or mission-level aggregated data, tailored for specific reporting requirements and analytical objectives. All transformations and business logic applied must be documented and version controlled.

Metadata & Naming Conventions: Governed by strict, semantic metadata tagging and standardized naming conventions consistent with the DoD Data Strategy's VAULTIS (Visible, Accessible, Understandable, Linked, Trustworthy, Interoperable, Secure) goals.

Access Model: Secured via robust Identity and Access Management (IAM) controls and Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC). Access is provisioned strictly to authorized end-users based on mission alignment and data classification.

Governance & Promotion: A data product can only be promoted to "Gold" after passing a formal governance gate that validates data quality, schema compliance, comprehensive metadata, auditable lineage back to the Bronze layer, and all security controls.

Decision-ready: Fit for operational or analytical use, quality-assured, traceable, timely, and aligned to agreed business rules and standards.

Authoritative source: Government-designated system or provider responsible for a given data element or dataset.

Conceptual Data Model: A high-level, mission-focused representation of the GFM data domain. It defines the core entities (e.g., Units, Forces, Equipment, Readiness) and the fundamental relationships between them, designed to align stakeholders on business requirements without technical database details.

Logical Data Model: A detailed, technology-independent blueprint of the GFM data architecture. It defines all specific data fields (attributes), unique identifiers (keys), semantic definitions, business rules, and precise relationships. This serves as the authoritative, vendor-agnostic representation of GFM business logic, independent of physical storage or AI technology.

Physical Data Model: A technology-specific database design that represents how GFM data is physically stored and structured within the War Data Platform (WDP) environment (e.g., as Databricks Delta tables, SQL schemas, or Vector Stores). It defines actual database data types, partitioning, indexing, and storage parameters required for technical execution.

AI Vectorization: The computational process of transforming human-readable data (text, documents, or structured tables) into numerical arrays (vectors) that Artificial Intelligence (AI) and machine learning models can read, process, and analyze.

Embedding Generation (Embeddings): The creation of advanced mathematical representations of data that capture its semantic meaning and context. Unlike traditional keyword matching, embeddings allow AI systems to understand the conceptual relationships and intent behind different GFM data points.

Vector Store (Vector Database): A specialized data storage system designed specifically to store, index, and efficiently query vector embeddings. It serves as the required infrastructure layer to connect curated Gold Tables to Large Language Models (LLMs) and autonomous agents.

Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG): An AI architectural pattern that queries a Vector Store for authoritative, trusted data to feed into an LLM before it generates a response. This grounds the AI in approved GFM data, ensuring accuracy and preventing fabricated outputs (hallucinations).

AI-Ready State: Data that has been cleaned, governed (Medallion Gold tier), vectorized, converted into embeddings, and loaded into a Vector Store, making it immediately available for consumption by an AI model without requiring further manual engineering or transformation.

Schema Standards: Data is explicitly modeled into analytical schemas optimized for read performance, such as Star or Snowflake schemas, and strictly aligned with JFN/IC "Golden Objects" (Red and Blue Object Management).

Storage & Performance: Stored in optimized Databricks Delta Lake format to support high-performance, low-latency analytical queries from tools like Power BI, Qlik, and Tableau, as well as AI/ML model training.

Aggregation & Business Logic: Contains business-level or mission-level aggregated data, tailored for specific reporting requirements and analytical objectives. All transformations and business logic applied must be documented and version controlled.

Metadata & Naming Conventions: Governed by strict, semantic metadata tagging and standardized naming conventions consistent with the DoD Data Strategy's VAULTIS (Visible, Accessible, Understandable, Linked, Trustworthy, Interoperable, Secure) goals.

Access Model: Secured via robust Identity and Access Management (IAM) controls and Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC). Access is provisioned strictly to authorized end-users based on mission alignment and data classification.

Governance & Promotion: A data product can only be promoted to "Gold" after passing a formal governance gate that validates data quality, schema compliance, comprehensive metadata, auditable lineage back to the Bronze layer, and all security controls.

5.0 Applicable Documents

The Government shall provide, as applicable:

GFM business rules, standards, and canonical models.

WDP technical guidance, patterns, and governance procedures.

SIPRNet and WDP security policies.

Source system access approvals, data sharing agreements, and interface specifications.

Existing reference data, code sets, and data dictionaries.

Any previously provided needs, capabilities, and deliverables germane to this effort shall be considered reference material. All contract performance, however, will be measured against the requirements defined within this PWS and any formal GFM business rules, standards, and canonical models provided by the government post-award.

6.0 Government-Furnished Information / Equipment

6.1 Government-Furnished Information (GFI)

The Government shall provide:

Access to SIPRNet WDP tenant, approved workspaces, and relevant services.

Available WDP-native ingestion, storage, transformation, governance, and AI capabilities.

Source system contacts, sample extracts, and Government SMEs.

Existing GFM schemas, quality rules, and governance artifacts.

WDP AI capabilities inventory on the SIPRnet.

The following criteria and metrics established by the Data SWG established under the GFM WG per CJCSI 3256.01B, C2 Governance & Management:

Named Gold Tables

Named source systems and source priority

Quantitative Service Level Agreements (SLA) and Service Level Objectives (SLO) as they relate to capability expectations

Gold promotion criteria for each or all Gold Tables as appropriate

Government approval authority and processes for mappings, rules, and release promotion.

6.2 Government-Furnished Equipment (GFE)

The Government will provide access to the approved inventory of WDP-native services on SIPRNet. This includes, but is not limited to, Databricks for data transformation, Unity Catalog for governance (or as appropriate for SIPR security fabric), and specific AI-enabled services for data profiling, schema discovery, anomaly detection, and assisted data mapping. The exact toolchain and service endpoints will be provided post-award.

7.0 Place of Performance

Work shall primarily be performed within the SIPRNet WDP. On-site support may be required for classified coordination, source onboarding, testing, or security-related activities.

8.0 Period of Performance

As specified in the contract. The contractor shall deliver initial operational capability nine months into the base period and incrementally expand Gold Table coverage thereafter.

9.0 Performance Requirements

9.1 Program Management

The contractor shall:

Provide a Program Management Plan (PMP) within 15 calendar days of award.

Provide and maintain an Integrated Master Plan / Integrated Master Schedule (IMP/IMS) focused on continuous delivery and predictable velocity.

Conduct recurring status reviews and provide progress, risk, and issue reporting.

Maintain a risk, issue, assumption, and dependency log.

Execute continuous Requirements Discovery: Led by the Data Product Manager, the contractor shall proactively engage stakeholders to elicit, validate, and document data requirements and schemas prior to engineering, rather than relying solely on Government-provided requirements.

9.2 Bronze Layer Source Onboarding and Ingestion

The contractor shall:

Identify, document, and onboard approved GFM source systems.

Implement secure WDP-native ingestion pipelines to Bronze, utilizing a mix of cloud-native (e.g., serverless functions) and non-native architectures to optimize automation.

Preserve source fidelity, provenance, timestamps, and source metadata.

Implement intake checks for schema, record counts, required fields, and change detection.

Title:  OIT Clinical Data Mart Operations and Maintenance (CDM)  
Agency:  Indian Health Service 
Issue Date: Friday June 26, 2026 
Due Date:  Monday July 13, 2026, no later than 2:00 p.m. EST 
POCs:  Responses must be submitted via email to Mario.Henriquez@ihs.gov and  
Julie.Corbin@ihs.gov.  
 
This Sources Sought Notice (SSN) is for market research and planning purposes only and shall 
not be construed as a solicitation or an obligation or commitment to issue a solicitation by the 
Indian Health Service (IHS). It seeks information from the specific types of entities listed below 
to assess their capabilities in fulfilling the requirements set forth in this SSN. The information 
from this SSN will be used to determine the appropriate acquisition strategy and whether 
adequate competition exists within one or more pools, in accordance with the applicable 
regulations including Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) 19, HHSAR subpart 326.600, and 
Indian Health Manual 5-1. 
 
Responses to this SSN must identify whether they: 
 
➢ Hold a GSA MAS contract; 
➢ Hold a STARS III contract; 
➢ Are 8(a) participant; 
➢ Are Indian Small Business Economic Enterprise (ISBEE); 
➢ Are ANC-owned or Tribal-owned; 
➢ Meet other relevant socioeconomic categories. 
 
The applicable primary NAICS code for this requirement is 541511 – Custom Computer 
Programing Services. An organization that is not a small business under the applicable 
NAICS code shall NOT submit a response to this notice. Contractors that hold a GSA MAS 
contract or a STARS III contract should identify the applicable contract number(s) in their 
response. Generic capability statements are not sufficient and may not be considered when 
assessing entity capabilities. 
 
 
Background 
The Data Mart program works with the Office of Clinical and Preventive Services (OCPS) for 
clinical programs/products, the Office of Public Health Support (OPHS) for Government 
Performance Results Act (GPRA) performance measures and services supported by this contract 
and is managed by the Office of Information Technology (OIT).   The program also uses the 
National Data Warehouse (NDW) General Data Mart and Behavioral and Community exports to 
refresh its production data marts and work in conjunction with the National Patient Information 
Reporting System (NPIRS). 
 
The Data Mart Program supports several “data marts” for various Indian Health Service (IHS) 
programs.  A data mart is an automated system that contains several core functions such as 
reporting, security, graphics and data refresh activities to satisfy a particular requirement.  Data 
mart requirements are defined by the requesting program.  Each data mart’s database structures, 

  
Sources Sought Notice: 75H70426Q00030 
OIT Clinical Data Mart Operations and Maintenance (CDM)  
Page 2 of 4 
 
data movement or data “refresh” processes, data validation, programming logic and code must be 
maintained and documented. 
 
IHS also supports the Joint Commission approved performance measurements at approximately 
19 sites. This program supports national hospital accreditation activities for both direct and 
tribally operated Joint Commission accredited hospitals. 
 
Program offices supported include, but are not limited to, the following: 
 
•   Division of Diabetes and Treatment (DDTP) 
•   Division of Behavioral Health (DBH) 
•   Public Health Nursing (PHN) 
•   Division of Oral Health (DOH) 
•   Community Health Representatives (CHR) 
•   Health Education (HE) 
•   Office of Environmental Health and Engineering (OEHE) 
•   Office of Resource Access and Partnership (ORAP) 
•   Center for Disease Control (CDC) 
•   Division of Planning, Evaluation and Research (DPER), OPHS 
•   Division of Program Statistics (DPS), OPHS 
•   Division of Epidemiology and Disease Prevention (DEDP), OPHS 
•   Office of Finance and Accounting (OFA), IHS 
•   Assistant Secretary for Financial Resources (ASFR), HHS 
•   Assistant Secretary for Planning and Evaluation, (ASPE), HHS 
•   Numerous State Cancer Registries 
•   Various area offices for program specific projects 
 
The purpose of this contract is for the contractor to provide support and maintenance (including 
minor enhancements) of existing data marts and any newly developed data marts created in the

1 
 
Sources Sought Notice 
 
The Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD is issuing this Sources Sought 
Notice as a means of conducting market research to identify parties having an interest in and the 
resources to support the requirement to stabilize, modernize, and operationally sustain National 
Standards for the Physical Inspection of Real Estate (NSPIRE) inspection program. The result of 
this market research will contribute to determining the method of procurement. The applicable 
North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code assigned to this procurement is 
541511 - Custom Computer Programming Services.  
 
There is no solicitation at this time. This request for capability information does not constitute a 
request for proposals; submission of any information in response to this market survey is purely 
voluntary; the government assumes no financial responsibility for any costs incurred.   
 
Background:  
 
This is a new requirement to replace the existing NSPIRE system: The solution will replace 
fragmented, manual processes with a scalable and secure digital ecosystem that supports real -
time data access, automation, and consistent outcomes.  Please review the PWS for detailed 
information. 
 
General Description of Work:  
 
OCIO requires contractor support to perform Development Modernization Enhancement 
(DME) work to stabilize, modernize, and operationally sustain the National Standards for the 
Physical Inspection of Real Estate (NSPIRE) inspection program. This includes rev iewing 
business and technical needs, developing reports in an application that supports not only  Public 
Indian Housing ’s (PIH) requirements but also those of HUD internal customers such as the 
Federal Housing Administrations (FHA) Office of Multifamily Hou sing (MFH), the Office of 
the HUD Chief Financial Officer (OCFO) and external customers such as Public Housing 
Authorities (PHAs), owners, and agents. Additionally, contractors must have deep product 
management, data query development, and experience in implementing reporting solutions 
using an approved highly customizable business intelligence platform. As part of the 
Contractor’s solution , HUD requires a highly customizable COTS inspection software or XaaS 
platform (NSPIRE NextGen System)  that can accommodate the NSPIRE inspection process 
and life cycle to properly support our mission of ensuring safe, decent and sanitary housing for 
our HUD-assisted tenants.  
 
NSPIRE NextGen must meet modernization objectives capabilities for HUD’s stakeholder 
needs and services includ ing: 
• Stabilize inspection operations and prevent data loss.  
• Support scalable, concurrent field inspections with offline capability.  
• Replace manual and fragmented workflows with automated, auditable processes.  

 
 
2 
 
• Improve transparency and usability for internal and external stakeholders.  
• Establish a modular architecture capable of supporting future NSPIRE phases without 
re-platforming. 
 
The NSPIRE NextGen must  deliver targeted enhancements across the following system 
modules areas: 
• Inspector Mobile App lication 
• Field Office Application 
• Scheduling Application 
• Vendor Management Application 
• Quality Control Application 
 
Internal HUD reporting  provided in Section 5 of the P erformance Work Statement will detail 
specific requirements and tasks for each of the system modules listed above.  
 
Successful NSPIRE NextGen system adoption requires a robust change management program 
embedded in the Contractor’s NSPIRE NextGen Services Solution . This includes training 
development and delivery, updated materials, stakeholder  communications, and operational 
readiness support for Assessment and Recovery Center (ARC), HUD field offices, Property 
Owners/Agents (POAs), HUD contractors , and inspectors.  
 
As part of the NSPIRE NextGen Services, the Contractor must provide support to OCIO to 
strengthen its Information Technology (IT) planning and operations function. NSPIRE NextGen 
Services shall include analyzing current OCIO policies and procedures and providing 
recommendations to assist with the modernization of those policies and procedures. In addition, 
the Contractor must provide support is needed to train HUD staff on all new processes.  
 
The Contractor shall provide support services to monitor and validate the quality and 
effectiveness of out-sourced infrastructure managed services through program oversight and 
analysis and provide resultant subsequent recommendations to the Government. The NSPIRE 
NextGen System support services shall include: 
 
• Program and Project Management  
• Core Stability & Continuity  
• Field Inspection Application  
• Inventory & Profile Management  
• Ordering & Scheduling  
• Health & Safety Defects  
• Inspection Quality Control Review  
• Analytics & Reporting  
• Appeals & Technical Reviews  
• Vendor, Property, & Inspector Administration  
• Protocols, Standards & Technical Assistance Center (TAC) Integration  

 
 
3 
 
• Training 
• System Security Compliance  
• Agile Sprint Planning  
• User Acceptance Testing (UAT)  
• Continuous Integration and Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) pipeline Release Software 
Package Support Installation and Coordination  
• Support Installation and Coordination  
• Change Management and Communications  
 
Detailed descriptions of specific tasks are provided in Section 5 – Specific Tasks and 
Deliverables. 
 
Special qualifications.  
 
The Contractor shall have and maintain SOC 2 Type II certification. 
 
The Contractor shall ensure the following professional certifications are possessed and 
maintained during the entire contract performance period:  
 
• Project Management Professional Certification (PMP)  
• SAFe Scrum Master Certified 
 
The Contractor shall meet these qualification requirements upon contract award.   
 
 
Contemplated place of performance: 
 
The place of performance shall be at the Contractors facilities.  
 
Contemplated period of performance: 
 
The performance period will be for one base period of 12 months and four (4) 12-month option 
periods. 
 
Submission Instructions:  
 
THIS IS AN RFI ONLY to identify sources that can provide a National Standards for the 
Physical Inspection of Real Estate (NSPIRE) inspection program. Interested vendors are those 
vendors who have interest in providing a response to RFI and who can provide a vendor 
capability statement demonstrating a commercial solution and technical experience for this 
requirement, including relevant scope in terms of its size, complexity and magnitude to the 
tasks/activities to be performed under this requirement, particularly, as it pertains to the support 
services and technical solutions required. All capable and available firms are encouraged to 

 
 
4 
 
participate.    
 
Please be advised that generic capability statements are not sufficient for effective review of 
respondents’ response. It must directly demonstrate the company’s capability, experience, and/or 
ability to marshal resources to effectively and efficiently perform each of the tasks described 
above in sufficient level of detail to allow definitive numerical evaluation; and evidence that the 
contractor can satisfy the minimum requirements listed above in compliance with FAR 52.219-
14 (“Limitations of Subcontracting”).  Failure to definitively address the requirement will result 
in a finding that respondent lacks the capability of performing the work. 
 
Responses to this notice shall be limited to ten pages, and must include: 
 
1. Company name, mailing address, e-mail address, telephone and FAX numbers, 
website address (if available), and the name, telephone number, and e-mail address of 
a point of contact having the authority and knowledge to clarify responses with 
Government representatives. 
2. Name, title, telephone number, and e-mail addresses of individuals who can verify the 
demonstrated capabilities identified in the responses. 
3. Business size for NAICS 541511 (size standard $34 million or number of employees) 
and status, if qualified as an 8(a) firm (must be certified by SBA), Small 
Disadvantaged Business (must be certified by SBA), Woman-Owned Small Business, 
HUBZone firm (must be certified by SBA), and/or Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned 
Small Business (must be listed in the VetBiz Vendor Information Pages). 
4. DUNS number, CAGE Code, Tax Identification Number, Unique Entity ID (UEI), 
and company structure (Corporation, LLC, partnership, joint venture, etc.).  
Companies also must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) at 
https://www.sam.gov/portal/SAM/#1 to be considered as potential sources. 
5. Identification of the firm's GSA Schedule contract(s) by Schedule number and 
contract number and SINs that are applicable to this potential requirement are also 
requested. 
6. If the company has a government approved accounting system, please identify the 
agency that approved the system. 
 
Please submit copies of any documentation such as letters or certificates to indicate the firm’s 
status (see item #3, above). 
 
Teaming arrangements are acceptable, and the information required above on the company 
responding to this announcement should also be provided for each entity expected to be 
teammates of the respondent for performance of this work.  
 
To the maximum extent possible, please submit non-proprietary information.  Any proprietary 
information submitted should be identified as such and will be properly protected from 
disclosure. This notice is for planning purposes only, and does not constitute an Invitation for 

 
 
5 
 
Bids, a Request for Proposals, a Solicitation, and a Request for Quotes, or an indication the 
Government will contract for the items contained in this announcement. This request is not to be 
construed as a commitment on the part of the Government to award a contract, nor does the 
Government intend to pay for any information submitted as a result of this request. The 
Government will not reimburse respondents for any cost associated with submission of the 
information being requested or reimburse expenses incurred to interested parties for responses to 
this announcement.  
 
Responses to this announcement will not be returned, nor will there be any ensuing discussions 
or debriefings of any responses.  However, information obtained as a result of this announcement 
may be reflected in the subsequent solicitation, and HUD, Office of the Chief Procurement 
Officer (OCPO) may contact one or more respondents for clarifications and to enhance the 
Government’s understanding.  This announcement is Government market research and may 
result in revisions in both its requirements and its acquisition strategy based on industry 
responses. RESPONDENTS MUST SUBMIT CAPABILITY STATEMENT VIA E-MAIL to 
Dwayne Gist, at dwayne.e.gist@hud.gov no later than Friday, July 10, 2026 2pm EST.

Notice of Intent to Sole Source

Pursuant to RFO 6.302-1 / RFO 5.101

Description of Requirement

The Bureau of Land Management (BLM), in coordination with the Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO), intends to award a six-month extension to the incumbent contractor for Information Technology (IT) Engineering and Operations Support (EOS) services. This extension will be executed pursuant to FAR 52.217-8 and is not within the scope of the current order.

The requirement encompasses enterprise systems engineering, cloud architecture (MS Azure), cybersecurity, UNIX/Windows system administration, enterprise network support, data storage and backup, and national data center operations at the Denver Federal Center, Lakewood, CO. 

Justification for Other Than Full and Open Competition

Statutory Authority: FAR 6.302-1 – Only One Responsible Source

Ongoing DOI enterprise IT consolidation efforts, including three Departmental Reorganization Plans (DRPs), have significantly reduced the IT support workforce responsible for enterprise-wide operations and maintenance of critical OCIO and BLM infrastructure, including systems supporting the newly established Wildland Fire Service.

DOI is currently conducting an enterprise analysis of hosting requirements—specifically the staffing levels, knowledge, skills, and abilities needed to sustain and modernize this infrastructure. Until that analysis is complete, BLM must retain all existing labor support contracts to ensure stable operations, maintain cybersecurity posture, and prevent service disruptions during this period of organizational transition.

The Acquisition Services Directorate awarded 140D0425P0154 under the procedures of FAR 19.8 and awarded a sole source 8(a) purchase order to ASRC Federal Technology Solutions, LLC. The incumbent contractor's personnel possess non-transferable, mission-specific expertise in BLM and DOI architectures, Azure implementations, legacy UNIX configurations, GSS/APSS Authorities to Operate, and security-sensitive Federal environments. Substituting alternative resources during this transitional period would introduce unacceptable risk of system instability, compliance failures, and disruption to national-level mission systems including AFMSS, MLRS, CBS, and blm.gov.

A six-month extension is necessary to preserve mission-critical support services, avoid operational risk, and provide sufficient time for DOI to complete its enterprise hosting and staffing analysis and determine a long-term sourcing strategy.

Period of Performance

Six (6) months from the current period of performance end date.

Interested Sources

This notice is not a solicitation. However, any responsible source that believes it can meet the requirement is invited to submit a capability statement to the Contracting Officer no later than the identified response date in the notice. Responses will be evaluated to determine whether full and open competition is appropriate.

Contracting Officer: Robert Brewer Interior Business Center robert_brewer@ibc.doi.gov 571-370-5697

NOTICE OF INTENT TO ISSUE A SOLE SOURCE CONTRACT FOR THE GLOBUS 
PLATFORM SOFTWARE, CONFIGURATION, TRAINING, SERVICE, AND 
DOCUMENTATION SUPPORT 
 
This Notice is issued in accordance with Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 
Overhaul (RFO) Part 5.101, Presolicitation Notice.  The U.S. Department of the Interior (DOI), 
Office of Acquisition and Property Management, Bureau of Safety and Environmental 
Enforcement/Bureau of Ocean Energy Management/Office of Surface Mining Reclamation and 
Enforcement (BSEE/BOEM/OSMRE) Programs, Acquisition Operations Branch (AOB), is the 
contracting office for this procurement. The purpose of this Notice is to announce the 
government’s intent to issue a sole source contract under the authority of RFO Part 12 to The 
University of Chicago, 455 N Cityfront Plaza Dr Ste 950, Chicago, IL 60611-5595, in 
accordance with RFO Part 6.103-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or 
Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements. 
 
BOEM has determined that the Globus Platform, a non-profit service managed by the University 
of Chicago, is the only high-performance managed data transfer solution that:  
 
 Is the only commercially available service utilizing the Globus GridFTP derived 
technology stack capable of multi Gbps reliable file movement with automated fault 
recovery; 
 Provides exclusive managed endpoints and connectors necessary for secure cross 
institutional transfers between DOI bureaus, federal High Performance Computing 
systems, and partner research institutions; 
 Holds a unique trust fabric and federated identity model integrated with academic and 
federal identity providers;  
 Is required to integrate with existing research datasets and scientific workflows 
dependent on Globus endpoints at partner institutions; and 
 Cannot be substituted with standard protocols due to:  
o Lack of automated fault recovery at scale 
o Inability to handle multi-Terabyte transfers over high latency networks 
o Lack of compatibility with established Globus based data exchanges 
 
The anticipated period of performance is 12 months from date of award. 
 
PLEASE NOTE: This notice is not a request for quote (RFQ). However, any firm that believes 
itself capable of meeting the requirement described herein may submit a capability statement or 
quotation which may be considered if received by the agency by 5:00pm Eastern Time on 14 
July 2026. All submissions in response to this notice must be submitted in writing via email to 
the Contracting Officer at david_villani@ios.doi.gov referencing 140M0126Q0037, on the 
subject line. A determination by the Government not to compete the Government’s requirements 
described in this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government.

REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) 
Business Systems Modernization Project* 
Purpose 
This Selective Service System (SSS) Request for Information (RFI) is issued solely for market 
research and acquisition planning purposes in accordance with FAR Parts 10 and 15.201. This 
RFI is not a solicitation and shall not be construed as a Request for Proposals (RFP), Invitation 
for Bids (IFB), or Request for Quotations (RFQ). The Government is not requesting proposals or 
pricing, and no contract will be awarded because of this notice. 
The Government seeks industry feedback to assist in developing an effective acquisition 
strategy, contract structure, and Contract Line-Item Number (CLIN) structure for the Business 
Systems Modernization Project. 
Responses are voluntary. The Government will not reimburse respondents for any costs 
associated with preparing or submitting a response. 
Background 
The Government has developed a draft Performance Work Statement (PWS) describing the 
required Business Systems Modernization Project. While the Government has identified the 
functional capability areas and performance requirements, it has not finalized the contract 
structure or CLIN schedule. 
The Government seeks industry recommendations regarding commercially accepted approaches 
for organizing, pricing, administering, and managing this requirement. 
*Note: This requirement was formally titled National Defense Readiness System 
Modernization and was originally published as an RFI to SAM.gov in the Feb/Mar 2026 
timeframe.  It has since been renamed as the SSS Business Systems Modernization Project.   


2 
 
Requested Industry Feedback 
The Government requests that interested parties review the attached draft PWS and provide 
recommendations addressing the following: 
Acquisition Strategy 
1. Based on the draft PWS, what contract vehicle would you recommend and why? 
Examples may include, but are not limited to: 
o Firm-Fixed-Price Contract 
o Single-Award IDIQ 
o Hybrid Contract 
o Other commercially accepted approach 
2. What are the advantages and disadvantages of your recommended contract approach? 
3. What risks should the Government consider when selecting the contract vehicle? 
CLIN Structure 
4. Based on the draft PWS, provide a recommended CLIN structure. 
5. Please identify the rationale supporting your recommended CLIN organization. 
6. Should CLINs be organized by: 
• Functional Capability Area 
• Phase of Performance (e.g., Transition, Operations, Modernization) 
• Deliverables 
• Service Categories 
• Performance Objectives 
• Other (please explain) 
7. Which services should be established as separate CLINs? 
8. Which services, if any, should be structured as sub-CLINs? 
9. Are there services that should be established as optional CLINs? 
10. Please provide a sample CLIN schedule illustrating your recommendation. 
Pricing and Administration 
11. What pricing methodology best supports this requirement? 
12. What invoicing structure would you recommend? 
13. What contract administration considerations should influence the CLIN structure? 
14. Are there best commercial practices the Government should consider when developing 
this acquisition? 
General Comments 

3 
 
15. Identify any areas of the draft PWS that could present challenges in pricing, contract 
administration, or performance management. 
16. Provide any additional recommendations that would improve the overall acquisition 
strategy. 
17. As an industry business professional, how would you structure this acquisition to 
maximize competition, simplify contract administration, and appropriately allocate 
performance risk between the Government and contractor?  Please explain your rationale. 
Response Format 
Responses from interested offerors should be concise but sufficiently detailed to explain the 
basis for each recommendation. Where practical, respondents are encouraged to provide sample 
CLIN schedules or illustrative contract structures such as the sample visual format indicated 
below. 
CLIN Description Contract Type Pricing Basis PWS Reference 
0001 Example FFP Monthly 2.1 
The Government may use the information received to refine the acquisition strategy, contract 
structure, solicitation documents, and CLIN schedule. Responses will be considered advisory 
only, and the Government reserves the right to adopt, modify, or reject any recommendation 
received. 
Submission of a response does not obligate the Government to issue a solicitation or award a 
contract.  
Government Contacts: 
Based on review of the stated requirement and the Government’s questions herein, please submit 
your response by 2:00 PM Eastern Standard Time on Monday, July 13, 2026, to:

1.0 AGENCY  
The Selective Service System (SSS) is a federal agency established under the Military Selective Service Act (MSSA), 
50 USC 3801 et seq. Its mission is to register men and maintain a system that, will rapidly provide manpower in a 
fair and just manner. The Agency carries out its statutory responsibilities through Mission Essential Functions 
(MEF). These functions are described at a high level to help industry understand the Agency operational areas.  
a. Registration: Maintaining complete and accurate registration information for individuals required 
to be registered. 
b. Selection: Conducting an impartial process to determine which eligible individuals would be selected for 
potential induction into military service.  
c. Notiﬁcation: Providing timely, reliable communication to individuals who have been selected, including 
instructions on required next steps.  
d. Delivery: Coordinating the movement of selected individuals to Military Entrance Processing Stations.  
e. Classiﬁcation: Administering a process to evaluate claims submitted by selected individuals, and assigning 
classiﬁcations  
f. Alternative Service Program: Managing a program that assigns individuals classiﬁed as Conscientious 
Objector to approved civilian work contributing to national health, safety, or welfare. 
1.1 Background  
The Selective Service System (SSS) currently operates multiple legacy systems and business processes supporting 
registration, readiness, data management, communications, reporting, and mission support functions. Many of 
these systems require modernization to improve interoperability, scalability, operational efficiency, cybersecurity, 
data governance, and long-term maintainability. 
The Government seeks to modernize and consolidate enterprise business capabilities through implementation of 
interoperable Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) technologies and associated integration, conﬁguration, 
deployment, training, sustainment, and operational support services. 
The Government intends to award a single Indeﬁnite Delivery Indeﬁnite Quantity (IDIQ) contract for services and 
capabilities within the scope of this Performance Work Statement (PWS). Task orders may be issued for discovery, 
implementation, integration, migration, sustainment, cybersecurity, analytics, operational support, or other 
related modernization activities as Government requirements evolve. 
1.2 Task Order Strategy 
The Government anticipates issuing task orders for discrete discovery, implementation, integration, migration, 
sustainment, cybersecurity, analytics, operational support, or related modernization activities within the scope of 
this PWS. 
Task orders may be structured as: 
• Discovery-only efforts intended to validate requirements, assess existing environments, identify risks, and 
support implementation planning;  
• Combined discovery and implementation efforts for well-deﬁned capability areas;  

Selective Service System - Business Systems Modernization Requirements Performance Work Statement (PWS) 
 
3 
• Implementation, enhancement, migration, sustainment, or operational support efforts informed by prior 
discovery activities.  
The Government anticipates using a phased and modular modernization approach to reduce technical, 
operational, schedule, and pricing risk associated with large-scale enterprise modernization activities. 
Initial task orders may focus on enterprise discovery, architecture assessment, requirements validation, and 
implementation planning activities intended to establish a modernization roadmap and support future 
implementation efforts. 
Subsequent task orders may include discrete capability implementation, system integration, data migration, 
analytics, cybersecurity, sustainment, or operational enhancement activities based on Government priorities and 
validated requirements. 
Speciﬁc task order scope, pricing structure, milestones, deliverables, performance requirements, and acceptance 
criteria will be deﬁned at the individual task order level.
 
2.0 SCOPE 
The Contractor shall provide all labor, materials, tools, equipment, facilities, management, supervision, and other 
resources necessary to modernize, integrate, deploy, and sustain enterprise business capabilities supporting 
Selective Service System operations. 
The solution shall support current operational requirements while maintaining the ﬂexibility and scalability 
necessary to support future mission expansion, surge operations, and national emergencies. 
The Contractor shall provide interoperable enterprise capabilities that support the full lifecycle of SSS operations, 
including but not limited to the following functional areas: 
2.1 Enterprise Registration and Data Management 
The Contractor shall provide capabilities to: 
• Ingest, validate, normalize, and manage data from authorized Federal, state, local, tribal, territorial, 
commercial, and other approved sources.  
• Maintain authoritative registrant records and associated lifecycle management processes.  
• Support structured and unstructured data collection and processing.  
• Support enterprise data governance, retention, archival, and records management requirements.  
• Provide data quality controls, auditability, traceability, and reporting capabilities.  
• Support secure automated data exchanges and API-based integrations.  
2.2 Registrant Services and Case Management 
The Contractor shall provide capabilities to: 
• Support secure registrant self-service operations.  
• Allow registrants to review, update, and manage authorized information.

• Provide workﬂow automation, notiﬁcations, correspondence management, and status tracking.  
• Maintain audit trails and records associated with registrant interactions and determinations.  
2.3 Future Operations 
The Contractor shall provide capabilities to:

• Support notiﬁcation and communication workﬂows.

• Support logistics and transportation management 
• Support personnel tracking and readiness, staffing levels, location operations, training, volunteer

• Support executive decision-making, operational oversight, and performance management.  
• Provide conﬁgurable reporting and business intelligence capabilities.

• Provide role-based access to reporting and analytical data.
