B.2  IT CONTRACT SECURITY

    VA INFORMATION AND INFORMATION SYSTEM SECURITY/PRIVACY

  1.  GENERAL

  Contractors, contractor personnel, subcontractors, and subcontractor personnel shall be subject to the same Federal laws, regulations, standards, and VA Directives and Handbooks as VA and VA personnel regarding information and information system security.

  2.  ACCESS TO VA INFORMATION AND VA INFORMATION SYSTEMS

  a.  A contractor/subcontractor shall request logical (technical) or physical access to VA information and VA information systems for their employees, subcontractors, and affiliates only to the extent necessary to perform the services specified in the contract, agreement, or task order.

  b.  All contractors, subcontractors, and third-party servicers and associates working with VA information are subject to the same investigative requirements as those of VA appointees or employees who have access to the same types of information.  The level and process of background security investigations for contractors must be in accordance with VA Directive and Handbook 0710, Personnel Suitability and Security Program.  The Office for Operations, Security, and Preparedness is responsible for these policies and procedures.

  c.  Contract personnel who require access to national security programs must have a valid security clearance.  National Industrial Security Program (NISP) was established by Executive Order 12829 to ensure that cleared U.S. defense industry contract personnel safeguard the classified information in their possession while performing work on contracts, programs, bids, or research and development efforts.  The Department of Veterans Affairs does not have a Memorandum of Agreement with Defense Security Service (DSS).  Verification of a Security Clearance must be processed through the Special Security Officer located in the Planning and National Security Service within the Office of Operations, Security, and Preparedness.

  d.  Custom software development and outsourced operations must be located in the U.S. to the maximum extent practical.  If such services are proposed to be performed abroad and are not disallowed by other VA policy or mandates, the contractor/subcontractor must state where all non-U.S. services are provided and detail a security plan, deemed to be acceptable by VA, specifically to address mitigation of the resulting problems of communication, control, data protection, and so forth.  Location within the U.S. may be an evaluation factor.

  e.  The contractor or subcontractor must notify the Contracting Officer immediately when an employee working on a VA system or with access to VA information is reassigned or leaves the contractor or subcontractor's employ. The Contracting Officer must also be notified immediately by the contractor or subcontractor prior to an unfriendly termination.

  3.  VA INFORMATION CUSTODIAL LANGUAGE

  a.  Information made available to the contractor or subcontractor by VA for the performance or administration of this contract or information developed by the contractor/subcontractor in performance or administration of the contract shall be used only for those purposes and shall not be used in any other way without the prior written agreement of the VA.  This clause expressly limits the contractor/subcontractor's rights to use data as described in Rights in Data - General, FAR 52.227-14(d) (1).

  b.  VA information should not be co-mingled, if possible, with any other data on the contractors/subcontractor's information systems or media storage systems in order to ensure VA requirements related to data protection and media sanitization can be met.  If co-mingling must be allowed to meet the requirements of the business need, the contractor must ensure that VA's information is returned to the VA or destroyed in accordance with VA's sanitization requirements.  VA reserves the right to conduct on site inspections of contractor and subcontractor IT resources to ensure data security controls, separation of data and job duties, and destruction/media sanitization procedures are in compliance with VA directive requirements.

  c.  Prior to termination or completion of this contract, contractor/ subcontractor must not destroy information received from VA, or gathered/ created by the contractor in the course of performing this contract without prior written approval by the VA.  Any data destruction done on behalf of VA by a contractor/subcontractor must be done in accordance with National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) requirements as outlined in VA Directive 6300, Records and Information Management and its Handbook 6300.1 Records Management Procedures, applicable VA Records Control Schedules, and VA Handbook 6500.1, Electronic Media Sanitization.  Self-certification by the contractor that the data destruction requirements above have been met must be sent to the VA Contracting Officer within 30 days of termination of the contract.

  d.  The contractor/subcontractor must receive, gather, store, back up, maintain, use, disclose and dispose of VA information only in compliance with the terms of the contract and applicable Federal and VA information confidentiality and security laws, regulations and policies.  If Federal or VA information confidentiality and security laws, regulations and policies become applicable to the VA information or information systems after execution of the contract, or if NIST issues or updates applicable FIPS or Special Publications (SP) after execution of this contract, the parties agree to negotiate in good faith to implement the information confidentiality and security laws, regulations and policies in this contract.

  e.  The contractor/subcontractor shall not make copies of VA information except as authorized and necessary to perform the terms of the agreement or to preserve electronic information stored on contractor/subcontractor electronic storage media for restoration in case any electronic equipment or data used by the contractor/subcontractor needs to be restored to an operating state.  If copies are made for restoration purposes, after the restoration is complete, the copies must be appropriately destroyed.

  f.  If VA determines that the contractor has violated any of the information confidentiality, privacy, and security provisions of the contract, it shall be sufficient grounds for VA to withhold payment to the contractor or third party or terminate the contract for default or terminate for cause under Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) part 12.

  g.  If a VHA contract is terminated for cause, the associated BAA must also be terminated and appropriate actions taken in accordance with VHA Handbook 1600.01, Business Associate Agreements.  Absent an agreement to use or disclose protected health information, there is no business associate relationship.

  h.  The contractor/subcontractor must store, transport, or transmit VA sensitive information in an encrypted form, using VA-approved encryption tools that are, at a minimum, FIPS 140-2 validated.

  i.  The contractor/subcontractor's firewall and Web services security controls, if applicable, shall meet or exceed VA's minimum requirements.  VA Configuration Guidelines are available upon request.

  j.  Except for uses and disclosures of VA information authorized by this contract for performance of the contract, the contractor/subcontractor may use and disclose VA information only in two other situations: (i) in response to a qualifying order of a court of competent jurisdiction, or (ii) with VA's prior written approval.  The contractor/subcontractor must refer all requests for, demands for production of, or inquiries about, VA information and information systems to the VA contracting officer for response.

  k.  Notwithstanding the provision above, the contractor/subcontractor shall not release VA records protected by Title 38 U.S.C. 5705, confidentiality of medical quality assurance records and/or Title 38 U.S.C. 7332, confidentiality of certain health records pertaining to drug addiction, sickle cell anemia, alcoholism or alcohol abuse, or infection with human immunodeficiency virus.  If the contractor/subcontractor is in receipt of a court order or other requests for the above mentioned information, that contractor/subcontractor shall immediately refer such court orders or other requests to the VA contracting officer for response.

  l.  For service that involves the storage, generating, transmitting, or exchanging of VA sensitive information but does not require C&A or an MOU-ISA for system interconnection, the contractor/subcontractor must complete a Contractor Security Control Assessment (CSCA) on a yearly basis and provide it to the COR.

  4.  INFORMATION SYSTEM DESIGN AND DEVELOPMENT

  a.  Information systems that are designed or developed for or on behalf of VA at non-VA facilities shall comply with all VA directives developed in accordance with FISMA, HIPAA, NIST, and related VA security and privacy control requirements for Federal information systems.  This includes standards for the protection of electronic PHI, outlined in 45 C.F.R. Part 164, Subpart C, information and system security categorization level designations in accordance with FIPS 199 and FIPS 200 with implementation of all baseline security controls commensurate with the FIPS 199 system security categorization (reference Appendix D of VA Handbook 6500, VA Information Security Program).  During the development cycle a Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA) must be completed, provided to the COR, and approved by the VA Privacy Service in accordance with Directive 6507, VA Privacy Impact Assessment.

  b.  The contractor/subcontractor shall certify to the COR that applications are fully functional and operate correctly as intended on systems using the VA Federal Desktop Core Configuration (FDCC), and the common security configuration guidelines provided by NIST or the VA.  This includes Internet Explorer 7 configured to operate on Windows XP and Vista (in Protected Mode on Vista) and future versions, as required.

  c.  The standard installation, operation, maintenance, updating, and patching of software shall not alter the configuration settings from the VA approved and FDCC configuration.  Information technology staff must also use the Windows Installer Service for installation to the default "program files" directory and silently install and uninstall.

  d.  Applications designed for normal end users shall run in the standard user context without elevated system administration privileges.

  e.  The security controls must be designed, developed, approved by VA, and implemented in accordance with the provisions of VA security system development life cycle as outlined in NIST Special Publication 800-37, Guide for Applying the Risk Management Framework to Federal Information Systems, VA Handbook 6500, Information Security Program and VA Handbook 6500.5, Incorporating Security and Privacy in System Development Lifecycle.

  f.  The contractor/subcontractor is required to design, develop, or operate a System of Records Notice (SOR) on individuals to accomplish an agency function subject to the Privacy Act of 1974, (as amended), Public Law 93-579, December 31, 1974 (5 U.S.C. 552a) and applicable agency regulations.  Violation of the Privacy Act may involve the imposition of criminal and civil penalties.

  g.  The contractor/subcontractor agrees to:

    (1)   Comply with the Privacy Act of 1974 (the Act) and the agency rules and regulations issued under the Act in the design, development, or operation of any system of records on individuals to accomplish an agency function when the contract specifically identifies:

      (a)  The Systems of Records (SOR); and

      (b)  The design, development, or operation work that the contractor/ subcontractor is to perform;

        (1)   Include the Privacy Act notification contained in this contract in every solicitation and resulting subcontract and in every subcontract awarded without a solicitation, when the work statement in the proposed subcontract requires the redesign, development, or operation of a SOR on individuals that is subject to the Privacy Act; and

        (2)   Include this Privacy Act clause, including this subparagraph (3), in all subcontracts awarded under this contract which requires the design, development, or operation of such a SOR.

  h.  In the event of violations of the Act, a civil action may be brought against the agency involved when the violation concerns the design, development, or operation of a SOR on individuals to accomplish an agency function, and criminal penalties may be imposed upon the officers or employees of the agency when the violation concerns the operation of a SOR on individuals to accomplish an agency function.  For purposes of the Act, when the contract is for the operation of a SOR on individuals to accomplish an agency function, the contractor/subcontractor is considered to be an employee of the agency.

    (1)   "Operation of a System of Records" means performance of any of the activities associated with maintaining the SOR, including the collection, use, maintenance, and dissemination of records.

    (2)   "Record" means any item, collection, or grouping of information about an individual that is maintained by an agency, including, but not limited to, education, financial transactions, medical history, and criminal or employment history and contains the person's name, or identifying number, symbol, or any other identifying particular assigned to the individual, such as a fingerprint or voiceprint, or a photograph.

    (3)   "System of Records" means a group of any records under the control of any agency from which information is retrieved by the name of the individual or by some identifying number, symbol, or other identifying particular assigned to the individual.

  i.  The vendor shall ensure the security of all procure

THIS IS A NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD A  SOLE SOURCE CONTRACT, NOT A 
REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE QUOTES.  A REQUEST FOR QUOTE (RFQ) WILL 
NOT BE ISSUED AND QUOTES WILL NOT BE REQUESTED. 
 
The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) intends to award a firm fixed price sole 
source contract under the authority of FAR 12.102(a), only one source being available to meet the 
Government's needs, to: 
 
COMSOL, Inc.  
100 District Ave  
Burlington, MA 01803. 
 
The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) hereby submits a notice of intent to award 
a sole source firm  fixed price purchase order for a Software as a  Service (SaaS)  for  COMSOL 
Multiphysics  Modeling Licenses  which are used by the  National Institute for Occupational Safety and 
Health (NIOSH) section for their  Panel Design Optimization and Mine Ventilation Considerations around 
the Gas Wells project.  The licenses are required to support the agency’s activities involving the duplication 
of mining environments while examining the synthesis, and interpretation of toxicological and exposure-
related data to estimate human exposure levels and associated health effects for miners.  The  North 
American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is 541511. 
 
COMSOL Multiphysics Modeling is used for the use  of mathematical modeling that creates a 
simulation of a physical mining phenomena such as airflow, heat transfer and contaminant 
transport in underground mines. This (COTS) software product  is used f or conducting the 
numerical modeling study on a project focusing on underground coal and stone mines. The 
multiphysics nature of the physics involved in modeling the problem as well as easy sharing of the 
modeling results among different physics  is streamlined with this software.  The goal of these 
studies and projects is to generate the necessary and sufficient scientific evidence to support 
conclusions regarding potential health effects and to inform the CDC. 
The period of performance will be for one (1) 12-month base period. 
 
This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals, and no solicitation document exists for 
the requirement. This hereby constitutes a synopsis of the requirement. 
CLOSING STATEMENT 
The determination not to compete this proposed contract action  is solely within the discretion of 
the Government. Information received will normally be considered for the purpose of determining 
whether to conduct a competitive procurement. The Government will not be responsible for any 
costs incurred by responding to this notice. This is NOT a request for quotes or proposals.

DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH & HUMAN SERVICES 
Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services 
7111 Security Boulevard, Mail Stop B3-30-03 
Baltimore, Maryland 21244-1850 
 
 
Office of Acquisition and Grants Management 
 
REQUEST FOR INFORMATION  
 
Agency:   Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services 
Office: Office of the Administrator (OA) in collaboration with the Office of Acquisition and 
Grants Management (OAGM) 
Title: National Provider Directory (NPD) Work Areas A and E: Ground Truth Datasets and 
Data Aggregation, Quality & Assurance Services 
The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) as a 
means of conducting market research to determine the availability and technical ability of vendors 
regarding the establishment of a trusted, accurate, and comprehensive source of healthcare provider 
information that serves as the foundation for improved care coordination, reduced administrative 
burden, and enhanced transparency across the U.S. healthcare system. The result of this market 
research will contribute to determining the agency’s method of procuring such services in the future.    
Purpose 
A draft Statement of Objectives (SOO) including National Provider directory Ground Truth Datasets 
and Data Aggregation, Quality & Assurance Services are being provided as part of this RFI.  CMS asks 
interested vendors review the SOO and address the questions based on their experience and 
expertise.  The feedback from this RFI may be used to help refine the SOO and future Request for 
Quotation (RFQ). 
Request for Information 
THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) ONLY. This RFI is issued solely for CMS’ information 
and planning purposes. This RFI does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), RFQ, or a promise 
to issue an RFP or RFQ in the future. This RFI does not commit the Government to contract for any 
supply or service. CMS is not soliciting quotes/proposals. Respondents are advised that the U.S. 
Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this RFI; 
all costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the respondent’s expense. Not 
responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future procurement. It is the 
responsibility of the interested vendors to monitor this site for additional information pertaining to 
this requirement. Information provided in the RFI is subject to change and is not binding on the 
Government. HHS, CMS, CM or OAGM have not made a commitment to procure any of the items or 
services discussed, and release of this RFI is not a commitment or an authorization to incur cost for 
which reimbursement would be allowed or sought. All submissions become Government property 
and will not be returned. 
Responses to this RFI shall be submitted by July 10, 2026, via email to the Contracting Officer, Alex 
Jarema at alex.jarema@cms.hhs.gov and the Contract Specialist, Walker Hare at 


 
 
walker.hare@cms.hhs.gov in a format that is readable in Microsoft Word or Adobe PDF formats. CMS 
will not accept hard-copy responses or other formats. CMS will consider only those responses that 
contain the information described below in the format requested.  Respondents are requested to 
provide a response to this RFI that includes three sections as follows below. 
 
Section I. General Vendor Information  
• Organization Name 
• Unique Entity Identification (UEI) 
• Business Size and Small Business subcategory if applicable 
• Mailing address  
• Name, title, phone number and e-mail address of designated point of contact  
• Provide a description of any licenses, specific expertise, any General Services 
Administration (GSA) credentials (if applicable), and information that is relevant 
to this RFI. 
• Active GSA MAS, GWAC, or other government contract vehicles (list vehicle 
number and expiration) 
Section II. The name and contact information of the organization whose views are represented in 
the submission, if different from the information provided in Section I.  
Section III.  Respondents are encouraged to provide complete but concise responses to the 
questions listed below. Please note that a response to every question is not required.  
For each question or remark, please include reference to the specific section(s) of the 
SOO to which the question/feedback applies following the format below (i.e., the 
format below assumes a table with columns associated with each element).  
Contractors should use a file format that will facilitate CMS merging questions from 
multiple respondents into a single file.

sources across multiple categories. For each data category below, indicate:  
(a) whether you ARE the authoritative source for this data, whether you HAVE an 
active agreement with the authoritative source, or both;  
(b) whether federal government use is permitted;

For state licensing boards specifically: list the number of states for which you currently are the source or 
hold active data access agreements. 
**Note on sensitive fields: CMS understands that some data fields may be used for internal validation 
purposes only and may not be appropriate for public publication. Please flag any such fields in the final 
column — this will help CMS design appropriate data handling and publication policies. 
2. A core requirement for this contract is that all data licensing agreements must permit CMS to 
freely redistribute reconciled NPD data without downstream licensing obligations on end 
users. CMS recognizes that achieving this in practice may require negotiating field-level 
publication terms — some data fields within an otherwise licensable dataset may be 
appropriate for internal validation use only and may not be appropriate for public publication 
due to sensitivity, commercial restrictions, or legal constraints. 
 
Describe a specific engagement in which you negotiated a data licensing agreement that 
explicitly permitted a federal government client to freely redistribute or publicly publish 
derived data. Your response should address: 
 
(a) What type of data source was involved? What specific licensing restriction did you 
encounter? How did you resolve it and what was the outcome? 
 
(b) Were there any fields within the dataset that could not be publicly published even 
after successful negotiation — for example, due to sensitivity, commercial restrictions, 
or state legal constraints? If so, how did you handle the distinction between fields that 
could be published and fields that could only be used internally? 
 
(c) If you have encountered situations where full license-free redistribution was not 
achievable but partial redistribution was negotiated — covering most but not all fields 
— describe how you structured that arrangement and how you ensured that restricted 
fields were not inadvertently included in public output. 
(d) If you have not negotiated this type of agreement before, describe how you would 
approach it for the data categories listed in Question 1, including how you would 
identify and handle fields that may be sensitive or legally restricted from public 
publication. 
3. Work Area A requires Initial Operating Capability within 30 days of award — defined as 
normalized data files delivered to CMS-designated storage for at least five (5) ground truth 

 
 
sources, with all priority sources in active negotiation. 
 
(a) State licensing boards are highly fragmented across 50+ jurisdictions. Describe 
your experience managing data relationships with state licensing boards at scale. How 
many active state board relationships do you currently hold? What is the most 
significant obstacle you have encountered in establishing a state board data agreement 
and how did you resolve it? 
 
(b) Based on your existing agreements, which specific sources could you have 
operational within 30 days of award? What would you do before award to prepare, 
and what is the primary risk to the 30-day timeline? 
 
(b) Are the IOC timelines realistic — 30 days for Work Area A and 45 days for Work 
Area E? If not, what would you recommend? 
 
4. Work Area E is an outcome-based framework. CMS anticipates evaluating vendors on the 
measurable quality of their data corrections — not on correction volume. WA E operates at 
both ends of the NPD data lifecycle: validating data quality as it enters the pipeline from 
ground truth sources AND validating the accuracy of data published in the public-facing 
directory, with findings fed back to improve ground truth sourcing decisions. 
 
(a) Describe a specific, production-scale engagement in which you delivered 
documented improvements to provider directory data accuracy. Include: the starting 
baseline, the types of errors corrected, the quantified outcome, the scale (number of 
records), and the methodology used. PoC or pilot results alone are not sufficient — 
describe a production deployment. 
 
(b) Have you assessed data quality at both the input end (data entering a pipeline) and 
the output end (data published to end users) for the same client? If yes, describe that 
engagement. If no, describe how you would approach it for NPD. 
 
(c) What correction acceptance rates have you achieved in prior engagements? 
Provide specific data. How do you ensure your methodology does not generate high 
volumes of low-quality corrections? Can you fully document your methodology — 
including any AI/ML model specifications — in a format CMS can review, audit, and 
own? Are there proprietary elements that could not be transferred to a successor 
contractor? 
 
5. Based on your review of the draft SOO: 
 
(a) Are there significant gaps, ambiguities, or over-specifications in the SOO that CMS should 
address before solicitation release? 
 
(b) Is the license-free output mandate achievable across all data categories described? Are 
there specific categories where this would be particularly difficult or costly — including 
categories where only partial field-level redistribution may be achievable? 
 

 
 
(c) Does the boundary between Work Area A and Work Area E make sense from an industry 
perspective? Are there aspects of the scope that are difficult to separate cleanly between the 
two work areas? 
 
(d) Are there any aspects of the scope that would significantly limit competition? 
 
6. What is the estimated market cost range for services of this nature, and what factors most 
significantly drive cost variability for an effort of this scope? Your response should include an 
estimated annual cost range for WA A (data sourcing and licensing) and WA E (aggregation 
and quality assurance) separately.

Statement of Requirements 
Annual Subscription for up to 50,000 Potential Subscribers 
GovDelivery Digital Communication Management Tool 
Naval Postgraduate School 
 
1.0 Background/Introduction:  
The Naval Postgraduate School (NPS) has a requirement to procure the brand-name GovDelivery platform, 
manufactured by Granicus, to satisfy public-sector digital communications and outreach requirements for up 
to 50,000 potential subscribers. GovDelivery provides the required capability to support targeted 
stakeholder engagement, subscriber management, and official communications with current and prospective 
audiences aligned with the NPS mission. As a Department of Defense activity, NPS requires cloud-based 
services that comply with applicable cybersecurity and authorization requirements, including FedRAMP 
certification and Defense Information Systems Agency approval. GovDelivery meets these mandatory 
requirements as a FedRAMP-certified and DISA-approved email marketing service provider. 
 
Since 2019, NPS has utilized the GovDelivery Digital Management Tool to support official 
communications, including targeted emails, bulletins, and audience-specific messages distributed to 
restricted and unlisted topics. The existing capability supports continuity of communications with current 
and future stakeholders and enables NPS to manage a subscriber base of approximately 26,000 users 
annually over the last five years. Based on projected growth over the anticipated ordering period, the 
requirement shall support scalability up to, but not exceeding, 50,000 potential subscribers. 
 
GovDelivery is a public-sector communications platform that provides the minimum required functionality 
for NPS stakeholder outreach and engagement. Any acceptable solution must meet the Government’s 
technical, operational, and cybersecurity requirements, including FedRAMP certification and DISA 
approval for cloud-based services. GovDelivery satisfies these salient characteristics and is authorized for 
use as a compliant email marketing service provider. 
 
GovDelivery is manufactured by Granicus through Carahsoft.

ATTACHMENT 1

STATEMENT OF REQUIREMENT

U.S. NMRTC SIGONELLA

GLUCOMETERS AND ABBOTT I-STAT ANALYZERS RALS

 DATA MANAGEMENT SYSTEM 

(Brand Name or Equal)

ORGANIZATION:  U.S. Navy Medicine Readiness and Training Command Sigonella is responsible for providing the U.S. Navy, other military branches, and their military families with reliable quality health care.  In addition, USNMRTC Sigonella is responsible for preparing for deployable support of operational forces and caring for their beneficiaries.

BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE:  In order to provide the expected standard of care for patients who receive their healthcare services at NMRTC Sigonella, the hospital shall be capable of providing certain point of care waived laboratory tests that are performed on a routine or emergent basis. Point of care testing is vital in the detection and monitoring of cardiac arrest, diabetes, electrolytes, renal function, blood gas and various other analyses that are essential in the treatment of pathologic processes. Some of these tests are vital to the expeditious screening and timely treatment of acute disease such as myocardial infarction and organ failure, the ability to perform testing at the treatment facility is paramount. 

Point of Care Testing devices require a software interface system that connects point-of-care test results and instruments to the MHS Genesis health record system and has been authorized by Defense Health Agency to operate on DoD networks. This authorization allows for the successful transfer of critical clinical information into patient electronic health records to allow for continued and safe patient care. The contractor shall perform installation, implementation, training and maintenance support for a data management system for Point of Care Testing.

GENERAL REQUIREMENTS:  The effort required hereunder shall be performed in accordance with this Statement of Work and with all other terms and conditions set forth herein.

SCOPE:  The contractor shall perform all tasks, including interface development, remotely through an already existing Virtual Private Network (VPN) connection between the current system and the Customer’s network. Services include managing the overall implementation, organizing the necessary resources to provide technical guidance, installation, testing, support for system configuration, on-site and/or virtual training and annual technology license for the system.

The contractor shall provide all training, services, materials and equipment necessary for the operation/repair/maintenance of the Rals Data Management System with the Glucose Module and the Abbott ISTAT Module located in the Laboratory at U.S. Navy Medicine Readiness and Training Command and the Souda Bay Clinic to ensure dependable and reliable equipment operation. The scope of work performed under these specifications includes the furnishing of all labor, and parts to perform all repairs on equipment listed, to ensure continued operation at their designed efficiency and capacity. 

PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE:

The period of performance shall be for base plus 4 options years:

Base Year: TBD 

Option Year 1: TBD 

Option Year 2: TBD

Option Year 3: TBD

Option Year 4: TBD

SPECIFIC REQUIREMENTS:  

Basic Services: Vendor shall provide software, software license, maintenance, and technical support on the data management system. 

•Interface between Point of Care testing analyzers and MHS Genesis. 

•Create and edit profiles in data management system to match Laboratory MHS Genesis test files. 

•Allow operator ID and information to be listed in system’s database. 

•Contractor shall provide all software maintenance releases as soon as possible after release but no later than 14 days after release. 

•All supplied software shall be certified free of malicious codes/damaging properties such as viruses, Trojan horses, worms, spyware etc. 

•All technical support personnel must be adequately trained and knowledgeable of supplied software.

Glucose Analyzers:  For a total quantity of six instruments – contractor must provide the customer with the ability to manage all glucose analyzers device support to the data management system, provide the Customer with the ability to manage all the devices, patient results, operator certifications, and Quality Control testing from a single Point of Care data manager for US NMRTC Sigonella and the Souda Bay Clinic. The Glucometer results shall also be added to the current LIS (laboratory interface system), MHS Genesis. 

Abbott i-STAT Analyzers: For a total quantity of five instruments – contractor must provide the customer with the ability to manage all i-STAT devices, patient results, operator certifications, and Quality Control testing from a single Point of Care data manager for US NMRTC Sigonella and the Souda Bay Clinic. The i-STAT results shall also be added to the current LIS (laboratory interface system), MHS Genesis.

CYBERSECURITY: Contractors shall be responsible for providing CYBERSECURITY maintenance support for as long as the contractor commercially supports the system/device. Contractor shall have a valid Authority to Operate (ATO) prior to installation. 

AUTHORITY TO OPERATE: Contractor shall ensure that the contractor’s device or system maintains its ATO or operating system platform and patches/updates for as long as the contractor commercially supports the system/device. 

PERFORMANCE REQUIREMENTS SUMMARY: The contractor service requirements are summarized into performance objectives that relate directly to mission essential items. The performance threshold briefly describes the minimum acceptable levels of service required for each requirement. These thresholds are critical to mission success.

The contractor shall provide 24/7 uninterrupted software service with zero downtime. all patient results must successfully transmit to electronic health records (MHS Genesis) 100% of the time.

The contractor shall provide software updates as needed to ensure zero interruptions to patient care. - All patient results are successfully transmitted to electronic health records (MHS Genesis) 100% of the time.

      PREVENTIVE MAINTENANCE:

	Perform service repair/maintenance to industry standards.

	Ensure that only FULLY QUALIFIED FIELD ENGINEERS and TECHNICIANS who have gone through original equipment manufacturer (OEM) or comparable third-party service schools for the above mentioned equipment, shall be employed in the performance of any and all work performed under this contract.  Upon request, the contractor shall provide training certificates (or notarized copies) to the Medical Repair Branch for verification.  The highest standard of professional capability and electrical/mechanica1 workmanship is to be maintained throughout the life of this contract.

	Make repairs to the extent necessary (as determined by inspection tests or disassembly) to ensure a functional system that will efficiently serve its intended purpose.

	CORRECTIVE MAINTENANCE: Correct inoperable condition in a timely manner.  Immediately upon contract award, the contractor shall provide Medical Repair Branch an emergency telephone number.  Contractor shall respond no later than eight (8) hours after telephone notification.

	Provide only the work necessary to restore the equipment to a serviceable/operating condition by adjustments, replacement parts, or minor repairs when it is determined that extensive repairs and parts replacements are not necessary.

	Equipment improvements/modifications shall be made only upon Medical Repair Branch written approval and direction.

	Notify the Medical Repair Branch immediately upon receipt of OEM or replacement parts/equipment safety recalls notices.

	Insure that original design and functional capabilities will not be changed, modified, or altered unless the Medical Repair Branch authorizes such changes.

	Provide suitable OEM recommended repair equipment/tools required for the satisfactory execution of all repairs made.

	Furnish manufacturer OEM approved lubricants and lubricate wear points within the equipment.

	Extend to the Government all commercial warranties on replacement parts, consistent with standard industry practices.

	Maintain an adequate spare parts inventory.

TITLE TO EQUIPMENT: The contractor shall not assume possession or control of any part of the equipment.  The Government retains ownership to title thereof.

LIABILITY:   The contractor shall not be liable for any loss, damage, or delay due to any cause beyond his reasonable control including but not limited to, acts of government, strikes, lockouts, fire, explosion, theft, floods, riot, civil commotion, war, malicious mischief or acts of God.

UTILITIES:   The contractor may use Government utilities, (e.g., electrical power, compressed air, and water) that are available and required for any service performed under this contract.  The building engineer, to ensure compatibility with the NMRTC Sigonella electrical wiring and equipment, must approve contractor electrical equipment.

 

GOVERNMENT PERSONNEL: U.S. NMRTC Sigonella employees will not perform maintenance, or attempt repairs to equipment while such equipment is under the purview of this contract unless agreed to in writing by the contractor.

SECURITY REQUIREMENTS: Contractor will be required to contact the U.S. NMRTC Sigonella laboratory department to be sponsored or request base access and wait at the main gate for an escort.

FIELD SERVICE REPORTS: Contractor must provide a written or electronic Field Service Report (FSR) and Certification in the English Language and to include the following: 

Contractor Name

Identification of the equipment serviced: ECN (Equipment Code Number) 

Serial Number 

Type of service/tests performed

Technician's Printed Name

Telephone Number 

Signature and Date

Time of Arrival Time Expended Repairing/Service

Labor Hours, Rate and Materials 

Summary of Work Performed

Accepted by End-User (Government Representative's Printed Name and Signature). 

All Field Service Reports shall be submitted within 72 hours of completion of service.

PARTS AVAILABILITY: To ensure minimal equipment downtime, the contractor shall maintain replacement repair parts and materials necessary to perform each repair or supply said parts and materials within three (3) days.

 

COMPENSATION:

Labor: All compensation for labor is included in the contract price. 

Parts and materials: All compensation for parts and materials is included in contract price.

Parts/Supplies Quality: Parts and Supplies provided under this contract shall be guaranteed to be equal in all respects, including performance, interchangeability, durability and quality to the OEM parts when new or as presently recommended by the manufacturer. 

INVOICE AND PAYMENTS INSTRUCTION:

The Contractor is required to submit certified invoices conform to the contract line-item number structure of this contract and must include banking information (IBAN CODE) to:

U.S. NMRTC Sigonella, Italy

SS 192 Km 76

95100 Catania

Attn: Material Management Department

Phone: 095-564930 Fax: 095-564583

Invoices shall be in the name of the Contractor and not any agent or a subcontractor. It will contain the following information:  contract number, order number and item number as listed herein, identification of services, quantities, unit price and extended total price.  The Contractor or his authorized representative will sign only the original of each invoice.  If the invoices are signed or received in the name of a company or corporation the name of the person signing, as well as the capacity in which he signs, must appear.

Invoice must include your bank account info and the following statement in English and Italian:

"Transaction not subject to tax in accordance with Art. 72, comma 1, Lettera b) del D.P.R. 26 October 1972, No. 633"

"Operazione non imponibile ai sensi dell'Art. 72, primo comma, Lettera b), DPR 26 Ottobre 1972, No. 633" 

Contractor shall maintain original paid invoices and other related records for the length of the contract plus one year and Contractor shall make historical invoicing data available to the government within ten (10) business days of a formal request.  Archived information shall be provided in a mutually acceptable format.

Payment will be made in Euro by the Disbursing Officer, U.S. Naval Support Activity, Naples.  Payment will be made as soon as possible after acceptance of the supplies or performance of the services. The Government will only pay for those supplies and services, or portions thereof, which have been accepted. Partial payments are authorized.  Invoices not in compliance with these instructions are not considered to be proper invoices and may be rejected.

Upon receipt of accepted and certified invoices, payment will be made by Commercial Bill Pay Office (CBPO) Naples Tel. (TBD)

-End-

Sources Sought Notice Number: IHS1527539 
This Sources Sought is to determine the availability of Indian Small Businesses Economic 
Enterprises (ISBEEs), Indian Economic Enterprises (IEEs),and other small businesses capable of 
performing the requirement. 
This is a Sources Sought notice. This notice DOES NOT constitute a request for proposal, request for 
quote or invitation for bid. This Sources Sought is a market research tool being utilized to determine the

No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this 
announcement. All responses will be provided by an e-mail response. No presentations will be scheduled. 
Your responses to the requested information will help the Government determine the appropriate 
acquisition method, including whether a set-aside is possible. The anticipated applicable NAICS code for 
this acquisition is 541519 (Other Computer Related Services); however, other relevant NAICS codes will 
be considered based on the responses received. 
 
1.0 BACKGROUND 
 
Firm Fixed-Price, Non-Personal Service Type, Commercial Service contract to provide IT Services for 
the Great Plains Area Office, Office of Information Technology, Aberdeen, South Dakota. 
 
2.0 OBJECTIVE 
 
The objective of this requirement is to maintain uninterrupted access to the InformaCast mass notification 
system through a one-year maintenance and support subscription that provides software updates, technical 
support, and continued compatibility with the existing telecommunications environment. 
 
3.0 SCOPE 
 
See the attached Performance Work Statement (PWS). 
4.0 CONTRACT REQUIREMENTS/ AND PERSONNEL QUALIFICATIONS 
 
The contractor is required to comply with all federal, state, and local requirements applicable to Other 
Computer Related Services. 
  
5.0 TYPE OF ORDER 
 
This is a Firm Fixed-Price (FFP) contract.

Period of Performance: date of award, plus one (1) year.  
 

 Sources Sought Number IHS1527539 - 2

- Great Plains Area Office, Office of Information Technology, 115 4th Avenue, SE, Aberdeen, 
South Dakota 57401. 
 
8.0 PAYMENT 
 
INVOICE SUBMISSION AND PAYMENT  
 
In compliance with the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) M-15-19 memorandum Improving 
Government Efficiency and Saving Taxpayer Dollars Through Electronic Invoicing, directing Federal 
agencies to adopt electronic invoicing as the primary means to disburse payment to vendors. Invoices 
submitted under any award resulting from this solicitation will be required to utilize the Invoice 
Processing Platform (IPP) in accordance with HHSAR 352.232-71, Electronic Submission and Processing 
of Payment Requests.  
 
IPP is a secure, web-based electronic invoicing system provided by the U.S. Department of the Treasury's 
Bureau of the Fiscal Service in partnership with the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRSTL). 
Respondents to this solicitation are encouraged to register an account with IPP if they have not already 
done so. If your organization is registered to use IPP, you do not need to re-register. However, we 
encourage you to ensure your organization and designated IPP user accounts are valid and up to date. The

Please contact the IPP Helpdesk at (866) 973- 3131 (M-F 8 AM to 6 PM ET) or

InformaCast Maintenance and Support Renewal  
Office of Information Technology  
Great Plains Area  Indian Health Service, Aberdeen, South Dakota 
1. Background  
The Great Plains Area Office of Information Technology utilizes InformaCast as its 
enterprise mass notiﬁcation system integrated with the existing Voice over Internet 
Protocol (VoIP) infrastructure. The system provides critical emergency notiﬁcation 
capabilities, operational messaging, and safety communications across healthcare 
facilities, including hospitals and clinics. 
Continued maintenance and support are required to ensure the availability, reliability, 
security, and functionality of the InformaCast platform. 
2. Objective  
The objective of this requirement is to maintain uninterrupted access to the InformaCast 
mass notiﬁcation system through a one-year maintenance and support subscription that 
provides software updates, technical support, and continued compatibility with the 
existing telecommunications environment. 
3. Scope  
The contractor shall provide all services, subscriptions, software maintenance, upgrades, 
patches, and technical support necessary to maintain the operational capability of the 
existing InformaCast system and all currently licensed endpoints throughout the period of 
performance. 
The contractor shall ensure that the system remains fully supported, secure, and 
functional without degradation of service.

Performance Work Statement (PWS): Enterprise Skills Assessment Platform:

1.  Introduction and Background. 

     a.  Mission Objective: The United States Army Special Operations Command (USASOC), hereafter referred to as "the Government," requires a commercially available Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) solution to systematically assess, measure, and guide the upskilling of its technical workforce. The primary objective is to enhance mission readiness by identifying and closing skill gaps in critical domains such as Artificial Intelligence (AI), Data Engineering, Cybersecurity, and Software Development. This PWS defines the performance outcomes required to achieve this objective.

     b.  Scope: The Contractor shall provide the platform, including all necessary licenses, technical support, and reporting to meet the performance standards outlined herein. The scope includes platform provisioning, user onboarding, role-based skills assessment, data analytics, and ongoing technical support for 500 users.

     c.  Period of Performance (PoP): The PoP shall be for one Base Year of 12 months.

          (1)  Base Period: 15 July 2026 to 14 July 2027

2.  Definitions and Acronyms.  A complete list of definitions and acronyms will be included in Appendix 1.

     a.  AQL: Acceptable Quality Level

     b.  COR: Contracting Officer's Representative

     c.  DoW: Department of War

     d.  PII: Personally Identifiable Information

      e.  PRS: Performance Requirements Summary

     f.  PWS: Performance Work Statement

     g.  QASP: Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan

     h.  Skill Circuit: A tailored assessment path for a specific job role or technical domain within the platform.

3.  Government Furnished Property, Material, Equipment and Services

     a.  Government Furnished Services: The Government will provide access to necessary points of contact (POCs) for technical coordination and subject matter experts (SMEs) for the Skill Circuit customization task. 

     b.  Government Furnished Equipment: No Government Furnished Equipment (GFE) will be provided.

4. Contractor Requirements.  Tasks and Performance Objectives: 

     a.  Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) and Performance Requirements Summary (PRS).  The Contractor is responsible for delivering the outcomes defined in the table below. The Government will measure performance against these standards in accordance with the Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan (QASP).

     b.  Specific Tasks

          (1)  Task 1: Platform Provisioning and Onboarding. The Contractor shall initialize the Government's enterprise tenant, configure it with 500 licenses, and provide administrative accounts to designated Government POCs. The Contractor shall also deliver user onboarding guides and training materials.

          (2)  Task 2: Skill Circuit Customization. The Contractor shall collaborate with Government SMEs to review and calibrate the following initial Skill Circuits to meet mission requirements:

          (a)  Artificial Intelligence (AI) / Machine Learning (ML) Engineer

          (b)  Data Engineer (Python, SQL, MSL, R)

          (c)  Cybersecurity Analyst

          (d)  Software Engineer (Python/C++)

          (e)  Cloud Architect

          (f)  Data Analyst (Python, SQL, MSL, R)

          (3)  Task 3: Reporting and Analytics. The Contractor shall provide the COR with a Quarterly Skills Gap Analysis Report and a Final Performance and Usage Summary as specified in the Deliverables section.

5.  Deliverables. 

     a.  D001 – Initial tenant access and admin accounts, within five business days of award.

     b.  D002 – User onboarding guide and training materials, within 10 business days of award.

     c.  D003 – Skill Circuit Calibration Plan (for approval), within 15 business days of award.

     d.  D004 – Quarterly Skills Gap Analysis Report, every 90 days after PoP start.

     e.  D005 – Final performance and usage summary, 30 days prior to PoP expiration.

6.  Security and Compliance.  The platform shall adhere to all relevant security protocols. The system must not store or process unauthorized PII. The platform shall maintain compliance with Section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act for accessibility.

Platform Availability | Ensure the SaaS platform is operational and accessible to all licensed users globally. | 99.9% uptime per month (excluding pre-scheduled maintenance). | Automated system monitoring logs; Periodic Government spot checks.

User Account Provisioning | Provision new user accounts and licenses upon Government request. | 100% of valid user account requests provisioned within 48 business hours. | Review of user provisioning reports; User feedback.

Skill Circuit Calibration | Calibrate standard Skill Circuits to align with DoW job roles and operational needs. | Initial calibration for all specified roles delivered and approved by the Government within 30 days of contract award. | Government SME review and formal acceptance.

Technical Support | Provide effective and timely resolution for all user-submitted technical support tickets. | 95% of critical tickets resolved within 24 business hours; 90% of all other tickets resolved within 72 business hours. | Review of Contractor-provided helpdesk metric reports.

Performance Reporting | Deliver accurate and timely reports on platform usage, user progress, and aggregated skill analytics. | 100% of required reports delivered on time by the 5th business day of each new quarter. | COR review and acceptance of deliverables.

2.  Contract Title. Legacy Application Software and Development Support

3.  Background.  

The Defense Information Systems Agency (DISA), a Combat Support Agency, engineers and provides command and control capabilities and enterprise infrastructure to continuously operate and assure a global net-centric enterprise. DISA directly supports joint warfighters, national level leaders, and other mission and coalition partners across the full spectrum of operations.  DISA’s Procurement Services Directorate (PSD) purchases telecommunications and information technology (IT) products and services for the military, other Defense Agencies, and Federal Organizations.

The primary legacy systems include the Contract Support System (CSS), Contractual Online Procurement System (COPS), Financial Accounting and Budget System (FABS), and the Defense Information Technology Contracting Organization (DITCO) Web.  Other subsystems include but are not limited to: Rates and Tariffs File System (RTFS), Joint Hawaii Information Transfer System (JHITS), and the Delivery Ticket Invoicing (DTI) process.

CSS is a web-based application used by the contracting staff and budget analysts to enter procurement, funding, contractor and user information.  CSS provides standard reporting and tracking capability of procurement, funding, contractor information using a central Oracle database.  Specific modules within CSS are Procurement Information (PI), Customer/Contractor Information (CCI), Telecommunications Status Information (TSI), Employee/User Identification (ID) Information, and Exception Handler. Related CSS modules include but are not limited to all application, processes, and details of pertinent information related to these services. Many of the related CSS modules execute from the File Transfer Protocol (FTP) server within the adTempus scheduler. Examples of related CSS modules include, for instance:

COPS IOS application

CSS TSI Document Processor application (to include the maintaining the DITCO Automatic Digital Network System mailbox)

CSS Telecommunication Status Information (TSI) Exception Handler lite application

CSS TSI Status of Acquisition Messages (SAMs) Email / Electronic Document Management System (EDMS) / Web application

CSS TSI SAMs Import application

CSS TSI Telecom Macros

CSS TSI Tech Refresh (TR) / SAMs Import/Distributor application

CSS Admin Tool consisting of Employee/User Identification (ID) Information and Customer/Contractor Information (CCI)

DITCO Web is the PSD contract tracking system used to track status of contracts awarded as well as requirements in process, monitor and assign workload, and ensure new awards and modifications are processed in a timely manner.

Related modules include but are not limited to:

CSS Reports

Web Email Import

WebPost application

COPS is an online and batch processing system used to establish, manage, change or discontinue telecommunication services and equipment.  An Inventory of Service (IOS) is a detail of pertinent information related to those services and equipment.  COPS records contain data fields describing service, location, equipment, mileage, and costs.  Batch applications are used to generate the IOS and other reports.  COPS will be phased out as SD2 migrates to an approved, modernized system using a Migrate/Sync web service.

FABS supports both vendor payment and customer billing.  Monthly reports are produced and are provided to Joint Enterprise Services Directorate (JESD)/DISA’s customers.  Customer billing data consists of monthly recurring charges, non-recurring charges, DISA managed program charges, overhead charges and other billing type information.  Information from FABS is used by customers to plan, program, budget, and execute funds.  Additionally, FABS provides data to the Financial Accounting Management Information System (FAMIS) General Ledger Subsystem so that DISA/ Resource Management (RM) can manage its internal telecommunications budgets and produce financial statements.  FABS also manages and tracks the financial aspects (e.g. accounts payables, vendor invoices, vouchers) associated with telecommunication circuits, equipment and services leased from various vendors on behalf of the Government through the Defense Wide Working Capital Fund (DWCF) / Telecommunications

Services and Enterprise Acquisition Services (TSEAS) Inventory and Billing Information (TIBI).  The contractor shall ensure that DISA’s customers are billed for services provided and vendors are paid according to Account Payable limits for services on behalf of the customer.  

RTFS is a mainframe application used to update equipment, mileage, and location records in COPS files based upon Federal Communications Commission (FCC) tariff regulations.  Updates reflect carrier changes, circuit reconfigurations, Number Plan Area (NPA) Code splits (e.g., area code 314 split into area codes 314 and 636).  New rates are provided by vendor price changes, contract price changes and subscriber rate changes.  RTFS also provides inquiry capability to verify current and historical circuit prices.  

JHITS is a contract that provides telecommunications service for the Hawaiian Islands.  In order to accomplish Customer Billing and Vendor Payment (i.e., DTI), all service orders are interfaced between the commercial provider’s system and the COPS.

EDMS (Electronic Document Management System) is a system used for the secure storage, retrieval, and management of electronic documents. Support for EDMS is limited. See PWS Section 6.4.2 for additional details.

4.  Objectives:  The objective of this requirement is to provide technical and development support Database Administration (DBA) support and System Administration (SA) for the contracting and financial management legacy systems. This is a follow-on effort to sustain the current portfolio of legacy systems. SD2 manages and operates a complex group of software applications across a wide range of computing environments, including, mainframe and web-based. This technical and development, DBA and SA support is essential to maintain legacy applications.  Analysis of the legacy systems and the data that resides within them will be required as part of the integration effort with related business systems.  

Integration support shall include accommodating the Defense Procurement and Acquisition Policy (DPAP) business systems office’s Clause Logic Service (CLS) Application Program Interface (API) as it evolves, maintaining existing integrations (e.g. Federal Procurement Data System – Next Generation (FPDS-NG), Global Exchange (GEX)/Electronic Document Access (EDA), etc.), and establishing new or updated integrations for IDEAS and TSEAS as DISA modernizes its other business systems (e.g. Oracle Financials integration using the Purchase Request Data Standard (PRDS)). Legacy production support shall include troubleshooting and resolving user problems and identification of opportunities to improve processes or business process models in the system. Overall, software development support shall include all aspects of the Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) necessary to sustain and modify the system baseline.  The legacy software development contractors shall work closely with other members of the team to include Government developers, SAs, DBAs, hosting, security, mission partners and end-users. The description of each skill for this effort is provided in section 6 of this PWS under the Tasks.

5.  Scope.  

The Government may require surge support during the base or any option period, and surge modifications will be within the scope of the contract and provide increased support for the defined task areas of this PWS. Surge support over the life of the contract will not exceed TBD% of the contractor’s total proposed cost/price for the base and all option periods, excluding any six-month extension of services pursuant to FAR 52.217-8.

The contractor shall provide technical and software development support for DISA’s Business Systems Portfolio Management Office (PMO). The contractor shall provide a solution and product consulting and programming to:

(1) Receive and respond to problems reported by the users (i.e., correct Tier 2 incidents).  This support shall address issues with the core legacy systems and involve transactions and indirect dependencies that occur between legacy systems, the Data Integration (DI) server, TIBI, EDMS, DISA Storefront (DSF), Integrated Defense Enterprise Acquisition System (IDEAS), and other systems as indicated in the “System Integrations” paragraph list. 

(2) Provide Tier 2 and Tier 3 centralized development support, database support and SA for the contracting and financial management legacy systems. 

(3) Sustain deployed capabilities in the legacy systems by rapidly troubleshooting and resolving software    issues impeding the execution of deployed contracting capability (i.e., correct Tier 3 defects); 

(4) Develop, test and implement change requests to include existing Visual Basic 6.0 (VB6) applications conversion to Web, .net, or appropriate solutions.

(5) Develop and implement new system capabilities.

(6) Provide technical expertise to ensure high availability of the legacy systems to meet the DISA mission. 

(7) Maintain and update system documentation such as Standard Operating Procedures.

(8) Create the necessary documentation for decommission.

(9) Modernize and sustain the existing application, data structures, system integrations, and reporting capabilities.

The activities listed above are in support of the legacy contracting and financial systems which involve transactions between IDEAS, TIBI, FAMIS-WCF and DISA StoreFront.  The contractor shall provide support to approximately 700-person primary contracting user base, which include personnel in three general locations, Europe – 10% (which includes Southwest Asia), continental United States – 80%, and Pacific region – 10%.  Each field office has technical support personnel who are responsible for most Tier 1 activities (e.g., client PC operation, network connectivity).  The contractor shall provide remote tier 2 and 3 technical support to all users, worldwide.  Different types of contracting users will conduct different types and amounts of transactions in the contracting systems, and consequently will have different levels of impact on support.

The contractor shall modernize and sustain the existing application, system integrations, and reporting capabilities. These areas are comprised of distinct key applications and operational capabilities that include:

Telecom Contracting

Orders against Indefinite Delivery (ID) Contracts Inquiry Quote Order (IQO) Contracting

FAMIS-WCF

Sam.gov

Standard Financial Information Structure (SFIS) United States Standard General Ledger (USSGL)

Reporting and Metrics 

Standard Reports

Ad-hoc Reports and Queries

Data Warehouse

6.  Performance Requirements.  

6.1.	Task 1 – Contract Management.  The contractor shall provide the planning, direction, coordination, and control necessary to accomplish all requirements in this PWS. The contractor shall designate key personnel responsible for the schedule and technical performance of the contract and shall serve as a primary Points-of-Contact for both management and technical matters. In addition, the contractor shall participate in monthly Program Management Review meetings where the status of the work and associated deliverables are reviewed in the context of the business processes supported by the system. 

The contract Management Plan, submitted as part of the contractor’s proposal, shall be updated as changes occur or upon request from the Government.

The TOMP shall include at a minimum:

This activity requires IT II, as authorized access is required to access the production, development, and test environments.  In response to this effort, the contractor shall submit an appropriate staffing plan commensurate with their technical approach to meet these requirements.

The IMS will align to the Program Manager’s (PM’s) monthly development cycle schedule and define the specific tasks associated to the items in the product roadmap.  Additionally, the IMS shall highlight interdependencies between contractors and tasks that pose a risk to the Government. General: 

The Contractor shall provide the following module to the existing RALS to allow for 54 Nova Glucometers, 21 Abbott I-Stat docking stations, 7 Clinitek Status instruments, 1 Hemosonics Quantra, RALs-MTE, and RALs-eQuiz to be connected/supported to the RALS Data Management System to maintain data management, support and connectivity module:

Licensed instrument interface (software) with RALS and individual connection licenses for transmitting laboratory results from remotely connected diagnostic test meters (Nova Glucometers, Abbott I-Stat, Clinitek Status, and Hemosonic Quantra) to the VA VISTA laboratory computer program, and then to the patient VA computer record (CPRS). Also, licensed software with RALs for RALs – MTE and RALs – eQuiz for manual result entry and user training/competency. 

Licensing for a test system that mirrors the functionality of the production (live) system is also required. This system is needed to be in compliance with the requirements of the Oracle/Cerner interface project within the VA. Only non-live (test data) will be used in this system to test the functionality of patches and updates before they are installed into the production system. 

The module must be compatible with the existing RALS data management system that is used by San Francisco VA Health Care System. Remote customer service is provided to maintain the interface, connectivity and troubleshooting 7 days per week 24 hours per day.

The module addition for the Meters will allow for managing remote test results including quality control and linearity, testing person identity, meter identity, patient results, critical values, flagged records, reference values, new lot reagent records, and hold back results based on pre-determined criteria.

Maintain service or upgrade the licensed software using HL7 protocols for the transmission of test results and quality control data from the meter to the patient chart.

The module addition must be compatible with the currently installed RALS data management system.  

System updates are provided at no charge.

The current RALS data management system is installed in a virtual space on the BioMed Virtual Server, located at the San Francisco VAMC, 4150 Clement Street, San Francisco, CA 94121.
