REQUEST FOR INFORMATION 
Syndicated Data Core Services 
 
1.0 PURPOSE AND INTRODUCTION 
The Army Contracting Command–Aberdeen Proving Ground (ACC-APG), Installation 
and Technology Division, Aberdeen Proving Ground, Maryland, is issuing this Request 
for Information (RFI) to conduct market research and assess industry capability to meet 
the requirement for Syndicated Data Core Services in support of the Defense 
Commissary Agency (DeCA).  
This is not a solicitation for proposals, a promise to issue a solicitation in the future, or a 
commitment to purchase any products or services. Interested parties are responsible for 
adequately marking proprietary or competition sensitive information contained within 
their response. Any information submitted by respondents to this RFI is strictly 
voluntary. The Government will not reimburse any company or individual for any 
expenses associated with preparing/submitting information in response to this posting. 
The information provided in this RFI is subject to change and is not binding on the 
Government. All costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the 
interested party’s expense. 
The purpose of this RFI is to identify sources capable of providing established, 
commercial SaaS platforms, tailored commercial consulting, and commercial data feeds 
across 13 severable Areas of Interest (AOIs). These services will allow DeCA to meet 
its legislative responsibility to provide commissary patrons with savings when compared 
to the commercial marketplace. This requirement encompasses the delivery of 
syndicated point-of-sale data, shopper behavior analysis, economic modeling for 
savings methodologies, geospatial location intelligence, and regulatory data 
management. 
2.0 BACKGROUND 
The Defense Commissary Agency (DeCA) is a component of the Department of War 
(DoW) that provides enterprise-wide mission support to all U.S. uniformed services, 
including the Army, Marine Corps, Navy, Air Force, Space Force, and Coast Guard, in 
both continental United States (CONUS) and outside of the continental United States 
(OCONUS) locations. DeCA’s mission is to deliver a vital benefit of the military 
compensation package that improves quality of life and readiness by providing grocery 
items at significant savings to military personnel and their families. DeCA operates a 
global system of 235 commissaries across 45 states, 13 countries, and two United 
States (U.S.) territories, with approximately 3,000 checkout lanes. 

To support this global operation, DeCA requires a comprehensive solution that includes 
Program Support; Platform Usability featuring secure, highly available, full functionality 
for end-users with intuitive, self-service ad-hoc reporting capabilities; a comprehensive 
training program with enduring materials to ensure DeCA user proficiency; and Data 
Access and DeCA System Integration. 
3.0 REQUESTED INFORMATION 
Interested parties are requested to provide responses to the following areas. Please be 
specific and provide sufficient details to demonstrate your capabilities. Please indicate 
clearly if your company can provide a total or a partial solution. If only providing a partial 
solution, clearly indicate which of the Areas of Interest (AOIs) your company can 
address. 
This document must address the following 13 Areas of Interest (AOIs): 
AOI 1: CONUS Non-Fresh Data Services 
The objective is to obtain market information on mature, syndicated Point-of-Sale (POS) 
data platforms covering the CONUS for all grocery retail competitors (non-fresh). DeCA 
is interested in identifying platforms with the capability to: 
• Exclude random weight and UPC-driven Fresh Produce, Fresh Meat, Fresh 
Seafood, and Deli-Bakery-Sushi departments (Non-Fresh designation). 
• Enable comparative analysis against all grocery retail competitors. 
• Provide a comprehensive suite of industry-standard retail performance metrics 
(e.g., sales, units, distribution, market share, lift, and patron savings). 
• Support high-volume ad-hoc querying for user-defined lists of at least 1,000 
unique products. 
• Deliver timely and comprehensive Post-Promotional Analysis reports following bi-
weekly events. 
• Accommodate grouped items and geographic locations in a DeCA-defined 
hierarchy. 
 
AOI 2: CONUS Fresh Data Services 
The objective is to obtain market information on mature, syndicated Point-of-Sale (POS) 
data platforms covering the CONUS for all grocery retail competitors (Fresh). DeCA is 
interested in identifying platforms with the capability to: 
• Include random weight and UPC-driven Fresh Produce, Fresh Meat, Fresh 
Seafood, and Deli-Bakery-Sushi departments (Fresh designation). 
• Enable comparative analysis against all grocery retail competitors. 
• Provide a comprehensive suite of industry-standard retail performance metrics 
(e.g., sales, units, distribution, market share, lift, and patron savings). 
 
 

AOI 3: CONUS Ecommerce Data Services 
The objective is to obtain market information on mature, syndicated Point-of-Sale (POS) 
data platforms covering Ecommerce within CONUS for all grocery retail 
competitors. DeCA is interested in identifying platforms with the capability to: 
• Include all items (both Fresh and Non-Fresh). 
• Enable comparative analysis against grocery retail competitors. 
• Provide a comprehensive suite of industry-standard retail performance metrics. 
 
AOI 4: OCONUS Non-Fresh Savings Methodology & Analysis 
The objective is to identify expert commercial economic consulting services to design 
and execute a savings model where standard syndicated data is unavailable. DeCA is 
seeking information on industry’s capability to: 
• Cover all available grocery retail competitors (including traditional grocery stores, 
supercenters, dollar stores, club stores, convenience stores). 
• Exclude random weight and UPC-driven Fresh Produce, Fresh Meat, Fresh 
Seafood, and Deli-Bakery-Sushi departments (Non-Fresh designation). 
• Develop, operate, and maintain a defensible, transparent, and verifiable 
methodology to calculate patron savings for OCONUS commissaries. 
• Ensure the methodology is based on a representative sample or full non-fresh 
assortment of product offerings (including food, non-food, national brand, and 
private label) against local grocery retail competitors. 
• Deliver, utilizing the approved methodology, a timely and highly accurate monthly 
savings report aggregated by Commissary, Country, DeCA Area 
(Europe/Pacific), Total OCONUS, and by Category at each geographic level, 
across current month, QTD, and YTD timeframes. 
 
AOI 5: OCONUS Fresh Savings Methodology & Analysis 
The objective is to identify expert commercial economic consulting services to design 
and execute a savings model where standard syndicated data is unavailable. DeCA is 
seeking information on industry’s capability to: 
• Cover all available grocery retail competitors (including traditional grocery stores, 
supercenters, dollar stores, club stores, convenience stores). 
• Include random weight and UPC-driven Fresh Produce, Fresh Meat, Fresh 
Seafood, and Deli-Bakery-Sushi departments (Fresh designation). 
• Develop, operate, and maintain a defensible, transparent, and verifiable 
methodology to calculate patron savings for OCONUS commissaries. 
• Ensure the methodology is based on a representative sample or full fresh 
assortment of product offerings against local grocery retail competitors. 
• Deliver, utilizing the approved methodology, a timely and highly accurate monthly 
savings report aggregated by Commissary, Country, DeCA Area 
(Europe/Pacific), Total OCONUS, and by Category at each geographic level, 
across current month, QTD, and YTD timeframes. 

AOI 6: Patron Panel Data Services 
The objective is to identify customizable panel data services capable of tracking military 
shopper behavior. DeCA is interested in identifying services with the capability to: 
• Establish and manage a statistically representative panel of DeCA-eligible patron 
households. 
• Collect and provide timely access to purchasing data (items, stores shopped, 
format) and comprehensive household demographic data (including, but not 
limited to: age, marital status, household size, income level, and commissary 
privilege status). 
• Deliver derived industry-standard metrics (e.g., purchase frequency, share of 
wallet, brand loyalty) and reporting capabilities that enable DeCA to answer 
critical shopper behavior questions, including who patrons are, where and when 
they shop, and what factors influence their purchasing decisions. 
 
AOI 7: Competitor Location Intelligence 
The objective is to identify commercially available geospatial/market datasets and 
tools. DeCA is interested in identifying tools with the capability to: 
• Include all CONUS commissary locations, Hawaii, Alaska, and OCONUS 
locations, where available. 
• Provide an accurate dataset identifying all grocery retail competitors (including 
traditional grocery stores, supercenters, dollar stores, club stores, convenience 
stores) within at least a 40-mile radius of specified commissaries. 
• Detail competitor name, address, format, distance, and estimated grocery/total 
sales. 
• Provide a user interface allowing filters by distance, DeCA Area, DeCA Zone, 
and Commissary. 
• Utilize recurring, highly accurate data refreshes. 
 
AOI 8: SNAP Eligibility Data Service 
The objective is to identify niche regulatory compliance data feeds. DeCA is interested 
in identifying services with the capability to: 
• Deliver a highly accurate, comprehensive master data file containing current, 
state/territory-specific SNAP-authorized item lists. 
• Provide this complete master file on a monthly basis, no later than five (5) 
business days prior to the start of the following month to allow sufficient time for 
ingestion and quality assurance. 
• Provide a rapid emergency response mechanism to investigate and correct any 
"Critical Data Errors" (incorrectly flagged SNAP items) within 24 hours of 
Government notification. 
 
 

AOI 9: Competitor Pricing Percentile Data Services 
The objective is to identify data services capable of providing DeCA with item-level 
market retails. DeCA is interested in identifying services with the capability to: 
• Break out retail data by market impact, including regional retails and varying 
percentiles by movement (15%, 25%, 50%, Average). 
• Cover all available grocery retail competitors (including traditional grocery stores, 
supercenters, dollar stores, club stores, convenience stores). 
 
AOI 10: CONUS Manual Basket Shops 
The objective is to identify industry capabilities for the manual collection and reporting of 
price data at commissaries and designated grocery retail competitors in the CONUS, 
Alaska, and Hawaii. DeCA is seeking information on industry’s capability to: 
• Conduct manual price shops to collect both regular and sale price data for brand 
name and private label products. 
• Deliver regular and sale price data for products shopped in accordance with 
DeCA-provided store locations and product lists. 
• Manage an annual scope of approximately 708 locations (177 commissaries and 
531 designated competitors), executing approximately 25% of the locations 
quarterly. 
• Shop a list of approximately 900 national brand SKUs and PLUs provided by 
DeCA. 
 
AOI 11: OCONUS Manual Basket Shops 
The objective is to identify industry capabilities for the manual collection and reporting of 
price data at commissaries and designated grocery retail competitors outside the 
contiguous United States (OCONUS), excluding Alaska and Hawaii. DeCA is seeking 
information on industry’s capability to: 
• Conduct manual price shops to collect both regular and sale price data for brand 
name and private label products. 
• Deliver regular and sale price data for products shopped in accordance with 
DeCA-provided store locations and product lists. 
• Manage an annual scope consisting of approximately 232 locations (58 
commissaries and 174 designated competitors), executing approximately 25% of 
the locations quarterly. 
• Shop a list of approximately 900 national brand SKUs and PLUs provided by 
DeCA. 
• Shop a list of approximately 900 national brand SKUs and PLUs provided by 
DeCA. 
 
 
 

AOI 12: CONUS Competitor Pricing Web Scrapes 
The objective is to identify data scraping services capable of providing DeCA with item-
level competitive retail pricing from websites within CONUS (including Alaska and 
Hawaii). DeCA is interested in identifying services with the capability to: 
• Provide competitive retail data for the top 10 most impactful large-format grocery 
competitors in the market on a regional basis. 
• Deliver this data on a bi-weekly basis. 
 
AOI 13: OCONUS Competitor Pricing Web Scrapes 
The objective is to identify data scraping services capable of providing DeCA with item-
level competitive retail pricing from websites within OCONUS (excluding Alaska and 
Hawaii). DeCA is interested in identifying services with the capability to: 
• Provide competitive retail data for the top 10 most impactful large-format grocery 
competitors in the market on a regional basis. 
• Deliver this data on a bi-weekly basis. 
 
In addition to the AOIs above, respondents should address the following questions: 
 
• Technical Approach: What established, commercially available SaaS platforms or 
commercial data delivery methods (e.g., APIs, secure SFTP, web portals) do you 
recommend to meet these requirements? What are your standard commercial 
licensing terms, user seat limitations, and data usage/sharing restrictions for 
Government clients? How do you ensure system adaptability? 
• Experience: Provide examples of similar systems developed for commercial or 
DoD/Government agencies. Describe your OCONUS implementation experience 
and your company's DoD security/CMMC certification level. 
• Cost & Schedule: Provide an estimated Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) price. 
Your ROM should include a detailed breakout of all primary software licensing 
costs, explicitly identify any additional commercial software required, and provide 
the itemized costs associated with those additional products. What contract or 
shared savings models incentivize early delivery?  What is a realistic timeline for 
account provisioning, data ingestion/mapping, user training, and full onboarding 
of DeCA users? 
• Risk Management: What are the primary risks associated with integrating a new 
system with other government systems, and how have you managed 
interoperability risks in the past? 
 
4.0 RESPONSE INSTRUCTIONS 
Please format your response as a single Portable Document Format (PDF) not to

Notice Type: Pre-Solicitation Notice 
This is a pre-solicitation notice issued per Materials Management Acquisition Regulation 
(MMAR) 5.204. The purpose of this notice is to inform industry of the Government’s 
planned requirement and upcoming solicitation. 
This notice is not a Request for Proposals, Request for Quotations, or Invitation for Bids. 
The Government is not requesting proposals in response to this notice.  
This notice does not constitute a solicitation and does not obligate the Government to 
issue a solicitation, award a contract, or reimburse any costs incurred in preparing a 
response. The Government reserves the right to modify or cancel this requirement at any 
time.  
Any formal solicitation, if issued, will be posted separately through SAM.gov. Interested 
vendors are encouraged and responsible for monitoring SAM.gov for future notices or 
solicitations related to this notice. 
The Government intends to issue a solicitation for a commercially available or 
configurable track and trace software solution to support end-to-end visibility, 
monitoring, reporting, and accountability of materials, assets, products, or shipments 
throughout the supply chain. 
1. Title: Production Environment Track and Trace Platform 
2. Agency: U.S. Government Publishing Office (GPO) 
3. Anticipated Solicitation Release Date: August 2026 
4. Contracting Office:  
U.S. Government Publishing Ofﬁce 
Agency Acquisitions 
732 North Capitol Street NW, A530 
Washington, DC 20401 
 
Points of Contact: 
Nataliya Holl, Contracting Ofﬁcer nholl@gpo.gov  
Jillian Martinez, Contract Specialist 
(Government Contractor for the U.S. Government Publishing Ofﬁce) jbmartinez@gpo.gov  
 

Page 2 of 4 
 
5. Questions: Questions regarding this notice shall be submitted in writing to the points 
of contact identiﬁed above. The Government is not obligated to respond to questions 
before issuance of the solicitation. 
6. Solicitation Number: 040ADV-26-R-0024 
7. NAICS: 541511 — Custom Computer Programming Services 
8. PSC/FSC: DA10 — IT and Telecom — Business Application/Application Development 
Software as a Service 
9. Anticipated Contract Type: The Government anticipates awarding a Firm-Fixed-Price 
contract with optional periods. The final contract type will be identified in the 
solicitation. 
10. Competition and Set-Aside Information: Unrestricted / Full and Open Competition 
11. Description: 
The U.S. Government Publishing Office (GPO) anticipates issuing a solicitation for the 
implementation, operation, and support of a new production environment track-and-trace 
platform. The Government has a requirement for a secure, scalable, and user-friendly 
track and trace software platform. The anticipated requirement includes services and 
related system capabilities to support production operations at GPO production facilities. 
The requirement is expected to include, but may not be limited to, the following functional 
areas: 
• Preferred commercially available Off-the-shelf (OTS)(commercial, ready-to-deploy 
or conﬁgurable) track-and-trace platform for production environments. 
o OTS system must meet all requirements concerning data 
tracking/retrieval/ﬁle processing 
o Customization needs will be determined based on off OTS system 
capabilities 
o Customization constraints should be resolved via software development as 
needed 
• User interface capabilities for ingesting vendor manifest ﬁles into a database 
environment. 
• Tools, reports, dashboards, and production metrics to support material tracking, 
production history, status reporting, and key performance indicators. 
• Data migration 
• Capability to allocate, modify, and maintain machine range assignments with 
change history. 
• Manifest ﬁle creation tools consistent with Government-provided formats and 
standards. 
• Support for continuous improvement and a continuous integration / continuous 
delivery approach. 

Page 3 of 4 
 
• Communication with existing production equipment, programmable logic 
controller conﬁgurations, Government applications, and database environments. 
• Network architecture planning and documentation. 
• Identiﬁcation or provision of required hardware, servers, workstations, and related 
technical support resources. 
• Use of radio frequency identiﬁcation technology, where applicable, to support 
material tracking. 
• Material tracking, reconciliation, and reporting throughout the production process. 
• Onsite and offsite technical support for production operations. 
• Weekly reporting and ad hoc documentation or information as requested by the 
Government. 
• Training for Government users at both locations 
• Technical support and help desk services; 
• Maintenance, updates, and patches; 
The system will be required to support accurate tracking, tracing, and reconciliation of 
materials throughout the production process. The contractor will be expected to provide 
personnel, equipment, tools, and resources necessary to perform the required services in 
accordance with the final solicitation and resulting contract. 
Contractor personnel may be required to comply with Government facility access 
requirements, background screening requirements, cybersecurity and information 
assurance requirements, non-disclosure requirements, and other applicable security 
procedures. 
Security and Compliance Requirements:  
The solicitation may include requirements for compliance with applicable Government 
cybersecurity, privacy, and information technology requirements, which may include, but 
are not limited to: 
• Role-based access controls 
• Data encryption  
• Audit logging 
• Secure user authentication 
• System availability and continuity requirements 
• Protection of Government data 
• Compliance with applicable federal, agency, or organizational IT security policies 
• Specific security requirements will be provided in the solicitation. 
 

Page 4 of 4 
 
12. Period of Performance: The Government anticipates one 12-month base period 
with four 12-month option periods.   
13. Place of Performance: Performance is anticipated to occur onsite at the following 
Government facilities and, where authorized, offsite at the contractor’s facility or another 
designated contractor location. 
 
Location 1: U.S. Government Publishing Ofﬁce 
732 North Capitol Street NW 
Washington, DC 20401 
 
Location 2: U.S. Government Publishing Ofﬁce 
9101 Leonard Kimble Road 
Stennis Space Center, MS 39529 
 
14. Response Instructions: 
This pre-solicitation notice is for informational purposes only. Interested vendors should 
not submit proposals or pricing in response to this notice. 
 
Once the solicitation is issued, offerors shall follow the instructions contained in the 
solicitation for submitting questions, proposals, quotations, or other required 
documentation. 
 
15. Disclaimer 
This notice does not obligate the Government to issue a solicitation or award a contract. 
The Government will not reimburse any costs incurred in response to this notice. Any 
information provided by industry in response to this notice may be used for acquisition 
planning purposes only. 
 
The ﬁnal solicitation, including all requirements, terms, conditions, instructions, and 
evaluation criteria, will govern the acquisition. 
 
 
 
Nataliya Holl 
Contracting Ofﬁcer 
 
End of Pre-solicitation Notice.

DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH &. HUMAN SERVICES Public Health Service 
 
National Institutes of Health 
Bethesda, Maryland 20892 
 
 
 
 
Date: June 25, 2026 
 
To: Contract File 
 
From: Justin M. Borden, Contracting Officer, Office of Acquisition & Logistics 
Management (OALM), National Institutes of Health (NIH) 
 
Subject: Justification for Cancellation of Solicitation No. CS-119444-O 
 
1. Background 
 
The Office of Innovation & Information Technology issued RFP No. CS-119444-0 under the 
NITAAC CIO-SP3 GWAC on behalf of the Center for Information Technology, Network 
Services (CIT/NS) on March 12, 2025. The purpose of the solicitation was to acquire 
comprehensive, professional Information Technology (IT) services in support of CIT/NS 
facilities-based operations. The scope of services encompasses a broad range of IT and 
Operational Technology (OT) support functions, including application modernization, 
SharePoint and cloud migration, cloud transformation, infrastructure support, 
modernization, engineering, and proof-of-concept activities. Additionally, the solicitation 
covered expanded governance and PMO support, software development, Level II helpdesk 
services, enterprise hosting, systems architecture and integration, IT operations, and 
maintenance, application sustainment, cybersecurity operations, network operations, asset 
management, database support, and operational cloud support. 
 
2. Reason for Cancellation 
 
After review, it has been determined that the requirements outlined in Solicitation 
No. CS-119444-O, no longer aligns with the agency's operational needs due to significant 
changes in NIH's enterprise IT governance, acquisition strategy, and service delivery 
structure. Since the development of the original Performance Work Statement (PWS) NIH 
has undergone a substantial transformation in how enterprise IT services are organized, 
governed, managed, and delivered across the agency. 
 
NIH is currently implementing NIH IT Centralization, an enterprise-wide initiative 
intended to consolidate, standardize, and modernize foundational or “commodity” IT 
functions across NIH while aligning operational responsibilities within distinct enterprise 
service domains. 
 
 

DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH &. HUMAN SERVICES Public Health Service 
 
 
 
This restructuring reflects NIH’s strategic direction to align IT support with the 
specialized technical requirements, operational risk profiles, governance structures, 
cybersecurity requirements, and mission responsibilities associated with each 
environment. 
 
Specifically, capabilities and responsibilities that were previously defined under a 
broader decentralized IT support model are now being reevaluated and restructured to 
align with NIH’s enterprise-wide FIT governance and operational framework. 
Proceeding under the current solicitation would risk substantial misalignment with NIH’s 
evolving enterprise IT strategy, create potential duplication of enterprise-managed 
services, and result in contract inefficiencies that are not in the best interest of the 
Government. 
 
Additionally, NIH’s IT Centralization initiative is consistent with broader Executive 
Branch priorities focused on improving operational efficiency, reducing duplicative 
administrative and technology spending, consolidating shared services where 
appropriate, strengthening cybersecurity, modernizing Federal IT infrastructure, and 
improving enterprise governance and oversight. 
 
Although Federal cybersecurity and enterprise modernization policies such as Executive 
Order 14028, “Improving the Nation’s Cybersecurity,” OMB Memorandum M-22-09, 
“Moving the U.S. Government Toward Zero Trust Cybersecurity Principles,” and OMB 
Circular A-130 predated issuance of the solicitation, NIH’s implementation of the FIT 
initiative materially changed how NIH intends to operationalize, govern, secure, and 
acquire enterprise IT services. 
 
This transition is part of the Administration’s broader initiative to consolidate 
federal procurement activities under GSA to reduce duplication, increase 
efficiency, leverage the government’s buying power, and promote greater fiscal 
stewardship across agencies. The transition is consistent with Presidential Executive 
Order 14240, Eliminating Waste and Saving Taxpayer Dollars by Consolidating 
Procurement, which directs agencies to streamline and centralize acquisition activities 
and reinforces the Administration’s policy objective of increasing use of GSA-managed 
acquisition solutions for common goods and services. As a direct result of this transition 
and the associated implementation of Executive Order 14240, the remaining ordering 
period under NITAAC’s CIO-SP3 contract vehicle has been significantly shortened. No 
period of performance past December 31, 2028. Therefore, the current solicitation can 
no longer support the Government’s anticipated period of performance and longer-term 
program requirements. Continuing with the procurement as presently structured would 
risk noncompliance with the Executive Order, conflict with the Administration’s 
procurement consolidation initiatives, and potentially result in an award under a 

DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH &. HUMAN SERVICES Public Health Service 
 
contract vehicle that cannot accommodate the agency’s full performance needs. 
 
Lastly, the existing PWS does not account for more recent technological developments 
such as Artificial Intelligence (AI), Automation, and Software Defined Access (SDA), all of 
which can significantly improve both network security and operational efficiency.  
 
Therefore, the agency has determined that cancellation of the current solicitation and 
re-solicitation under an appropriate GSA-managed acquisition or other appropriate 
vehicle is necessary to ensure compliance with Executive Order 14240, align with 
current federal procurement policy and Administration direction, preserve full and open 
competition under the appropriate contract framework, and satisfy the Government’s 
ongoing mission requirements without unacceptable contractual or performance risk. 
Proceeding with the current solicitation would therefore not be in the best interest of 
the Government. 
 
3. Impact Assessment 
 
Cancelling the subject solicitation will avoid unnecessary expenditure, allow sufficient 
time to revise and properly scope requirements for future re-solicitation, and maintain 
compliance with applicable procurement regulations. 
 
Failure to cancel the solicitation and proceed with award under the current scope would 
introduce significant programmatic and fiscal risk. Specifically, awarding a contract 
based on outdated requirements would likely necessitate immediate and substantial 
contract modifications, resulting in additional administrative burden, cost, and delay. 
NIH further believes that many of the anticipated changes associated with FIT 
implementation would likely exceed the scope of the current solicitation and materially 
alter the nature of the competition originally contemplated. 
 
Furthermore, proceeding without cancellation could compromise the integrity of the 
acquisition by holding vendors to evaluation criteria and technical requirements that no 
longer reflect the Government's actual needs. 
 
 
Signed:  
 
 
 
 
Justin M. Borden, Section Chief, Contracting Officer, Office of Acquisition & Logistics Management 
(OALM), National Institutes of Health (NIH)

United States Department of the Interior 

INTERIOR BUSINESS CENTER

PRESOLICITATION NOTICE 

	 	 

Title:  	Engine Health Monitoring Services

 

Issue Date:   	 June 25, 2026 

 

Response Due Date:   July 10, 2026 @ 3:00 PM, Eastern Standard Time (EST) 

 

THIS IS A PRESOLICITATION NOTICE ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR QUOTE (RFQ). THIS DOES NOT CONSTITUTE SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. 

_____________________________________________________________________________ 

 

Issued by: This Notice of Intent to Solicit from a Sole Source is being issued by the Department of the Interior (DOI), Acquisition Services Directorate (AQD), Interior Business Center (IBC), on behalf of the US Wildland Fire Service (USWFS). 

 

Requirement: DOI, IBC, AQD on behalf of USWFS, intends to negotiate with CAMP Systems International, Inc. (CAMP), a large business, on a sole source basis under the authority of Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) Subpart 12.102(a) - Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements, to implement the following:  

 

USWFS is intending to obtain Engine Health Monitoring Services. DOI currently has nine (9) aircraft in the USWFS fleet that use Pratt and Whitney Canada (P&WC) engines. These engines use an engine health monitoring system in order to increase engine reliability and operational time. P&WC has designated CAMP as the only authorized provider of this service for their entire engine line-up in the United States and Canada. This service provides the Fleet Manager with additional helpful information to ensure the engines are operated in a safe manner.  

 

The objective of this sole source award is to procure a services contract with an estimated period of performance of August 1, 2026, through July 31, 2031, if all option periods are exercised. Anticipated award date is no later than July 31, 2026.

The anticipated North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code is 541511 –Custom Computer Programming Services with small business size standard is $34M. The anticipated Product Service Code (PSC) is J028, Maintenance, Repair and Rebuilding of Equipment: Engines, Turbines, and Components. AQD anticipates negotiating and awarding a firm-fixed-price contract to CAMP in the fourth quarter of Fiscal Year 2026. Interested parties that believe they could satisfy the requirements listed above for USWFS may clearly and unambiguously identify their capability to do so in writing on or before the response date for this notice.  

 

This notice of intent is not a solicitation. Information submitted in response to this notice will be used solely to determine whether competitive procedures could be used for this acquisition. All responses to this notice of intent must be submitted to the Contracting Officer, Sonja Crockett,  at sonja_crockett@ibc.doi.gov so that they are received no later than July 10, 2026, at 3:00 PM EST.

1     Purpose 
The Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) is procuring and implementing an enterprise-
level acquisition lifecycle solution – Appian’s Government Acquisition Management Suite (GAMS).  
Specifically, the FDIC will be implementing three GAMS solutions:
1. Contract Writing
2. Award Management
3. Requirements Management
These solutions will provide contract writing (CW), contract filing (CF), and early acquisition 
planning (EAP) capabilities to the FDIC. CW will enable Contracting Officers (COs) to create, 
update, and track solicitations and awards; Program Offices (POs) to nominate Oversight 
Managers (OMs) and appoint Technical Monitors (TMs); and COs and OMs to initiate and monitor 
contractor performance evaluations. CF will allow users to easily store, access, and manage 
contract files and documents. EAP refers to the collaboration between COs and Program Offices 
to create, update, and track complete requirements packages. 
Within the FDIC and throughout this Statement of Objectives (SOO), the new acquisition solution 
will be referred to as the Acquisition System-Next Generation (AS-NG). AS-NG is intended to 
significantly enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of activities across the acquisition lifecycle 
by automating and integrating acquisition workflows and processes used by key end users across 
the FDIC. It is also expected to improve compliance with policies and procedures by reducing 
workarounds to existing systems and manually performed tasks. Furthermore, it will expand 
transparency and enhance data-driven decisions by enabling robust reporting and data query 
capabilities.  
 
The purpose of this SOO is to obtain contractor support to develop, deploy, and maintain AS-NG 
across the FDIC. The Awardee’s technical approach – to include specific tasks, performance 
standards, and the Quality Control Plan (QCP) – will be incorporated into the final contract as the 
Performance Work Statement (PWS). The FDIC’s desired PWS will focus on measurable 
performance standards rather than prescribed methods.
2     Background 
2.1   General 
The FDIC is a non-Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR), non-appropriated agency that follows its 
own acquisition policy and procedures implemented by the Division of Administration (DOA), 
Acquisition Services Branch (ASB). ASB is responsible for awarding and administrating Contracts, 
Basic Ordering Agreements (BOAs), Receivership Basic Ordering Agreements (RBOAs), and Task 
Orders in support of the FDIC’s mission. On average, ASB awards 425 new agreements/contracts 
and administers approximately 900 agreements/contracts annually. The acquisition process is 
supported by a network of OMs and TMs whose roles are similar to those of Contracting Officer 
Representatives (CORs) in the FAR contracting environment.  
Section C - Description/Specifications/Work Statement PAGE 6 OF 161
CORHQ-26-R-0167

3
2.2   Current Acquisition Systems and Tools
Contract Writing
AS-NG will replace the FDIC’s heavily customized contract writing system, the Automated 
Procurement System (APS). APS is a Commercial-off-the-Shelf (COTS) product built on an 
Appian platform running on Version 18.2. APS is supported on-premises and is not aligned with 
the FDIC’s target cloud architecture.  See Appendix B – Contract Writing Business Process 
Models. Due to limited reporting capabilities within APS, the FDIC uses visualization tools like 
Power BI and other tools listed in Figure 1, Technology Stack to create dashboards and reports 
with APS and other related FDIC data.  
Contract Filing
The FDIC will also replace its official contract document storage repository, the Consolidated 
Document Information System – Contract Electronic Filing (CDIS-CEFile). CEFile is a component 
of CDIS, a centralized digital repository which utilizes Documentum. CDIS will not be replaced 
under the scope of this project; however, the sub-component CEFile will be replaced by the AS-
NG’s contract filing module. 
Early Acquisition Planning
The FDIC does not have an automated solution for early acquisition planning. These tasks are 
currently accomplished using Microsoft SharePoint and email. 
2.3   Technology Stack
Figure 1 depicts a representative Development, Security, and Operations (DevSecOps) toolchain 
that is part of an ecosystem that supports the FDIC’s product development. It is not a 
comprehensive list and includes only the major tech stacks and target platforms. The Contractor 
shall utilize only FDIC-approved DevSecOps tools and pipelines when developing, integrating, 
testing, and deploying solutions within the Corporation’s technical environment. Any new tools, 
such as new Appian plugins,  would need to pass enterprise architecture and security 
authorizations to be approved for use within the FDIC environment. Lead time for incorporating 
such approvals would need to be included in any project planning materials.

4
Figure 1
3     Scope
The scope of this contract includes all services required to deliver a secure enterprise-level, end-
to-end acquisition lifecycle solution consisting of the three modules and associated 
functionalities described in this SOO and Appendices across both mobile and desktop devices. 
The contractor shall provide all labor, management, tools, and materials to deliver a secure 
enterprise solution inclusive of program/project management, discovery and fit-gap, 
Section C - Description/Specifications/Work Statement PAGE 8 OF 161
CORHQ-26-R-0167

5
configuration and development, data and information management, testing and QA, security and 
compliance, authority to operate, deployment and cutover, training and organizational change 
management, operations and maintenance, and continuous improvement activities for products 
released into production. Support also includes creating interfaces to FDIC’s training 
management system (Blackboard-based), financial systems (PeopleSoft-based), required 
connectivity to Enterprise Data Warehouse databases, and migrating documents and data from 
two legacy systems, APS and CDIS/CEFile. The FDIC estimates that approximately 1,100 people 
will need to be trained in AS-NG based on roles assigned (i.e., CO, OM, TM, System 
Administrators).
AS-NG modules and expected timelines are listed below in priority order.  The FDIC expects AS-
NG to be developed iteratively across three functional modules, with capabilities delivered in 
timeboxed sprints. While development of modules may overlap, legacy systems may not operate 
in parallel with AS-NG in Production.
Table 1 - Projected Timeline for AS-NG Development

Discovery Period 1 Month
Module 1. Contract Writing (CW) 70 17 Months
Module 2. Contract File (CF) 900 12 Months
Module 3. Early Acquisition Planning (EAP) 100 6 Months
4     General Approach 
The FDIC’s preferred approach is the use of Agile methodologies focused on iterative delivery, 
flexibility, collaboration, and rapid development, breaking projects into small, manageable cycles 
(sprints) to adapt to change and incorporate continuous customer feedback, prioritizing working 
software, people, and responding to evolving needs. The approach shall also utilize human-
centered feedback and design to include software that is easy to learn and navigate, allowing 
users to accomplish tasks efficiently while creating an enjoyable and engaging experience. The 
contractor's Agile development team(s) shall work closely with FDIC’s Program Manager, Product 
Owner, Data Team, and end users to ensure cross-functional collaboration. 
The Contractor will be responsible for the delivery of a solution that meets the objectives stated 
in this SOO and the requirements included in the SOO Appendices (A-G). The Contractor will also 
be responsible for the maintenance and operation of the solution, which will begin immediately 
after the first module is released to Production and continue through the final Production release 
of this development effort. 
In support of Agile development, the Contractor shall:  
• Develop and enhance Product Vision and Goal, and the Product Roadmap to support 
consistent delivery of high-quality, mission-aligned functionality. 
• Foster effective collaboration with the Product Owner through the ongoing process of 
refining and prioritizing the product backlog (new features, bug fixes, enhancements,

CORHQ-26-R-0167

6
technical work) including clear acceptance criteria, estimating size of user stories and 
sprint timeframes, resulting in well-define, actionable backlog that supports timely 
delivery of capabilities.  
• Assist in the development of Constraints, Limitations, Users, and Exclusions (CLUE) to 
help focus development team and prevent scope creep during a sprint.  See Appendix A: 
User Stories.
• Design, code, test, and deliver functional software increments and supporting artifacts 
based on refined, prioritized product backlog and user stories.
• Support Continuous Integration and Continuous Delivery (CI/CD) to trigger automated 
builds and tests to catch bugs early, and ensure code is always ready to deploy.  
• Identify, document, and track all system components (code, documentation, servers) to 
ensure system integrity, consistency, and traceability throughout the software lifecycle to 
include process for reviewing, approving, and implementing changes to those assets to 
minimize risks. 
• Plan, create, and validate scripts for AS-NG deployment, directly support AS-NG 
deployment and provide release planning and management support.
• Work daily to include daily stand-up meetings to synchronize progress, discuss blockers, 
and align goals.
Note: This list is not meant to be comprehensive, but to illustrate the FDIC’s desire to have a 
solution built using Agile methodologies.  
5       Objectives
5.1   Discovery Period
Perform the ‘up-front planning work’ (see SOO Section 6 for specific deliverables) necessary to 
provide overall vision, scope, objectives, initial high-level requirements, architecture, estimates, 
plans and agreement on roles, responsibilities, working practices, etc., to ensure sufficient 
consideration is given to these factors early on at the beginning to avoid significant problems 
later. The Discovery Period shall include a mapping of AS-NG requirements to GAMS out of the 
box functionality to identify any gaps. 
5.2   User Stories
Implement Appian GAMS to me

52.219-1   SMALL BUSINESS PROGRAM REPRESENTATIONS (FEB 2026) – ALTERNATE II (MAR 2023) 

  

(a) Definitions. As used in this provision-

Economically disadvantaged women-owned small business (EDWOSB) concern means a small business concern that is at least 51 percent directly and unconditionally owned by, and the management and daily business operations of which are controlled by, one or more women who are citizens of the United States and who are economically disadvantaged in accordance with 13 CFR part 127, and the concern is certified by SBA or an approved third-party certifier in accordance with 13 CFR 127.300. It automatically qualifies as a women-owned small business concern eligible under the WOSB Program.

HUBZone small business concern means a small business concern that meets the requirements described in 13 CFR 126.200, is certified by the Small Business Administration (SBA) and designated by SBA as a HUBZone small business concern in the Small Business Search (SBS) ( 13 CFR 126.103).

Service-disabled veteran-owned small business (SDVOSB) concern eligible under the SDVOSB Program means an SDVOSB concern that is designated in the System for Award Management (SAM) as certified by the Small Business Administration (SBA) in accordance with 13 CFR 128.300.

Small business concern—

(1) Means a concern, including its affiliates, that is independently owned and operated, not dominant in its field of operation, and qualified as a small business under the criteria in 13 CFR part 121 and the size standard in paragraph (b) of this provision.

(2) Affiliates, as used in this definition, means business concerns, one of whom directly or indirectly controls or has the power to control the others, or a third party or parties control or have the power to control the others. In determining whether affiliation exists, consideration is given to all appropriate factors including common ownership, common management, and contractual relationships. SBA determines affiliation based on the factors set forth at 13 CFR 121.103.

Small disadvantaged business concern means a small business concern that-

(1) Is at least 51 percent unconditionally and directly owned (as defined at 13 CFR 124.105) by one or more socially disadvantaged (as defined at 13 CFR 124.103) and economically disadvantaged (as defined at 13 CFR 124.104) individuals who are citizens of the United States, and

(2) The management and daily business operations of which are controlled (as defined at 13 CFR 124.106) by individuals who meet the criteria in paragraph (1) of this definition.

Women-owned small business (WOSB) concern eligible under the WOSB Program (in accordance with 13 CFR part 127) means a small business concern that is at least 51 percent directly and unconditionally owned by, and the management and daily business operations of which are controlled by, one or more women who are citizens of the United States, and the concern is certified by SBA or an approved third-party certifier in accordance with 13 CFR 127.300.

52.219-28    POSTAWARD SMALL BUSINESS PROGRAM REREPRESENTATION (FEB 2026)

(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—

Long-term contract means a contract of more than five years in duration, including options. However, the term does not include contracts that exceed five years in duration because the period of performance has been extended for a cumulative period not to exceed six months under the clause at 52.217-8, Option to Extend Services, or other appropriate authority.

Small business concern—

(1) Means a concern, including its affiliates, that is independently owned and operated, not dominant in its field of operation, and qualified as a small business under the criteria in 13 CFR part 121 and the size standard in paragraph (c) of this clause.

(2) Affiliates, as used in this definition, means business concerns, one of whom directly or indirectly controls or has the power to control the others, or a third party or parties control or have the power to control the others. In determining whether affiliation exists, consideration is given to all appropriate factors including common ownership, common management, and contractual relationships. SBA determines affiliation based on the factors set forth at 13 CFR 121.103.

(b) If the Contractor represented that it was a small business concern, a small disadvantaged business concern, or a joint venture that was any of the small business concerns identified in 19.000(a)(3) prior to award of this contract, the Contractor shall rerepresent its size and socioeconomic status according to paragraph (e) of this clause or, if applicable, paragraph (g) of this clause, upon occurrence of any of the following:

(1) Within 30 days after execution of a novation agreement or within 30 days after modification of the contract to include this clause, if the novation agreement was executed prior to inclusion of this clause in the contract.

(2) Within 30 days after a merger or acquisition that does not require a novation or within 30 days after modification of the contract to include this clause, if the merger or acquisition occurred prior to inclusion of this clause in the contract.

(3) For long-term contracts-

(i) Within 60 to 120 days prior to the end of the fifth year of the contract; and

(ii) Within 60 to 120 days prior to the date specified in the contract for exercising any option thereafter.

(c) The Contractor shall rerepresent its size status in accordance with the size standard in effect at the time of this rerepresentation that corresponds to the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code(s) assigned to this contract. The small business size standard corresponding to this NAICS code(s) can be found at https://www.sba.gov/document/support--table-size-standards.

(d) The small business size standard for a Contractor providing an end item that it does not manufacture, process, or produce itself, for a contract other than a construction or service contract, is 500 employees, or 150 employees for information technology value-added resellers under NAICS code 541519, if the acquisition—

(1) Was set aside for small business and has a value above the simplified acquisition threshold;

(2) Used the HUBZone price evaluation preference regardless of dollar value, unless the Contractor waived the price evaluation preference; or

PRODUCT DESCRIPTION (PD ) 
DEPARTMENT OF VETERAN S AFFAIRS 
Office of Information & Technology 
Cyber Secure Operation Centers  
 
Enterprise Vulnerability Management Maintenance and Support 
 
Date: May 27, 2026 
VA-26-00048094  
PD Version Number: 2.0 
 
  


Enterprise Vulnerability Management Maintenance and Support  
TAC Number: VA-26-00048094 
 
Page 2 of 13 
1.0  PRODUCT REQUIREMENTS 
1.1 PURPOSE 
The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Office of Information and Technology (OIT), Office of 
Information Security, requires an enterprise vulnerability management capability that supports 
authoritative vulnerability scanning, compliance scanning, authenticated endpoint visibility, vulnerability 
reporting, and operational support for VA Cybersecurity Operations Center (CSOC) Vulnerability 
Scanning Services (VSS). 
The requirement may be satisfied through maintenance and support of VA’s existing production 
vulnerability management architecture, including the current Tenable Security Center product family 
and associated subscriptions, or through a new commercial vulnerability management capability that 
meets the operational outcomes, scale, security, reporting, support, compliance, and transition 
requirements identified in this Product Description (PD). 
1.2 BACKGROUND AND CURRENT ENVIRONMENT 
VA currently operates Tenable Security Center products in production to support enterprise vulnerability 
scanning and reporting. The current production baseline includes an enterprise license supporting 
approximately 1.8 million IPs, console installations across VA datacenters, a centralized director 
capability, continuous view/monitoring capability, and FedRAMP Moderate agent subscriptions 
supporting authenticated visibility for laptops, remote endpoints, and other assets that may be offline or 
connected through VA’s Virtual Private Network (VPN). 
The existing environment supports the BOD 23-01 twice a month Asset Vulnerability Scan (AVS) 
operations, Payment Card Industry (PCI) compliance scans, external vulnerability scans, Authority to 
Operate (ATO) assessments, Security Control Assessments (SCAs), Compliance Readiness Division 
(CRD) support, and scans supporting remediation of Office of Inspector General (OIG) material 
weaknesses. The capability also supports rapid-response and ad hoc scans for emergent or imminent 
threats, including requests or direction from CISA, GAO, HHS, IRS, and other oversight or security 
organizations. 
1.3 ACQUISITION APPROACH 
This requirement is structured as an open-specification enterprise vulnerability management 
acquisition. VA is not limiting the response to a brand-name-or-equal construct. VA may fulfill the 
requirement through continued maintenance and support of the existing production vulnerability 
management architecture or through a new commercial vulnerability management solution that satisfies 
the required operational outcomes and minimum salient characteristics. 
• Existing architecture maintenance and support approach: Offerors may propose maintenance, 
support renewals, subscription quantities, software updates, security patches, technical support, 
license activation, and associated support entitlements necessary to keep VA’s existing production 
architecture operational, supported, patched, and current throughout the period of performance. 
• New commercial vulnerability management capability approach: Offerors may propose a 
commercial solution that provides equivalent or superior enterprise vulnerability management 
capabilities, including enterprise-scale scanning, authenticated endpoint visibility, vulnerability 
reporting, compliance evidence support, dashboarding, role-based access, data export, integration 
support, and technical support. 
• Offerors proposing a new commercial capability shall clearly identify transition activities, 
implementation timelines, data migration or data recreation requirements, training requirements, 
licensing assumptions, integration dependencies, required VA actions, authorization pathway, and 
any operational limitations during transition. 
Any proposed approach shall avoid disruption to VA’s enterprise vulnerability scanning mission. 
Offerors shall describe how continuity of scanning, compliance reporting, emergency response 

Enterprise Vulnerability Management Maintenance and Support  
TAC Number: VA-26-00048094 
 
Page 3 of 13 
scanning, ATO/SCA support, PCI scanning, and OIG remediation support will be maintained during the 
period of performance and, if applicable, during transition to a new solution. 
1.4 SCOPE 
The scope includes the products, subscriptions, maintenance, support, software updates, security 
updates, major and minor releases, problem resolution, technical support, license activation, and 
operational continuity necessary to sustain VA’s enterprise vulnerability management mission. For a 
new commercial capability, scope also includes implementation planning, transition support, 
configuration, integration support, training, acceptance testing, and documentation necessary for VA to 
determine whether the proposed capability can replace or augment the existing production environment 
without mission degradation. 
The contractor shall provide all labor, tools, subscriptions, product access, technical support, 
documentation, and OEM-backed support necessary to deliver the proposed approach. VA will not 
accept a solution that creates an avoidable gap in enterprise vulnerability scanning, compliance 
evidence production, emergency scanning, or security reporting. 
1.5 REQUIRED OPERATIONAL OUTCOMES 
• Maintain uninterrupted enterprise vulnerability scanning and compliance scanning operations 
across VA. 
• Support a VA enterprise footprint of approximately 1.8 million IPs and associated assets across 
distributed environments and datacenters. 
• Support centralized management, distributed scanning, role-based administration, dashboarding, 
reporting, and data export. 
• Support authenticated endpoint visibility for approximately 675,000 FedRAMP Moderate agents or 
an equivalent endpoint visibility model that meets or exceeds VA’s current operational need. 
• Support ad hoc and emergency vulnerability scans for emergent threats, external oversight 
requests, and time-sensitive cyber response requirements. 
• Provide reporting outputs sufficient to support CSOC, VSS, ATO, SCA, CRD, PCI, OIG 
remediation, and enterprise risk reporting requirements. 
• Keep the software and/or solution current, patched, supported, secure, accessible, and operational 
throughout the period of performance. 
1.6 MINIMUM SALIENT CHARACTERISTICS 
The proposed approach shall meet or exceed the following minimum salient characteristics. Offerors 
shall identify whether each characteristic is satisfied through the existing architecture 
maintenance/support approach or through a new commercial vulnerability management capability. 
EXISTING PRODUCTION ARCHITECTURE MAINTENANCE BASELINE 
The following baseline identifies the current production architecture maintenance and subscription 
quantities associated with the existing VA environment. This baseline is provided to support pricing and 
response development for offerors proposing continued support of the existing architecture. Offerors 
proposing a new commercial capability shall use the operational outcomes and salient characteristics 
above to explain how their proposed solution meets or exceeds the current capability, including any 
transition, licensing, implementation, or migration assumptions. 
Area Minimum Capability Requirement 
Enterprise Scale Enterprise footprint Support approximately 1.8 million IPs/assets and associated scanning 
operations across VA environments. 
Scanning Vulnerability scanning Support authenticated and unauthenticated vulnerability scanning, 
including scheduled, ad hoc, external, internal, and rapid-response 
scans. 
Endpoint Visibility Agent or equivalent model Support 675,000 FedRAMP Moderate agents or an equivalent 
authenticated endpoint visibility model for laptops, remote systems, 
and intermittently connected assets.

distributed scanner control, policy management, and enterprise 
dashboarding. 
Compliance Evidence and reporting Support AVS, PCI, ATO, SCA, CRD, OIG remediation, and enterprise 
risk reporting needs. 
Data Export and integration Support data export, dashboarding, reporting, and integration with VA 
operational reporting or security workflows. 
Support Technical support Provide phone and web-based technical support during at least 
Monday through Friday, 6:00 AM to 9:00 PM Eastern Time, excluding 
federal holidays, unless a higher level is proposed. 
Maintenance Updates and patches Provide software patches, vulnerability security updates, major and 
minor releases, maintenance releases, and problem resolution 
throughout the period of performance. 
Security Authorization posture Identify FedRAMP, agency ATO/ATU, DoD authorization, or other 
federal authorization status for all hosted, SaaS, cloud, or managed 
components. 
Accessibility Section 508 Comply with Section 508 standards or provide an OEM-supported 
remediation plan identifying deficiencies, corrective steps, responsible 
party, milestones, and timeline. 
Transition No operational gap For any new commercial capability, provide a transition plan that 
maintains scanning, reporting, compliance, and emergency response 
continuity. 
1.7 INDUSTRY RESPONSE ASSUMPTIONS AND CLARIFICATIONS 
To reduce avoidable industry questions and support comparable responses, offerors shall prepare 
submissions using the following assumptions unless the solicitation, attachments, or Government 
responses provide different direction. 
• Response structure: Offerors shall clearly state whether they are proposing to maintain and support 
the existing production architecture, provide a new commercial vulnerability management capability, 
or propose a hybrid/transition approach. 
• Evaluation consistency: VA may evaluate different technical approaches against the same required 
operational outcomes and minimum salient characteristics. Offerors shall provide sufficient detail for 
VA to compare risk, continuity, transition impact, lifecycle cost, supportability, and mission fit. 
• Current architecture information: VA will provide releasable baseline information through the 
solicitation or during performance as appropriate. Offerors shall identify any additional architecture 
details required to validate pricing, transition, implementation, or risk assumptions. 
• Continuity of operations: VA cannot accept a gap in AVS, PCI, external scanning, ATO/SCA 
support, CRD support, OIG remediation support, emergency scanning, dashboarding, or required 
reporting. Any new commercial capability shall describe parallel operations, phased deployment, 
testing, cutover, rollback, and risk controls. 
• Authorization status: Proposed cloud, hosted, SaaS, or managed components shall identify 
FedRAMP, agency ATO/ATU, DoD authorization, or other federal authorization status. A product 
that is not currently authorized for VA production use shall identify the proposed authorization 
pathway, estimated timeline, required Government actions, data boundary, hosting model, and 
limitations prior to authorization. 
• Data migration: Offerors shall describe whether existing scan data, dashboards, reports, asset 
groupings, credentials, scan policies, user roles, exports, and evidence artifacts will be migrated, 
recreated, archived, or otherwise retained. 
• Pricing and licensing: Offerors shall explain the licensing metric used by the proposed approach, 
including IPs, assets, endpoints, agents, users, scanners, consoles, cloud connectors, storage, or 
other cost drivers. Pricing shall separately identify subscription/software, support, professional 
services, migration, training, and transition costs as applicable. 
• Endpoint visibility: VA identifies 675,000 FedRAMP Moderate agents as the current baseline. A new 
commercial capability may propose an equivalent authenticated endpoint visibility model if it 
provides equal or better coverage, security, reporting, scalability, and operational control. 

Enterprise Vulnerability Management Maintenance and Support

• Section 508: Submission of a Section 508 remediation plan does not by itself guarantee technical 
acceptability or acceptance. The plan shall specifically identify each shortcoming, corrective step, 
responsible party, milestone, and proposed completion timeline. 
• Acceptance testing: VA expects acceptance to include validation of enterprise scanning, 
authenticated endpoint visibility, dashboarding, reporting, data export, role-based administration, 
support access, and operational continuity.

Web-based Environmental Health Reporting System: Scope of Work

This is a request for a highly configurable commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) database driven, web-based environmental health system (Web-EHRS) that will support a nationwide environmental health program. The system will be configured or modified as described in section 2. The system will be utilized at the national, regional, and field levels by approximately 250 environmental health specialists. The contractor must have technical experience or competency in the fields of environmental and public health. The anticipated start of performance date is February 2027.

The COTS System shall

Document establishment and operator information where environmental health services are provided by IHS. Users can add or modify establishment information. Managers can verify and approve changes.

Allow users to document, track and report on 1) work including inspections and other activities related to establishments and 2) work that may not be related to establishments such as referrals, complaints, investigations, projects, and training.

Allow users to attach pictures, PDFs, spreadsheets and other common electronic files to any work record.

Allow users to email completed reports, with selected electronic attachments (photos spreadsheets, etc.), directly from the system.

Referrals, complaints, investigations, and projects should permit multiple related activities to be entered under a single overarching referral, complaint, investigation, or project. System should allow users to associate individual activities with an establishment of their choosing.

Provide electronic inspection data collection capability to be used by environmental health inspectors both in the field on mobile devices and in the office using a web-based version. The mobile version can be run while not connected to the internet and brings all browser-based features to mobile devices for real-time use in the field.

Electronic inspection forms/checklists will provide access to applicable code and regulatory references related to specific violations such that they can be integrated into the inspection report.

Electronic inspection forms/checklists, referrals, complaints, investigations, projects activities available on the web browser-based version will also be available on the mobile version.

The inspection form/checklist format, regardless of subject material, will emulate the form, function, and layout of the FDA Food Code checklist. An example of this checklist can be seen in Annex 7, Form 3a of the FDA 2022 Food Code.

Electronic inspection forms/checklists can be printed from both the web and mobile versions. Print format will follow the same layout described in Annex 7, Form 3a of the FDA 2022 Food Code.

Provide user permission levels based on user roles and geographic locations.

User administration interface for use by IHS mangers to add/edit users or user permissions.

Table update/edit interface for use by IHS Headquarters managers. Ability to add/edit/modify survey types, violation codes, definitions, canned comments and electronic inspection forms.

Allow users to select, monitor, trend, and report specific electronic inspection violations.

Provide comprehensive data export functionality with parameters defined by the user.

Provide user support which includes the following items:

Application documentation

User Manuals for Environmental Health Inspectors.

Administrator Manuals for HQ and Area (regional) managers.

Ability to broadcast email to system users.

A help desk which has a toll free number and email address and is available 8 am to 8 pm Eastern Time, Monday through Friday.

Meet Federal IT/Security/FedRAMP/Accessibility requirements.

Offerors shall provide their FedRAMP certification/authorization status of the proposed solution and cloud service provider or describe their current security authorization status and ability to support IHS Office of Information Technology review and IHS Authorization to Operate requirements.

Offerors shall describe available deployment models, including SaaS, Government cloud-hosted, contractor-hosted, and deployments capable of operating within an IHS-managed environment or behind the IHS firewall.

Offerors must demonstrate how their solution can provide secure user authentication and access management, including Single Sign-On (SSO) and Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA), role-based access control, audit logging, and support for both federal and non-federal users.

Offerors shall describe how their solution supports PIV-compatible authentication or other federal identity requirements as determined by the IHS Office of Information Technology.

Have data redundancy and backup.

Ensure error resolution as follows:

Issues that impact overall system usability shall be resolved within 8 hours of discovery.

Issues that do not impact overall system usability but do impact system users shall be resolved within 72 hours of discovery.

Have the capacity to support standards-based Application Programming Interfaces, web services, scheduled exports, and data exchange/integration methods to support reporting and connection with external database products or commercial databases.

Offerors shall describe any available mapping or geographic information capabilities, including the ability to capture location information, display records geographically, or support geographic reporting.

Have routine evaluations for system and data quality assurance.

Have routine system maintenance (hardware and software) provided by the contractor.

Provide a minimum of 24 hours’ notice prior to any action that will result in the system being inaccessible to users. An expected time of the system being back online will be included in the notice.

The contractor shall configure or modify the system to include these requirements

Provide additional electronic inspection forms/checklists as requested by the IHS. IHS will provide applicable violations lists and associated code or regulatory references for each additional inspection type as needed.

Calculate Resource Requirements Methodology (RRM) figures to determine workload and support current and historical RRM reporting. The RRM value is based on the number of establishments and the work-day factor associated with each type of establishment as well as other pre-defined factors. (Calculation methodology for RRM is available upon request).

Allow IHS to track the current service responsibility/status for tribes and establishments, including changes over time, to support workload tracking, reporting, and RRM calculations.

Establishments shall be identified using codes from the IHS coding system for Area, Service Unit, Tribe, Reservation, and Community. The IHS Standard Code Book may be viewed at http://www.ihs.gov/scb/index.cfm?module=disp_tablesSCB&newquery=1. Other IHS codes may be required and will be provided by IHS.

Document, track, and report tribal codes and ordinances such as food codes, fire codes, primary seat belt ordinances, and housing codes.

The implementation phase must incorporate the following critical transition activities:

Data Migration: The contractor shall plan and execute the migration of historical inspection and establishment data from the legacy system into the new platform.

User Acceptance Testing (UAT): Prior to final launch and acceptance, the contractor shall conduct a formal UAT period to allow IHS environmental health specialists to test the system.

Reporting Capability

The system shall generate the following reports:

Resource Requirements Methodology (RRM)

Environmental health and management related pre-existing reports and the ability to create ad-hoc reports from all data fields

System flexibility to allow IHS the ability to add/modify/delete and manage ad-hoc reporting fields

Summary reports based on user selected parameters

User selected inspection violation trend reports

Service responsibility/status reports

Tribal code and ordinance reports

Workload planning and prioritization reports (i.e. next survey or activity due date calendar)

Training

The contractor shall provide:

Up to two on-site train-the-trainer sessions the first and third years of the contract

Up to two live webinars per year

Mandatory References:

IHS Standard Code Book - http://www.ihs.gov/scb/index.cfm?module=disp_tablesSCB&newquery=1

Resource Requirements Methodology

Annex 7, Form 3a of the FDA 2022 Food Code - https://www.fda.gov/food/fda-food-code/food-code-2022

SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE SS-26-PHX-025 Indian Health Service (IHS) 
Strategic Quality Support System (SQSS) 
Fort Yuma Health Care Center (FYHCC) 
401 Picacho Road 
Winterhaven, CA 92283 
 
THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE FOR MARKET RESEARCH PURPOSES ONLY . THIS IS 
NOT A REQUEST FOR QUOTATION (RFQ), REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP), OR INVITATION 
FOR BID (IFB). THIS NOTICE IS NOT TO BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE 
GOVERNMENT TO AWARD A CONTRACT OR OTHERWISE PAY FOR INFORMATION 
RECEIVED IN RESPONSE TO THIS NOTICE. 
NOTICE TO INTERESTED VENDORS 
This Sources Sought Notice is being issued for market research purposes in support of 
acquisition planning and to determine the availability of qualified Indian Economic 
Enterprises (IEEs) and Indian Small Business Economic Enterprises (ISBEEs) capable of 
satisfying the Government's requirements under the Buy Indian Act, 25 U.S.C. § 47, and 
applicable implementing regulations. 
The Government is seeking information from qualified ISBEEs and IEEs capable of providing 
a web-based accreditation and compliance management system meeting the 
requirements identified herein. Responses will be used to assess the availability of Indian-
owned businesses and to determine the appropriate acquisition strategy. 
In addition to capability information, respondents shall identify whether they qualify as an 
Indian Economic Enterprise (IEE) or Indian Small Business Economic Enterprise (ISBEE) 
and provide documentation supporting such status. 
If insufficient responses are received from qualified ISBEEs or IEEs, the Government may 
expand its market research to other small business concerns and/or pursue another 
acquisition strategy as permitted by applicable regulations. 
BACKGROUND 
Fort Yuma Health Care Center (FYHCC) requires a comprehensive, web-based Strategic 
Quality Support System (SQSS) or equivalent accreditation and compliance management 
system to support Accreditation Association for Ambulatory Health Care (AAAHC) 
accreditation readiness and ongoing healthcare quality management activities. 
The system must support the management, tracking, documentation, reporting, and 
monitoring of accreditation, compliance, quality assurance, risk management, 

credentialing, patient safety, emergency preparedness, and performance improvement 
activities. 
REQUIRED CAPABILITIES 
Interested vendors shall demonstrate the capability to provide a system that can: 
• Track and document approximately 4,000–5,000 accreditation and compliance-related 
tasks; 
• Provide automated reminders, alerts, and notifications for due, overdue, and non-
compliant tasks; 
• Generate compliance, accreditation readiness, and performance reports; 
• Support assignment and reassignment of tasks by department, role, and responsible staff 
member; 
• Provide centralized access to accreditation documentation, policies, procedures, and 
supporting records; 
• Support monitoring, trending, dashboards, and corrective action tracking; 
• Support healthcare quality management functions including credentialing, infection 
control, safety, compliance, patient satisfaction, peer review, continuing education, and 
related accreditation activities; 
• Be fully web-based and accessible without local installation requirements; 
• Provide ongoing technical support, maintenance, updates, and training; 
• Support data ownership, security, privacy, and reporting requirements applicable to 
Federal healthcare environments. 
PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE 
The anticipated requirement consists of one (1) twelve-month base period and four (4) 
twelve-month option periods. 
SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS 
Interested vendors shall submit the following information: 
1. Company name, address, UEI, and point of contact. 
2. Business size and socioeconomic status (ISBEE, IEE, Small Business, HUBZone, 
SDVOSB, WOSB, 8(a), etc.). 
3. Documentation supporting IEE or ISBEE status, if applicable. 
4. Description of the proposed system and how it satisfies the required capabilities 
identified above. 

5. Description of experience supporting accreditation, compliance, quality 
management, or healthcare operational environments. 
6. Description of experience supporting Federal healthcare facilities, Indian Health 
Service facilities, Tribal healthcare facilities, VA facilities, or similar healthcare 
environments. 
7. Estimated implementation timeline. 
8. Identification of the commercial software platform proposed. 
9. Description of training, technical support, maintenance, and reporting capabilities. 
10. Capability statement and any relevant product literature or supporting 
documentation. 
11. If proposing to provide the Strategic Quality Support System (SQSS) brand-name 
platform, respondents who are not the software developer or owner shall provide 
documentation demonstrating authorization to market, license, resell, implement, 
maintain, or otherwise provide SQSS on behalf of the software owner. Acceptable 
documentation may include an authorized reseller letter, distributor agreement, 
partner agreement, or other written authorization from the software owner. 
The Government reserves the right to verify reseller, distributor, implementation, licensing, 
or support authority directly with the software owner. 
Responses should be limited to five (5) pages, excluding capability statements, reseller 
documentation, and product literature. 
The Government will use information received solely for market research and acquisition 
planning purposes. Responses will assist the Government in determining: 
• The availability of qualified Indian Economic Enterprises (IEEs) and Indian Small Business 
Economic Enterprises (ISBEEs); 
• Whether two or more qualified ISBEEs are capable of satisfying the Government's 
requirement; 
• Whether a Buy Indian Act set-aside is appropriate; 
• Whether qualified vendors are capable of providing the brand-name SQSS platform or 
equivalent capabilities; 
• The appropriate acquisition strategy for this requirement. 
No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with responding to this notice.
