Performance Work Statement

Strategic Quality Support System (SQSS)

Background

Fort Yuma Health Care Center (FYHCC) requires a comprehensive, web-based Strategic Quality Support System (SQSS) to support Accreditation Association for Ambulatory Health Care (AAAHC) accreditation readiness and ongoing healthcare quality management activities.

The contractor shall provide a system capable of tracking, documenting, monitoring, and reporting accreditation and compliance-related activities across all required healthcare quality functions. The system shall support FYHCC’s operational need to manage accreditation tasks efficiently while reducing administrative burden on healthcare personnel.

The contractor shall provide all software, system configuration, implementation support, maintenance, reporting, training, technical support, and related services necessary for successful operation of SQSS throughout the period of performance.

Scope and Performance Requirements

The contractor shall provide a secure, fully web-based Strategic Quality Support System (SQSS) that enables FYHCC personnel to manage accreditation, compliance, quality assurance, risk management, and performance improvement activities.

The system shall:

Track and document up to 4,000–5,000 accreditation and compliance-related tasks;

Provide automated reminders, alerts, and notifications for due, overdue, and non-compliant tasks;

Generate compliance, accreditation readiness, and performance reports;

Allow assignment and reassignment of tasks by department, role, and responsible staff member;

Support monitoring and trending of deficiencies and corrective actions;

Provide centralized access to policies, procedures, and supporting accreditation documentation;

Support all 16 major healthcare quality functions identified by FYHCC;

Be accessible to authorized staff through a secure web-based platform without requiring local installation; and

Maintain system availability, security, and technical support in accordance with this Performance Work Statement.

The contractor shall provide all labor, materials, supervision, equipment, software, hosting, maintenance, and technical support necessary to perform the requirements of this contract.

System Requirements

Functional and Performance Requirements

The contractor shall provide a Strategic Quality Support System (SQSS) that shall:

Be designed to function within healthcare systems and manage activities across all sixteen (16) major quality functions in a typical healthcare organization, including:

Infection Control

Safety

Corporate Compliance

Utilization Management

Patient Clinical Management

Credentialing and Privileging

Peer Review

Performance Evaluation

Orientation

Continuing Education

Patient Complaint Management

HIPAA Compliance

Pharmacy and Therapeutics

Service Recovery

Patient Satisfaction

Patient Advocacy

Track between 4,000 and 5,000 accreditation and compliance-related tasks.

Provide daily task or “to-do” lists for staff to identify required activities, due dates, and pending actions.

Send automated messages, reminders, and alerts for tasks that are due, overdue, incomplete, or non-compliant.

Provide task instruction fields detailing procedures necessary to complete tasks in accordance with accreditation and regulatory standards.

Be accessible to authorized staff members across all departments.

Be fully web-based and contractor-hosted, eliminating the need for local installation or routine technical support by the Service Unit IT department.

Allow real-time uploading and documentation of task completion activities and generation of compliance reports.

Create and assign tasks to individual staff members, groups, departments, or functional areas.

Support assignment of primary and secondary responsible individuals and allow reassignment or transfer of tasks when staff are absent or leave the Service Unit.

Allow flexibility in scheduling tasks by frequency, interval, department, shift, recurring cycle, or rotating staff assignment.

Enable transfer of task completion, validation, and oversight responsibilities without loss of historical documentation.

Provide readily retrievable compliance reports sortable by individual, department, task, accreditation function, or reporting category.

Display trends, dashboards, graphs, metrics, and outlier analyses for identification of deficiencies and targeting of corrective actions.

Provide readily accessible and knowledgeable technical support.

Required System Features

The system shall:

Upload documents and supporting materials to provide a centralized location for accreditation-related records and activities.

Upload links to training resources, policies, procedures, websites, and reference materials necessary for task completion.

Graph data and visually display trends, metrics, dashboards, and other performance activities.

Encrypt patient-specific and sensitive information in accordance with HIPAA, HHS, and Federal cybersecurity requirements.

Create spontaneous or ad hoc quality improvement initiatives related to existing tasks or as stand-alone projects.

Reporting Requirements

The contractor shall provide monthly compliance and accreditation readiness reports summarizing:

Task completion rates;

Overdue items;

Compliance trends and identified deficiencies;

Corrective actions taken or pending;

Department-level performance metrics; and

Performance and compliance status by responsible staff member.

Reports shall be exportable in PDF and Microsoft Excel formats and shall be available to authorized Government personnel upon request.

Service Level Requirements

System uptime shall be at least 99% excluding scheduled maintenance periods.

Contractor shall provide at least seventy-two (72) hours advance notice to the Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR) for any scheduled system outages or maintenance activities expected to impact system availability.

Contractor shall maintain technical support processes sufficient to address system outages, user access issues, and critical functionality failures in a timely manner.

Data Ownership and Security Requirements

All data entered into the Strategic Quality Support System (SQSS) shall remain the sole property of the Government.

Contractor shall comply with all applicable Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA), Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), Indian Health Service (IHS), and Federal cybersecurity and privacy requirements.

Contractor shall implement appropriate administrative, technical, and physical safeguards to protect Government information and prevent unauthorized access, disclosure, alteration, or destruction of data.

Contractor shall notify the COR within twenty-four (24) hours of discovery of any suspected or confirmed data breach, cybersecurity incident, or unauthorized access involving Government data.

Contractor shall not use, disclose, distribute, or retain Government data except as required for performance of this contract.

Period of Performance

The period of performance shall consist of:

One (1) twelve-month base year; and

Four (4) twelve-month option years.

The anticipated period of performance is as follows:

The contract shall include:

An implementation and configuration period beginning at contract award and continuing through successful system deployment and validation.

A recurring services period for ongoing system access, technical support, maintenance, updates, reporting, and training support throughout the duration of the contract.

Deliverables and Acceptance Criteria

Transition and Offboarding Requirements

Upon expiration, termination, or non-renewal of the contract, the contractor shall:

Provide all Government-owned data in a mutually agreed-upon electronic format within thirty (30) calendar days.

Assist with transition activities necessary to support migration of data to the Government or a successor contractor.

Ensure all Government data remaining in contractor-controlled systems is securely removed or destroyed in accordance with applicable Federal records management and cybersecurity requirements after written Government confirmation of successful transfer.

Provide documentation necessary to support continuity of operations and system transition activities.

System Acceptance

Final system acceptance shall occur after:

Successful implementation and configuration of required functionality;

Validation by the COR that all required quality functions are operational;

Completion of user training;

Demonstration of required reporting capabilities; and

Resolution of critical system deficiencies identified during testing.

The Government reserves the right to require correction of deficiencies prior to final acceptance.

Performance Work Statement (PWS) 
Rockwell Automation TechConnect Services 
  
1.0 Introduction & Background 
The purpose of this Performance Work Statement (PWS) is to establish the requirements for a 
Rockwell Automation TechConnect℠ support services agreement. This agreement will provide 
necessary technical support, software maintenance, and troubleshooting resources to maintain the 
reliability, security, and operational readiness of the organization's industrial automation control 
systems and Rockwell Automation hardware and software. 
2.0 Performance Work Statement 
The Contractor shall provide a comprehensive TechConnect support contract that encompasses 
two specific tiers of service: Self-Assist Support and Product Support. These services are 
critical to reducing operational risk, managing legacy equipment, and resolving operating issues 
rapidly. The support will cover the designated inventory of programmable logic controllers 
(PLCs), human-machine interfaces (HMIs), drives, and associated Rockwell Automation 
software. 
3.0 Requirements 
3.1 Self-Assist Support 
The Contractor shall provide base-level self-service tools and resources to enable internal 
engineers and technicians to troubleshoot and maintain systems independently. This includes: 
 Online Support Center: 24/7 access to the Rockwell Automation Knowledgebase 
containing over 100,000 technical notes, interactive forums, and product lifecycle 
notifications. 
 Digital Assist Library: Access to a cloud-hosted augmented reality (AR) library 
providing step-by-step work instructions for the repair and maintenance of Allen-Bradley 
hardware. 
 Software Maintenance I: Entitlement to electronic downloads for software updates and 
patches to ensure systems remain current and secure. 
 Service Ticket Management: The ability to submit, track, and manage service tickets 
and email inquiries via the online portal. 
3.2 Product Support 

 
 
The Contractor shall provide comprehensive product-level support, which includes all features of 
the Self-Assist tier, plus direct access to Rockwell Automation technical experts. This includes: 
 Real-Time Product Support: Telephone and live chat support for standard product and 
programming software, available in 20 languages. 
 Software Maintenance II: Provision of physical software update media and emergency 
software replacement services.

The purpose of this Sources Sought is to conduct market research to procure Patient Queuing System (Kiosk). This notice serves to survey the market to ascertain whether-or-not sources are capable of providing the requested supply. 

This notice also allows potential contractors/vendors to submit a non-binding statement of interest and documentation demonstrating their capability. Please review the DRAFT Statement of Work (SOW) to compare your supply/service to what is requested. Complete the line-items below and submit any documentation supporting your product/service for consideration. Network Contracting Office 22 (NCO 22) is requesting responses from qualified business concerns; the qualifying NAICS code for this effort is 541511 – Custom Computer Programming Services.  The Small Business Administration (SBA) Size Standard for this request is $34 Mil.

Statement of Work

Patient Queuing System (Kiosk)

 

1. INTRODUCTION 

The purpose of this procurement is to acquire a standalone patient queuing system to manage patient workflow at VA Greater Los Angeles Healthcare System, Pathology and Laboratory Medicine Services, Interim Bakersfield Clinic. The solution will include an easy-to-use patient self-service kiosk, visual and audio mechanisms for patient notification, ease of use for laboratory personnel, provide reports for quality assurance purposes. 

2. SCOPE 

Period of Performance: The period of performance of the resulting contract shall be for a five-year base period where the Patient Queuing System shall be acquired as a capital purchase and service/maintenance, software licenses, and supplies shall be renewed/ordered on an annual basis. 

Participating Facilities: VA Greater Los Angeles Healthcare System, Bakersfield Clinic.

3. MINIMUM SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS 

3.1. Patient Queuing System 3.1.1. System is capable of patient self-check-in with option to utilize existing Veteran Health Identification Card (VHIC) 

3.1.2. System is capable of generating a ticket with sequentially numbered (alphanumeric) ticket. 3.1.2.1. System ticketing capability of SMS message to mobile device is a plus but not required. 

3.1.3. System is capable of separating patients into multiple queues 

3.1.4. Ability to move queued patients from one location, or queue, to another as needed 

3.1.5. System capable of communications with multiple workstations simultaneously 

3.1.6. System includes an audio system in patient waiting areas for audible patient notification 

3.1.7. All required software, hardware, operating system, and database licenses must be included 

3.1.8. System must be able to accommodate all users the Bakersfield Clinic as illustrated in 

Attachment A – Schedule of Pricing, Tab 2. Site Requirements 

3.1.9. Must be able to provide method for patient feedback to capture patient satisfaction 

3.2. DA Section 508 requirements 

3.2.1. Kiosks shall comply with ADA Section 508 requirements as applicable. Please see Attachment C – Section 508 Requirements. 

3.3. Self-Check-in 

3.3.1. System includes number of standup and desktop model kiosks according to each site requirement provided in Attachment A 

3.3.2. Each kiosk shall include a printing system for patient queuing ticket printout 

3.3.3. System must have multiple check-in categories for separation of patient into multiple queues (i.e., blood draw, drop off, research, no orders) 

3.3.4. Kiosk/check-in device can allow patients to check-in manually using alphanumeric characters 

3.3.5. Patient check-in information will be visible to staff after patient self-check-in 

3.3.6. System includes number of freestanding floor kiosks according to each site requirement provided in Attachment A 

3.3.7. Patient queuing ticket available immediately upon patient check-in 

3.3.8. Ticket printed must include sequential number assigned to the patient 

3.3.9. Ticket printout is customizable by the end user 

3.3.10. Must include sufficient annual printer paper volumes to meet VISN 22 healthcare system requirements as per Attachment A, Tab 2. Site Requirements, column J - Estimated Annual Patient Volumes. 

3.3.11. Includes all necessary power cords for a 110V operation 

3.3.12. Kiosk/device can be sanitized with commonly used disinfectants used by healthcare settings to stop the spread of disease and contagions 

3.3.13. Patient check-in Kiosk/device utilizes touch screen technology 

3.4. Main Lobby Visual Display 

3.4.1. System includes display monitor(s) in patient waiting areas for visual patient notification 

3.4.2. VAGLA Activations Team will provide Monitor 

3.4.3. Must include power cord/supply for 110V operation 

3.5. Departmental Display Monitor 

3.5.1. System includes display for departmental use to manage patient queuing assignments 

3.5.2. VAGLA Activation Team will provide Monitor 

3.5.3. Must include power cord/supply for 110V operation 

3.6. Signage 

3.6.1. System must include digital signage displays for each work/draw station 

3.6.2. Digital display of assigned numbers visible to patients in waiting area 

3.6.3. Display will direct patient to appropriate work/draw station 

3.7. Audible Notification 

3.7.1. Adjustable audible alert in waiting area including installation of speakers in specified locations 

3.8. Reports 

3.8.1. Patient Wait Time report with details for each phase in the workflow (i.e., Transaction/Encounter time i.e., time spent with patient at each station) 

3.8.2. Customizable patient satisfaction survey with detailed reports 

3.8.3. Reports include number of overall encounters per day, per unique user, specific workstation, user, and/or draw station location 

3.8.4. Remote monitoring of current wait times by location manager 

3.8.5. Ability to customize reports by established user parameters 

4. STATEMENT OF WORK AND OTHER REQUIREMENTS 

4.1. Network and Interface Requirements 

4.1.1. Must provide server specifications for virtual environment 

4.1.2. Must include Microsoft SQL specifications database system loaded onto server, to include system configuration diagram 

4.1.3. Must include any licensing, software and/or hardware necessary to interface all parts of the system 

4.1.4. Must include all necessary power cords for a 110V operation 

4.1.5. Must include any hardware necessary for installation (i.e., power cords and network cables) 

4.1.6. Must include ability for VA system administrator/super user or IT staff to access server as administrator 

4.1.7. All software updates must be compatible and tested with VA current/approved operating systems and database versions 

4.1.8. If the contractor provides remote support, the contractor has established a VA national MOU/ISA between Contractor and VA. If the Contractor currently has a valid MOU/ISA, the Contractor shall include a copy of the MOU/ISA as part of their quote with the file named “VA MOU/ISA”. The Contractor shall provide all hardware and software in order to implement the remote support system. 

4.1.9. The vendor hardware and software proposed solution meets all VA Information Security, Hardware, Software and Network requirements (VA 6500). Any wireless equipment must be FIPS 140-2 compliant as well, and vendor must provide the FIPS 140-2 certification for any wireless equipment. 

4.1.10. The Contractor supplies responses to required documents in order to add systems to the VA network including but not limited to the VA Form 6550, MSD2, and the Risk Analysis Tool. 

4.2. Service Maintenance / Warranty 

4.2.1. The Contractor shall provide 24 hour, 7 days a week Technical Support for troubleshooting and resolving issues by calling a toll-free number. 

4.2.2. Vendor will provide onsite technical support within 24 hours when telephone technical troubleshooting does not resolve the issue. 

4.2.3. Vendor will provide replacement parts for failed components during the service contract period at no cost to the VA. 

4.2.4. Vendor will provide all software upgrades needed during the contract period with currently supported operating systems and database. 

4.2.5. Vendor will provide all hardware upgrades necessary for functionality during the contract period. 

4.2.6. The Contractor shall provide documentation of services performed. 

4.2.7. The Contractor shall provide a warranty for all items and services provided under the Contract for the duration of the Contract and all associated delivery orders. 

4.3. Installation 

4.3.1. Installation/Site Preparation: 

4.3.1.1. Site preparation specifications shall be furnished in writing by the Contractor as a Site Preparation Report after award of the delivery/task order. The Contractor shall provide coordinated professional installation and implementation project management services to implement the system specified in the SOW at all identified sites. The Contractor shall provide a firm estimate of working days required from the date of the delivery order to go-live based upon the SOW. The initial installation site report shall be provided to the CO no later than one week after the initial post-award conference, and all other site reports shall be provided at least forty-five (45) days before the installation of all those sites unless the CO approves for a shorter timeframe. Contractor shall assess each site and propose specific site prep requirements including but not limited to: 

• VA responsibilities 

4.3.2. In collaboration with VA IT staff and system administrators install patient queuing system and hardware to the VA network. Must install hardware and software at designated patient. 

4.3.3. Installation includes collaboration with Biomedical Engineering and OIT to ensure installation follows VA regulations. 

4.3.4. Contractor must provide all additional cable drops for locations which are not already configured. 

4.4. Implementation 

4.4.1. Implementation/transition timeframe: All sites shall have a complete installation and go-live of their system within 90 days of award of this Contract. 

4.4.2. Contractor shall execute an implementation plan which includes: 

4.4.2.1. Installation - The Contractor shall make every effort to conduct a concurrent implementation at all sites with a weekly collaborative meeting. The Contractor shall provide a dedicated project manager throughout the entire implementation. Installation shall also include conversion of all current data minimally, including operator profiles. 

4.4.2.2. Testing - Shall include, at minimum, testing of the system to ensure all functions are fully operational. In addition, training must be provided to all sites. 

4.4.2.3. Acceptance - Must meet all technical, functional, and performance requirements of this SOW and Contractor’s proposal. 

4.4.2.4. Go-Live - Dedicated project management and technical support must be available above the requirements of Section 4.1 on the day of go-live at each site for 3 days. 

4.4.2.5. Post Go-Live Follow Up- Check-in should include at least two weeks and 30 days after the go-live date. 

4.5. Training 

4.5.1. Initial onsite laboratory personnel training

Maritime Information Resource
1. Scope: United States Fleet Forces Command (USFFC) N3 Maritime Domain Awareness, provides 24/7/365 support to the Fleet Command Center 
Battle Watch, Navy Fleet assets, United States Northern Command, and interagency partners. Our focus is behavioral and predictive analysis of 
information and data pertaining to vessels, people, cargo, infrastructure and events in the maritime domain. This support shall include, at a minimum, 
comprehensive geo-visual based user interface to access maritime industry data; support user-defined analysis of vessel activities and associated 
maritime businesses; and provide predictive risk analysis based on observed activities. The user display and products will contribute directly to the 
Commander's decision-making cycle for providing situational awareness of the maritime domain.
USFFC Maritime Domain Awareness (MDA) requires a multi-source maritime fusion and maritime trade analytic resource that is web-based, non-
classified, non-PKI commercial maritime information to provide near-real time, relevant and reliable data and information pertaining to the 
commercial maritime industry and provided by the commercial industry. Required data and information should include but is not limited to Section 2

SOURCES SOUGHT SYNOPSIS (Not a Notice of Solicitation) 
F2FT576085A001 
 
The United States Air Force, 99 CONS, Nellis AFB, NV is seeking capabilities packages of 
potential sources, including but not limited to small business (SB), 8(a), HUBZone, and Service-
Disabled Veteran-Owned (SDVO) small businesses that are capable of providing IL4 
Environment Enterprise equipment as defined in the attached items list. Firms that respond shall 
specify that their services meet the specifications provided in the attachment below and provide 
detailed information to show clear technical compliance.  
 
Detailed Specifications are listed in the attachment identified below: 
 
1. Attachment 1- Items List  
 
All interested firms shall submit a response demonstrating their capability to provide these items 
to the Primary Point of Contact listed below. As stipulated in FAR 15.201, responses to this 
notice are not considered offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding 
contract. No solicitation (Request for Quotes) exists; therefore, do not request a copy of the 
solicitation. The decision to solicit for a contract shall be solely within the Government's 
discretion.  
 
The NAICS Code assigned to this acquisition is 541519 - Information Technology Value 
Added Resellers with a size standard of 150 persons. Firms responding should indicate their 
size in relation to this size standard, and indicate socio-economic status (SB, 8(a), SDVO, or 
HUBZone). Respondents are further requested to indicate their status as a Foreign-
owned/foreign-controlled firm and any contemplated use of foreign national employees on this 
effort. The Government reserves the right to consider a small business set-aside based upon 
responses hereto for any subsequent action. All prospective contractors must be registered in the 
System for Award Management (SAM) database to be awarded a DoD contract.  No set-aside 
decision has been made.  Note that a key factor in determining an acquisition to be a Small 
Business Set Aside is that small business prime contractors must perform at least 50% of the 
effort, as defined in Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) clause 52.219-14.   
 
Any information submitted by respondents to this sources sought synopsis is voluntary. This 
sources sought notice is not to be construed as a commitment by the Government, nor will the 
Government reimburse any costs associated with the submission of information in response to 
this notice. Respondents will not be individually notified of the results of any Government 
assessments. The Government's assessment of the capability statements received will factor into 
whether any forthcoming solicitation will be conducted as a full and open competition or as a 
set-aside for small businesses, or any particular small business program.  To ensure your 
response along with any and all attachments are received, attachment(s) must be less than 
10 MB [in total].  It is the responsibility of the respondent to contact the government to 
confirm receipt prior to the offer due date and time. 
 
 
 

 
 
CAPABILITIES PACKAGE: All interested firms shall submit a capabilities package that 
explicitly demonstrates their capability to provide the required commodities. The capabilities 
package should be brief and concise, yet clearly demonstrate an ability to meet the stated 
requirements. 
 
Responses may be submitted electronically to the following e-mail address: 
sencere.gilbert@us.af.mil. All correspondence sent via email shall contain a subject line that 
reads “F2FT576085A001- IL4 Environment Enterprise” If this subject line is not included, 
the email may not get through email filters at Nellis AFB. Filters are designed to delete emails 
without a subject or with a suspicious subject or attachments. Attachments with files ending in 
.zip or .exe are not allowable and will be deleted. Ensure only .pdf, .doc, .docx, .xsls or .xls 
documents are attached to your email. All other attachments may be deleted. Responses shall be 
emailed to: 
 
99 CONS,  
POC – SSgt Sencere Gilbert   
Email: sencere.gilbert@us.af.mil 
 
RESPONSES ARE DUE NOT LATER THAN 01 July 2026 BY 10:00 AM Pacific Time. 
Direct all questions concerning this acquisition to SSgt Sencere Gilbert at 
sencere.gilbert@us.af.mil.

PURCHASE DESCRIPTION 
Gartner Licenses 
1. INTRODUCTION
This scope of work is for Program Executive Office Integrated Warfare Systems’ (PEO IWS) Front 
Office which seeks to procure subscription-based access to Gartner products. Gartner’s commercial-off-
the-shelf (COTS) license products enable immediate, web-based access to an online database of published 
reports, tools, and guides that are Gartner intellectual property (IP).  These tools are critical for PEO IWS 
software, data, digital, process, strategy, and architecture efforts. Gartner offers more than 98,000 
documents and tools accessible only through a research subscription.  
2. BACKGROUND
PEO IWS seeks to procure 12-month subscriptions to Gartner’s subscription-based solution to enable 
faster results, smarter decisions and stronger performance on PEO IWS mission-critical priorities, 
including technology modernization, software effectiveness, enhanced government efficiency and 
productivity.  
3. REQUIREMENTS
The contractor shall provide 1 Base year license subscription + 4 Option years of Gartner for Enterprise 
IT Leadership Team Plus — Team Leader (Quantity 1), Gartner for Enterprise IT Leadership Team Plus 
— Advisor Member (Quantity 5), CDAOs Executive – Team Leader (Quantity 1), CDAOs Executive – 
Team Advisor (Quantity 1), and GTP Advisor Team (Comprised of 1 Team Leader + 4 Team Members) 
(Quantity 1).  
Licenses will include access to research topics covering software development, software integration, 
Model-based systems engineering (MBSE), Process improvement, Digital transformation, IT landscape 
and strategy, Technical infrastructure, and Integrated data environments. 
The contractor shall provide IT research and advisory support for implementation and adoption of 
software development and model-based system engineering. The contractor shall support IT system 
accreditation of cloud-native technologies via inheritance model and understanding the intricacies of 
developing and visualizing software across multiple environments.  The contractor shall support 
development of automated monitoring capabilities for IT systems in unmanned vessels, and integration of 
technologies enabling IT system updates at geographically dispersed sites. 
General Security 
The contractor will require a facility security clearance at the SECRET level. Contractor will need cleared 
personnel able to attend classified meetings and review classified information up to the TOP SECRET 
level at another contractor’s facility or government activity. The contractor will be required to access CUI 
and receive, store, and generate CUI.   
The Contractor is required to protect critical information associated with this contract to prevent 
unauthorized disclosure and will observe OPSEC requirements.

This recommendation is for the acquisition of supplies or services determined to be reasonably available 
from only one source/only one manufacture. Competition is impractical for the following reasons (please 
answer the questions below): 
 
1. What are the reasons for soliciting only the suggested source/suggested brand name? Please provide 
the unique characteristics of the items or services along with the supporting rationale and the market 
research performed to substantiate your reason for the suggested source/brand name. 
    
Only two vendors were considered for the 600-kip load frame controller upgrade: MTS and Instron. The 
MTS FlexTest 40 controller enables the use of the same software used to operate the majority of the 
servohydraulic load frames in our laboratory. MTS is the developer and exclusive vendor of the MTS 
Multipurpose Testware (MPT) software. Additionally, choosing the MTS FlexTest 40 controller 
enhances capability beyond that of an Instron controller by offering 8 analog input channels, 8 output 
channels, and 5 conditioned channels suitable for connecting and powering LVDTs from the FlexTest 
controller. An Instron controller would require new software—Bluehill Universal—which may not be 
familiar to current operators. Furthermore, MTS personnel are exclusively qualified to install the 
controller, verify its compatibility with the load frame, and perform system calibration. Only trained 
MTS technicians are authorized to carry out these tasks with the FlexTest 40 Controller, as other vendors 
are not trained in its installation and setup. 
 
2. What is the impact to the government if another vendor/brand is used? Include any dollar, schedule, 
or compatibility impacts if possible. 
 
The potential impact of switching to another vendor or brand is not fully predictable. However, since the 
MTS 793 Multipurpose Testware (MPT) software is exclusively available from MTS and is compatible 
only with MTS controllers, utilizing a controller from a different vendor would incur additional costs for 
the government. This would include expenses related to training operators on the new software and 
ensuring consistent usage to maintain proficiency. Both the training process and the time required to 
achieve and sustain proficiency would lead to added costs. Currently, operators are already trained on the 
MTS MPT software, which is widely used in the majority of load frames within NASA’s Langley 
Research Center’s structures labs. Furthermore, because operators regularly utilize this software when 
operating other load frames, the time needed to remain proficient is reduced.  The FlexTest 40 Controller 
serves as a replacement for a failing FlexTest SE controller, and both models utilize the same software.

Training would be necessary for multiple operators to become proficient with the software, resulting in 
additional costs and potential delays to testing schedules as personnel learn and verify the new system.

Statement of Work (SOW)/Performance Work Statement (PWS): Molecular Modeling Simulation Platform or comparable

The Office of Product Quality and Research (OPQR) conducts research to advance the adoption of emerging technologies for pharmaceutical manufacturing and support the regulatory review, inspection of FDA regulated products. OPQR uses artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) based advanced molecular dynamic simulation tools for assessing the impact of manufacturing process parameters, material attributes and end user handling on the quality and performance of complex drug products and biologics. These studies include but are not limited to atomic and molecular level modeling and simulation of protein-excipient interaction in liquid, frozen and dried products, drug-interface interaction, liposome and nanomaterials structural dynamics, drug-excipient interactions, etc. To this end OPQR is seeking to extend the license for the current molecular simulation platform or comparable platform and associated technical support to support ongoing research.  

The MD simulation platform shall provide a comprehensive workflow, data management, and storage management, computing resource management capability. The platform needs to enable parallel simulation of at least two MD simulation projects. The platform and technical service providers shall have a proven track record on solving pharmaceutical and regulatory science challenges involving molecular dynamics and simulation. This platform will be deployed on FDA High-performance workstation (Precision 7920 Tower) with a Linux based system that meets the required specifications.

As the system will be installed in FDA DPQR proprietary High-performance workstation (Precision 7920 Tower), there is no security risk. Technical risks on knowledge transfer are mitigated via training and support packages included. Administrative and financial risks are mitigated via annual renewal of the subscription contract.

Item 1 : Molecular Dynamic Modeling and Simulation Platform

The required technical features of molecular dynamic simulation software package are:

Shall allow seamless transfer of current workflow and projects without the need to rebuild and validate current models

Shall be a high-performance molecular dynamics simulations platform capable of designing, modeling and simulating biological interactions, antisense oligonucleotides, protein-excipient and protein-ice interactions, protein-ligand complexes, viral capsid and macromolecular complexes with high throughput and scientific accuracy.

Shall include an all-atom ad coarse grain model

Shall include a machine learning model for predicting the interactions between formulation components and biologics or small molecule active pharmaceutical ingredients

Shall employ an accurate and scalable machine learning force fields with broad molecular coverage to describe the interactions between atoms and predict relative energies

Shall have a validated, proven, stable and robust framework for the calculation of energies and forces for atomistic force field models.

Shall describe interactions between atoms in system using modern force fields with comprehensive coverage of chemical space for small molecules, biologics and materials science applications.

Shall be a professionally managed software that is broadly available and used by the pharmaceutical industry to facilitate knowledge transfer from and to the FDA.

Shall leverage machine learning to accurately and rapidly predict the aqueous phase pKa values and protonation state distributions of monoclonal antibodies and globular proteins. 

Shall employ supervised machine learning (ML) for predicting molecular properties based on chemical structure.

The supervised learning platform shall be easy to implement by novice and experienced users. 

Shall be a user-friendly machine learning tool for relating properties derived from molecular simulations to key experimental properties.

Shall predict quantitative structure activity/property relationship models.

Shall offer a robust workflow for data management, storage, and computing resource management to streamline simulation projects.

Shall manage and stores large volumes of image and quantitative data efficiently.

Shall perform stability and reactivity analysis and facilitates the study of biologics and small molecule drug stability and reactivity under various conditions.

Shall be a fast, general-purpose computing on graphics processing units (GPGPU) enabled molecular dynamics simulation program.

Shall simulate systematic temperature variation and the progressive removal of water from a complex model system.

Shall include well validated workflows for protein structure preparation including homology modeling particularly for antibodies, protein loop sampling, structural relaxation and protonation state assignment. 

Shall simulate and analyzes protein-excipient combination and identify excipient hotspots near protein surfaces in solutions and freeze-dried products.

Shall simulate protein excipient interactions of not less than 70000 atoms over a simulation duration of not less than 270 ns

Shall support three-dimensional visualization of reactions and analysis.

Shall include analysis tools for protein structures sampled during simulations of protein containing systems such as secondary structure analysis, protein patch analysis.

Shall be capable of constructing systems containing a mixture of proteins with complex composition of non-biological components.

Shall characterize complex mixtures of components including radial distribution functions, spatial density analysis, glass transition temperatures and diffusion rates.

Shall conduct simulations in NPT or NP𝝻T ensembles (constant temperature and pressure), with typical temperatures of 233.15 K and 300 K, or other mutually agreed-upon values.

Shall simulate interactions between formulations and lipid-based systems, liposomes, or other nanomaterials.

Shall analyzes the 3D distribution of components within lyophilized formulations, including small and complex molecules.

Shall include parameter analysis including but not limited to trajectories, root mean square deviation (RMSD), energy profiles, and other critical data from simulation systems.

The MD simulation platform shall have a user accessible script-based automation of complex modeling workflows.

The above features shall be available in a single, integrated suite of software with a well-developed graphical user interface for visualizing molecular systems, enable interpretation of results and facile interoperability of the protein-focused and materials science-focused capabilities for molecular dynamics and machine learning.

Shall be deployable on DPQR network. and compatible with hardware in OPQR Precision 7920 Tower:

Memory: 128GB 

GPU: Dual Nvidia RTX A5000 (8192 CUDA cores each), 24GB

Operation System: Ubuntu

CPU: Intel Xeon Gold 5220R 2.2GHz (24 cores)

Storage: 512GB

Shall accelerate performance of above Graphics processing unit (GPU) or comparable by at least 60%

Alternatively, the vendor may supply software with compatible government approved hardware, GPUs or high-performance computing platform.

The platform and the vendor’s scientists shall be well published and have a proven track record on solving pharmaceutical and regulatory science challenges involving MD simulation.

Shall provide technical support and perform simulation parallel to FDA’s projects at client requests.

Shall including packages, license, and libraries for: 

Machine learning-based predictive modeling.

Molecular visualization and chemical informatics.

Conformational sampling.

Scaffold replacement for novel molecule design.

pKa and protonation state prediction tool.

3D-QSAR modeling.

Ligand-receptor docking.

Ligand preparation and stereochemical variation.

Molecular mechanics simulations.

Predicts drug permeability across membranes and interfaces.

Protein structure prediction and refinement.

Quantum mechanics and Molecular mechanics simulations for reactions of proteins and ligands.

Binding site identification for proteins.

Design, characterization, and optimization of drug formulations and delivery systems at the molecular level.

Biologics modeling (e.g., antibodies).

KNIME, Maestro, and OPLtS Access Licenses: Data workflows, GUI, and force field support 

Item 2:  Delivery, Installation, On-site training and Technical Support

The vendor will cover all costs associated with the following:

System software, shipping, and delivery.

Full system installation in person or screen sharing support on FDA OPQR in house high-performance workstation with the help of client’s IT professional.

Provide all necessary training to run the projects on simulating, analyzing and visualizing the formulations, molecular interactions, and manufacturing of complex drugs.

All necessary training and technical support to execute associated projects on simulating, analyzing and visualizing of formulations, interfacial and molecular interactions, and manufacturing of complex drugs.

Shall offer a minimum of 3 days of full time employee hours for comprehensive support, services for constructing protein formulation structures and simulation with their resources parallel to FDA DPQR Precision 7920 Tower at FDA OPQR requests.

Comprehensive modeling support including documentation, rapid response to queries and knowledge transfer to the FDA,

SOLE SOURCE – NOTICE OF INTENT 
 
Title: DMAP Galaxy Works support for NIDAP Bioinformatics Workflows  
 
Solicitation/Reference Number: 75N98026Q00474 
Posted Date: 6/24/26   
Response Date: 7/07/26  
PSC Code: D302 IT and Telecom – Systems Development  
NAICS Code: 541512 - Computer Systems Design Services 
 
1.0 DESCRIPTION 
The Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), Office of Mission Acquisition 
Solutions (OMAS) on behalf of National Institutes of Health (NIH), National Cancer Institute 
(NCI), Center for Biomedical Informatics and Information Technology (CBIIT), Office of the 
Chief Information Officer (OCIO), intends to procure on a sole source basis, specialized 
professional services to support integration, deployment, and operation of Galaxy software 
and migration of custom-built bioinformatic applications into the NCI Integrated Data 
Analysis Portal (NIDAP) environment.  
 
GalaxyWorks LLC 
8 The Green Ste 5008 
Dover, DE 199901 
 
This acquisition will be processed under FAR Part 12 – Acquisition of Commercial Products 
and Commercial Services and will be made pursuant to the authority at 41 U.S.C. 1901, 
utilizing simplified procedures in accordance with RFO 12.201-1. Competition is being 
restricted in accordance with RFO FAR 12.102(a), based on the Contracting Officer’s 
determination that only one source is available to meet the Government’s requirements. 
The North American Industry Classification System code is 541512 and the business size 
standard is $34 Million. 
 
The following is the requirement for the solicitation number 75N98026Q00474 
 
Professional services will be used by DMAP to: 
• Ensure our Galaxy instance is running on the latest supported version of Galaxy to 
take advantage of bug fixes, security patches, and new features.  
• Provide support for managing logins, scaling compute instances, and storing data 
so our team can focus on research workflows rather than infrastructure operations.  
• Integrate NIH-compatible authentication (e.g., NIH login/iTrust) to meet federal 
security and data privacy requirements for our collaborators.  
• Fix the known existing bug where dropdown (select) parameters do 
not render correctly when tools are composed into Galaxy workflows.  

• Enable running individual tool nodes independently within a workflow, rather than 
requiring a full re-run from the beginning when only one step needs to be re-
executed.  
• Support DMAP staff with developing and running ad-hoc tools or custom Python 
code directly from the Galaxy front end for exploratory analysis.  
• Ensure that the published/released version of workflows shared with collaborators 
is under version control, maintained alongside the corresponding Tool XML files in 
our repository.  
• Develop new custom workflows 
• Assist DMAP with the preparation of training materials for end users.  
 
 
2.0 UNIQUE QUALIFICATIONS OF THE CONTRACTOR 
The proposed contractor, GalaxyWorks LLC, is a commercial entity founded by several core 
members of the original academic Galaxy Project team to provide managed professional 
services and support for Galaxy open-source software. Galaxy is an open-source platform 
originally developed in 2005 by researchers at Johns Hopkins University and Pennsylvania 
State University with sustained support from the National Institutes of Health (NIH). 
GalaxyWorks provides a managed version of Galaxy designed for organizations requiring 
dedicated support, enterprise implementation expertise, and security-focused deployment 
support, as required by Federal entities. 
NCI requires specialized professional services to deploy, integrate, optimize, and sustain 
the Galaxy platform within the NCI Integrated Data Analysis Portal (NIDAP), including 
integration with NIH-compatible authentication, operation within a hybrid infrastructure 
environment, migration and optimization of bioinformatics workflows, development of 
custom workflows, remediation of platform-specific workflow issues, and support for user 
training and adoption. Based on market research, GalaxyWorks is the only source 
identified with the combination of direct Galaxy platform expertise, development 
knowledge, and experience necessary to perform these requirements in NCI’s environment 
without substantial duplication of effort or unacceptable performance risk. 
Due to time and resource constraints, NCI cannot accommodate the significant ramp-up 
that would be required for an alternate vendor to obtain comparable platform knowledge, 
learn the NIDAP environment, and perform the required integration and workflow migration 
activities. Use of another source would create increased risk of performance delays, 
rework, and disruption to critical bioinformatics capabilities. 
 
3.0 RESPONSE INSTRUCTIONS 
 
This notice is not a request for competitive quotations. However, all responsible sources 
may submit a capability statement, which will be considered by the agency. The response 

and any other information furnished must be in writing and must contain material in 
sufficient detail to allow the Office of Mission Acquisition Solutions (OMAS) to determine if 
the party can perform the requirement. All responses must be sent via email to Contracting 
Officer, Rukshani Levy, at Rukshani.Levy@hhs.gov and Contract Specialist, Teferi 
Gebremariam, at teferi.gebremariam@hhs.gov by no later than 11:00 am EST on 
Tuesday, July 07, 2026. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed 
requirement based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the 
Government. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining 
whether to conduct a competitive procurement. In order to receive an award, Contractors 
must be registered and have valid certification through SAM.gov. Reference solicitation 
number: 75N98026Q00474 on all correspondence.

1.0  BACKGROUND 
The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Office of Information Technology (OIT), 
Infrastructure Operations (IO) requires software upgrade perpetual licensing—from 25 
devices to 50 devices—along with continued maintenance and technical support for 
Schneider Electric (SE) EcoStruxure Power Monitoring Expert (PME) software. 
EcoStruxure PME collects system data from SE networked meters integrated 
throughout IO’s data center support infrastructure, enabling critical monitoring of 
electrical performance and power quality. The requirement includes a perpetual 
software license (1–50 devices), ongoing maintenance and technical support, and 
access to Schneider Electric software engineering personnel familiar with IO’s metered 
architecture and SE source code. This software is critical for collecting and analyzing 
power consumption, quality, and load flow data from proprietary SE networked meters 
currently deployed across VA data centers.

Veterans Health Administration (VHA) Print & Mail Requirements 
 
1. Program Objectives 
• Establish a compliant, efficient bulk print-and-mail solution for VHA, based on Veterans 
Integrated Service Networks (VISNs) and stations. 
 
• Support the Oracle Health bulk printing to process Portable Document Format (PDF) letters 
and metadata outputs. 
 
• Provide a scalable framework for national rollout across multiple VISNs. 
 
• Ensure regulatory compliance, including the Cures Act and Department of Veterans Affairs 
(VA) security requirements. 
 
• Commercial Off-The-Shelf/Government Off-The-Shelf/Managed Print/Mail as a Service 
product to consume manifest metadata ﬁles and PDF letters to print and mail to 
customers. 
 
• Custom Development solutions, minimally for integration efforts (e.g., Application 
Programming Interface (API)) 
 
• Solution can be on or off-site. 
 
• Meet VHA Policy 1088 requirements and Service-Level Agreements (SLAs) for print and 
mail delivery. 
 
• Projections for economies of scale. 
 
• The Contractor shall provide all necessary resources to ensure compliant, reliable, 
scalable, and auditable services in support of Veteran communications (mailing and 
printing). 
 
2. Technical Integration Requirements 
 
• Ability to integrate with the Veterans Affairs Enterprise Cloud (VAEC) and VISNs.  
 
• Support for APIs, Amazon Web Services (AWS)/Azure File Storage, and secure system 
interfaces. 
 
• Provide development, test, staging, and production environments. 
 
• Provide integration test plans, data, and results. 

Page 2 of 8 
 
• Nightly automated data transfer of print and mail metrics to VHA Data Warehouses. 
 
• Provide a complete and updated data dictionary when appropriate. 
 
• Use secure connectivity compliant with VA security and governance policies.  VA 
Handbook 6500 – Risk Management Framework for VA Information Systems. 
 
• VA handbook 6500.6 for Protected Health Information (PHI) & Personally Identiﬁable 
Information (PII) security handling and compliance. 
 
• Transfer data via AWS S3 between VAEC and contractor Federal Risk and Authorization 
Management (FedRAMP) type / GovCloud West account. 
 
• Support either account-to-account permissions or keys/secrets for secure transfer. 
 
• VHA deposits letters twice daily (5am & 5pm Central Time) 
 
– Each batch has a single consolidated Extensible Markup Language (XML) manifest 
text ﬁle that has metadata for all the letters in that batch  
 
– Each batch has a separate PDF for each letter that needs to be printed 
 
• The Contractor must consume XML metadata to generate coversheets. 
 
• Support two monitoring models: 
– AWS S3/Azure Storage object-creation event notiﬁcations to contractor Simple 
Queue Service; or 
– Contractor polling the bucket at the scheduled times 
 
• Automate deletion of letters from VHA VAEC AWS/Azure Storage immediately after 
contractor pulls them. 
 
• Automated management of letter lifecycle, including but not limited to intake, printing, 
mailing, archiving, and deleting. 
 
• The Contractor deletes letters and metadata from their own bucket after 60 days, unless 
otherwise directed: 
– The Contractor shall securely destroy retained ﬁles after the retention period 
– The Contractor shall provide certiﬁcates of destruction upon request 
– The Contractor shall support legal hold requirements when directed by VA 
 
• Support both PDF-to-PDF (current) and text-to-PDF (future) workﬂows. 
 
• Validate ﬁle transfer, parsing, and printing workﬂows against Oracle Health output. 
 

Page 3 of 8 
 
• Establish discrepancy handling for manifest mismatches (reporting or email). 
 
• Full continuity of operations (COOP) and disaster recovery plans, capabilities, and periodic 
testing: 
 
– The Contractor shall support geographically redundant operations and secondary 
print capabilities 
– Recovery Time Objective shall not exceed four hours 
– Recovery Point Objective shall not exceed ﬁfteen minutes 
– The Contractor shall conduct annual failover and restoration testing 
 
• The Contractor solution shall comply with the following frameworks and directives: 
 
– VA Directive 6502 – Enterprise Privacy Program 
– VHA Directive 1605.01 – Privacy and Release of Information 
– Federal Information Security Modernization Act requirements 
– Federal Information Processing Standards 140-2 (or successor) encryption 
requirements 
– Section 508 accessibility requirements 
– Role-based access control and multifactor authentication 
 
3. Printing Requirements 
 
• Daily capacity to process black-and-white letter print jobs/day, scaling from 50,000 to 
millions per month per VISN, equating to over 11,000,000 per month for all clinical bulk 
printing needs. 
 
• Surge support for print and mail events that will increase by a Rough Order of Magnitude. 
 
• High volume print production with commercial-grade output quality. 
 
• Support letters – pages on standard 8.5x11 paper. 
 
• Large letters supporting up to 25 pages or greater. 
 
• Generate a templated cover page compatible with window envelopes. 
 
• Printed pages must include barcode margins to support insertion accuracy. 
 
• The Contractor shall comply with applicable Government Publishing Office (GPO) Quality 
Assurance Through Attributes Program standards, including current versions of GPO 
Publications 310.1 and 310.2, or approved equivalent commercial print-quality standards 
acceptable to VHA. 
 

Page 4 of 8 
 
• Automated folding, insertion, envelope preparation. 
 
• Print accuracy SLA of 99.7% or higher. 
 
4. Mailing Requirements 
 
• Provide envelopes and all mailing supplies. 
 
• Provide First-Class mail services using VISN/station existing postage account 
o Domestic and Foreign mailings 
 
• Implement pre-sorting to optimize postage cost and delivery time. 
 
• Include VA-provided Quick Response codes on coversheets directing Veterans to 
MyHealtheVet. 
 
• Process mail according to United States Postal Service (USPS) National Change of Address 
(NCOA) rules. 
 
• The Contractor shall notify VA whenever a National Change of Address (NCOA) update is 
identiﬁed. The Contractor shall not change the mailing address on its own. Unless VA 
provides conﬁrmation or updated address instructions, the Contractor must mail each 
letter to the address exactly as printed on the original VA-provided correspondence. 
 
• 99.7% mailing accuracy SLA. 
 
• The Contractor shall support USPS Intelligent Mail Barcode standards and USPS Informed 
Visibility tracking integration. 
 
5. Reporting & Audit Requirements 
 
• Provide full-lifecycle status transparency for all letters.  Lifecycle statuses shall include at a 
minimum: Received, Validated, Queued, Printed, Inserted, Mailed, USPS Accepted, 
Archived, Deleted, and Failed. 
 
• Monthly and annual cost summaries aligned to volume projections. 
 
• Reports must include delivery tracking, volume statistics, and processing timelines 
– End to end tracking for every letter 
 
• Support for barcode/unique identiﬁer tracking. 
 
• Timestamp capture for: 
– Received jobs  
– Processed jobs  

Page 5 of 8 
 
– Printed jobs  
– Mailed jobs  
– Failures/exceptions  
– Trends over time 
– Breakdown by VISN and Facility Codes 
– Letter Type  
– Mail transmission  
– USPS handoff 
 
• Status updates returned to originating system. 
 
• Nightly automated data transfer or report metrics to VHA Data Warehouse. 
 
• The Contractor shall provide automated rejects for failed prints, failed mailings, manifest 
mismatches, and operational exceptions -- 
– Daily alerts for failure of letters to print of mail (format to be jointly determined by 
VHA and contractor) 
– Report missing/extra ﬁles based on manifests 
– Alerts to VISN/Station for mailing failures requiring reprint or remail 
 
• Provide VHA access to contractor’s internal reporting system. 
 
• Support real-time tracking using barcodes and USPS’s Informed Visibility API. 
 
• Graphical self-service reporting dashboard for 500+ authorized users. 
 
• The Contractor shall provide ad hoc reporting capabilities. 
 
• The Contractor shall support audit logging for all administrative and operational actions. 
 
• The Contractor shall retain audit logs for a minimum of seven years unless otherwise 
directed by VA. 
 
• The Contractor shall notify VA of security incidents within one hour of discovery. 
 
6. Testing & Pilot Requirements 
 
• Conduct comprehensive mock testing using VA-provided sample datasets. 
 
• Validate workﬂows, tracking, and connectivity before production. 
 
• No production PHI or PII shall be used in non-production environments unless expressly 
authorized. 
 
  

Page 6 of 8 
 
7. Deliverables 
 
• Plan for scaling when needed. 
 
• Completed secure AWS transfer conﬁguration. 
 
• No production PHI or PII shall be used in non-production environments unless expressly 
authorized. 
 
• Pilot test report, test plans, test scripts, expected results, and test evidence validating 
workﬂows and connectivity. 
 
• Automated daily operational print-and-mail status reports. 
 
• Automated monthly operational and cost reports per VISN. 
 
• Reporting must be grouped and ﬁlterable by VISN, Station ID, Zip Codes, States, Countries, 
Letter statuses. 
 
• Postage cost reports per VISN. 
 
• System architecture documentation. 
 
• Interface control documentation and XML schema deﬁnitions. 
 
• Security documentation supporting Authority to Operate (ATO) activities. 
 
• Disaster Recovery and COOP documentation. 
 
8. Security, Privacy, & Compliance 
 
• Ability to obtain and maintain ATO/Interim ATO per VA Handbook 6500. 
  
• Must meet National Institute of Standards and Technology Special Publication 800 53 Rev5 
Moderate baseline controls.  
 
• FedRAMP compliance for cloud-hosted systems. 
 
• Encrypted transfer and storage of all PHI/PII/ Controlled Unclassiﬁed Information (CUI).  All 
PHI, PII, and CUI shall be encrypted in transit and at rest. 
 
• No production PHI or PII shall be used in non-production environments unless expressly 
authorized. 
 

Page 7 of 8 
 
• All contractor staff must complete annual VA security/privacy training. 
 
• Support VA audits, vulnerability scanning, and penetration tests. 
 
• Print facilities must meet all VA contract and privacy standards and be open to VA 
inspections by VA Security teams. 
 
• Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1196 Privacy, Security, and Breach 
Notiﬁcation Rules (45 CFR Parts 160 and 164). 
 
9. Assumptions & Constraints 
 
• Both VHA and contractor operate in AWS GovCloud us-gov-west. 
 
• Both parties provide required AWS access and sample test data. 
 
• The Contractor must meet VA policies, FedRAMP , and Cures Act standards. 
 
• VISN/Station postage account used for mailing; costs managed via each VISN. 
 
• The Contractor must send letters to the printer twice daily — aligning to the morning and 
evening deposit cycles — and both batches must meet the established cutoff times.  
Letters must be mailed immediately upon receipt to meet the 7-calendar day delivery 
requirement. 
 
• VHA deposits letters seven days per week. 
 
• Each letter has a unique Event ID. 
 
• Each address must contain at least two lines or be rejected. 
 
• No international letters unless country ﬁelds are added. 
 
• No portfolio PDFs (no embedded ﬁles). 
 
10. Governance and Operational Support 
 
• The Contractor shall provide designated program management and escalation contacts. 
 
• The Contractor shall maintain documented incident management and change 
management processes. 
 
• The Contractor shall provide operational support during all approved production 
processing windows. 
 

Page 8 of 8 
 
• The Contractor shall support recurring governance meetings with VA stakeholders. 
 
11. SLAs 
 
• System availability shall be 99.9% monthly, excluding approved maintenance windows. 
 
• Critical incidents shall receive an initial response within 30 minutes. 
 
• Letters received before established processing cutoff times shall be printed and inducted 
into USPS within agreed operational windows. 
 
• The Contractor shall support reprint and remail workﬂows for failed correspondence. 
 
12. Optional Features 
 
• Color printing and the capacity to bind folios or magazine type booklets and patient 
education materials, posters and ﬂyers.  Also, both front and back printing for A4 letter and 
post cards, and the capacity to send inserts like community announcements.

GENERAL INFORMATION

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

DESCRIPTION

NOTICE OF INTENT

INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE: SIEMENS SYNGO.VIA SERVER MIGRATION AND SOFTWARE UPDATE SUPPORT SERVICE.

THIS IS NOTICE OF INTENT TO SINGLE SOURCE FOR A SERVER MIGRATION SUPPORT AND SOFTWARE UPDATES FOR THE SIEMENS SYNGO.VIA SERVERS UTILIZED IN RADIOLOGY AND NUCLEAR MEDICINE FOR THE SAN DIEGO VA HEALTHCARE SYSTEM: This is not a request for competitive proposals. This is not a solicitation or request for offers. No solicitation package is available, and telephone requests will not be honored.  

The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), VISN 22 Long Beach, intends to award a new Firm Fixed Price, Single Source contract to Siemens Medical Solutions USA, the sole provider of software maintenance and support for its proprietary software products, which includes the Syngo.via software. 

Awarding this contract directly to Siemens Medical Solutions USA—the sole provider of software maintenance and support for its proprietary software products, including Syngo.via—ensures the VA maintains continuity of service and support for these critical systems, leverages Siemens’ technical expertise and exclusive access to necessary proprietary components, and aligns with government security and operational standards. This single source strategy minimizes service disruption, supports compliance, and streamlines contract and system management for both ongoing maintenance and future software updates

The authority for applying this statute implemented for restricting competition on this procurement is FAR 8.405-6(a)(1)(i)(B) per the requirements of FAR 6.302-1(a)(2)(i).     

The intent is to provide the server migration support and applicable software updates for the Siemens Syngo.via servers mentioned above on a single source basis. No solicitation will be posted to Contract Opportunities. The primary North American Classification System Code (NAICS) is 541511: Custom Computer Programming Services. The most current Business Size Rating for this NAICS is $34 Million. 

Capable parties may identify their interests and authorization to respond to this requirement by July 2nd, 2026, at 04:00 PM (PST).

   

A determination by the Government not to compete with this proposed award upon response to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Contracting Officer.

PART 1: GENERAL INFORMATION

1.1. DESCRIPTION OF SERVICES/INTRODUCTION: The contractor shall provide all necessary management, personnel, equipment, tools, materials, and supervision required to reconfigure critical communications equipment within the Emergency Communications Center (ECC) at Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson (JBER), AK, at Bldg. 8517, room #2 as defined in this Performance Work Statement (PWS).

1.2. SCOPE: The contractor shall safely shut down, disconnect, relocate, and restore full functionality to specified communications systems. This includes the Monaco fire dispatch/alarm system, VESTA 911 system, Motorola base station radios, and other associated miscellaneous items. The work involves moving equipment to new workstations, modifying network infrastructure including moving ethernet ports and fabricating new cables, and providing professional cable management. A critical component of this PWS is the requirement that all systems are brought back to full operational status post-relocation.

1.3. PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE: The Period of Performance will be determined at the time of award and coordinated with the Technical Adviser POC. 

1.4. GENERAL INFORMATION:

1.4.1. PRE-WORK CONFERENCE: The contractor shall attend a pre-work conference with the Technical Adviser POC to discuss the project plan and schedule prior to commencing any work.

1.4.2. WORKING HOURS: The contractor shall perform work during regular business hours, 0800-1630, Monday through Friday. The final work schedule must be coordinated with and approved by the Technical Adviser POC at least 14 days prior to the start of work.

1.4.3. SECURITY REQUIREMENTS:  The contractor is responsible for obtaining all required base access passes. Contractor personnel shall be clearly identifiable and must maintain a professional appearance.

1.4.4. SAFETY REQUIREMENTS: The contractor shall perform all work in a safe manner and shall comply with all applicable Federal, State, and local safety laws and regulations, including OSHA standards for electrical work and Electrostatic Discharge (ESD) handling procedures.

1.5. QUALITY ASSURANCE: The Government will monitor the contractor’s performance in accordance with the Performance Requirements Summary (See Part 7).

PART 2: DEFINITIONS & ACRONYMS

2.1. DEFINITIONS:

Technical Adviser POC: The Government official responsible for technical oversight and administration of the contract.

2.1.2	Critical System: A system whose failure would impact the mission capability of the Joint Emergency Communications Center.

2.1.3	Fully Functional: A state where a system, including all its hardware and software components, operates in accordance with manufacturer specifications and mission requirements without any degradation of performance.

2.1.4	Professional Cable Management: The practice of organizing, securing, and labeling cables in a neat, orderly, and professional manner to ensure system serviceability and prevent hazards.

2.2. ACRONYMS:

ESD: Electrostatic Discharge

JBER: Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson

JECC: Joint Emergency Communications Center

OSHA: Occupational Safety and Health Administration

PWS: Performance Work Statement

QC: Quality Control

PART 3: GOVERNMENT FURNISHED ITEMS AND SERVICES

3.1. SERVICES: The Government will provide access to available utilities, including water, electricity, heating, and cooling, at no cost to the contractor for the sole purpose of accomplishing the work specified herein.

3.2. FACILITIES: The Government will provide the contractor with access to the ECC work site.

PART 4: CONTRACTOR FURNISHED ITEMS AND RESPONSIBILITIES

4.1. GENERAL: The Contractor shall furnish all supervision, labor, equipment, tools, and materials required to perform all work specified in this PWS.

4.2. MATERIALS: The contractor shall provide all consumable materials, including but not limited to ethernet cabling (Cat 6 or higher), RJ-45 connectors, cable ties, and labeling materials required for the reconfiguration and cable management tasks.

PART 5: SPECIFIC TASKS

5.1. TASK 1: PROJECT MANAGEMENT AND COORDINATION: The contractor shall coordinate with the Technical Adviser POC to develop a detailed project and cutover plan. This plan must be approved by the Technical Adviser POC prior to any work commencing and must include a phased approach to minimize system downtime. The primary ECC should not be down for more than 5-7 business days. 

5.2. TASK 2: EQUIPMENT SHUTDOWN AND RELOCATION: The contractor shall perform a coordinated shutdown of all systems to be moved in accordance with manufacturer specifications. The contractor shall carefully disconnect, label, and safely move the following equipment to new workstations as identified by the Technical Adviser POC:

Monaco fire dispatch/alarm system components.

VESTA 911 system components.

Motorola base station radio consoles and associated equipment.

All associated peripherals: monitor tower mount, 2 keyboards, 2 mice, 2 landline phones and 1 clock.

5.3. TASK 3: RE-INSTALLATION AND SYSTEM RESTORATION: The contractor shall re-install all equipment at the new workstations. A critical requirement of this task is the complete restoration of system functionality. Should any system or component fail to come back online or function as required due to the contractor's performance of the work, the contractor shall be solely responsible for all labor, parts, and services necessary to remedy the issue and restore full functionality at the contractor's own expense.

5.4. TASK 4: CABLE MANAGEMENT AND INFRASTRUCTURE: The contractor shall be responsible for all network and power cable modifications. This includes moving existing ethernet ports where feasible and creating, terminating, and testing new ethernet cables as required to reach the new workstation locations. The contractor shall provide professional cable management for all relocated workstations, ensuring all cables are neatly routed, secured, and labeled at both ends.

5.5. TASK 5: SYSTEM TESTING AND ACCEPTANCE: Upon completion, the Technical Adviser POC and ECC personnel will conduct a full functional test of all relocated systems. Final acceptance will be granted only after the Technical Adviser POC verifies that all systems are 100% functional and all work described in this PWS has been completed to a satisfactory standard.

5.6. TASK 6: SITE CLEAN-UP: The contractor shall remove all debris, excess materials, and tools from the work site upon completion, leaving the area in a clean and orderly condition.

PART 6: APPLICABLE PUBLICATIONS

The contractor shall adhere to the latest editions of relevant industry standards for telecommunications cabling, such as those from the Telecommunications Industry Association (TIA), TIA-568 and TIA-606. 

PART 7: ATTACHMENT/TECHNICAL EXHIBIT LISTING:

Statement of Work 
1. Project Name: Assurance on Autonomous System 
2. Background 
As NASA begins deploying artificial intelligence in safety-critical applications such as 
mission control and flight software, traditional verification and validation (V&V) methods 
prove insufficient for addressing the non-deterministic behavior inherent to AI systems. 
The challenge is particularly acute for autonomous spacecraft in congested and contested 
space environments that must detect threats, resolve failures, and maintain trust without 
human intervention through self-diagnosis, self-healing, and zero-trust operations. This 
effort will culminate in actionable recommendations tailored to NASA's software 
assurance practices, with findings validated through collaborative testing with pilot flight 
projects to ensure practical applicability and effectiveness. 
 
3. Scope 
The contractor shall perform the following tasks: 
- Perform a comprehensive review of cutting-edge AI V&V approaches across various 
AI-enabled systems operating at different autonomy levels 
- Examine relevant government agency standards and frameworks (including DoD 
and NIST guidelines 
- Analyze private sector practices for safety-critical AI implementations to the extent 
that the information is made public 
- Talk to NASA’s projects that plan to employ autonomous systems to understand 
their specific requirements and workflows 
- Identify two open-source AI testing tools and apply the tools on the ASTRA 
framework (or other example/similar AI models); and identify strength, weaknesses, 
and gaps. 
- Synthesize the findings as a report and provide actionable recommendations 
tailored to NASA’s Software Assurance practices 
- Build a basic software prototype that illustrates selected findings and is compatible 
with the ASTRA framework 
 
4. Schedule, deliverable dates 
Milestones: 
- Demonstrations of open-source tools: 2 months after the start date for first tool, 3 
months after the start date for the 2nd tool. 
- Progress and strategic meeting: Every week after the start date 
- Report synthesizing findings and actionable recommendations: 4 months after the 
start date 
- Software Prototype: 4 months after the start date 
 

5. Place of Performance: Contractor’s Facility 
 
6. Period of Performance: June 15, 2026 through October 15, 2026 
 
Protection of Background IP. Contractor retains ownership of all Background IP 
incorporated into, used in, or related to the performance of this effort. No license or other 
rights to such Background IP are granted except as expressly provided herein. Any rights to 
use Contractor Background IP beyond the specific project deliverables shall be subject to 
a separate written license agreement defining the scope of rights and any applicable 
licensing fees or other consideration. No license shall be granted by implication, 
disclosure, delivery, or performance under this effort.
