FORT BELKNAP INDIAN HEALTH SERVICE                                                                                                                                
STATEMENT OF WORK FOR HEALTH INSURANCE VERIFICATION AND 
MEDICARE CLAIMS MANAGEMENT SERVICES 
 
1. PROJECT TITLE: Medicare and Private Insurance Claims Management and Insurance 
Eligibility Services 
 
2. BACKGROUND/PURPOSE:  
 
The Mission of the F ort Belknap Service Unit is to provide the best possible healthcare 
services to the Fort Belknap Service Unit community members and all other eligible Native 
Americans.  The purpose of this contract is to enhance and to maximize third party revenue 
and collection activities for the business aspect of health care and its revenue generation 
activities.  
 
The Fort Belknap Service Unit aims to maintain and to create an efficient, streamlined 
process for claims management and insurance eligibility verification services. To meet this 
mission, the Fort Belknap Indian Health Service has identified a need for an online claims 
management and eligibility verification software to provide a centralized service for billing 
services and to track revenue generation.  
 
 
The vendor will provide technology that works with the Electronic Health Record of Indian 
Health Service and identified third party eligibility information and workflow plus 
Medicare AR reporting and workflow for the Fort Belknap Service Unit. The need to verify 
eligibility for the various health insurance programs in real time will enhance operations 
for the business aspect of health care. Effective services for Medicare claims will keep the 
hospital on top of capturing reimbursement dollars from the patie nt’s initial point of 
service. These services make an impact on the reduction of staff overtime costs and will 
drastically reduce the need for follow-up of the claims denied. 
 
The Fort Belknap Service Unit requires an application that will provide daily Medicare AR 
report for efficient account management. These services shall be in compliance with 
HIPAA, IHS OIT mandates, and the Privacy Act.  
       
3. SCOPE:  
 
The contract resulting from this solicitation shall: 
 
1. Attain comprehensive eligibility information– make eligibility requests to 
Medicare. 
 
2. Perform batch eligibility checks – determine eligibility status for multiple 
patients at one time. 
 

3. Better manage workflow with a customizable dashboard that prioritizes and 
assigns patients, payers and daily task lists. The application allows user to set up 
reminders and notes to staff at multiple locations.  
 
4. Experience integration between eligibility and claims functions.  
 
5. Eliminate repetitive tasks with the ability to run multiple payers and patients in 
one session. 
 
6. Increase efficiency when checking eligibility – verify a patient’s eligibility 
status with Medicare. 
 
7. Save significant time using batch imports of eligibility data files.  
 
8. Enhance record-keeping with access to all eligibility transaction history. 
 
 
Claims Management  Monthly Estimated 
Number of Claims 
Annual Estimated 
Number of Claims 
Medicare             310          3,720 
Private Insurance            360          4,320 
 
The contractor shall provide a secure exchange data software solution that provides 
technology for: 
 
• Connectivity to the Medicare DDE (Direct Data Entry/FISS (Fiscal 
Intermediary Standard System) and automated claims status reporting, 
payment floor details and other reports 
• Eligibility verification Medicare 
• Eligibility results must include start and end dates of coverage 
• Third party insurance medical claims validation, approval and processing 
services via a clearinghouse for Medicare, Medicaid, VA and Commercial 
Payers for the Fort Belknap Service Unit 
• Processes all claim types: Emergency, Inpatient, Outpatient and Specialty 
Clinics; and provide both solicited and unsolicited claims status 
• The software must provide rigorous and thorough claims rules and custom 
business rules 
• Capability for self-monitoring usage of services for thresholds 
• Training and support related to scope of work-training provided either on-site 
or via teleconference 
 
The software services shall comply with the following constraints: 
 
• The software service shall not require the Fort Belknap Service Unit to install 
contractor software within the Fort Belknap Service Unit or Indian Health 
Service network. 

 
• The service shall enable the Fort Belknap Service Unit to exchange data 
utilizing a Secure File Transfer Protocol (SFTP) as approved by the Indian 
Health Service Office of Information Technology. 
 
• The service shall support Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) transactions and 
interactive Telnet application protocol sessions. 
 
• The service shall support unlimited users and access shall be workstation 
independent. 
 
• The service shall not entail development of Health Insurance Portability and 
Accountability Act (HIPAA) transaction set translation or mapping processes, 
non-CMS or non-IHS generated data or messages, or data reformatting.   
 
 
4. APPLICABLE DOCUMENTS:   
 
Secure internet-based connectivity to all current fiscal intermediaries. 
 
Ability to send medical emergency, Inpatient, Outpatient, and Specialty claims to 
Medicare Contractor using secure date exchange technology. 
 
Unlimited Direct Data Entry (DDE) online Medicare claims status/corrections for 
Medicare Part A. 
 
All electronic transactions and DDE/FISS shall provide confidentiality, authentication, 
integrity and non-repudiation. 
 
Automated batch 837/835 file transfers. 
 
Automated batch 276/277 claims status capability. 
 
Accept electronic claims from Resource Patient Management System (RPMS). 
 
Reports and acknowledgements on all claims sent. 
 
5. TASKS:   
 
Simple user-friendly interface with a single sign-on login and ID. Eligibility verification 
for hundreds of payers, with information that includes co-pays, termination dates, 
deductibles and coinsurance  
1. Consistent data displays of response results by payer class  
2. Quick batch entry – check eligibility status for multiple patients with a single 
payer  

3. Multiple insurance eligibility verification – check a patient’s eligibility status at 
multiple insurance plans simultaneously  
4. Alerts to indicate other coverage for Medicare patients – instances of HMO 
enrollment, dual eligibility, Medicare as a Secondary Payer, and many more 
admissions scenarios are brought to the attention of designated personnel  
5. Ability to filter Service Type Code (STC) queries and responses and save your 
favorites, organized by payer  
6. All-payer eligibility access 24/7 – easily verify data after hours and on weekends  
7. Storage of all validation transactions for historical proof of eligibility status 
when eligibility is challenged retroactively  
8. Flexible revalidation option for either an individual patient or batch without 
having to rekey demographic data  
9. Option to run recurring batches for your patient census to regularly monitor 
insurance coverage  
 
10. Easy implementation, with minimal IT involvement –web-based services are 
compatible with current versions of industry-leading browsers 
 
6. DELIVERABLES AND DELIVERY SCHEDULE:  
 
Provide a single secure electronic location to manage all electronic claims, including VA claims.   
Verify Medicare and Commercial Payer eligibility in real time and batches. 
Provide knowledgeable support personnel to assist with any issues regarding the processing of the 
medical claims. 
The Contractor shall provide toll free telephone/technical support during normal business hours, 7 
AM to 7 PM, Monday thru Friday, except Government holidays. 
The Contractor shall provide a two (2) hour minimum response time from notification by IHS at 
no additional cost to the Fort Belknap Service Unit. 
The medical claim processing services shall meet the following standards: 
insurance medical claims shall be submitted to the appropriate carrier/payer via the 
Contractor provided clearinghouse by close of the next business day after receipt from 
IHS. 
Medical insurance shall be transmitted electronically to the appropriate carrier/payer. 
The Contractor shall use routine editing procedures to detect defects in medical claims 
information supplied by the government.  The Contractor shall reject and not process all 
medical claims with defects.  The Contractor shall provide the service location with edit 
status reports listing the defect to aid the service location in the correction of the detected 
defects.   
The Contractor shall provide for correction all claims rejected by the all carriers/payers 
for any reason other than the inappropriate format to the claims. 

The Contractor shall provide the capability for medical claim errors to be corrected and 
resubmitted electronically and provide a report of rejected medical claims within 4 hours 
of batch submission. 
The Contractor shall make available productivity and submission reports within 24 hours 
of batch transmission. 
 
7. GOVERNMENT-FURNISHED EQUIPMENT AND INFORMATION:   
 
Secure internet-based connectivity to all current fiscal intermediaries. 
 
Ability to send medical emergency, Inpatient, Outpatient, and Specialty claims to 
Medicare Contractor using secure date exchange technology. 
 
Unlimited Direct Data Entry (DDE) online Medicare claims status/corrections for 
Medicare Part A. 
 
All electronic transactions and DDE/FISS shall provide confidentiality, 
authentication, integrity and non-repudiation. 
 
Automated batch 837/835 file transfers. 
 
Automated batch 276/277 claims status capability. 
 
Accept electronic claims from Resource Patient Management System (RPMS). 
 
Reports and acknowledgements on all claims sent. 
 
8. PLACE OF PERFORMANCE:   
 
Online insurance verification software access.   
 
9. PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE: 
    
 Base Year:  10/01/2026 – 09/30/2027 
 Option Year 1: 10/01/2027 – 09/30/2028 
 Option Year 2: 10/01/2028 - 09/30/2029 
 Option Year 3: 10/01/2029 – 09/30/2030 
 Option Year 4: 10/01/2030 – 09/30/2031 
 
 
   
10. SECURITY:   
 
Secure internet-based connectivity to all current fiscal intermediaries. 

 
 
 
 
 
 
11. PRIVACY ACT CLAUSES 
 
                                      Privacy or Security Safeguards (Aug 1996) 
 
(a) The Contractor shall not publish or disclose in any manner, without the Contracting Officer’s 
written consent, the details of any safeguards either designed or developed by the Contractor under 
this contract or otherwise provided by the Government. 
(b) To the extent required to carry out a program of inspection to safeguard against threats and 
hazards to the security, integrity, and confidentiality of Government data, the Contractor shall 
afford the Government access to the Contractor’s facilities, i nstallations, technical capabilities, 
operations, documentation, records, and databases. 
(c) If new or unanticipated threats or hazards are discovered by either the Government or the 
Contractor, or if existing safeguards have ceased to function, the discoverer shall immediately bring 
the situation to the attention of the other party. 
 
Privacy Act (December 18, 2015) 
 
This contract requires the Contractor to perform one or more of the following: (a) design; (b) 
develop; or (c) operate a Federal agency system of records to accomplish an agency function in 
accordance with th e Privacy Act of 1974 (Act) ( 5 U.S.C. 552a(m)(1))  and applicable agency 
regulations. 
The term system of records means a group of any records under the control of any agency from 
which information is retrieved by the name of the individual or by some identifying number, 
symbol, or other identifying particular assigned to the individual. Violations of the Act by the 
Contractor and/or its employees may result in the imposition of criminal penalties ( 5 U.S.C. 
552a(i)). 
The Contractor shall ensure that each of its employees knows the prescribed rules of conduct in 45 
CFR part 5b and that each employee is aware that he/she is subject to criminal penalties for 
violation of the Act to the same extent as Department of Health and Hu

STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW) 
Discharge Care Plan 
Overton Brooks VAMC 
510 E. Stoner Avenue 
Shreveport, LA. 71101 
1. PURPOSE   
The purpose of this Statement of Work (SOW) is to procure access to a subscription-based, 
patient-centered discharge care planning platform, specifically the Engineered Care Patient Care 
Plan (or equal), for use at Overton Brooks VA Medical Center (OBVAMC), 510 E. Stoner 
Avenue, Shreveport LA 71101. 
This procurement supports the implementation and sustainment of Project Greenlight, a facility-
led quality improvement initiative designed to enhance discharge communication, improve 
patient understanding of post-hospital care instructions, and reduce avoidable readmissions. The 
Engineered Care platform provides a standardized, evidence-based, and patient-friendly 
discharge care plan that translates complex clinical information into clear, actionable guidance 
tailored to a health literacy level appropriate for the Veteran population.  
The system will replace or augment existing discharge documentation processes by delivering 
individualized, easy-to-understand care plans that improve care transitions from inpatient to 
outpatient settings. This solution is expected to improve key performance metrics, including 
patient experience, care coordination, medication understanding, and overall patient safety.  
This acquisition will be conducted as a brand name or equal procurement for a base year with 
four option years, ensuring continuity, scalability, and sustained impact on discharge processes 
across the facility.  
 
2. SCOPE.  
 
The successful vendor will license the use of the Discharge Care Plan  software to the Overton 
Brooks VAMC and support the installation, implementation, and customization of the Discharge 
Care Plan software.   
The license grant includes, at no additional charge, the right to make and use a reasonable number 
of copies of the Software for testing, back-up, archival and disaster recovery purposes, and of the 
Documentation for internal training, support and deployment.  
The successful vendor will provide the following solution: 
 
• Creation of Discharge Care Plans  with health literacy appropriate patient discharge 
instructions for patients. 

2 
 
• Report functionality to enable continual quality improvement and performance tracking.  
• Administrative interface to perform user management, application configuration and 
auditing. 
• Integrate the DCP software with the hospital-based Vista software used for evidence-
based, Vista-Integrated Discharge Instructions.  Care Transition Portal replaces a site`s 
existing CPRS discharge note with a patient-friendly discharge instruction booklet that: 
* Has been shown to reduce unnecessary readmissions * Is customized for the VA 
environment to help educate veterans about their care and additional VA programs * 
Improves the discharge process at a VA site while providing leadership opportunities for 
clinical staff. This is new software that will interface with CPRS to improve the discharge 
process. It allows the care givers to have one source to print Care Plans, discharge 
medication list, the patients schedule appointments, etc. End-users will access via CPRS 
Tools.  Engineered Care grants to the Customer a license for the Customer and its Users 
to use the Product, during the Term. Term of license is 5 years. 
 
• Allow care givers to have one source to print Care Plans, the patients schedule 
appointments, etc., through access via CPRS Tools. 
 
• Clear discharge instructions compiled in a booklet to keep instructions in one place and 
be easier for veteran patients to review and understand and follow their Care Plans, in 
one easy booklet.  
 
• Technology that is table integrated application intended to improve the patient discharge 
process by providing education regarding patient diagnosis, documentation follow -up 
appointment and discharge services, confirms the medication plan, reviews steps on what 
to do if a problem arises, assesses the patient’s understanding of the plan, gives the 
patient a written discharge plan to take home review and follow. 
 
 
3. SPECIFICATIONS.   
The successful vendor will work with designated clinical and IT representatives of the Overton 
Brooks VAMC to deploy the Vista integrated Discharge Care Plan. This work will include 
installation, configuration and customization as required. 
 
3.1 Salient Characteristics/Deliverables: 
  
The proposed software will include the following features: 
 
• Discharge planning software for providers 
• Creation of health literacy appropriate patient discharge instructions  configured for 
optimal access by Overton Brooks VAMC staff 
• Reporting functionality to enable continual quality improvement and performance 
tracking 

3 
 
• IT Professional interface to perform user management, application configuration and 
auditing 
• User accounts will be created for all users 
• Customized to match Overton Brooks  VAMC branding requirements including logo 
placement 
• Addition of Overton Brooks VAMC is related Congestive Heart Failure (CHF) discharge 
instructions 
Vendor will create and print a Care Plan booklet for every veteran discharged from the Overton 
Brooks VAMC site.  The Care Plan will include the following data to the extent that they are 
available within the system: 
 
• Branded Site Logo 
• Patient Aligned Care Team details 
• Patient Demographics 
• Medications 
• Appointment Information 
• Instructions on care and management of primary discharge diagnosis 
• Diet and Activity Instructions 
• Additional Instructions 
• My HealtheVet information 
 
3.2 Discharge Care Plan Software Installation and Configuration  
 
DCP Software setup.  Install the software on the designated server system and create initial user 
accounts for testing.     
3.3 Implementation and Customization of Discharge Care Plan 
Vendor will customize the Discharge Care Plan for the Overton Brooks VAMC concerning 
specific medicines and procedures at Overton Brooks VA Medical Center.  The DCP booklet 
will be customized to address/improve care delivery. 
4. PERFORMANCE MONITORING 
 
The successful vendor will p rovide periodic performance reporting during the course of DCP 
software installation and deployment. Overton Brooks VAMC will have real-time access to the 
DCP software during this time and may conduct periodic product sampling to verify compliance 
with requirements.  
 
5. SECURITY REQUIREMENTS 

4 
 
Software shall operate within the VA internal/intranet side of the web system (VAWW).   VA 
sensitive information will reside within the vendor database. 
DCP uses an MDWS interface to VISTA and uses Remote Procedure Calls already defined in 
VISTA (RPC Broker calls). At least 3 other technologies were reviewed. This one has the most 
complete discharge instructions that meet the needs of our veterans. There is no existing 
technology for a discharge planning booklet in the VA. It is the only standard that integrates with 
the CPRS Chart.   
 
6. TRAINING 
 
Contractors shall provide comprehensive training on the use of the DCP software being 
purchased for all staff members that are to use this software.   At a minimum, training shall 
include but not be limited to technical and operational training.  Instruction/user guides shall be 
provided for both training and technical and operational usage.  
 
Training shall occur at Overton Brooks VAMC, 510 E. Stoner Avenue Shreveport, LA. 71101 
via online, instructor drives classes during normal business hours, 8:00am-4:30pm, Monday 
through Friday. Training date and time shall be prescheduled and preapproved by the contracting 
officer’s representative prior to initiation. 
 
7.  EVALUATION FACTORS: 
 
a. Technical Capability 
b. Past Performance 
c. Price 
 
Technical Capability and Past Performance, when combined, are more important than price. 
 
8. CHANGES TO STATEMENT OF WORK 
 
Any changes to this Statement of Work shall be authorized and approved only through written 
correspondence from the contracting officer or their representative.  
 
9. CONTRACT AWARD MEETING 
 
An award meeting will not be held.  
 
10. POP (Modify based on contract award date) 
 
Term of License ("Term") 
The Term of the license will be firm-fixed for 1 (one) Base Year and 4 (four) Option Years, as follows: 
 
Base Year  04/01/26  03/31/27  $24,000 
Option Year 1  04/01/27  03/31/28  $24,000 
Option Year 2  04/01/28  03/31/29  $24,000 
Option Year 3  04/01/29  03/31/30  $24,000 
Option Year 4  04/01/30–  03/31/31  $24,000

Request for Information:  
Digital Asset Management Platform for WeRemember.ABMC.gov and the Burial 
Memorialization Electronic Directory (BMed) 
June 12, 2026 
Overview: 
American Battle Monuments Commission is issuing this Request for Information for market 
research. ABMC seeks industry input on cloud based digital asset management platforms and 
transition approaches that can enhance or replace the current platform at WeRemember.ABMC.gov 
and support long term stewardship of burial and memorialization records, digital assets, and public 
access services. 
ABMC is particularly interested in digital asset management platforms that are proven, 
support federal requirements, and can be configured without excessive custom development 
such as (in alphabetical order): Alfresco, Aprimo, ArchivesSpace, AtoM, Axiell DAMS powered by 
Piction, Bynder, Canto, Hyland, Nuxeo, OpenText, Preservica, ResourceSpace, and comparable 
digital asset management or archival platforms.   
Background: 
ABMC maintains burial and memorialization records for approximately 250,000 service members 
and related digital content used by families, researchers, staff, and the public. The current 
environment relies on Knowvation and Microsoft SQL and contains both structured data and large 
volumes of unstructured content such as scanned documents, photographs, and other historical 
materials. ABMC seeks a secure, modern, and easy to use digital asset management platform that 
supports public research and internal records operations in one governed environment. The solution 
should improve search, digital asset control, records stewardship, public usability, internal 
workflows, role based access, reporting, secure integration, staff managed administration, and long 
term support while preserving record integrity, data history, and public trust and avoiding vendor 
lock in. 
Response Criteria: 
Interested vendors should address the following topics with enough detail to support platform, 
migration, security, schedule, and cost comparisons. General capability statements without 
specific platform, migration, schedule, cost, and security detail may not be useful for acquisition 
planning. 
1. Platform Overview 
Identify the proposed digital asset management platform and any major supporting products. 

Page 2 of 4 
 
State whether the solution is vendor hosted, customer hosted, or hybrid. State whether the 
platform is delivered primarily through configuration or requires custom development. 
Please explain why it fits ABMC’s mission better than other options. 
2. Public Portal and Search 
Describe how the solution supports public search by name, date, cemetery, memorial, unit, 
state, branch, conflict, and other attributes. Address faceted filtering, fuzzy search, OCR, 
accessibility, map-based exploration, and presentation of individual service member profiles 
and cemetery pages. 
3. Digital Asset Management Capabilities 
Describe how the solution manages documents, images, media, metadata, version history, 
rights or visibility rules, and relationships between digital assets and authoritative records. 
Explain how the platform supports archival stewardship, long term discoverability, and 
controlled public release. 
4. Internal Records and Workflow 
Describe internal records and case management capabilities, including access to supporting 
files, update and correction workflows, approvals, task management, reporting, and audit 
support. 
5. Migration from Knowvation 
Explain how the solution will transition data and content from Knowvation and Microsoft 
SQL into the target DAM environment. Address source inventory, source preservation, 
metadata mapping, normalization, discrepancy handling, duplicate review, attachment 
migration, record linking, audit history preservation, rehearsal loads, validation, cutover, 
rollback, and ABMC approval gates. Vendors shall also explain how source and target data 
will remain fully exportable and traceable for future transition or replacement. 
6. API and Integration Capabilities 
Describe support for secure RESTful APIs, metadata exchange, bulk import and export, 
record synchronization, approved dataset publication, and integration with internal and 
external systems. Address compatibility with V A Veterans Legacy Memorial, OAI PMH or 
equivalent metadata publishing, authentication methods, logging, monitoring, rate limiting, 
and interface documentation. 
7. Administration and Maintainability 
State what ABMC staff can manage directly without contractor support, including metadata, 
forms, workflows, branding, reports, search settings, user roles, and digital asset 
presentation. Explain how the solution reduces lock in, avoids dependence on proprietary 
administration tools, and preserves ABMC control over configuration, documentation, and 
day to day operations. 
8. Security, Information Assurance, and Secure Development 
Describe the security approach, including team roles, escalation paths, incident handling, 
continuous monitoring, secure development practices, code review, dependency and 
vulnerability scanning, hardening, secrets management, logging, audit trails, encryption, role 

Page 3 of 4 
 
based access, least privilege, records protection, and support for federal security reviews and 
audits. 
9. Hosting and Compliance 
Describe hosting options, data residency, backup and recovery, continuity of operations, and 
alignment with federal security and records requirements. ABMC prefers a FedRAMP 
Moderate provider but will consider commercial systems that demonstrate robust 
information security controls, sound compliance practices, and clear support for federal 
security and records requirements. State current authorizations and security posture clearly. 
If the solution relies on future or pending authorizations, state that plainly. 
10. Implementation Approach 
Provide a high level implementation approach covering discovery, requirements validation, 
experience or prototype validation, migration planning, configuration, testing, training, 
cutover, stabilization, and transition to support. Distinguish clearly between product 
configuration and custom development. 
11. Support Model 
Describe help desk support, patching, upgrades, defect resolution, service levels, post go live 
monitoring, ticket management, escalation, vendor accountability, and transition out support 
at the end of the contract, including knowledge transfer, documentation handoff, open ticket 
disposition, and orderly turnover to ABMC. 
12. Relevant Experience and Registration 
Identify similar projects involving federal agencies, digital asset management, archival 
systems, historical collections, memorialization, cemetery records, research portals, or 
records centric platforms.  
Provide past performance for similar projects with enough detail to show platform 
relevance, delivery scale, scope, customer type, and operating maturity. State whether the 
company is registered in SAM.gov. 
13. Rough Order of Magnitude 
Provide a rough order of magnitude for licensing, implementation, migration, training, 
hosting, and ongoing operations and maintenance. Identify key assumptions, major cost 
drivers, and expected schedule ranges. 
14. Transition Out and No Vendor Lock In 
ABMC does not accept vendor lock in. Vendors shall explain how ABMC can transition out 
at the end of the contract without loss of data, metadata, audit history, records relationships, 
documents, configurations, or administrative control. Describe data export formats, bulk 
export capabilities, documentation, interface ownership, configuration portability, source 
code ownership for custom components, knowledge transfer, and any tools or licenses 
ABMC would need to continue operations or transition to another provider. 

Page 4 of 4 
 
Important Considerations for Vendors: 
1. ABMC is more interested in practical transition plans, controlled migration, and durable 
records and asset management than in generic web redesign concepts. 
2. ABMC wants clear platform identification, not open ended or undefined backend choices. 
3. ABMC is interested in better public research usability, including search quality, geographic 
context, and respectful presentation of memorialization data. 
4. ABMC encourages vendors to identify where standard platform capability ends and where 
custom work begins. 
5. ABMC is interested in digital asset management approaches that support archival 
collections, descriptive metadata, public discovery, and secure internal stewardship. 
 
Response Format and Submission Instructions:  
Responses should be limited to 20 pages, excluding product literature, and should include the 
following: 
1. Company information and primary point of contact 
2. Platform overview and hosting model 
3. Technical approach and key capabilities 
4. Implementation and migration approach 
5. Relevant experience, past performance for similar projects, and SAM.gov registration status 
6. Rough order of magnitude pricing and major assumptions 
 
This RFI is for market research only. It does not constitute a solicitation or a commitment by 
ABMC to issue a future procurement. ABMC will not reimburse vendors for the cost of preparing a 
response. Information received may be used to refine acquisition strategy, requirements, and 
evaluation criteria for any future action. 
ABMC encourages vendors to propose practical digital asset management alternatives and transition 
strategies that improve reliability, usability, search quality, digital asset stewardship, administrative 
control, and long-term support while preserving mission data and minimizing disruption. 
Please submit your responses to Ms. Jessica Young at youngj.ctr@abmc.gov by Friday, July 10, 
2026.

Deep Space Advanced Radar Capability (DARC) Interim 
Contractor Support (ICS) Industry Day Instructions  
Introduction  
The United States Space Force (USSF), Space Systems Command (SSC), System Delta (SYD 85) is hosting 
an Industry Day to discuss the upcoming Interim Contractor Support (ICS) requirements for the Deep 
Space Advanced Radar Capability (DARC). DARC is a critical, multi-site global radar network designed to 
provide continuous, 24/7 space domain awareness in contested environments. The Government’s intent 
during the ICS period is to secure robust, cadence-based sustainment, maintenance, and logistics 
support while simultaneously laying the groundwork for a seamless transition to long-term Contractor 
Logistics Support (CLS). We are seeking industry partners with proven expertise in operating and 
sustaining geographically dispersed mission-critical infrastructure, executing complex supply chain 
management under strict Financial Improvement and Audit Remediation (FIAR) standards, and 
maintaining stringent Department of War (DoW) cybersecurity standards within an Impact Level 5 (IL5) 
boundary. 
Problem Set  
Sustaining the DARC enterprise during the ICS period presents a highly complex, multi-tiered logistical 
and operational challenge. The successful contractor must simultaneously manage Level 1 (on-site) and 
Level 2 (Depot-Level) maintenance across remote, global sites while operating within strict host-nation 
environmental, security, and power connection regulations. Furthermore, the contractor must establish 
a fully functional Contractor-Inventory Control Point (C-ICP) to manage peculiar spares and support 
equipment, utilizing Scope IMS (Scope Inventory Management System) to ensure 100% accountability 
and FIAR compliance in the Government's Accountable Property System of Record (APSR). Compounding 
these logistical hurdles is the requirement to maintain strict system availability (Ao) and cybersecurity 
compliance Authority to Operate / Risk Management Framework (ATO/RMF) through cadence-managed 
software version releases, continuous vulnerability remediation, and seamless transition of Contractor 
Acquired Property (CAP) to Government Furnished Property (GFP). The Government is challenging 
industry to present agile, data-driven sustainment strategies that resolve these global logistical 
bottlenecks, minimize peculiar support equipment, and ultimately deliver draft Performance Work 
Statement (PWS) frameworks that enable a risk-free transition to steady-state CLS.

This D&F is prepared in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 7.107-2 (a) to 
support a consolidated acquisition over $2M.  
 
FINDINGS 
 
1. Mission Area and Contracting Activity.   
 
 Requesting Activity Agency: FPAC 
 
 Contracting Activity: OCP-POD 
 
2. Acquisition Information:  
 
Solicitation/Contract/Order Number 12314426Q0100 
Period of Performance 07/01/2026-06/30/2031 
Estimated Total Amount $44,065,708.98 
 
3. Description of the Requirement:  The requirement consolidates the ongoing requirement for 
AWS cloud operational support services that currently sustain approximately 400 business 
applications. Historically, the network services were fulfilled using four separate contracts.  
These contracts contained overlapping and related requirements.  Market research determines 
that the consolidation of these commercially available services would result in significant 
cost savings, reducing administrative burden, and improved mission support.    
 
The proposed consolidation includes the following scope of work:

4. Selection of Acquisition Strategy 
 
a. Market Research Summary: Market research included a review of multiple federal and 
USDA acquisition channels, including the GSA Polaris Governmentwide Acquisition 
Contract (GWAC), the USDA Sustainment Operations of Applications Blanket Purchase 
Agreement (BPA), the USDA STRATUS Pool 2 Basic Ordering Agreement (BOA)

Authority to Consolidate Contract Requirements 
Solicitation Number: 12314426Q0100 
 
 
Page 2 of 6 
Rev. 4/9/26 
vendors, and the NIH Information Technology Acquisition and Assessment Center 
(NITAAC).   STRATUS Pool 2 includes a broad base of qualified vendors, with 21 small 
and 15 other-than-small businesses responding, demonstrating robust competition 
consistent with USDA cloud procurement policy requirements. USDA Departmental 
Regulation DR-3650-001 requires mandatory consideration of STRATUS cloud 
acquisition vehicles. The STRATUS program is further characterized as a preferred and 
modernized cloud acquisition platform designed to support federal agencies with scalable 
cloud solutions, per USDA cloud policy and vendor program descriptions. STRATUS’s 
competitive structure and wide vendor base are documented benefits, including rapid 
access to cloud capabilities and maximized contractor competition.  Compared with other 
acquisition pathways reviewed, specifically GSA POLARIS, USDA’s Sustainment 
Operations of Applications BPA, and NITAAC, the STRATUS BOA offers the most 
targeted alignment with USDA’s cloud governance framework, providing cost 
optimization, streamlined ordering, and defined compliance with USDA IT policy. 
STRATUS is consistently identified as the preferred next-in-priority solution when 
internal BPA options either do not apply or do not provide equivalent technical breadth or 
capacity.  Given the documented vendor diversity within STRATUS Pools, especially 
Pool 2, which includes dozens of awardees across the small business track as 
demonstrated in publicly posted award information, this acquisition vehicle ensures 
ample competitive opportunity for small businesses, aligning with USDA small-business 
utilization goals.  Based on these findings, the contracting officer can be assured that 
utilizing STRATUS will provide a highly competitive environment with meaningful 
small business participation and represents the most efficient and policy-aligned 
acquisition strategy for this requirement.   
 
b. Alternative Contracting Approaches: If the projected efficiencies and cost savings are not 
realized, the USDA could transition to individual contracts to cover the requirement.  
This alternative may be less advantageous as it results in increased administrative burden, 
firewall and network security risks, higher costs and reduced efficiency.    
 
c. Coordination: The determination has been coordinated with the Office of Small 
Disadvantaged Business Utilization Office.   
 
d. Impact on Small Business: This acquisition will be set aside for small businesses, 
ensuring continued opportunities for small business participation, mitigating the risk that 
consolidation could otherwise concentrate work among larger contractors. The USDA 
has taken significant steps to ensure minimal disruption to small businesses while 
achieving substantial cost savings through consolidation. This approach balances the 
need for efficiency with the commitment to supporting small businesses. By leveraging 
the STRATUS Pool 2 small business track, the USDA creates a competitive environment 
that encourages innovation and cost-effectiveness among participating vendors. This 
strategy underscores the importance of a collaborative relationship between the 
government and small businesses, fostering growth and maintaining high-quality service 
delivery.

5.  Benefits of Consolidations 
a. The consolidation was justified in accordance with FAR 7.107-1 and FAR 7.107-2.  
By consolidating these requirements, the Government anticipates projected 
efficiencies. Consolidation reduces duplicative efforts, eliminates technical debt, 
strengthens security, and ensures consistent best‑practice implementation across all 
Mission Areas.  The approach improves management efficiency, operational 
reliability, and accountability by using a single contractor coordination framework. 
 
Pricing will be firm-fixed price under a level-of-effort task order structure. Labor 
categories and planned staffing levels (e.g., 1,920 hours per FTE per year) are used to 
assess the technical approach; however, invoicing will be based solely on fixed 
monthly CLIN prices, which represent the agreed-upon level of effort and defined 
outcomes. Payments will not be tied to hours expended but to the contractor’s 
delivery of the specified effort, outcomes, and service levels. 
  
 
b. Cost Savings or Price Reductions:

The costs across all four contracts were compared to the consolidated effort IGCE of 
$44,065,708.98 for a base plus four option periods resulting in a total quantifiable savings of 
$116,811,386.19 (72.6%). 
 
The IGCE was developed using historical pricing and General Services Administration 
(GSA) labor rates mapped to the requirement outlined in the consolidated Performance Work 
Statement (PWS). 
 
6. Quality Improvements that will save time or enhance performance or efficiency: A 
single consolidated procurement reduces workload and administrative duplication 
compared to four separate contracts.  A single procurement cycle produces a single

award structure and standardized tasking framework, reducing future ordering lead 
time. 
 
7. Reduction in acquisition lead time: A single consolidate procurement aligns the period 
of performance and offers an opportunity to use an established basic BOA with defined 
compliance with USDA IT policy, standardized tasking framework and reduced future 
ordering lead time.  
 
8. Terms and Conditions: Consolidation allows USDA to apply a single, consistent set of 
security, SLAs, governance, and reporting requirements across all 400 applications, 
aligning with enterprise needs. Reduced variance in contractor performance with a 
single prime to meet consistent obligations rather than different vendors operating 
under different clauses 
 
 
9. Other Benefits: Consolidation improves mission support by removing duplication and 
strengthening operational continuity.  By consolidating under an acquisition vehicle 
that maintains competitive vendor pools the USDA ensures multiple small businesses 
can propose and participate. One contract requires one set of reviews, COR oversight 
structures, performance tracking, and reporting cycles rather than four. 
    
 
10. The total benefits quantified in dollar amounts are: a savings of $106,638,997.89 for the 
aggregate contract value.

notifications in FAR 7.103-3 will be issued within the required timelines and no solicitation 
will be issued until the approved timeframe after required notifications.

NCIA Request for Information (RFI) 
 
To: Industry Partners 
 
  
1. The NATO Communications and Information Agency (NCIA) is conducting market 
research to identify qualified vendors and gather input on potential solutions to support the 
upcoming acquisition for Encrypted Traffic Interception (ETI) solutions . To that end, we 
are issuing the attached Request for Information (RFI)  424365 to solicit feedback from 
capable and interested industry partners. 
 
2. This RFI is issued for planning purposes only and is not a request for bids . It is part of 
NCIA’s effort to ensure it has a clear understanding of the marketplace, available 
capabilities, and potential acquisition strategies.

recommendations for improving performance outcomes,  competition, and

A. Introduction 
 
1. The NATO Communications and Information Agency (NC IA) is conducting market 
research to identify potential sources and gather information regarding industry 
capabilities to support the requirement to create an accurate and current view of the 
state-of-the-art Encrypted Traffic Interception (ETI) solutions that can be provided 
through Commercial of the Shelf (COTS) products, solutions and/or services . This 
Request for Information (RFI) is issued solely for informational purposes and does not 
constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Quotation (RFQ), or invitation 
for bid.  
 
B. Purpose 
 
1. The purpose of this RFI is to obtain input from industry to help inform the NCIA’s 
acquisition planning. Responses to this RFI will assist in refining requirements, 
identifying capabilities, and shaping the strategy for any future solicitation. 
 
C. Background 
 
1. The purpose of this Request for Information (RFI) is to create an accurate and current 
view of the state -of-the-art Encrypted Traffic Interception (ETI) solutions that can be 
provided through Commercial of the Shelf (COTS) products, solutions and/or services. 
The feedback received through the RFI will be used to evolve existing capabilities in 
NATO and define future needs. The inputs will be used to help NATO define future 
requirements within these capabilities and to shape future acquisitions.  Responses 
should focus on current mature solutions, products or services, although  responders 
are also provided an opportunity in a separate section to volunteer details of 
evolutionary plans and future roadmaps.

Sources Sought Notice for the United States Marine Corps (USMC) Aviation Distributed 
Virtual Training Environment (ADVTE) III 
  
1.0 Description 
 
The Naval Air Warfare Center Training Systems Division (NAWCTSD), Procurement Department, 
at Orlando, FL, announces its intention to procure for the Naval Air Systems Command 
(NAVAIRSYSCOM), PMA205,  the Aviation Distributed Virtual Training Environment (ADVTE) 
III which is the United States Marine Corps (USMC) ADVTE and Tactical Environment (Ten) 
Subsystem combined requirement; henceforth known as ADVTE III. 
 
ADVTE is the Marine Corps Aviation’s currently implemented solution that provides integrated and 
networked training.  ADVTE, as a persistent and integrated system-of-systems solution, currently has 
the capability to network various Type/Model/Series (T/M/S) Marine Corps Aviation Training 
System (MC ATS) training devices located across First (1D), Second (2D), Third (3D), and Fourth 
(4D) Marine Aircraft Wing (MAW) locations for the purposes of conducting multi-site, multi T/M/S 
simulated networked training missions to maintain proficiency and enhance aircrew readiness.    
 
The USMC TEn is a key software and hardware subsystem that is currently installed in nearly every 
USMC Aviation Training System. The USMC TEn is the current Marine Aviation’s Semi-
Automated Force (SAF) / Computer Generated Forces (SAF/CGF) solution and also provides the 
High Level Architecture interface enabling MC ATS training devices to link with other trainers for 
distributed mission training. The government is open to a different SAF/CGF solution for providing 
this capability to meet the needs of the USMC distributed and stand-alone training requirements. 
 
The current ADVTE baseline serves and provides the capability to connect multiple MC ATS 
training devices together at the following locations: Marine Corps Air Station (MCAS) Camp 
Pendleton, CA; MCAS Miramar, CA; MCAS Yuma, AZ; Marine Corps Air Ground Combat Center 
(MCAGCC) Twentynine Palms, CA; Marine Corps Base (MCB) Camp Lejeune, NC; MCAS Cherry 
Point, NC; MCAS New River, NC; MCAS Beaufort, SC; MCAS Futenma, Japan; MCAS Kaneohe 
Bay, HI; and Joint Reserve Base (JRB) Fort Worth, TX.  By Light Professional IT Services (formerly 
known as Veraxx Engineering Corp) delivered the current ADVTE and current Tactical Environment 
(TEn) baselines.  ADVTE in its current configuration was procured under multiple Delivery Orders 
under a single awardee indefinite delivery indefinite quantity (IDIQ) contract (N61340-22-D0002) 
that was competitively awarded.  The current, “as delivered” ADVTE configuration is anticipated to 
be completed no later than FY2028. 
 
The Tactical Environment configuration and software baseline was procured under a Sole Source 
IDIQ contract (N61340-22-D0009) that was awarded to By Light Professional IT Services. By Light 
IT Services was the only company with the highly specialized knowledge and experience with the 
current TEn software code, and who could modify it without unacceptable delay in meeting the 
Government’s requirement to provide full-scale integration into USMC trainers and ADVTE 
infrastructure at the time this IDIQ Contract was awarded. The current TEn hardware baseline is 
anticipated to be completed no later than FY2028. The current TEn subsystem is integrated into 
multiple training devices at the following locations:  MCAS Camp Pendleton, CA, MCAS Miramar,

CA; MCAS Yuma, AZ; MCAS Cherry Point, NC; MCAS New River, NC: MCAS Futenma, Japan; 
and MCAS Kaneohe Bay, HI.  In addition, there are Distributed Interactive Simulation Bridges and 
Navy Aviation Simulation Master Plan (NASMP) bridges used to connect training devices that do 
not have a TEn subsystem installed to perform distributed training. 
ADVTE III periodically is in need of technical upgrades due to obsolescence issues with earlier 
fielded locations and the TEn software will require updates for functionality improvements such as 
adding new entities, weapons, players, graphical user interface updates, and sensors. 
 
The anticipated contract action for ADVTE III described herein includes: 1) the technological 
upgrade of the currently fielded ADVTE equipment to include the TEn Software and hardware 
baseline or different SAF/CGF solution.  Overall, this effort is considered to be a comprehensive 
update to continue to modernize existing equipment and update the TEn software baseline or other 
SAF/CGF solution as required for new capabilities and functionality. If a different SAF/CGF 
solution is planned to be proposed to meet the requirements in this effort, this solution is required to 
be non-proprietary and have government purpose rights. The necessary Government Furnished 
Information (GFI) will be provided to potential offerors in order to be able to bid (to include the TEn 
executable software code).   
 
Components of ADVTE III include: 
 
MC ATS training devices. Fielded MC ATS training devices located at USMC Marine Aviation 
Training System Sites that connect, or are planned to be connected into ADVTE that utilize the 
USMC Tactical Environment (TEn) as the interoperability solution. 
 
USMC Tactical Environment (TEn) and bridges. The USMC TEn is a key software and hardware 
subsystem that is installed in nearly every USMC Aviation Training System. The USMC TEn is 
Marine Aviation’s required Semi-Automated Force (SAF) / Computer Generated Forces (SAF/CGF) 
solution and also provides the High-Level Architecture interface enabling MC ATS training devices 
to link with other trainers for distributed mission training. This subsystem facilitates stand-alone 
(independent) and networked modes of trainer operation with other training systems across the 
USMC ADVTE.   The ADVTE Navy Aviation Simulation Master Plan (NASMP) bridge is used to 
connect the F-18 MC ATS training devices to other MC ATS training devices that have a TEn 
subsystem integrated into them. The ADVTE Distributed Interactive Simulation (DIS) bridges are 
used to connect MC ATS training devices to other training devices that use DIS for distributed 
training.   
 
Network Exercise Control Centers (NECC). Each NECC is a centralized point of connection, control, 
and coordination for all USMC ATS devices located at each site.  The NECCs support training 
federations operating simultaneously, and digital recording of missions for playback from selectable 
audio and video channels to support Joint Brief/De-Brief requirements. They also provide 
instructor/operator, observer stations, and TEn functionality; 2D/3D visualization from any 
geographic location or tactical environment entity; simulated tactical radios with the ability to 
connect to all MC ATS training devices when connected to ADVTE; and (IP-based) Secure Video 
Teleconferencing (VTC). Each NECC is capable to connect to all other NECCs. NECCs are 
currently installed at MCAS Camp Pendleton, CA; MCAS Miramar, CA; MCAS Yuma, AZ; MCAS 
New River, NC; MCAS Futenma, Japan; MCAS Kaneohe Bay, HI. Each NECC is configured per 
individual site requirements.

ADVTE Point of Presence connections.  ADVTE Point of Presence connections consists of ADVTE 
equipment to support distributed mission training are located at the MCB Camp Lejeune, NC; MCAS 
Beaufort, SC; MCAS Cherry Point, NC; BSC Camp Pendleton, CA; JRB Fort Worth, TX; and

Common Virtual Training Area (CVTA). CVTA is a MC ATS term and is anticipated to be 
analogous to a common synthetic visual data base area (or areas).  It is anticipated that the CVTA 
will be implemented to minimize MC ATS training device visual system correlation issues under this

Statement of Requirements 

eTesting Officer Training School/Holm Center/DE

 

 

1.0  PURPOSE. Modernize assessment capabilities across the USAF officer school training complex. The Holm Center is responsible for commissioning approximately 80 percent of all USAF officers, making a robust, reliable yet flexible testing essential. The system must support validation of learning outcomes through both paper-based and online testing—paper-based delivery when campus internet connectivity is limited or unavailable, and online testing when connectivity is reliable. The solution must also interface seamlessly with existing test bank architecture (ParTest and ParScore) to preserve historical test item performance statistics and enable long-term tracking of curriculum effectiveness.    

 

2.0  DESCRIPTION OF ITEMS. The requested requirement is for comprehensive test delivery and scoring software. The software must provide hybrid assessment delivery (both paper and online administration). Online assessments must allow test-takers to log in and complete their assessments; software must be able to receive student data in multiple formats (e.g. Excel, PDF, etc.) and export student data (test results) in multiple formats (e.g. Excel, PDF, etc.); activate lockdown and time-elapse features when test is initiated to prevent test compromise and ensure test-taker time requirements. Software must analyze test results; store tests as individual test-takers and/or across multiple class rosters for data aggregation; capture test-taker date; rescore tests when applicable test item analysis/challenges are requested; enable test-takers to retake test when required; and contain immediate test soring feature. In addition, the software must include the ability to create (build), modify, and store multiple test item banks;  provide detailed test item analysis to evaluate the effectiveness of test questions; allow questions to be imported from various sources or creation of new ones; employ testing lockdown features in alignment with emergency test stoppage (continuation feature upon emergency completion). It must also generate printed test booklets for use with Scantron forms or deliver tests online; provide test statistics and test validation features.  Software must have the capability to seamlessly provide over 5000 student assessments annually.

Brand name: Scantron Eva Exam software is the updated direct replacement for the now unsupported Scantron ParTest and ParScore software suite. It is fully backward compatible with the existing proprietary architecture, allowing us to seamlessly import test question banks from the obsolete (existing) platform into the new system. This compatibility is critical, as it preserves historical test item performance statistics and aggregated data across multiple cohorts, both past and present. In addition, the existing test banks represent thousands of labor hours. Upgrading to a compatible, modern solution is the most efficient use of time, funding, and personnel, and avoids significant costs associated with recreating assessment content.

2.1  SOFTWARE SPECIFICATIONS REQUIRED  

 

2.1.1 Software must be compatible with ParTest and ParScore allowing direct import of existing test banks and historical data from obsolete (existing) software.   

2.1.2 Must capture test item performance past to present in content transfer conversion. 

2.1.3 Have robust customizable analytics package that is customizable to organizational hierarchy used in OTS: overall class performance, squadron performance, and individual flight performance. 

2.1.4 Role-based security allowing different permissions between the test administrator, department chairs on instructional design teams, and leadership; ability to view performance across the enterprise. 

2.1.5 Operate in both paper-based and digital environments. 

2.1.6 Ability to import student data with customized student IDs used to onboard students in OTS environment. 

2.1.7 Provide browser lockdown capability to preclude test compromise in a digital environment.   

2.1.8 Platform agnostic for end-users (laptop and tablet with different operating systems (Windows and Apple device compatibility)

2.1.9 Test Administrator must operate in Windows 11 or higher environment (with software upgrades coinciding with any Windows upgrades)

2.2.0 Software compatible with relevant plug-ins to ensure test security

2.2.1 Software “sandbox” experience for 30 days to ensure compatibility with current system using current test items 

2.2.2 Supported by multiple browsers for online exam participants (Microsoft Edge, Chrome, Firefox, etc.)

2.2.3 Ability to export test result data in multiple formats and reports.

 

        2.2.  EQUIPMENT AND OTHER PERIPHERALS REQUIRED 

 

      2.2.1 Software (Scan Station License) downloads to stand-alone computer (nonNIPR). 

2.2.2 Tech support (US-based) Monday – Friday. 

2.2.3 Software updates completed outside testing timeframes. 

2.2.4 WCAG 2.0 Level AA compliant

2.2.5 iNSIGHT ES4 scanner (document feeder; duplex capability; B/W with 200 dpi resolution; twain driver; multipage TIFF files with group IV compression)

2.2.6 24-pound scantron paper or equivalent

 3.0  DELIVERY REQUIREMENTS:   

 

3.1 Cloud-based software that downloads operational program and subsequent software updates.  

 3.2 OTS: 550 E. Maxwell Blvd, Bldg. 1487, Room C106, Maxwell AFB AL 36112

 

4.0  INSTALLATION REQUIREMENTS: Concise software installation instructions.

 

5.0 TRAINING REQUIREMENTS: Provide initial software training to test administrators and instructional design department chairs. Provide a digital User’s Guide that clearly explains how to configure the software. Technical Support: The contractor shall provide hands-on user training and comprehensive technical support, including unlimited US-based technical telephone support.

  

6.0 STANDARD WARRANTY: The contractor shall provide any Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) standard commercial warranty applicable to the products being purchased at no additional cost to the Government.  

 

 6.1 Prior to project acceptance, the contractor shall provide the customer with all manufacturer warranties as needed for any component incorporated into this project such as equipment manuals, literature, CDs and DVDs and other documentation on all equipment and software. 

 

6.2 Prior to project acceptance, the contractor shall provide written procedures, points of contact within company, and required information for all warranty services prior to project acceptance. This information shall include written confirmation of the warranty period, phone numbers and contact information/procedures for technical support, troubleshooting assistance, and replacement of faulty equipment and software. 

 

7.0   GENERAL INFORMATION: Items must be brand new.  Refurbished items are not authorized. The design of Eva Exam is such that it will allow downward compatibility with ParTest and ParScore currently in use by the Holm Center.  Scantron created both software products and the proprietary architecture is compatible between these software products.  The upgrade (Eva Exam) will streamline the upgrade conversion and support both paper-based and online testing. Additionally, this supports AFAC line of effort to recruit the Airmen and Guardians the Nation needs to win any future fight.

Draft Requirement

Enterprise Artificial Intelligence Governance, Management, and Implementation Support

Purpose

The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Chief AI Officer (CAIO) and associated offices requires contractor support to facilitate enterprise-level artificial intelligence (AI) management, standards, and strategic implementation. The Contractor shall provide a multidisciplinary team capable of managing the full lifecycle of AI use case review, regulatory compliance tracking, stakeholder engagement, data pipeline management, and governance product development – as well as a dedicated capability to assess VA’s enterprise AI landscape, prioritize investments, and drive scalable AI adoption across VA. This support will enable the VA to responsibly adopt, scale, and oversee AI technologies in a manner consistent with federal law, policy, and the best interests of Veterans and VA personnel. VA requires contractor support to meet these obligations across the workforce with widely varying degrees of AI familiarity and across program offices with distinct missions, cultures, and risk tolerances.

Background

VA is one of the largest federal agencies in the United States, serving millions of Veterans across hundreds of facilities and digital touchpoints. As AI technologies become increasingly embedded in VA operations from clinical decision support to benefits adjudication and workforce tools the need for structured, enterprise-wide AI governance has grown significantly.

Federal mandates have established clear expectations for responsible AI use in government. OMB Memorandum M-25-21 (Accelerating Federal Use of AI through Governance, Innovation, and Leadership) requires agencies to implement governance frameworks that enable AI adoption while managing risk, promoting transparency, and protecting civil liberties. Compliance with this memo and related Executive Orders requires dedicated expertise, robust tooling, active stakeholder management, and a continuous feedback loop between policy, technology, and operations.

 Scope / Mission

The Contractor shall support the VA's enterprise AI governance mission through two functional tracks:

Track 1 – AI Management and Standards: AI use case review and inventory management; AI and large language model (LLM)-enabled governance tooling; AI-augmented response quality improvement; data pipeline and validation management; human-centered design and user experience (UX) testing for governance products; strategic communications and enterprise solutioning; and transition support for a federated AI governance model. 

Track 2 – AI Strategy and Enterprise Execution: Enterprise AI and agentic AI landscape assessment and platform evaluation; AI investment prioritization and roadmap development; and implementation coordination.

Period and Place of Performance

The Period of Performance consists of one 12-month base period with four 12-month option periods for continued support.

Place of Performance: 

Work shall be performed primarily at Contractor facilities. Contractor personnel may be required to support on-site activities at VA Central Office (Washington, D.C.) or other VA facilities as mission needs dictate. Travel requirements, if any, shall be coordinated in advance and reimbursed in accordance with the Federal Travel Regulation (FTR).

5. Performance Objectives (Required Results)

The Contractor shall provide and sustain a single, integrated team capable of achieving all of the following required results concurrently:

Track 1 – AI Management and Standards

AI Use Case Review & Inventory Management: The Contractor shall conduct structured intake, review, and risk tiering of all VA AI use cases in accordance with applicable federal policy and VA governance frameworks. The Contractor shall baseline workload assumptions, including estimated monthly use case volume, anticipated number of stakeholder engagements, expected number of technical assessments and reporting cadence. The Contractor shall maintain a current, accurate, and auditable enterprise AI use case inventory and produce regular summary reports on use case pipeline status, risk distribution, and review outcomes for VA leadership. The Contractor shall deliver a Monthly Enterprise AI Use Case Inventory and Pipeline Report, including status, risk tier, owner, review stage, aging, pending decisions, and required federal reporting fields.

AI/LLM-Enabled Governance Tooling: The Contractor shall design, develop, implement, and maintain LLM- and AI-enabled technical solutions that automate or augment use case tracking, documentation management, and compliance status monitoring. All AI/LLM-enabled tooling must operate only within VA-approved environments and must be interoperable with VA-approved systems, repositories, identity/access controls, and reporting environments. Solutions shall be scalable, interoperable with existing VA systems, and aligned with VA security and privacy requirements. Contractor-developed workflows, prompts, configurations, data schemas, dashboards, documentation, and technical artifacts shall be reusable by VA and transferable at contract closeout. The Contractor shall continuously improve tooling based on user feedback and evolving policy requirements. 

AI-Augmented Response Quality: The Contractor shall apply AI and LLM capabilities to review, improve, and quality-assurance governance guidance, policy responses, use case decisions, and stakeholder-facing communications. AI-generated outputs must be subject to documented human review before being used for high-impact, rights-impacting, clinical, benefits, privacy, safety, or compliance-sensitive decisions. The Contractor shall establish and maintain, in collaboration with VA, quality standards and feedback mechanisms that ensure consistent, accurate, and policy-aligned outputs while reducing turnaround time across the enterprise.

Data Pipeline & Validation Management: The Contractor shall build and manage data pipelines supporting AI governance workflows, including use case intake, compliance tracking, and reporting dashboards. The Contractor shall perform ongoing data validation, cleansing, and integrity checks to ensure governance decisions are informed by accurate and complete data, and shall maintain documentation for all data flows, schemas, and validation rules. The contractor shall deliver a Monthly Data Governance and Validation Report documenting data sources, validation results, error rates, remediation actions, and unresolved data quality issues.

Design & UX Testing for Governance Products: The Contractor shall apply human-centered design principles to develop and iteratively improve governance-facing products, portals, and tools. The Contractor shall conduct UX research and usability testing with representative VA user populations — including staff with limited AI familiarity — and shall ensure all governance products meet federal accessibility standards (Section 508). Prior to development of governance-facing products, portals and tools, though, the contractor and VA will establish the minimum expectations for user research, usability testing, accessibility testing, representative VA user groups and Section 508 validation.

Strategic Communications & Enterprise Solutioning: The Contractor shall develop and execute communications strategies that effectively convey AI governance requirements, processes, and decisions to a large, diverse enterprise audience. This includes a recurring Strategic Communications and Stakeholder Engagement deliverable covering completed communications, planned outreach, training materials, stakeholder feedback, risks, and adoption barriers. The Contractor shall produce plain-language content, briefings, training materials, and change management support tailored to stakeholders with varied levels of AI literacy, from frontline staff to senior leaders. The Contractor shall identify and solution for cross-cutting governance challenges spanning multiple VA components, facilitating stakeholder engagement sessions, working groups, and feedback mechanisms to ensure governance processes remain inclusive and responsive.

Federated Governance Model Transition: The Contractor shall support the VA's transition from a centralized to a federated AI governance model, enabling distributed governance responsibilities across VA administrations, staff offices, and program offices while maintaining enterprise-wide consistency and accountability. This includes developing and implementing a federated governance framework and a Federated AI Governance Transition Plan that defines roles, responsibilities, decision rights, escalation paths, readiness criteria, training needs and component-level governance expectations. The framework should identify and support component-level AI governance leads, establishing clear roles, responsibilities, and decision rights at each tier of the governance structure, and designing scalable processes and tools that empower distributed teams to execute governance activities within VA-wide standards. The Contractor shall provide training and training deliverables, including training schedule, materials, attendance tracking, stakeholder feedback and updates based on policy or process changes. The Contractor shall provide change management support and ongoing advisory services to federated governance stakeholders to ensure a smooth and sustainable transition that does not create compliance gaps or inconsistencies across the enterprise.

Regulatory Compliance: The Contractor shall support VA’s compliance by maintaining a Federal AI Compliance Tracking Report that identifies applicable requirements, compliance status, open actions, risks and upcoming reporting deadlines.  The Contractor shall continuously monitor the federal regulatory landscape for new or amended AI requirements, proactively advise VA of compliance obligations and recommended actions, and maintain compliance tracking documentation suitable for audit and reporting to the Office of Management and Budget (OMB), Congress, or other oversight bodies. A written impact assessment will be delivered when new federal AI guidance, OMB memoranda, Executive Orders, National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) guidance, or VA policy changes affect the scope of the PWS. The contractor will be required to support VA compliance

Sources Sought Notice 
INTRODUCTION 
This Sources Sought Notice is for planning purposes only and shall not be considered as an 
Invitation for Bid, Request for Quotation, Request for Proposal or as an obligation on the part of 
the Government to acquire any products or services described herein. Your response to this 
sources sought will be treated as information only. No entitlement to payment direct or indirect 
costs or charges to the government’s use of such information. This request does not constitute a 
solicitation for proposals or the authority to enter into negotiations to award a contract. No funds 
have been authorized, appropriated or received by the Government for this Sources Sought 
Notice. The information provided by contractors may be used by the Navy in developing its 
acquisition strategy, Performance Work Statement (PWS) and/or Performance Specifications. 
Interested parties are responsible for adequately marking proprietary or competition sensitive 
information contained in their response. The Government does not intend to award a contract on 
the basis of this Sources Sought notice or to otherwise pay for the information submitted in 
response to this Sources Sought Notice. 
BACKGROUND 
The Naval Supply Systems Command (NA VSUP) Fleet Logistics Center (FLC) Norfolk is 
seeking information on qualified and experienced sources for planning purposes in an effort to 
derive a contract vehicle that will provide support for Navy Cyber Defense Operations 
Command (NCDOC) for Data Protection and Recovery services.  
This requirement is for secure vaulting, protection, and preservation of magnetic media and 
related film and tape material; provide tape vaulting to serve as major disaster recovery center 
during emergencies and disaster testing, as well as daily tape vaulting requirements; provide 
secure transportation to/from the secure vault and NCDOC on a weekly basis; provide immediate 
(within 4 hours) delivery of media to NCDOC located in the Hampton Roads area in case of 
emergency; provide full accountability of all media, to include online tracking; and, a dedicated 
account manager assigned to NCDOC, for the ability to contact 24/7 as needed in emergency 
situations.  Anticipated requirements for the continuation of this requirement can be found in the 
draft Performance Work Statement included within the Sources Sought. 
NA VSUP FLC Norfolk is issuing this Sources Sought as a means of conducting market research 
to identify parties having an interest in and the resources to support the requirement for data 
protection and recovery support services to support NCDOC.  
This is a follow-on requirement to contract N0018921P0362. 
 
 

ELIGIBILITY 
The purpose of this Sources Sought notice is to identify authorized and verified sources of 
services for an anticipated Firm-Fixed Price (FFP) Services contract under NAICS code 541519, 
Other Computer Related Services, with a Small Business Size Standard of $34 million. The 
product Service Code is DA01, IT and Telecom – Business Application/Application 
Development Support Services (Labor). The proposed contract vehicle will provide all the 
required services.  
A draft Performance Work Statement (PWS) which entails tasks and the description of work is 
attached for review (Attachment I). 
Responses to this Sources Sought Notice shall reference the Opportunity Name “NCDOC Data 
Protection” and shall include the following information in this format: 
1. Company name, address, point of contact name, phone number, and email address. 
2. Contractor, Government Entity (CAGE) Code, and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI). 
3. Size of Business – Large Business, Small Business, 8(a), HubZone, Women-Owned 
Small Business, Economically Disadvantaged Women-Owned Small Business, and/or 
Service Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business. 
4. Capability Statement displaying the contractor’s experience and ability to provide the 
minimum requirements of the PWS to include past performance information. If past 
performance information is used, please include only relevant information on the 
same/similar work within the last five (5) years. 
5. Include any other supporting documentation to include your Seaport-NxG and or GSA 
contract number and contracting experience under Seaport-NxG or GSA task orders 
awarded, task order number, award date, dollar value, period of performance/lead time 
for delivery, sub or prime, and brief description for each contract referenced. 
6. Provide any questions, comments, feedback regarding the draft PWS, planned contract 
type or any other associated information. 
 
Standard company brochures will not be reviewed. Submissions are not to exceed five (5) pages 
in length in Times New Roman font of not less than 12-point font. 
This is not a solicitation announcement for proposals and no contract will be awarded from this 
announcement. This Sources Sought Notice is not to be constructed in any way as a commitment 
by the Government, nor will the Government pay for the information submitted in response.  
The deadline for responses to this request is no later than 12 PM, EST 29 June 2026. 
All responses under this Sources Sought Notice shall be emailed to Kirsten Day, 
kirsten.t.day.civ@us.navy.mil and Amy Barnes, amy.m.barnes14.civ@us.navy.mil 

Again, this is not a request for a proposal. Respondents will not be notified of the results and the 
Government is not required to answer any questions submitted in regards to this Sources Sought 
Notice.
