Appendix A: Estimated Breakdown of Workflows by Site .......................................................... 27 

 
4 
 
 
SECTION 1: BACKGROUND 
American Battle Monuments Commission (ABMC) is an independent federal agency responsible 
for commemorating the service and sacrifice of members of the United States Armed Forces. 
ABMC operates and maintains 26 cemeteries and numerous memorials and monuments across 
17 countries, with staff located in Arlington, Virginia; Paris, France; and at overseas sites.  
 
ABMC currently utilizes ManageEngine for IT service management (ITSM) functions and 
requires an integrated, enterprise-wide platform capable of supporting structured enterprise case 
management workflows across Public Affairs, Historical Services, Human Resources, 
Operations, Finance, and other mission-support offices. 
Statement of Needs 
ABMC requires a consolidated, cloud-based Commercial-Off-The-Shelf (COTS) Freshworks 
enterprise service management (ESM) platform to replace its existing ITSM solution and 
implement standardized customer and enterprise case management capabilities across the 
agency. The solution must support approximately 550 internal users and designated agents, 
public media and historical service inquiries, and enable consistent intake, routing, Service Level 
Agreement (SLA) management, reporting, automation, and role-based access control.  
The platform must integrate with Microsoft 365 E5 and Microsoft Entra ID, support secure 
public-facing intake where required, and provide enterprise-grade auditability and data 
governance.  
ABMC requires subscription licenses and professional services necessary to configure, migrate, 
integrate, secure, train, and deploy the platform in phased increments, beginning with ITSM 
migration, Historical Services, Human Resources and Public Affairs case workflows and 
expanding to additional departments and global sites. 
Information Technology (IT) Environment 
ABMC operates a Microsoft 365 E5 hybrid enterprise environment with identity services 
managed through Microsoft Entra ID, supporting Single Sign-On (SSO), multi-factor 
authentication, and conditional access policies. Endpoint and mobile device management are 
administered through Microsoft Intune. The enterprise architecture emphasizes role-based access 
control, centralized logging, and secure cloud integrations.  
Any proposed solution must integrate with Microsoft Entra ID for identity federation, support 
standards-based provisioning such as SCIM where available, and align with federal 
cybersecurity, identity governance, and audit requirements. 
ABMC currently utilizes ManageEngine as its enterprise ITSM platform supporting incident 
management, service requests, change management, and asset tracking. The system maintains 
historical service records and a Configuration Management Database (CMDB) containing 
enterprise hardware and software assets across domestic and international locations. Core 
workflows support ticket intake, routing, escalation, and resolution. However, the current 

 
5 
 
platform is limited to IT service management functions and does not provide integrated ESM or 
structured case management capabilities for non-IT departments, resulting in additional inquiry 
and workflow processing occurring outside the ITSM system. 
SECTION 2: SCOPE OF WORK 
This contract is structured using Contract Line Item Numbers (CLINs) to organize the 
acquisition of software, implementation services, optional capabilities, and long-term 
sustainment in a phased and controlled manner.  
1. CLIN 0001 provides the required Freshworks software licenses for ITSM and business 
agents, structured with a base year and four option years and aligned to the phased 
rollout.  This CLIN shall be firm-fixed price.  
2. CLIN 0002 establishes the foundational implementation of the Freshworks platform, 
including core ITSM configuration, migration from ManageEngine, and initial 
departmental workflows. This CLIN shall be firm-fixed price. 
3. CLIN 0003 expands the platform to additional departments and global sites, deploying 
standardized enterprise service management and case management capabilities across the 
enterprise. This CLIN shall be firm-fixed price. 
4. CLIN 0004 focuses on optimization, enterprise standardization, and additional workflow 
deployment. This CLIN shall be firm-fixed price. 
5. CLIN 0005 provides optional Freddy AI licensing to enable AI-assisted capabilities. 
This CLIN shall be firm-fixed price. 
6. CLIN 0006 provides optional consulting and configuration services for future workflow 
expansion or new facilities. Work shall be authorized in writing by the Contracting 
Officer and is priced as fixed-price per authorized task unless otherwise authorized by the 
Contracting Officer. 
7. CLIN 0007 provides operations and maintenance support to sustain the platform during 
the base year and option periods. This CLIN shall be firm-fixed price. 
This CLIN structure allows ABMC to implement the platform in phases, control licensing 
activation, and maintain flexibility for future expansion while ensuring predictable costs across 
the contract period. 
Contractor shall manage kickoff meetings for each CLIN with different stakeholders, maintain a 
project schedule, track milestones, provide weekly status reports, and maintain a log of risks, 
issues, actions, and decisions. Contractor shall provide a project manager, a business analyst, and 
a configuration specialist and/or developer. 
CLIN 0001-Software Licensing (Base and Four Option Years) 
CLIN 0001 provides the Freshworks software subscriptions required to operate the IT service 
management and ESM platform implemented under CLINs 0002 through 0006. Contractor shall 
coordinate with the software manufacturer, Freshworks, to provide the licenses necessary to 
support IT service management agents, departmental agents, and case management users. 
Licensing shall support management of approximately 2,500 hardware and software assets 
within the Freshservice platform. Licenses shall be provided for one base year and four option 

 
6 
 
years and shall be activated in phases consistent with the implementation schedule defined under 
CLINs 0003 and 0004. 
 
Scope 
1. License Provisioning 
Contractor shall provide the Freshworks licenses required to operate the platform for 
ABMC personnel. Licenses shall support Office of the Chief Information Officer’s IT 
service management agents and business agents supporting departmental workflows, and 
agents supporting Historical Services, Human Resources, and Public Affairs case 
management functions. 
2. Year One Licensing Structure 
Licenses for the first year shall be activated according to the implementation schedule 
and shall include the following: 
Licenses for CLIN 0001 (12-month term) 
• Twelve (12) Freshservice Pro Agent licenses supporting the IT service management team 
• Fifteen (15) Freshservice Business Agent licenses supporting Human Resources departments 
in US and overseas locations 
• Ten (10) Freshdesk Pro Agent licenses supporting Public Affairs and Historical Services 
public-facing intake and communications (when Freshdesk is used for those functions) 
• Freshservice capability to manage approximately 2,500 hardware and software assets 
Licenses for CLINs 0003 & 0004 (6-month term) 
• Fifty-five (55) Freshservice Business Agent licenses supporting additional operations, 
administration, and Cemetery sites 
Licenses for CLIN 0005 (Optional) 
• Freddy AI for 12 IT agents 
Licenses associated with CLIN 0001 shall be activated at project kickoff. CLINs 0003 and 0004 
licenses shall be activated when expansion activities begin. CLIN 0005 licensing shall be 
activated when directed in writing by the Contracting Officer. 
3. Option Year Licensing Structure (Years 2 to 5) 
Beginning in Year 2 and continuing through each exercised option year, the following annual 
license quantities shall be maintained: 
• Twelve (12) Freshservice Pro Agent licenses supporting the IT service management team 
• Seventy (70) Freshservice Business Agent licenses supporting non-IT departments and global 
operations 
• Ten (10) Freshdesk Pro Agent licenses supporting Public Affairs and Historical Services public-
facing intake and communications (when Freshdesk is used for those functions) 
• Freshservice capability to manage approximately 2,500 hardware and software assets 

 
7 
 
 
 
Each option year represents a twelve-month subscription period that may be exercised at 
ABMC’s discretion. 
4. License Administration 
Contractor shall coordinate with Freshworks to ensure the correct license quantities are 
provisioned and available for assignment. Contractor shall ensure ABMC administrators 
are able to view license allocations and reassign licenses as needed within the purchased 
quantities. 
5. Compliance Requirements 
All software provided under this CLIN shall meet the security and hosting requirements 
defined in this Performance Work Statement. The platform shall support integration with 
Microsoft Entra ID for authentication and shall maintain appropriate access control and 
logging capabilities.

Question # Reference SOW Section Paragraph No. Question DHS Response
1 N/A N/A Will NCCS 2.0 require support across the full RMF lifecycle, including ATO package 
development, POA&M management, and ongoing continuous monitoring activities within 
NOSC environments?
No. DHS does not expect this contract offering to directly support governance, risk and compliance 
activities relating to ATO's or ISSO support services within this offering.
2 N/A N/A Will there be opportunities for small businesses, including SDVOSBs, to support ISSO functions 
and compliance efforts as part of prime contractor teams? No, ISSO and Compliance Support services are not included in the scope  of this contract.
3 What acquisition approach is DHS considering for NCCS 2.0 to best support scalable, long term 
network, cloud, and cyber operations (e.g., single vs. multiple award IDIQ/BPA, new or existing 
vehicle)?
DHS is considering a DHS Wide Strategic Sourcing Vehicle (SSV) Single award IDIQ. 
4 Will NCCS 2.0 operate as an enterprise wide NOSC capability across DHS, or be delivered 
through component specific operational models?
NCCS 2.0 is intended to operate as an enterprise-wide NOSC capability across DHS, serving as the central 
hub for IT service management, network, cloud, system, application, and cybersecurity monitoring and 
incident response for the DHS Onenet at all information processing and classification levels. Component-
specific operational models may be supported as needed. The primary focus is enterprise-wide coverage, 
with flexibility for component-specific needs. The DHS NOSC will continue to supprt other DHS 
Compenets as both the senior reporting point for the department and through the Cyber Security 
Provider program within DHS for components that choose to leverage the NOSC to provide those 
services.
5 How does DHS envision integrating prime contractors and specialized service providers for 
cloud engineering, cybersecurity operations, Zero Trust implementation, and managed NOSC 
services?
This offering is a single award IDIQ and the NOSC expects that any awardee will manage and maintain 
their awarded contract appropriately.
6 What level of emphasis does DHS anticipate on cloud native operations versus hybrid or on 
premises environments within AWS GovCloud and Azure Government?
DHS is a hybrid computing environment and will continue to have on premises, off premises and 
managed services providers depending upon the needs of service procured to support DHS.
7 Which security and operational frameworks will be most critical to NCCS 2.0 success, and how 
should service providers demonstrate ongoing alignment and compliance?
As a government agency DHS NSOC must follow all applicable laws, regulations and policies, including 
NIST Frameworks.
8 Is DHS seeking expanded use of automation and AI enabled capabilities (e.g., SOAR, 
automated remediation, predictive analytics) to enhance NOSC efficiency and resilience?
Yes, DHS NOSC expects the awardee to be able to support and recommend additional capabilities to 
improve the efficiency and resilience of the DHS NOSC and its capabilities.
9 Will NCCS 2.0 contractors be responsible for providing and managing core network and 
security tools, or will DHS retain platform ownership with contractors focused on operations 
and optimization?
DHS will continue to provide and maintain the tools that the staff within DHS NOSC leverage or operate.
10 What small business participation goals or socioeconomic considerations does DHS anticipate 
for NCCS 2.0?
DHS proposed subcontracting goals will be provided in the draft/final RFP
11 When evaluating proposals, will DHS place greater weight on DHS specific NOSC experience, 
broader federal cyber/cloud operations, or large scale enterprise managed services 
experience?
The instructions on how the government will evaluate proposals will be provided in the solicitation once 
it is finalized.  
12 What is the anticipated timeline from Industry Day to draft RFP, final solicitation, and award, 
and does DHS plan additional industry engagements?
Please see notional time line in Industry day slides.  The government anticipates a presoliciation 
conference.
13 Will DHS provide guidance for small businesses interested in teaming or subcontracting under 
NCCS 2.0?
Yes, information about teaming and subcontracting requirements will be in the solicitation. 
14 Are there specific capability areas where DHS expects small business participation to be 
especially valuable?
DHS expects small business participation to be especially valuable in areas such as field engineering 
technical services, surge support, vulnerability assessments, cybersecurity audits, training and exercise 
programs, and specialized operational support for network, cloud, and cybersecurity monitoring and 
analysis as deemed necessary or required. Small businesses may also contribute to innovation, 
automation, and continuous service improvement initiatives, as well as provide niche expertise for 
incident response and operational optimization. DHS supports the inclusion of small businesses in these 
roles to enhance flexibility, responsiveness, and technical depth within NOSC operations.
15 Will an attendee list, teaming forum, or prime contractor contact list be made available after 
Industry Day?
This list has been released on sam.gov and includes only those attendees who have agreed to share their 
information
16 Will the Government entertain One-on-One meetings with the industry?
At this time, we do not anticipate conducting one on one meetings. However, we will keep the possibility 
under consideration and will keep industry abreast of any changes to this approach. 
17 Does the Government have plans to release this as a Small Business? Or any other categories 
within Small Business?
At this time, DHS is planning to release this as a full and open solicitation.
18 Will there be opportunities for small businesses, including SDVOSBs, to support ISSO functions 
and compliance efforts as part of prime contractor teams?
No, ISSO and Compliance Support services are not included in the scope of this contract.
19 How does DHS anticipate the contractor's role in supporting AI governance, risk management, 
and oversight obligations for AI-enabled capabilities operating within the NOSC environment, 
including alignment to the NIST AI Risk Management Framework?
AI Governance or policy support services are not included in the scope of this contract.
20 Does DHS expect AI governance and policy support to be performed within the NCCS 2.0 
scope, or addressed through a separate vehicle or task?
AI Governance or policy support services are not included in the scope of this contract.
21 Will DHS encourage or require small business teaming arrangements that bring AI governance 
and policy expertise alongside traditional network and cyber operations capabilities?
AI Governance or policy support services are not included in the scope of this contract.
22 Will DHS be submitting the final RFP to all firms who responded to the RFI or only selected 
organizations? 
The RFP will be posted on Sam.gov to all of industry.
23 Will DHS be having a small business set-aside awardee as part of the multi-award approach? No this is a single award IDIQ
24 Will the final procurement require an active Top Secret Facility Clearance at the time of 
proposal submission?
Yes.
25 Will DHS permit subcontractor Facility Clearance reliance, or must the prime contractor 
independently possess the required clearance level?
Under the National Industrial Security Program (NISP), the prime contractor must independently possess 
the required Facility Clearance (FCL) and cannot begin a classified contract based solely on a 
subcontractor’s FCL. However, unclassified support may be provided for the contract until the prime 
obtains its final FCL.
26 Is DHS anticipating a single award or multiple award IDIQ structure? DHS anticipates a single award IDIQ.
27 What contract type is currently anticipated for this effort: Time & Materials, Labor Hour, Firm 
Fixed Price, Hybrid structure
DHS is anticipating an IDIQ that allows LH, T&M, FFP or hybrid task orders.
Industry Day for NCCS 2.0 (May 19, 2026)

28 Will DHS require an approved purchasing system, EVMS, or other contractor business system 
requirements?
NCCS 2.0 is a services contract and not a system. EVMS will not be required.  Since the Government 
anticipates T&M and cost reimbursement CLINS for Travel/ODCs, offerors must have an adequate 
accounting system in accordance with RFO 16.301-3(a)
29 Will small business Joint Ventures, Contractor Teaming Arrangements, or mentor protege 
structures be permitted?
Yes
30 Who are the current incumbent prime contractors supporting NCCS and NOSC operations? This is not an all inclusive list:  Leidos , Caci, APF Technology, LLC, Decision Point
31 Approximately how many total FTEs currently support this environment? 100+ current FTEs.
32 Approximately what percentage of personnel require Secret, Top Secret, TS/SCI, SAP 
elegibility?
Specific personnel requirements will be addressed in the solicitation or RFP instructions. DHS will require 
contractors to maintain staff with the requisite security clearances, compartment accesses, and DHS 
suitability statuses to perform work at all NOSC locations, including classified system and resource 
monitoring. The actual percentage will depend on task order requirements and the mix of classified and 
unclassified work, which will be defined at the task order level.
33 What is the approximate operational split between Network Operations, Cloud Operations, 
Cybersecurity Operations, Program Management/PMO Support?
Selected material will be shared in the technical library.  Instructions to review materials in the technical 
library will be released within the RFP
34 Is the incumbent workforce retention anticipated to be a significant consideration? Incumbent workforce retention is always a so und practice for any awardee to pursue, but not required by 
DHS.
35 Which locations are expected to require permanent onsite support? The locations will be defined in each Task Order.
36 Will contractor personnel require access to SCIF environments for operational support 
activities?
Yes, supporting classified environments is within scope of this contract and will be defined at the task 
order.
37 Will Government furnished SCIF workspace be provided, or will accredited contractor SCIF 
capability be required for portions of performance?
Yes, government furnished SCIF workspace will be provided and No, contractor accredited SCIF 
space is not required.  
38 What major enterprise platforms and environments are currently in scope, including SIEM, 
cloud, and IT service management platforms?
DHS is a hybrid computing environment and will continue to have on premises, off premises and 
managed services providers depending upon the needs of service procured to support DHS.  DHS will 
continue to provide and maintain the tools that the staff within DHS NOSC leverage or operate.
39 Are there Government furnished tools currently supporting operations, or is DHS anticipating 
contractor provided tooling in certain areas?
Yes but DHS will continue to provide and maintain the tools that the staff within DHS NOSC leverage or 
operate. A list of tools will be provided in the technical library.
40 Is DHS expecting operational maturity demonstrations related to automation, AI assisted 
analysis, or agentic AI capabilities?
No
41 What transition period is currently anticipated? This will be determined by the individual Task Order awards
42 Are there known stfafing shortage areas or historically difficult to fill labor categories within 
the currently operational environment?
No, no more than DHS has experienced with other IT Contracts. Competition for more senior developed 
personnel with clearances has historically been observed.
43 Is surge staffing currently utilized to support operational requirements? Surge staffing is leveraged when necessary to support efforts on an as needed basis.
44 What operational capability areas are expected to be most critical to successful contract 
performance?
All areas are considered critical for successful contract performance
45 Will DHS evaluate demonstrated experience supporting DHS Cybersecurity Service Provider 
maturity requirements and classified cyber operations environments?
Yes. DHS will evaluate demonstrated experience supporting DHS Cybersecurity Service Provider (CSP) 
maturity requirements and classified cyber operations environments. The SOW requires contractors to 
maintain CSP Program Center of Excellence accreditation, comply with CSP Evaluator Scoring Metrics, and 
support operations across all classification levels, including Secret, Top Secret, TS/SCI, and SAP. Offerors 
will be expected to show relevant experience and maturity in these areas as part of the evaluation 
process.
46  Can DHS confirm whether NCCS 2.0 is anticipated to utilize a single-award IDIQ structure to 
streamline contract administration, establish clear accountability, improve responsiveness to 
evolving mission requirements, and enable rapid operational scaling and surge support?
Yes, DHS anticipates a single award IDIQ.
47 Would DHS consider a multi-phase source selection approach in which Phase 1 evaluates 
recent and relevant past performance to efficiently narrow the competitive range to the most 
qualified offerors, followed by a Phase 2 evaluation focused on operational expertise, 
technical approach, mission alignment, and price realism in support of selecting the highest 
technically rated offeror with a fair and reasonable price?
Yes. DHS will consider a phased approach as we continue to formulate the source selection process.  Past 
performance is not being considered as an evaluation factor at this time.  
48 Would DHS consider incorporating oral presentations, including scenario-based discussions, 
into the NCCS 2.0 evaluation process to accelerate procurement timelines, reduce evaluation 
burden, and better assess an offeror’s operational understanding, technical approach, and the 
real-world decision-making capabilities of proposed key personnel and SMEs?
At this time oral presentations are not being considered.  
49  If oral presentations are utilized, would DHS consider a structured format in which offerors 
provide a 30-minute technical and management presentation followed by 90 minutes of 
interactive response to realistic operational scenarios, enabling DHS to evaluate real-time 
collaboration, technical problem solving, and operational leadership among proposed 
performing personnel?
At this time oral presentations are not being considered.

current three-level approach (e.g., High Confidence, Some Confidence, Low/No Confidence) to

BACKGROUND

The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Veterans Health Administration (VHA), Human Capital Management (HCM) is committed to providing high-quality, efficient, and modern human resources (HR) support to those who deliver care to our Nation’s Veterans. With increasing workforce transparency and accountability demands, evolving regulations and policies, and a growing need to accelerate hiring there is a requirement for the evolution of VHA’s talent acquisition strategy and HR service management capabilities. This evolution is essential to ensure VHA can quickly source, attract, and hire top talent while improving service delivery and the employee experience.   

To meet these challenges, VHA HCM is pursuing the acquisition of a next generation Human Resource Service Management (HRSM) Software as a Service (SaaS) solution that is a cohesive suite of applications designed to streamline HR services across the enterprise. This initiative will augment USA Staffing and USA Hire capabilities to assist in the recruitment and hiring of healthcare professionals, as well as onboarding of other employee types identified in Optional Task 8. The solution will integrate modern technologies, including analytics, to identify bottlenecks, hiring trends, and gaps to assist in tracking and reducing of VA’s Time‑to‑Hire, currently averaging 80–100 days. The solution will also include digital tools that enhance service delivery for our current employees by providing a range of knowledge, resources, service desk and self-service tools, resulting in enhanced candidate and employee experience as well as productivity. Integrating enterprise systems and consolidating capabilities into a single modern solution, the HRSM initiative directly supports VA’s enterprise talent acquisition strategy and HR service delivery goals.  

The HRSM solution will also integrate with VA’s personnel system, the future Federal HR 2.0 system and core architecture to ensure seamless, secure, and scalable operations across VHA’s 374,000+ user enterprise.

ACKNOWLEDGMENT OF AMENDMENTS: The offeror acknowledges receipt of amendments to the Solicitation numbered and dated as follows:

B.2 GOVERNING LAW CLAUSE

Federal law and regulations, including the Federal Acquisition Regulations (FAR), shall govern this Order.  Commercial license agreements may be made a part of this Order but only if both parties expressly make them an addendum hereto, as permitted by FAR 12.212.  If the commercial license agreement is not made an addendum, it shall not apply, govern, be a part of or have any effect whatsoever on the Order; this includes, but is not limited to, any agreement embedded in the computer software (clickwrap), any agreement that is otherwise delivered with or provided to the Government with the commercial computer software or documentation (shrinkwrap), or any other license agreement otherwise referred to in any document.  If a commercial license agreement is made an addendum, only those provisions addressing data rights regarding the Government’s use, duplication and disclosure of data (e.g., restricted computer software) are included and made a part of this Order, and only to the extent that those provisions are not duplicative or inconsistent with Federal law, Federal regulation, the incorporated FAR clauses and the provisions of this Order; those provisions in the commercial license agreement that do not address data rights regarding the Government’s use, duplication and disclosure of data shall not be included or made a part of the Order.  Federal law and regulation including, without limitation, the Contract Disputes Act (41 U.S.C. § 7101 et seq.), the Anti-Deficiency Act (31 U.S.C. § 1341 et seq.), the Competition in Contracting Act (41 U.S.C. § 3301 et seq.), the Prompt Payment Act (31 U.S.C. § 3901 et seq.), Contracts for Data Processing or Maintenance (38 USC § 5725), and FAR clauses 52.212-4, 52.227-14, 52.227-19 shall supersede, control, and render ineffective any inconsistent, conflicting, or duplicative provision in any commercial license agreement.  In the event of conflict between this clause and any provision in the Order or the commercial license agreement or elsewhere, the terms of this clause shall prevail.  The Contractor shall deliver to the Government all data first produced under this Order with unlimited rights as defined by FAR 52.227-14.  Claims of patent or copyright infringement brought against the Government as a party shall be defended by the U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ) in accordance with 28 U.S.C. § 516; at the discretion of DOJ, the Contractor may be allowed reasonable participation in the defense of the litigation.  Any additional changes to the Order must be made by modification (Standard Form 30) and shall only be made by a warranted Contracting Officer.  Nothing in this Order or any commercial license agreement shall be construed as a waiver of sovereign immunity.

B.3 SOFTWARE LICENSE, MAINTENANCE AND TECHNICAL SUPPORT

(1). Definitions.

Licensee.  The term “licensee” shall mean the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (“VA”) and is synonymous with “Government.” 

Licensor.  The term “licensor” shall mean the Contractor having the necessary license or ownership rights to deliver license, software maintenance and support of the computer software being acquired.  The term “Contractor” is the party identified in Block 17a on the SF1449.  If the Contractor is a reseller and not the Licensor, the Contractor remains responsible for performance under this Contract/Order. 

Software.  The term “software” shall mean the licensed computer software product(s) cited in the Schedule of Supplies/Services. 

Maintenance.  The term “maintenance” is the process of enhancing and optimizing software, as well as remedying defects.  It shall include all new fixes, patches, releases, updates, versions and upgrades, as further defined below. 

Technical Support.  The term “technical support” refers to the range of services providing assistance for the software via the telephone, email, a website or otherwise. 

Release or Update.  The term “release” or “update” are terms that refer to a revision of software that contains defect corrections, minor enhancements or improvements of the software’s functionality.  This is usually designated by a change in the number to the right of the decimal point (e.g., from Version 5.3 to 5.4).  An example of an update is the addition of new hardware. 

Version or Upgrade.  The term “version” or “upgrade” are terms that refer to a revision of software that contains new or improved functionality.  This is usually designated by a change in the number to the left of the decimal point (e.g., from Version 5.4 to 6). 

(2). Software License.

a) Notwithstanding any contrary provisions contained in the Contractor’s standard commercial license or lease agreement, the Contractor agrees that the Government will have the rights that are set forth in paragraph (e) of this clause to use, duplicate or disclose any commercial computer software delivered under this contract. The terms and provisions of this contract shall comply with Federal laws and the Federal Acquisition Regulation. 

b) Unless otherwise stated in the Schedule of Supplies/Services, the Product Description, the software license provided to the Government is a perpetual, nonexclusive license to use the software. 

c) The Government may use the software in a networked environment. 

d) All limitations of software usage are expressly stated in the Schedule of Supplies/Services and the Product Description.

e) The commercial computer software delivered under this contract may not be used, reproduced, or disclosed by the Government except as provided below or as expressly stated otherwise in this contract. The commercial computer software may be: Used or copied for use with the computer(s) for which it was acquired, including use at any Government installation or agency to which the computer(s) may be transferred; ii. Used or copied for use with a backup computer if any computer for which it was acquired is inoperative; iii. Reproduced for safekeeping (archives) or backup purposes; iv. Modified, adapted, or combined with other computer software; v. Disclosed to and reproduced for use by support service Contractors or their subcontractors, subject to the same restrictions set forth in this contract; and vi. Used or copied for use with a replacement computer.

f) Unauthorized Obligations.

 i. Except as stated in paragraph (ii), when any supply or service acquired under this contract is subject to any commercial supplier agreement (as defined in 502.101) that includes any language, provision, or clause requiring the Government to pay any future fees, penalties, interest, legal costs or to indemnify the Contractor or any person or entity for damages, costs, fees, or any other loss or liability that would create an Anti-Deficiency Act violation ( 31 U.S.C. 1341), the following shall govern: 

1) Any such language, provision, or clause is unenforceable against the Government. 

2) Neither the Government nor any Government authorized end user shall be deemed to have agreed to such clause by virtue of it appearing in the commercial supplier agreement. If the commercial supplier agreement is invoked through an “I agree” click box or other comparable mechanism (e.g., “click-wrap” or “browse-wrap” agreements), execution does not bind the Government or any Government authorized end user to such clause.

 3) Any such language, provision, or clause is deemed to be stricken from the commercial supplier agreement.

 ii. Paragraph (u)(1) of this clause does not apply to indemnification or any other payment by the Government that is expressly authorized by statute and specifically authorized under applicable agency regulations and procedures. 

Commercial supplier agreements unenforceable clauses.

This agreement is a part of a contract between the commercial supplier and the U.S. Government for the acquisition of the supply or service that necessitates a license or other similar legal instrument (including all contracts, task orders, and delivery orders under FAR 12). 

ii. End user. This agreement shall bind the ordering activity as end user but shall not operate to bind a Government employee or person acting on behalf of the Government in his or her personal capacity. 

iii. Law and disputes. This agreement is governed by Federal law. Any language purporting to subject the U.S. Government to the laws of a U.S. state, U.S. territory, district, or municipality, or a foreign nation, except where Federal law expressly provides for the application of such laws, is hereby deleted.

1) Any language requiring dispute resolution in a specific forum or venue that is different from that prescribed by applicable Federal law is hereby deleted. Any dispute regarding the license grant or usage limitations shall be resolved in accordance with the Disputes Clause incorporated in FAR 52.212-4(d). 

2) Any language prescribing a different time period for bringing an action than that prescribed by applicable Federal law in relation to a dispute is hereby deleted. 

3) Continued performance. The supplier or licensor shall not unilaterally revoke, terminate or suspend any rights granted to the Government except as allowed by this contract. If the supplier or licensor believes the ordering activity to be in breach of the agreement, it shall pursue its rights under the Contract Disputes Act or other applicable Federal statute while continuing. 

4) Arbitration; equitable or injunctive relief. In the event of a claim or dispute arising under or relating to this agreement, a binding arbitration shall not be used unless specifically authorized by agency guidance, and equitable or injunctive relief, including the award of attorney fees, costs or interest, may be awarded against the U.S. Government only when explicitly provided by statute (e.g., Prompt Payment Act or Equal Access to Justice Act)

Updating terms. After award, the contractor may unilaterally revise commercial supplier agreement terms if they are not material. A material change is defined as: 

1) Terms that change Government rights or obligations;

 2) Terms that increase Government prices; 

3) Terms that decrease overall level of service; or

4) Terms that limit any other Government right addressed elsewhere in this contract. 

5) For revisions that will materially change the terms of the contract, the revised commercial supplier agreement must be incorporated into the contract using a bilateral modification. 

6) Any agreement license terms or conditions unilaterally revised subsequent to award that are inconsistent with any material term or provision of this contract shall not be enforceable against the Government, and the Government shall not be deemed to have consented to them.

v. No automatic renewals. If any license or service tied to periodic payment is provided under this agreement (e.g., annual software maintenance or annual lease term), such license or service shall not renew automatically upon expiration of its current term without prior express consent by an authorized Government representative. vi. Indemnification. Any clause of this agreement requiring the commercial supplier or licensor to defend or indemnify the end user is hereby amended to provide that the U.S. Department of Justice has the sole right to represent the United States in any such action, in accordance with 28 U.S.C. 516.

 vii. Audits. Any clause of this agreement permitting the commercial supplier or licensor to audit the end user's compliance with this agreement is hereby amended as follows: 

1) Discrepancies found in an audit may result in a charge by the commercial supplier or licensor to the ordering activity. Any resulting invoice must comply with the proper invoicing requirements specified in the underlying Government contract or order.

 2) This charge, if disputed by the ordering activity, will be resolved in accordance with FAR 52.212-4(d); no payment obligation shall arise on the part of the ordering activity until the conclusion of the dispute process.

 3) Any audit requested by the contractor will be performed at the contractor's expense, without reimbursement by the Government.
